subject: IfcActor
rationale: IfcActor can be a person (IfcPerson) who performs actions within the building context.
conditions: IfcActor represents a person acting in a role

subject: IfcActor
rationale: IfcActor can represent an organization that takes on a role in the project.
conditions: IfcActor represents an organizational entity

subject: IfcActor
rationale: IfcActor entities often underpin ownership and responsibility tracking in the model.
conditions: Actors are responsible for the creation and modification of model data

subject: IfcActor
rationale: The IfcRelAssignsToActor relationship links actors to the building elements they are responsible for.
conditions: An actor can be assigned to objects, processes, or resources through this relationship

subject: IfcActor
rationale: IfcActor aggregates IfcPerson or IfcOrganization to define who the actor is.
conditions: When IfcActor represents an individual

subject: IfcActor
rationale: IfcActor can contain organizational information as part of its definition.
conditions: When IfcActor represents a group or company

subject: IfcActor
rationale: By assigning ownership and responsibility, actors protect the integrity of project data.
conditions: Actors ensure that project information is correctly assigned and traceable

subject: IfcActionRequest
rationale: IfcActionRequest in IFC is typically associated with a work plan that schedules the requested actions.
conditions: when action requests are part of planned maintenance or construction workflows

subject: IfcActionRequest
rationale: An IfcActionRequest can assign an actor (requester or responsible party).
conditions: when the request identifies who made or is responsible for the request

subject: IfcActionRequest
rationale: IfcActionRequest can be related to building elements, systems, or processes via control relationships.
conditions: when the action request controls or is assigned to other IFC objects

subject: IfcActionRequest
rationale: Action requests typically have property sets for metadata like status, priority, date raised, date due.
applicability: IfcActionRequest does not strictly 'require' IfcPropertySet. Property sets are optional in the IFC schema and can be attached via IfcRelDefinesByProperties. Many valid use cases exist where an action request uses only its predefined attributes (like RequestID, Description, Status, etc.) without needing additional property sets.
conditions: when additional properties like request status, priority, or date are needed

subject: IfcActionRequest
rationale: Every IfcActionRequest must be associated with a project (IfcProject) context in IFC data structure.
conditions: when the request exists within a specific project context

subject: IfcActionRequest
rationale: IfcActionRequest inherits from IfcRoot and requires owner history for data management.
applicability: IfcOwnerHistory is mandatory for all IFC entities in the IFC2x3 and IFC4 schemas (it is a required attribute of the IfcRoot supertype from which IfcActionRequest inherits), not optional 'when tracking changes and ownership is needed.' The assertion correctly identifies the relationship but incorrectly frames it as conditional.
conditions: when tracking changes and ownership of the request is needed

subject: IfcActionRequest
rationale: Action requests can be assigned to processes via IfcRelAssignsToProcess to link requests to tasks.
conditions: when the action request is assigned to a process or task

subject: IfcActorRole
rationale: IfcActorRole defines a role for an actor; an actor is typically a person or organization, so it requires an IfcPerson or IfcOrganization to be meaningful.
conditions: when an actor role is assigned to a specific person

subject: IfcActorRole
rationale: IfcActorRole is associated with IfcActor through IfcPerson or IfcOrganization, as the role context is meaningless without an actor entity.
conditions: when an actor role is assigned to an organization

subject: IfcActorRole
rationale: IfcActorRole is used as a role assignment for IfcActor; it depends on being referenced by an IfcActor entity to have context in a building model.

subject: IfcActorRole
rationale: While not a direct dependency, IfcActorRole is typically meaningful only in the context of an IfcProject that defines the overall project team and stakeholder structure.
conditions: when used within the context of a building project

subject: IfcActuator
rationale: Valve actuators are mechanically coupled to valves to regulate fluid flow.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcActuator depends_on Valves' with condition 'when actuator is a valve actuator' has a circular dependency issue: a valve actuator by definition relates to a valve, so this is a tautology rather than a meaningful dependency. Additionally, the existing exception already acknowledges that the actuator may be for dampers or louvers, which means the condition effectively only covers the tautological case.
conditions: when actuator is a valve actuator
exceptions: actuators used for dampers or louvers

subject: IfcActuatorType
rationale: IfcActuatorType defines the type information for IfcActuator occurrences; the type requires the occurrence entity to be instantiated for it to have practical function.
conditions: When defining the type for an actuator element

subject: IfcActuatorType
rationale: IfcActuatorType is a subtype of IfcDistributionControlElementType, inheriting its properties and relationships.
conditions: Generalization relationship

subject: IfcActuatorType
rationale: The relationship between the type and occurrences is established through IfcRelDefinesByType.
applicability: The assertion is correct only if the IfcActuatorType actually has occurrences assigned to it. IfcRelDefinesByType is only required when one or more IfcActuator occurrences are assigned to this type. A bare IfcActuatorType with no occurrences does not depend on IfcRelDefinesByType.

subject: IfcActuatorType
rationale: IfcActuatorType provides the shared type definitions (e.g., PredefinedType) that govern the behavior and properties of actuator occurrences.

subject: IfcActuatorType
rationale: Property sets defining the actuator type's characteristics are assigned via IfcRelDefinesByType.
applicability: The condition 'If property sets are assigned to the type' is already stated, but the assertion uses 'depends_on' which implies a mandatory dependency. If property sets are not assigned, there is no dependency on IfcPropertySetDefinition, so the unqualified 'depends_on' label is misleading without reading the full context.
conditions: If property sets are assigned to the type

subject: IfcActuatorType
rationale: Actuators are typically connected to distribution flow elements (valves, dampers) to physically operate them.
conditions: When the actuator operates a flow control device like a valve or damper

subject: IfcActuatorType
rationale: The type can contain property sets that define its characteristics.
conditions: When property sets are assigned to the type

subject: IfcAddress
rationale: IfcAddress is an abstract supertype; IfcPostalAddress is its primary concrete subtype for postal/mailing addresses.
conditions: when representing a physical mailing address

subject: IfcAddress
rationale: IfcTelecomAddress is the other concrete subtype of IfcAddress for telecommunications contact information.
conditions: when representing telephone, email, or web addresses

subject: IfcAddress
rationale: IfcAddress is typically assigned to IfcBuilding via the IfcRelAddresses relationship to provide the building's location and contact information.
conditions: when the address is assigned to a building

subject: IfcAddress
rationale: IfcAddress can be related to IfcSite via IfcRelAddresses to provide the site's address.
conditions: when the address is assigned to a site

subject: IfcAddress
rationale: IfcAddress can be assigned to IfcOrganization via IfcRelAddresses for contact information.
conditions: when the address is assigned to an organization

subject: IfcAddress
rationale: IfcAddress can be assigned to IfcPerson via IfcRelAddresses for personal contact details.
conditions: when the address is assigned to a person

subject: IfcAddress
rationale: IfcAddress connects to spatial elements like IfcBuilding and IfcSite through the IfcRelAddresses relationship.
conditions: via IfcRelAddresses

subject: IfcAdvancedBrep
rationale: For proper spatial positioning, IfcAdvancedBrep relies on IfcAxis2Placement3D to define its local coordinate system.
conditions: when IfcAdvancedBrep is placed in 3D space

subject: IfcAdvancedBrep
rationale: IfcAdvancedBrep's boundary representation is composed of faces, edges, and vertices defined by IfcCartesianPoint.
applicability: IfcCartesianPoint is required indirectly via the topological structure (IfcClosedShell > IfcFace > IfcFaceBound > IfcEdgeLoop > IfcOrientedEdge > IfcEdge > IfcVertex > IfcVertexPoint > IfcCartesianPoint), not directly 'for defining vertex coordinates of the B-rep structure' as stated. The assertion oversimplifies the indirect chain.
conditions: for defining vertex coordinates of the B-rep structure

subject: IfcAdvancedBrep
rationale: IfcAdvancedBrep uses IfcFaceBound (specifically IfcClosedShell) to define the outer boundary of the solid.
conditions: to define the closed shell of the B-rep

subject: IfcAdvancedBrep
rationale: IfcAdvancedBrep typically uses IfcAdvancedFace to define faces that may have non-planar surface geometries such as B-spline surfaces.
conditions: when the B-rep includes faces with advanced surface geometry
exceptions: Basic B-reps may use simpler IfcFace subtypes

subject: IfcAdvancedBrep
rationale: IfcAdvancedBrep can be mapped via IfcRepresentationMap for reuse, but this is optional.
conditions: when IfcAdvancedBrep is used in a mapped representation
exceptions: Not needed when used directly without mapping

subject: IfcAdvancedBrep
rationale: IfcAdvancedBrep provides high-fidelity 3D geometry for building product definitions.
applicability: Building elements like IfcWall, IfcSlab, IfcBeam, etc.
conditions: when IfcProduct uses IfcAdvancedBrep as its geometry representation

subject: IfcAdvancedBrep
rationale: IfcAdvancedBrep supports the representation of complex building elements with non-planar surfaces such as curved curtain walls, sculptural columns, or organic roof shapes.
conditions: when advanced double-curved or free-form geometry is needed

subject: IfcAdvancedBrep
rationale: IfcAdvancedBrep can result from IfcBooleanClippingResult operations that cut or combine geometric shapes.
conditions: when the B-rep is a result of a Boolean clipping operation

subject: IfcAdvancedBrep
rationale: An IfcAdvancedBrep logically contains an IfcClosedShell as the fundamental structure representing the solid's boundary.
conditions: for defining the closed volume of the solid

subject: IfcAdvancedBrep
rationale: The shell contains edges connecting vertices to form the wireframe of the boundary.
conditions: as part of the boundary representation structure

subject: IfcAdvancedBrep
rationale: IfcAdvancedBrep can contain IfcFaceSurface to bind each face to a surface such as a B-spline surface.
applicability: Advanced boundary representations with curved surfaces
conditions: when faces are defined on underlying surfaces
exceptions: Planar faces use IfcFace or IfcFaceBound

subject: IfcAdvancedBrepWithVoids
rationale: IfcAdvancedBrepWithVoids is a subtype of IfcAdvancedBrep, so it inherits all properties and depends on the base class definition.
applicability: Any building model using advanced boundary representation
conditions: When representing a solid with internal voids

subject: IfcAdvancedBrepWithVoids
rationale: The advanced B-rep with voids uses closed shells to define the outer boundary of the solid.
conditions: When defining the outer boundary of the solid

subject: IfcAdvancedBrepWithVoids
rationale: Advanced B-rep geometries are built from face-based surface models with advanced face definitions.
conditions: When the geometry is defined by faces

subject: IfcAdvancedBrepWithVoids
rationale: Advanced B-rep with voids uses IfcAdvancedFace (faces with advanced surface types) to define its boundaries.
conditions: When defining the bounding faces of the solid or its voids

subject: IfcAdvancedBrepWithVoids
rationale: Like all topology representations, it needs to be referenced through an IfcShapeRepresentation.
applicability: When IfcAdvancedBrepWithVoids is placed in a product model
conditions: When used within a product representation context

subject: IfcAdvancedBrepWithVoids
rationale: IfcAdvancedBrepWithVoids is a specialized form of manifold solid B-rep, supporting the manifold solid concept.
conditions: In subtype hierarchy

subject: IfcAdvancedBrepWithVoids
rationale: The closed shells that define the solid and voids are composed of connected face sets.
conditions: When the shells are composed of connected faces

subject: IfcAdvancedFace
rationale: IfcAdvancedFace requires an IfcEdgeLoop or similar topological boundary definition to define its edges and vertices in accordance with the advanced BREP representation.
conditions: The advanced face must be defined by an edge loop boundary

subject: IfcAdvancedFace
rationale: Advanced faces often use IfcEdgeCurve objects to define curved edges in the face boundary.
conditions: When edges are curved
For advanced face with non-planar boundaries

subject: IfcAdvancedFace
rationale: Cartesian points define the geometric coordinates of vertices that form the face boundary.
conditions: For defining vertex geometry of the face

subject: IfcAdvancedFace
rationale: IfcAdvancedFace is typically contained within an IfcAdvancedBrep representation to form a complete solid geometry.
conditions: When used as part of an advanced boundary representation

subject: IfcAdvancedFace
rationale: The face depends on a valid placement and coordinate system to position its geometry correctly in 3D space.
applicability: IfcAdvancedFace does not directly depend on IfcAxis2Placement3D. The surface geometry referenced by IfcAdvancedFace (via IfcSurface) may use IfcAxis2Placement3D for positioning, but the face entity itself does not have a direct dependency or attribute referencing IfcAxis2Placement3D. This is an indirect dependency at best.
conditions: When the face is defined in a 3D coordinate system

subject: IfcAdvancedFace
rationale: Multiple advanced faces can be assembled into IfcConnectedFaceSet to represent complex building geometry.
conditions: When part of a larger connected topological structure

subject: IfcAdvancedFace
rationale: IfcAdvancedFace can serve as a face element in advanced boundary representations supporting solid geometry.
conditions: When representing faceted geometry with advanced face topology

subject: IfcAdvancedFace
rationale: According to the IFC schema, an IfcAdvancedFace contains one or more IfcFaceBound objects that define its outer and inner boundaries.
conditions: An IfcAdvancedFace always contains at least one face bound
exceptions: Void faces or openings may have inner bounds as well

subject: IfcAdvancedFace
rationale: IfcPolyLoop can be used within the face bound to define a polygonal boundary of the advanced face.
conditions: When the face boundary is defined by a closed polygon

subject: IfcAdvancedFace
rationale: IfcAdvancedFace can connect to IfcFaceSurface instances when forming part of a shell or connected face set.
conditions: When sharing edge geometry with adjacent faces

subject: IfcAdvancedFace
rationale: Each IfcAdvancedFace references an IfcSurface (e.g., IfcPlane, IfcCylindricalSurface, IfcBSplineSurface) which defines the underlying surface geometry of the face.
conditions: The advanced face must reference a surface geometry

subject: IfcAirTerminal
rationale: IfcAirTerminal requires ductwork to transport conditioned air to and from the terminal device.
conditions: air distribution system must be properly designed
exceptions: decentralized systems with direct wall openings

subject: IfcAirTerminal
rationale: The air terminal is the endpoint of an HVAC system and cannot function without the upstream system.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcAirTerminal depends_on HVAC System' is so broad (applicable to 'all buildings with mechanical ventilation') that it provides limited semantic value. Nearly every building component depends on some system. The assertion should clarify what specific type of dependency is meant (e.g., control dependency, air supply dependency, structural support). As stated, it is a truism that could apply to virtually all HVAC components.
conditions: system must be operational

subject: IfcAirTerminal
rationale: The AHU conditions and moves air that passes through the air terminal.
conditions: AHU must supply conditioned air
exceptions: dedicated outdoor air systems (DOAS) with terminal units

subject: IfcAirTerminal
rationale: Fire dampers may be required at air terminal connections through fire-rated partitions.
conditions: where duct penetrates fire-rated separation
exceptions: non-rated barriers
ducts with fire-rated construction

The assertion states 'IfcAirTerminal requires Fire damper' with condition 'where duct penetrates fire-rated separation'. However, some types of air terminals (e.g., ceiling diffusers with integral fire dampers, or combination fire/smoke dampers) may have the fire damper integrated into the terminal unit itself. In such cases, the fire damper is not a separate, additional required component but part of the terminal assembly. This could cause double-counting or redundant requirements in a model.

subject: IfcAirTerminal
rationale: Insulation prevents condensation and thermal bridging at the terminal-to-duct connection.
conditions: to prevent condensation on cold air terminals
exceptions: warm air supply only
non-condensing environments

subject: IfcAirTerminal
rationale: The air terminal physically connects to the duct system as the endpoint of air distribution.
exceptions: terminal may be ductless in some unitary systems

subject: IfcAirTerminal
rationale: Some specialized air terminals include filters, but this is less common.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcAirTerminal contains Air Filter' with condition 'if terminal includes integral filtration' is circular — it essentially states that air terminals with integral filters contain air filters. This reduces to a tautology. The assertion should instead specify which types of air terminals typically or always include integral filtration (e.g., some VAV terminal units with integral filter sections, or certain critical environment diffusers), or should clarify the containment relationship as optional rather than asserting it as a general rule.
conditions: if terminal includes integral filtration
exceptions: central filtration only

subject: IfcAirTerminal
rationale: Ceiling-mounted air terminals compete with lighting fixtures for ceiling grid space.
conditions: when locations overlap in ceiling grid
exceptions: integrated lighting/air distribution systems

subject: IfcAirTerminalBox
rationale: The box is connected in-line within the ductwork system.
conditions: upstream and downstream connections
exceptions: An IfcAirTerminalBox may also connect directly to an IfcAirTerminal (e.g., diffuser, grille) without intervening ductwork, particularly in VAV box with integral diffuser configurations. In such cases the box does not connect to ductwork on the downstream side.

An IfcAirTerminalBox may connect to ductwork that is not explicitly modeled as IfcDuctSegment (e.g., flexible duct classified under different Ifc classifications or connection via an IfcFlowFitting directly). In models where flexible duct is omitted or simplified, the 'connects_to Ductwork' relationship may not be present.

subject: IfcAirTerminalBoxType
rationale: Air terminal boxes connect to supply ductwork (inlet) and downstream ductwork or directly to diffusers.
applicability: All building types with ducted HVAC
conditions: Upstream and downstream connections
exceptions: IfcAirTerminalBoxType does not always require ductwork in all contexts. In some VAV systems with fan-powered terminal boxes, the terminal box may include an internal fan that draws from a plenum rather than requiring direct upstream ductwork. Additionally, some terminal boxes can be connected directly to a fan coil unit without intermediate duct runs.

subject: IfcAirTerminalBoxType
rationale: The terminal box control system connects to a zone thermostat or space temperature sensor.
conditions: For zone temperature feedback

subject: IfcAirTerminalType
rationale: Air terminals are typically connected to duct segments to convey air to/from the space.
conditions: when part of a ducted air system

subject: IfcAirTerminalType
rationale: An air terminal's function is to supply/return air to a conditioned space; without a space there is no purpose.
conditions: mounted in or serving a conditioned room

subject: IfcAirTerminalType
rationale: The terminal depends on being placed in an opening (e.g., ceiling, wall) via a relationship to the building element.
conditions: when installed in an opening or ceiling grid

subject: IfcAirTerminalType
rationale: Fittings may be needed to connect the terminal to the ductwork.
conditions: when used with transitions, tees, or diffuser connections

subject: IfcAirTerminalType
rationale: Air terminals serve a zone by delivering conditioned air to maintain thermal comfort.
conditions: as part of HVAC zoning

subject: IfcAirTerminalType
rationale: Some air terminals integrate or require dampers for airflow regulation.
conditions: when volume control or balancing is needed

subject: IfcAirToAirHeatRecoveryType
rationale: Filters are essential before the heat exchanger to maintain efficiency and prevent fouling.
conditions: To protect heat exchanger surfaces from dust and debris
exceptions: Many enthalpy wheels and plate heat exchangers in the Air-to-Air Heat Recovery category rely on the pressure drop across the heat exchanger itself to self-clean or have coatings that resist fouling, and do not require a separate Air Filter upstream. Additionally, ERV (Energy Recovery Ventilator) cassettes integrated into AHUs often omit dedicated Air Filter elements immediately preceding the heat recovery core when the AHU already provides MERV filtration elsewhere.

subject: IfcAirToAirHeatRecoveryType
rationale: The unit connects upstream of an AHU or as an integral part of a packaged AHU.
applicability: The condition 'when used as a separate module upstream of an AHU' covers only one deployment scenario. The assertion should also cover cases where the heat recovery device is integrated into the AHU casing itself (factory-installed) — in that scenario the entity is still connected to the AHU but is not a 'separate module upstream.'
conditions: When used as a separate module upstream of an AHU
exceptions: An IfcAirToAirHeatRecoveryType can also be integrated inside a DOAS (Dedicated Outdoor Air System), a packaged rooftop unit, or a heat recovery ventilator (HRV/ERV) that is itself a standalone unit — not merely 'upstream of an AHU.' In such cases, the connection is to the DOAS unit or the HRV cabinet, not to an AHU.

subject: IfcAlarmType
rationale: Wired alarm systems need cable trays, conduits, or raceways to route signal and power cables.
applicability: all building types with wired systems
conditions: for wired connection of detectors and panels
exceptions: wireless alarm systems may not require cable carriers

subject: IfcAlarmType
rationale: Electrical cables carry power and signals between alarm devices and the control panel.
applicability: all building types with wired systems
conditions: for wired communication between alarm components
exceptions: wireless systems use radio frequency instead

subject: IfcAlarmType
rationale: Many alarm types (e.g., smoke alarms) contain or are intrinsically linked to sensors that detect hazards.
applicability: Modern multi-sensor alarms can integrate multiple sensor types (e.g., combined smoke/heat/CO), but the assertion frames this as IfcAlarmType containing IfcSensor entities, whereas the correct IFC modeling approach is to assign detection functions via property sets (Pset_AlarmTypeSmoke, Pset_AlarmTypeHeat, etc.) or through IfcRelDefinesByProperties.
conditions: alarm types may integrate sensors like smoke, heat, gas, motion detectors
exceptions: some alarm types are simple push-button manual stations without sensors

subject: IfcAlarmType
rationale: An IfcAlarmType represents a type of alarm device; it contains sounders, strobes, or buzzers.
conditions: as notification devices (audible/visual)
exceptions: some alarm types only trigger external notification

subject: IfcAlarmType
rationale: Alarm types typically connect to control panels (e.g., fire alarm control units) that manage detection and notification.
conditions: for control and indication at fire alarm control panels or security panels
exceptions: standalone alarms may not connect to control elements

subject: IfcAnnotation
rationale: IfcAnnotation is often used to associate annotation geometry or text with building elements; it depends on those elements for context.
conditions: when IfcAnnotation is used to tag or label building elements

subject: IfcAnnotation
rationale: IfcAnnotation can contain fill area occurrences for graphical annotation purposes.
conditions: when representing filled regions or hatching

subject: IfcAnnotation
rationale: IfcAnnotations commonly contain IfcCurve subtypes for annotation lines.
applicability: IfcAnnotation contains IfcCurve only through specific representation maps (IfcShapeRepresentation), not directly as a containment relationship in the IFC object graph. The assertion conflates geometric representation with object containment.
conditions: when annotation includes 2D curves like dimensions, leader lines, or section marks

subject: IfcAnnotation
rationale: IfcAnnotation can contain text literals for textual annotations.
applicability: IfcTextLiteral is contained in IfcAnnotation only via IfcShapeRepresentation items, not as a direct containment relationship in the IFC object model.
conditions: when annotation includes text labels or notes

subject: IfcAnnotation
rationale: Annotations may support grid visualization by marking axis labels.
conditions: when used to annotate grid lines or design grids

subject: IfcAnnotation
rationale: IfcAnnotation typically depends on layer assignments to control graphical presentation.
conditions: when annotations are organized in layers for visibility and styling

subject: IfcAnnotation
rationale: Annotations improve the clarity and documentation of building elements by adding dimensions, notes, or symbols.
applicability: The term 'improves' is ambiguous in IFC semantics. IfcAnnotation does not functionally 'improve' IfcBuildingElement; it provides annotation data about it. This is a semantic modeling concern, not a formal IFC relationship.
conditions: when annotations provide additional documentation, labeling, or clarification

subject: IfcAnnotationFillArea
rationale: IfcAnnotationFillArea is a subtype of IfcAnnotation which defines a 2D fill area within annotation elements. It contains the geometric representation of a filled region used in annotations.
conditions: When used as a fill area within annotation elements

subject: IfcAnnotationFillArea
rationale: IfcAnnotationFillArea requires one or more IfcCurve entities (via IfcPolyline, IfcCompositeCurve, etc.) to define the closed outer boundary of the fill region.
conditions: When defining the outer boundary of the fill area

subject: IfcAnnotationFillArea
rationale: IfcAnnotationFillArea can contain or be styled by IfcFillAreaStyleHatching as part of its presentation style.
conditions: When a hatched fill pattern is assigned

subject: IfcAnnotationFillArea
rationale: IfcAnnotationFillArea can contain or be styled by IfcFillAreaStyleTiles as part of its presentation style.
conditions: When a tiled fill pattern is assigned

subject: IfcAnnotationFillArea
rationale: IfcAnnotationFillArea typically depends on being assigned to an IfcRepresentation (e.g., IfcShapeRepresentation) that places it within a geometric model context.
conditions: When the fill area is part of a product representation

subject: IfcAnnotationFillArea
rationale: As a subtype of IfcAnnotation, IfcAnnotationFillArea depends on being associated with a parent IfcAnnotation entity to provide context and placement in a drawing or model view.
conditions: As the parent annotation element containing the fill area

subject: IfcAnnotationFillArea
rationale: IfcAnnotationFillArea requires a geometric representation context (typically 'Plan' view) to define the coordinate system and scaling for the fill region.
conditions: When placed in a 2D geometric representation context

subject: IfcApplication
rationale: IfcApplication is always associated with an IfcProject to identify the originating software application that created the project data.
conditions: when used as part of an IFC data exchange

subject: IfcApplication
rationale: IfcApplication is referenced by IfcOwnerHistory to record which application created or modified entity instances.
conditions: when tracking data provenance and modifications

subject: IfcApplication
rationale: IfcApplication provides the 'OwningApplication' reference within IfcOwnerHistory, supporting data provenance tracking.
conditions: when recording the last modification session

subject: IfcApplication
rationale: IfcApplication instances are typically associated with a project to indicate the originating application.
conditions: to be meaningful in an IFC data exchange context

subject: IfcAppliedValue
rationale: IfcAppliedValue often references IfcCostValue for monetary cost representation in IFC schema.
conditions: when the applied value represents a cost

subject: IfcAppliedValue
rationale: IfcAppliedValue can have an AppliedValue attribute that is an IfcMeasureWithUnit for quantitative values.
conditions: when the applied value includes a measured quantity

subject: IfcAppliedValue
rationale: IfcAppliedValue can be assigned to construction resources like labor, material, or equipment.
applicability: IfcAppliedValue also supports other IFC entities beyond IfcConstructionResource, such as IfcProduct (via IfcRelDefinesByProperties) and IfcCostSchedule, meaning this relationship is not exclusive to construction resources but also applies more broadly in cost estimation contexts.
conditions: when used to assign unit costs or base costs to resources

subject: IfcAppliedValue
rationale: IfcAppliedValue can be composed of sub-values through IfcAppliedValueRelationship forming a containment hierarchy.
conditions: when the applied value aggregates multiple cost values under a single unit cost
exceptions: IfcAppliedValue.Components is a list of IfcAppliedValue, not specifically IfcCostValue. While IfcCostValue is a subtype of IfcAppliedValue, the relationship is via inheritance, meaning the assertion should say 'IfcAppliedValue contains IfcAppliedValue (including IfcCostValue)' to be precise.

subject: IfcAppliedValue
rationale: IfcAppliedValue relates to IFC objects (products, processes, resources) through property assignment relationships.
conditions: when the applied value is assigned to an object via IfcRelDefinesByProperties or similar

subject: IfcApproval
rationale: IfcApproval requires an IfcPerson (or IfcOrganization) as the actor who gives or authorizes the approval.
conditions: When approval is given by a person

subject: IfcApproval
rationale: IfcApproval requires an IfcOrganization as the actor who gives or authorizes the approval.
conditions: When approval is given by an organization

subject: IfcApproval
rationale: IfcApproval supports the approval association relationship that links it to other IFC objects (products, processes, controls, resources, etc.) that are being approved.
conditions: For any object that has an approval associated with it

subject: IfcApproval
rationale: IfcApproval connects to building products (IfcProduct subtypes like IfcWall, IfcSlab, etc.) that are being approved through the IfcRelAssociatesApproval relationship.
conditions: When a building element/product is approved

subject: IfcApproval
rationale: IfcApproval can connect to processes (e.g., IfcTask, IfcProcedure) to approve specific construction or design activities.
conditions: When a construction or design process is approved

subject: IfcApproval
rationale: IfcApproval can connect to documents (drawings, specifications, reports) that require formal approval.
conditions: When a document is approved

subject: IfcApproval
rationale: IfcApproval can connect to cost items for budget or cost approval processes.
conditions: When a cost item or budget is approved

subject: IfcApproval
rationale: IfcApproval can connect to property sets that describe approved properties or performance values.
conditions: When property sets carry approval status

subject: IfcApproval
rationale: IfcApproval can depend on other approvals through the IfcApprovalRelationship for multi-level approval workflows.
conditions: When approvals are hierarchically related (sub-approvals, superseding approvals)

subject: IfcApproval
rationale: IfcApproval supports work plans by providing the approval status that allows work to proceed.
conditions: When a work plan requires approval before execution

subject: IfcApproval
rationale: IfcApproval can support permit issuance by serving as evidence that design or construction aspects have been approved.
conditions: When a permit is granted based on approvals

subject: IfcApprovalRelationship
rationale: IfcApprovalRelationship is a relationship entity that links approval objects (IfcApproval) to other objects; without an IfcApproval instance, the relationship has no meaning.
conditions: IfcApprovalRelationship must reference at least one IfcApproval

subject: IfcApprovalRelationship
rationale: The relationship connects an approval to other IFC objects (products, processes, controls, etc.), which are all subtypes of IfcRoot.
conditions: IfcApprovalRelationship relates one IfcApproval to one or more IfcRoot entities

subject: IfcApprovalRelationship
rationale: The relationship contains references (via relatedObjects) to the approvals being applied.
conditions: IfcApprovalRelationship associates approvals with objects

subject: IfcApprovalRelationship
rationale: As a subtype of IfcRoot, IfcApprovalRelationship depends on IfcOwnerHistory for tracking authorship and change history.
conditions: IfcApprovalRelationship inherits from IfcRoot and thus has an OwnerHistory attribute

subject: IfcArbitraryOpenProfileDef
rationale: IfcArbitraryOpenProfileDef is a subtype of IfcProfileDef; it depends on the base entity for its fundamental profile definition properties.
conditions: When defining the base profile type

subject: IfcArbitraryOpenProfileDef

subject: IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef

subject: IfcAsset

subject: IfcAsset

However, IfcRelAssignsToControl typically relates a control (e.g., a work schedule) to controlled objects. The condition 'controlled or managed by a process, procedure, or actor' is too broad — only IfcProcess, IfcProcedure, or IfcActor subtypes that are also IfcControl are valid related objects. This should be scoped more precisely.

subject: IfcAsset
rationale: Every IFC entity, including IfcAsset, requires ownership and creation history for traceability.

subject: IfcAsset
rationale: IfcAsset typically has asset-specific properties (e.g., depreciation, warranty, replacement cost) linked through property set definitions.

subject: IfcAsset
rationale: Property sets carry asset-specific data such as purchase date, serial number, maintenance schedule.

subject: IfcAsset
rationale: An IfcAsset can contain or represent physical building elements that are being managed as assets.

The relationship between IfcAsset and IfcElement is through IfcRelAssignsToActor (when an actor assigns elements as assets) or IfcRelAssignsToGroup, not a containment relationship.

subject: IfcAsset

subject: IfcAsset

The relationship typically goes through IfcRelAssignsToActor, where IfcActor is the RelatingActor and IfcAsset is a RelatedObject. The assertion should specify that the dependency is via IfcRelAssignsToActor rather than a direct dependency on IfcActor.
conditions: when an actor (person or organization) is responsible for the asset's management

subject: IfcAxis1Placement

rationale: 2D circles use IfcAxis2Placement2D as their placement reference.

subject: IfcAxis2Placement3D

The dependency is conceptual rather than a direct IFC relationship path dependency.
conditions: When defining the origin of the coordinate system

subject: IfcAxis2Placement3D

applicability: The assertion states IfcAxis2Placement3D depends_on IfcDirection, but both Axis and RefDirection are optional attributes per the IFC schema (Axis defaults to (0,0,1) if not provided, RefDirection is always optional). When both directions are omitted, there is no dependency on IfcDirection at all.
conditions: When defining the Z axis direction (Axis) and optionally the X axis direction (RefDirection)

conditions: When used within a 3D geometric representation context

subject: IfcAxis2Placement3D

applicability: IfcProduct does not directly reference IfcAxis2Placement3D. IfcProduct has ObjectPlacement of type IfcObjectPlacement, and only when that is specifically IfcLocalPlacement (rather than IfcGridPlacement) which in turn references IfcAxis2Placement3D as RelativePlacement does a transitive dependency exist. The chain is long and depends on the specific placement type used.
conditions: When IfcProduct uses an IfcLocalPlacement that references IfcAxis2Placement3D

subject: IfcAxis2Placement3D
rationale: 3D shape representations require a placement axis system to define the orientation of geometry in 3D space.
applicability: IfcShapeRepresentation does not directly use IfcAxis2Placement3D. The representation uses IfcRepresentationItem subclasses (e.g., IfcExtrudedAreaSolid) which contain placement attributes. The placement within IfcShapeRepresentation items is independent of the representation context placement. Only some geometric items within the representation use IfcAxis2Placement3D, not the representation itself.
conditions: When shape representations use 3D coordinate systems defined by IfcAxis2Placement3D

subject: IfcAxis2Placement3D
rationale: IfcMappedItem uses placement transformations that can be based on IfcAxis2Placement3D for 3D mapping.
applicability: IfcMappedItem references an IfcRepresentationMap which contains a mapping origin of type IfcAxis2Placement (abstract). This can be IfcAxis2Placement3D or IfcAxis2Placement2D. The assertion holds only when the mapping source is in 3D, not in 2D contexts.
conditions: When mapping source geometry into a coordinate system defined by IfcAxis2Placement3D

subject: IfcAxis2Placement3D
rationale: IfcAxis2Placement3D contains a reference to an IfcCartesianPoint as its Location defining the origin.
conditions: As the Location attribute

subject: IfcAxis2Placement3D
rationale: IfcAxis2Placement3D contains references to IfcDirection entities for its axis definitions.
conditions: As the Axis attribute (Z axis) and/or RefDirection attribute (X axis)
exceptions: RefDirection is optional

The assertion states IfcAxis2Placement3D 'contains' IfcDirection as Axis and RefDirection, but both attributes are optional. IfcAxis2Placement3D can exist with only Location set and no IfcDirection instances referenced at all — in which case Axis defaults to (0,0,1) logically but no IfcDirection entity is instantiated or contained.

subject: IfcBeam
rationale: Beams typically transfer loads to columns in framed structures.
conditions: when beam is supported by columns
exceptions: A beam may depend on a column indirectly via a corbel or bracket connection, not directly on the column itself. Additionally, in moment-resisting frames, beams frame into columns but the relationship is closer to 'connected_to' rather than a load-bearing 'depends_on' dependency in the pure sense, as the connection can be rigid and mutual.

subject: IfcBeam
rationale: Beams may be supported by walls in certain structural systems.
conditions: when beam rests on load-bearing walls
exceptions: when beam is supported by columns only
In cavity wall construction or where beams are supported by lintels or steel shelves within the wall assembly, the beam may depend on a lintel or shelf angle rather than directly on the wall itself.

subject: IfcBeam
rationale: Beams provide support for floor and roof slabs, transferring loads to vertical elements.
conditions: beam acts as primary horizontal support member
exceptions: In composite decking systems, the slab may be supported by profiled metal decking that spans between beams, meaning the slab does not directly depend on the beam as a primary support member; the deck acts as an intermediate element.

subject: IfcBeam
rationale: Beams may support finishes like gypsum board encasement or spray-applied fireproofing.
conditions: when beam is finished or fire-protected

subject: IfcBeam
rationale: Concrete beams require steel reinforcement to resist tensile stresses.
conditions: concrete beam
exceptions: steel beams do not require reinforcement

subject: IfcBeam
rationale: Every beam must have a material and cross-section profile defining its mechanical properties.
conditions: always

subject: IfcBeam
rationale: Beams may support non-structural building elements like cladding attachments, though this is less direct than supporting slabs.
conditions: when curtain wall or cladding system is attached
exceptions: when facade is self-supporting

subject: IfcBeam
rationale: Prestressed beams contain tendons (strands/cables) under tension.
conditions: prestressed or post-tensioned concrete beam
exceptions: non-prestressed beams

subject: IfcBeam
rationale: Reinforced concrete beams contain rebar cages within the concrete section.
conditions: reinforced concrete beam
exceptions: steel beams
timber beams

In fiber-reinforced concrete beams (e.g., steel fiber or glass fiber reinforced), there may be no discrete reinforcing bars present. The beam contains fibers distributed throughout the matrix rather than traditional rebar. This should be noted as an exception.

subject: IfcBeam
rationale: Beams can indirectly protect spaces by maintaining structural integrity during fire, but 'protects' is an indirect relationship.
conditions: beam is part of structural fire protection system
exceptions: beams not designed for fire protection

subject: IfcBeam
rationale: Beams depend on structural connections (e.g., moment connections, shear connections) to properly transfer loads.
conditions: for load transfer at joints
exceptions: In some structural systems, such as pinned-base frames or structures with continuous beams, the beam may transfer load directly to the foundation or to another beam without going through a discrete IfcStructuralConnection element. Also, in timber or steel structures, connections may be modeled as simple fasteners or as part of the element itself rather than as IfcStructuralConnection.

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Beam types require columns or other vertical supports to transfer loads to foundation.
conditions: when beam is supported by columns
exceptions: IfcBeamType does not always require IfcColumn; beams can be supported by walls, other beams, or cantilevered from cores. The condition 'when beam is supported by columns' actually describes the scenario where the assertion holds, making the assertion circular—it says IfcBeamType requires IfcColumn when the beam is supported by columns, which is tautological.

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Beams often require slabs to distribute loads.
conditions: when beam supports floor slabs
exceptions: IfcBeamType does not require IfcSlab even when supporting floor slabs—a beam can exist and be modeled as supporting a slab without the slab being required in the model. The beam type definition is independent of whether a specific slab instance exists.

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Beam types require a material definition to have physical properties.
conditions: concrete
steel
timber
exceptions: IfcBeamType does not strictly require IfcMaterial; beams can have material assignments or be abstract/analytical elements without material definition. Even concrete, steel, and timber beams can reference material via IfcMaterialConstituentSet rather than a single IfcMaterial.

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Beam types require property sets for structural and dimensional definitions.

exceptions: IfcBeamType does not require IfcPropertySet for structural analysis—structural analysis properties can be assigned via IfcStructuralActivity or other means without a dedicated IfcPropertySet on the beam type. Additionally, structural analysis properties are often specified via IfcRelDefinesByProperties on occurrences, not on the type itself.

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Structural behavior of beam type depends on analysis model.
conditions: when used in load-bearing context

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Beam types depend on connection definitions to other structural members.
conditions: when connected to other structural elements

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Beam types support floor and roof slabs.
conditions: load-bearing slabs

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Beams can support wall loads above openings.
conditions: when beams act as lintels over openings

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Beam types support roof structures.
conditions: when used as roof beams or rafters

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Beams may support coverings or cladding.
conditions: when beam is part of exposed structure

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Fire-rated beams can protect spaces from fire spread between compartments.
conditions: when beam is part of fire-rated construction

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Prestressed beam types contain tendons.
conditions: for prestressed concrete beams
exceptions: IfcBeamType does not contain IfcTendon in the IFC schema—IfcTendon is an element that may be associated with an IfcBeam (occurrence) via IfcRelConnectsElements or IfcRelNests, but it is not contained within IfcBeamType. Also, tendons can be in post-tensioned beams, not only prestressed.

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Beam types connect to columns at joints.
conditions: at beam-column joints

subject: IfcBeamType

conditions: when steel beams have connection plates

subject: IfcBeamType

subject: IfcBeamType
rationale: Openings through beams conflict with structural capacity.
applicability: The 'conflicts_with' relationship between IfcBeamType and IfcOpeningElement is misleading—IfcOpeningElement can be applied to a beam (e.g., as an opening in a beam web) but this is a valid design pattern, not a conflict. The beam and opening coexist in proper designs with reinforcement or detailing around openings. The assertion inaccurately treats a design consideration as a conflict.

subject: IfcBeamType

A deep beam can still be suitable for a space if the clearance reduction is acceptable per design requirements, or if the space is non-occupiable (e.g., ceiling plenum, attic). The assertion should note that it applies only when minimum clearance requirements are violated.

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: A standard case beam typically transfers loads to columns at its ends in framed structures.
conditions: when used as a horizontal structural element spanning between vertical supports
exceptions: cantilevered beams or beams supported on walls

The existing exceptions already list 'cantilevered beams or beams supported on walls' but the assertion's own conditions say 'when used as a horizontal structural element spanning between vertical supports' — a cantilevered beam also spans (projects) from a vertical support, so there is ambiguity. Additionally, beams supported on one side by a column and on the other by a wall would be partially covered by both the condition and the exception, creating a conflicting classification.

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: Beams require proper structural connections (supports) to transfer loads safely.
conditions: at beam ends for load transfer
exceptions: simply supported beams on walls

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: A beam must have a material definition (e.g., steel grade, concrete class, timber grade) to have structural properties.
conditions: assigned via material profile or material layer set usage

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: Load-bearing beams require definition of applied loads (dead, live, wind, etc.) for structural design.
conditions: for structural analysis and design verification
exceptions: pure architectural beams not participating in structural analysis

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: IfcBeamStandardCase requires a profile definition (I-section, rectangular, etc.) to represent the beam's shape.
conditions: to define cross-section geometry

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: Beams in framed structures often support slabs which span between beams.
conditions: when beams act as primary framing supporting floor slabs
exceptions: flat slab systems without beams

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: Beams can support walls above openings (lintel function) or serve as edge beams for cladding.
conditions: when beams act as lintels or spandrel beams above openings or at floor edges
exceptions: non-load-bearing walls that bypass the beam

The assertion 'supports IfcWall' with condition 'when beams act as lintels or spandrel beams above openings or at floor edges' is not comprehensive. There are also cases where beams act as ring beams or bond beams at the top of masonry walls (not just above openings), or as edge beams supporting precast wall panels. The existing exception only covers non-load-bearing walls that bypass the beam, but misses these other support configurations.

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: Beams may support applied coverings for fire protection, insulation, or aesthetic purposes.
applicability: all beams requiring fire rating or finish
conditions: when beams receive fireproofing, cladding, or architectural finishes
exceptions: exposed architectural beams not requiring covering

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: Beams connect to columns in structural frames, forming the primary load-resisting system.
conditions: at beam-column joints in rigid or semi-rigid frames

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: Beams may connect to other beams (e.g., secondary beams connected to primary beams).
conditions: when beams frame into each other at intersections or when beams are continuous

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: Reinforced concrete beams contain reinforcing bars as embedded components for tensile strength.
conditions: when the beam is made of reinforced concrete
exceptions: steel beams
timber beams
prestressed concrete with tendons only

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: Prestressed beams contain tendons (strands or bars) to apply compressive pre-stress.
conditions: when the beam is prestressed or post-tensioned
exceptions: non-prestressed beams

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: Fireproofing materials applied to beams protect the structural element from fire damage.
conditions: when beams are fire-protected by encasement or spray-applied materials modeled as proxies

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: The relationship object is needed to formally associate material properties with the beam instance.
conditions: to link the beam to its material definition

subject: IfcBeamStandardCase
rationale: Including beams improves the accuracy of structural analysis models by capturing the framing behavior.
conditions: when the beam is included in the structural analysis model
exceptions: non-structural beams

subject: IfcBlobTexture
rationale: IfcBlobTexture is a subtype of IfcImageTexture which represents texture images provided as a binary blob; it depends on the base texture concept for rasterization and mapping.
conditions: When used as a texture map for surfaces

subject: IfcBlobTexture
rationale: IfcBlobTexture inherits from IfcSurfaceTexture, which defines texture coordinates and mapping, so the blob texture depends on the surface texture supertype for proper rendering.
applicability: Any IFC model using surface textures
conditions: When assigned to a geometric surface

subject: IfcBlobTexture
rationale: Texture coordinates are required to map the blob texture onto a geometric surface correctly.
applicability: Any IFC model using mapped textures
conditions: When the texture is applied to a geometry surface

subject: IfcBlobTexture
rationale: IfcBlobTexture can be referenced by IfcSurfaceStyleRendering to define surface texture mapping and visual appearance.
conditions: When the blob texture is used for rendering a surface's appearance

subject: IfcBlobTexture

conditions: When the blob texture is part of a styled item for a building element

subject: IfcBlock
rationale: IfcBlock requires an IfcCartesianPoint to define its position in 3D space through the Position attribute.
conditions: for position placement

subject: IfcBlock
rationale: IfcBlock is typically used as part of an IfcRepresentation (e.g., IfcShapeRepresentation) to represent a product's geometry.
applicability: IfcBlock is a subtype of IfcCsgPrimitive3D which is a subtype of IfcGeometricRepresentationItem. The dependency on IfcRepresentation is not a direct schema-level dependency but rather a usage-level relationship—IfcBlock is used within an IfcRepresentation via IfcRepresentationItem. The assertion is acceptable as a semantic dependency but is a conceptual rather than a direct schema dependency.
conditions: when used as a geometric representation item

subject: IfcBlock
rationale: IfcBlock is typically assigned to an IfcProduct (e.g., IfcBuildingElement) via a representation relationship to describe its shape.
conditions: when used as representation of a building element

subject: IfcBlock
rationale: IfcBlock's Position attribute connects to an IfcLocalPlacement (via IfcAxis2Placement3D) to locate the block in space.
conditions: when placed within a coordinate system

subject: IfcBoilerType
rationale: IfcBoilerType is a subtype of IfcEnergyConversionDevice and requires conversion of fuel to heat energy.
applicability: All building types with hydronic heating systems
conditions: When boiler is used for heating purposes

subject: IfcBoilerType
rationale: A boiler typically requires a burner to combust fuel (gas, oil, etc.) to generate heat.
conditions: For combustion-type boilers
exceptions: Electric boilers do not require burners

The existing exception lists electric boilers, but also oil-fired boilers that use vaporizing burners (non-mechanical) or dual-fuel boilers with integrated burner assemblies may not have a distinct IfcBurner as a separate modeled element. Additionally, some solid fuel boilers (wood/pellet) use combustion but may not have a separate 'burner' entity modeled in IFC.

subject: IfcBoilerType
rationale: Piping is required to circulate heated water or steam from the boiler to distribution points.
conditions: For water/steam distribution

subject: IfcBoilerType
rationale: Circulation pumps are needed to move heated water through the piping network.
conditions: For forced circulation hydronic systems
exceptions: Gravity-fed systems may not require a circulation pump

subject: IfcBoilerType
rationale: Combustion boilers require flue gas exhaust systems to safely vent combustion products.
conditions: For combustion boilers burning fossil fuels
exceptions: Electric boilers and condensing boilers with side-venting

The existing exceptions list electric and condensing boilers with side-venting, but also missing: outdoor boilers (e.g., rooftop or exterior packaged boilers with integral flue), boilers venting through existing chimney liners where IfcChimney is not modeled separately, and condensing boilers using plastic venting systems (PVC/CPVC) that are not modeled as IfcChimney but rather as IfcPipeSegment.

subject: IfcBoilerType
rationale: A boiler contains a heat exchanger to transfer heat from combustion/electric elements to water.
conditions: For internal heat exchange

subject: IfcBoilerType
rationale: The boiler connects to the piping system via fittings, flanges, and connections.
applicability: IfcBoilerType (a type definition) does not directly 'connect_to' IfcPipeFitting in IFC — it is the boiler occurrence (IfcBoiler) that connects via IfcRelConnectsPorts or similar relationships. Type-level connection relationships are not standard in IFC. If this refers to occurrence-level connections, the assertion should reference IfcBoiler, not IfcBoilerType.
conditions: For system connections

subject: IfcBoilerType
rationale: As a flow element, the boiler connects to the overall distribution network.

subject: IfcBoiler
rationale: Pumps circulate heated water from the boiler through the distribution system and back.
conditions: Required for forced hot water systems
exceptions: Steam systems and gravity-circulation systems may not require pumps

Condensing boilers with built-in primary/secondary pump configurations may have an internal pump that is part of the boiler assembly, not a separate circulation pump in the system sense. This could be an edge case where the dependency on an external circulation pump does not hold.

subject: IfcBoiler
rationale: Water expands when heated; without an expansion tank, pressure can damage the system.
conditions: Needed in closed-loop hydronic systems to accommodate thermal expansion of water
exceptions: Open-loop systems may not require expansion tanks

subject: IfcBoiler
rationale: The heat exchanger transfers thermal energy from combustion gases or electric elements to the water.
conditions: Integral component inside boiler

subject: IfcBoiler
rationale: Boilers in larger buildings are often connected to a BMS for monitoring and optimization.
conditions: When integrated with automated building controls
exceptions: Simple residential systems may not connect to BMS

subject: IfcBooleanResult

subject: IfcBooleanResult

subject: IfcBooleanResult

subject: IfcBooleanResult
rationale: IfcBooleanResult is often used to create openings, cuts, or complex shapes in building elements.

subject: IfcBooleanResult

conditions: when representing subtracted Boolean results for openings

subject: IfcBooleanClippingResult

conditions: When clipping is performed using a half-space solid

subject: IfcBooleanClippingResult
rationale: IfcBooleanClippingResult can be used as a child in CSG tree structures, supporting the creation of complex solid geometry through sequential boolean operations.

subject: IfcBooleanClippingResult
rationale: IfcBooleanClippingResult is commonly used within IfcShapeRepresentation to define the 3D shape of building elements through clipping operations.
conditions: When used in geometric representation contexts

subject: IfcBooleanClippingResult
rationale: IfcBooleanClippingResult is a subtype of IfcBooleanResult which is a subtype of IfcGeometricRepresentationItem, inheriting placement and representation context dependencies.
conditions: As a subtype, it inherits from this base class

subject: IfcBooleanClippingResult
rationale: IfcBooleanClippingResult is often used to model openings and clipping of building elements (e.g., windows in walls, doors in slabs) by subtracting volumes from solid elements.
applicability: Doors, windows, walls, slabs with openings
conditions: When used to define element geometry through clipping

subject: IfcBooleanClippingResult
rationale: The boolean operation result itself doesn't directly require placement, but the operands or the containing representation may require local placement for proper positioning in the building model.
conditions: When the result needs to be positioned in world coordinates
exceptions: Placement may be inherited from parent representation

subject: IfcBooleanClippingResult
rationale: IfcBooleanClippingResult can be used to define the void geometry for IfcOpeningElement by clipping the opening shape from the host element.
conditions: When modeling openings in walls, slabs, or roofs

subject: IfcBoundaryCondition
rationale: IfcBoundaryCondition typically references structural loads to define the conditions at supports or boundaries of a structural model.
conditions: when defining boundary conditions for structural analysis

subject: IfcBoundaryCondition
rationale: Boundary conditions are commonly applied to structural connection elements to constrain their degrees of freedom.
conditions: when assigned to a structural connection or support

subject: IfcBoundaryCondition
rationale: Boundary conditions are applied to structural members to represent supports, fixed ends, or released connections.
conditions: when the boundary condition defines the support of a beam, column, or other member

subject: IfcBoundaryCondition
rationale: Boundary conditions are essential inputs to structural analysis models to define how the structure interacts with its environment.
applicability: all building types requiring structural analysis
conditions: as part of the boundary condition definitions in a structural analysis model

subject: IfcBoundaryCondition
rationale: The assignment of boundary conditions to structural members often occurs through connection relationships in the IFC model.
conditions: when the boundary condition is associated via a connection relationship

subject: IfcBoundaryCondition
rationale: IfcBoundaryCondition is an abstract supertype; IfcBoundaryEdgeCondition is a concrete subtype that actually provides translational and rotational stiffness values.
conditions: when detailed edge-based boundary conditions are modeled

subject: IfcBoundaryCondition
rationale: IfcBoundaryCondition is abstract; IfcBoundaryNodeCondition is one of its concrete subtypes used for node-level conditions.
conditions: when nodal boundary conditions with stiffness values are needed

subject: IfcBoundaryCondition
rationale: IfcBoundaryCondition is abstract; IfcBoundaryFaceCondition is a subtype used for face-based conditions.
conditions: when boundary conditions are applied to faces or surfaces

subject: IfcBoundaryCurve
rationale: IfcBoundaryCurve is a subtype of IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface and is typically defined using polylines to create closed boundary loops for profile definitions in IFC.
conditions: when defining the outer boundary of a parametric profile

subject: IfcBoundaryCurve
rationale: IfcBoundaryCurve is a subtype of IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface, meaning it inherently requires the properties and structure of the parent type.

subject: IfcBoundaryCurve
rationale: Boundary curves often need trimmed curves to define precise start/end points of the boundary segments.
conditions: when curves need to be bounded to form a closed loop

subject: IfcBoundaryCurve
rationale: As a subtype of IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface, the boundary curve is defined on a reference surface.
conditions: when the boundary curve lies on a surface (p-curve context)

subject: IfcBoundaryCurve
rationale: IfcBoundaryCurve defines the outer boundary of profile definitions, enabling the creation of cross-sections for structural and architectural elements.
conditions: when defining the boundary of a parametric profile

subject: IfcBoundaryCurve
rationale: IfcBoundaryCurve directly supports IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef by providing its outer boundary geometry.
conditions: when the profile is defined by an arbitrary closed curve

subject: IfcBoundaryCurve

conditions: when the profile has voids and the boundary curve defines the outer perimeter

subject: IfcBoundaryCurve
rationale: Boundary curves contribute to shape representations by defining boundaries of profiles used in extruded or swept solid geometry.
conditions: when representing the geometric shape of a building element

subject: IfcBoundaryCurve
rationale: The boundary curve defines the profile that is extruded to create 3D solid geometry.
conditions: when the profile defined by the boundary curve is extruded

subject: IfcBoundaryCurve
rationale: The boundary curve defines the profile that is revolved to create 3D solid geometry.
conditions: when the profile defined by the boundary curve is revolved

subject: IfcBoundaryCurve
rationale: IfcBoundaryCurve is a subtype of IfcBoundedCurve, inheriting its bounded nature.

subject: IfcBoundaryEdgeCondition
rationale: IfcBoundaryEdgeCondition is a subtype of IfcBoundaryCondition, specializing in edge-related boundary conditions; it inherits core boundary condition properties from its parent class.
conditions: When defining edge boundary conditions for structural analysis models

subject: IfcBoundaryEdgeCondition
rationale: Boundary edge conditions are typically assigned to structural connections to define how edges of structural elements are restrained.
conditions: When applied in structural analysis contexts

subject: IfcBoundaryEdgeCondition
rationale: The relationship entity IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity is used to assign boundary conditions (as structural activities) to structural members or connections.
conditions: When linking boundary conditions to structural members or connections

subject: IfcBoundaryEdgeCondition
rationale: Edge boundary conditions are typically applied to curve-type structural members (beams, columns) at their ends or along edges.

subject: IfcBoundaryEdgeCondition
rationale: Edge boundary conditions can be applied along the edges of surface structural members such as slabs and walls.

subject: IfcBoundaryFaceCondition

subject: IfcBoundaryFaceCondition

subject: IfcBoundaryFaceCondition
rationale: IfcBoundaryFaceCondition is a subtype of IfcBoundaryCondition, so it inherits all properties of its parent class.

Boundary conditions are typically assigned through IfcRelConnectsPathElements or via the Condition attribute on IfcRelSpaceBoundary. IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements is used for connections where a 'realizing element' (e.g., a fastener, adhesive) mediates the connection, which is a very narrow case.

subject: IfcBoundaryFaceCondition

conditions: when visual or surface properties influence the boundary condition

subject: IfcBoundaryFaceCondition
rationale: IfcBoundaryFaceCondition is associated with the connection between a space and a building element through IfcRelSpaceBoundary.

subject: IfcBoundaryNodeCondition

subject: IfcBoundaryNodeCondition

subject: IfcBoundaryNodeCondition

subject: IfcBoundedCurve
rationale: IfcCompositeCurve is a concrete subtype of IfcBoundedCurve.

subject: IfcBoundedCurve
rationale: IfcBSplineCurve is a concrete subtype of IfcBoundedCurve.

subject: IfcBoundedCurve

subject: IfcBoundedCurve

IfcProductDefinitionShape contains one or more IfcShapeRepresentation objects, which in turn contain IfcRepresentationItem subtypes. The chain is indirect, and 'supports' is misleading at best. subject: IfcBoundedCurve

subject: IfcBoundedCurve

subject: IfcBoundaryNodeConditionWarping

subject: IfcBoundaryNodeConditionWarping

subject: IfcBuilding
rationale: IfcBuilding requires building elements (walls, slabs, columns, beams) as structural and enclosure components to function as a building.

subject: IfcBuilding
rationale: The building provides structural support and enclosure for building systems such as HVAC, electrical, plumbing, and fire protection systems.

subject: IfcBuilding

subject: IfcBuildingElementPart
rationale: IfcBuildingElementPart typically participates in aggregation relationships (IfcRelAggregates) to relate to its parent building element or system. It depends on this relationship for context.
applicability: The assertion says IfcBuildingElementPart depends_on IfcRelAggregates, but IfcBuildingElementPart can also participate in hierarchical decomposition via IfcRelNests (nesting) in addition to IfcRelAggregates. The assertion over-constrains the relationship to only IfcRelAggregates.

exceptions: when used as an independent element without parent aggregation

subject: IfcBuildingElementPart
rationale: IfcBuildingElementPart is contained within a spatial structure element (e.g., IfcBuildingStorey) via IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure for spatial context and placement.

subject: IfcBuildingElementPart

subject: IfcBuildingElementPart

applicability: IfcBuildingElementPart may have geometric representation via IfcMappedItem or if it inherits shape representation from its parent element, without requiring its own IfcProductDefinitionShape. The assertion is too narrow.
conditions: when 3D representation or geometric shape is required
exceptions: if the element part is defined purely by properties without geometry

subject: IfcBuildingElementPart
rationale: Property sets (IfcPropertySet) are used to assign properties to IfcBuildingElementPart instances.
conditions: when property definitions are attached

subject: IfcBuildingElementPart

subject: IfcBuildingElementPart

subject: IfcBuildingElementPartType

subject: IfcBuildingElementPartType

subject: IfcBuildingElementPartType

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxyType

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxyType
rationale: IfcBuildingElementProxyType depends on property sets (IfcPropertySet) to capture non-geometric attributes specific to the proxy element.
applicability: The assertion says 'depends_on' but IfcBuildingElementProxyType inherits from IfcTypeObject which has a 'HasPropertySets' relationship to IfcPropertySetDefinition (not directly to IfcPropertySet). IfcPropertySet is itself a subtype of IfcPropertySetDefinition, so this is directionally correct but the relationship is through the supertype's 'HasPropertySets' inverse attribute, making the dependency implicit in the IFC schema rather than a configurable dependency.
conditions: When additional properties beyond the standard type definition are needed

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxyType
rationale: IfcBuildingElementProxyType requires the IfcRelDefinesByType relationship to associate individual IfcBuildingElementProxy occurrences to this type definition.

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxyType

applicability: IfcBuildingElementProxyType inherits from IfcTypeProduct which has 'HasAssociations' inverse to IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, not a direct dependency on IfcMaterial. The assertion oversimplifies by saying depends_on IfcMaterial directly.

exceptions: If the proxy is purely a placeholder or spatial container without material definition

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxyType

conditions: When IfcBuildingElementProxy instances are created from this type

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxyType

conditions: When the proxy type has a predefined geometric representation
exceptions: If the proxy type has no geometric representation

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxyType
rationale: Material associations at the type level require IfcRelAssociatesMaterial to link the proxy type to its material definition.

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxyType
rationale: IfcBuildingElementProxyType contains property set definitions that describe its static attributes shared across all instances.
conditions: When the proxy type defines standard property sets

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxyType
rationale: The type definition supports property assignment relationships that link property sets to the proxy instances.
conditions: When property definitions need to be propagated from type to instances

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxyType
rationale: As an IFC entity, IfcBuildingElementProxyType depends on IfcOwnerHistory for ownership and versioning information.
applicability: IfcBuildingElementProxyType inherits from IfcRoot which has the 'OwnerHistory' attribute as mandatory. This is not a 'depends_on' relationship in a domain/logical sense but a schema-level mandatory attribute. The owner history is always present for all IFC root entities per the IFC schema specification, not a conditional dependency.
conditions: For tracking authorship, creation date, and modification history

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxyType
rationale: Using typed proxy definitions improves project-level data consistency and classification compared to using generic proxy occurrences.

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxy

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxy
rationale: IfcBuildingElementProxy requires property sets to define its specific behavior and characteristics since the class is generic.

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxy
rationale: As a building element proxy representing actual construction components, a material is typically required to define its physical properties.
conditions: When representing a physical object with material composition
exceptions: Conceptual or placeholder proxies

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxy
rationale: Building element proxies typically need to be contained within a spatial structure element like a building story.
conditions: When the proxy must be placed within a building story or other spatial container
exceptions: Freestanding elements in early design

The assertion says 'depends_on IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure' when condition is 'placed within a building story or other spatial container' with exception 'Freestanding elements in early design'. However, in IFC2x3 and IFC4, IfcBuildingElementProxy can also be contained in IfcExternalSpatialStructureElement (e.g., outdoor elements). An additional exception is needed for proxies located outside the building spatial structure entirely, such as site-level elements or exterior elements not within any story.

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxy
rationale: IfcBuildingElementProxy depends on local placement to define its position and orientation within the project.
conditions: When the proxy has a defined location in 3D space

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxy

conditions: When the proxy has a geometric representation in 3D

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxy

conditions: When the proxy contains an opening that is later filled by another element like a door or window

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxy
rationale: Every IFC entity requires owner history information as per the IFC schema.
conditions: Always required in IFC data exchange

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxy
rationale: IfcBuildingElementProxy can be connected to other elements via connection relationships when part of an assembly or system.
conditions: When the proxy is connected to other building elements structurally or functionally
exceptions: Isolated proxies

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxy
rationale: Material assignment requires a relationship to associate the material with the proxy element.
conditions: When a material is explicitly assigned
exceptions: Proxies without material assignment

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxy
rationale: Property set definitions need to be linked to the proxy through a relationship entity.
conditions: When property sets are assigned to the proxy
exceptions: Proxies without property sets

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxy
rationale: IfcBuildingElementProxy can support system assignments when it functions as part of a larger building system.
conditions: When the proxy is part of a building system (e.g., HVAC, electrical, structural)
exceptions: Standalone elements not belonging to a system

subject: IfcBuildingElementProxy
rationale: IfcBuildingElementProxy allows representation of unique or custom building elements that improve design flexibility.
applicability: The assertion states 'improves IfcBuilding' which is not a standard IFC relationship concept. In IFC, IfcBuilding is not directly linked to IfcBuildingElementProxy in an 'improves' sense. IfcBuilding is part of the spatial hierarchy (IfcProject -> IfcSite -> IfcBuilding -> IfcBuildingStorey) and contains elements through IfcRelContainerdInSpatialStructure. The verb 'improves' is ambiguous and not a recognized IFC relationship predicate.
conditions: When the proxy represents a custom design element that fulfills a specific architectural or functional need not covered by standard element types
exceptions: Placeholder proxies without design intent

The assertion states 'depends_on IfcPropertySetDefinition' but IfcPropertySetDefinition is abstract (cannot be instantiated directly). The relationship actually depends on concrete subtypes like IfcPropertySet or IfcElementQuantity. Also, property sets are not always required for types that have no specific properties.

exceptions: conceptual types without physical material

conditions: when a geometric representation is shared across all occurrences of the type
exceptions: types defined without geometry

IfcRepresentationMap is only required when using mapped representations (IfcMappedItem). For types using swept solid, extrusion, or other direct representations, the type does not require IfcRepresentationMap. The assertion states 'requires' which is too strong.

subject: IfcBuildingElementType
