subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: An IfcBuildingStorey contains slabs (floor slabs) as part of its spatial structure.
conditions: when defining floor levels
exceptions: IfcSlab may represent a land survey point, a site slab, or a roof slab (e.g., IfcSlabTypeEnum: LANDING, ROOF, APPROACH, PAVING, TRACK_SLAB) that are not floor-level slabs and would not be contained by IfcBuildingStorey. For instance, a roof slab is typically contained by IfcBuilding or IfcRoof, not an individual storey.

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: IfcBuildingStorey contains walls that are within or bound that storey level.
conditions: when bounding the storey
exceptions: IfcWall may span multiple storeys (e.g., curtain walls, shear walls, load-bearing walls that extend through multiple floors). In such cases, the wall is typically contained by the IfcBuilding or a higher-level spatial structure rather than a single IfcBuildingStorey.

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Beams spanning the storey are contained within it.
conditions: when part of the storey structure
exceptions: IfcBeam can span across multiple storeys (e.g., transfer beams, deep beams) or be part of a roof structure, in which case it would be contained by IfcBuilding or IfcRoof rather than an individual IfcBuildingStorey.

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Columns on a given storey are contained by that storey.
conditions: when located on that storey
exceptions: IfcColumn can span multiple storeys (continuous columns passing through floor slabs). Such columns are typically related to the building as a whole via IfcRelAggregates to IfcBuilding, not contained within a single storey.

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Windows are contained within the storey's walls.
conditions: when placed in walls of the storey

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Doors are contained within the storey's walls.
conditions: when placed in walls of the storey

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Coverings (finishes) are contained in the storey spaces.
conditions: floor finishes, wall finishes, ceiling finishes

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Stairs that serve and are within a storey are contained.
conditions: when serving the storey level

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Railings on the storey are contained.
conditions: when located on the storey

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Spaces (rooms, zones) are directly contained in a building storey.
conditions: when the space is on that storey level

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Furniture items are typically contained in storey spaces.
conditions: when placed within spaces of the storey
exceptions: furniture in movable/open-plan layouts may not be explicitly contained

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: A building storey must be part of a parent building; it cannot exist without an IfcBuilding.
conditions: always

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Each storey needs a local placement relative to the building.
conditions: for spatial positioning and coordinate reference
exceptions: IfcBuildingStorey can use IfcRelativePlacement (relative placement) when its parent IfcBuilding already provides the local coordinate system. Also, in some IFC exchange scenarios, IfcBuildingStorey may have no explicit placement (e.g., when only elevation is defined via the Elevation attribute). The assertion that it 'requires' IfcLocalPlacement is too strong.

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: The aggregation relationship linking the building to its storeys is essential.
conditions: for hierarchical decomposition of building into storeys

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Elements must be linked to the storey via containment relationships.
conditions: to relate building elements to the storey

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Storeys provide the spatial framework that supports the definition of spaces.
conditions: by providing vertical subdivision and spatial organization

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Stairs connect one storey to another vertically.
conditions: for vertical circulation between storeys
exceptions: A stair that is internal to a single storey (e.g., a few steps between split levels within the same storey) does not connect storeys and does not exhibit a connects_to relationship between IfcBuildingStorey and IfcStair for vertical circulation between storeys.

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Ramps connect storeys for accessibility.
conditions: for accessible vertical circulation between storeys
exceptions: A ramp that is internal to a single storey (e.g., a small ramp within a lobby or a ramp to a stage) does not connect different storeys and thus does not participate in a connects_to relationship between IfcBuildingStorey and IfcRamp for vertical circulation between storeys.

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Distribution system elements (e.g., ducts, pipes) are contained within the storey.
conditions: MEP distribution elements like ducts, pipes, cables within the storey

subject: IfcBuildingStorey
rationale: Flow terminals are located within storey spaces.
conditions: air terminals, diffusers, sanitary terminals on the storey

subject: IfcBuildingSystem
rationale: An IfcBuildingSystem groups multiple building elements (e.g., walls, slabs) into a functional system.
conditions: when acting as a container for building elements

subject: IfcBuildingSystem
rationale: IfcBuildingSystem can contain distribution elements for service systems.
conditions: when representing a distribution system such as HVAC, electrical, or plumbing

subject: IfcBuildingSystem
rationale: A building system may contain or be decomposed into sub-systems.
conditions: when representing a hierarchical system breakdown

subject: IfcBuildingSystem
rationale: The system depends on the relationship object that links it to a building.
conditions: when establishing which building(s) the system serves

subject: IfcBuildingSystem
rationale: A building system is typically defined in the context of a building project.
conditions: the system must be assigned to a building context
exceptions: a system can exist in a project without being explicitly assigned to a building

subject: IfcBuildingSystem
rationale: Building systems like structural frames or vertical distribution systems support the functions of building storeys.
applicability: 'Supports' is vague in IFC semantics. IfcBuildingSystem does not have a direct 'supports' relationship to IfcBuildingStorey. Systems like HVAC or plumbing may span storeys but are not said to 'support' them structurally. The assertion confuses service distribution across storeys with structural support.
conditions: when the system provides structural or service support across storeys

subject: IfcBuildingSystem
rationale: A building system often requires property sets to define its technical characteristics.
conditions: when defining performance or technical properties of the system
exceptions: Not all IfcBuildingSystem instances require IfcPropertySet. Simple systems or those without performance/technical documentation requirements can exist without property sets. The assertion as stated ('requires') is too strong - it should be conditional on the need for such properties.

subject: IfcBuildingSystem
rationale: Systems composed of physical elements require material definitions.
conditions: when the system has material composition requirements
exceptions: Not all building systems with material composition requirements need an IfcMaterialConstituentSet. They could use IfcMaterialList, IfcMaterialLayerSet, or IfcMaterialProfileSet depending on the type of system. 'Requires' is too restrictive - many alternative material definition approaches exist in IFC.

subject: IfcBuildingSystem
rationale: IfcBuildingSystem is assigned to group relationship objects to collect its members.
conditions: when the system is assigned to a group relationship

subject: IfcBurnerType
rationale: IfcBurnerType defines the type information for IfcBurner instances; the type requires the actual occurrence entity to function.
applicability: all building types with combustion heating
conditions: when burner is part of a combustion system

subject: IfcBurnerType

conditions: when burner provides heat input to a boiler

subject: IfcBurnerType

conditions: when burner flame heats a heat exchanger surface
exceptions: direct-fired systems may not use a separate heat exchanger

subject: IfcBurnerType
rationale: Advanced burner types improve the overall efficiency of energy conversion devices by achieving more complete combustion.
conditions: when burner is a high-efficiency condensing type

subject: IfcBurnerType
rationale: The burner type may include safety features that protect surrounding building elements from heat damage or fire.
applicability: The assertion says 'IfcBurnerType protects_from IfcBuildingElementProxy' but IfcBuildingElementProxy is a generic catch-all for undefined or placeholder building elements. The fire-rated assembly or cabinet protects people and surrounding building elements generally, not specifically IfcBuildingElementProxy. This relationship is misleadingly narrow and the condition should specify what the enclosure actually protects (e.g., occupants, combustible materials, other building elements).
conditions: when burner is enclosed in a fire-rated assembly or cabinet

subject: IfcCableCarrierFitting
rationale: Cable carrier fittings (e.g., bends, tees, crosses) are used to connect and transition between cable carrier segments to form a complete cable management pathway.
applicability: The assertion states IfcCableCarrierFitting depends_on IfcCableCarrierSegment, but in many installations a cable carrier fitting (e.g., a junction box, pull box, or conduit body) can be installed at the end of a run connected to only one segment, or as a standalone fitting. A 'continuous cable routing system' often implies multiple segments, but a single-segment termination is a valid counterexample.
conditions: when used as part of a continuous cable routing system

subject: IfcCableCarrierFitting
rationale: The fitting exists to support or route cables; without cables to carry, the fitting serves no functional purpose.
applicability: The assertion states IfcCableCarrierFitting depends_on IfcCableSegment, but a cable carrier fitting (e.g., conduit body, junction box) can exist in a cable containment system that only carries cable trays or cable ladder without any IfcCableSegment instances yet modeled (e.g., empty raceway installed for future use, or a fitting that terminates a conduit run with no cable assigned).
conditions: when the fitting is part of a cable containment system carrying cables

subject: IfcCableCarrierFitting
rationale: Fittings often require brackets, screws, bolts, or other fasteners to be mounted in place.
conditions: when the fitting needs to be secured to a structure or another component

subject: IfcCableCarrierFitting
rationale: Fittings like conduit bodies or cable trays fittings physically support and guide cables through changes in direction.
conditions: when the fitting acts as a support or guide for cables passing through it
exceptions: The assertion states IfcCableCarrierFitting supports IfcCableSegment. However, a cable carrier fitting's primary purpose is to connect, contain, or change direction of cable carrier segments, not to structurally support cable segments (conductors/cables). Cable segments are typically supported by the carrier itself (conduit, tray, trunking) or by dedicated cable supports, not by the fitting. A bushing or reducer inside a conduit body does not 'support' an IfcCableSegment in the IFC sense — it guides it.

subject: IfcCableCarrierFitting
rationale: Fittings are connection devices that join two or more cable carrier segments together or change the direction of the routing.
conditions: in all typical installations
exceptions: The assertion states 'in all typical installations' that IfcCableCarrierFitting connects_to IfcCableCarrierSegment. Some fittings (e.g., a blind end cap, a dead-end box, a conduit sealing fitting) terminate a carrier run and do not connect to another segment. Also, some fittings like service entrance caps or weatherheads connect to only one segment at the end of a run, contradicting the 'in all typical installations' blanket scope.

subject: IfcCableCarrierFitting
rationale: The fitting depends on a supporting structure (beam, slab, wall) for its physical installation.
applicability: The assertion states IfcCableCarrierFitting depends_on IfcStructuralMember when mounted. However, many fittings are supported by the carrier segments themselves (e.g., a conduit coupling between two conduit runs supported by trapeze hangers on a beam — the coupling does not directly depend on the structural member, only the conduit does). Also, cable tray fittings are often supported by the tray splices or by trapeze supports that may not be modeled as IfcStructuralMember.
conditions: when the fitting is mounted to a wall, ceiling, or structural frame

subject: IfcCableCarrierSegmentType
rationale: Cable carrier segments collectively form the cable management system that organizes and supports electrical and data cabling infrastructure.
conditions: When installed as part of a complete cable management solution

subject: IfcCableCarrierSegment
rationale: Cable carrier segments connect to fittings like elbows, tees, and reducers to form a complete routing system.
applicability: IfcCableCarrierSegment connects to IfcCableCarrierFitting only applies when using a fitting-based carrier system (e.g., cable tray with fittings). In many real-world installations, cable carriers connect directly to other segments via couplers/connectors that are not modeled as separate IfcCableCarrierFitting entities, or connections are made using splice plates/joints that are considered part of the segment itself in IFC modeling.
conditions: at junctions, bends, and transitions in the cable carrier system
exceptions: for continuous straight runs without fittings

subject: IfcCableCarrierSegment
rationale: Cable carriers often connect at their ends to electrical distribution boards, panels, or enclosures.
conditions: at the origin or termination of cable runs
exceptions: when cables terminate directly at equipment

subject: IfcCableSegment
rationale: Cable segments contain insulation material surrounding the conductors to prevent short circuits and ensure safety.
conditions: in all insulated cables
exceptions: bare conductors without insulation

The assertion says IfcCableSegment 'contains' Insulation, but in IFC the relationship between an element and its material (including insulation) is typically via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial or IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage, not a direct containment. There may be cables where insulation is documented via material layers rather than as a separate 'contained' element.

subject: IfcCableSegmentType
rationale: Cable segments often require fittings for connections, splices, and terminations.
conditions: when cables need to be joined, terminated, or change direction

subject: IfcCableSegmentType
rationale: Cable segments typically connect to distribution boards for power distribution.
conditions: when cable segment is part of power distribution

subject: IfcCableSegmentType
rationale: Cable segments often depend on cable carrier segments for mechanical support and protection.
applicability: The assertion uses 'depends_on' which is ambiguous — it is not a standard IFC relationship (IfcRelConnectsElements, IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, etc.). IfcCableSegmentType is a type entity and does not have a direct dependency relationship with IfcCableCarrierSegment in the IFC schema; instances of IfcCableSegment (the occurrence) might be placed on IfcCableCarrierSegment, but the type definitions are independent.
conditions: when cables are not self-supporting and require tray or ladder support
exceptions: direct burial cables
cables in underground ducts

subject: IfcCableSegmentType
rationale: Cable segments connect distribution boards to electrical appliances and devices.
conditions: when cable segment provides power to equipment

subject: IfcCableSegmentType
rationale: Cable segments connect to light fixtures in lighting systems.
conditions: when part of lighting circuit

subject: IfcCableSegmentType
rationale: Cable segments connect to electrical outlets for power delivery.
conditions: when cable segment is part of power outlet circuit

subject: IfcCableSegmentType
rationale: Cable segments require being part of a defined electrical building system for proper management and maintenance.
conditions: when cable segment is part of a structured electrical system

conditions: When chiller is water-cooled type

subject: IfcChillerType
rationale: Chillers require pumps to circulate chilled water and condenser water.
applicability: Not all chiller types require pumps. Some small package chillers have integral pumps, but they are not always modeled as separate IfcPump entities. In a BMS control context, the chiller might be a self-contained unit without a distinct pump object. The 'Always' condition is too strong.
conditions: Always

subject: IfcChillerType
rationale: Chiller requires electrical power supply to run compressors and controls.
conditions: Always

subject: IfcChillerType
rationale: A chiller contains one or more compressors as core refrigeration components.

subject: IfcChillerType
rationale: Chiller contains an evaporator where heat exchange occurs to cool the chilled water.
applicability: While many chillers contain evaporators, absorption chillers use a generator/absorber pair rather than a mechanical compressor/evaporator cycle. The assertion does not hold for absorption-type chillers.
conditions: Always

subject: IfcChillerType
rationale: Chiller contains a condenser where refrigerant heat is rejected.
applicability: Same issue as evaporator: absorption chillers use a generator and absorber instead of a conventional condenser. Additionally, air-cooled chillers integrate the condenser as part of the unit, but it may not be modeled as a separate IfcCondenser entity in the type decomposition.
conditions: Always

subject: IfcChillerType
rationale: Chiller protects building occupants and equipment from overheating by providing cooling.
conditions: When installed in a mechanical room
exceptions: If not properly maintained

subject: IfcChiller
rationale: A cooling tower is typically paired with water-cooled chillers to dissipate heat.
conditions: For water-cooled chiller systems

subject: IfcChiller
rationale: Chillers typically interface with a BMS for sequencing, setpoint control, and alarm monitoring.
applicability: 'depends_on BMS' is too strong. While a BMS enables optimal control and monitoring, many chillers operate independently or with standalone controllers without a full BMS, especially in smaller buildings. The condition says 'for optimal control and monitoring' but the assertion states it 'depends_on' BMS as a hard dependency, which is misleading.
conditions: For optimal control and monitoring

subject: IfcChiller
rationale: Chillers supply chilled water to AHUs for cooling supply air.

subject: IfcChiller
rationale: Chillers provide chilled water to FCUs for zone-level cooling.

subject: IfcChiller
rationale: Chilled water from chillers feeds cooling coils in VAV boxes.
applicability: 'IfcChiller supports VAV Box' is misleading even with the condition. A chiller does not directly support a VAV box—it supplies chilled water to an air handling unit that conditions air, which is then distributed to VAV boxes. The relationship is indirect (chiller → AHU → VAV box). The condition 'when equipped with a cooling coil' is also incomplete; the VAV box would need a reheat coil or fan-powered box with a cooling coil, but the chiller is still not directly 'supporting' it.
conditions: When equipped with a cooling coil

subject: IfcChiller
rationale: Water-cooled chillers connect to cooling towers via condenser water piping.
conditions: For water-cooled chillers

subject: IfcChimney
rationale: Chimneys must be supported on a foundation to transfer dead and live loads to the ground.

subject: IfcChimney
rationale: A chimney often connects to a fireplace or combustion appliance to vent smoke and gases.
conditions: When the chimney serves a solid-fuel or gas fireplace
exceptions: Free-standing or industrial chimneys without attached fireplace

subject: IfcChimney
rationale: The chimney connects to flashing at the roof penetration to ensure weathertightness.
conditions: At the point where the chimney exits the roof
exceptions: Chimneys that are entirely external to the building (e.g., exterior-mounted chimneys on the outside wall) do not penetrate the roof — they rise alongside the exterior wall. The condition 'at the point where the chimney exits the roof' therefore does not apply, yet the applicability says 'All chimneys penetrating a roof.' There is a gap: the assertion is correctly scoped to penetrating chimneys but needs an explicit exception for external/exterior-mounted chimneys that do not penetrate.

subject: IfcChimneyType

conditions: when chimney serves a heating appliance

subject: IfcChimneyType

conditions: structural support needed
exceptions: Not all chimneys require a foundation. A lightweight prefabricated double-wall metal chimney (e.g., for a pellet stove) that is cantilevered from a wall or supported by a roof brace may transfer structural loads directly to the wall framing or roof structure without a dedicated foundation. The condition 'structural support needed' is tautological and does not capture these cases.

subject: IfcChimneyType
rationale: Proper flashing and sealing at roof/wall penetrations are critical to prevent water ingress and maintain building envelope integrity.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcChimneyType depends_on Building Envelope' is vague — 'Building Envelope' is a broad concept (walls, roof, windows, doors). The dependency should specify which envelope component(s) (e.g., roof sheathing, wall cladding) and what kind of dependency (physical penetration, thermal bridging, air sealing). Without this specificity, the assertion is too imprecise for a knowledge base.
conditions: where chimney penetrates roof or wall

subject: IfcChimneyType
rationale: The chimney connects to roof flashing assemblies to create a watertight seal at the roof penetration point.
conditions: where chimney passes through roof
exceptions: wall-mounted chimneys may not penetrate roof

IfcCircleProfileDef is one of many valid subtypes of IfcProfileDef that can be used here. The assertion is directionally correct but oversimplifies the relationship: the connection is via the SweptArea attribute, not a direct 'connects_to' association, and any subtype of IfcProfileDef is valid.

subject: IfcCircleHollowProfileDef

subject: IfcCivilElementType
rationale: The type connects to property definitions through relationship objects in the IFC schema.
conditions: When property sets are assigned to the type

subject: IfcClassificationReference
rationale: IfcClassificationReference is a reference to an external classification system; it depends on the IfcClassification entity to define the classification source.
conditions: When used as a reference to an external classification system

subject: IfcClassificationReference
rationale: IfcClassificationReference is contained within or used by IfcRelAssociatesClassification to associate classification data with IFC objects.
conditions: When objects are associated with the classification reference

subject: IfcClassificationReference
rationale: IfcClassificationReference connects to IfcClassification to identify the originating classification system.
conditions: When referencing a classification source

subject: IfcClassificationReference
rationale: IfcClassificationReference can support IfcProject by providing classification references for project-wide classification systems.
conditions: When classification is applied at the project level

subject: IfcClassificationReference
rationale: IfcClassificationReference supports IfcObjectDefinition entities by providing external classification references for building elements, systems, and other objects.
conditions: When objects are classified using this reference

subject: IfcClosedShell
rationale: IfcClosedShell is defined in IFC as a closed shell composed of a set of IfcFace entities that form a topological boundary of a closed volume.
conditions: When the closed shell is defined as a collection of faces bounding a closed volume

subject: IfcClosedShell
rationale: An IfcClosedShell must consist of at least four IfcFace entities to form a closed 3D volume.
conditions: For the closed shell to be valid

subject: IfcClosedShell
rationale: IfcClosedShell faces are often bounded by IfcPolyLoop to define planar polygonal boundaries.
applicability: All building types with faceted geometry

IfcClosedShell does not directly require IfcPolyLoop — the shell contains IfcFace, and IfcFace may reference IfcPolyLoop via IfcFaceBound. The assertion omits the intermediate IfcFace and IfcFaceBound layers, which is a simplification that could mislead users about the actual IFC inheritance and composition structure.
conditions: When the shell uses polygonal geometry representation
exceptions: When using advanced surface representations like IfcRationalBSplineSurface

subject: IfcClosedShell
rationale: IfcClosedShell is a subtype of IfcConnectedFaceSet, thus depends on its parent class definition.
conditions: Inheritance structure in IFC

subject: IfcClosedShell
rationale: IfcClosedShell can be a component within IfcShellBasedSurfaceModel to represent complex surfaces.
conditions: When used to define shell-based surface models

subject: IfcClosedShell
rationale: IfcFacetedBrep uses IfcClosedShell to define the outer boundary of a solid.
applicability: Architectural and structural elements with faceted geometry
conditions: When the closed shell defines the boundary of a faceted Boundary Representation

subject: IfcClosedShell
rationale: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids uses one outer IfcClosedShell and one or more inner IfcClosedShell for voids.
applicability: Complex building elements with holes or voids
conditions: When the solid contains interior voids

subject: IfcCoil
rationale: Circulation pumps are required to move water through the coil for thermal transfer.
conditions: when part of a hydronic system (chilled water or hot water loop)

subject: IfcCoil
rationale: Coils are housed in AHUs or FCUs which connect to supply and return ductwork.
applicability: The condition 'installed in an air handling system' is limiting - fan coil units (IfcCoil) are often installed in terminal units like FCUs not in central air handling systems, yet they still connect to ductwork (supply and return air ducts). The condition should also cover terminal unit contexts.
conditions: when installed in an air handling system
exceptions: While the assertion says IfcCoil connects_to Ductwork when in an air handling system, there are exceptions. Chilled water coils and hot water coils (hydronic coils) have both air-side connections to ductwork and hydronic-side connections to piping. The statement omits this dual nature. Also, refrigerant coils (DX coils) connect to refrigeration piping. Additionally, a heating coil in a VAV box with reheat connects to ductwork but also to hot water piping. The assertion is too narrow by stating only ductwork connections.

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: IfcCoilType is a subtype of IfcEnergyConversionDevice and typically requires connection to energy conversion systems.
conditions: When coil is used for energy transfer

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Coils depend on distribution flow elements (pipes, ducts) to carry heating/cooling medium.
applicability: The statement 'IfcCoilType depends_on IfcDistributionFlowElement' is overly broad. IfcDistributionFlowElement includes pumps, fans, valves, pipes, ducts, and many other elements. While a coil is part of a distribution system, it does not generically depend on all distribution flow elements — it depends on specific ones (pumps, fans, pipes, ducts). This broad dependency is too generic to be practically useful without narrowing.
conditions: For proper fluid or air flow

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Hydronic heating/cooling coils require pumps to circulate water/glycol.
conditions: For hydronic coils
exceptions: Not all hydronic coils require an IfcPump. For example, gravity-fed or thermosiphon hydronic systems (common in some solar thermal or steam systems) can circulate without a pump. Also, in district heating systems, the coil may connect to a network where the pump is external and not modeled as part of the coil's local system.

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Air coils require fans to move air across the coil surface for heat exchange.
conditions: For air coils (AHU/FCU)
exceptions: Not all air coils require an IfcFan. In naturally ventilated systems or passive air coils (e.g., gravity coils, or coils in natural draft cooling towers), there may be no fan present. Also, some air handlers use an external fan that is not directly associated with the coil as a separate IfcFan entity.

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Control valves are required to regulate flow through the coil.
conditions: For flow control

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Pipes connect coils to the central plant or distribution system.
conditions: For hydronic coils

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Ducts deliver air to/from coil sections in air handling units.
conditions: For air coils

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Chilled water coils depend on chillers for cold water supply.
conditions: When coil supplies chilled water
exceptions: The assertion 'IfcCoilType depends_on IfcChiller' with condition 'When coil supplies chilled water' is incorrect. The coil does not depend on a chiller as a direct dependency; it depends on a chilled water source which could be a chiller, a heat pump, district cooling, a cooling tower with plate heat exchanger, or a ground-source loop. The chiller is an indirect dependency at best, and in many building models the chiller may be in a separate system entirely.

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Hot water coils depend on boilers for heated water supply.
conditions: When coil supplies hot water
exceptions: The assertion 'IfcCoilType depends_on IfcBoiler' with condition 'When coil supplies hot water' is too restrictive. The hot water source could be a boiler, a heat pump, district heating, a heat recovery system, or a solar thermal system. The coil does not directly depend on a boiler entity specifically.

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Coils support thermal conditioning of building spaces.
conditions: When coil serves zone heating/cooling

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Coils support HVAC zone temperature control.
conditions: When part of HVAC zone

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Coils connect to pipe fittings for branch connections.

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Coils in ducted systems connect to duct fittings.
conditions: When in ducted system

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Filters protect coils from particulate fouling and debris.
conditions: When upstream filter is present

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Dampers can protect coils from freezing by closing when not in use.
conditions: Freeze protection or isolation

subject: IfcCoilType
rationale: Flow controllers modulate the fluid flow through the coil to meet load.
conditions: For modulating flow

subject: IfcColourRgb
rationale: IfcColourRgb is a subtype of IfcColourSpecification, so it depends on the parent type for its specification structure.
conditions: when used as a color definition

subject: IfcColourRgb
rationale: IfcColourRgb provides the color definition for IfcSurfaceStyleShading to define surface rendering colors.
conditions: when used as the SurfaceColour attribute

subject: IfcColourRgb
rationale: IfcColourRgb provides color values used in surface rendering definitions for realistic visualization.
conditions: when used as the SurfaceColour or any of the color factor attributes

subject: IfcColourRgb
rationale: IfcColourRgb can be used to define the color of text literals in annotation and presentation contexts.
applicability: IfcTextLiteralWithExtent uses IfcColourRgb indirectly through IfcTextStyle which includes a TextColour attribute of type IfcColour (potentially IfcColourRgb). The annotation text color is defined via IfcTextStyle, not directly on IfcTextLiteralWithExtent. The assertion oversimplifies the relationship chain.
conditions: when used to define text color in annotation

subject: IfcColourRgb
rationale: Colors defined by IfcColourRgb can be assigned to presentation layers for visual styling of geometric elements.
applicability: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment does not directly use IfcColourRgb. It assigns presentation layer information to geometric representation items via IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle, which uses IfcCurveStyle, IfcSymbolStyle, IfcFillAreaStyleHatching, IfcSurfaceStyle, IfcTextStyle, etc. IfcColourRgb is consumed by those styles, not directly by IfcPresentationLayerAssignment. The assertion misrepresents the indirect relationship chain.
conditions: when assigned to presentation layers that specify color

subject: IfcColourRgb
rationale: IfcColourRgb contributes to IfcStyledItem for visually styling building elements in IFC models.
conditions: when used as part of a style definition for geometric representation

subject: IfcColourRgb
rationale: While color does not affect structural function, applying RGB colors to building elements improves visual communication, identification, and presentation of the model.
conditions: when colors are applied for visualization or identification purposes

subject: IfcColourRgbList
rationale: IfcColourRgbList is an IFC entity that contains a list of IfcColourRgb colour values. It is a container for multiple RGB colour definitions.

subject: IfcColourRgbList
rationale: IfcColourRgbList depends on IfcColourRgb entities as its constituent colour entries; without at least one IfcColourRgb, the list would be empty and non-functional.
applicability: The 'depends_on' relationship implies a dependency, but IfcColourRgbList merely aggregates IfcColourRgb instances. IfcColourRgbList does not functionally depend on IfcColourRgb—it is simply a collection type. The dependency direction may be inverted or the relationship type may be inappropriate.
conditions: when defining a list of RGB colours

subject: IfcColourRgbList
rationale: IfcColourRgbList can be referenced by presentation style assignments to provide a colour list for surface styles, lighting, or rendering in IFC models.
conditions: when used in presentation style definitions

subject: IfcColourRgbList
rationale: IfcColourRgbList can be used within surface style rendering definitions to specify colour lists for shading and rendering of building surfaces.
conditions: when used for surface colour properties

subject: IfcColourSpecification
rationale: IfcColourSpecification is an abstract supertype; its primary concrete subtype is IfcColourRgb which provides the actual RGB colour definition.
conditions: when colour is defined by RGB values
exceptions: when colour is defined by other colour models like HSL or CMYK

subject: IfcColourSpecification
rationale: IfcColourSpecification is assigned to surface style rendering to define colour properties of surfaces.
conditions: when used for surface appearance definition

subject: IfcColourSpecification
rationale: IfcColourSpecification can be used within IfcSurfaceStyleShading for surface colour definition.
conditions: when defining basic shading colour

subject: IfcColourSpecification
rationale: Colour specifications support graphical presentation layers in IFC models.
conditions: when colour is part of a presentation layer

subject: IfcColourSpecification
rationale: IfcColourSpecification can be referenced by IfcStyledItem for graphical styling.
conditions: when colour is used in styled graphical elements

subject: IfcColourSpecification
rationale: Colour specifications define colours used in fill area styles for graphical presentation.
conditions: when defining fill area colours for diagrams and drawings

subject: IfcColourSpecification
rationale: IfcColourSpecification can define text colour within IfcTextStyle.
conditions: when defining text colour in annotations

subject: IfcColourSpecification
rationale: IfcColourSpecification supports surface style definitions by providing colour information.
conditions: when colour is used as part of surface style definition

subject: IfcColourSpecification
rationale: Colour specifications depend on presentation style assignment context for application.
conditions: when assigned to a presentation style

subject: IfcColourSpecification
rationale: Colour specifications support annotation elements by defining their appearance colours.
applicability: IfcColourSpecification does not directly 'support' IfcAnnotation. IfcAnnotation is a product representation that can have styled representations, but the colour specification is used through surface styles, text styles, or fill area styles that are then assigned to annotation elements. The relationship is indirect, and 'supports' suggests a direct relationship that does not exist in the schema.
conditions: when colour is used in annotation elements

subject: IfcColumn
rationale: An IfcColumn requires a foundation to transfer its vertical loads safely to the ground.
conditions: when transferring vertical loads to the ground

subject: IfcColumn
rationale: In framed structures, columns often require beams to distribute floor/roof loads to the column.
conditions: when part of a framed structural system
exceptions: load-bearing wall systems where columns are not used with beams

subject: IfcColumn
rationale: Columns support slabs that carry floor loads.
conditions: when columns are load-bearing elements in a framed structure
exceptions: IfcColumn supports Slab is not always true in framed structures — in flat slab or flat plate systems (without drop panels), slabs are supported directly by columns, but the relationship is more accurately a connection or load transfer rather than 'support' in the typical beam-to-column sense. Also, in pre-cast concrete structures, columns may support slabs via corbels or brackets, which is a different structural behavior than framed slab support.

subject: IfcColumn
rationale: Columns provide vertical support for beams.
conditions: in beam-column frame systems
exceptions: In moment-resisting frames (rigid frames), beams frame into columns and the relationship is mutual (beam-to-column moment connection) rather than column 'supporting' beam in a simple bearing sense. Also in certain structural systems like mega-columns or outrigger systems, beams may be supported by other beams or walls, not columns.

subject: IfcColumn
rationale: Columns in upper levels support roof structures.
applicability: The assertion assumes columns always extend to roof level to support a roof, but in buildings with attic spaces, roof trusses, or where the roof structure is supported by rafters or trusses that bear on walls rather than columns, columns may not necessarily support the roof even if they extend to roof level. Also, in multi-level buildings, the topmost columns support the roof, but intermediate columns do not.
conditions: when columns extend to roof level

subject: IfcColumn
rationale: Concrete columns depend on the concrete material to provide compressive strength.
conditions: when column is a reinforced concrete column
exceptions: steel columns
timber columns

Even for reinforced concrete columns, the dependency on 'Concrete' is not universally applicable — the column depends on concrete as a material, but in Ifc terms 'depends_on' may imply a different relationship. Additionally, pre-stressed precast concrete columns may have a more complex material dependency involving pre-stressing strands. Also for composite columns (concrete-filled steel tubes), the dependency is on both concrete and steel, not just concrete.

subject: IfcColumn
rationale: Steel columns connect to base plates which transfer loads to the foundation.
applicability: The assertion limits applicability to 'steel structures' but steel columns in some building types (e.g., industrial buildings, pipe racks, temporary structures) may connect directly to anchor bolts on a foundation pedestal or grout pad without a discrete 'Column Base Plate' Ifc element being modeled or present. The connection may be modeled as a direct connection to the foundation.
conditions: when column is a steel column anchored to foundation
exceptions: concrete cast-in-place columns without base plates

subject: IfcColumn
rationale: In classical orders, the column shaft supports the capital at its top.
conditions: in classical or decorative architectural styles
exceptions: modern minimalist columns without capitals

subject: IfcColumn
rationale: Columns often occur at wall intersections or corners and connect structurally or architecturally to walls.
applicability: Columns that are embedded in walls (e.g., concealed columns) may have a relationship to the wall, but adjacent columns may be separated by an air gap, insulation, or be structurally independent with a seismic joint, meaning they do not actually connect to the wall. The assertion should clarify that this applies only when there is physical contact or structural interaction.
conditions: when columns are embedded in or adjacent to walls

subject: IfcColumnStandardCase
rationale: IfcColumnStandardCase is a subtype of IfcColumn representing standardized column geometries, so it depends on the base IfcColumn entity.
conditions: when IfcColumnStandardCase represents a standardized column profile
exceptions: custom non-standard column profiles

subject: IfcColumnStandardCase
rationale: Columns require material definitions (concrete, steel, timber, etc.) for structural performance.
conditions: for defining column material properties

subject: IfcColumnStandardCase
rationale: Columns must be designed to support vertical loads; load definitions are required for engineering.
conditions: for structural analysis and design verification

subject: IfcColumnStandardCase
rationale: Columns connect to beams, slabs, and foundations; relationship objects formalize these connections.
conditions: when connecting column to other structural elements

subject: IfcColumnStandardCase
rationale: Columns provide vertical support for beams in framed structural systems.
conditions: when beams rest on or are connected to columns
exceptions: beams supported by walls or other columns directly

subject: IfcColumnStandardCase
rationale: Columns transfer slab loads to foundations in multi-story structures.
conditions: when slab loads transfer to columns
exceptions: slabs supported directly by walls or ground

subject: IfcColumnStandardCase
rationale: Columns may be covered with fireproofing, cladding, or finishes for protection.
conditions: for fire protection, insulation, or aesthetic finishing
exceptions: exposed architectural columns without covering

subject: IfcColumnStandardCase
rationale: Columns typically connect to footings to distribute loads to the ground.
conditions: when column transfers loads to foundation
exceptions: columns on raft foundations or pile caps without distinct footing

subject: IfcColumnStandardCase
rationale: Columns help define and stabilize the spatial organization of building stories.
applicability: The assertion that IfcColumnStandardCase 'improves IfcBuildingStorey' is vague. Columns provide vertical support but their relationship to IfcBuildingStorey is spatial containment (IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure) rather than 'improving' the storey. The terminology is ambiguous.
conditions: when columns define vertical spatial structure

subject: IfcColumnStandardCase
rationale: Material association relationship is needed to link material definitions to the column element.
conditions: to formally assign material to column

subject: IfcColumnStandardCase
rationale: Every column requires a placement in 3D space within the building model.
conditions: for positioning column in building coordinate system
exceptions: IfcColumnStandardCase may use IfcLocalPlacement relative to another placement (e.g., grid placement via IfcGridPlacement) or may be placed using IfcLinearPlacement. Local placement is not the only positioning method.

subject: IfcColumnStandardCase
rationale: IfcColumnStandardCase typically references a column type for standardized properties.
conditions: when using predefined column types
exceptions: if geometry is defined directly without type

subject: IfcColumnType
rationale: IfcColumnType as a structural column requires proper foundations to transfer loads to the ground.
conditions: When supporting vertical loads from columns
exceptions: IfcColumnType does not require a foundation in all cases — for example, columns supported by pile caps, footings, or mat slabs connect to Foundation subclasses indirectly; in some structural systems columns bear on grade beams or caissons rather than a discrete IfcFoundation element.

subject: IfcColumnType
rationale: Columns support floor slabs above them, transferring vertical loads.
conditions: When column extends from floor to floor
exceptions: In steel frame buildings, IfcColumnType instances may be used with steel columns that pass through floor slabs with only a shear connection (not supporting the slab structurally). The slab is supported by beams or metal deck, not the column type itself.

subject: IfcColumnType
rationale: Columns support beams which in turn transfer loads from slabs and other elements.
conditions: In beam-column frame systems
exceptions: In flat slab systems beams may not be present

subject: IfcColumnType
rationale: Columns at the topmost level support the roof structure.
conditions: When column extends to roof level

subject: IfcColumnType
rationale: Columns connect to beams at each floor level forming structural frames.
conditions: At beam-column joints

subject: IfcComplexProperty
rationale: IfcComplexProperty typically belongs to an IfcPropertySet which groups properties together for an object.
applicability: All building information models using IFC schema
conditions: When used as part of a property set definition

subject: IfcComplexProperty
rationale: IfcComplexProperty is designed to contain one or more sub-properties (IfcProperty instances) as its child properties.
applicability: All building information models using IFC schema
conditions: When it contains nested sub-properties

subject: IfcComplexProperty
rationale: IfcComplexProperty specifically exists to group multiple simple properties into a hierarchical structure.
applicability: All building information models using IFC schema
conditions: When defining complex, nested property structures

subject: IfcComplexProperty
rationale: IfcComplexProperty inherits from IfcProperty and is part of the property definition hierarchy in IFC.
applicability: All building information models using IFC schema
conditions: When associated with an object through property definition relationships

subject: IfcComplexProperty
rationale: IfcComplexProperty provides structured property data to building objects, enabling detailed descriptions of their characteristics.
applicability: All building elements, systems, and objects that have property definitions
conditions: When assigned to an object via IfcRelDefinesByProperties

subject: IfcComplexProperty
rationale: IfcComplexProperty enhances the property set with hierarchical organization of data.
applicability: All building information models using IFC schema
conditions: When contained within a property set

subject: IfcComplexProperty
rationale: The relationship that assigns IfcComplexProperty (via its parent property set) to an IfcObject depends on IfcRelDefinesByProperties.
applicability: All building information models using IFC schema
conditions: When being assigned to an object
exceptions: If the complex property is not assigned to any object

subject: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate
rationale: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate is a subtype of IfcPropertyTemplate and inherits its properties for defining property templates in IFC
applicability: All building information modeling workflows using IFC

The assertion uses 'depends_on' which is ambiguous. In the IFC schema, IfcComplexPropertyTemplate has a HasPropertyTemplates attribute that contains IfcPropertyTemplate instances. This is a composition/aggregation relationship, not merely a dependency. The term 'depends_on' under-specifies the actual containment semantics defined in the IFC specification.
conditions: When defining complex property templates that group multiple properties
exceptions: Simple property templates that don't contain sub-properties

subject: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate
rationale: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate can contain multiple IfcPropertyTemplate instances as its sub-properties
conditions: When the complex property template has sub-properties defined
exceptions: Empty complex property templates with no sub-properties

subject: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate
rationale: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate is typically contained within IfcPropertySetTemplate to define property sets
conditions: When used as part of a property set template definition
exceptions: Standalone complex property templates not assigned to any property set

subject: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate
rationale: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate enables hierarchical property structures within property set templates
conditions: When complex properties are needed to group related properties
exceptions: Simple property sets using only single-value properties

subject: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate
rationale: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate may reference IfcPropertyEnumeration for defining property ranges
applicability: IFC property definitions with enumerated values
conditions: When the complex property template references enumerated property values
exceptions: Complex property templates that don't use enumeration values

subject: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate
rationale: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate contributes to the overall property definition framework in IFC
conditions: When defining complex property structures for building elements

subject: IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface
rationale: IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface is a subtype of IfcCompositeCurve that is defined on a parametric surface. It requires an underlying IfcSurface (the basis surface) to exist and define the curve in 3D space.
conditions: The composite curve must lie on the surface

subject: IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface
rationale: As a composite curve, IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface is composed of ordered IfcCompositeCurveSegment entities, each representing a segment of the overall curve on the surface.
conditions: Each segment must correspond to a p-curve (parameter space curve) on the same surface

subject: IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface
rationale: IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface can serve as a boundary curve for a surface (e.g., for an IfcFaceBound or IfcFaceOuterBound), depending on the geometric context.
conditions: When the composite curve is closed and forms the boundary of a face

subject: IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface
rationale: IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface helps define the edges or boundaries of an IfcFace, enabling accurate surface modeling in BRep geometry.
applicability: IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface as a curve entity does not directly 'improve' IfcFace. In IFC, the boundary of a face is defined via IfcFaceBound which references IfcBoundaryCurve (a subtype). A plain IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface can be used as a boundary curve but the specialized IfcBoundaryCurve subtype is typically used for face boundaries. The improvement is indirect and the standard mechanism uses IfcBoundaryCurve.
conditions: When used to define the boundary of a face

subject: IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface
rationale: IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface is a key geometric element for defining faces in advanced BRep (boundary representation) models with complex surface geometry.
conditions: Used in advanced boundary representation models

subject: IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface
rationale: The segments of IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface use parameter space curves (p-curves) defined on the underlying surface's 2D parameter domain.
conditions: Each segment references a p-curve in the parameter space of the surface

subject: IfcCompositeCurve
rationale: IfcCompositeCurve inherits from IfcCurve in the IFC schema.
conditions: IfcCompositeCurve is a subtype of IfcCurve

subject: IfcCompositeCurve
rationale: IfcCompositeCurve inherits from IfcBoundedCurve.
conditions: IfcCompositeCurve is a subtype of IfcBoundedCurve

subject: IfcCompositeCurve
rationale: Specialization of IfcCompositeCurve for curves lying on a surface.
conditions: IfcCompositeCurveOnSurface is a subtype of IfcCompositeCurve

subject: IfcCompositeCurve
rationale: Alternative bounded curve type; related but not directly dependent.
conditions: Both are bounded curve types in IFC

subject: IfcCompositeCurveSegment
rationale: IfcCompositeCurveSegment is a subtype of IfcBoundedCurve and represents a segment within an IfcCompositeCurve, so it requires the parent curve definition.
conditions: when acting as a composite curve segment

subject: IfcCompositeCurveSegment
rationale: IfcCompositeCurveSegment is always defined as a segment of an IfcCompositeCurve, which aggregates these segments into a continuous curve.
conditions: when used as a segment within a composite curve

subject: IfcCompositeCurveSegment
rationale: IfcCompositeCurveSegment contains a reference to an IfcCurve (the ParentCurve) which defines the actual geometry of the segment.
conditions: when ParentCurve attribute is assigned

subject: IfcCompositeCurveSegment
rationale: The ParentCurve may be a trimmed curve, requiring the trim definition to properly interpret the segment.
conditions: when the segment uses a trimmed portion of a curve

subject: IfcCompositeCurveSegment
rationale: The composite curve segment's start and end points depend on Cartesian points defined within its parent curve.
conditions: for defining the start and end points of the segment

subject: IfcCompositeCurveSegment
rationale: Multiple IfcCompositeCurveSegment instances collectively support the definition of an IfcCompositeCurve.
conditions: as a constituent segment

subject: IfcCompositeCurveSegment
rationale: IfcCompositeCurveSegment can support the creation of complex polylines by assembling multiple segment definitions.
conditions: when ParentCurve is an IfcPolyline

subject: IfcCompositeCurveSegment
rationale: Using composite curve segments improves the modeling of complex continuous curves by allowing different curve types to be joined together.
conditions: when modeling complex curves that cannot be represented by a single curve type

subject: IfcCompositeProfileDef
rationale: IfcCompositeProfileDef is a subtype of IfcProfileDef that combines multiple IfcProfileDef instances into a single profile definition. Therefore it directly requires one or more IfcProfileDef as its constituent parts.
conditions: When defining composite profiles

subject: IfcCompositeProfileDef
rationale: The composite profile definition depends on having multiple base profile definitions to compose the combined cross-section geometry.
conditions: At least two profile definitions must be combined
exceptions: A single profile cannot form a composite profile alone

subject: IfcCompositeProfileDef
rationale: Composite profile definitions (e.g., built-up steel sections) support the definition of material profile sets used in structural member definitions.
applicability: The assertion says IfcCompositeProfileDef 'supports' IfcMaterialProfileSet, but in IFC4 it is IfcMaterialProfileSet that references IfcProfileDef (via MaterialProfiles attribute of IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage), not the other way around. IfcCompositeProfileDef does not directly 'support' anything — it is a geometric/profile definition that can be referenced. The directionality of 'supports' may cause confusion about the actual IFC relationship.
conditions: When the composite profile is assigned to a material profile set for structural members

subject: IfcCompositeProfileDef
rationale: IfcCompositeProfileDef provides the cross-section geometry for structural members that are composed of multiple profiles (e.g., a steel beam with a channel cap).
conditions: When the composite profile defines the cross-section of a structural element such as a composite beam, column, or girder

subject: IfcCompositeProfileDef
rationale: Positioning multiple profile definitions relative to each other may require a 2D Cartesian transformation operator to specify offsets, rotations, or scaling.
conditions: When constituent profiles need to be positioned relative to each other via transformation
exceptions: If profiles are already positioned in the correct relative locations without transformation

subject: IfcCompositeProfileDef
rationale: IfcCompositeProfileDef is typically referenced by IfcShapeRepresentation to define the geometric representation of an element's cross-section.
conditions: When the composite profile is used as part of the shape representation of a product

subject: IfcCompressorType
rationale: A compressor requires a motor connection to receive mechanical power for operation.
conditions: for mechanical power transmission

subject: IfcCompressorType
rationale: Compressors typically require an electric motor as the prime mover.
conditions: for electrical-to-mechanical energy conversion

subject: IfcCompressorType
rationale: In a refrigeration cycle, the compressor depends on the condenser to reject heat from the compressed refrigerant.
conditions: in refrigeration/AC systems

subject: IfcCompressorType
rationale: The compressor depends on the evaporator to absorb heat and return vapor for re-compression.
conditions: in refrigeration/AC systems

subject: IfcCompressorType
rationale: Compressors contain suction and discharge valves to control refrigerant flow into and out of the compression chamber.
conditions: suction and discharge valves

subject: IfcCondenserType
rationale: The coil is the primary heat exchange surface where refrigerant condenses.
exceptions: Air-cooled condensers (e.g., finned-tube heat exchangers with fans) do not have a 'coil' in the traditional sense — they use finned tube bundles or microchannel heat exchangers. The assertion 'requires Condenser Coil' is ambiguous or incorrect for these types.

subject: IfcCondenserType
rationale: Cooling towers reject heat from condenser water to the atmosphere, enabling water recirculation.
conditions: For water-cooled condenser systems with recirculating water
exceptions: Once-through water systems (e.g., city water) do not require a cooling tower

Air-cooled condenser systems do not use a cooling tower at all. The condition already partially addresses water-cooled systems, but the assertion as stated could be interpreted to apply to all IfcCondenserType, which is incorrect.

subject: IfcCondenserType
rationale: Condensers enable heat rejection for cooling systems, supporting overall HVAC function.
applicability: Condensers are also used in standalone refrigeration systems (e.g., walk-in coolers, display cases, ice machines) where there is no chiller or heat pump system. The condition 'When part of a chiller or heat pump system' excludes these common use cases.
conditions: When part of a chiller or heat pump system

subject: IfcCondenserType
rationale: Refrigerant lines connect the condenser to the compressor and expansion device.
exceptions: Air-cooled condensers with remote air-cooled condensing units connect to refrigerant piping, but evaporative condensers and some packaged units (e.g., self-contained rooftop units with integral condensers) may not have separate field-installed refrigerant piping as an explicit connection; the piping may be factory-sealed within the package.

subject: IfcCondenser
rationale: Piping connects the condenser to the compressor, expansion device, and evaporator.
applicability: Not all condenser installations have refrigerant piping — air-cooled condensers (e.g., those in packaged DX units) may use direct-expansion coils with no discrete refrigerant piping run between a separate condenser and other components. The assertion assumes a split-system or remote-condenser configuration.

subject: IfcCondenser
rationale: The coil is the heat exchange surface essential for condensing refrigerant vapor to liquid.

subject: IfcConic
rationale: IfcConic is an abstract supertype in IFC for conic curves (circles, ellipses, etc.) and requires an IfcPlacement (specifically IfcAxis2Placement) to define its position and orientation in space.
conditions: When defining the conic curve's position in 3D space

subject: IfcConic
rationale: IfcConic is the abstract supertype that contains IfcCircle as one of its subtypes.

subject: IfcConic
rationale: IfcConic is the abstract supertype that contains IfcEllipse as one of its subtypes.

subject: IfcConic
rationale: IfcConic curves are typically used within IfcShapeRepresentation, which requires an IfcRepresentationContext.
applicability: All IFC models using geometric representations
conditions: When the conic curve is part of a geometric representation
exceptions: IfcConic is abstract and instances of its subtypes reference a Representation through the inherited Representation attribute of IfcProduct, not directly from IfcConic. The dependency on IfcRepresentationContext is indirect through the geometric representation item hierarchy, not a direct dependency from IfcConic.

subject: IfcConic
rationale: Conic curves can serve as the boundary curve for IfcCurveBoundedPlane.
applicability: All IFC models using bounded surfaces
conditions: When defining a bounded plane surface with conic boundary

subject: IfcConic
rationale: Conic curves (IfcConic subtypes) can be used as the BasisCurve in IfcTrimmedCurve to create trimmed segments of circles or ellipses.
conditions: When trimming a conic curve to a specific segment

subject: IfcConic
rationale: Conic curves can be segments within an IfcCompositeCurve.
conditions: When building a composite curve that includes a conic segment

subject: IfcConic
rationale: The IfcPlacement used by IfcConic ultimately references IfcCartesianPoint for position definition.
applicability: IfcConic does not directly connect to IfcCartesianPoint. The Placement attribute (IfcAxis2Placement) references an axis placement that itself contains a Location of type IfcCartesianPoint. The connection is indirect (via IfcAxis2Placement -> IfcPlacement -> IfcCartesianPoint), not a direct connects_to relationship.
conditions: Through the placement definition

subject: IfcConnectedFaceSet
rationale: IfcConnectedFaceSet is composed of connected IfcFace entities, forming a topologically connected set of faces.
conditions: when representing a connected set of faces

subject: IfcConnectedFaceSet
rationale: An IfcConnectedFaceSet contains a collection of faces that are connected along shared edges.
conditions: as part of its definition

subject: IfcConnectedFaceSet
rationale: IfcConnectedFaceSet is a subtype of IfcTopologicalRepresentationItem and participates in topological shape models.
conditions: when used within a shape representation

subject: IfcConnectedFaceSet
rationale: IfcConnectedFaceSet can be the basis for IfcClosedShell when the faces form a closed boundary.
conditions: when the face set forms a closed shell
exceptions: if the face set is open, it does not form a closed shell

subject: IfcConnectedFaceSet
rationale: IfcConnectedFaceSet can be the basis for IfcOpenShell when the faces do not form a closed boundary.
conditions: when the face set forms an open shell
exceptions: if the face set is closed, it does not form an open shell

subject: IfcConnectedFaceSet
rationale: IfcConnectedFaceSet is used as the outer geometry in faceted boundary representations of solid shapes.
applicability: IfcFacetedBrep has an 'Outer' attribute of type IfcClosedShell, not IfcConnectedFaceSet directly. IfcConnectedFaceSet may be used indirectly (IfcClosedShell is a subtype of IfcConnectedFaceSet), but the direct relationship in IfcFacetedBrep is through IfcClosedShell, not the more general IfcConnectedFaceSet.
conditions: when used as the outer geometry boundary representation

subject: IfcConnectedFaceSet
rationale: Connected face sets may reference IfcFaceSurface instances where each face carries surface geometry information.
conditions: when the faces have associated surface geometry

subject: IfcConnectedFaceSet
rationale: The geometry of faces depends on underlying coordinate points that define their vertices and edges.
conditions: for defining the vertices of the faces in the set

subject: IfcConnectedFaceSet
rationale: Faces are bounded by edges; an IfcConnectedFaceSet relies on edge connectivity between faces.
conditions: for defining the boundaries of each face in the set

subject: IfcConnectedFaceSet
rationale: Many faces in a connected face set use poly loops to define their outer and inner boundaries.
conditions: when faces are defined using polygonal boundaries

subject: IfcConnectedFaceSet
rationale: Each face in the set requires at least one face bound to define its boundary.
conditions: for defining the boundaries of each face

subject: IfcConnectionCurveGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionCurveGeometry uses IfcCurve to define the geometric representation of the connection between two curve edges.
conditions: For representing the connection geometry along a curve

subject: IfcConnectionCurveGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionCurveGeometry is a subtype of IfcConnectionGeometry, inheriting its properties.
conditions: As the parent type/superclass

subject: IfcConnectionCurveGeometry
rationale: The curve geometry connection is typically applied between two edge-based topological representations.
conditions: To define the curve edge where the connection geometry is applied

subject: IfcConnectionCurveGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionCurveGeometry provides the geometric definition for connections between path elements.
conditions: When connecting path-based elements along curves
exceptions: IfcRelConnectsPathElements may connect path-based elements using curve geometry, but the entity IfcConnectionCurveGeometry itself does not 'support' that relationship type. Rather, IfcRelConnectsPathElements has a ConnectionGeometry attribute that can accept an IfcConnectionCurveGeometry instance. The wording 'supports' suggests a dependency inversion that does not match the IFC schema hierarchy.

subject: IfcConnectionCurveGeometry
rationale: As a connection geometry type, it is used in relationships that connect building elements along curves.
conditions: When establishing physical or logical connections between building elements
exceptions: IfcConnectionCurveGeometry 'connects_to' IfcRelConnectsElements is misleading. While IfcRelConnectsElements has a ConnectionGeometry attribute that can hold an IfcConnectionCurveGeometry (via its parent IfcConnectionGeometry), this is a unidirectional attribute relationship, not a bidirectional connection. Also, IfcRelConnectsPathElements is the more specific relationship type that typically uses IfcConnectionCurveGeometry, as IfcRelConnectsElements is more general.

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionGeometry is an abstract supertype; its most common subtype IfcConnectionPointGeometry defines the actual point of connection between elements.
applicability: IfcConnectionGeometry is an abstract supertype in IFC. The actual dependency is that the subtype IfcConnectionPointGeometry can be used when a point-based connection is defined, but IfcConnectionGeometry (the abstract class) does not directly 'depend_on' IfcConnectionPointGeometry in a schema sense. The relationship is through inheritance hierarchy.
conditions: when a point-based connection topology is defined

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionCurveGeometry is another subtype of IfcConnectionGeometry used for edge/cuve connections.
applicability: Same issue as with the point geometry variant - IfcConnectionGeometry is abstract, and the relationship with IfcConnectionCurveGeometry is via subtype specialization, not a direct dependency of the abstract supertype.
conditions: when a curve-based connection topology is defined

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry is another subtype for surface-based connections.
applicability: Same issue - IfcConnectionGeometry is abstract and the actual relationship is with the subtype IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry.
conditions: when a surface-based connection topology is defined

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionVolumeGeometry is another subtype for volumetric connections.
conditions: when a volume-based connection topology is defined

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: Connection geometry often references placement coordinates of the connected elements.
conditions: when the connection geometry is defined relative to the local coordinate system of the related element

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionGeometry provides the geometric details for IfcRelConnectsElements relationships.
conditions: when a relationship between two elements needs geometric connection information

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: Connection geometry can be used to define port connections in distribution systems.
conditions: when ports of distribution elements are connected

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: Path element connections use connection geometry for their path-based topology.
conditions: when path-based elements (like walls) are connected along paths

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: Connection geometry describes the spatial relationship in realized connections.
conditions: when a realizing element (like a bolt or weld) makes the connection

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionPointGeometry may contain IfcAxis2Placement3D to define the connection point.
conditions: when a point connection uses 3D placement data

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionPointGeometry can contain a point defined on a curve.
conditions: when the connection point lies on a curve

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionPointGeometry can contain a point defined on a surface.
conditions: when the connection point lies on a surface

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionCurveGeometry contains a curve entity.
conditions: when connection uses IfcConnectionCurveGeometry

subject: IfcConnectionGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry contains a surface entity.
conditions: when connection uses IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry

subject: IfcConnectionPointEccentricity
rationale: IfcConnectionPointEccentricity is a subtype of IfcConnectionGeometry used to describe the eccentricity of a structural connection point relative to a structural member or connection.
conditions: when modeling structural connections with eccentricity

subject: IfcConnectionPointEccentricity
rationale: The eccentricity is typically defined using a 3D placement coordinate system to specify the offset.
conditions: when eccentricity is defined in 3D space

subject: IfcConnectionPointEccentricity
rationale: Eccentricity definitions are closely related to the connection condition (e.g., rigid, pinned) which influences how the offset is applied in analysis.
conditions: when the connection condition affects the eccentricity definition

subject: IfcConnectionPointEccentricity
rationale: IfcConnectionPointEccentricity supports the relationship between structural members by defining the exact eccentric connection point geometry.
conditions: when defining eccentric connection between structural members

subject: IfcConnectionPointEccentricity
rationale: Accurate eccentricity data is essential for structural analysis models to properly simulate load transfer at connections with offsets.
conditions: when performing structural analysis with eccentric connections

subject: IfcConnectionPointEccentricity
rationale: The connection point eccentricity defines how a structural member connects to another at an offset from its centroid.
conditions: when a structural member is connected eccentrically to another element

subject: IfcConnectionPointGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionPointGeometry uses an IfcPoint (or subclass like IfcCartesianPoint) to define the geometric location of the topological connection element.
conditions: for defining the connection geometry location

subject: IfcConnectionPointGeometry
rationale: As a subtype, IfcConnectionPointGeometry may relate to IfcConnectionCurveGeometry in the hierarchy of connection geometries.
conditions: when the connection involves a curve-based topology

subject: IfcConnectionPointGeometry
rationale: The point geometry definition supports connections between topological face sets in the IFC model.
conditions: when used in a topological network context where points connect face sets

subject: IfcConnectionPointGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionPointGeometry is referenced as the connection geometry in IfcRelConnectsElements to define how two elements meet at a point.
conditions: when the connection geometry is used to describe the spatial relationship between two elements

subject: IfcConnectionPointGeometry
rationale: Port connections in MEP systems often use point geometry to define where ports connect.
conditions: when connecting distribution ports at a point location

subject: IfcConnectionPointGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionPointGeometry contains or references a Cartesian point coordinate (x,y,z) as its primary geometric data.
conditions: as the point coordinate reference

subject: IfcConnectionPointGeometry
rationale: Point connection geometry can define the meeting point of path elements in systems like ductwork or piping.
conditions: when path elements meet at connection points in a distribution system

subject: IfcConnectionPointGeometry
rationale: The point geometry may be defined in the context of a local placement for an element or connection.
conditions: when the point coordinates are defined relative to a local coordinate system

subject: IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry is part of the IfcConnectionGeometry hierarchy; it depends on IfcConnectionCurveGeometry as a related subtype for certain connection types.
conditions: when surface-based connections are present
exceptions: Even if a connection involves a surface geometry, there is no requirement in the IFC schema that IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry depends on or requires IfcConnectionCurveGeometry. They are sibling types under IfcConnectionGeometry used for different geometric representations.

subject: IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry contains or references an IfcSurface entity to define the surface at which two elements connect.

subject: IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry is a subtype of IfcConnectionGeometry, inheriting its properties and requiring the parent class for definition.

subject: IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry is used in relationships of type IfcRelConnects to define the geometric surface of connection.
applicability: IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry does not directly 'connect_to' IfcRelConnects. Rather, IfcRelConnects subtypes such as IfcRelConnectsPathElements, IfcRelConnectsWithEccentricity, IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements, etc., may use IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry as a connection geometry attribute. The relationship is indirect via an attribute (ConnectionGeometry) on IfcRelConnects, not a direct connection. The assertion is overly simplistic.
conditions: when defining a connection between building elements

subject: IfcConnectionVolumeGeometry
rationale: IfcConnectionVolumeGeometry is a subtype of IfcConnectionGeometry, inheriting its geometric representation properties for connection volumes.
conditions: When representing volumetric connection geometry

subject: IfcConnectionVolumeGeometry
rationale: Connection volume geometry is typically referenced by relationship entities that define physical connections between building elements.
conditions: When used in element-to-element connections

subject: IfcConnectionVolumeGeometry
rationale: Port connections in MEP systems may reference volume geometry for spatial connection definition.
conditions: When used in port-based connections for distribution systems

subject: IfcConnectionVolumeGeometry
rationale: Volume geometry in 3D space requires coordinate points to define its position and shape.
conditions: When the geometry is defined using a 3D coordinate system
exceptions: When geometry is defined parametrically without explicit points

subject: IfcConnectionVolumeGeometry
rationale: Volume connection geometry can support the definition of spatial boundaries where elements meet volumetrically.
conditions: When defining spatial boundaries between connected elements

subject: IfcConnectionVolumeGeometry
rationale: In some cases, volume geometry may reference or build upon curve geometry for the axis or path of the connection.
conditions: When the volume connection encompasses a curve-based connection path
exceptions: For simple direct volume connections without curve paths

subject: IfcConstraint
rationale: IfcObjective is a subtype of IfcConstraint, so IfcConstraint directly supports the definition of objectives.
applicability: all projects using IFC for objectives
conditions: when constraints are used to define objectives

subject: IfcConstraint
rationale: IfcMetric is a subtype of IfcConstraint, so IfcConstraint supports the definition of measurable metrics.
conditions: when constraints define measurable criteria

subject: IfcConstraint
rationale: Constraints often refer to property sets to define limiting values on properties.
applicability: projects where property-based constraints are applied
conditions: when constraints reference property values

subject: IfcConstraint
rationale: IfcRelAssociatesConstraint is the relationship class that links IfcConstraint to other IFC objects.
conditions: when a constraint is assigned to a product or object

subject: IfcConstraint
rationale: Constraints can define allowable limits on building elements such as beams, columns, etc.
conditions: when constraint defines a design rule for an element (e.g., max deflection)

subject: IfcConstructionEquipmentResource
rationale: Construction equipment resources typically need associated product resources (materials, components) to function meaningfully in a construction schedule.
conditions: when defining resource usage in construction planning

subject: IfcConstructionEquipmentResource
rationale: Construction equipment usually requires operators (labor resources) to function.
applicability: all construction projects with manned equipment
conditions: when equipment requires operators for proper use
exceptions: fully automated equipment

subject: IfcConstructionEquipmentResource
rationale: Equipment resources are assigned to tasks in IFC; they depend on task context for meaningful deployment.
conditions: when assigned to a specific construction task via IfcRelAssignsToProcess

subject: IfcConstructionEquipmentResource
rationale: IfcConstructionEquipmentResource is linked to other IFC entities via IfcRelAssignsToResource.
conditions: when assigning actors, products, or processes to the resource

subject: IfcConstructionEquipmentResource
