rationale: Equipment resources often require property sets to define technical specifications.
conditions: when detailed equipment properties (capacity, power, dimensions) are needed

subject: IfcConstructionEquipmentResource
rationale: Classifying equipment resources may depend on classification references for standardized identification.
conditions: when equipment is classified according to a standard classification system (e.g., OmniClass, Uniclass)

subject: IfcConstructionEquipmentResource
rationale: Construction equipment resources often have associated costs that need to be captured via cost items.
conditions: when equipment costs need to be tracked and estimated

subject: IfcConstructionEquipmentResourceType
rationale: The type definition depends on having occurrences (IfcConstructionEquipmentResource) that reference it.
conditions: When instantiated as occurrences

subject: IfcConstructionEquipmentResourceType
rationale: Construction equipment resources are typically assigned to specific construction tasks via IfcRelAssignsToProcess.
conditions: When equipment resources are assigned to tasks

subject: IfcConstructionEquipmentResourceType
rationale: Equipment resources are one sub-type of construction resources alongside product and labor resources.
conditions: When co-located in a construction project resource hierarchy

subject: IfcConstructionEquipmentResourceType
rationale: Type definitions often depend on property sets to define technical characteristics like capacity, power, dimensions.
conditions: When specific equipment properties are defined

subject: IfcConstructionEquipmentResourceType
rationale: Construction equipment requires labor resources (operators) to function, creating a connection between equipment types and labor types.
conditions: When equipment requires operators

subject: IfcConstructionEquipmentResourceType
rationale: The type definition depends on the relationship entity IfcRelDefinesByType to link occurrences to this type.
conditions: When type-object relationships are established

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResource
rationale: Material resources may be transformed into product resources during construction.
conditions: When materials are fabricated into products on-site

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResource
rationale: Materials often require equipment for handling, mixing, or placement.
conditions: When equipment is needed to transport or process materials

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResource
rationale: Construction tasks consume materials; IfcConstructionMaterialResource defines the material supply for task execution.
conditions: When tasks require material input

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResource
rationale: IfcConstructionMaterialResource aggregates or references specific IfcMaterial instances defining the actual material type (e.g., concrete, steel).
conditions: When resource has a defined material composition

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResource
rationale: IfcConstructionMaterialResource is a subtype of IfcConstructionResource, connecting it to the broader resource management schema.
conditions: In the general resource hierarchy

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResource
rationale: As a subtype of IfcConstructionResource, it inherits base attributes and relationships from this parent class.
conditions: For base resource management properties

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResource
rationale: Work schedules reference material resources to ensure availability aligns with planned work.
conditions: When material availability is scheduled

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResource
rationale: Material resources are linked to building elements via material association relationships.
conditions: For associating materials to building elements
exceptions: IfcRelAssociatesMaterial associates IfcMaterial to IfcObjectDefinition (building elements, products), not to IfcConstructionMaterialResource. The resource entity may reference materials, but the association entity IfcRelAssociatesMaterial does not directly relate to IfcConstructionMaterialResource - materials are related to elements, not to construction resource entities.

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResourceType
rationale: IfcConstructionMaterialResourceType is a subtype of IfcConstructionResource in the IFC schema, so it depends on the parent class for its base definitions.
conditions: When representing a type of construction material resource

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResourceType
rationale: In IFC, a Type entity defines the shared properties and templates for occurrences. IfcConstructionMaterialResourceType contains the type-level definitions used by IfcConstructionMaterialResource occurrences.
conditions: When instantiated as occurrences

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResourceType
rationale: Construction material resource types typically reference material definitions (IfcMaterial) to specify what material is being consumed or tracked as a resource.
conditions: When defining material resource types with specific material properties
exceptions: If no material assignment is needed

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResourceType
rationale: Type entities in IFC often have associated property set templates that define the properties applicable to all occurrences of that type.
applicability: All IFC-based projects with extended property definitions
conditions: When custom properties are defined for the resource type

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResourceType
rationale: Construction material resource types support construction tasks (IfcTask) by providing the material inputs needed to complete the work.
conditions: When construction tasks consume materials

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResourceType
rationale: Material resources often support product resources by supplying the raw materials that are transformed into construction products.
conditions: When both material and product resources are assigned to the same construction process

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResourceType
rationale: Material resource types are typically linked to cost items to track the cost of materials used in construction.
applicability: Cost estimation and control in construction projects
conditions: When cost tracking is applied to material resources
exceptions: When no cost information is associated

subject: IfcConstructionMaterialResourceType
rationale: The IfcRelAssignsToProcess relationship object connects resources to processes, and material resource types support this assignment structure.
conditions: When material resource types are assigned to processes

subject: IfcConstructionProductResourceType
rationale: IfcConstructionProductResourceType is the type definition for IfcConstructionProductResource entities, so it requires instances of that class to be useful.
conditions: When defining construction product resource types
exceptions: The type can exist without any instantiated resources — if the type is defined but no actual resources of that type are assigned in the project, IfcConstructionProductResource may never be instantiated. The 'requires' is too strong.

subject: IfcConstructionProductResourceType
rationale: Type definitions in IFC often depend on property set definitions to specify their characteristics.
conditions: When property sets are assigned to the type
exceptions: If no property sets are defined

subject: IfcConstructionProductResourceType
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByType is the relationship that associates IfcConstructionProductResourceType with its occurrences.
applicability: IfcRelDefinesByType is used to link the type definition to occurrences. However, IfcConstructionProductResourceType itself does not directly 'depend on' IfcRelDefinesByType — the relationship is that IfcConstructionProductResource (occurrences) use IfcRelDefinesByType to point to the type. The type exists independently of whether any occurrences are linked to it.
conditions: When linking type to occurrences

subject: IfcConstructionProductResourceType
rationale: Construction product resources may depend on material definitions to specify what they are made of.
conditions: When the construction product resource has associated materials
exceptions: If no material information is specified

subject: IfcConstructionProductResourceType
rationale: The type definition contains or defines the template for its occurrences.
conditions: When occurrences are instantiated from the type

subject: IfcConstructionProductResourceType
rationale: Material association in IFC is done through IfcRelAssociatesMaterial.
conditions: When materials are associated to the type
exceptions: IfcConstructionProductResourceType can have materials associated via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial at the type level, but this is not required for the type to exist — many resource types are defined without material associations, especially at early design stages or for generic resource definitions.

subject: IfcConstructionProductResourceType
rationale: Construction product resources may involve labor allocation, but this is more typical of IfcConstructionEquipmentResource or IfcCrewResource.
conditions: When the resource requires labor/crew information
exceptions: For purely material-based resources without labor

subject: IfcConstructionProductResourceType
rationale: Construction product resource types support construction tasks by providing the necessary products for task execution.
conditions: When used in construction scheduling and work breakdown structures

subject: IfcConstructionProductResourceType
rationale: Resource types in construction often depend on cost items for cost estimation purposes.
conditions: When cost information is associated with the resource
exceptions: If no cost data is modeled

subject: IfcConstructionProductResourceType
rationale: Quantity sets provide measurable properties for construction product resource types.
conditions: When quantity information is needed for the resource type
exceptions: If no quantity takeoffs are defined

subject: IfcConstructionProductResource
rationale: IfcConstructionProductResource requires an associated type definition via IfcRelDefinesByType to define its specific nature.
conditions: When a resource is defined by a type

subject: IfcConstructionProductResource
rationale: The resource requires relationship objects to be assigned to construction processes or tasks.
applicability: IfcConstructionProductResource can also be assigned to resources (not just construction processes or tasks) via IfcRelAssignsToResource. The 'resource' in IfcRelAssignsToResource is the resource being assigned, and IfcConstructionProductResource can be the RelatingResource in that relationship, meaning it can be assigned to other resources as well, not just construction processes or tasks.
conditions: When the resource is assigned to a construction process or task

subject: IfcConstructionProductResource
rationale: IfcConstructionProductResource supports IfcTask by providing consumable product materials needed for completing the work task.
conditions: When the resource is assigned to a task via IfcRelAssignsToResource

subject: IfcConstructionProductResource
rationale: As a subtype of IfcResource, it supports construction processes by providing consumable products needed during construction.
conditions: When the resource is assigned to a construction process

subject: IfcConstructionProductResource
rationale: IfcConstructionProductResource often requires property sets to define quantities, cost values, or other specific attributes.
applicability: All projects requiring detailed resource properties
conditions: When additional properties need to be defined

subject: IfcConstructionProductResource
rationale: IfcConstructionProductResource can be connected to IfcCostItem to associate costs with the resource usage.
conditions: When resource costs are tracked

subject: IfcConstructionResource
rationale: IfcConstructionResource is the abstract supertype; IfcLaborResource is a subtype representing human resources needed for construction.
applicability: IfcConstructionResource does not subtype or directly depend on IfcLaborResource in the IFC schema. IfcLaborResource is a subtype of IfcConstructionResource, not the other way around. The 'depends_on' terminology is ambiguous — if it means subtype dependency, this is backwards.
conditions: when resource type is labor-related

subject: IfcConstructionResource
rationale: IfcSubContractResource is a subtype of IfcConstructionResource for subcontracted work.
conditions: when work is subcontracted

subject: IfcConstructionResource
rationale: IfcConstructionEquipmentResource is a subtype representing machinery and equipment used in construction.
conditions: when resource type is equipment-related

subject: IfcConstructionResource
rationale: IfcConstructionMaterialResource is a subtype representing material resources used in construction.
conditions: when resource type is material-related

subject: IfcConstructionResource
rationale: IfcConstructionProductResource is another subtype of IfcConstructionResource representing product-based resources.
conditions: when resource is a product resource

subject: IfcConstructionResource
rationale: Construction resources are assigned to IfcTask entities via IfcRelAssignsToProcess to support construction work.
applicability: IfcConstructionResource does not 'support' IfcTask directly via a named attribute. The assignment is mediated through IfcRelAssignsToResource. The assertion simplifies this relationship but may be misleading without noting the indirect relationship through IfcRelAssignsToResource.
conditions: resources are assigned to tasks

subject: IfcConstructionResource
rationale: IfcRelAssignsToResource is the relationship used to assign resources to objects, connecting IfcConstructionResource to other IFC entities.
conditions: when resource assignment relationship is needed

subject: IfcConstructionResource
rationale: IfcConstructionResource can reference IfcOrganization as the party providing the resource.
applicability: IfcConstructionResource does not have a direct 'depends_on' relationship to IfcOrganization in the IFC schema. IfcOrganization is referenced via IfcActorRole or other indirect relationships, not as a direct dependency of the resource entity.
conditions: when resources are linked to organizational roles

subject: IfcConstructionResource
rationale: IfcConstructionResource (especially labor subtypes) can reference IfcPerson for individual workers.
applicability: IfcConstructionResource does not have a direct 'depends_on' relationship to IfcPerson. IfcPerson may be referenced indirectly through assignments (e.g., IfcRelAssignsToResource with IfcPerson as an assigned object), but it is not a direct dependency of the IfcConstructionResource entity.
conditions: when labor resource involves specific persons

subject: IfcConstructionResource
rationale: IfcConstructionResource can have associated cost information via IfcCostSchedule for resource costing.
applicability: IfcConstructionResource does not have a direct 'depends_on' relationship to IfcCostSchedule. Resource costs are typically captured through IfcCostValue assigned via IfcRelAssignsToResource or IfcRelAssociatesAppliedValue, not a direct dependency on IfcCostSchedule.
conditions: when resource cost data is needed

subject: IfcConstructionResourceType
rationale: IfcConstructionResourceType is the parent abstract type; specific subtypes include IfcConstructionProductResource for product-related resources.
conditions: When resource type is a product resource (materials/components)
exceptions: Not applicable for labor or cost resources

subject: IfcConstructionResourceType
rationale: IfcConstructionResourceType subtypes include IfcConstructionEquipmentResource for equipment resources.
conditions: When resource type is equipment/machinery
exceptions: Not applicable for labor-only tasks

subject: IfcConstructionResourceType
rationale: IfcConstructionResourceType subtypes include IfcSubContractResource for subcontracted resources.
conditions: When work is performed by subcontractors
exceptions: Not applicable for in-house only work

subject: IfcConstructionResourceType
rationale: IfcConstructionResourceType subtypes include IfcConstructionMaterialResource for material resources.
conditions: When resource type involves materials
exceptions: Not applicable for labor-only or equipment-only resources

subject: IfcConstructionResourceType
rationale: Resources typically have associated costs that need to be tracked via cost schedules.
applicability: IfcCostSchedule is typically associated with IfcProject or IfcWorkOrder rather than directly with IfcConstructionResourceType. While cost schedules can reference resources, the direct 'requires' relationship is not an explicit relationship in the IFC schema. Resources reference cost rates via IfcAppliedValue or IfcCostValue, not directly via IfcCostSchedule.
conditions: For cost/resource rate assignment

subject: IfcConstructionResourceType
rationale: Resource availability is often governed by work calendars.
applicability: IfcWorkCalendar is associated with IfcProject, IfcFacility, IfcSpatialStructureElement, or IfcTask, not directly with IfcConstructionResourceType in the IFC schema. While resource availability can be defined using calendars, the direct 'requires' relationship between IfcConstructionResourceType and IfcWorkCalendar is not standard IFC relationship.
conditions: To define resource availability and working times
exceptions: Not needed for continuous 24/7 operations

subject: IfcConstructionResourceType
rationale: Construction resource types are used to define resources that are then assigned to tasks in the work plan.
conditions: When resources are assigned to specific construction tasks

subject: IfcConstructionResourceType
rationale: IfcConstructionResourceType defines the type information; IfcConstructionResource is the occurrence that represents individual instances.

subject: IfcConstructionResourceType
rationale: Resource types support the work plan by defining what resources are available for planned tasks.
conditions: By providing resource definitions needed for work planning

subject: IfcContext
rationale: IfcContext is the root container that aggregates other objects using IfcRelAggregates relationships.
conditions: When representing decomposition relationships
exceptions: IfcContext does not directly 'contain' IfcRelAggregates. IfcRelAggregates links an IfcObjectDefinition (e.g., IfcProject) to its parts. While IfcContext (as a subtype of IfcObjectDefinition) can be the RelatingObject in an aggregation, the assertion phrasing 'IfcContext contains IfcRelAggregates' is misleading—IfcRelAggregates is not a child element stored within the context, but a relationship where the context plays the relating role.

subject: IfcContext
rationale: IfcContext uses IfcRelDeclares to declare relationships to property set templates, quantity set templates, and other declaration objects.
conditions: When declaring project-specific property sets or type definitions
exceptions: IfcRelDeclares is used to relate IfcContext to IfcPropertySetTemplate or IfcTypeObject, but IfcContext does not 'contain' IfcRelDeclares as a child. It is an inverse relationship: IfcRelDeclares.RelatingContext points to the IfcContext. The phrasing 'IfcContext contains IfcRelDeclares' inverts the actual schema relationship.

subject: IfcContext
rationale: IfcContext is the abstract supertype; IfcProject is its primary concrete subtype representing a project context.
conditions: IfcContext is specialized as IfcProject for building projects

subject: IfcContext
rationale: IfcContext is also specialized as IfcProjectLibrary to hold library items.
conditions: When a library context is needed separate from the project

subject: IfcContext
rationale: IfcContext (through IfcProject) relies on unit assignments to define measurement units for the entire model.
conditions: When units need to be defined for the project
exceptions: IfcUnitAssignment is referenced via IfcContext.UnitsInContext attribute (a direct attribute, not a 'depends_on' relationship), and it is mandatory in IFC2x3 but optional in IFC4+. In IFC4, IfcContext.UnitsInContext is optional (WHERE rule WR1 only requires it to exist if units are defined). The assertion should reflect that it's an optional attribute in newer schema versions.

subject: IfcContext
rationale: IfcContext requires geometric representation contexts to define coordinate systems and spatial structure for model geometry.
conditions: When 3D spatial representation is needed
exceptions: IfcContext does not have a direct attribute or relationship 'depends_on' to IfcGeometricRepresentationContext. The geometric representation contexts are referenced through the HAS_ASSOCIATION relationship via IfcRelAssociates or through the IfcProduct representation tree, not directly on IfcContext. IfcContext does not have a mandatory or optional direct reference to IfcGeometricRepresentationContext.

subject: IfcContext
rationale: IfcContext references IfcOwnerHistory for ownership and modification tracking information.
applicability: All IFC files adhering to the schema
conditions: For tracking model ownership and change history
exceptions: IfcOwnerHistory is a mandatory attribute of IfcContext (and all IFC root entities) per the IFC schema. The assertion is listed as 'depends_on' but it's actually a direct mandatory attribute of IfcContext (IfcContext.OwnerHistory). The phrasing 'depends_on' is imprecise and the 'conditions' clause unnecessarily suggests it's conditional when it is schema-mandatory for all IFC entities derived from IfcRoot.

subject: IfcContext
rationale: IfcContext provides the root context that supports the decomposition into sites, buildings, storeys, and spaces.
applicability: All building projects with spatial decomposition
conditions: When establishing a spatial hierarchy

subject: IfcContext
rationale: IfcContext serves as the root container supporting all IfcProduct instances placed within the project.
applicability: All IFC models containing building elements
conditions: All products placed within the project context

subject: IfcController
rationale: An IfcController typically sends control signals to an actuator (e.g., a valve actuator or damper actuator) to perform physical actions.
applicability: IfcController depends_on IfcActuator is stated with condition 'When the controller sends a control signal', but actuators are typically output devices that receive signals, not inputs the controller depends on. The controller 'actuates' or 'sends signal to' the actuator, rather than 'depends_on' which implies a dependency direction. The dependency direction may be inverted.
conditions: When the controller sends a control signal

subject: IfcController
rationale: Controllers frequently rely on sensor inputs (temperature, pressure, flow, etc.) to regulate systems.
conditions: For closed-loop control

subject: IfcController
rationale: Controllers may be directly associated with flow control devices like valves or dampers.
conditions: When controlling flow in HVAC or plumbing systems

subject: IfcController
rationale: Controllers need wiring (cables) for power and communication.
applicability: IfcController requires IfcCableSegment 'For signal transmission' - many modern controllers use wireless communication (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, LoRaWAN, Zigbee) and do not require a physical cable segment for signal transmission.
conditions: For signal transmission

subject: IfcController
rationale: A controller may contain or be composed of unitary control elements (e.g., a thermostat with an embedded controller).
conditions: When the controller is a unitary control device

subject: IfcController
rationale: Controllers may depend on switching devices (relays, contactors) to interface with high-power equipment.
conditions: When the controller needs to switch loads

subject: IfcControl
rationale: IfcControl relies on IfcRelAssignsToControl to link it to the objects it controls.
conditions: When establishing control relationships

subject: IfcControl
rationale: IfcControl may require constraint association relationships to define its control parameters.
conditions: When constraints are assigned to the control

subject: IfcControl
rationale: As an IFC root entity, IfcControl depends on IfcOwnerHistory for tracking creation and modification.
conditions: For traceability and ownership

subject: IfcControl
rationale: IfcControl often depends on property set definitions to specify control parameters like thresholds and setpoints.
conditions: When property sets define control parameters

subject: IfcControl
rationale: IfcCostSchedule is a subtype of IfcControl and contains cost-related control items.
conditions: When IfcControl is used for cost control

subject: IfcControl
rationale: IfcWorkPlan is a subtype of IfcControl, containing work schedule and task control information.
conditions: When IfcControl is used for project scheduling

subject: IfcControl
rationale: IfcPerformanceHistory is a subtype of IfcControl for recording performance over time.
conditions: When tracking actual vs required performance

subject: IfcControl
rationale: IfcPermit is a subtype of IfcControl for permit-related control.
conditions: When managing permits and approvals

subject: IfcControl
rationale: IfcControl supports building elements by providing regulation, constraint, or specification data.
conditions: When control relationships are assigned to building elements
exceptions: If the control is not relevant to the element type

subject: IfcControl
rationale: IfcControl supports building systems by defining control logic, setpoints, and operational parameters.
conditions: When controlling system performance

subject: IfcControl
rationale: IfcControl may use IfcRelAggregates to group sub-controls or control items hierarchically.
conditions: When the control has sub-controls or nested items

subject: IfcControl
rationale: IfcControl can be assigned to IfcGroup entities to control collections of objects collectively.
conditions: When controls are assigned to groups of objects

subject: IfcControl
rationale: IfcControl (as cost schedule) protects cost data from being exceeded by enforcing budget limits.
conditions: In cost control scenarios

subject: IfcControl
rationale: IfcControl (e.g., work plans, schedules) supports processes by defining constraints and milestones.
conditions: When controlling construction or facility management processes

subject: IfcControllerType
rationale: IfcControllerType defines the type information for IfcController instances — the controller instances depend on the type definition for their configuration and behavior.
conditions: When used in building management systems

subject: IfcControllerType
rationale: A controller type typically sends control signals to actuators to perform physical actions (e.g., open/close valves, dampers).
conditions: When control loops are closed via actuation

subject: IfcControllerType
rationale: Controllers depend on sensor input for reading environmental conditions (temperature, pressure, etc.) to make control decisions.
conditions: When feedback-based control is implemented

subject: IfcControllerType
rationale: IfcControllerType often references property set definitions to specify operational parameters, setpoints, and configuration data.
conditions: When detailed type properties are needed
exceptions: Simple controllers may use predefined types without custom property sets

The existing exception notes simple controllers may use predefined types without custom property sets. However, another exception exists: IfcControllerType can also reference IfcPreDefinedPropertySet via IfcRelDefinesByType without requiring an explicit IfcPropertySetDefinition, and in IFC2x3 and IFC4, certain predefined controller types (e.g., IfcControllerTypeEnum values like PROPORTIONAL, TWOPOSITION) inherently define their properties without requiring custom IfcPropertySetDefinition.

subject: IfcControllerType
rationale: Controller types are associated with distribution ports for communication and power connectivity.
conditions: When controller is networked or wired to other devices

subject: IfcControllerType
rationale: An IfcControllerType can contain property sets that define performance characteristics, control algorithms, and configuration parameters.

subject: IfcControllerType
rationale: Instances of IfcController are assigned to the IfcControllerType via IfcRelDefinesByType relationship; without this relationship the type has no instantiated controllers.

subject: IfcControllerType
rationale: Controller types can trigger or process alarm conditions based on sensor readings, supporting alarm functionality.
conditions: When the controller is used in safety or monitoring scenarios

subject: IfcControllerType
rationale: A controller type may depend on or be subordinated to unitary control elements in a control hierarchy (e.g., zone controllers vs. central controllers).
conditions: In hierarchical control architectures

subject: IfcConversionBasedUnit
rationale: IfcConversionBasedUnit must be assigned to a project via IfcUnitAssignment to be part of the unit system.
applicability: Any IFC model using conversion-based units
conditions: When used in an IFC model

subject: IfcConversionBasedUnit
rationale: IfcConversionBasedUnit relies on IfcMeasureWithUnit to define the conversion factor and base unit relationship.
conditions: When converting between units

subject: IfcConversionBasedUnit
rationale: IfcConversionBasedUnit uses IfcDimensionalExponents to define its physical dimension.
conditions: When the unit is derived from base SI units

subject: IfcConversionBasedUnit
rationale: IfcConversionBasedUnit references a base IfcSIUnit and a conversion factor to define itself.
applicability: When defining a unit derived from SI
conditions: As the base unit in the conversion relationship

subject: IfcConversionBasedUnit
rationale: IfcConversionBasedUnit is ultimately assigned to an IfcProject through IfcUnitAssignment.
applicability: All IFC projects using conversion units
conditions: When part of the project unit assignments

subject: IfcConversionBasedUnit
rationale: Conversion-based units allow quantities to be expressed in non-SI units (like imperial units) that downstream processes may require.
applicability: IfcConversionBasedUnit supports IfcQuantitySet is too vague. IfcQuantitySet physically contains IfcPhysicalQuantity instances which have a 'Unit' attribute of type IfcNamedUnit (which can be IfcConversionBasedUnit). The dependency is that IfcQuantitySet uses/references IfcConversionBasedUnit for its quantities, not that IfcConversionBasedUnit actively 'supports' IfcQuantitySet. The direction is that IfcQuantitySet references IfcConversionBasedUnit.
conditions: When quantities are expressed in conversion-based units

subject: IfcConversionBasedUnit
rationale: Property values may use IfcConversionBasedUnit as their unit type.
applicability: IfcConversionBasedUnit supports IfcPropertySingleValue is too vague. IfcPropertySingleValue has a 'Unit' attribute of type IfcUnit (which can be an IfcConversionBasedUnit via IfcNamedUnit). The relationship is that IfcPropertySingleValue may reference IfcConversionBasedUnit as its unit, not that IfcConversionBasedUnit actively 'supports' IfcPropertySingleValue. Also, IFC2x3 and IFC4 have different rules about when Unit can be defined at the property level vs inherited.
conditions: When property values use conversion-based units

subject: IfcConversionBasedUnitWithOffset
rationale: IfcConversionBasedUnitWithOffset is assigned via IfcUnitAssignment in an IFC model to define a conversion-based unit with an offset.
conditions: When the unit is assigned to a project or model

subject: IfcConversionBasedUnitWithOffset
rationale: IfcConversionBasedUnitWithOffset inherits from IfcConversionBasedUnit which uses IfcMeasureWithUnit to define the conversion factor.
conditions: For specifying the conversion factor and offset value

subject: IfcConversionBasedUnitWithOffset
rationale: IfcConversionBasedUnitWithOffset inherits from IfcNamedUnit which references IfcDimensionalExponents for unit dimension.
conditions: When dimensional exponents need to be specified

subject: IfcConversionBasedUnitWithOffset
rationale: IfcConversionBasedUnitWithOffset typically converts from a base SI unit to a derived unit with offset.
conditions: When the conversion is from an SI base unit
exceptions: Conversion from non-SI units

subject: IfcConversionBasedUnitWithOffset
rationale: The unit defined can be used as the unit for property single values in IFC models.
applicability: IfcPropertySingleValue uses IfcUnit (the abstract supertype) not IfcConversionBasedUnitWithOffset specifically. The assertion is too specific — any IfcUnit subtype can be used with IfcPropertySingleValue, not just conversion-based units with offset.
conditions: When property values are expressed using this unit

subject: IfcCooledBeamType
rationale: A cooled beam system depends on air terminals for ventilation air delivery, as chilled beams are typically hydronic devices that require a separate primary air system.
conditions: when used as active chilled beam

subject: IfcCooledBeamType
rationale: Cooled beams require chilled water supply, typically from a chiller plant.
applicability: The assertion states IfcCooledBeamType depends_on IfcChiller when connected to central chilled water system, with exception for decentralized refrigerant-based systems. However, a cooled beam connected to a central chilled water system might be served by a chiller plant that is modeled as IfcChillerType or could be served by a district cooling source where no IfcChiller entity exists in the local model. The dependency on IfcChiller is not universal even for hydronic systems.
conditions: when connected to central chilled water system
exceptions: decentralized refrigerant-based systems

subject: IfcCooledBeamType
rationale: Circulation pumps are necessary to move chilled water through the beam coils.
conditions: for hydronic chilled beam types

subject: IfcCooledBeamType
rationale: Piping is required to transport chilled water to and from the cooled beam.

subject: IfcCooledBeamType
rationale: A cooled beam must be part of a distribution system (e.g., chilled water or refrigerant loop) to function.
conditions: hydronic or refrigerant-based

subject: IfcCooledBeamType
rationale: Ductwork delivers primary air to active chilled beams for induction.
conditions: for primary air supply to active chilled beams
exceptions: passive chilled beams which do not require ducted primary air

subject: IfcCooledBeamType
rationale: A cooled beam internally contains a fin-and-tube heat exchanger (coil) to transfer heat between the chilled water and room air.

subject: IfcCooledBeamType
rationale: Pipe fittings such as connections, valves, and manifolds are integral parts of the cooled beam assembly.

subject: IfcCooledBeamType
rationale: The cooled beam supports the conditioned space by removing sensible heat loads.
applicability: IfcCooledBeamType supports IfcSpace is asserted when providing sensible cooling to conditioned zone. However, the relationship 'supports' in IFC implies a structural or hosting relationship (e.g., IfcColumn supports IfcSlab). A cooled beam does not structurally support a space; it services or conditions the space. The correct IFC relationship would be 'serves' (IfcRelServicesBuildings) or 'assigns' to space, not 'supports'.
conditions: when providing sensible cooling to the conditioned zone

subject: IfcCooledBeamType
rationale: Mounting brackets, hangers, or support structures are needed to physically install the cooled beam.
conditions: for mounting and structural support

subject: IfcCooledBeamType
rationale: Acoustic silencers may partially conflict with airflow performance if not properly integrated.
applicability: active cooled beams in noise-sensitive spaces
conditions: when acoustic treatment is placed too close to active beam air nozzles
exceptions: properly designed duct layouts with sufficient distance

subject: IfcCoordinateOperation
rationale: IfcCoordinateOperation transforms coordinates between coordinate reference systems; it requires IfcCartesianPoint to define source and target coordinate origins.
applicability: all building projects using coordinate transformations
conditions: for defining coordinate reference system origin

subject: IfcCoordinateOperation
rationale: The entity specifically defines an operation between two coordinate reference systems (source and target CRS).
applicability: all building projects using coordinate transformations
conditions: for transformation between coordinate systems

subject: IfcCoordinateOperation
rationale: Coordinate operations are used to place building elements within geometric representation contexts.
applicability: BIM models with multiple coordinate contexts
conditions: when transforming geometric representations of building elements

subject: IfcCoordinateOperation
rationale: IfcMapConversion is a subtype of IfcCoordinateOperation used for converting between projected coordinate systems.
applicability: site and infrastructure projects requiring geolocation
conditions: when converting from a local engineering CRS to a global map CRS

subject: IfcCoordinateOperation
rationale: IfcCoordinateOperation supports transformation to/from projected coordinate reference systems for site positioning.
conditions: when map projection transformations are needed

subject: IfcCoordinateOperation
rationale: Coordinate operations enable proper geolocation of IfcSite elements in global coordinate systems.
applicability: IfcCoordinateOperation does not directly support IfcSite. IfcSite can be associated with a coordinate operation through IfcObjectPlacement and IfcLocalPlacement/IfcGridPlacement with a transformation, but there is no direct containment or support relationship between IfcCoordinateOperation and IfcSite in the IFC schema.
conditions: when positioning the site in global coordinates

subject: IfcCoordinateOperation
rationale: Coordinate operations support accurate placement of buildings within coordinate reference systems.
applicability: all BIM projects with defined coordinate systems

IfcCoordinateOperation does not directly support IfcBuilding. Similar to IfcSite, IfcBuilding inherits its coordinate context through IfcObjectPlacement and spatial containment hierarchy, not through a direct relationship with IfcCoordinateOperation.
conditions: when transforming building coordinates between local and global systems

subject: IfcCoordinateOperation
rationale: Coordinate operations may contain or reference conversion-based unit definitions for proper measurement transformations.
conditions: when unit conversions are part of the coordinate transformation

subject: IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem
rationale: A projected CRS requires a map projection definition (e.g., mapping from geodetic to Cartesian coordinates) which is defined by IfcProjectedCRS.
applicability: Projects using projected coordinates like UTM or State Plane
conditions: When the CRS is a projected coordinate system (map projection)
exceptions: Not needed for geographic (latitude/longitude) or engineering CRS

subject: IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem
rationale: IfcMapConversion defines the transformation parameters (translation, rotation, scale) between the engineering CRS of the IFC model and the geographic/projected CRS.
applicability: Projects combining local engineering coordinates with global coordinates
conditions: When converting between engineering and projected/geographic CRS
exceptions: Not needed if only one CRS type is used

subject: IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem
rationale: IfcCoordinateOperation defines the mathematical transformation between two coordinate reference systems, necessary for converting coordinates between CRS.
conditions: When coordinate transformations between different CRS are needed

subject: IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem
rationale: IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem provides the reference system that gives meaning to the coordinates of an IfcSite, enabling geolocation of the building.
applicability: All building projects with site location data
conditions: When the site has georeferenced coordinates

subject: IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem
rationale: The CRS provides the spatial reference frame that gives geographic meaning to the building's placement within the site.
conditions: When the building position is defined in world coordinates

subject: IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem
rationale: IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem is referenced by IfcMapConversion to define the source and target CRS during coordinate transformations.

subject: IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem
rationale: The geometric representation context in IFC can reference a coordinate reference system to align the local engineering coordinates with a global CRS.
conditions: When the geometric representation uses world coordinates

subject: IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem
rationale: IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem is assigned to an IfcProject through the IfcRelAssociatesCRS relationship, linking the CRS definition to the overall project context.

subject: IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem
rationale: A coordinate reference system may depend on unit definitions (e.g., meters, degrees) to properly interpret coordinate values, typically defined as IfcNamedUnit.
applicability: Projects using units other than default
conditions: When the CRS needs explicit unit definitions for coordinates

subject: IfcCostItem
rationale: IfcCostItem is typically aggregated into IfcCostSchedule for meaningful project cost control; the schema defines cost items as entries within schedules.
conditions: when cost data needs to be organized and structured
exceptions: standalone cost items may exist without a schedule in informal contexts

subject: IfcCostItem
rationale: IfcCostItem uses IfcCostValue to represent the actual cost amount per unit or total, making it essential for proper function.
conditions: when a monetary amount or quantity is assigned to a cost line
exceptions: if the cost item is used only as a placeholder without a value

subject: IfcCostItem
rationale: Cost items often reference quantity sets to tie costs to physical work amounts, enabling accurate cost estimation.
conditions: when cost is calculated based on measured quantities of work
exceptions: lump-sum cost items may not need separate quantities

subject: IfcCostItem
rationale: IfcCostItem commonly references IfcConstructionResource to trace costs to specific construction resources used.
conditions: when cost items represent labor, material, or equipment costs
exceptions: purely monetary budget lines may not reference resources

subject: IfcCostItem
rationale: IfcCostItem can be associated with processes (e.g., IfcTask) to support cost tracking per activity.
conditions: when costs are linked to construction or design processes
exceptions: if the cost item is used purely for reporting without process linkage

subject: IfcCostItem
rationale: The IfcCostItem entity can contain nested IfcCostValue sub-entities for detailed cost breakdown.
conditions: when multiple cost values (e.g., base cost, tax, contingency) are grouped under one item
exceptions: single-value cost items may use direct attributes instead of contained values

subject: IfcCostItem
rationale: IfcCostItem provides cost data that supports the financial planning and tracking of building elements like walls, slabs, etc.
conditions: when cost items are assigned to building elements for cost estimation

subject: IfcCostItem
rationale: Cost items can support budget control for proxy elements representing non-standard building components.
conditions: when cost containment is needed for generic or custom building elements

subject: IfcCostSchedule
rationale: IfcCostSchedule groups IfcCostItem entities, which represent individual cost line items within the schedule.
conditions: When detailed cost breakdown is needed

subject: IfcCostSchedule
rationale: An IfcCostSchedule contains multiple IfcCostItem entities that break down the costs.

subject: IfcCostSchedule
rationale: IfcCostSchedule can be linked to IfcWorkSchedule to map costs to construction tasks and time phasing.
conditions: When cost control is integrated with construction planning

subject: IfcCostSchedule
rationale: IfcCostSchedule is typically assigned to a specific IfcProject via IfcRelDeclares relationship.
exceptions: IfcCostSchedule does not directly 'connect_to' IfcProject in the IFC schema. IfcCostSchedule is part of a project via IfcRelAggregates (project aggregates controls) or through IfcRelDeclares. The relationship is an aggregation/declaration relationship, not a direct connection as implied.

subject: IfcCostSchedule
rationale: Property sets associated via IfcRelDefinesByProperties define key attributes of the cost schedule.
conditions: When property sets define schedule attributes like currency, status

subject: IfcCostSchedule
rationale: IfcCostSchedule supports the overall project by providing cost management and budget tracking.

subject: IfcCostSchedule
rationale: IfcCostSchedule may depend on assignment of responsible actors via IfcRelAssignsToControl.
conditions: When cost schedule is assigned to a responsible person or organization

subject: IfcCostSchedule
rationale: The schedule depends on IfcCostValue entities which hold the monetary amounts and rates for cost items.

subject: IfcCostSchedule
rationale: IfcCostSchedule can contain applied values representing costs and rates.

subject: IfcCostValue
rationale: IfcCostValue is a subtype of IfcAppliedValue and inherits its relationship to cost schedules and assignments to products, tasks, or resources.
conditions: when assigning cost information to elements

subject: IfcCostValue
rationale: IfcCostValue instances are typically aggregated within IfcCostSchedule to form cost estimates, budgets, or tenders.
conditions: when the cost value is part of a structured cost estimate or budget

subject: IfcCostValue
rationale: IfcCostValue's AppliedValue can be defined using IfcMeasureWithUnit for explicit cost rates per unit.
conditions: when a cost value is expressed as a quantity with a unit
exceptions: IfcCostValue can also have a cost expressed without an IfcMeasureWithUnit (e.g., using a simple string or a category reference). The condition 'when a cost value is expressed as a quantity with a unit' already covers this, but the assertion as stated does not reflect that IfcMeasureWithUnit is optional in the schema (the AppliedValue attribute is an IfcMetricValue that may or may not have a unit).

subject: IfcCostValue
rationale: IfcCostValue provides the numeric cost data that supports IfcCostItem (cost types) in cost planning and control.
conditions: when cost values are assigned to cost items for project cost control

subject: IfcCostValue
rationale: IfcCostValue can represent the base cost of construction resources, supporting resource costing in a project.
conditions: when resource costs are estimated for labor, material, or equipment

subject: IfcCostValue
rationale: IfcCostValue can be related to IfcProduct via IfcRelDefinesByProperties or IfcRelAssociatesAppliedValue, supporting element-level cost tracking.
conditions: when cost values are assigned to building elements/products for cost estimation

subject: IfcCoveringType
rationale: IfcCoveringType defines a type of covering (e.g., cladding, flooring, roofing) which may be composed of material layers; the IFC schema allows association with material layer sets.
conditions: when defining layered coverings

subject: IfcCoveringType
rationale: IfcCoveringType depends on material association via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial to define its physical composition in the IFC data model.
conditions: when material information is assigned

subject: IfcCoveringType
rationale: IfcCoveringType serves as the type definition that defines common properties for IfcCovering occurrences.
conditions: as a type definition for covering instances

subject: IfcCoveringType
rationale: Covering types such as cladding or roofing protect structural elements from weather and environmental exposure.
conditions: when applied as cladding or weatherproofing

subject: IfcCoveringType
rationale: IfcCoveringType can contain multiple material layers when associated with a material layer set.
conditions: when the covering type is defined with layers

subject: IfcCoveringType
rationale: IfcCoveringType requires IfcRelDefinesByType relationship to associate itself with instances of IfcCovering.
conditions: to link type to occurrences

subject: IfcCoveringType
rationale: IfcCoveringType depends on property set definitions to specify its non-geometric properties.
conditions: when custom properties are defined for the type

subject: IfcCoveringType
rationale: Wall cladding coverings connect to wall elements physically.
conditions: when the covering type is a wall cladding type

subject: IfcCoveringType
rationale: Flooring and ceiling coverings connect to slab elements.
conditions: when the covering type is a flooring or ceiling type

subject: IfcCoveringType
rationale: Covering types with insulation layers contribute to thermal performance of the building envelope.
applicability: 'IfcCoveringType supports Thermal Insulation' is not a standard IFC relationship or property. IfcCoveringType does not directly 'support' thermal insulation as a relationship; rather, thermal insulation properties may be defined via IfcMaterialLayer (within a layer set) assigned to the covering. The phrasing implies a functional relationship that is not modeled explicitly in IFC.
conditions: when the covering includes insulation layers

subject: IfcCovering
rationale: IfcCovering requires an IfcElement to be applied to, as coverings are always associated with a host element.
conditions: when functioning as a building element covering

subject: IfcCovering
rationale: The material layering defines the covering's functional properties like thermal resistance and fire rating.
applicability: IfcCovering can depend_on IfcMaterialLayer (single material layer, not necessarily IfcMaterialLayerSet). The assertion excludes the case where a single IfcMaterialLayer is used directly.
conditions: when covering has layered material composition

subject: IfcCovering
rationale: Some coverings like metal decking can support loads above them, but most coverings are non-structural.
conditions: when used as a structural deck or subfloor
exceptions: does not apply to finishes or claddings

subject: IfcCovering
rationale: IfcCovering can be composed of one or more materials including coatings, tiles, panels, or continuous layers.
applicability: IfcCovering relates to IfcMaterial through IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, but it can also be associated with IfcMaterialLayerSet (which aggregates IfcMaterial). The direct 'contains IfcMaterial' relationship is imprecise - the association is via IfcMaterialLayerSet or IfcMaterialLayer, not a direct containment in most IFC schemas.
conditions: when covering is assigned material properties

subject: IfcCovering
rationale: The relationship entity IfcRelCoversBldgElements formalizes the connection between a covering and the element it covers.
conditions: for IFC model connectivity

subject: IfcCovering
rationale: Certain coverings (e.g., insulated metal panels, exterior insulation finish systems) improve the building envelope thermal performance.
conditions: when covering has insulating properties
exceptions: non-insulating coverings like paint or thin tiles

subject: IfcCovering
rationale: IfcCovering instances are typically connected to walls via IfcRelCoversBldgElements.
conditions: when covering is applied to a wall

IfcBooleanResult in turn contains IfcCsgPrimitive3D operands. So IfcCsgSolid contains a Boolean result only at the root level, not as multiple nested containment. The TreeRootExpression can be an IfcBooleanResult, whose Operands are IfcCsgPrimitive3D instances or nested IfcBooleanResults. So the primitive appears at leaves of the Boolean tree, not directly in the IfcCsgSolid. The assertion incorrectly states 'IfcCsgSolid contains IfcCsgPrimitive3D always' whereas it should say 'IfcCsgSolid contains primitives indirectly via IfcBooleanResult in complex cases'.
