subject: IfcDamperType
rationale: Dampers are components of HVAC distribution systems (air distribution subsystem)
applicability: all building types with mechanical systems
conditions: any HVAC or ventilation system
exceptions: Not all dampers depend on IfcDistributionSystem. Fire dampers in fire-rated separations may be part of a fire safety system rather than an HVAC distribution system, especially when installed purely for passive fire protection without being connected to the mechanical system.

subject: IfcDamperType
rationale: Dampers can be nested subcomponents of larger equipment like VAV boxes
conditions: when damper is part of an assembly (e.g., VAV box assembly)
exceptions: standalone damper installation

subject: IfcDerivedProfileDef
rationale: IfcDerivedProfileDef is a subtype of IfcProfileDef and must reference a parent profile (IfcProfileDef) via its ParentProfile attribute to define the base profile being modified.
conditions: When IfcDerivedProfileDef is used to define a profile derived from an existing profile
exceptions: IfcDerivedProfileDef is a subtype of IfcProfileDef itself, so the depends_on relationship is also recursive — IfcDerivedProfileDef can have another IfcDerivedProfileDef as its ParentProfile, not just a base IfcProfileDef. This is not an exception per se but should be clarified.

subject: IfcDerivedProfileDef
rationale: IfcDerivedProfileDef uses an Operator attribute of type IfcCartesianTransformationOperator2D to define the geometric transformation (translation, rotation, scaling) applied to the parent profile.
conditions: When transformation operations are applied to derive the profile

subject: IfcDerivedProfileDef
rationale: IfcDerivedProfileDef can be used as the profile definition for IfcSweptAreaSolid and its subtypes (e.g., IfcExtrudedAreaSolid) to create 3D geometries by sweeping the derived profile along a path.
applicability: All building types using swept solid geometry
conditions: When used as the profile for extrusion or sweeping operations

subject: IfcDerivedProfileDef
rationale: The derived profile can be used in IfcRevolvedAreaSolid to create solids of revolution.
applicability: All building types using revolved geometry
conditions: When the derived profile is revolved around an axis

subject: IfcDerivedProfileDef
rationale: IfcDerivedProfileDef contributes to the shape representation (IfcShapeRepresentation) of building elements by defining the 2D profile used in swept area representations.
conditions: When the derived profile is included in a shape representation of a building element

subject: IfcDerivedUnit
rationale: IfcDerivedUnit must be assigned to a project via IfcUnitAssignment to be part of an IFC model.
applicability: All IFC models using derived units
conditions: When derived units are used in an IFC model

subject: IfcDerivedUnit
rationale: Derived units are typically composed from base SI units (e.g., m, kg, s) as defined in IFC schema.
applicability: All IFC models using derived units with SI base units
conditions: When derived units are based on SI units

subject: IfcDerivedUnit
rationale: Derived units can also be composed from conversion-based units in the IFC schema.
applicability: All IFC models using derived units with conversion-based base units
conditions: When derived units are based on conversion-based units

subject: IfcDerivedUnit
rationale: IfcDerivedUnit is composed of a list of IfcDerivedUnitElement items, each defining a unit and its exponent.
conditions: Always

subject: IfcDerivedUnit
rationale: Derived units can be referenced by quantity elements to define measured values in derived units.
applicability: All IFC models with element quantities using derived units
conditions: When element quantities use derived units

subject: IfcDerivedUnitElement
rationale: IfcDerivedUnitElement is always part of an IfcDerivedUnit, which is assigned via IfcUnitAssignment to define units in an IFC model.
applicability: all IFC models using derived units
conditions: when used in an IfcMeasureWithUnit context

subject: IfcDerivedUnitElement
rationale: IfcDerivedUnitElement is a constituent part of an IfcDerivedUnit, so it functionally depends on being aggregated into a derived unit definition.
applicability: all IFC models with derived units
conditions: when used to define complex units

subject: IfcDerivedUnitElement
rationale: A derived unit element typically references a base SI unit (via IfcUnitEnum) to define its unit type before applying an exponent.
applicability: IFC models using metric SI units
conditions: when the derived unit is based on SI units
exceptions: when using imperial or other non-SI base units

subject: IfcDerivedUnitElement
rationale: IfcDerivedUnitElement helps define derived units (e.g., m/s², N/m²) which are used in IfcMeasureWithUnit to express measured quantities in building models.
applicability: quantity take-off, cost estimation, energy analysis

The 'supports' relationship is too indirect. IfcDerivedUnitElement itself is a simple entity defining a factor and a base unit within a derived unit. It does not directly interface with IfcMeasureWithUnit — rather, IfcDerivedUnit (the container) is used within IfcMeasureWithUnit for quantities. IfcDerivedUnitElement alone has no direct role in 'expressing physical quantities in derived units' — this role is played by IfcDerivedUnit as a whole combined with IfcMeasureWithUnit.
conditions: when used to express physical quantities in derived units

subject: IfcDimensionalExponents
rationale: IfcDimensionalExponents defines the exponents of base SI units (e.g., length, mass, time) that are used within IfcUnitAssignment to define derived units. Without IfcUnitAssignment, the dimensional exponents have no context.
conditions: when dimensional exponents need to be associated with units

subject: IfcDimensionalExponents
rationale: IfcDimensionalExponents is a direct attribute of IfcDerivedUnit, providing the dimensional representation (exponents for each base SI unit) that defines how a derived unit is composed from base units.
applicability: all IFC models using derived units
conditions: when defining derived units from base units

subject: IfcDimensionalExponents
rationale: IfcDimensionalExponents provides the dimensional analysis foundation that ensures IfcMeasureWithUnit values are dimensionally consistent across the model.
applicability: all IFC models with quantified properties
conditions: when expressing measured quantities with specific units

subject: IfcDimensionalExponents
rationale: IfcDimensionalExponents provides the dimensional exponents that define the base SI dimension of a conversion-based unit.
applicability: ifcConversionBasedUnit has a 'Dimensions' attribute of type IfcDimensionalExponents, so the assertion is correct in that it connects to IfcConversionBasedUnit. However, 'supports' is vague — the dimension exponents are a mandatory attribute in the definition of IfcConversionBasedUnit, not merely a validation aid. The dimensional exponents are part of the unit definition itself.
conditions: when defining conversion-based units with dimensional validation

subject: IfcDimensionalExponents
rationale: IfcDimensionalExponents connects to IfcSIUnit by verifying that SI units have the correct dimensional exponents for their type.
applicability: IfcSIUnit also has a 'Dimensions' attribute of type IfcDimensionalExponents (inherited from IfcNamedUnit), so the 'connects_to' relationship is valid. However, the attribute is optional (OPTIONAL Dimensions) in IfcNamedUnit, meaning the connection is not always present. The assertion should clarify that the connection is conditional on the Dimensions attribute being defined.
conditions: when SI units need dimensional validation

subject: IfcDirection
rationale: IfcDirection often depends on IfcVector for representation in geometric contexts, as direction can be expressed as a unit vector.
conditions: when representing a direction as a normalized vector

subject: IfcDirection
rationale: IfcDirection direction ratios are interpreted in the context of a coordinate system that references IfcCartesianPoint origins.
conditions: when direction is defined by direction ratios relative to a coordinate system

subject: IfcDirection
rationale: IfcDirection is used as RefDirection or Axis in IfcAxis2Placement3D for positioning objects in 3D space.
conditions: when used in 3D placement contexts

subject: IfcDirection
rationale: IfcDirection is used as RefDirection in IfcAxis2Placement2D for positioning objects in 2D space.
conditions: when used in 2D placement contexts

subject: IfcDirection
rationale: IfcDirection provides the directional component for IfcLocalPlacement, enabling objects to be oriented in 3D space.
conditions: when defining the orientation of objects relative to a local coordinate system

subject: IfcDirection
rationale: IfcDirection can represent true north or other directional references within a project's geometric representation context.
conditions: when defining the direction of the true north or other reference directions within a geometric representation context

subject: IfcDirection
rationale: IfcDirection defines the extrusion direction for IfcExtrudedAreaSolid, determining how shapes are extruded.
conditions: when direction is used as the extrusion direction parameter

subject: IfcDirection
rationale: IfcDirection specifies the axis direction for revolution of a swept area to form a solid.
conditions: when direction defines the axis of revolution

subject: IfcDirection
rationale: IfcDirection is a subtype of IfcGeometricRepresentationItem, which in turn is a subtype of IfcRepresentationItem, inheriting properties from the representation item hierarchy.
conditions: when inherited as a geometric representation item

subject: IfcDirection
rationale: IfcDirection can provide orientation for proxy elements that need directional placement in the building model.
conditions: when a building element proxy requires orientation in the model

subject: IfcDirection
rationale: IfcDirection supports the orientation of slabs (e.g., sloped slabs) by providing directional information in their placement.
conditions: when defining the orientation or placement of slabs in a building structure

subject: IfcDirection
rationale: IfcDirection can define roof slope directions, important for drainage and structural orientation.
conditions: when defining roof slope direction or orientation

subject: IfcDirection
rationale: IfcDirection can define the direction of IfcGridAxis elements in a building design grid layout.
conditions: when defining the direction of grid axes in a design grid

subject: IfcDiscreteAccessory
rationale: Discrete accessories are used at connection interfaces between beams and other elements.
applicability: The conditions restrict to beam-to-beam or beam-to-column connections, but IfcDiscreteAccessory can also connect a beam to other elements such as walls or foundations (e.g., beam bearing plates on masonry walls). The assertion is too narrow in its stated conditions.
conditions: At beam-to-beam or beam-to-column connections

subject: IfcDiscreteAccessory
rationale: Discrete accessories such as base plates and splice plates connect columns to foundations or join column segments.
applicability: The conditions restrict to column base plates or column splices, but IfcDiscreteAccessory can also connect columns to beams at moment connections (e.g., shear tabs, clip angles) which are neither base plates nor splices. The condition is too restrictive.
conditions: At column base plates or column splices

subject: IfcDiscreteAccessory
rationale: Anchor bolts and base plates anchor structural members to concrete foundations.
applicability: The conditions restrict to anchor bolts or bearing plates at base connections, but discrete accessories can also connect a foundation to other elements such as embedded plates for column base connections or hold-down anchors in shear wall to foundation connections which are not strictly 'anchor bolts or bearing plates'.
conditions: When used as anchor bolts or bearing plates at base connections

subject: IfcDiscreteAccessoryType
rationale: Discrete accessories like gusset plates and brackets connect beams and columns (IfcMember elements).
conditions: in structural steel connections
exceptions: IfcDiscreteAccessoryType instances such as anchor rods, bolts, or washers in a steel connection may connect to IfcElementAssembly (e.g., a built-up column or truss) rather than directly to a single IfcMember.

subject: IfcDiscreteAccessoryType
rationale: Discrete accessories are often used in conjunction with fasteners to form a complete connection assembly.
conditions: when used together in a bolted connection
exceptions: In welded connections or adhesive connections, IfcDiscreteAccessoryType (e.g., a gusset plate or bracket) does not connect to IfcFastener because no fasteners are present. The assertion should note this exception.

subject: IfcDistributionChamberElement
rationale: Below-grade distribution chambers must be waterproofed to prevent water ingress that could damage equipment.
applicability: all building types with below-grade spaces
conditions: when chamber is below grade
when chamber is in contact with soil or groundwater
exceptions: above-grade chambers in dry interior locations

A distribution chamber that is intentionally designed to allow groundwater ingress (e.g., a 'wet pit' for sump pumps or a drainage collection chamber) may not 'depend on' waterproofing – it may be designed with drainage and pumping instead. The assertion treats waterproofing as a dependency, but some chambers are designed to be wet and rely on active dewatering.

subject: IfcDistributionCircuit
rationale: IfcDistributionCircuit represents a logical grouping of distribution elements and typically contains distribution ports that serve as connection points.

subject: IfcDistributionCircuit
rationale: An IfcDistributionCircuit groups distribution flow elements (such as pipes, ducts, cables) that together form a logical circuit.

subject: IfcDistributionCircuit
rationale: IfcDistributionCircuit is typically a sub-grouping within an IfcDistributionSystem and connects to the overall system.
applicability: The relationship 'connects_to' is ambiguous in IFC. IfcDistributionCircuit relates to IfcDistributionSystem via IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure or indirectly through assigned elements. This is not a direct connection but a logical grouping relationship. The condition 'when the circuit is part of a larger network' is too vague to properly constrain this.
conditions: when the circuit is part of a larger network

subject: IfcDistributionCircuit
rationale: The circuit depends on relationship entities to define how its constituent elements are connected physically.
applicability: IfcDistributionCircuit does not directly 'depend_on' IfcRelConnectsElements. That relationship connects individual elements (e.g., two IfcDistributionFlowElements). The circuit itself is related to its members via IfcRelAssignsToGroup, not via IfcRelConnectsElements. The assertion confuses element-level relationships with circuit-level relationships.
conditions: when physical connectivity between elements must be represented

subject: IfcDistributionCircuit
rationale: The circuit depends on assignment relationships to link its member distribution elements.
applicability: While IfcRelAssignsToGroup is indeed the correct way to assign elements to an IfcDistributionCircuit (via the Inherited 'IsGroupedBy' inverse relationship), the phrasing 'depends_on' is vague. This is a defining relationship (membership), not a dependency. The condition correctly identifies logical assignment but the relationship type name is misleading.
conditions: when elements are logically assigned to the circuit

subject: IfcDistributionCircuit
rationale: A distribution circuit requires actual distribution elements (cables, pipes, ducts) to exist as a functional circuit.

subject: IfcDistributionCircuit
rationale: Flow segments such as pipes, ducts, or cable carrier segments are required components for a functional distribution circuit.
conditions: when the circuit includes pipe/duct/cable runs

subject: IfcDistributionChamberElementType
rationale: Distribution chamber elements are typically nested within larger distribution systems through aggregation relationships.
applicability: IfcDistributionChamberElementType inherits from IfcDistributionFlowElementType, which already uses IfcRelNests to relate to property sets. The assertion that it 'depends_on IfcRelNests' when aggregated into a larger distribution system is misleading because IfcRelNests is typically used for type decomposition (e.g., sub-element types), not for aggregation into a distribution system. Aggregation into a system is handled by IfcRelConnectsElements or IfcDistributionSystem via IfcRelAssignsToGroup, not IfcRelNests.
conditions: when aggregated into a larger distribution system

subject: IfcDistributionChamberElementType
rationale: Distribution chambers connect to distribution ports (inlets/outlets) for cables, pipes, or ducts passing through the chamber.
conditions: at entry and exit points for distribution flow
exceptions: IfcDistributionChamberElementType is an object type definition (a type product), not an occurrence. IfcDistributionPort is an occurrence (subtype of IfcPort). In IFC, IfcRelConnectsPorts connects ports to distribution elements, and the port is typically related to the element occurrence, not the element type. An IfcDistributionChamberElementType cannot directly 'connect_to' an IfcDistributionPort because ports are related to occurrences (IfcDistributionChamberElement), not types.

subject: IfcDistributionChamberElementType
rationale: The type definition depends on material definitions to specify construction materials (concrete, metal, plastic, etc.) for the chamber.
applicability: IfcDistributionChamberElementType can use IfcMaterialDefinition through material layers or material constituents assigned via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, but this is a generic capability of any IfcElementType, not a specific dependency unique to distribution chamber element types. The assertion implies a specific dependency relationship that is neither exclusive nor architecturally distinct for this type.
conditions: for defining the material composition of the chamber type

subject: IfcDistributionControlElementType
rationale: As a type entity, IfcDistributionControlElementType defines the common properties for distribution control element occurrences (IfcDistributionControlElement).
conditions: For functional deployment as a type definition

subject: IfcDistributionControlElementType
rationale: Types can contain property set definitions that define shared properties for all occurrences.
conditions: When property sets are assigned to the type

subject: IfcDistributionControlElementType
rationale: The relationship object IfcRelDefinesByType links type definitions to their occurrences.
conditions: For establishing the type-occurrence relationship

subject: IfcDistributionControlElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionControlElementType is the parent type for specializations like IfcSensorType, IfcActuatorType, IfcAlarmType, IfcControllerType, IfcFlowInstrumentType, IfcProtectiveDeviceTrippingUnitType.
conditions: When the distribution control element type is specifically a sensor type

subject: IfcDistributionControlElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionControlElementType is the parent type for specialization IfcActuatorType.
conditions: When the distribution control element type is specifically an actuator type

subject: IfcDistributionControlElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionControlElementType is the parent type for specialization IfcAlarmType.
conditions: When the distribution control element type is specifically an alarm type

subject: IfcDistributionControlElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionControlElementType is the parent type for specialization IfcControllerType.
conditions: When the distribution control element type is specifically a controller type

subject: IfcDistributionControlElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionControlElementType is the parent type for specialization IfcFlowInstrumentType.
conditions: When the distribution control element type is specifically a flow instrument type

subject: IfcDistributionControlElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionControlElementType is the parent type for specialization IfcProtectiveDeviceTrippingUnitType.
conditions: When the distribution control element type is specifically a protective device tripping unit type

subject: IfcDistributionControlElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionControlElementType inherits from IfcDistributionElementType, requiring the distribution element hierarchy.
conditions: For inheritance of distribution element properties

subject: IfcDistributionControlElementType
rationale: Inherits from IfcTypeProduct through IfcDistributionElementType, which defines the general type mechanism.
conditions: As part of the type hierarchy

subject: IfcDistributionControlElementType
rationale: Types can have associated materials via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial.
conditions: When materials are assigned to the type

subject: IfcDistributionControlElementType
rationale: Distribution control elements may connect to distribution ports for signal or power connections within a distribution system.
conditions: When the control element type has ports for logical or physical connections

subject: IfcDistributionControlElement
rationale: IfcDistributionControlElement is a subtype of IfcDistributionElement and is designed to participate in an IfcDistributionSystem, controlling distribution of energy, media, or signals.
conditions: when functioning as part of building services distribution

subject: IfcDistributionControlElement
rationale: Control elements regulate the operation of energy conversion devices like boilers, chillers, or transformers.
conditions: when controlling energy distribution

subject: IfcDistributionControlElement
rationale: Control elements often require flow controllers (dampers, valves) to regulate flow based on control signals.
conditions: when managing flow of media such as air or water

subject: IfcDistributionControlElement
rationale: Control elements typically depend on sensors to provide feedback on temperature, pressure, humidity, or occupancy.
conditions: for closed-loop control
exceptions: simple open-loop control systems

subject: IfcDistributionControlElement
rationale: Control elements output signals to actuators, which physically move or adjust controlled devices.
conditions: when physical movement of a device is required
exceptions: software-based control only

subject: IfcDistributionControlElement
rationale: IfcDistributionControlElement includes controllers that implement control logic and algorithms.
conditions: when logic-based regulation of processes is needed

subject: IfcDistributionControlElement
rationale: Alarms are triggered by or inform control elements to signal abnormal states.
conditions: for monitoring and alerting on abnormal conditions

subject: IfcDistributionControlElement
rationale: Control elements may be mounted on or integrated into duct segments or pipe segments.
conditions: when part of a fluid or airflow system

subject: IfcDistributionControlElement
rationale: Control elements may be associated with flow terminals to modulate output to zones.
applicability: The assertion uses 'connects_to' rather than 'depends_on,' which shifts the relationship type. However, IfcDistributionControlElement does not typically 'connect_to' IfcFlowTerminal in a spatial or port-connection sense — control elements are usually connected via IfcRelFlowControlElements or control relationships (IfcRelAssignsToControl), not physical connection. The relationship type is inconsistent with the other assertions.
conditions: when controlling terminal units like VAV boxes or diffusers

subject: IfcDistributionElementType
rationale: As a type definition in IFC, IfcDistributionElementType defines types for IfcDistributionElement occurrences. The 'Type' contains the common properties and templates for distribution elements.

subject: IfcDistributionElementType
rationale: Distribution elements typically belong to distribution systems (e.g., HVAC, electrical, plumbing). IfcDistributionElementType defines the type for elements that are part of such systems.
conditions: When part of a building services network

subject: IfcDistributionElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionElementType can have property set definitions assigned to it, which define the specific properties of the distribution element type.
conditions: For defining specific type properties

subject: IfcDistributionElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionElementType participates in the IfcRelDefinesByType relationship to assign the type definition to individual distribution element occurrences.
conditions: When type is assigned to occurrences

subject: IfcDistributionElementType
rationale: Distribution elements are typically contained within spatial structures like building stories or zones.
conditions: When spatial containment is required for placement
exceptions: Standalone distribution elements not requiring spatial context

IfcDistributionElementType itself is a type definition and does not have spatial placement. Spatial containment (IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure) applies to IfcDistributionElement occurrences, not the type definition. The type does not require spatial context; only its occurrences do.

subject: IfcDistributionElementType
rationale: Distribution elements (like pipes, ducts, cables) connect to other elements via IfcPort. The type defines the connection characteristics.
conditions: When distribution element has connectivity requirements
exceptions: Elements that are stand-alone without connections

subject: IfcDistributionElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionElementType can have material definitions associated via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, containing the material specification for the type.
conditions: When material information is defined at the type level

subject: IfcDistributionElement
rationale: IfcDistributionElement is designed to participate in an IfcDistributionSystem, requiring connection to a system for proper operation.
applicability: The assertion states IfcDistributionElement depends_on IfcDistributionSystem, but in IFC schema, IfcDistributionElement is a subtype of IfcElement and can exist without being assigned to any IfcDistributionSystem via IfcRelAssignsToGroup. Many distribution elements are modeled in isolation during early design phases before system assignment.
conditions: when functioning as part of building service distribution
exceptions: standalone distribution elements not connected to a system

subject: IfcDistributionElement
rationale: Distribution elements typically require IfcPorts for logical connectivity to other elements in a distribution network.
applicability: The assertion says IfcDistributionElement depends_on IfcPort, but in IFC, IfcPort is connected via IfcRelConnectsPortToElement which is optional. Many distribution elements (e.g., simple duct runs, pipes) can be modeled without explicit port definitions, especially in early design or when using simplified representations.
conditions: when needing to connect to other distribution elements or systems
exceptions: simple pass-through elements without connectivity

subject: IfcDistributionElement
rationale: Distribution elements often need terminals like diffusers, outlets, or fixtures to deliver the distributed medium.
conditions: when part of HVAC, plumbing, or electrical distribution
exceptions: structural distribution elements without terminals

subject: IfcDistributionElement
rationale: Flow segments such as ducts, pipes, and cables are fundamental components for distribution elements to transport media.
conditions: when conveying fluids, air, or electrical current
exceptions: junction or fitting elements that are not segments

subject: IfcDistributionElement
rationale: Fittings like elbows, tees, and reducers are necessary to route and reconfigure distribution paths.
applicability: IfcDistributionElement depends_on IfcFlowFitting is stated as applicable to 'all building types', but in many simple distribution networks (e.g., a straight pipe run, a simple electrical cable run), no flow fittings are present. The condition already captures 'when changes in direction... are needed', but the applicability 'all building types' is misleadingly broad as there are many distribution elements in all building types that do not involve fittings.
conditions: when changes in direction, branching, or diameter are needed in the distribution network
exceptions: straight runs without fittings

subject: IfcDistributionElement
rationale: Control elements regulate the flow and operation of distribution systems.
conditions: when automated control of distribution is needed (e.g., dampers, valves, switches)
exceptions: passive distribution without control requirements

subject: IfcDistributionElement
rationale: IfcDistributionElement provides the structural/logical host for distribution ports used in system connectivity.
conditions: when acting as a host for connectivity points
exceptions: elements without ports

subject: IfcDistributionElement
rationale: Distribution elements can contain or be part of distribution circuits in electrical and data systems.
conditions: when electrical or other networked distribution is organized into circuits
exceptions: mechanical or plumbing distribution not arranged as circuits

subject: IfcDistributionElement
rationale: Distribution elements connect to building spaces to deliver or extract air, water, power, or data.
applicability: IfcDistributionElement connects_to IfcSpace is listed with applicability 'all building types', but in IFC, the relationship between distribution elements and spaces is typically via IfcRelSpaceBoundary or IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure, not a direct 'connects_to' relationship. Many distribution elements (e.g., those in ceiling plenums, service shafts, or exterior walls) are not directly connected to a specific IfcSpace.
conditions: when serving conditioned or serviced spaces
exceptions: elements in service voids or shafts not directly serving a space

subject: IfcDistributionElement
rationale: Distribution elements are typically routed through, mounted on, or supported by other building elements like walls, slabs, and ceilings.
applicability: IfcDistributionElement connects_to IfcBuildingElement with applicability 'all building types' and condition 'when physically supported by or passing through structural elements'. However, many distribution elements are supported by hangers, brackets, or trapezes which are typically classified as IfcBuildingElementProxy or IfcElementComponent, not IfcBuildingElement. Also, passing through a structural element (e.g., a pipe through a wall) does not necessarily constitute a 'connects_to' relationship in IFC terms.
conditions: when physically supported by or passing through structural elements
exceptions: freestanding distribution elements

subject: IfcDistributionElement
rationale: Some distribution systems require storage devices to buffer supply and demand.
conditions: when storage of distributed media is needed (e.g., water tanks, batteries)
exceptions: continuous-flow distribution without storage

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: IfcDistributionFlowElement is typically assigned to an IfcDistributionSystem to define the network context for flow distribution.
conditions: when functioning as part of a building's mechanical, electrical, or plumbing infrastructure

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: IfcDistributionFlowElement uses IfcDistributionPort as connection points for flow distribution.
conditions: when connected to other distribution elements
exceptions: standalone elements with no connectivity

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: IfcFlowSegment is a subtype of IfcDistributionFlowElement used for transporting media through ducts, pipes, cables, etc.
conditions: when transporting fluids, air, or electrical energy along a path

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: IfcFlowFitting connects segments in flow distribution systems.
conditions: when changing direction, branching, or connecting segments

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: IfcFlowTerminal represents endpoints such as diffusers, outlets, or radiators served by flow distribution.
conditions: at endpoints of distribution systems where media is delivered or extracted

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: IfcFlowController regulates flow within a distribution system.
conditions: when regulation of flow (e.g., dampers, valves, switches) is needed

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: IfcEnergyConversionDevice provides heating, cooling, or power conversion for distribution networks.
conditions: when energy conversion (e.g., boiler, chiller, motor) is required to drive the distribution

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement relationship defines logical connections between ports and flow elements.
conditions: when establishing connectivity between ports and distribution elements

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: IfcRelConnectsPorts establishes connectivity between distribution ports in a system.
conditions: when connecting two ports to form a path for flow distribution

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: General connectivity relationship used in some distribution scenarios.
conditions: when physical connection information between distribution elements is needed

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: IfcFlowMovingDevice (e.g., pumps, fans, compressors) is a subtype contained within the DistributionFlowElement concept.
conditions: when active movement of fluid, air, or electricity is needed

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: Distribution flow elements connect to building elements such as walls, slabs, or ceilings.
conditions: when physically embedded in or attached to building construction elements

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: IfcDistributionFlowElement components collectively define a distribution circuit.
conditions: when forming part of an electrical or fluid circuit

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElement
rationale: Distribution flow elements serve IfcSpaces by delivering or removing environmental media.
conditions: when serving specific rooms or zones with conditioned air, water, or power

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionFlowElementType is typically associated with an IfcDistributionSystem to define the type of flow elements (e.g., ducts, pipes, cables) that belong to that system.
conditions: When defining the type for distribution flow elements within a system

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionFlowElementType inherits from IfcTypeObject the ability to have property sets defining its characteristics.
applicability: IfcDistributionFlowElementType does not strictly require IfcPropertySet. Property sets are optional in IFC; a type can be defined without any property sets attached. While it is common practice to attach property sets for detailed properties, it is not a requirement.
conditions: When detailed type properties are needed

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElementType
rationale: The relationship IfcRelDefinesByType is used to associate occurrences (IfcDistributionFlowElement) to their type definition (IfcDistributionFlowElementType).
applicability: IfcDistributionFlowElementType depends on IfcRelDefinesByType only when instances of the type are actually created. If a type is defined in the model without any occurrences (e.g., in a type library context), IfcRelDefinesByType relationships are not needed.
conditions: When associating occurrences to the type

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionFlowElementType can define types of distribution ports (e.g., inlet/outlet) that belong to the element type for connecting to other distribution elements.
conditions: When the flow element type has connection points

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElementType
rationale: For linear distribution flow element types (e.g., pipe segment types, duct segment types), material and profile definitions are typically required.
conditions: When the flow element type represents linear elements like pipes or ducts

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElementType
rationale: Some distribution flow element types may require layered material definitions for insulation or other composite constructions.
conditions: When the flow element type has layered materials (e.g., insulated pipes)

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionFlowElementType defines types of elements that carry media, which need flow controllers (e.g., valves, dampers) to regulate flow.
conditions: When the system requires regulation of flow

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElementType
rationale: Distribution flow elements transport media to or from flow terminals (e.g., diffusers, sprinklers, faucets).
conditions: When the distribution system ends at terminals

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionFlowElementType can participate in nesting relationships to compose complex distribution assemblies.
conditions: When the type contains sub-components or sub-types

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionFlowElementType defines the common properties and geometry for occurrences of IfcDistributionFlowElement.
conditions: When defining the type-instance relationship

subject: IfcDistributionFlowElementType
rationale: IfcDistributionFlowElementType can have an associated representation map for defining the geometric representation of all occurrences.
applicability: IfcDistributionFlowElementType does not strictly 'depend on' IfcRepresentationMap. While type products often have a RepresentationMaps attribute for predefined geometry, this is optional in IFC. A type can be defined without any geometric representation.
conditions: When the type has a predefined geometry representation

subject: IfcDistributionPort
rationale: An IfcDistributionPort is a connection point in a distribution system and typically belongs to an IfcDistributionSystem for proper functioning.
conditions: port must be assigned to a distribution system

subject: IfcDistributionPort
rationale: IfcDistributionPort is usually attached to an IfcDistributionElement (such as an air terminal, pipe fitting, or electrical device) as its host.
conditions: port is attached to a parent element

subject: IfcDistributionPort
rationale: The relationship between a port and its host element is established via IfcRelConnectsPortToElement.
conditions: port is physically or logically connected to an element

subject: IfcDistributionPort
rationale: The connection between two ports is formalized through IfcRelConnectsPorts.
conditions: port is connected to another port

subject: IfcDistributionPort
rationale: Distribution ports support the connection of flow segments (pipes, ducts, cables) at system boundaries.
applicability: IfcDistributionPort can also serve as endpoint of other distribution elements such as IfcFlowTerminal, IfcFlowController, IfcFlowStorageDevice, etc. It is not limited to supporting only IfcFlowSegment.
conditions: port serves as endpoint of a flow segment (duct, pipe, cable, etc.)

subject: IfcDistributionPort
rationale: Ports on flow fittings (elbows, tees, junctions) support network connectivity.
applicability: IfcDistributionPort can be on many other element types besides IfcFlowFitting, such as IfcFlowTerminal, IfcFlowController, IfcFlowStorageDevice. The port supports the connection to these elements as well, not just fittings.
conditions: port is used on a fitting for system branching or connection

subject: IfcDistributionPort
rationale: Ports on energy conversion devices allow them to interface with distribution systems.
applicability: IfcDistributionPort is used on many device types beyond IfcEnergyConversionDevice, including IfcFlowTerminal, IfcFlowMovingDevice, IfcFlowController, etc. The port supports these equally.
conditions: port is on a device that consumes or generates energy (e.g., boiler, chiller)

subject: IfcDistributionPort
rationale: Ports often have associated property sets defining technical characteristics (e.g., nominal diameter, voltage, fluid type).
conditions: port has properties like port type, fluid type, or electrical characteristics

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: IfcDistributionSystem requires IfcDistributionPort elements as connection points for its distribution components (e.g., ducts, pipes, cables).
conditions: for connectivity between distribution elements

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: An IfcDistributionSystem contains IfcDistributionElement components (e.g., ducts, pipes, cables, fittings) that form the physical distribution network.
conditions: when the element is part of the distribution network
exceptions: standalone elements not assigned to any system

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: IfcFlowSegment (pipes, ducts, conduits) are contained within an IfcDistributionSystem as the main transport elements.
conditions: when part of a flow distribution system

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: IfcFlowFitting (elbows, tees, junctions) are contained within a distribution system to connect flow segments.
conditions: when connecting flow segments within the system

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: IfcFlowController (dampers, valves, switches) are contained in distribution systems to regulate flow.
conditions: when regulating flow within the distribution system

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: IfcFlowTerminal (diffusers, grilles, faucets) are end points contained within a distribution system.
conditions: where the distribution system delivers or collects substance/energy

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: IfcFlowTreatmentDevice (filters, heat exchangers) may be contained in distribution systems for air/water treatment.
conditions: when part of a treatment process within the distribution system

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: IfcEnergyConversionDevice (boilers, chillers, fans, pumps) can be contained as part of a distribution system.
conditions: when converting energy forms within the distribution system

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: IfcDistributionSystem depends on IfcRelConnectsPorts relationships to define how distribution elements are connected via ports.
conditions: for establishing logical connectivity between distribution elements

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: IfcDistributionSystem depends on IfcRelServicesBuildings to define which building elements or spaces it services.
applicability: IfcRelServicesBuildings is a legacy relationship deprecated in IFC4. The assertion should note that for IFC2x3 compatibility only, as newer IFC versions use IfcRelAssignsToGroup or spatial containment.
conditions: when the system serves specific building elements or spaces

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: IfcDistributionSystem depends on IfcRelAssignsToGroup relationship to group its constituent distribution elements.
conditions: when group assignment is used to define the system membership

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: Distribution systems (HVAC, plumbing, electrical) support building spaces by delivering heating, cooling, water, power, and data services.
applicability: IfcDistributionSystem 'supports' IfcSpace is not a standard IFC relationship. In IFC, distribution systems serve spaces via IfcRelServicesBuildings (legacy) or through connectivity analysis, but there is no direct 'supports' relationship between IfcDistributionSystem and IfcSpace.
conditions: when the distribution system provides conditioned air, water, power, or data to spaces
exceptions: unconditioned spaces not requiring services

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: Distribution systems collectively support the building's operational performance by enabling essential services.
applicability: IfcDistributionSystem 'supports' IfcBuilding is not a standard IFC relationship. A building is typically a spatial structure element that contains distribution elements, but there is no direct 'supports' relationship from system to building.
conditions: as a whole for the building's operational functionality

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: Distribution systems support HVAC or electrical zones by providing conditioned air or power to those zones.
applicability: IfcDistributionSystem 'supports' IfcZone is not a standard IFC relationship. A zone groups spaces, and a system serves those spaces, but there is no direct relationship between IfcDistributionSystem and IfcZone.
conditions: when serving a defined thermal or functional zone

subject: IfcDistributionSystem
rationale: Well-designed distribution systems protect building elements by managing moisture (drainage), fire (sprinklers), and thermal loads.
applicability: IfcDistributionSystem 'protects_from' IfcBuildingElement is not a standard IFC relationship. Protection from moisture, fire, or structural overload is a functional property, not an IFC relationship. The assertion describes a design intent, not an IFC-defined relationship.
conditions: when proper installation prevents moisture damage, fire spread, or structural overload
exceptions: improperly designed or overloaded systems

subject: IfcDocumentInformation
rationale: IfcDocumentInformation requires relationships to other document information objects to form document structures as per IFC schema.
conditions: When documents need to be hierarchically organized

subject: IfcDocumentInformation
rationale: IfcDocumentInformation is typically referenced via IfcDocumentReference to associate with IFC objects.
conditions: When document information is linked to specific building elements

subject: IfcDocumentInformation
rationale: Document information often depends on actors (persons/organizations) for authorship and responsibility.
conditions: When document author/owner information is needed

subject: IfcDocumentInformation
rationale: Documents may depend on classification references for categorization.
conditions: When documents are classified according to a standard classification system

subject: IfcDocumentInformation
rationale: IfcDocumentInformation supports the overall project by providing documentation context.
applicability: The assertion uses 'supports' which is ambiguous in IFC terms. IfcDocumentInformation does not directly support IfcProject; it can be associated via IfcRelAssociatesDocument or IfcDocumentInformationRelationship. The direct semantic is not defined in the IFC schema.
conditions: When project documentation is managed within the IFC model

subject: IfcDocumentInformation
rationale: Document information supports building elements by providing associated documentation.
applicability: The assertion uses 'supports' which is ambiguous. IfcDocumentInformation does not directly support IfcBuilding in the IFC schema; association is through IfcRelAssociatesDocument or IfcDocumentInformationRelationship.
conditions: When building-specific documentation is required (e.g., permits, specifications)

subject: IfcDocumentInformation
rationale: IfcDocumentInformation supports building elements by linking documentation to physical components.
applicability: The assertion uses 'supports' which is ambiguous. IfcDocumentInformation does not directly support IfcBuildingElement; the relationship goes through IfcRelAssociatesDocument.
conditions: When elements have associated documents like datasheets, manuals, certificates

subject: IfcDocumentInformation
rationale: IfcDocumentInformation connects to IFC objects via IfcRelAssociatesDocument relationship entity.
conditions: When document information is associated with IFC objects

subject: IfcDocumentInformation
rationale: IfcDocumentInformation connects to other document information entities via relationship entities.
conditions: When documents are organized in hierarchies (parent-child)

subject: IfcDocumentInformationRelationship
rationale: IfcDocumentInformationRelationship links IfcDocumentInformation entities together, so it depends on the existence of IfcDocumentInformation objects to relate.
applicability: Any building project using document management
conditions: when establishing relationships between documents

subject: IfcDocumentInformationRelationship
rationale: The relationship entity supports document structure by defining parent-child, sequential, or replacement relationships between documents.
applicability: Any building project with structured documentation
conditions: when organizing document hierarchies

subject: IfcDocumentInformationRelationship
rationale: Document information relationships are often used in conjunction with document associations to building elements.
conditions: when documents need to be linked to building elements

subject: IfcDocumentReference
rationale: IfcDocumentReference points to the location of a document; the document information (metadata) is needed to interpret the reference.
applicability: The assertion says 'depends_on' but in the IFC schema, IfcDocumentReference has an optional 'ReferenceToDocument' relationship to IfcDocumentInformation via IfcDocumentInformationRelationship, not a direct dependency. The 'depends_on' semantics are misleading without clarifying that IfcDocumentInformation can exist independently without any IfcDocumentReference.
conditions: When referencing an external document

subject: IfcDocumentReference
rationale: The relationship entity IfcRelAssociatesDocument is required to formally link IfcDocumentReference to IFC objects.
applicability: The assertion says 'depends_on IfcRelAssociatesDocument' — the relationship is actually the opposite: IfcRelAssociatesDocument links to IfcDocumentReference, not the other way around. IfcDocumentReference does not depend on IfcRelAssociatesDocument; rather, IfcDocumentReference can exist without any association relationship.
conditions: When the reference is associated to building elements

subject: IfcDocumentReference
rationale: IfcDocumentReference provides external documentation (specs, drawings, manuals) that supports the definition and use of building elements.
applicability: The assertion says IfcDocumentReference 'supports' IfcBuildingElement. IfcDocumentReference does not directly support IfcBuildingElement — it is linked via IfcRelAssociatesDocument which associates an IfcDocumentReference (or IfcDocumentInformation) to IfcBuildingElement. This indirect relationship is not captured by a direct 'supports' predicate.
conditions: When a building element has an associated document reference

subject: IfcDocumentReference
rationale: IfcDocumentReference provides supporting documentation for any IFC product.
applicability: Same issue as with IfcBuildingElement: IfcDocumentReference does not directly 'support' IfcProduct — it is mediated through IfcRelAssociatesDocument. The relationship is indirect and the 'supports' predicate oversimplifies the IFC schema.
conditions: When a product has an associated document reference

subject: IfcDocumentReference
rationale: While IfcDocumentReference can stand alone with just a location, proper function in IFC data exchange typically requires the associated document information.
conditions: For full metadata context
exceptions: Can exist without IfcDocumentInformation if only a direct location is needed

The assertion says 'requires' IfcDocumentInformation but the existing exception correctly notes it can exist without it. However, beyond 'direct location', IfcDocumentReference can also be used as a bare URI reference in some IFC implementations without a corresponding IfcDocumentInformation object, which is a valid scenario not captured by 'only a direct location'.

subject: IfcDocumentReference
rationale: IfcDocumentReference is connected to IFC objects via the IfcRelAssociatesDocument relationship entity.
applicability: IfcDocumentReference does not directly 'connect_to' IfcRelAssociatesDocument. IfcRelAssociatesDocument has a RelatingDocument attribute that points to either IfcDocumentInformation or IfcDocumentReference, and RelatedObjects that point to elements. The direction and nature of the connection is not fully captured by a simple 'connects_to' with no further qualification.

subject: IfcDocumentReference
rationale: IfcDocumentReference connects to IfcDocumentInformation to provide the metadata context for the referenced document.

subject: IfcDoor
rationale: A wall provides the structural support and opening for a door
conditions: Doors are typically installed in wall openings
exceptions: Free-standing door frames in open spaces

subject: IfcDoor
rationale: A door may contain glass panels for visibility or aesthetics
applicability: Doors with windows, sidelights, or vision panels
conditions: When the door includes a window or vision panel
exceptions: Solid doors without glazing

subject: IfcDoor
rationale: A threshold is often part of the door assembly at the floor level
conditions: At the bottom of the door opening
exceptions: Doors without a raised threshold

subject: IfcDoor
rationale: Doors connect rooms to circulation spaces
conditions: When the door opens onto a hallway

subject: IfcDoorLiningProperties
rationale: IfcDoorLiningProperties defines the lining geometry and properties for an IfcDoor element; the door is the parent element that the properties are applied to.
applicability: IfcDoorLiningProperties does not depend on IfcDoor in the IFC schema sense. IfcDoorLiningProperties is assigned to an IfcDoor via IfcRelDefinesByProperties, but it is not a direct dependency — an IfcDoorLiningProperties instance can exist without any IfcDoor referencing it.
conditions: IfcDoorLiningProperties is used to define the lining properties of a door

subject: IfcDoorLiningProperties
rationale: IfcDoorLiningProperties can be associated with an IfcDoorStyle to define the lining parameters for that style type.
applicability: Doors that follow a predefined style
conditions: When the door lining is associated with a specific door style

subject: IfcDoorLiningProperties
rationale: Door linings are typically installed within wall openings; the wall provides the structural context for the lining.
conditions: The door opening is cut into a wall where the lining is installed
exceptions: Walls that are not load-bearing may not require a lining

subject: IfcDoorLiningProperties
rationale: IfcDoorLiningProperties is applied to a door that is typically placed within an IfcOpeningElement in the wall.
conditions: The door is placed in a predefined opening

subject: IfcDoorLiningProperties
rationale: IfcDoorLiningProperties is associated to an IfcDoor via IfcRelDefinesByProperties in the IFC data model.
applicability: IfcDoorLiningProperties depends on IfcRelDefinesByProperties in the sense that IfcRelDefinesByProperties is the mechanism to assign property sets to objects. However, this is a relationship that applies to all property set definitions in IFC, not specific to IfcDoorLiningProperties. The assertion is overly generic at the applicability level: IfcRelDefinesByProperties is not limited to 'all IFC instances' — it relates property sets to objects, so the dependency is definitional rather than domain-specific.
conditions: The relationship linking the door to its lining properties

subject: IfcDoorLiningProperties
rationale: IfcDoorLiningProperties and IfcDoorPanelProperties are complementary property sets both applying to the same IfcDoor.
applicability: Doors with both lining and panel property definitions
conditions: When both lining and panel properties are defined for the same door

subject: IfcDoorPanelProperties
rationale: IfcDoorPanelProperties defines properties for door panels that are part of an IfcDoor. The door panel properties cannot exist without the parent door element.
applicability: The assertion states IfcDoorPanelProperties depends_on IfcDoor, but in IFC, IfcDoorPanelProperties can be associated with IfcDoorStyle (via IfcRelDefinesByProperties) rather than directly with an IfcDoor occurrence. The condition only mentions Door occurrences, missing the more common case where properties are assigned through a style.
conditions: IfcDoorPanelProperties is associated with a Door occurrence

subject: IfcDoorPanelProperties
rationale: Door panel properties can be assigned to a door style to define standard panel configurations.
conditions: When the door panel properties are defined as part of a door style
exceptions: Can also be defined per occurrence

The assertion states IfcDoorPanelProperties depends_on IfcDoorStyle, but the existing exception correctly notes it can also be defined per occurrence (directly on IfcDoor). This means the 'depends_on' relationship is not exclusive to IfcDoorStyle, and the assertion as stated (without the exception being baked in) is misleading about the dependency being required.

subject: IfcDoorPanelProperties
rationale: Shape representation of the door panel can be associated via IfcShapeAspect for the panel's geometric definition.
conditions: When the panel has a defined shape representation or product definition shape

subject: IfcDoorPanelProperties
rationale: Door panels and linings work together as part of the door assembly; the panels fit within the lining frame.
applicability: Doors with both panels and linings
conditions: When panels and linings are part of the same door assembly

subject: IfcDoorPanelProperties
rationale: The panel's material composition (e.g., layers of wood, insulation, facing) can be defined via material layer sets.
applicability: IfcDoorPanelProperties depends_on IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage is not always true. IfcDoorPanelProperties can define material information via IfcMaterial (directly) or IfcMaterialLayerSet, not necessarily through IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage specifically. IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage is a more specific entity used for layered constructions in building elements like walls, and door panels often use simpler material assignments.
conditions: When the panel construction is defined by material layers

subject: IfcDoorStandardCase
rationale: The door assembly depends on the surrounding wall for support and anchorage.
conditions: Interior or exterior wall
exceptions: Some building codes and practices allow doors to be installed in non-bearing lightweight partitions or in openings of free-standing enclosure systems where the door does not structurally depend on a wall. In IFC, IfcDoorStandardCase may also be placed in IfcCurtainWall or IfcWallStandardCase with non-loadbearing relationship being 'filling' rather than 'dependence'.

subject: IfcDoorStandardCase
rationale: The door frame connects to the surrounding wall structure.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcDoorStandardCase connects_to Wall' with condition 'Standard installation' does not specify whether this includes all types of walls (load-bearing, non-loadbearing, partition, exterior, interior, curtain walls). In many IFC models, IfcDoorStandardCase connects to IfcWallStandardCase via IfcRelFillsElement, but in curtain wall systems the door connects to IfcCurtainWall which is a subtype of IfcBuildingElement, not IfcWall.
conditions: Standard installation

subject: IfcDoorStyle
rationale: IfcDoorStyle defines the style/type properties for IfcDoor instances; doors depend on their style definition.
conditions: when IfcDoorStyle is used as a type definition for door instances

subject: IfcDoorStyle
rationale: IfcDoorStyle references IfcDoorLiningProperties for lining geometry and parameters.
conditions: when the door style includes a lining
exceptions: doors without linings

subject: IfcDoorStyle
rationale: IfcDoorStyle references IfcDoorPanelProperties for panel geometry and parameters.
conditions: when the door style includes panels
exceptions: doors without panels e.g., sliding doors

subject: IfcDoorStyle
rationale: Door styles may reference material definitions via IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage or material selectors.
conditions: when material assignment is part of the style definition

subject: IfcDoorStyle
rationale: IfcDoorStyle can have associated property sets defining additional parameters.
conditions: when custom property sets are assigned to the style

subject: IfcDoorStyle
rationale: IfcDoorStyle aggregates IfcDoorLiningProperties as part of its definition.

subject: IfcDoorStyle
rationale: IfcDoorStyle aggregates IfcDoorPanelProperties as part of its definition.

subject: IfcDoorStyle
rationale: IfcDoorStyle can contain associated property sets.
conditions: when property sets are assigned

subject: IfcDoorStyle
rationale: IfcDoorStyle provides the type definition (geometry, parameters) that supports door instances.

subject: IfcDoorStyle
rationale: The relationship object that links IfcDoor instances to IfcDoorStyle.

subject: IfcDoorStyle
rationale: IfcDoorStyle exists to define door instances; without doors the style has no functional purpose.
conditions: when the style is actually used in a model
exceptions: if the style is defined but not instantiated

subject: IfcDoorStyle
rationale: IfcDoorStyle may reference an IfcRepresentationMap for its geometric shape.
conditions: when the style defines a geometric representation
exceptions: if no geometric representation is defined

subject: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour
rationale: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour may be used alongside predefined curve fonts in drafting presentations, but does not functionally depend on them.
applicability: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour is used alone without curve font
conditions: when used in drafting presentation

subject: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour
rationale: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour can be used to define colours for presentation layers in IFC models, supporting visual representation.
applicability: drafting and CAD-like presentations in BIM
conditions: when colour is assigned to presentation layers

subject: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour
rationale: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour is a subtype of IfcPreDefinedColour and does not contain other colour types; it references a name-based colour definition.
exceptions: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour does not contain IfcColourRgb; they are alternatives

subject: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour
rationale: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour can be assigned to text styles for draughting purposes.
applicability: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour does not directly 'connect_to' IfcTextStyleForDefinedFont. In IFC, IfcTextStyleForDefinedFont uses IfcColour (which can be IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour) via the TextColour attribute, and IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour is related indirectly through IfcTextLiteralWithExtent or presentation assignments, not through a direct connection relationship.
conditions: when text styles include colour assignment

subject: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour
rationale: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour and IfcColourSpecification are alternative ways to define colours and may conflict if used interchangeably in the same assignment.
conditions: when both are used in the same context without clear assignment
exceptions: they can coexist in different assignments

subject: IfcDoorType
rationale: Most doors are installed within wall elements that provide structural support and the required opening.
conditions: for typical wall-mounted doors
exceptions: free-standing door assemblies exist

subject: IfcDoorType
rationale: Door types may contain glass panes for visibility or aesthetics.
conditions: when the door type includes vision panels or full glazing
exceptions: solid doors contain no glazing

subject: IfcDoorType
rationale: Door types are physically connected to surrounding wall elements via the door opening.
conditions: when installed in a wall opening
exceptions: doors in curtain walls or partitions connect differently
Doors used in elevator shafts or as emergency egress doors connected directly to slabs without a wall opening are exceptions where IfcDoorType may connect to IfcSlab or IfcPlate rather than IfcWall.

subject: IfcDoorType
rationale: Doors connect spaces; the door type is associated with space boundaries that define adjacency between rooms.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcDoorType connects_to IfcRelSpaceBoundary' is imprecise: IfcDoorType does not directly connect to IfcRelSpaceBoundary. Rather, an IfcDoor occurrence (IfcDoor) is associated with IfcRelSpaceBoundary via relationship objects. The type-level (IfcDoorType) connection to space boundaries is indirect and type definitions do not typically hold space boundary relationships in IFC schema.
conditions: when defining spatial relationships between rooms

subject: IfcDoorType
rationale: IfcDoorType depends on property sets (e.g., DoorCommon, FireRating) for full specification in IFC models.
conditions: for IFC data exchange
exceptions: simple type definitions may use minimal properties

subject: IfcDuctFitting
rationale: Duct fittings (e.g., elbows, tees, transitions) are installed between straight duct segments to change direction, branch, or adjust cross-section.
conditions: When used in HVAC ductwork systems
exceptions: IfcDuctFitting can be used in isolation for design intent models or early-stage coordination without requiring IfcDuctSegment in all cases, such as when representing a standalone component library element or a placeholder fitting before duct routing is finalized.

subject: IfcDuctFitting
rationale: As a subtype of flow fitting, IfcDuctFitting connects to flow segments in the HVAC network.
applicability: all buildings with HVAC or ventilation systems
conditions: when integrated into fluid distribution systems

subject: IfcDuctFitting
rationale: Port-based connectivity via IfcRelConnectsPorts defines how the fitting connects to adjacent duct segments.
conditions: for connectivity data in BIM

subject: IfcDuctFitting
rationale: Duct fittings are made from materials like galvanized steel, stainless steel, or aluminum; material properties affect pressure drop, durability, and fire rating.
conditions: for fabrication and structural integrity

subject: IfcDuctFitting
rationale: Fittings connect duct mains to branches that lead to diffusers, grilles, and registers.
applicability: IfcDuctFitting does not directly 'support' IfcAirTerminal in a topological sense; air terminals connect via duct segments (IfcDuctSegment), not directly to fittings. The assertion uses vague terminology ('supports') that may misrepresent the actual IFC relationship (typically through IfcRelConnectsElements via intermediate segments).
conditions: via duct system connections

subject: IfcDuctFitting
rationale: Each duct fitting has inlet and outlet connections to adjoining straight duct segments.
conditions: at inlet and outlet ports

subject: IfcDuctFitting
rationale: Duct fittings can connect to silencers to control acoustic performance in the duct system.
conditions: in noise-sensitive applications

subject: IfcDuctFitting
rationale: Performance parameters like pressure loss coefficient, friction factor, and dimensions are stored in property sets.
conditions: for specification data in BIM

subject: IfcDuctFitting
rationale: Duct fittings (HVAC air) and pipe fittings (fluid) may compete for the same overhead or vertical shaft space.
applicability: buildings with combined HVAC and plumbing systems

IfcDuctFitting and IfcPipeFitting are distinct entity types in IFC and do not inherently 'conflict'; they represent different systems (duct vs. pipe). The real conflict is spatial (space allocation), not a semantic or relationship conflict between the IFC entities themselves. The assertion conflates physical spatial coordination issues with IFC entity relationships.
conditions: when space is constrained in mechanical rooms or ceiling plenums
exceptions: when separate dedicated zones are allocated

subject: IfcDuctFittingType
rationale: IfcDuctFittingType represents fittings like elbows, tees, transitions, etc. that require connecting ductwork segments to function as part of an air distribution system.
conditions: for air distribution system

subject: IfcDuctFittingType
rationale: Duct fittings connect to air terminals (diffusers, grilles) via ductwork to deliver or extract air.
conditions: when part of an HVAC supply/return system
exceptions: non-ducted systems

subject: IfcDuctFittingType
rationale: IfcDuctFittingType components (elbows, tees, reducers) connect different duct segments together to form a continuous duct network.
conditions: always required as duct fittings connect duct segments
exceptions: While duct fittings often connect duct segments, IfcDuctFittingType is a type entity (defining properties like shape, material, etc.) and does not 'depend on' IfcDuctSegment as a modeling dependency in the IFC schema. In IFC, IfcDuctFitting and IfcDuctSegment are both subtypes of IfcFlowSegment/Fitting and are associated via connectivity (IfcRelConnectsPorts), not via a type-level dependency. The assertion conflates type definitions with occurrence-level relationships.

subject: IfcDuctFittingType
rationale: Fans provide the pressure differential required to move air through duct fittings and ductwork.
conditions: when used in forced air systems
exceptions: gravity ventilation systems

subject: IfcDuctFittingType
rationale: Duct silencers may be needed near duct fittings to attenuate noise generated by airflow changes at fittings.
conditions: when noise control is required in the duct system
exceptions: systems without noise constraints

subject: IfcDuctFittingType
rationale: While not a direct functional connection, duct routing (and hence fittings) must coordinate with architectural elements like doors.
conditions: when duct passes through a wall/door opening is adjacent

subject: IfcDuctSegmentType
rationale: Insulation is often required on duct segments to prevent condensation, heat loss/gain, and reduce noise.
conditions: Where thermal or acoustic insulation is specified
exceptions: Non-conditioned spaces where no thermal barrier is needed

subject: IfcDuctSegmentType
rationale: Duct segments function as part of a larger HVAC system, depending on air handling units, fans, and terminal devices.
conditions: For conditioned air supply and return
exceptions: There are duct segments that are not part of conditioned air supply or return, such as exhaust-only ducts (toilet exhaust, general exhaust, kitchen exhaust hood ducts), fresh air intake ducts not connected to conditioning equipment, or ducts in naturally ventilated buildings that only serve transfer air. These duct segments exist without a mechanical HVAC system for conditioning.

subject: IfcDuctSegmentType
rationale: Duct routing depends on structural elements (floors, walls, ceilings) for support and spatial coordination.
applicability: The assertion 'depends_on Building Structure' with the condition 'For routing and support attachment' is overly broad for 'All buildings'. In many cases, duct segments may be supported by ceiling grids, strut systems, or trapeze hangers that attach to the building structure indirectly, but there are also scenarios where ducts are installed independently without relying on building structural elements (e.g., duct segments in packaged rooftop units, duct segments within prefabricated mechanical rooms, or duct segments in open fields/factory settings that are self-supporting or mounted on non-structural frames). The dependency on building structure is more context-specific than 'All buildings' implies.
conditions: For routing and support attachment

subject: IfcDuctSilencer
rationale: A duct silencer must be connected to duct segments to be installed in an air distribution system.
conditions: Duct silencer is installed inline within a ductwork system

subject: IfcDuctSilencer
rationale: Duct silencers often work together with dampers and other flow controllers to manage airflow and pressure.
conditions: The duct silencer is preceded or followed by dampers or air terminals
exceptions: Standalone silencer installations without flow control elements

subject: IfcDuctSilencer
rationale: Silencers may be placed adjacent to air terminals (diffusers, grilles) to reduce terminal noise.
conditions: Silencer is installed at the end of a duct near supply/return openings
exceptions: Silencers installed mid-duct, not directly at terminals

subject: IfcDuctSilencer
rationale: Duct silencers reduce noise from fans and air movement in ERV systems, supporting occupant comfort.
conditions: Used in balanced ventilation systems with heat recovery
exceptions: Systems without heat recovery

subject: IfcDuctSilencer
