exceptions: Fan-less natural ventilation systems

The assertion 'IfcDuctSilencer connects_to IfcFan' does not cover cases where the silencer is installed between duct segments without being directly adjacent to the fan — e.g., silencer located several duct sections away from the fan on the discharge side.

subject: IfcDuctSilencer
rationale: Larger duct silencers may require hangers, brackets, or supports attached to building structure.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcDuctSilencer depends_on IfcBuildingElementProxy' uses IfcBuildingElementProxy as a catch-all for structural supports. IfcBuildingElementProxy is a generic proxy object and using it as a dependency may not properly capture the intended structural support relationships (which should use proper structural elements like IfcBeam, IfcColumn, or specific hanger elements). This could lead to modeling ambiguity.
conditions: Silencer requires structural support or hangers
exceptions: Small, lightweight silencers supported directly by ductwork

subject: IfcDuctSilencer
rationale: Duct silencers connect to fittings such as transitions, reducers, and elbows to integrate into the duct system.
conditions: Ductwork configuration includes transitions, elbows, or branches
exceptions: Straight-duct-only installation

subject: IfcDuctSilencer
rationale: A duct silencer requires a flow-moving device (fan) to have airflow to silence in the first place.
conditions: Airflow is mechanically driven
exceptions: Natural ventilation systems without fans

subject: IfcEdge
rationale: IfcEdge is a topological representation connecting two IfcVertex points. It requires two vertices to define the edge.
conditions: When defining an edge in a topological representation

subject: IfcEdge
rationale: IfcEdge depends on IfcVertex for its geometric definition, as each edge is defined by a start and end point (EdgeStart and EdgeEnd).
conditions: For edge definition

subject: IfcEdge
rationale: An IfcEdge contains exactly two vertices (EdgeStart and EdgeEnd) as its constituent parts.
conditions: As part of its topological structure

subject: IfcEdge
rationale: IfcEdge can be linked to IfcEdgeCurve (a subtype) which associates a curve with the edge topology. The base IfcEdge itself is a purely topological construct, but its subtype IfcEdgeCurve connects it to geometric curve information.
conditions: When the edge has an associated curve geometry

subject: IfcEdge
rationale: IfcSubedge is a subtype of IfcEdge used in composite curves, so IfcEdge can be specialized into sub-edges.
conditions: When an edge is part of a larger composite curve

subject: IfcEdge
rationale: IfcEdge is a fundamental building block for constructing IfcPath, which is an ordered collection of edges forming a path.
conditions: When edges are assembled into a path

subject: IfcEdge
rationale: Edges indirectly support the construction of faces (via loops), which in turn form shells. IfcEdge is part of the topological hierarchy (vertex → edge → loop → face → shell).
conditions: When edges form part of a face/loop structure

subject: IfcEdge
rationale: Edges are used to define loops, which serve as boundaries (IfcFaceBound) of faces in the topology model.
conditions: When defining boundaries of faces through loops

subject: IfcEdge
rationale: By definition, IfcEdge requires exactly two IfcVertex references (EdgeStart and EdgeEnd) to exist as a valid topological entity.
conditions: Always, to define the edge endpoints

subject: IfcEdge
rationale: IfcOrientedEdge is a subtype of IfcEdge that adds a directional orientation; the base edge concept connects to this specialized form.
conditions: When directional orientation is needed

subject: IfcEdgeCurve
rationale: IfcEdgeCurve is a subtype of IfcEdge and inherits its properties; it specifically combines an edge with a curve geometry, so it requires the base IfcEdge concept.
conditions: When representing a topological edge curve

subject: IfcEdgeCurve
rationale: IfcEdgeCurve has an attribute EdgeGeometry that references an IfcCurve, thus it requires a curve entity for its geometric representation.
conditions: When defining the geometric representation of the edge

subject: IfcEdgeCurve
rationale: IfcEdgeCurve inherits from IfcEdge the attributes EdgeStart and EdgeEnd, which reference IfcVertex objects defining the topological boundary.
conditions: When defining the start and end vertices of the edge

subject: IfcEdgeCurve
rationale: IfcEdgeCurve participates in topological data structures (e.g., edge loops, faces) and depends on a proper topology representation context to be meaningful.
applicability: IFC models with topological geometry representations
conditions: When used within a topological representation context

subject: IfcEdgeCurve
rationale: IfcEdgeCurve's vertices can be IfcVertexPoint instances that connect the edge curve to specific geometric points in 3D space.
applicability: IFC models where vertices carry point geometry

The assertion states IfcEdgeCurve connects_to IfcVertexPoint, but IfcEdgeCurve's edge start and end are defined via IfcVertex (abstract), not specifically IfcVertexPoint. The vertices could be any subtype of IfcVertex (e.g., IfcVertexPoint or other hypothetical subtypes). The connection is to IfcVertex, not exclusively to IfcVertexPoint.
conditions: When edge start or end vertices are defined with geometric points

subject: IfcEdgeCurve
rationale: IfcEdgeCurve can be aggregated into IfcEdgeLoop, which defines closed boundaries of topological faces.
conditions: When the edge curve is part of a closed boundary loop
exceptions: If the edge curve is used as a standalone topological edge

subject: IfcEdgeCurve
rationale: IfcEdgeCurve contributes to the boundary of IfcFace via edge loops, supporting the definition of topological faces.
conditions: When bounding a topological face

subject: IfcEdgeCurve
rationale: Edge curves are fundamental building blocks for face-based surface models, providing the geometric boundary for faces.
conditions: When used in a surface model representation

subject: IfcEdgeCurve
rationale: IfcOrientedEdge is a subtype of IfcEdgeCurve that adds orientation information, so IfcEdgeCurve connects conceptually to oriented edge definitions.
applicability: IFC models requiring oriented topological edges
conditions: When edge direction/orientation needs to be explicitly specified

subject: IfcEdgeLoop
rationale: IfcEdgeLoop is defined in IFC as a closed path defined by an ordered collection of IfcEdge objects, so it depends on IfcEdge entities to exist.
conditions: The loop must be composed of oriented edges

subject: IfcEdgeLoop
rationale: IfcEdgeLoop can contain IfcOrientedEdge subtypes which specify the orientation (direction) of each edge in the loop.
conditions: When edges have direction information

subject: IfcEdgeLoop
rationale: Each edge in an IfcEdgeLoop connects two vertices, so IfcVertex instances are required to define the edge endpoints within the loop.
conditions: Edges in the loop must connect at vertices

subject: IfcEdgeLoop
rationale: IfcPolyLoop is a subclass of IfcLoop (similar to IfcEdgeLoop) used for polygonal geometry; IfcEdgeLoop is a topological construct that can be used as an alternative, but does not strictly depend on IfcPolyLoop.
conditions: When the loop defines a planar polygonal boundary

subject: IfcEdgeLoop
rationale: IfcEdgeLoop is commonly used to define the boundary (outer or inner) of an IfcFaceBound, which in turn bounds an IfcFace in topological models.
conditions: When used as the boundary of a face

subject: IfcEdgeLoop
rationale: IfcEdgeLoop contributes to the topological definition of IfcFace through IfcFaceBound, enabling surface representation.
conditions: When the edge loop defines a face boundary

subject: IfcEdgeLoop

applicability: Advanced B-rep geometry in IFC models
conditions: When used in advanced boundary representation models

subject: IfcEdgeLoop

conditions: When the loop is part of a connected set of faces

subject: IfcEdgeLoop
rationale: IfcEdgeLoop is a subtype of IfcLoop, so the IfcLoop supertype definition is required for the entity to exist.
conditions: As the parent type in the inheritance hierarchy

subject: IfcElectricApplianceType
rationale: Certain electric appliance types connect to plumbing terminals for water supply and drainage.
applicability: The assertion incorrectly states IfcElectricApplianceType 'connects_to' IfcFlowTerminal. In IFC schema, IfcElectricApplianceType is a subtype of IfcFlowTerminalType itself (via IfcFlowTerminal -> IfcFlowTerminalType -> IfcElectricApplianceType), so an electric appliance is a flow terminal, not something separate that connects to one. The relationship should model the appliance as being connected to a distribution system (IfcFlowSegment/IfcFlowFitting) rather than another terminal.
conditions: for appliances requiring water supply or drainage (e.g., washing machines, dishwashers, water heaters)

subject: IfcElectricApplianceType
rationale: Electric appliances connect to electrical outlets or junction boxes to receive power.
conditions: via plug or direct wiring
exceptions: Some IfcElectricApplianceType instances (e.g., built-in hardwired ovens, cooktops, permanently wired HVAC equipment) connect directly to a circuit via IfcCableCarrierFitting/IfcJunctionBox or IfcProtectiveDevice, not to an IfcOutlet. An outlet is only one possible connection point, and many appliances conforming to this type do not terminate at an outlet.

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: An electric distribution board requires cable segments to connect incoming power and distribute outgoing circuits.
conditions: for power supply and distribution
exceptions: battery-backed systems may have local storage

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: Distribution boards always contain or require protective devices (circuit breakers, fuses) for electrical safety.
conditions: for overcurrent and short-circuit protection
exceptions: While most boards contain protective devices, some small distribution boards (e.g., consumer units in simple residential settings) might only have an RCD/main switch without a dedicated protective device modeled as IfcProtectiveDevice. Additionally, the protective device could be external (upstream) rather than internal to the board, meaning the board doesn't 'require' it as a direct relationship.

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: Distribution boards require switches or circuit breakers for manual isolation and control of circuits.
conditions: for circuit isolation and control
exceptions: Simple distribution boards (e.g., in small residential buildings) may consist only of a main switch and protective devices without individual switching devices for each circuit. A distribution board fed directly from a main isolator upstream does not necessarily contain or require its own IfcSwitchingDevice.

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: Distribution boards may depend on storage devices like batteries or UPS for uninterrupted power.
applicability: Applicability lists hospitals, data centers, and critical infrastructure but omits other building types that commonly have backup power such as hotels, airports, stadiums, large residential buildings, and telecommunications facilities. The 'depends_on' relationship is conditional on presence of backup power, so the applicability should be broader or stated as conditional.
conditions: when backup power or UPS systems are present
exceptions: not required in buildings without backup power

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: Distribution boards often depend on transformers to step down voltage to usable levels.
conditions: when voltage transformation is needed between utility and building systems
exceptions: low-rise buildings with direct utility supply may not need transformers

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: Cable carriers (trays, conduits, trunking) support cables feeding into and out of the distribution board.
conditions: for cable management and routing within the building
exceptions: may use conduit or cable trays alternatively

The assertion states IfcElectricDistributionBoard depends_on IfcCableCarrierSegment, but the existing exception already acknowledges alternative cable management like conduit or trays. The 'depends_on' relationship implies necessity, yet cable management can be achieved through other means (e.g., cast-in conduits, cable trenches, or exposed cabling with clips). A board does not strictly depend on a cable carrier segment modeled as IfcCableCarrierSegment.

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: The distribution board supplies power to downstream electric appliances throughout the building.
conditions: by providing distributed power to appliances

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: Lighting circuits are fed from distribution boards, supporting all light fixtures.
conditions: by distributing power to lighting circuits

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: Power outlets derive their supply from the distribution board via branch circuits.
conditions: by providing power to receptacle outlets

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: A distribution board physically contains circuit breakers, fuses, and other protective devices.
exceptions: Not all distribution boards 'contain' IfcProtectiveDevice. In some designs, especially main distribution boards, the protective device might be external (e.g., a separate switchgear assembly upstream). Additionally, very simple distribution boards (like a split-load consumer unit) might not have overcurrent protection modeled explicitly as IfcProtectiveDevice, relying instead on an RCD-only setup.

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: Distribution boards contain switches, contactors, or isolators for circuit control.
exceptions: Some small distribution boards, particularly sub-distribution boards in existing buildings or simple residential panels, may not contain switching devices. They may function as distribution points with only protective devices and busbars, with switching performed upstream.

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: The distribution board connects to generators to receive backup power during outages.
applicability: Applicability is limited to hospitals, data centers, emergency services, and critical facilities, but many other building types also have standby generators including hotels, large residential complexes, telecommunications towers, airports, commercial buildings, and industrial facilities. The applicability should be broader or clearly tied to the conditional presence of a generator.
conditions: when an emergency or standby generator is part of the electrical system
exceptions: buildings without generators

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: Distribution boards connect to energy conversion devices for voltage or current transformation.
applicability: all buildings with complex electrical systems
conditions: when connected to devices like transformers or inverters

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: The distribution board is physically and electrically connected to incoming and outgoing cable segments.

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: Protective devices inside the distribution board protect downstream cables from overcurrent damage.
conditions: by housing overcurrent protection devices that prevent cable overload and fire

subject: IfcElectricDistributionBoard
rationale: Appliances are protected from electrical faults by the breakers/fuses in the distribution board.
conditions: by providing overcurrent and short-circuit protection to branch circuits

subject: IfcElectricMotor
rationale: Electric motors drive pumps for water supply, HVAC circulation, and drainage.
applicability: IfcElectricMotor supports pumps only when the motor is the prime mover for the pump. In variable frequency drive (VFD) installations, the motor is controlled by a drive system that may be modeled separately as an IfcMotorConnection or IfcController, and the direct 'supports' relationship may not hold or may be mediated by additional elements. The assertion lacks this context.
conditions: Motor drives pump shaft directly or via coupling
exceptions: IfcElectricMotor also supports fans, compressors, conveyors, and other rotating equipment — not only pumps. The assertion over-specifies 'Pumps' as if it were exclusive, which could mislead knowledge base users into thinking pumps are the only supported equipment.

subject: IfcElement
rationale: IfcElement is a subtype of IfcObjectDefinition in the IFC schema hierarchy.

subject: IfcElement
rationale: IfcElement instances are typically contained in a spatial structure via IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure.

subject: IfcElement
rationale: Openings in walls require IfcRelFillsElement to associate the filling element.

subject: IfcElement
rationale: IfcElement can participate in connectivity relationships via IfcRelConnectsElements.
conditions: when elements are physically connected

subject: IfcElement

subject: IfcElement
rationale: IfcElement can contain material layers via IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage.

subject: IfcElement
rationale: IfcElement uses IfcLocalPlacement for positioning within the building model.
conditions: when the element has a defined position in 3D space
exceptions: elements without geometric representation

subject: IfcElement
rationale: IfcElement typically requires a geometric representation via IfcProductRepresentation.
conditions: when the element has a geometric representation
exceptions: non-geometric elements

subject: IfcElement
rationale: IfcElement can be part of an aggregation relationship via IfcRelAggregates.
conditions: when the element is part of a larger assembly

subject: IfcElement
rationale: IfcElement connects to voids via IfcRelVoidsElement relationship.
conditions: when the element has an opening or void created in it

subject: IfcElementAssembly
rationale: IfcElementAssembly is a type of IfcElement that groups multiple elements together, so it logically contains other IfcElements.
conditions: when the assembly is composed of multiple elements
exceptions: single-element assemblies

subject: IfcElementAssembly

conditions: to define the hierarchical decomposition of the assembly

subject: IfcElementAssembly
rationale: Structural element assemblies like trusses or frames support the building's load-bearing system.
applicability: The assertion says IfcElementAssembly 'supports' Load-Bearing Frame, but this mixes a physical building system concept (load-bearing frame) with an abstract entity type. IfcElementAssembly can be used for load-bearing frames, but the 'supports' relation is ambiguous - it could mean spatial containment (IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure) or structural connection (IfcRelConnectsStructural). The assertion lacks specificity about which IFC relationship is meant.
conditions: when the assembly is part of the structural system
exceptions: non-structural assemblies like curtain walls

subject: IfcElementAssembly
rationale: Reinforced concrete element assemblies may contain reinforcing bars or meshes.
conditions: when the assembly is a reinforced concrete or masonry assembly
exceptions: unreinforced assemblies

subject: IfcElementAssembly
rationale: IfcElementAssembly can be decomposed into IfcBuildingElementPart components via aggregation relationships.
conditions: when the assembly is decomposed into parts

subject: IfcElementAssemblyType
rationale: IfcElementAssemblyType defines the type information for IfcElementAssembly occurrences
conditions: When representing assemblies of building elements

subject: IfcElementAssemblyType
rationale: IfcElementAssemblyType is used with IfcRelAggregates to define element composition/decomposition relationships
conditions: When defining hierarchical assemblies

subject: IfcElementAssemblyType
rationale: Type definitions often have associated property sets defining performance or material characteristics
conditions: When applying type-specific properties

subject: IfcElementAssemblyType
rationale: IfcElementAssemblyType participates in IfcRelDefinesByType relationship to assign type information to IfcElementAssembly instances
conditions: When assigning type to occurrences

subject: IfcElementAssemblyType
rationale: IfcElementAssemblyType can relate to sub-components via nesting relationships in some IFC schemas
applicability: IfcRelNests is used for part-whole relationships between types (e.g., IfcElementAssemblyType nesting other types), but this only applies to type-level nesting, not occurrence-level assembly composition. The condition should explicitly note this applies only to type-level decomposition.
conditions: When assembly has nested sub-assemblies or components

subject: IfcElementAssemblyType
rationale: Type definitions may have associated representation maps for geometry
conditions: When a geometric representation is defined for the type

subject: IfcElementAssemblyType
rationale: Element assembly types can be classified using external classification systems like OmniClass, Uniclass
conditions: When the assembly type needs classification according to standards

subject: IfcElementComponent
rationale: IfcElementComponent is a subtype of IfcElement and is typically used as a sub-part or component of IfcBuildingElement instances (e.g., reinforcement in a beam, bolt in a structural connection).
conditions: when serving as a component of a building element

subject: IfcElementComponent
rationale: IfcElementComponent typically participates in aggregation relationships (IfcRelAggregates) where it is the child element within a parent assembly.
conditions: when it is part of a larger assembly
exceptions: when IfcElementComponent is used standalone

IfcElementComponent can also participate in IfcRelNests relationships (not just IfcRelAggregates) to indicate part-of hierarchy in certain domains. The dependency on IfcRelAggregates is too narrow when nesting via IfcRelNests is also valid for assemblies.

subject: IfcElementComponent
rationale: Element components often rely on connection relationships to be properly positioned and function within an assembly.
conditions: when it needs to be connected to other elements
exceptions: IfcElementComponent does not necessarily depend on IfcRelConnectsElements when connected via IfcRelConnectsPathElements, IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements, or other subtypes of IfcRelConnects. The dependency should be generalized to the supertype IfcRelConnects or more specific subtypes depending on connection semantics.

subject: IfcElementComponent
rationale: Element components like brackets, bolts, and connectors provide support to structural members in load paths.
conditions: when acting as a bracket, connector, or fastener
exceptions: when the component is purely decorative

subject: IfcElementComponent
rationale: Every element component must have an associated material (e.g., steel, concrete, timber) to define its physical behavior and properties.
applicability: IfcElementComponent does not require IfcMaterial in all cases; material assignment is optional in IFC. Many components may have material defined by their parent assembly or be assigned a material through IfcMaterialConstituentSet or other indirect methods, not a direct IfcMaterial assignment.
conditions: when a material assignment defines its physical properties

subject: IfcElementComponent
rationale: Element components often depend on property sets to define their specific dimensions, performance ratings, and classification.
conditions: when specific performance or geometric properties are defined
exceptions: IfcElementComponent does not require IfcPropertySet for its existence; property sets are optional in IFC. A component can exist with only basic attributes (e.g., Name, Description) and no property sets. The condition 'when specific performance or geometric properties are defined' correctly identifies this as conditional, making the assertion effectively correct when conditional, but the 'depends_on' language implies a stronger dependency than warranted.

subject: IfcElementComponent
rationale: Some element components (e.g., a panel filling an opening) require the IfcRelFillsElement relationship to be properly positioned.
conditions: when the component fills an opening in an element
exceptions: when the component does not occupy an opening

subject: IfcElementComponent
rationale: IfcElementComponent includes fastener types; fasteners connect to the elements they join together.
conditions: when the component is a mechanical connector type

subject: IfcElementComponentType
rationale: In IFC, an IfcElementComponentType defines common properties for one or more IfcElementComponent occurrences. The type 'contains' the element occurrences that instantiate it.
conditions: When representing a type definition that contains common properties for multiple occurrences

subject: IfcElementComponentType
rationale: IfcElementComponentType depends on IfcPropertySetDefinition to define its type-level properties (e.g., material thickness, mechanical properties).
conditions: When type properties are defined via property sets

subject: IfcElementComponentType
rationale: Element component types often depend on material definitions to specify composition and structural behavior.
conditions: When material properties are assigned at the type level

subject: IfcElementComponentType
rationale: IfcElementComponentType supports IfcRelDefinesByType which links the type to its individual element occurrences, enabling consistent property assignment.
conditions: When establishing the relationship between type and occurrences

subject: IfcElementComponentType

conditions: When the type defines a geometric representation shared by occurrences
exceptions: Not required if no shared geometry is defined at the type level

subject: IfcElementComponentType
rationale: As an IFC entity, IfcElementComponentType requires IfcOwnerHistory for ownership and versioning information.
conditions: Always required for IFC entity creation

subject: IfcElementComponentType
rationale: IfcElementComponentType can be connected via IfcRelNests to parent types or sub-types in an assembly hierarchy.
applicability: The assertion says IfcElementComponentType 'connects_to IfcRelNests'. However, IfcRelNests relates an object (the whole) to related objects (parts). IfcElementComponentType, being an abstract type definition, would be the RelatingObject in IfcRelNests only if it represents a whole composition. While technically possible, this is extremely uncommon for IfcElementComponentType which represents components like bolts, connectors, or reinforcement elements — it would more typically be a RelatedObject. The assertion lacks this directional context.
conditions: When the type is part of a nested composition hierarchy
exceptions: Not all types participate in nesting relationships

subject: IfcElementComponentType
rationale: IfcElementComponentType may depend on external references for classification or catalog-based component definitions.
conditions: When referencing external standards, catalogs, or classification systems

subject: IfcElementComponentType
rationale: Element component types support higher-level building assemblies by providing standardized component types that can be assembled together.
conditions: When element components are assembled into larger building assemblies

subject: IfcElementQuantity
rationale: IfcElementQuantity is defined in IFC schema and must be associated with elements through IfcRelDefinesByProperties relationship to be meaningful.

subject: IfcElementQuantity
rationale: IfcElementQuantity contains one or more instances of IfcPhysicalQuantity subtypes (e.g., IfcQuantityLength, IfcQuantityArea, IfcQuantityVolume, IfcQuantityCount, IfcQuantityWeight, IfcQuantityTime) to store actual measured values.
applicability: IfcElementQuantity contains IfcPhysicalQuantity is too broad. IfcElementQuantity specifically contains IfcPhysicalQuantity subtypes via IfcQuantitySet (IfcElementQuantity IS-A IfcQuantitySet), but the relationship is a composition of specific subtypes like IfcQuantityLength, IfcQuantityArea, etc., not the abstract IfcPhysicalQuantity directly in all contexts. In IFC2x3 and IFC4, IfcElementQuantity inherits from IfcPropertySetDefinition, and its contained quantities are IfcPhysicalQuantity subtypes, but the direct containment is through the 'Quantities' attribute which expects IfcPhysicalQuantity.

subject: IfcElementQuantity

subject: IfcElementQuantity
rationale: IfcElementQuantity uses IfcQuantityArea as a contained physical quantity for area-related measurements of building elements (e.g., wall surfaces, floor areas).

subject: IfcElementQuantity
rationale: IfcElementQuantity uses IfcQuantityVolume as a contained physical quantity for volume measurements (e.g., concrete volumes).

subject: IfcElementQuantity
rationale: IfcElementQuantity uses IfcQuantityCount as a contained physical quantity for counting items (e.g., number of windows, doors).

subject: IfcElementQuantity
rationale: IfcElementQuantity uses IfcQuantityWeight as a contained physical quantity for weight measurements (e.g., steel weight).

subject: IfcElementQuantity
rationale: IfcElementQuantity uses IfcQuantityTime as a contained physical quantity for time-based measurements.

subject: IfcElementQuantity
rationale: IfcElementQuantity provides quantitative property information (like areas, volumes, counts) for IfcElement instances, supporting quantity takeoffs, cost estimation, and analysis.

subject: IfcElementQuantity
rationale: IfcElementQuantity inherits from IfcPropertyDefinition which relates to IfcObjectDefinition, and quantities are typically defined relative to object definitions in the IFC model.

subject: IfcElementQuantity
rationale: In IFC2x3 and some Model View Definitions, IfcElementQuantity can be related to property sets, though in IFC4 it is more commonly used independently.

The assertion states IfcElementQuantity depends_on IfcPropertySetDefinition, but in IFC4, IfcElementQuantity IS-A IfcPropertySetDefinition (subtype), so it does not depend on it. The existing exception correctly notes it can exist independently. The assertion itself is architecturally incorrect as IfcElementQuantity inherits from IfcPropertySetDefinition in the IFC schema.

rationale: IfcElementType relies on IfcRelDefinesByType to define which occurrences (IfcElement instances) are of that type.

subject: IfcElementType
rationale: IfcElementType can have property sets assigned through IfcRelDefinesByProperties, which provide functional parameters.

subject: IfcElementType
rationale: IfcElementType aggregates property set definitions that describe its technical characteristics.
conditions: When property sets are assigned to the type

subject: IfcElementType
rationale: Element types often require defined materials (through IfcRelAssociatesMaterial) to specify what they are made of.

rationale: IfcElementType can have a representation map defining the geometric shape shared by all occurrences.

subject: IfcElementType
rationale: To link element occurrences to their type, the IfcRelDefinesByType relationship is required.

subject: IfcElementarySurface
rationale: IfcElementarySurface has a Position attribute of type IfcAxis2Placement3D, which is a subtype of IfcPlacement.
applicability: While IfcElementarySurface does use IfcPlacement for its position, the dependency is specifically on IfcAxis2Placement3D (a subtype of IfcPlacement), not on the general IfcPlacement class. The assertion is too broad as it suggests a dependency on the abstract supertype rather than the specific concrete placement type used.
conditions: For defining the coordinate system and position of the surface

subject: IfcElementarySurface
rationale: The Position attribute of IfcElementarySurface is of type IfcAxis2Placement3D.
conditions: For specifying the location and orientation of the surface in 3D space

subject: IfcElementarySurface
rationale: IfcPlane is a subtype of IfcElementarySurface, meaning the elementary surface can contain/represent a planar surface.
applicability: In IFC, IfcPlane is a subtype of IfcElementarySurface (via IfcElementarySurface specialization), not a separately 'contained' item. The 'contains' relationship is misleading - IfcPlane IS an IfcElementarySurface, not an element that IfcElementarySurface contains. The assertion describes a subtype relationship rather than a containment/composition relationship.
conditions: When IfcElementarySurface is instantiated as an unbounded plane

subject: IfcElementarySurface
rationale: IfcCylindricalSurface is a subtype of IfcElementarySurface.
conditions: When IfcElementarySurface is instantiated as a cylindrical surface

subject: IfcElementarySurface
rationale: IfcSphericalSurface is a subtype of IfcElementarySurface.
applicability: In IFC, IfcSphericalSurface IS a subtype of IfcElementarySurface, not a separately 'contained' element. The 'contains' relationship terminology is incorrect - this is a subtype (inheritance) relationship, not a containment or aggregation relationship.
conditions: When IfcElementarySurface is instantiated as a spherical surface

subject: IfcElementarySurface
rationale: IfcToroidalSurface is a subtype of IfcElementarySurface.
applicability: In IFC, IfcToroidalSurface IS a subtype of IfcElementarySurface, not a separately 'contained' element. The 'contains' relationship terminology is incorrect - this is a subtype (inheritance) relationship, not a containment or aggregation relationship.
conditions: When IfcElementarySurface is instantiated as a toroidal surface

subject: IfcElementarySurface
rationale: IfcElementarySurface can be used as the geometry underlying faces in surface models.
conditions: When used as a face geometry in a surface model

subject: IfcElementarySurface
rationale: IfcCurveBoundedPlane uses an IfcPlane (subtype of IfcElementarySurface) as its BasisSurface.
conditions: When providing the unbounded basis surface for a bounded plane

subject: IfcEllipse
rationale: An IfcEllipse is defined geometrically by its centre point (location), semi-axis 1 and semi-axis 2 lengths, which are positioned using IfcCartesianPoint coordinates.
applicability: The assertion states IfcEllipse 'depends_on' IfcCartesianPoint, but IfcEllipse in IFC is not an entity that directly depends on IfcCartesianPoint. IfcEllipse is a geometric representation item that may reference placement via IfcAxis2Placement which uses IfcCartesianPoint, but the direct dependency is inaccurate. IfcEllipse uses IfcAxis2Placement (2D or 3D) which in turn references IfcCartesianPoint; the dependency is indirect.
conditions: When used to define the position and axes of the ellipse

subject: IfcEllipse
rationale: The ellipse's orientation and position in a 2D coordinate system are defined by an IfcAxis2Placement2D, which provides the location and direction of axes.
conditions: When defining the ellipse in a 2D plane

subject: IfcEllipse
rationale: IfcEllipse can serve as the basis for IfcEllipseProfileDef, which defines a 2D elliptical cross-section used in extrusion.
conditions: When the ellipse is used as a profile definition for extruded shapes

subject: IfcEllipse
rationale: The ellipse geometry provides the dimensional basis for the profile definition, which in turn defines the shape of extruded solid elements.
conditions: When the ellipse defines a profile for structural members like columns or beams

subject: IfcEllipseProfileDef
rationale: IfcEllipseProfileDef defines an ellipse as a 2D profile; its position and orientation depend on IfcAxis2Placement2D.
conditions: When defining the ellipse in a 2D plane

subject: IfcEllipseProfileDef
rationale: IfcEllipseProfileDef can be used as the SweptArea in IfcExtrudedAreaSolid to create elliptical solid geometry for columns or decorative elements.
conditions: When the ellipse profile is extruded to create a solid shape

subject: IfcEllipseProfileDef
rationale: IfcEllipseProfileDef can serve as the SweptArea in IfcRevolvedAreaSolid for creating revolved solid geometry.
conditions: When the ellipse profile is revolved to create a solid shape

subject: IfcEllipseProfileDef
rationale: IfcEllipseProfileDef is contained within IfcShapeRepresentation as a geometric representation item for products.
conditions: When used as part of a product representation

subject: IfcEllipseProfileDef
rationale: IfcEllipseProfileDef is a subtype of IfcProfileDef, from which it inherits the ProfileName and ProfileType attributes.
conditions: Inheritance relationship

subject: IfcEllipseProfileDef
rationale: The ellipse profile can be referenced by IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage to associate material properties with the elliptical cross-section.
conditions: When the ellipse profile defines a structural cross-section with material assignment

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDevice
rationale: Energy conversion devices are part of building distribution systems (e.g., heating, cooling, electrical) and require connection to these systems.
conditions: Must be connected to the relevant distribution system

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDevice
rationale: Devices like boilers, chillers, and heat exchangers require piping or duct segments to transport the working fluid.
applicability: The assertion says IfcEnergyConversionDevice requires IfcFlowSegment for fluid-based conversion devices, but in IFC, a device may connect directly to another device without an intervening IfcFlowSegment (e.g., a chiller connected directly to a pump via a port). The requirement is too strong; connections can be direct port-to-port.
conditions: For fluid-based energy conversion devices
exceptions: Solid-state conversion devices may not need flow segments

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDevice
rationale: Valves, dampers, and other controllers are needed to regulate the flow of energy carriers through conversion devices.
conditions: For regulating flow of energy carrier
exceptions: Not all IfcEnergyConversionDevice requires Therefore, IfcFlowController for regulating flow. For example, a solid-state heat pump or a photovoltaic inverter performs energy conversion without needing a flow controller in the IFC decomposition. The assertion should allow exceptions for devices where flow regulation is not modeled or not applicable.

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDevice
rationale: Energy conversion devices depend on building elements like slabs, walls, or structural frames for physical support.
conditions: For physical mounting and support

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDevice
rationale: Energy conversion devices support distribution ports by providing converted energy to the building's distribution network.
conditions: When acting as a terminal or source

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDevice
rationale: Energy conversion devices may contain internal distribution elements like coils, pipes, or electrical windings.
conditions: As internal components

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDevice
rationale: Some energy conversion devices contain integrated pumps or fans to move the energy carrier fluid.
conditions: For integrated pump/fan assemblies
exceptions: Devices without moving parts

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDevice
rationale: Energy conversion devices connect to distribution circuits to deliver converted energy throughout the building.
conditions: When part of an electrical or fluid circuit
exceptions: IfcEnergyConversionDevice typically connects to IfcDistributionCircuit through its ports (IfcDistributionPort -> IfcDistributionPort -> IfcDistributionCircuit via IfcRelConnectsPorts). The direct 'connects_to' relationship between the device and the circuit is not a native IFC relationship; it is mediated by ports. The assertion oversimplifies the connection model.

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDevice
rationale: Hydronic energy conversion devices (boilers, chillers) connect to pipe segments for fluid transport.
conditions: For hydronic systems
exceptions: Air-based or electrical systems

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDevice
rationale: Air-based energy conversion devices connect to duct segments for air distribution.
conditions: For air-based systems
exceptions: Hydronic or electrical systems

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDevice
rationale: Electrical energy conversion devices like transformers connect to cable segments for power distribution.
conditions: For electrical conversion devices
exceptions: Non-electrical devices

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDeviceType
rationale: IfcEnergyConversionDeviceType is the type definition for IfcEnergyConversionDevice occurrences; the type depends on the occurrence concept for instantiation.
conditions: when considering physical realization

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDeviceType
rationale: Property sets are required to define performance characteristics like efficiency, capacity, pressure ratings for energy conversion devices.
conditions: when specifying product properties

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDeviceType
rationale: The type definition is connected to its occurrence via the 'DefinesType' relationship in IFC.

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDeviceType
rationale: Material definitions may be associated with the type to specify materials used in device construction.
conditions: when defining material composition of device types

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDeviceType
rationale: The relationship entity IfcRelDefinesByType is required to link occurrence objects to their type definition.
conditions: in IFC data model instantiation

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDeviceType
rationale: Energy conversion device types support the distribution systems they serve by providing converted energy (heat, cooling, electricity).
conditions: when the device is assigned to a system

subject: IfcEnergyConversionDeviceType
rationale: An IfcEnergyConversionDeviceType can contain property set definitions that define its technical characteristics.

subject: IfcEngine
rationale: Engines commonly drive pumps for fluid transport in building systems.
applicability: The applicability is limited to water supply, HVAC, and industrial processes, but the assertion does not capture that in other contexts (e.g., automotive, marine, portable equipment) the relationship between an engine and a pump may be modeled differently or may not be supported by IfcEngine at all.
conditions: Engine shaft coupled to a pump
exceptions: Engine not used for pumping applications

subject: IfcEngineType
rationale: Engines can provide mechanical power to drive water or fuel pumps.
applicability: The assertion only applies to engines that directly drive a pump shaft via mechanical coupling (e.g., internal combustion engines). It does not cover engines that drive pumps through belts, gearboxes, clutches, or other indirect mechanical linkages, even though such configurations are common in fire pump and cooling water pump installations.
conditions: Engine directly drives a pump shaft
exceptions: Electric motor-driven pumps

An engine driving a pump via a flexible coupling with a long shaft (non-direct) or through a right-angle gear drive, which is common in vertical turbine fire pumps, does not strictly satisfy 'directly drives a pump shaft' yet is functionally identical. The assertion's condition is ambiguous about what constitutes 'directly drives'.

subject: IfcEvaporativeCoolerType
rationale: A bleed-off or purge system is needed to flush out concentrated minerals and maintain water quality.
conditions: For bleed-off/water purge to prevent mineral buildup

subject: IfcEvaporativeCoolerType
rationale: The cooler connects to the building water supply piping for automatic fill.
conditions: For makeup water connection

subject: IfcEvaporativeCooler
rationale: The evaporative cooler requires a connection to the building water supply system.
applicability: The assertion does not address whether the connection includes necessary backflow prevention devices, which are typically required by plumbing codes and could affect the IfcElement modeling of the connection point.
conditions: Permanent installations with automatic water feed
exceptions: Manual fill units do not require connection

subject: IfcEvaporator
rationale: The evaporator is connected to the rest of the refrigeration system via refrigerant piping (suction line and liquid line).
applicability: All building types with mechanical cooling

Not all IfcEvaporator instances connect to refrigerant piping. In some hydronic or evaporative cooling systems (e.g., chillers with shell-and-tube evaporators), the evaporator may connect to chilled water piping on the secondary side rather than directly to refrigerant piping. Also, in district cooling or certain industrial setups, the evaporator is part of a heat exchanger arrangement where the primary connection is to a brine or water loop.
conditions: For all refrigeration cycle configurations

subject: IfcEvaporatorType
rationale: Piping connects the evaporator to other HVAC components for refrigerant circulation.
applicability: The assertion states 'IfcEvaporatorType depends_on Refrigerant Piping' with applicability 'All refrigeration systems', but evaporators can also be used in air conditioning and heat pump systems (not just refrigeration), and in some cases (e.g., air-cooled chillers) the refrigerant piping may be part of a packaged unit rather than a separate depended-upon system. Additionally, some evaporator types (e.g., flooded evaporators) have different piping dependencies than DX evaporators.
conditions: For refrigerant transport between components
exceptions: A direct-expansion (DX) evaporator in a packaged rooftop unit may include integral refrigerant piping within the factory-assembled package rather than having a dependency on external refrigerant piping as a separate system. The dependency on external field-installed piping is not universal.

subject: IfcEventTime
rationale: In a schedule, IfcEventTime may reference lag time between activities, which is modeled via IfcLagTime.
conditions: when defining predecessor/successor relationships with lag

subject: IfcEventTime
rationale: IfcEventTime directly provides timing attributes (early/late start, early/late finish, duration) for an IfcEvent.
applicability: all building types with project scheduling

subject: IfcEventTime
rationale: IfcEventTime defines the temporal constraints of events within an IfcWorkPlan, supporting schedule generation and tracking.
conditions: when the event is part of a work plan schedule

subject: IfcEventTime
rationale: IfcEventTime provides the timing information for events aggregated in an IfcWorkSchedule.
conditions: when the event is part of a work schedule

subject: IfcEventTime
rationale: IfcEvent is a subtype of IfcProcess, and IfcEventTime is associated with IfcEvent, thereby indirectly connecting to the process hierarchy for scheduling.
conditions: when an IfcEvent is a subtype of IfcProcess

subject: IfcEvent
rationale: IfcEvent is assigned to processes via IfcRelAssignsToProcess, which defines the relationship between events and the tasks/processes they trigger or depend on.
conditions: when IfcEvent is associated with a process or task

subject: IfcEvent
rationale: IfcEvent uses IfcRelSequence to define the predecessor/successor relationships with other events or processes, establishing a timeline.
conditions: when events are ordered in a sequence (time-based dependency)

subject: IfcEvent
rationale: IfcEvent requires IfcEventTime to define occurrence dates, durations, and schedules for the event.
conditions: when scheduling or timing is required

subject: IfcEvent
rationale: IfcEvent exists within the context of an IfcProject which aggregates all project-related information including events.
conditions: as part of a project work breakdown structure

subject: IfcEvent
rationale: IfcEvent can be assigned to IfcControl entities (e.g., IfcWorkPlan, IfcWorkSchedule) via IfcRelAssignsToControl.
conditions: when the event is controlled by or related to a control (like a schedule or work plan)

subject: IfcEvent
rationale: IfcEvent supports the execution of work plans by defining key milestones, triggers, or time-based occurrences that affect project flow.
conditions: when events are part of project planning and scheduling

subject: IfcEvent
rationale: IfcEvent instances serve as milestones or time-dependent triggers within work schedules.
conditions: when events define milestones or deadlines within a schedule

subject: IfcEvent
rationale: IfcEvent is a subtype of IfcProcess, and may depend on other processes (IfcTask, IfcProcedure) via sequence relationships.
conditions: when the event triggers or is triggered by a process

subject: IfcEvent
rationale: IfcEvent can contain IfcPropertySet instances via IfcRelDefinesByProperties to hold additional property definitions.
conditions: when event attributes need to be extended with custom properties

subject: IfcEvent
rationale: IfcEvent can be linked to other IFC objects through IfcRelDefinesByObject for general object relationships.
conditions: when the event is related to other objects in the model

subject: IfcEvent
rationale: IfcEvent may reference IfcActor or IfcActorRole to define who is responsible for or participates in the event.
conditions: when the event involves specific actors or roles

subject: IfcEvent
rationale: IfcEvent can be related to IfcProduct entities (building elements, systems, etc.) via IfcRelAssignsToProduct, linking events to physical components.
conditions: when the event is assigned to building products or components

subject: IfcEventType
rationale: IfcEventType is a subtype of IfcTypeProcess and is used to define event type information in a process model. It depends on the general IfcProcess structure for its scheduling and process representation.
conditions: when representing event-based processes in a construction or facility management schedule

subject: IfcEventType
rationale: IfcEventType defines the shared properties for IfcEvent instances. The type contains the common attributes that apply to multiple event occurrences.
conditions: when defining the type of an event occurrence

subject: IfcEventType
rationale: The IfcEventType is related to IfcEvent instances via IfcRelDefinesByType relationship, which is the standard IFC mechanism for assigning type objects to occurrences.
conditions: when linking event type definitions to event occurrences

subject: IfcEventType
rationale: IfcEventType can have property sets (IfcPropertySetDefinition) assigned to define its characteristics, making it dependent on these property definitions for complete type specification.
conditions: when event types have specific property sets assigned

subject: IfcEventType
rationale: IfcEventType defines event types (e.g., milestones, arrivals, inspections) that support the creation of work plans and construction schedules.
conditions: when event types are used in construction scheduling and work planning
exceptions: not applicable if event types are used purely for non-scheduled event classification

subject: IfcEventType
rationale: Event types can support task definitions by defining start/trigger events or completion events within a work schedule.
conditions: when events are part of a task sequence or depend on tasks

subject: IfcEventType
rationale: IfcEventType may be associated with external classifications (e.g., UniClass, OmniClass) through IfcRelAssociatesClassification for better semantic definition.
conditions: when event types are classified according to external classification systems

subject: IfcEventType
rationale: Event types may be associated with materials (e.g., a 'Material Delivery' event type) through material association relationships.
conditions: when event types are associated with specific materials being delivered or inspected

subject: IfcExtendedProperties
rationale: IfcExtendedProperties is an abstract supertype that extends IfcPropertySet to allow properties to be organized into hierarchical groups, thus depends on property sets for context.
applicability: all IFC models using property definitions
conditions: when extended properties are defined as part of a property set

subject: IfcExtendedProperties
rationale: Extended properties contain individual property definitions (IfcProperty entities) as their members.
conditions: when defining individual property entries within the extended set

subject: IfcExtendedProperties
rationale: IfcExtendedProperties (specifically its subtypes like IfcMaterialProperties) contains a list of IfcProperty instances.
conditions: when the extended properties entity holds property definitions
exceptions: IfcExtendedProperties contains IfcProperty generally, but the List of IfcProperty can also include subtypes like IfcComplexProperty. However, there is a cardinality constraint - if the IfcExtendedProperties is empty (zero properties), the containment does not hold. Also, IfcExtendedProperties can exist without containing any properties in certain intermediate states.

subject: IfcExtendedProperties
rationale: IfcExtendedProperties can contain IfcComplexProperty to allow nested property groupings.
conditions: when properties are nested in hierarchical structures
exceptions: IfcExtendedProperties contains IfcComplexProperty only indirectly. The 'Properties' attribute is of type LIST OF IfcProperty, and IfcComplexProperty is a subtype of IfcProperty, so it can be included. However, the assertion states 'contains IfcComplexProperty' as a direct relationship, which is correct only because of inheritance. More importantly, IfcComplexProperty is not always present - it's only present when hierarchical/nested properties are defined, which is a specific condition.

subject: IfcExtendedProperties
rationale: As a subtype of IfcPropertyDefinition, IfcExtendedProperties supports the definition of properties that can be assigned to objects.
conditions: when extended properties are used to define characteristics of elements

subject: IfcExtendedProperties
rationale: IfcExtendedProperties is a subtype of IfcPropertySetDefinition, therefore it depends on the property set definition mechanism for assignment to IFC objects.
conditions: when extended properties are part of a property set definition assigned to objects

subject: IfcExtendedProperties
rationale: IfcMaterialProperties (a subtype of IfcExtendedProperties) defines properties for IfcMaterialDefinition entities.
conditions: when using IfcMaterialProperties subtype, which extends IfcExtendedProperties for material-specific properties

subject: IfcExtendedProperties
rationale: IfcProfileProperties (a subtype of IfcExtendedProperties) defines properties associated with IfcProfileDef entities.
conditions: when using IfcProfileProperties subtype for profile-specific extended properties

subject: IfcExtendedProperties
rationale: Extended properties ultimately support IFC objects (products, processes, controls, etc.) by providing structured property data.
applicability: all IFC objects requiring property assignment

IfcExtendedProperties does not directly support IfcObject. IfcExtendedProperties (or its subtypes) are typically part of IfcMaterialProperties which are assigned via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial to IfcMaterial or via IfcRelDefinesByProperties only if wrapped in an IfcPropertySet. The direct 'supports IfcObject' statement bypasses the intermediate relationship through IfcMaterial or IfcPropertySet, which is a significant context limitation.
conditions: when property sets containing extended properties are assigned to objects via IfcRelDefinesByProperties

subject: IfcExtendedProperties
rationale: IfcExtendedProperties connects to IfcRelDefinesByProperties to associate property definitions with IFC objects.
conditions: when establishing the relationship between property sets and objects

subject: IfcExternalInformation
rationale: IfcExternalInformation is typically referenced through IfcExternalReferenceRelationship to attach external classification, document, or library data to IFC building elements.
conditions: when used to associate external data with IFC objects

subject: IfcExternalInformation
rationale: IfcExternalInformation is typically part of an IfcProject context, but can also exist independently as a shared external reference.
conditions: when instantiated within a building model context
exceptions: can exist as standalone external data without project context

subject: IfcExternalReference
rationale: IfcExternalReference is used to link external references (like classification systems, library references) to objects. IfcExternalReferenceRelationship is the relationship object that associates an IfcExternalReference with IfcObjects. Without It, the reference cannot be linked to building elements.

subject: IfcExternalReference
rationale: IfcExternalReference is often used to reference external classification systems. IfcClassification provides the classification notation/source that IfcExternalReference can point to.

subject: IfcExternalReference
rationale: IfcExternalReference can reference external documents. IfcDocumentInformation provides the metadata for documents that IfcExternalReference may link to.

subject: IfcExternalReference
rationale: IfcExternalReference can reference external library items. IfcLibraryInformation provides metadata about a library that an IfcExternalReference may point to.

subject: IfcExternalReference
rationale: IfcExternalReference is linked to IfcObjects via IfcExternalReferenceRelationship instances. The 'connects_to' captures the bidirectional association between the reference and its relationship object.

subject: IfcExternalReference
rationale: IfcClassificationReference is a subtype of IfcExternalReference specifically used for classification references. IfcExternalReference supports this specialization.

subject: IfcExternalReference
rationale: IfcDocumentReference is a subtype of IfcExternalReference specifically used for document references. IfcExternalReference supports this specialization.

subject: IfcExternalReference
rationale: IfcLibraryReference is a subtype of IfcExternalReference specifically used for library references. IfcExternalReference supports this specialization.

subject: IfcExternalReferenceRelationship
rationale: The relationship connects an external reference (e.g., a classification or document reference) to an object. Without an IfcExternalReference, there is nothing to relate.
conditions: for the relationship to have meaning

subject: IfcExternalReferenceRelationship
rationale: The related objects in this relationship are typically subtypes of IfcRoot (objects, properties, etc.) that need external classification or documentation references.
conditions: when associating external references to IFC objects

subject: IfcExternalReferenceRelationship
rationale: IfcExternalReferenceRelationship links IfcClassificationReference (a subtype of IfcExternalReference) to objects, enabling classification systems like Uniclass or OmniClass.
conditions: when used for classification referencing

subject: IfcExternalReferenceRelationship
rationale: The relationship can link IfcDocumentReference (subtype of IfcExternalReference) to objects, supporting document management.
conditions: when used for document referencing

subject: IfcExternalReferenceRelationship
rationale: The relationship can link IfcLibraryReference to objects, supporting library/catalogue references.
conditions: when used for library referencing

subject: IfcExternalReferenceRelationship
rationale: IfcExternalReferenceRelationship can associate external references to property definitions (subtypes of IfcRoot) for enhanced metadata.
conditions: when associating external references to property definitions

subject: IfcExternalReferenceRelationship
rationale: The relationship can optionally connect external references to actor roles, though this is less common.
conditions: when associating external references to roles

subject: IfcExternalReferenceRelationship
rationale: By attaching external references (classifications, documents, libraries) to building objects, this relationship enriches the information model.
conditions: when enriched with external classification or documentation

subject: IfcExternalSpatialElement
rationale: IfcExternalSpatialElement represents the external spatial environment that contains or bounds a building.
conditions: when serving as the external spatial container

subject: IfcExternalSpatialElement
rationale: The external spatial element can contain site-related spatial context.
conditions: when used for external spaces beyond the building footprint

subject: IfcExternalSpatialElement
rationale: The relationship between external spatial elements and building spaces is defined via space boundaries.
conditions: to define spatial boundaries between internal spaces and the external environment

subject: IfcExternalSpatialElement
rationale: Elements can be contained in the external spatial structure via this relationship.
conditions: to associate building elements contained in the external spatial context

subject: IfcExternalSpatialElement
rationale: External spatial elements can be connected to storeys at the building perimeter.
conditions: when defining multi-storey external spaces or balconies

subject: IfcExternalSpatialElement
rationale: External spatial elements define the outer boundary that internal spaces relate to via space boundaries.
conditions: by providing the external boundary reference for internal spaces

subject: IfcExternalSpatialElement
rationale: To be properly placed in the project spatial decomposition hierarchy.
applicability: IfcExternalSpatialElement is not typically part of a decomposed spatial structure via IfcRelAggregates. In IFC4, IfcExternalSpatialElement is used as a spatial zone representing the external space. It is usually not aggregated into larger spatial elements via IfcRelAggregates, but rather placed within the IfcSite or IfcProject as a decomposed element. The condition 'if the external spatial element is part of a decomposed spatial structure' is very narrow and rarely applies to IfcExternalSpatialElement.
conditions: if the external spatial element is part of a decomposed spatial structure

subject: IfcExternalSpatialElement
rationale: External spatial elements can conceptually bound protective elements but are not themselves protective.
conditions: when used to model external shading devices or weather barriers

subject: IfcExternalSpatialElement
rationale: All spatial structure elements including external spatial elements are part of the IfcProject spatial hierarchy.
conditions: as the root spatial context of the IFC model

subject: IfcExternalSpatialElement
rationale: Opening elements may be conceptually related to the external spatial boundary.
conditions: when representing external wall openings as part of the building envelope

subject: IfcExternalSpatialStructureElement
rationale: IfcExternalSpatialStructureElement depends on being part of an IfcBuilding to define the external spatial boundaries of the building.
conditions: when defining external spatial context

subject: IfcExternalSpatialStructureElement
rationale: IfcExternalSpatialStructureElement often depends on IfcSite as the top-level spatial container for external space definitions.
conditions: when used as the outermost external spatial container

subject: IfcExternalSpatialStructureElement
rationale: IfcExternalSpatialStructureElement can contain or aggregate IfcExternalSpatialElement instances that represent portions of external space.
conditions: as subtypes or related elements

subject: IfcExternalSpatialStructureElement
rationale: External spatial structure elements often connect to proxy building elements that represent external features like landscaping or site furniture.
applicability: IfcBuildingElementProxy is a proxy element and its connection to external spatial boundaries depends on its specific usage. In many IFC schemas, there is no direct 'connects_to' relationship between IfcExternalSpatialStructureElement and IfcBuildingElementProxy — spatial relationships are handled through IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure or IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure, not a direct connect. The assertion would benefit from specifying the relationship type.
conditions: when building elements occupy or intersect the external spatial boundary

subject: IfcExternalSpatialStructureElement
rationale: Uses IfcRelAggregates to define the containment relationship within the spatial structure.
conditions: for aggregating external spatial sub-elements

subject: IfcExternalSpatialStructureElement
rationale: Depends on this relationship type to link building elements that are placed in the external spatial context.
conditions: for containing building elements within the external space
exceptions: IfcExternalSpatialStructureElement (e.g., IfcSite) can contain building elements, but the relationship uses IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure only if the building element has a well-defined spatial placement within the site. For elements that intersect or touch the external boundary without being fully contained (e.g., a cantilevered structure extending beyond the building footprint), IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure is used instead of IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure. The assertion does not account for this exception.

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedHatchStyle
rationale: IfcExternallyDefinedHatchStyle is a subtype of IfcExternalReference, meaning it inherently depends on an external reference (location, URI, etc.) to locate the hatch pattern definition.
conditions: When the hatch style is defined by reference to an external source (e.g., a standard pattern library)

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedHatchStyle
rationale: A hatch style can be used to define the visual appearance of a surface, typically as part of a surface style rendering property set.
conditions: When surface rendering requires hatch pattern fill for graphical representation
exceptions: Not used if surface style uses only solid color or image textures

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedHatchStyle
rationale: Hatch pattern lines often reference curve styles; if the hatch pattern is externally defined, there may be an implicit dependency on curve style definitions for the hatch line geometry.
conditions: If hatch lines are defined using curves from external sources

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedHatchStyle
rationale: Externally defined hatch styles contribute to the graphical presentation of model elements and may be grouped within presentation layer assignments.
conditions: When the hatch pattern is assigned to a presentation layer for visual organization

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedHatchStyle
rationale: A transformation operator is often required to position and orient the externally defined hatch pattern correctly on the target element.
conditions: When the hatch pattern is transformed (scaled, rotated) relative to the element it fills

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedHatchStyle
rationale: An externally defined hatch style might contain indexed colour information as part of its pattern definition in the external reference.
conditions: When colour information is embedded in the external hatch definition

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedSurfaceStyle
rationale: IfcExternallyDefinedSurfaceStyle is a subtype of IfcSurfaceStyle and references an external source for surface style definition; it depends on the existence of a valid IfcSurfaceStyle definition or external reference.
conditions: When the external definition references a surface style

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedSurfaceStyle
rationale: Potentially similar external definition mechanism may be related, but no direct dependency is specified in the IFC schema.

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedSurfaceStyle
rationale: IfcExternallyDefinedSurfaceStyle can support rendering definitions by providing externally-defined surface appearance data.
conditions: When the external definition defines rendering properties

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedSurfaceStyle
rationale: Surface style definitions support the visual presentation of building elements in IFC models.
conditions: When used in a presentation context

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedSurfaceStyle
rationale: Surface styles may be connected to materials through association relationships, though not directly.
conditions: If the surface style is associated with a material definition

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedSurfaceStyle
rationale: The style may be assigned via presentation style assignment, creating a dependency on that assignment mechanism.
conditions: When assigned to a presentation style

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedTextFont
rationale: IfcExternallyDefinedTextFont references an external source via IfcDocumentReference to locate the font definition.
applicability: All IFC models using externally defined fonts
conditions: When the font is defined by an external document reference

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedTextFont
rationale: IfcExternallyDefinedTextFont inherits from IfcExternalReference to specify the location of the font definition.
conditions: When the font is defined via external URI or location

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedTextFont
rationale: The font defined by IfcExternallyDefinedTextFont can be used to render IfcTextLiteral instances in presentations.
applicability: While IfcTextLiteral can have a font assigned via IfcPresentationLayerAssignment or similar mechanisms, the direct relationship between IfcExternallyDefinedTextFont and IfcTextLiteral is indirect. IfcTextLiteral uses IfcTextFontSelect which includes IfcExternallyDefinedTextFont, but this is a select type alternative, not a direct 'supports' relationship. The connection exists but is mediated through IfcTextFontSelect.
conditions: When text literals require a specific external font for rendering

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedTextFont
rationale: IfcExternallyDefinedTextFont can be assigned as part of a presentation style to text elements.
applicability: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment can include IfcTextStyleForDefinedFont or IfcExternallyDefinedTextFont as part of presentation styles, but the path is: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment > IfcPresentationStyleSelect (select type) which does NOT directly include IfcExternallyDefinedTextFont. Instead, it's typically included via IfcTextStyle > IfcTextFontSelect. The relationship is more indirect than 'supports' implies.
conditions: When presentation styles include text font styling

subject: IfcExternallyDefinedTextFont
rationale: The externally defined font is connected to the project via the presentation and styling layer of the IFC model.
applicability: All IFC projects using custom fonts
conditions: When the project defines text styles using external fonts

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
rationale: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid requires a profile definition (swept area) as its basis for extrusion.
conditions: when defining the cross-section shape for extrusion

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
rationale: A 3D placement (position + axis) is needed to locate the extruded shape in 3D space.
conditions: when defining the position and orientation of the extruded solid

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
rationale: For physical element representations, the profile may be associated with a material profile set for material properties.
conditions: when the extruded solid represents a physical structural member requiring material properties
exceptions: geometric representations not tied to physical materials

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
rationale: The extruded solid is typically placed relative to an IfcLocalPlacement of the parent element.
conditions: when the extruded solid is used as the representation of a building element in a spatial context

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
rationale: The extruded solid can be faceted into a boundary representation for certain operations like mesh generation.
conditions: when the extrusion is converted to a boundary representation for rendering or analysis

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
rationale: IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered is a subtype that builds upon the base extrusion concept by allowing a different end profile.
conditions: when a tapered (varying cross-section) extrusion is needed

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
rationale: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid is typically contained within an IfcShapeRepresentation that specifies the representation context.
conditions: when the extruded solid is used as part of a shape representation (e.g., 'Body' or 'Axis' representation)

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
rationale: Beams are commonly represented as extruded area solids from a profile.
conditions: when the beam's geometry is defined by extrusion of a profile along a linear path

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
rationale: Columns are commonly represented as extruded area solids from a column profile.
conditions: when the column's geometry is defined by extrusion of a profile vertically

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
rationale: Walls can be represented by extruding a wall profile along a linear or vertical path.
conditions: when the wall's geometry is defined by vertical extrusion of a wall cross-section

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
rationale: Slabs can be represented using extruded area solids from a slab-like profile.
conditions: when the slab's geometry is defined by extrusion of a slab cross-section

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
rationale: Footings often use extruded area solids for their geometric representation.
conditions: when the footing is modeled as an extruded prismatic shape

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid
rationale: Piles can be represented as extruded solids from a circular or rectangular profile.
conditions: when the pile's geometry is defined by extrusion of a cross-section

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered requires profile definitions for both the start and end cross-sections to define the tapered solid.
conditions: For defining the cross-sectional shape

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered is a subtype of IfcExtrudedAreaSolid and inherits its extrusion properties.
conditions: As the base representation type

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: An extrusion direction vector is required to define how the profile is extruded.
conditions: For defining the extrusion direction

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: A position coordinate system is needed to place the extruded solid correctly in the model.
conditions: For positioning the solid in 3D space

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: The tapered solid representation is commonly used to define the geometry of structural building elements that have varying cross-sections along their length.
applicability: Structural columns, beams, walls, and other linear elements with varying cross-section
conditions: When used as the representation of a building element

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: Tapered extruded solids are commonly used to represent columns that taper from a wider base to a narrower top (or vice versa).
conditions: When modeling tapered columns

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: Tapered beams (e.g., haunched beams) can be represented using IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered.
conditions: When modeling tapered beams or haunches

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: For tapered elements, material profiles may need to be associated with the different cross-sectional profiles.
applicability: Tapered structural elements with varying materials

IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered is a geometric representation item, not a material-assigned entity. IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage is assigned to IfcElement subtypes (e.g., IfcColumn, IfcBeam) via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, not directly to IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered. The dependency should be framed as through the element being represented, not direct.
conditions: When material properties vary with profile
exceptions: If material is uniform across profiles

subject: IfcExtrudedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: The extruded area solid is typically positioned relative to a local placement defined by the parent element.
conditions: For spatial positioning within a building structure

subject: IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel
rationale: An IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel consists of faces (IfcFace) which are defined by loops referencing Cartesian points. The point geometry is essential to define the surface model.
conditions: When defining face boundaries

subject: IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel
rationale: An IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel is explicitly composed of a set of IfcFace entities. Without faces, there is no surface model.
applicability: IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel requires IfcFace only when it has at least one face. An empty IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel (which is schema-valid with zero faces) would not require any IfcFace. The assertion says 'Always required' which is too strong for the zero-face edge case.
conditions: Always required as the core constituent element

subject: IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel
rationale: Faces within a face-based surface model use bounds to define their outer and inner loops, requiring IfcFaceBound definitions.
conditions: When faces have boundaries defined

subject: IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel
rationale: Like all geometry in IFC, the surface model depends on a geometric representation context for correct placement in the model coordinate system.
applicability: IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel does not have a direct depends_on relationship with IfcGeometricRepresentationContext. The geometric representation context is a property of the representation (IfcShapeRepresentation) not of the geometric item itself. IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel as a geometric representation item does not directly depend on the representation context.
conditions: For coordinate system placement and geometric validity

subject: IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel
rationale: An IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel is a container for one or more IfcFace objects that constitute the surface model.
conditions: Always
exceptions: IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel contains IfcFace only if the faces list is non-empty. An IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel with an empty Faces list (schema-valid) would not contain any IfcFace instances. The 'Always' condition is too broad.

subject: IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel
rationale: IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel can be used as the representation item within an IfcShapeRepresentation to provide the geometric shape of a building element.
conditions: When used as the geometric representation of a product

subject: IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel
rationale: The surface model supports defining the shape of building products (e.g., IfcBuildingElementProxy, IfcFurnishingElement) via IfcProductDefinitionShape.
conditions: When assigned to a product as its shape

subject: IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel
rationale: The surface model can be placed in an IfcRepresentationMap to allow reuse as a mapped item, connecting to it as a source geometry.
conditions: When used in a mapped representation (as a block/insert)

subject: IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel
rationale: Faces in the surface model can have presentation styles assigned via IfcStyledItem to control visual appearance.
conditions: When visual presentation/layering or color is assigned

subject: IfcFace
rationale: IfcFace requires IfcFaceBound to define its boundaries (edges/loops).
conditions: when defining the geometry of a face

subject: IfcFace
rationale: An IfcFace contains IfcFaceBound entities that define its outer and inner boundaries.
conditions: when representing a bounded face

subject: IfcFace
rationale: IfcFace relies on edge loops (through IfcFaceBound) to define its topology.
applicability: IfcFace does not directly depend on IfcEdgeLoop.
