IfcFace references IfcFaceBound, and IfcFaceBound may be specialized as IfcFaceOuterBound which references IfcLoop, and IfcEdgeLoop is a subtype of IfcLoop. So the dependency is indirect (through two intermediate relationships). Stating a direct depends_on relationship skips the intermediate IfcFaceBound, which is misleading for accurate dependency modeling.
conditions: when the face is bounded by a closed loop of edges

subject: IfcFace
rationale: IfcFace can be aggregated into IfcConnectedFaceSet to form larger topological structures.
conditions: when part of a topological shell or solid model

subject: IfcFace
rationale: IfcFace supports the definition of IfcClosedShell by providing the constituent faces that enclose a volume.
conditions: when faces are assembled into a closed shell

subject: IfcFace
rationale: IfcFace supports the definition of IfcOpenShell by providing constituent faces.
conditions: when faces are assembled into an open shell

subject: IfcFace
rationale: IfcFace is a fundamental component in faceted Brep geometry representations.
conditions: when representing a boundary representation model

subject: IfcFace
rationale: IfcFace supports the creation of surface models composed of face sets.
conditions: when representing a surface model

subject: IfcFace
rationale: IfcFace indirectly requires Cartesian points through its underlying edge and vertex geometry.
applicability: IfcFace does not directly require IfcCartesianPoint. IfcFace references IfcFaceBound, which references IfcLoop, which is specialized as IfcEdgeLoop (which references IfcEdge via IfcOrientedEdge) or IfcPolyLoop (which directly references IfcCartesianPoint). The path is indirect through multiple entities, so stating a direct 'requires' relationship oversimplifies and may misrepresent the actual dependency chain.
conditions: when defining edges and vertices that bound the face

subject: IfcFaceOuterBound
rationale: IfcFaceOuterBound has a property 'Bound' of type IfcBoundaryCurve, and IfcPolyLoop is a common subtype used to define the polygonal outer boundary of a face.
conditions: when boundary is defined by a polygon

subject: IfcFaceOuterBound
rationale: The IfcFaceOuterBound entity has an attribute 'Bound' of type IfcBoundaryCurve, which defines the curve or loop forming the outer boundary.
conditions: for any face outer boundary definition

subject: IfcFaceOuterBound
rationale: IfcFaceOuterBound is used as the outer boundary of an IfcFace, providing the geometric/topological limit of the face.
applicability: all building models with topological face representation
conditions: when defining the outer loop of a face

subject: IfcFaceOuterBound
rationale: IfcAdvancedFace uses IfcFaceOuterBound as its outer boundary for advanced boundary representation (B-rep) geometry.
conditions: when advanced boundary representation is used

subject: IfcFaceOuterBound
rationale: IfcFaceOuterBound contributes to defining the topological structure of face-based surface models by specifying which bounds are outer.
conditions: when the face model topology requires outer boundary definitions

subject: IfcFaceOuterBound
rationale: IfcFaceOuterBound inherits from IfcFaceBound the attribute 'Bound' of type IfcBoundaryCurve, which is mandatory.
conditions: always required as the bound attribute

subject: IfcFaceOuterBound
rationale: IfcFaceOuterBound is typically used on faces that reference an IfcFaceSurface to define the underlying surface geometry.
applicability: all models with surface geometry on faces
conditions: when the face is associated with a surface geometry

subject: IfcFaceBound
rationale: IfcFaceBound is a subtype of IfcTopologicalRepresentationItem and uses an IfcFace to define a boundary. The face is the core geometric entity that bounds a region.
conditions: For defining the boundary geometry

subject: IfcFaceBound
rationale: IfcFaceBound can reference an IfcBoundaryCurve (or its subtype IfcPolyLoop) to define the outer or inner boundary of a face.
conditions: When the bound is defined by a curve rather than a polygon

subject: IfcFaceBound
rationale: IfcFaceBound typically uses an IfcPolyLoop (a subtype of IfcBoundaryCurve) to define a closed loop of points forming the boundary of a face.
conditions: When defining a closed boundary as a polygon

subject: IfcFaceBound
rationale: IfcFaceBound's boundary can be defined by an IfcVertexLoop in special topological cases, though IfcPolyLoop is more common.
conditions: When the boundary is defined by a single vertex

subject: IfcFaceBound
rationale: IfcPolyLoop requires a set of IfcCartesianPoint coordinates to define the vertices of the boundary loop.
applicability: IfcFaceBound depends_on IfcCartesianPoint only indirectly. IfcPolyLoop references IfcCartesianPoint via its 'Polygon' attribute (LIST of IfcCartesianPoint). So IfcFaceBound -> IfcPolyLoop -> IfcCartesianPoint is a two-step dependency, not a direct one. The assertion should clarify the indirect nature of this dependency.
conditions: When the boundary is defined as a polygon (IfcPolyLoop)

subject: IfcFaceBound
rationale: IfcFaceBound provides the topological boundary structure that IfcFaceSurface relies on for defining bounded surface geometry.
conditions: When the face boundary is associated with a surface geometry

subject: IfcFaceBound
rationale: IfcAdvancedFace uses IfcFaceBound instances to define its boundary loops in advanced boundary representation models.
conditions: In advanced B-rep representations

subject: IfcFaceBound
rationale: IfcFaceBound entities form the faces of an IfcClosedShell, which is used to represent a closed volume boundary.
conditions: When the face bound is part of a closed shell topology

subject: IfcFaceBound
rationale: IfcFaceBound entities can form the faces of an IfcOpenShell, representing an open surface boundary.
conditions: When the face bound is part of an open shell topology

subject: IfcFaceBound
rationale: IfcFaceBound is a subtype of IfcTopologicalRepresentationItem which inherits from IfcRepresentationItem.
conditions: Inheritance relationship

subject: IfcFaceBound
rationale: IfcFaceBound is a direct subtype of IfcTopologicalRepresentationItem.
conditions: Inheritance relationship

subject: IfcFaceBound
rationale: IfcFaceBound can be used as part of the geometry definition of IfcRelSpaceBoundary relationships that define boundaries between spaces.
conditions: When defining space boundaries for thermal/energy analysis

subject: IfcFaceBound
rationale: IfcFaceBound provides the underlying topological structure used in surface-based connection geometry definitions.
conditions: When defining surface-based connection geometry between elements

subject: IfcFaceSurface
rationale: IfcFaceSurface is a subtype of IfcFace in IFC, so it directly depends on the IfcFace entity for its topological structure.
applicability: All building information models using IFC schema
conditions: When defining topological representation of a surface

subject: IfcFaceSurface
rationale: IfcFaceSurface contains an IfcSurface as its underlying geometry definition according to the IFC schema.
applicability: All IFC models with surface geometry representation
conditions: When the face is bounded by a surface geometry

subject: IfcFaceSurface
rationale: IfcFaceSurface requires an IfcSurface to define the geometry of the face.
conditions: For geometric definition of the face

subject: IfcFaceSurface
rationale: IfcFaceSurface can be connected to IfcFaceBound entities that define its boundaries.
applicability: All IFC models with bounded surfaces
conditions: When defining boundaries of the face surface

subject: IfcFaceSurface
rationale: IfcAdvancedFace is a subtype that extends IfcFaceSurface for more advanced surface representations in IFC4 and later.
applicability: Advanced IFC models with B-rep geometry
conditions: When defining more complex face geometries with advanced surface definitions

subject: IfcFaceSurface
rationale: IfcFaceSurface can be part of an IfcConnectedFaceSet which groups connected faces for topological representation.
applicability: All IFC models using topological face sets
conditions: When faces are grouped into a connected set

subject: IfcFaceSurface
rationale: IfcFaceSurface may require IfcRepresentationMap for mapping surface definitions in product representations.
applicability: IFC models with mapped item representations
conditions: When used in mapped representations

subject: IfcFaceSurface
rationale: IfcFaceSurface can be used within IfcShellBasedSurfaceModel for defining shell structures.
applicability: IFC models with shell-based surface representation
conditions: When representing shell-based surface models

subject: IfcFaceSurface
rationale: IfcFaceSurface depends on coordinate points when its underlying surface geometry is defined using point sets.
applicability: IFC models with B-spline or point-defined surfaces

IfcFaceSurface depends on IfcCartesianPoint only indirectly and transitively through its reference to IfcSurface. IfcBSplineSurface depends on IfcCartesianPoint for control points, but many other surface types (IfcPlane, IfcCylindricalSurface) do not use IfcCartesianPoint at all. The dependency is not a direct characteristic of IfcFaceSurface.
conditions: When the underlying IfcSurface uses point-based definitions (e.g., IfcBSplineSurface)

subject: IfcFaceSurface
rationale: IfcFaceSurface depends on placement definitions when its surface type requires positioning in 3D space.
applicability: IFC models with placed elementary surfaces

IfcFaceSurface depends on IfcAxis2Placement3D only transitively through some surface types. IfcPlane and IfcCylindricalSurface have a 'Position' attribute of type IfcAxis2Placement3D, but not all surfaces used by IfcFaceSurface use placement (e.g., IfcBSplineSurface does not use IfcAxis2Placement3D). This dependency is not inherent to IfcFaceSurface itself.
conditions: When the underlying IfcSurface uses placement (e.g., IfcPlane, IfcCylindricalSurface)

subject: IfcFacetedBrep
rationale: IfcFacetedBrep is defined by a set of polygonal faces, which are bounded by polygons defined using Cartesian points. The points are essential to define the vertices of the faces.
applicability: any building element using faceted representation
conditions: for defining the geometry of the faceted brep

subject: IfcFacetedBrep
rationale: IfcFacetedBrep consists of an outer shell made of connected faces; IfcFace is the fundamental building block.
applicability: any building element using faceted representation
conditions: for constructing the faceted boundary representation

subject: IfcFacetedBrep
rationale: In IfcFacetedBrep, each face is bounded by one or more poly loops (closed polylines), which define the edges of the faceted surfaces.
applicability: any building element using faceted representation
conditions: for bounding each face of the faceted brep

subject: IfcFacetedBrep
rationale: IfcFacetedBrep directly references IfcClosedShell, which groups the collection of faces bounding the solid.
applicability: any building element represented as a faceted brep
conditions: IfcFacetedBrep must reference an IfcClosedShell as its outer topology

subject: IfcFacetedBrep
rationale: IfcFacetedBrep is a subtype of IfcManifoldSolidBrep, providing a simplified (faceted) representation of manifold solids.
applicability: any building element requiring manifold solid geometry
conditions: as a subtype of boundary representation solids

subject: IfcFacetedBrep
rationale: IfcFacetedBrep can be used as the geometry representation of any IfcBuildingElement subtype via IfcShapeRepresentation.
applicability: walls, slabs, roofs, columns, beams, etc.
conditions: when the building element's shape is defined by a faceted boundary representation

subject: IfcFacetedBrep
rationale: IfcFacetedBrep uses planar faces only, whereas IfcAdvancedBrep supports curved surfaces; they are alternatives for different accuracy levels.
applicability: design stages requiring high geometric precision

The assertion says IfcFacetedBrep 'conflicts_with' IfcAdvancedBrep, but this is misleading. In IFC, IfcFacetedBrep and IfcAdvancedBrep are both subtypes of IfcManifoldSolidBrep and can be used for different LODs of the same element (as noted in the existing exceptions). They are alternatives, not conflicting representations - they serve different precision needs.
conditions: when an exact curved surface representation is needed
exceptions: both can coexist in different LOD representations of the same element

subject: IfcFacetedBrep
rationale: The faceted brep geometry is positioned in 3D space using a local placement coordinate system.
applicability: building elements positioned relative to a local placement
conditions: when the faceted brep is defined in a local coordinate system
exceptions: not required if using world coordinates directly

subject: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids
rationale: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids is a boundary representation (B-rep) solid with voids, which depends on IfcCartesianPoint to define the vertices of its polygonal faces and the void geometry.
applicability: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids does not directly depend on IfcCartesianPoint. The dependency chain is: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids -> IfcClosedShell -> IfcFace -> IfcFaceBound -> IfcPolyLoop -> IfcCartesianPoint. IfcCartesianPoint is multiple levels removed in the hierarchy, so calling it a direct dependency is misleading.
conditions: when defining the geometry of the faceted B-rep

subject: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids
rationale: The faceted B-rep uses polygonal loops (IfcPolyLoop) composed of Cartesian points to define the boundaries of each planar face.
applicability: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids does not directly depend on IfcPolyLoop. The path goes through IfcFaceBound, and IfcPolyLoop itself is an abstract supertype — the actual instantiable types are IfcPolyLoop (concrete) but the dependency is indirect via IfcFaceBound which references IfcBoundaryCurve (not IfcPolyLoop directly). IfcPolyLoop is referenced as a subtype of IfcCurve used in face boundaries, but not a direct dependent of IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids.
conditions: when defining face boundaries

subject: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids
rationale: The solid is composed of a set of faces that bound the exterior shell and the voids.
applicability: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids does not directly depend on IfcFace. The dependency is indirect: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids references IfcClosedShell (via 'Voids' attribute uses IfcClosedShell), which then contains IfcFace. IfcFace is not a direct attribute or direct referenced type of IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids.
conditions: when constructing the B-rep shell

subject: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids
rationale: The outer shell of the faceted B-rep must be a closed shell, and each void is also defined as a closed shell.
applicability: While IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids does reference IfcClosedShell (via its 'Voids' attribute), the assertion says 'when representing the outer boundary' but the voids are inner voids, not the outer boundary. The outer boundary is already handled by the inherited 'Outer' attribute from IfcFacetedBrep which references IfcClosedShell. The 'Voids' attribute references IfcClosedShell instances for the void boundaries, not the outer boundary.
conditions: when representing the outer boundary

subject: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids
rationale: Each face in the B-rep is associated with a face bound which defines its outer and possible inner boundaries.
applicability: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids does not directly depend on IfcFaceBound. IfcFace is used in IfcClosedShell, and IfcFace references IfcFaceBound via its 'Bounds' attribute. This is multiple levels of indirection away from IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids.
conditions: when defining oriented face boundaries

subject: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids
rationale: IfcFacetedBrepWithVoids is a specialization of IfcManifoldSolidBrep, supporting the representation of solids with cavities/voids in a faceted (planar polygonal faces) form.
conditions: as subtype of manifold solid B-rep

subject: IfcFailureConnectionCondition
rationale: IfcFailureConnectionCondition is a subtype of IfcStructuralConnectionCondition in the IFC schema.
applicability: The term 'connects_to' is vague and not a standard IEA relationship name. IFC uses 'IsTypedBy', 'Decomposes', 'Associates', etc. as relationship types. A subtype relationship is expressed via 'IsTypedBy' or inheritance in the EXPRESS schema, not 'connects_to'. Additionally, IfcFailureConnectionCondition is not a relationship entity at all but a condition class used for structural analysis.
conditions: as a subtype relationship in the IFC schema

subject: IfcFan
rationale: Fans are typically connected to ductwork to move air through the ventilation or air conditioning system.
applicability: all building types with HVAC systems
conditions: fan is installed within an air distribution system
exceptions: IfcFan can be used in free-air applications (e.g., exhaust fans discharging directly to the outside) where no ductwork is present on the discharge side. Also, ceiling extractor fans may be mounted in a ceiling opening with no connected ductwork on the room side.

subject: IfcFanType
rationale: Fans are typically connected to ductwork to move air through HVAC systems.
applicability: The assertion applies only to fans that are part of a ducted air distribution system. IfcFanType is also used for fans in non-ducted systems (e.g., ceiling fans, pedestal fans, or circulation fans with no duct connection), where the requirement for ductwork does not apply.
conditions: connected to air distribution system
exceptions: In some building systems, a fan may be mounted in a wall or roof opening without any ductwork connected (e.g., an exhaust fan discharging directly to the exterior, or an attic ventilation fan). In such cases, the fan type is still IfcFanType but the condition of being connected to ductwork does not hold.

subject: IfcFastener
rationale: IfcFastener is an abstract entity that connects or joins other IFC elements, per IFC schema definition.
conditions: when used as a joining element
exceptions: IfcFastener can also be used standalone (e.g., a bolt modeled as a product representation item without explicitly connecting two elements), not always in a connecting role.

subject: IfcFastener
rationale: A fastener functionally requires at least two elements to join together — without connected elements, a fastener has no purpose.
conditions: to be fastened together

subject: IfcFastener
rationale: Fasteners hold assemblies together, enabling the collective structural or architectural function.
conditions: when used in assemblies like steel frames, curtain walls, timber connections
exceptions: IfcFastener does not always 'support' IfcElementAssembly. Fasteners are joining elements but not necessarily load-bearing support elements. In many assemblies (e.g., bolted connections), the fastener joins elements but the structural support is provided by the elements themselves (e.g., bearing plates, contact surfaces).

subject: IfcFastener
rationale: IfcFastener is the supertype that includes IfcMechanicalFastener (bolts, nuts, screws, rivets) per IFC hierarchy.
applicability: any IFC model with detailed fastener representation

IfcMechanicalFastener is a subtype of IfcFastener, not something that IfcFastener 'contains'. The assertion uses 'contains' which implies a part-whole relationship (composition), but in the IFC hierarchy, IfcMechanicalFastener is a specialization (subtype), not a component contained within a fastener.
conditions: if specialized fastener types are modeled

subject: IfcFastener
rationale: In IFC2x3 and IFC4, IfcDiscreteAccessory is separate from IfcFastener, but both serve fastening/connection roles. Some interpretations treat washers, plates as accessories to fasteners.
conditions: when modeled in IFC as a fastener-related accessory
exceptions: IfcDiscreteAccessory is a sibling, not a subtype, of IfcFastener in some IFC versions

subject: IfcFastener
rationale: Fasteners realize structural connections between members in load-bearing joints.
conditions: when fasteners are part of a structural joint
exceptions: IfcFastener connects_to IfcStructuralConnection is only valid if the structural connection model explicitly includes fasteners as relational objects. In many structural models, fasteners are abstracted out and connections are modeled directly between structural members without explicit fastener entities.

subject: IfcFastener
rationale: Fasteners are physical objects made of materials (steel, aluminum, plastic, etc.) and are assigned material properties in IFC.
applicability: The assertion says 'depends_on IfcMaterial' always, but material assignment in IFC is optional via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial. A fastener may be modeled without an explicit material reference (e.g., generic representation or type-based material assignment at the type level rather than the occurrence level).
conditions: always

subject: IfcFastenerType
rationale: IfcFastenerType defines a type of fastener; it requires actual fastener instances (IfcFastener) to be placed in the building model.
conditions: When used in structural connections

subject: IfcFastenerType
rationale: Fastener types depend on relationships that connect building elements, as fasteners are used to join components together.
conditions: When modeling connections between elements

subject: IfcFastenerType
rationale: Fastener type definitions often require material specifications to denote the material from which the fastener is made.
conditions: When material properties affect fastener selection (e.g., steel, wood, concrete fasteners)
exceptions: IfcFastenerType does not always require IfcMaterial. In IFC, fastener types that are predefined in the standard (e.g., using IfcFastenerTypeEnum) may not require an explicit material assignment — the material can be inherited from the assembly or implied by the predefined type.

subject: IfcFastenerType
rationale: Fasteners such as bolts, screws, and anchors support structural connections by transferring loads between connected elements.
conditions: When used in load-bearing connections
exceptions: Non-structural fasteners like cable ties or clips

subject: IfcFastenerType
rationale: IfcFastenerType contains property sets that define its mechanical and geometric properties (e.g., diameter, length, tensile strength).
conditions: When defining technical properties of the fastener type

subject: IfcFastenerType
rationale: Fasteners often depend on being assigned to element assemblies that group connected building elements together.
conditions: When the fastener is part of a larger assembly (e.g., steel frame connection assembly)

subject: IfcFastenerType
rationale: To associate material information with the fastener type, IfcRelAssociatesMaterial is required.
conditions: When material association is needed for the fastener type

subject: IfcFastenerType
rationale: Fastener types support building elements by enabling their connection and assembly into the overall structure.
conditions: When fasteners are used to join building elements (e.g., bolting steel beams, screwing drywall)

subject: IfcFastenerType
rationale: While the type definition itself doesn't directly depend on points, placement of fastener instances depends on coordinate definitions.
conditions: When defining the location of fasteners in 3D space

subject: IfcFastenerType
rationale: IfcMechanicalFastenerType is a subtype of IfcFastenerType, so IfcFastenerType connects to its more specific subtypes.
conditions: When the fastener is a mechanical fastener such as a bolt, screw, or rivet

subject: IfcFeatureElement
rationale: IfcFeatureElement is the abstract supertype that contains subtypes like IfcFeatureElementSubtraction (e.g., openings, cutouts) and IfcFeatureElementAddition (e.g., projections).

subject: IfcFeatureElement
rationale: IfcFeatureElement is the abstract supertype that contains subtypes including IfcFeatureElementAddition (e.g., chamfers, fillets).

subject: IfcFeatureElement
rationale: A feature element (opening, recess, projection) cannot exist independently; it always requires a host element (wall, slab, beam, etc.) that it modifies.
applicability: The assertion states IfcFeatureElement 'depends_on IfcElement' with conditions about HasOpenings or VoidsElement relationship. However, IfcFeatureElementAddition uses IfcRelProjectsElement (not HasOpenings or VoidsElement) for attachment to the host. The stated conditions only cover IfcFeatureElementSubtraction, not IfcFeatureElementAddition. The applicability should be narrowed or the conditions expanded.
conditions: IfcFeatureElement must be assigned to a host IfcElement via the HasOpenings or VoidsElement relationship

subject: IfcFeatureElement
rationale: IfcFeatureElement participates in the IfcRelVoidsElement relationship, which supports the decomposition of elements by voids.

subject: IfcFeatureElement
rationale: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction requires IfcRelVoidsElement to define the relationship between the feature and its host element.
conditions: When the feature element is a subtraction type (opening)
exceptions: IfcFeatureElement does not directly depend on IfcRelVoidsElement. Rather, IfcRelVoidsElement.RelatesTo points to IfcFeatureElementSubtraction. The dependency direction stated may be inverted. IfcRelVoidsElement depends on IfcFeatureElementSubtraction as its target, not the other way around.

subject: IfcFeatureElement
rationale: IfcFeatureElementAddition requires IfcRelProjectsElement to define the relationship between the feature and its host element.
conditions: When the feature element is an addition type (projection)
exceptions: IfcFeatureElement does not directly depend on IfcRelProjectsElement. Rather, IfcRelProjectsElement.RelatesTo points to IfcFeatureElementAddition. The dependency direction stated may be inverted.

subject: IfcFeatureElement
rationale: Feature elements often require placement definition relative to the host element's local coordinate system.
applicability: IfcFeatureElement does not always 'require' IfcLocalPlacement — it depends on the representation approach. Some features are defined purely by a profile or 2D representation without an explicit local placement (e.g., parametric voids defined by extrusion from the host's coordinate system). The condition correctly notes 'if it has a distinct placement' but the assertion title still says 'requires' which can be misleading.
conditions: If the feature element has a distinct placement relative to its host

subject: IfcFeatureElement
rationale: Feature elements need geometric representation (e.g., extrusion for an opening) to define their shape within the host.
applicability: The condition states 'when 3D geometry is defined' but IfcShapeRepresentation can also be 2D (e.g., footprint or profile representations). The assertion could be clarified to specify that IfcShapeRepresentation is required when any geometric representation (2D or 3D) is needed, not just 3D.
conditions: When 3D geometry of the feature is defined

subject: IfcFeatureElementAddition
rationale: IfcFeatureElementAddition is a subtype of IfcFeatureElement and is used to add features to existing IfcElements. It depends on a host IfcElement to which the addition is applied.
conditions: when IfcFeatureElementAddition is applied to a building element

subject: IfcFeatureElementAddition
rationale: IfcFeatureElementAddition often contains geometric representations such as IfcExtrudedAreaSolid to describe the added feature's shape.
conditions: when geometric representation is defined as a swept solid

subject: IfcFeatureElementAddition
rationale: As part of the IFC model, IfcFeatureElementAddition supports the overall project model by contributing to the complete representation of building elements.
conditions: when aggregated within a project structure

subject: IfcFeatureElementAddition
rationale: IfcFeatureElementAddition may depend on IfcRelVoidsElement relationships if the feature requires a prepared opening or void in the host element.
conditions: when addition involves opening or void before applying feature
exceptions: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction is used instead of IfcFeatureElementAddition for voids

subject: IfcFeatureElementAddition
rationale: IfcFeatureElementAddition could depend on material layers when representing added finishes or coatings.
conditions: when the addition represents a material layer applied to an element

subject: IfcFeatureElementAddition
rationale: IfcFeatureElementAddition supports IfcBuildingElement by adding geometric or functional features such as projections, niches, or attachments.
conditions: when adding features like projections, corbels, or attachments to building elements

subject: IfcFillAreaStyle
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyle can define hatch patterns via IfcFillAreaStyleHatching entities to produce patterned fills.
conditions: when using hatch pattern fill

subject: IfcFillAreaStyle
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyle can define tiled fills via IfcFillAreaStyleTiles entities.
conditions: when using tiled/fill pattern

subject: IfcFillAreaStyle
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyle may use color definitions for its fill patterns.
conditions: when defining explicit solid fill colors as RGB values

subject: IfcFillAreaStyle
rationale: Fill area styles may be externally defined hatch patterns.
conditions: when referencing external hatch pattern definitions

subject: IfcFillAreaStyle
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyle is used within IfcSurfaceStyle to define fill patterns for surfaces in 2D annotations or hatched surfaces.
conditions: when used as part of a surface style rendering

subject: IfcFillAreaStyle
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyle is specifically intended to define the visual appearance (fill pattern) of IfcAnnotationFillArea occurrences.
conditions: when used to fill annotation areas

subject: IfcFillAreaStyle
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyle includes (contains) one or more IfcFillAreaStyleHatching entities as its pattern definition.
conditions: when the fill style includes hatch patterns

subject: IfcFillAreaStyle
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyle includes (contains) one or more IfcFillAreaStyleTiles entities as its pattern definition.
conditions: when the fill style includes tile patterns

subject: IfcFillAreaStyle
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyle can contain an externally defined hatch style reference.
conditions: when the fill pattern is defined externally

subject: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction
rationale: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction is a subtype of IfcFeatureElement in the IFC schema, thus it requires the base class definition to function.
conditions: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction is a subtype of IfcFeatureElement

subject: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction
rationale: IfcOpeningElement is the most common subtype of IfcFeatureElementSubtraction used for openings in building elements.
applicability: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction does not universally depend on IfcOpeningElement. IfcOpeningElement is a specific subtype of IfcFeatureElementSubtraction, not a dependency. Other subtypes like IfcCutOut exist and do not involve IfcOpeningElement for doors/windows.
conditions: When modeling openings such as doors or windows

subject: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction
rationale: Reinforcement may be required around subtractive features (e.g., openings, recesses) to maintain structural strength.
conditions: When subtractive features affect structural integrity

subject: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction
rationale: Door openings (subtractive features) support the installation of doors.
conditions: When IfcFeatureElementSubtraction is an IfcOpeningElement for a door

subject: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction
rationale: Window openings (subtractive features) support the installation of windows.
conditions: When IfcFeatureElementSubtraction is an IfcOpeningElement for a window

subject: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction
rationale: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction is always applied to (subtracted from) an IfcBuildingElement via the 'VoidsElement' relationship.

subject: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction
rationale: The subtractive feature contains a shape representation defining its geometry (e.g., a void shape).
conditions: When geometric representation is defined for the subtraction

subject: IfcFeatureElementSubtraction
rationale: IfcRelVoidsElement is the relationship that connects IfcFeatureElementSubtraction to the element it voids.

subject: IfcFillAreaStyleHatching
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyleHatching is a subtype of IfcFillAreaStyle and thus depends on the base style definition.
conditions: when used as a fill style for annotation

subject: IfcFillAreaStyleHatching
rationale: A Cartesian point is used to define the reference point for the hatch pattern origin.
conditions: when defining start point of hatch lines

subject: IfcFillAreaStyleHatching
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyleHatching provides the visual pattern to fill annotation areas, supporting the visual representation.
conditions: when used to fill an annotation fill area

subject: IfcFillAreaStyleHatching
rationale: Hatching can support surface lighting effects in certain visual representations.
conditions: when used in rendering or visualization contexts

subject: IfcFillAreaStyleHatching
rationale: The hatch line pattern may contain curve style definitions for line type, width, and color.
conditions: when hatch lines follow a curve style pattern

subject: IfcFillAreaStyleHatching
rationale: In a structured BIM model, the hatching style may require assignment to a presentation layer for proper organization.
applicability: The assertion says IfcFillAreaStyleHatching 'requires' IfcPresentationLayerAssignment, but the existing exception acknowledges 'if not explicitly assigned to a layer' it does not apply. This means the dependency is conditional, not a strict requirement. The wording 'requires' is misleading as it implies a mandatory relationship that the exception negates.
conditions: when the hatching is assigned to a presentation layer
exceptions: if not explicitly assigned to a layer

subject: IfcFillAreaStyleTiles
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyleTiles is referenced by IfcFillAreaStyle via the attribute 'FillStyles', which can contain tiled patterns as one type of fill.
conditions: Must be assigned to an IfcFillAreaStyle that defines the overall fill style

subject: IfcFillAreaStyleTiles
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyleTiles supports the definition of fill area styles by providing tiled pattern capabilities for filling areas in 2D presentation contexts.
conditions: When used as a fill style pattern definition in a presentation style assignment

subject: IfcFillAreaStyleTiles
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyleTiles provides the tiling pattern that fills IfcAnnotationFillArea objects, enabling patterned hatching or tiling in annotation drawings.
conditions: When annotation fill areas use tiled fill styles

subject: IfcFilter
rationale: Filters are often associated with air terminals (diffusers, grilles) as part of air distribution but can function without them in duct-mounted configurations.
conditions: When part of a ventilation system
exceptions: Recirculating standalone filter units

subject: IfcFilter
rationale: A fan is typically needed to move air through the filter, unless natural ventilation is used.
conditions: When filter requires forced airflow
exceptions: Passive gravity ventilation filters

In VAV terminal units with integral filters, the fan may be upstream of the filter or there may be no fan directly associated with the filter unit (e.g., duct-mounted filter banks relying on a central AHU fan). The dependency on IfcFan is not universal even in mechanical ventilation.

subject: IfcFilter
rationale: Filters protect downstream coils from dust and debris buildup, maintaining heat transfer efficiency.
conditions: When cooling or heating coils are downstream
exceptions: Systems without coils

subject: IfcFilter
rationale: Filters prevent particulate accumulation on damper blades and seals.
applicability: The assertion states IfcFilter 'protects_from' IfcDamper, but dampers typically do not require protection from particulate matter in the same way coils or fans do. Dampers are robust metal components not damaged by normal dust loading. The protective relationship is marginal at best.
conditions: When dampers are downstream of filter

subject: IfcFilter
rationale: Filters protect fan blades and bearings from dust abrasion and accumulation.
conditions: When fan is downstream of filter
exceptions: Fan-powered filters where fan is upstream

subject: IfcFilter
rationale: Filters often connect to duct fittings such as transitions, reducers, or filter housings.
conditions: When filter is installed in ductwork via transitions or housings

subject: IfcFilter
rationale: An IfcFilter instance requires an IfcFilterType to define its specific filter class/performance characteristics.
conditions: For proper specification and classification

subject: IfcFilterType
rationale: Air filter types require air terminals (diffusers, grilles) to distribute filtered air into spaces.
conditions: when part of HVAC air distribution system

subject: IfcFilterType
rationale: Filters are typically housed in or connected to duct segments; airflow depends on ductwork.
conditions: when installed in ducted HVAC system
exceptions: standalone filter units without ductwork

subject: IfcFilterType
rationale: Most filters require a fan to move air through the filter media; without fan, filtration does not occur.
conditions: when part of mechanical ventilation system
exceptions: passive/gravity filters without fan assist

subject: IfcFilterType
rationale: IfcFilterType defines the type properties, but the actual physical IfcFilter instance is required for installation.
conditions: for physical installation

subject: IfcFilterType
rationale: Filters protect coils from dust and particulate buildup, maintaining heat transfer efficiency.
conditions: when placed upstream of heating/cooling coils
exceptions: coils in cleanroom systems with pre-filtration

subject: IfcFilterType
rationale: Filters protect fan blades and bearings from airborne particulates, extending fan life.
applicability: The existing exception 'fan with direct outdoor intake without filtration' is ambiguous—it could describe a setup with no filter at all, which is outside the scope of any filter-to-fan relationship. The assertion should be clarified to only apply when a filter is actually present upstream of the fan, not when the entire filter component is absent from the system.
conditions: when filter is positioned before the fan
exceptions: fan with direct outdoor intake without filtration

subject: IfcFilterType
rationale: Filters connect to duct segments on upstream and downstream sides for airflow passage.
conditions: when installed inline in ductwork
exceptions: ceiling-mounted return air grille filters

subject: IfcFireSuppressionTerminalType
rationale: Fire suppression terminals (e.g., sprinkler heads, nozzles) require piping to deliver water, foam, or gaseous extinguishing agents.
conditions: for water or agent delivery to the terminal

subject: IfcFireSuppressionTerminalType
rationale: Valves and flow controllers regulate the supply of extinguishing agent to the terminal devices.
conditions: such as valves and flow control devices upstream

subject: IfcFireSuppressionTerminalType
rationale: Fire pumps may be needed to maintain adequate pressure at sprinkler heads and other terminals.
conditions: when gravity-fed pressure is insufficient

subject: IfcFireSuppressionTerminalType
rationale: Fire suppression terminals (sprinklers, nozzles) actively suppress or extinguish fires, protecting the building structure and occupants.
applicability: all building types with fire suppression installed
conditions: during a fire event

subject: IfcFireSuppressionTerminalType
rationale: Terminals discharge extinguishing agent into specific spaces to control or extinguish fires.
conditions: when activated in response to heat/smoke

subject: IfcFireSuppressionTerminalType
rationale: Fire suppression helps control fire spread and reduces risk to occupants, though life safety also depends on alarms and egress.
conditions: in occupied spaces with fire suppression coverage

subject: IfcFireSuppressionTerminalType
rationale: Fire suppression terminal types typically contain distribution ports for connection to piping.
conditions: as part of its connection interface

subject: IfcFireSuppressionTerminalType
rationale: Terminal devices connect to pipe fittings that branch off main supply lines.
conditions: at branch connections or tees

subject: IfcFireSuppressionTerminalType
rationale: Control panels and actuators interface with fire suppression terminals for release of extinguishing agent.
conditions: in electrically actuated suppression systems

subject: IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid
rationale: IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid is a subtype of IfcSweptAreaSolid, inheriting its geometric definition of a swept area along a directrix.
applicability: all building types using advanced solid geometry
conditions: when modeling swept area geometry with a fixed reference direction

subject: IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid
rationale: The swept area solid requires a profile definition as the basis of the extrusion/sweep operation.
conditions: must define the cross-sectional area to be swept

subject: IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid
rationale: FixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid requires a directrix (sweep path) defined as a curve along which the profile is swept.
conditions: directrix curve must be defined for the sweep path

subject: IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid
rationale: The 'FixedReference' aspect means a fixed reference direction vector is used to orient the cross-section along the sweep.
conditions: fixed reference direction must be specified for the sweep orientation

subject: IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid
rationale: The swept area solid typically requires a placement to locate it within the coordinate system.
conditions: position of the swept solid in 3D space must be defined

subject: IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid
rationale: IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid contributes to the shape representation of a building element.
conditions: when used as part of a product shape representation

subject: IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid
rationale: IfcFixedReferenceSweptAreaSolid is a more general concept that can be specialized into straight extrusions.
conditions: when the directrix is a straight line and fixed reference is perpendicular
exceptions: not a direct subtype relationship but a specialization

subject: IfcFlowController
rationale: IfcFlowController regulates flow within a distribution system; it depends on connected IfcFlowSegment (ducts/pipes) to channel the medium to/from the controller.
applicability: The assertion that IfcFlowController 'depends_on IfcFlowSegment' with condition 'when part of a ducting or piping system' is too broad. IfcFlowController includes valves, dampers, pumps, and fans. A pump (IfcPump, subtype of IfcFlowController) in a piping system does not depend on IfcFlowSegment (duct segments) — it depends on IfcPipeSegment. Similarly, a damper in a duct system depends on IfcDuctSegment, not IfcFlowSegment. The assertion conflates duct and pipe segments under the generic IfcFlowSegment, but in practice controllers connect to either duct-specific or pipe-specific segments, not the abstract parent class directly in a meaningful dependency sense.
conditions: when part of a ducting or piping system

subject: IfcFlowController
rationale: Flow controllers often require fittings (elbows, tees) to connect properly within piping or ductwork systems.
conditions: when changes in direction or branching are needed

subject: IfcFlowController
rationale: In IFC, IfcFlowController connects to other distribution elements via IfcPorts for logical connectivity in the building information model.
conditions: for connectivity in the IFC model

subject: IfcFlowController
rationale: In hydronic or plumbing systems, flow controllers (valves) connect to pipe segments to regulate flow.
applicability: buildings with plumbing or hydronic systems
conditions: when part of a piping system

subject: IfcFlowController
rationale: In air distribution systems, flow controllers (dampers) connect to duct segments to regulate airflow.
conditions: when part of an air distribution system

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: IfcFlowControllerType is the type definition for IfcFlowController entities in IFC, so it depends on instances of IfcFlowController to represent specific devices.
conditions: When defining flow distribution control logic

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: The IFC schema uses IfcRelDefinesByType relationship to associate type information with occurrences.
conditions: When assigning type to flow controller occurrences

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: IfcFlowControllerType can have property set definitions that define its characteristics.
conditions: When type has predefined property sets

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: Flow controller types may have material specifications for manufacturing.
conditions: When specifying material composition of flow controller type

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: Flow controllers (valves, dampers) connect to pipes or ducts (IfcFlowSegment) in building service systems.
conditions: When installed in a distribution system

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: Flow controllers may connect to fittings in distribution systems.
conditions: When connected via fittings in a piping or ducting network

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: Flow controller types (e.g., valve types, damper types) support distribution systems by regulating flow of media.
conditions: When used as part of HVAC, plumbing, or fire protection system

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: Certain flow controller types like shut-off valves or backflow preventers protect building elements from water damage or contamination.
conditions: When used as shut-off valve or backflow preventer

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: Complex flow controller types may nest sub-components via IfcRelNests.
conditions: When defining component parts of composite flow controller types

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: Flow controller types often reference technical documentation for performance specifications.
conditions: When product documentation or datasheets are referenced

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: IfcFlowControllerType contains property sets that define its technical parameters.

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: Flow controller types can be classified using industry classification systems like Uniclass or Omniclass.
conditions: When classified under a standard classification system

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: Proper flow control improves the performance of terminal devices like diffusers or faucets.
conditions: When properly sized flow controllers regulate flow to terminals

subject: IfcFlowControllerType
rationale: Undersized flow controllers can conflict with pumps or fans (moving devices) by increasing system resistance.
conditions: When improperly sized causing excessive pressure drop

subject: IfcFlowFittingType
rationale: IfcFlowFittingType is an abstract definition of a flow fitting type; it requires the corresponding occurrence entity IfcFlowFitting for instantiation in a building model.
applicability: all building types with flow distribution systems
conditions: when representing a flow fitting type in IFC data model

subject: IfcFlowFittingType
rationale: Flow fittings (elbows, tees, reducers) contain or connect flow segments in a distribution network.
conditions: when the fitting connects pipe or duct segments

subject: IfcFlowFittingType
rationale: Flow fittings are junction components that connect flow segments to change direction, diameter, or branch.
applicability: IfcFlowFittingType is a type definition (enumeration of predefined types like ELBOW, TEE, REDUCER, etc.) and does not have a direct 'connects_to' relationship with IfcFlowSegment. The connection relationship exists at the occurrence level (IfcFlowFitting connects to IfcFlowSegment via IfcRelConnectsPortToElement or similar relationships), not at the type level. The existing exception about dead-end caps/plugs is correct conceptually but should apply to occurrences not types.
conditions: when used in piping or ductwork networks
exceptions: dead-end caps or plugs may not connect to further segments

subject: IfcFlowFittingType
rationale: The type definition depends on property sets to capture technical characteristics like nominal diameter, material, pressure class.
conditions: when specifying material, dimensions, and pressure ratings
exceptions: While IfcFlowFittingType can be associated with IfcPropertySet via IfcRelDefinesByProperties, it is not a strict dependency that always holds. Simple flow fitting types may be defined purely by the predefined type enumeration (e.g., P_LOSS for pressure loss coefficient) without needing a full property set. The assertion overstates the dependency.

subject: IfcFlowFitting
rationale: IfcFlowFitting connects segments of a flow distribution system (e.g., pipes or ducts), so it requires adjacent flow segments to function.
conditions: when part of a piping or ducting system

subject: IfcFlowFitting
rationale: IfcFlowFitting includes subtypes like elbows, tees, reducers that are pipe fittings; these require pipe segments to be connected.
conditions: for fluid transport systems

subject: IfcFlowFitting
rationale: IfcFlowFitting includes subtypes like duct transitions, bends, junctions that require duct segments to be connected.
conditions: for air distribution systems

subject: IfcFlowFitting
rationale: IfcFlowFitting depends on IfcPort objects (via IfcRelConnectsPorts) to define its connection points within the flow distribution network.
conditions: for logical connectivity in BIM models

subject: IfcFlowFitting
rationale: IfcFlowFitting depends on relationship objects that define how ports of fittings connect to ports of segments or other fittings.
applicability: IfcRelConnectsPorts is only required when logical port-based connectivity is explicitly modeled. Many BIM workflows use geometric connectivity or simplified representations without IfcRelConnectsPorts. This is a modeling choice, not a universal dependency.
conditions: for establishing logical connectivity between elements

subject: IfcFlowFitting
rationale: IfcFlowFittings connect to flow terminals (e.g., diffusers, grilles, faucets) via intermediate segments to deliver or collect the medium.
conditions: when the fitting is at the end of a branch serving a terminal device

subject: IfcFlowFitting
rationale: Flow fittings connect to flow controllers (valves, dampers) that regulate the flow passing through the fitting or adjacent segments.
conditions: when a valve, damper, or regulator is installed in the system

subject: IfcFlowFitting
rationale: Fittings connect to flow-moving devices (pumps, fans, compressors) to route flow to/from these devices.
conditions: when the fitting is near pumps or fans in the distribution network

subject: IfcFlowFitting
rationale: A flow fitting requires a material definition for physical fabrication, strength, corrosion resistance, and code compliance.
conditions: for defining the physical material of the fitting (e.g., metal, PVC, or composite)

subject: IfcFlowFitting
rationale: In rare cases where a fitting passes through a building element, it depends on an opening relationship, but this is atypical.
conditions: when the fitting is installed in an opening in a wall or slab
exceptions: most fittings are not placed in openings

subject: IfcFlowFitting
rationale: Some fittings like strainers or traps protect downstream segments from debris or unwanted flow.
conditions: when the fitting includes a filter, strainer, or trap
exceptions: not all fittings provide protection

subject: IfcFlowInstrument
rationale: Inline flow instruments are physically installed within a pipe or duct segment to measure flow.
applicability: The assertion does not address that the 'depends_on' relationship in IFC may require IfcFlowSegment to be present as a parent container, but in some IFC export workflows, inline instruments can be placed directly on IfcDistributionPort or IfcPort without an explicit IfcFlowSegment. This is a modeling convention issue rather than a physical dependency.
conditions: instrument is inline type
exceptions: clamp-on or non-invasive instruments

subject: IfcFlowInstrument
rationale: Flow instruments often feed signals to control valves or dampers that regulate flow.
applicability: The assertion states IfcFlowInstrument depends_on IfcFlowController when part of a control loop. However, in a typical HVAC control loop, the instrument provides a measurement signal to the controller but does not have a physical or spatial dependency in the IFC model — they are connected via IfcDistributionControlElement relationships, not physical port connections. The 'depends_on' semantics conflate physical connectivity with control dependency.
conditions: when part of a control loop
exceptions: standalone monitoring only

subject: IfcFlowInstrument
rationale: IfcFlowInstrument is physically connected to pipe segments at its inlet and outlet flanges or threads.
conditions: instrument is inline in a piping system

subject: IfcFlowInstrument
rationale: Air flow measurement instruments are installed in duct segments.
conditions: instrument is in an air duct
exceptions: While the assertion states IfcFlowInstrument connects_to IfcDuctSegment when in an air duct, this is not universally true. Some inline duct instruments (e.g., thermal dispersion airflow measuring stations, pitot tube arrays) are mounted on IfcDuctFitting (e.g., measuring sections, straightening sections) rather than directly on an IfcDuctSegment. Additionally, insertion-style sensors in ducts connect via ports on access doors or collars, not directly to a duct segment.

subject: IfcFlowInstrumentType
rationale: IfcFlowInstrumentType defines the type information for IfcFlowInstrument, which measures or regulates flow properties in a building system.
conditions: when used to measure flow properties

subject: IfcFlowInstrumentType
rationale: Flow instruments must be connected to flow segments (pipes, ducts) to measure media flowing through them.
conditions: when installed in a piping or ducting system
exceptions: standalone instruments

subject: IfcFlowInstrumentType
rationale: Flow fittings may be needed to transition from pipe/duct sizes to instrument ports.
conditions: when requiring branch connections or transitions for installation

subject: IfcFlowInstrumentType
rationale: IfcFlowInstrumentType instances are typically assigned to a distribution system (e.g., HVAC, plumbing, fire suppression) to monitor or control flow.
conditions: when the instrument is part of a larger building service system

subject: IfcFlowInstrumentType
rationale: Flow instruments often connect to flow controllers (valves, dampers) to enable closed-loop flow regulation.
conditions: when the instrument is paired with a control valve or damper
exceptions: simple monitoring-only instruments

subject: IfcFlowInstrumentType
rationale: Flow instruments may connect to or incorporate sensors for temperature, pressure, or flow measurement.
conditions: when the instrument incorporates or interfaces with sensing elements

subject: IfcFlowMeterType
rationale: IfcFlowMeterType defines the type information for IfcFlowMeter flow meter elements, so the type requires the actual meter element to be instantiated for functional use.
conditions: When metering fluid flow in building service systems

subject: IfcFlowMeterType
rationale: A flow meter must be connected to flow segments (pipes/ducts) to measure fluid flow within a distribution system.
conditions: When installed in a piping or ducting network

subject: IfcFlowMeterType
rationale: IfcFlowMeterType relies on property sets to define its performance parameters and specifications.
applicability: While IfcFlowMeterType can be associated with IfcPropertySet via IfcRelDefinesByType, this is an optional relationship, not a dependency. A flow meter type can exist without a property set (e.g., as a placeholder type from a catalog with no defined properties yet).
conditions: For defining meter characteristics like flow rate range, accuracy, and calibration

subject: IfcFlowMeterType
rationale: An IfcFlowMeterType requires distribution ports as connection points to the piping/ducting network.
conditions: For connecting to distribution network pipes or ducts

subject: IfcFlowMeterType
rationale: Flow meter types are typically connected to pipe segments in plumbing, gas, or hydronic systems.
conditions: In water or gas metering applications

subject: IfcFlowMeterType
rationale: Flow meter types can connect to duct segments for air flow measurement in ventilation systems.
conditions: In HVAC air flow measurement applications

subject: IfcFlowMeterType
rationale: The type entity depends on the IFC relationship object to be assigned to actual product occurrences in the model.
conditions: For proper IFC model structure and relationships

subject: IfcFlowMeter
rationale: An IfcFlowMeter typically depends on upstream flow controllers (valves, dampers) to regulate the flow before measurement.
conditions: when installed in a piping or ducting system

subject: IfcFlowMeter
rationale: Flow meters in fluid systems are installed in pipe segments and require them for proper physical integration.
conditions: when measuring liquid or gas flow in piping systems
exceptions: if measuring electrical energy via a different connector type

subject: IfcFlowMeter
rationale: Advanced flow meters may interface with flow instruments (sensors, transmitters) for data processing.
conditions: when the meter requires external sensing or data logging
exceptions: simple mechanical meters operate independently

subject: IfcFlowMeter
rationale: Many modern flow meters require power supplies or signal converters to operate.
conditions: when the flow meter is powered or requires signal conversion
exceptions: purely mechanical meters do not require energy conversion

subject: IfcFlowMeter
rationale: An IfcFlowMeter is part of a distribution system (e.g., water, gas, HVAC) and depends on that system for context.
applicability: all building types with building services

The assertion states IfcFlowMeter depends_on IfcDistributionSystem for proper integration. In IFC, a flow meter is assigned to a distribution system via IfcRelAssignsToGroup, not a hard dependency. Many flow meters can exist as standalone components (e.g., sub-metered tenant units) without being integrated into a formal IfcDistributionSystem. The 'depends_on' relationship is overstated.
conditions: for proper integration into building services

subject: IfcFlowMeter
rationale: Flow meters are typically connected via pipe fittings (couplings, flanges, unions) to the piping network.
conditions: when installed inline in a piping system

subject: IfcFlowMeter
rationale: Wired flow meters require cable trays or conduits for signal/power cables.
conditions: when the meter has electrical signal output cables
exceptions: wireless meters do not require cable carriers

subject: IfcFlowMeter
rationale: Many electronic flow meters contain internal sensors (e.g., ultrasonic, electromagnetic, turbine) for flow measurement.
conditions: when the flow meter integrates a sensing element internally
exceptions: mechanical meters may not contain electronic sensors

subject: IfcFlowMeter
rationale: IfcFlowMeter can contain or be categorized by its type definition (e.g., turbine, ultrasonic, magnetic).
conditions: when defining a specific type or variant of flow meter

subject: IfcFlowMovingDevice
rationale: Flow moving devices are connected to piping or ductwork segments (IfcFlowSegment) to move fluid/air through a system.
conditions: must be connected via inlet/outlet ports

subject: IfcFlowMovingDevice
rationale: Fittings such as elbows, tees, reducers are required to connect the moving device to the distribution network.
conditions: needed for direction changes, branches, or transitions
exceptions: simple straight runs

subject: IfcFlowMovingDevice
rationale: Flow moving devices function as part of a distribution system such as a ventilation system, water supply system, or drainage system.
conditions: device must be assigned to a system (e.g., HVAC, plumbing, fire suppression)

subject: IfcFlowMovingDevice
rationale: Devices such as fans, pumps, and compressors need physical space for installation, access, and maintenance.
applicability: The assertion states IfcFlowMovingDevice depends_on IfcSpace for installation and maintenance space, but in IFC, spatial relationships are typically represented via IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure, not as a dependency. A flow-moving device 'depends on' IfcSpace in a design sense, but this is not how IFC defines the relationship. The assertion mixes semantic requirements with IFC schema relationships without clarifying which is intended.
conditions: installation and maintenance space required
exceptions: inline devices in accessible ceilings/voids

subject: IfcFlowMovingDevice
rationale: IfcFlowMovingDevice connects to the distribution network via IfcPort objects representing inlet/outlet connections.
conditions: inlet and outlet ports for fluid/air connection

subject: IfcFlowMovingDevice
rationale: Pumps connect to pipe segments for liquid transport.
conditions: for liquid systems
exceptions: air systems use duct segments

subject: IfcFlowMovingDevice
rationale: Fans and air handlers connect to duct segments for air transport.
conditions: for air systems
exceptions: liquid systems use pipe segments

subject: IfcFlowSegmentType
rationale: IfcFlowSegmentType is the type definition for IfcFlowSegment instances. The type defines common properties for flow segments.
conditions: when defining a flow segment type in IFC

subject: IfcFlowSegmentType
rationale: IfcFlowSegmentType can contain property sets that define the characteristics of the flow segment type.
conditions: when type has property sets defined

subject: IfcFlowSegmentType
rationale: Flow segment types are made from materials (e.g., steel, copper, PVC for pipes, ducts) which determine their physical properties.
conditions: when material is specified for the flow segment type

subject: IfcFlowSegmentType
rationale: Flow segment types belong to distribution systems like piping systems, ducting systems, or cable carrier systems.
conditions: when the flow segment type is part of a distribution system

subject: IfcFlowSegmentType
rationale: Flow segment types serve as the straight/running portions of a flow distribution system that fittings connect to.
conditions: when flow fittings connect to flow segments in the system

subject: IfcFlowSegmentType
rationale: Flow segment types provide the conveyance path that supplies flow terminals (e.g., diffusers, taps, outlets).
conditions: when terminals are connected to the flow distribution system

subject: IfcFlowSegmentType
rationale: Flow segment types may require controllers (dampers, valves) to regulate flow within the segments.
conditions: when flow control is required in the system

subject: IfcFlowSegmentType
rationale: Flow segments connect to other flow segments to form continuous distribution pathways.
conditions: when multiple segments form a continuous run

subject: IfcFlowSegmentType
rationale: IfcFlowSegmentType requires the IfcRelDefinesByType relationship to associate occurrences to the type.
conditions: when instantiating the type definition relationship

subject: IfcFlowSegment
rationale: Flow segments often connect via fittings (elbows, tees, reducers) to form a complete network.
conditions: When the flow path changes direction, branches, or reduces/expands
exceptions: For straight uninterrupted segments without fittings

subject: IfcFlowSegment
rationale: Flow segments depend on port connections to transfer fluid/air between components.
applicability: The assertion says IfcFlowSegment 'depends_on' IfcRelConnectsPortToElement, but this relationship is only relevant in IFC2x3 and earlier. In IFC4 and later, port connectivity can use different mechanisms such as IfcRelNests or IfcRelConnectsElements via distribution ports. The existing exception 'disconnected segments with no ports' does not address IFC version limitations.
conditions: When the segment is connected at its ports to other elements
exceptions: Disconnected segments with no ports

subject: IfcFlowSegment
rationale: Flow segments transport medium from source to terminal devices (diffusers, faucets, sprinklers).
applicability: HVAC diffusers, Plumbing fixtures, Sprinkler heads
conditions: When the segment delivers flow to terminal devices
exceptions: Supply-only segments not connected to terminals

subject: IfcFlowSegment
rationale: IfcFlowSegment provides connection points (distribution ports) for system connectivity.
conditions: When ports are defined for connectivity
exceptions: Segments without defined ports

subject: IfcFlowSegment
rationale: Flow segments connect to moving devices that drive the flow (pumps, fans, compressors).
applicability: The assertion says IfcFlowSegment 'connects_to' IfcFlowMovingDevice, but the existing exception 'gravity-driven systems without moving devices' is too narrow. There are also closed-loop systems where the segment is between two moving devices (e.g., pump-to-pump connection) or segments downstream of a moving device that feed storage, not another moving device. The condition should also note that this is typically via a fitting or port, not a direct connection.
conditions: When the segment is upstream or downstream of a pump, fan, or compressor
exceptions: Gravity-driven systems without moving devices

subject: IfcFlowSegment
rationale: The physical realization of a flow segment depends on material assignment for its construction properties.
conditions: When the segment has a defined material composition
exceptions: Conceptual segments without material assignment

IfcFlowSegment may also depend on IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage (in IFC4+) instead of IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage, especially for duct segments with profile-based material definitions. The existing exception only covers conceptual segments without material assignment, but does not account for the different material definition mechanisms across IFC versions.

subject: IfcFlowSegment
rationale: Path element connections define the logical flow path between segments in BIM.
conditions: When modeling connectivity in a distribution system
exceptions: In IFC versions without path elements

subject: IfcFlowTerminal
rationale: Flow terminals depend on flow segments (pipes, ducts, cables) to connect them to the broader system.
applicability: all building types with flow distribution systems
conditions: when transporting flow between terminals

subject: IfcFlowTerminal
rationale: Flow terminals often require fittings to properly connect to piping or ductwork systems.
applicability: IfcFlowFitting is not always in the dependency chain between terminal and segment. For example, a diffuser may branch directly from a main duct without a formal fitting entity, or a register may attach to ductwork via a simple opening. The assertion assumes branching/routing always triggers a fitting, but in simple cases no explicit fitting exists.
conditions: when branching or routing is required in the flow distribution network

subject: IfcFlowTerminal
rationale: Flow terminals like diffusers, registers, or faucets depend on energy conversion devices (e.g., boilers, chillers) to condition the flow.
conditions: when the flow terminal is part of an active HVAC or plumbing system
exceptions: There are HVAC terminals (e.g., natural convection heaters, passive chilled beams) that do not depend on an IfcEnergyConversionDevice. In passive chilled beam systems, the terminal depends on a cooling source that may be represented as a chiller (IfcEnergyConversionDevice), but the dependency is indirect. Also, some flow terminals in non-active HVAC systems (e.g., simple grilles in natural ventilation) do not depend on energy conversion devices.

subject: IfcFlowTerminal
rationale: Flow terminals often need upstream valves, dampers, or regulators to control flow rate or pressure.
applicability: all building types with mechanical systems
conditions: when flow regulation is needed

subject: IfcFlowTerminal
rationale: Flow terminals are typically installed in or serve specific spaces within a building.
conditions: when the flow terminal is located within a conditioned or serviced zone
exceptions: Outdoor flow terminals such as roof exhaust fans, louvers, or stormwater outlets may not be located within a conditioned or serviced IfcSpace. They can be located externally and still be flow terminals.

subject: IfcFlowTerminal
rationale: Flow terminals are components of larger distribution systems (e.g., air distribution, water supply, waste disposal).
applicability: all building types with building services
conditions: when the flow terminal is part of a formal system like HVAC, plumbing, or fire suppression

subject: IfcFlowTerminal
rationale: Flow terminals have ports (IfcDistributionPort) that enable connection to pipes, ducts, or cables.
conditions: for connectivity to the distribution network

subject: IfcFlowTerminal
rationale: Flow terminals are the endpoint devices that support the overall function of a distribution system by delivering or collecting flow.
applicability: IfcFlowTerminal supports IfcSystem only when the terminal performs final delivery or extraction. However, the assertion does not account for cases where the same terminal participates in multiple systems (e.g., a heat recovery terminal may be part of both supply and exhaust systems). The 'supports' relationship may be ambiguous in such cases.
conditions: when the terminal executes the final delivery or extraction of flow

subject: IfcFlowTerminal
rationale: Flow terminals connect to flow-moving devices (fans, pumps) that provide the motive force for the flow.
applicability: all building types with mechanical systems
conditions: when the system requires fans, pumps, or compressors to move the flow
exceptions: gravity-fed systems

Gravity-fed systems already listed as exceptions, but there are also systems where the flow moving device is not explicitly modeled as an IfcFlowMovingDevice. For example, in a district heating system, the pump may be outside the scope of the model. Additionally, natural ventilation relies on wind/stack effect, not an IfcFlowMovingDevice.

subject: IfcFlowTerminal
rationale: Each flow terminal contains one or more distribution ports for physical connection to the network.
conditions: always

subject: IfcFlowTerminal
rationale: Some terminals may require bespoke brackets, enclosures, or supports.
conditions: when custom mounting or support structures are needed
exceptions: when the terminal is directly mounted on a standard wall, floor, or ceiling

subject: IfcFlowTerminalType
rationale: Flow terminals are endpoints of flow distribution systems and require connecting segments (ducts, pipes) to operate.
conditions: when part of a ducted or piped network

subject: IfcFlowTerminalType
rationale: Flow terminals (e.g., air diffusers, radiators) are located within or adjacent to spaces to deliver or extract air/water.
conditions: for spatial placement within a conditioned or serviced zone
exceptions: IfcFlowTerminalType does not universally require IfcSpace. Flow terminals placed in interstitial spaces, plenums, or outside the building envelope (e.g., roof exhaust fans, exterior louvres) may not be placed within a conditioned or serviced zone/space.

subject: IfcFlowTerminalType
rationale: Flow terminal types such as diffusers, grilles, and VAV boxes are essential endpoints that deliver conditioned air or water to occupied zones, thus supporting the HVAC system's function.
conditions: when the terminal is part of an HVAC system

subject: IfcFlowTerminalType
rationale: Many flow terminals (e.g., radiators, fan coil units) depend on upstream energy conversion devices (boilers, chillers) to function.
conditions: when the terminal is part of a heating/cooling system

subject: IfcFlowTerminalType
rationale: Flow terminals often require dampers, valves, or VAV controllers to regulate flow rates.
applicability: all building types with mechanical systems
conditions: when flow regulation or balancing is required

subject: IfcFlowTerminalType
rationale: IfcFlowTerminalType defines the type information for IfcFlowTerminal occurrences. As a type object, it 'contains' the common property set and geometry definition shared by terminal instances.
applicability: IfcFlowTerminalType (a type definition, IfcTypeObject subtype) cannot 'contain' IfcFlowTerminal (occurrence/product instances). The relationship 'contains' is ambiguous: IfcFlowTerminalType defines properties for instances but does not contain them in a spatial or aggregative sense. IfcRelDefinesByType links the type to occurrences, which is a typing relationship, not containment.

subject: IfcFlowTerminalType
rationale: IfcFlowTerminalType depends on property sets (Pset_FlowTerminalTypeXxx) to define performance characteristics like airflow rate, pressure drop, or sound level.
conditions: when predefined properties are assigned to the terminal type

subject: IfcFlowTerminalType
rationale: To form a consistent type hierarchy, IfcFlowTerminalType may be nested under higher-level types or aggregate subtypes via IfcRelNests.
conditions: when the terminal type is part of an assembly or nested system

subject: IfcFlowTreatmentDevice
rationale: Air treatment devices (silencers, air filters, coils) require ductwork for air conveyance.
conditions: when handling air or gases in HVAC
exceptions: An IfcFlowTreatmentDevice like a silencer or sound attenuator in an HVAC system may be installed inline within ductwork but is not always 'requiring' ductwork in a causal sense — the ductwork already exists and the device is placed within it. Some modular or packaged HVAC units integrate treatment devices without separate ductwork runs. The phrasing 'requires' is too strong; a more accurate phrasing would be 'is typically installed within' or 'connects to' ductwork.

subject: IfcFlowTreatmentDevice
rationale: Valves are often installed adjacent to treatment devices for maintenance isolation and flow control.
conditions: for isolation, drainage, or bypass arrangements

subject: IfcFlowTreatmentDeviceType
rationale: Flow treatment devices often depend on flow moving devices (pumps, fans) to push fluid through the treatment process.
applicability: all building types with mechanical flow systems
conditions: when fluid flow requires active mechanical movement
exceptions: gravity-driven flow systems

subject: IfcFlowTreatmentDeviceType
rationale: Flow treatment devices are connected via piping/ducting to bring fluid to and from the device.
conditions: for liquid or gas flow treatment

subject: IfcFlowTreatmentDeviceType
rationale: Air treatment devices (filters, coils) are installed within ductwork.
conditions: for air treatment applications

subject: IfcFlowTreatmentDeviceType
rationale: Flow controllers (valves, dampers) are often required to regulate flow through treatment devices.
conditions: when flow regulation is needed before or after treatment
exceptions: simple inline treatment devices without control valves/dampers

The existing exception mentions 'simple inline treatment devices without control valves/dampers' but this omits devices like in-line strainers, check valves (which are flow controllers but not regulation-oriented), and backflow preventers where the flow controller is integral to the device itself rather than a separate IfcFlowController element. Also, many treatment devices in fire protection systems (e.g., fire sprinkler system backflow preventers) may not require a separate IfcFlowController.

subject: IfcFlowTreatmentDeviceType
rationale: Treatment devices support the overall distribution system by conditioning the fluid (air, water, gas) to required quality standards.
conditions: when treating fluid for a distribution network

subject: IfcFlowTreatmentDeviceType
rationale: IfcFlowTreatmentDeviceType is the parent type that includes IfcFilter as a subtype for particle removal.
conditions: when the treatment device type is a filter or filter assembly

subject: IfcFlowTreatmentDeviceType
rationale: Interceptors (grease traps, oil separators) are a subtype of flow treatment device.
applicability: plumbing systems in commercial kitchens, garages, industrial facilities
conditions: when the treatment device type is an interceptor (grease, oil, sediment trap)

subject: IfcFlowTreatmentDeviceType
rationale: Duct silencers are flow treatment devices that treat noise in air distribution systems.
conditions: when the treatment device type is an acoustic treatment device for air ducts

subject: IfcFlowTreatmentDeviceType
rationale: Some dampers (fire dampers, smoke dampers) can be classified as treatment devices for safety rather than flow control.
conditions: when the damper is used for smoke control or fire protection purposes
exceptions: simple volume control dampers which are flow controllers

subject: IfcFooting
rationale: Reinforced concrete is the most common material for footings due to compressive strength and durability.
conditions: Typically reinforced concrete
exceptions: Stone masonry footings in historic construction
Timber footings in temporary structures

subject: IfcFooting
rationale: Footings provide a base for columns, spreading concentrated column loads over the soil.
conditions: Direct load transfer
exceptions: Load-bearing walls may bear directly on strip footings

subject: IfcFooting
rationale: Strip footings support continuous load-bearing walls.
conditions: Load-bearing walls
exceptions: Non-load-bearing partition walls

subject: IfcFooting
rationale: Footings provide a bearing surface for foundation walls.
conditions: In buildings with basements or crawlspaces
exceptions: Slab-on-grade foundations without walls

subject: IfcFooting
rationale: Moisture protection may be needed to prevent concrete deterioration and water ingress.
applicability: Waterproofing is not always directly applied to the IfcFooting element itself; in many cases it is applied to the IfcWall (foundation wall) or as a separate IfcCovering layer. The assertion implies the footing entity requires waterproofing, but in IFC modeling practice, waterproofing is typically a property or covering of the wall or slab, not a requirement of the footing entity.
conditions: In areas with high water table or moisture exposure
exceptions: Dry climate or well-drained sites

subject: IfcFootingType
rationale: IfcFootingType defines the type information for IfcFooting instances; footings require concrete footings or foundation elements to transfer loads to the ground.
conditions: when used as a structural foundation element

subject: IfcFootingType
rationale: IfcFootingType may be associated with IfcPropertySet to define type-level properties like dimensions, material grades, and load capacities.
conditions: when type-specific properties are needed

subject: IfcFootingType
rationale: IfcFootingType depends on IfcRelDefinesByType relationship to associate occurrences (IfcFooting) with the type definition.
conditions: when defining occurrences of the type

subject: IfcFootingType
