rationale: Footing types depend on material definitions (e.g., concrete, reinforced concrete, stone) for structural performance.
conditions: when material properties are assigned to the type

subject: IfcFootingType
rationale: Footings support columns by transferring vertical loads from columns to the soil.
conditions: when footings are used as column foundations
exceptions: pile foundations instead of spread footings

subject: IfcFootingType
rationale: Strip footings support load-bearing walls by distributing wall loads to the ground.
conditions: when footings are used as strip footings under walls

subject: IfcFootingType
rationale: Footings can provide edge support or point support for foundation slabs.
applicability: buildings with slab-on-grade or raft foundations
conditions: when footings support foundation slabs or raft foundations

subject: IfcFootingType
rationale: Properly designed footings protect the superstructure from damage caused by uneven soil settlement.
conditions: when footings protect against differential settlement

subject: IfcFootingType
rationale: Footings protect the building from being overturned or displaced by lateral loads.
applicability: buildings in seismic or high-wind zones
conditions: when designed to resist uplift, overturning, and sliding forces

subject: IfcFootingType
rationale: Footings connect the building structure to the ground (IfcSite), transferring loads to the earth.
conditions: when footings bear directly on soil or rock

subject: IfcFootingType
rationale: Footings (pile caps) connect to piles to transfer loads through weak soil to competent strata.
conditions: when footings are combined with pile foundations (pile caps)

subject: IfcFootingType
rationale: Footing types require structural actions (loads) to be defined for analysis and design.
conditions: for structural analysis and design verification

subject: IfcFootingType
rationale: Reinforced concrete footings contain reinforcing elements (rebar, mesh) as an integral part.
conditions: when footings are reinforced
exceptions: plain concrete footings without reinforcement

subject: IfcFootingType
rationale: Footings may contain grounding conductors or connection ports for electrical earthing systems.
conditions: when footings include grounding or earthing connections

subject: IfcFurnishingElement
rationale: In the IFC schema, IfcFurnishingElement must be related to a spatial structure via IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure.
conditions: for containment relationship in the IFC data model

subject: IfcFurnishingElement
rationale: Furnishing elements are typically assigned to a specific building storey in the IFC spatial hierarchy.
conditions: when placed on a specific floor level

subject: IfcFurnishingElement
rationale: In the IFC schema, IfcFurnishingElement can participate in IfcRelAggregates relationships for assembly decomposition.
applicability: all building types with IFC modeling

IfcRelAggregates is used for whole-part decomposition, not for 'connecting' furnishing elements to assemblies. While IfcFurnishingElement can participate in IfcRelAggregates as a related element (e.g., a chair as part of a furniture set), the assertion uses 'connects_to' which suggests a connection relationship. IFC has IfcRelConnectsElements for actual connections. The phrasing conflates aggregation with connection, which are semantically distinct.
conditions: when furnishing element is part of a larger furniture system assembly

subject: IfcFurnishingElementType
rationale: IfcFurnishingElementType objects are types of furnishing elements that are placed within spaces (IfcSpace). The IFC schema defines that furnishing elements are typically contained within spaces.
conditions: when furnishing elements are assigned to a spatial structure

subject: IfcFurnishingElementType
rationale: IfcFurnishingElementType may be aggregated into composite furnishing types via IfcRelAggregates relationship, defining part-whole hierarchies.
conditions: when used to define hierarchical assemblies of furnishing elements

subject: IfcFurnishingElementType
rationale: IfcFurnishingElementType defines the common properties for occurrences (IfcFurnishingElement). The type contains definitions that are shared across multiple occurrences.
conditions: when instantiated as type-occurrence relationships

subject: IfcFurnishingElementType
rationale: IfcFurnishingElementType may have property sets (IfcPropertySetDefinition) assigned to define type-level properties.
conditions: when type-specific properties are defined

subject: IfcFurnishingElementType
rationale: Furnishing element types (e.g., furniture, cabinets) are typically manufactured from materials that need to be defined for specifications and cost estimation.
applicability: all building types with physical furnishings
conditions: when furnishing elements are made of specific materials
exceptions: virtual or conceptual furnishing types without physical material

The existing exception only mentions 'virtual or conceptual furnishing types without physical material', but should also cover cases where material is defined at the occurrence level (IfcFurnishingElement) rather than at the type level, which is common when individual instances have different materials.

subject: IfcFurnishingElementType
rationale: Some furnishing element types may be supported by or attached to building elements (walls, floors, ceilings), though this is not inherent to all furnishing types.
conditions: when furnishing elements are built-in or attached to building elements
exceptions: freestanding furniture not attached to building structure

subject: IfcFurnishingElementType
rationale: The IFC schema uses IfcRelDefinesByType to link IfcFurnishingElement occurrences to their IfcFurnishingElementType, which is fundamental to the type-occurrence pattern.
conditions: when occurrences are associated to the type

subject: IfcFurnishingElementType
rationale: Furnishing element types may be assigned to other products or systems through assignment relationships.
conditions: when furnishing types are assigned to products or systems

subject: IfcFurniture
rationale: Furniture is always located within a space (room, zone, or area) in building models.
applicability: The assertion says 'requires' but IfcFurniture can exist in IFC models without being placed inside an IfcSpace (e.g., outdoor furniture, furniture in corridors that are not modeled as spaces, or during early design stages). IFC does not mandate that every IfcFurniture must be within an IfcSpace.
conditions: Furniture must be placed within a defined room or area

subject: IfcFurniture
rationale: Furniture requires a floor slab or raised floor for physical support.
conditions: Furniture rests on a floor surface

subject: IfcFurniture
rationale: In IFC, furniture is contained within a spatial structure element like IfcBuildingStorey.
conditions: Furniture must be assigned to a spatial container in IFC

subject: IfcFurniture
rationale: Some built-in furniture may fill openings or niches, but this is not typical for most furniture.
conditions: When furniture is built-in and fills an opening
exceptions: IfcFurniture 'supports' IfcRelFillsElement. IfcRelFillsElement is used for elements that fill openings (like doors, windows in wall openings). Built-in furniture like kitchen cabinets typically do not fill openings in walls; they occupy space. This relationship is rarely applicable to furniture and may be semantically incorrect.

subject: IfcFurniture
rationale: Complex furniture items (e.g., shelving units, workstations) can contain sub-assemblies.
conditions: When furniture has sub-components or modular parts

subject: IfcFurniture
rationale: Furniture is typically placed on a specific floor/storey in the building.
conditions: Furniture is assigned to a specific floor level

subject: IfcFurniture
rationale: Furniture may be assigned to groups (e.g., furniture sets, room inventories).
conditions: When furniture belongs to a furniture group or system

subject: IfcFurniture
rationale: Furniture requires property sets for detailed specification in IFC models.
conditions: For specifying furniture properties like dimensions, material, and fire rating

subject: IfcFurniture
rationale: Furniture items are often classified for asset management and procurement.
conditions: When furniture needs to be classified according to standards (e.g., Uniclass, OmniClass)

subject: IfcFurniture
rationale: Furniture placement requires positioning data in 3D space.
conditions: For specifying exact placement coordinates

subject: IfcFurniture
rationale: Furniture supports building occupants by providing seating, work surfaces, storage, etc.
applicability: IfcFurniture does not 'support' IfcOccupant. IfcOccupant is an actor role related to IfcActor, not directly related to furniture. Furniture is designed for human use, but the IFC schema does not define a 'supports' relationship between IfcFurniture and IfcOccupant.
conditions: Furniture is designed for human use

subject: IfcFurniture
rationale: Some furniture may have coverings that protect the base material, but this is not universal.
conditions: When furniture has upholstery, protective finishes, or coatings

subject: IfcFurniture
rationale: Furniture often is instantiated from a type definition in IFC.
conditions: When furniture is defined by a type template (e.g., a specific product model)

subject: IfcFurnitureType
rationale: Furniture instances are contained within a spatial structure via this relationship.
conditions: when associating furniture to a spatial container

subject: IfcFurnitureType
rationale: Furniture types are physically made from materials like wood, metal, plastic, or fabric, which need to be defined as IfcMaterial.
applicability: IfcFurnitureType does not require IfcMaterial in all cases. Material association via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial is optional. Furniture types may be defined without explicit material definitions (e.g., conceptual design phases, generic types).
conditions: when furniture is physically manufactured

subject: IfcFurnitureType
rationale: Properties like dimensions, weight, and fire rating are assigned via property sets associated to the furniture type.
applicability: IfcPropertySet is not required for IfcFurnitureType. Property sets are optional; an IfcFurnitureType can be defined with only geometric representation and no property sets.
conditions: when specifying furniture properties

subject: IfcFurnitureType
rationale: Built-in furniture types may fill openings or be connected to building elements like walls via this relationship.
conditions: when furniture is built-in or fitted (e.g., kitchen cabinets)
exceptions: free-standing furniture

subject: IfcGeographicElement
rationale: IfcGeographicElement represents geographic features (terrain, bodies of water, etc.) which are typically situated within or related to an IfcSite.
conditions: when representing geographic features within a site context
exceptions: IfcGeographicElement can exist without IfcSite in early design stages or when used purely for GIS-based analysis without a modeled site. IFC allows geographic elements at the project root level.

subject: IfcGeographicElement
rationale: Accurate geographic positioning depends on a defined coordinate reference system to map the element to global coordinates.
conditions: for accurate georeferencing and alignment with real-world coordinates

subject: IfcGeographicElement
rationale: An IfcGeographicElement can be associated with an IfcGeographicElementType defining common properties for the element type (e.g., terrain type, water body type).
conditions: when type information is assigned to the geographic element instance

subject: IfcGeographicElement
rationale: Geographic elements like terrain or land parcels provide the physical ground support for building structures.
conditions: when the geographic element forms the terrain or foundation ground for a building
exceptions: floating or suspended building structures

IfcGeographicElement can support IfcBuilding via IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure, but IfcBuilding may also be placed directly on IfcSite without a geographic element acting as terrain. The assertion overstates the necessity of the relationship.

subject: IfcGeographicElement
rationale: Geographic features such as ground surfaces support roads, bridges, tunnels, and other civil elements.
conditions: when the geographic element serves as base or context for civil engineering works

subject: IfcGeographicElement
rationale: Geographic elements are typically spatially connected to the IfcSite that contains them.
applicability: all IFC models with geographic elements and sites
conditions: when the geographic element is spatially contained within a site

subject: IfcGeographicElement
rationale: Geographic elements may require property sets to define their specific characteristics (e.g., soil type, vegetation coverage, water depth).
applicability: IfcGeographicElement does not always require IfcPropertySet; it can be used with only basic IFC attributes and no custom property sets. This is an optional enhancement, not a requirement.
conditions: when additional properties beyond the basic definition are needed

subject: IfcGeographicElement
rationale: Certain geographic elements such as hills or tree lines can protect buildings from wind, erosion, or flooding, but this is context-dependent.
applicability: sites with natural topography providing shelter
conditions: when the geographic element is a natural barrier (e.g., hill, embankment) shielding a building from environmental forces

subject: IfcGeographicElementType
rationale: IfcGeographicElementType defines types for geographic elements (like terrain, land parcels, bodies of water) which depend on site context for placement and meaning.
conditions: when geographic element is a land parcel or terrain feature

subject: IfcGeographicElementType
rationale: Geographic elements are typically aggregated within or referenced to spatial structure elements like site, building, or facility.
conditions: for proper spatial containment and reference

subject: IfcGeographicElementType
rationale: IfcGeographicElementType defines the type information that applies to one or many IfcGeographicElement instances; it 'contains' the type definition shared by those elements.

subject: IfcGeographicElementType
rationale: Geographic elements like terrain or soil bodies support building structures by providing foundational ground.
conditions: when geographic element is a foundation soil or terrain feature
exceptions: if geographic element is a body of water or vegetation unrelated to structural support

subject: IfcGeographicElementType
rationale: To define a geographic element type meaningfully, property sets describing geometric and material characteristics are typically required.
applicability: The assertion says 'requires IfcPropertySetDefinition' but IfcTypeObject (parent of IfcGeographicElementType) has an optional HasPropertySets relationship, not a required one. The statement overstates mandatory nature.
conditions: when specific properties like area, volume, material composition are needed

subject: IfcGeographicElementType
rationale: Geographic elements (terrain, existing ground) and building elements may spatially conflict if not properly modeled and coordinated.
conditions: when geographic element occupies the same physical space as a building element without proper coordination
exceptions: when properly coordinated by design

subject: IfcGeographicElementType
rationale: IfcGeographicElementType may connect to other spatial elements through aggregation relationships, linking geographic features to the broader project structure.
conditions: when used in a spatial decomposition hierarchy

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationContext
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationContext is a subtype (inherits from) IfcRepresentationContext, so it fundamentally depends on the parent type's structure and attributes.
applicability: All IFC models using geometric representations
conditions: When the geometric representation context needs to be placed within a broader modeling context

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationContext
rationale: The world coordinate system axes (default or custom) are defined using IfcDirection, which is essential for establishing the orientation of the 3D space.
conditions: When specifying coordinate axes directions (x, y, z)

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationContext
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationContext can have parent-child relationships with IfcGeometricRepresentationSubContext, which subdivide the context into specific representation targets.
applicability: IFC models with multiple representation views
conditions: When the context has sub-contexts for different representation types (e.g., plan view, model view)

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationContext
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationContext provides the context (coordinate space, precision, etc.) within which IfcShapeRepresentation instances are defined and interpreted.
applicability: All IFC models with shape representations
conditions: When geometric representations are assigned to this context

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationContext
rationale: Geometric sets may be placed within or referenced by the geometric representation context to define collections of geometric elements.
applicability: IFC models using geometric sets for representation
conditions: When the geometric context groups geometric items as a set

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationContext
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationContext defines the spatial framework (coordinate system, precision) that all IfcProduct instances (walls, slabs, beams, etc.) use for their geometric placement and representation.
conditions: When products need to be positioned and represented geometrically in the model

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationContext
rationale: In IFC, IfcProject has a relationship to IfcGeometricRepresentationContext as the default representation context for the project, establishing the coordinate space for all building elements.
conditions: When the project defines the default geometric representation context for the entire model

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationContext
rationale: The geometric representation context's world coordinate system serves as the absolute reference frame for all IfcLocalPlacement definitions throughout the model hierarchy.
conditions: When local placements are defined relative to the world coordinate system

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem is the abstract supertype for all geometric representation items used within IfcRepresentation. It depends on IfcRepresentation to be placed within a model context.
conditions: when used as a geometry representation in IFC models

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem is the parent type for IfcPoint and its subtypes (e.g., IfcCartesianPoint).
conditions: when modeling point-based geometry

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem is the parent type for IfcCurve and its subtypes (e.g., IfcLine, IfcCircle).
conditions: when modeling curve-based geometry

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem is the parent type for IfcSurface and its subtypes.
conditions: when modeling surface geometry

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem is the parent type for IfcSolidModel and its subtypes (e.g., IfcExtrudedAreaSolid, IfcRevolvedAreaSolid).
conditions: when modeling 3D solid geometry

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem includes IfcBooleanResult as a subtype for CSG operations.
conditions: when performing Boolean operations on solid geometry

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem includes IfcGeometricSet for collecting points, curves, and surfaces.
conditions: when grouping multiple geometric items

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem includes IfcPlacement and its subtypes (IfcAxis2Placement2D, IfcAxis2Placement3D).
conditions: when defining coordinate placement

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem provides the geometry that IfcProduct subtypes use for their shape representations.
conditions: when providing shape representation for building elements

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem
rationale: Geometric representation items form the core geometry data in IfcShapeRepresentation, enabling visualization and analysis.
conditions: when used as Items in an IfcShapeRepresentation

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcStyledItem can be associated with geometric items to provide rendering information like color and transparency.
conditions: when visual presentation properties are assigned

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationItem
rationale: Geometric items depend on the geometric representation context for coordinate space, dimensionality, and precision settings.
conditions: when the coordinate system and precision need to be defined

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationSubContext
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationSubContext is a subtype of IfcGeometricRepresentationContext and requires a parent context (IfcGeometricRepresentationContext) to define the coordinate space it refines.
conditions: When establishing the parent coordinate system for the subcontext

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationSubContext
rationale: The subcontext serves as a container or coordinate frame for geometric representation items, which depend on it for correct spatial interpretation.
conditions: When geometric items are assigned to this subcontext

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationSubContext
rationale: IfcShapeRepresentation can reference an IfcGeometricRepresentationSubContext to define which view (e.g., plan, model) the shape representation belongs to.
conditions: When representing product shape in a specific view

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationSubContext
rationale: Products (IfcProduct subtypes) use shape representations that may be assigned to a subcontext for proper display and analysis.
conditions: When products have geometric representations defined in a subcontext

subject: IfcGeometricRepresentationSubContext
rationale: The subcontext, as a refined coordinate context, contains the geometric representation items that define shapes within its view.
conditions: When geometric items are aggregated under this subcontext

subject: IfcGeometricSet
rationale: IfcGeometricSet is a collection of geometric representation items; IfcCartesianPoint is the fundamental building block for defining points in 3D space.
conditions: when representing point-based geometric sets

subject: IfcGeometricSet
rationale: IfcGeometricSet can contain curves (e.g., IfcLine, IfcPolyline) as part of its geometric representation.
conditions: when the geometric set includes curve-based geometry

subject: IfcGeometricSet
rationale: IfcGeometricSet can contain surface items such as IfcPlanarSurface or IfcCurveBoundedSurface.
conditions: when the geometric set includes surface geometry

subject: IfcGeometricSet
rationale: IfcGeometricSet can directly contain geometric items, including points.
conditions: when the set is composed of points

subject: IfcGeometricSet
rationale: The IfcGeometricSet may be a collection of curves representing wireframe geometry.
conditions: when the set is composed of curves

subject: IfcGeometricSet
rationale: IfcGeometricSet can contain surface representations for non-manifold surface geometry.
conditions: when the set is composed of surfaces

subject: IfcGeometricSet
rationale: IfcGeometricSet is a subtype of IfcGeometricRepresentationItem, meaning it provides geometric data that supports the representation of building elements.
conditions: when used as a geometric representation within an IfcProduct or IfcTypeProduct

subject: IfcGeometricSet
rationale: IfcGeometricSet inherits from IfcRepresentationItem and requires the representation context to be meaningful.
conditions: when included in an IfcShapeRepresentation

subject: IfcGrid
rationale: An IfcGrid is composed of grid axes (IfcGridAxis) which define the grid lines; without axes the grid has no spatial definition.
conditions: grid axes must be defined

subject: IfcGrid
rationale: IfcGrid contains one or more IfcGridAxis entities that define the grid lines.

subject: IfcGrid
rationale: Grids provide the reference layout for structural and spatial organization of a building, supporting coordination of columns, walls, and modules.
conditions: when used as a layout reference for structural columns, walls, or modules

subject: IfcGrid
rationale: IfcGrid can be the spatial container for building elements placed along the grid.
conditions: elements are placed relative to the grid

subject: IfcGrid
rationale: An IfcGrid requires an IfcLocalPlacement to define its position within the project.
conditions: grid must have a placement relative to the project coordinate system
exceptions: IfcGrid does not strictly require IfcLocalPlacement. An IfcGrid can be defined with no placement in certain modeling scenarios (e.g., when used as a conceptual design grid not yet positioned in the project coordinate system, or when the grid is defined relative to another placement context). The ObjectPlacement attribute is optional.

subject: IfcGrid
rationale: Grids serve as the reference for column placement, connecting structural columns to grid intersections.
conditions: columns are typically placed at grid intersections
exceptions: free-form or non-rectilinear layouts

subject: IfcGrid
rationale: Grids provide reference lines for wall alignment in orthogonal building designs.
conditions: walls may be aligned to grid lines
exceptions: curved or non-orthogonal walls

subject: IfcGrid
rationale: A regular grid improves load distribution clarity and structural coordination.
conditions: when structural elements are placed on a regular grid

subject: IfcGrid
rationale: Every IFC entity, including IfcGrid, depends on IfcOwnerHistory for ownership and audit trail.
applicability: IfcGrid does not semantically depend on IfcOwnerHistory. IfcOwnerHistory is a mandatory attribute for all IFC root entities (including IfcGrid) as part of the IFC schema's data model, but this is a schema-level requirement, not a domain or design dependency. The assertion conflates schema compliance with domain relationships.
conditions: as part of the IFC data model requirements

subject: IfcGridAxis
rationale: IfcGridAxis is a component of an IfcGrid, which groups multiple axes together.
conditions: as a parent container

subject: IfcGridAxis
rationale: Grid axes often reference virtual grid intersections to define their start/end points within the grid.
conditions: for intersecting axes to define grid points

subject: IfcGridPlacement
rationale: IfcGridPlacement is a placement that places an object relative to a grid axis (IfcGrid). The grid defines the coordinate reference.
applicability: All building types using grid-based design
conditions: Grid placement must reference a valid IfcGrid

subject: IfcGridPlacement
rationale: IfcGridPlacement uses IfcVirtualGridIntersection to define the location where grid axes cross.
conditions: When placement is defined by intersection of two grid axes
exceptions: When using offset placement only, may not need explicit intersection

IfcGridPlacement can use IfcVirtualGridIntersection but the 'depends_on' relationship is too strong. IfcGridPlacement can also be placed by offset placement (PlacementOffsets attribute) without requiring any IfcVirtualGridIntersection at all. The assertion already notes this exception, but the assertion title should be more conditional.

subject: IfcGridPlacement
rationale: Grid axes define the directional lines within the grid that the placement references.
conditions: Grid axes must exist in the referenced IfcGrid

subject: IfcGridPlacement
rationale: IfcGridPlacement provides the coordinate system for positioning building elements relative to a design grid.
applicability: Structural columns, beams, slabs aligned to grid
conditions: Elements placed using grid placement reference
exceptions: Elements placed using local placement or other placement types

subject: IfcGridPlacement
rationale: Columns are commonly placed at grid intersections using IfcGridPlacement.
applicability: Multi-story buildings with regular column grids
conditions: Columns located at grid intersections

subject: IfcGridPlacement
rationale: Beams often run along grid axes and use grid placement for positioning.
conditions: Beams spanning between grid axes

subject: IfcGridPlacement
rationale: IfcGridPlacement can be the PlacementRelTo for IfcLocalPlacement, creating a chain of placements.
applicability: Complex positioning where grid and local placements are combined
conditions: When grid placement is nested within a local placement or vice versa
exceptions: When grid placement is used standalone

subject: IfcGridPlacement
rationale: The intersection point is an inherent part of the grid placement definition.
applicability: All IfcGridPlacement instances with intersection-based positioning
conditions: Placement defined by two intersecting axes

subject: IfcGroup
rationale: IfcGroup depends on the IfcRelAssignsToGroup relationship entity to semantically link group members. Without this relationship, an IfcGroup instance has no content.

subject: IfcGroup
rationale: IfcSystem is a subtype of IfcGroup; thus IfcGroup conceptually can contain building service systems (e.g., HVAC, electrical) grouped together.
applicability: While IfcSystem is a subtype of IfcGroup, the 'contains' relationship is not direct instantiation. IfcSystem is assigned to IfcGroup via IfcRelAssignsToGroup, not by simple subtyping containment. The condition states it's a subtype relationship but the mechanism is through assignment, which may mislead about the nature of containment.
conditions: IfcSystem is a subtype of IfcGroup

subject: IfcGroup
rationale: IfcZone is a subtype of IfcGroup used to group spaces by thermal, lighting, or functional zones.
applicability: Similar to IfcSystem: IfcZone is a subtype of IfcGroup but assignment to an IfcGroup occurs via IfcRelAssignsToGroup, not through direct subtype relationship. The containment semantics are mediated through a relationship entity, not inheritance.
conditions: IfcZone is a subtype of IfcGroup

subject: IfcGroup
rationale: IfcGroup can group assets for facility management purposes (e.g., all furniture in a floor).
conditions: IfcAsset is assignable to IfcGroup via IfcRelAssignsToGroup

subject: IfcGroup
rationale: IfcGroup can contain inventory items for tracking building contents.
conditions: IfcInventory can be assigned to IfcGroup

subject: IfcGroup
rationale: IfcGroup can contain work plans and schedules for construction or renovation activities.
conditions: IfcWorkPlan is a subtype of IfcWorkControl which can be grouped

subject: IfcGroup
rationale: IfcGroup can contain cost schedules for cost management purposes.
conditions: IfcCostSchedule can be assigned to IfcGroup

subject: IfcGroup
rationale: By grouping related components into systems, IfcGroup supports the overall organization and management of the building model.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcGroup supports IfcBuilding' with the condition 'When IfcGroup is used to organize building systems' is vague. IfcBuilding is not a direct participant in IfcRelAssignsToGroup in standard IFC schema usage — IfcBuilding is a subtype of IfcSpatialStructureElement and is typically part of IfcRelAggregates or IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure, not grouping via IfcGroup. The relationship between IfcGroup and IfcBuilding is not well-defined in the IFC schema.
conditions: When IfcGroup is used to organize building systems (e.g., IfcSystem)

subject: IfcGroup
rationale: IfcGroup supports project management by grouping related project tasks, resources, or controls.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcGroup supports IfcProject' is problematic. IfcProject is a subtype of IfcObjectDefinition and serves as the root container for the entire model. IfcGroup does not meaningfully 'support' IfcProject in the IFC schema; IfcRelAssignsToGroup does not typically assign IfcProject to IfcGroup. Project-level grouping is handled through IfcRelDeclares or IfcRelAggregates.
conditions: When IfcGroup aggregates project-related objects such as processes or controls

subject: IfcHalfSpaceSolid
rationale: IfcHalfSpaceSolid is always defined by a base surface (IfcSurface) that separates the half-space from the rest of the domain.
conditions: When defining the half-space solid as a subtype of IfcSolidModel

subject: IfcHalfSpaceSolid
rationale: IfcHalfSpaceSolid uses a placement coordinate system typically defined via IfcAxis2Placement3D to orient the base surface.
conditions: When the half-space solid requires positioning in 3D space

subject: IfcHalfSpaceSolid
rationale: IfcHalfSpaceSolid serves as the second operand in IfcBooleanClippingResult to clip a solid shape.
conditions: When the half-space solid is used as a clipping volume

subject: IfcHalfSpaceSolid
rationale: IfcHalfSpaceSolid is a valid operand in any IfcBooleanResult subtype for creating complex geometries.
conditions: When used in CSG Boolean operations (difference, intersection, union)
exceptions: IfcHalfSpaceSolid can be used in IfcBooleanResult operations only as the second operand (the clipping volume), not as the first operand. IfcHalfSpaceSolid cannot serve as the 'first operand' in a Boolean operation because it doesn't represent a finite solid volume by itself; it represents a half-space. When used the wrong operand order, the assertion does not hold.

subject: IfcHalfSpaceSolid
rationale: IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace is a subtype of IfcHalfSpaceSolid that adds a polygonal boundary to the otherwise infinite half-space.
conditions: When the half-space is bounded by a polygonal boundary

subject: IfcHalfSpaceSolid
rationale: Half-space solids are often used in conjunction with extruded area solids to create trimmed prismatic shapes like sloped roofs or excavation pits.
conditions: When clipping an extruded solid to create a sloped or trimmed shape

subject: IfcHalfSpaceSolid
rationale: In some workflows, the base surface of a half-space may reference a curve set, though this is less common.
conditions: When defining complex clipping boundaries

subject: IfcHeatExchanger
rationale: Pumps are required to circulate fluids through the heat exchanger unless natural convection suffices.
conditions: When the fluid is not moved by gravity alone
exceptions: Natural convection systems where no pump is needed

subject: IfcHeatExchanger
rationale: Piping is necessary to route fluids to and from the heat exchanger.
conditions: Always

subject: IfcHeatExchanger
rationale: Heat exchangers often work in conjunction with boilers, chillers, or heat pumps as energy conversion devices.
conditions: When the heat exchanger is part of a larger energy system

subject: IfcHeatExchanger
rationale: A heat exchanger supports the conditioning of indoor spaces by transferring thermal energy.
conditions: When the heat exchanger provides heating or cooling to occupied spaces
exceptions: Process heat exchangers not serving occupied spaces

subject: IfcHeatExchanger
rationale: Heat exchangers supply conditioned fluid to thermal zones.
conditions: When serving a thermal zone in a building
exceptions: Equipment-only installations

subject: IfcHeatExchanger
rationale: A heat exchanger can protect chiller equipment by separating the chiller loop from the building loop, preventing contamination and pressure issues.
conditions: When the heat exchanger acts as a condenser or evaporator in a chiller loop

subject: IfcHeatExchanger
rationale: A heat exchanger can protect a boiler by isolating it from system water that may cause corrosion or thermal shock.
applicability: Boiler systems with separate primary/secondary loops
conditions: When used as a hydronic separation heat exchanger

subject: IfcHeatExchanger
rationale: The heat exchanger connects to the building distribution system (e.g., hot water loop, chilled water loop).
conditions: Always when part of a building distribution network

subject: IfcHeatExchanger
rationale: Shell-and-tube heat exchangers contain tube bundles as the primary heat transfer surface.
applicability: The assertion states 'contains IfcTubeBundle' but applies only to shell-and-tube type. However, even within shell-and-tube exchangers, the tube bundle is typically a subassembly that may be modeled as an aggregate of tubes (IfcTubeType or IfcPipeSegment) rather than a single IfcTubeBundle entity. Additionally, IfcTubeBundle is not a standard IFC entity class in common schemas (IFC2x3 or IFC4).
conditions: For shell-and-tube type heat exchangers
exceptions: Plate heat exchangers, finned-tube exchangers

subject: IfcHeatExchanger
rationale: Flow meters may be needed to monitor fluid flow rates to ensure proper heat transfer performance.
conditions: When performance monitoring or balancing is required
exceptions: Simple systems without metering

subject: IfcHeatExchangerType
rationale: Pumps are required to circulate fluids through the heat exchanger to maintain flow.
conditions: In liquid-to-liquid systems
Unless relying on natural convection

subject: IfcHeatExchangerType
rationale: Heat exchangers connect to boilers to transfer heat from combustion to water or air.
conditions: In heating systems

subject: IfcHeatExchangerType
rationale: Heat exchangers connect to chillers to reject heat from the refrigeration cycle.
conditions: In cooling systems

subject: IfcHumidifier
rationale: In-duct humidifiers depend on the HVAC duct system to distribute humidified air.
conditions: When in-duct type humidifier

subject: IfcIShapeProfileDef
rationale: IfcIShapeProfileDef is commonly used as the cross-section for IfcBeam elements in IFC models.
conditions: When the profile is assigned to a beam element
exceptions: IfcIShapeProfileDef does not always connect to IfcBeam — I-shaped profiles are also used for purlins, girts, bracing members, and other secondary steel elements classified as IfcMember, not just IfcBeam. The condition 'when assigned to a beam element' conflates classification with profile usage.

subject: IfcIShapeProfileDef
rationale: I-shaped profiles are also commonly used as the cross-section for IfcColumn elements.
conditions: When the profile is assigned to a column element
exceptions: IfcIShapeProfileDef is also used for columns in non-building structures (e.g., bridge piers, sign gantries, industrial pipe supports) which are outside the stated 'steel framed buildings' applicability, but more importantly, columns in steel buildings often use H-shaped profiles (IfcIShapeProfileDef with wide-flange proportions) — the assertion is correct but the applicability restriction is too narrow.

subject: IfcIShapeProfileDef
rationale: IfcIShapeProfileDef is often used as the SweptArea within IfcExtrudedAreaSolid to create a 3D swept solid representation.
conditions: When creating a 3D representation of the profile

subject: IfcImageTexture
rationale: IfcImageTexture is a subtype of IfcSurfaceTexture in the IFC schema, inheriting its texture coordinate mapping and surface appearance properties.
applicability: all building models using image-based textures
conditions: when representing textured surfaces

subject: IfcImageTexture
rationale: Texture coordinates define how the image maps onto the surface geometry.
applicability: all building models with mapped textures
conditions: when mapping the texture to geometry

subject: IfcImageTexture
rationale: Texture transformation (translation, rotation, scaling) is handled via this operator.
applicability: textured surfaces where origin, scale, or orientation differs from default
conditions: when non-default texture placement is needed

subject: IfcImageTexture
rationale: IfcImageTexture contributes to the styled representation of building elements for visual appearance.
conditions: when used in a styled item for visual rendering

subject: IfcImageTexture
rationale: The texture is a component within surface style definitions to achieve realistic material appearances.
conditions: when the texture is part of a surface style definition

subject: IfcImageTexture
rationale: IfcPixelTexture is a sibling subtype of IfcSurfaceTexture but may be considered a different representation form; IfcImageTexture references external images, not embedded pixels.
conditions: when the texture data is embedded pixel-by-pixel rather than referenced from an external file

subject: IfcImageTexture
rationale: The texture is connected to surfaces to define their visual appearance.
applicability: textured building surfaces such as walls, floors, ceilings
conditions: when applied to a geometric surface

subject: IfcIndexedColourMap
rationale: IfcIndexedColourMap maps colour indices to RGB colour definitions; it depends on IfcColourRgb entries to provide the actual colour values for each index.
conditions: when colour values are defined as RGB triplets

subject: IfcIndexedColourMap
rationale: IfcIndexedColourMap is typically referenced by IfcSurfaceStyle to apply per-vertex or per-face colours to a surface representation.
conditions: when used for rendering shaded surfaces
exceptions: If used only for wireframe or non-visual analysis

subject: IfcIndexedColourMap
rationale: The indexed colour map is assigned to a geometric representation item to provide colour information, thereby supporting the visual representation of the building element.
conditions: when the representation is of type 'ColourMap' or similar visual presentation

subject: IfcIndexedColourMap
rationale: IfcIndexedColourMap can be applied to geometric items that may be instanced via IfcMappedItem, depending on the Cartesian transformation context.
conditions: when the coloured geometry is part of a mapped (instanced) representation

subject: IfcIndexedColourMap
rationale: IfcIndexedColourMap provides colour indexing that can be consumed by styling/presentation constructs in the IFC model.
conditions: when visual styling is assigned via IfcPresentationLayerAssignment

subject: IfcIndexedPolyCurve
rationale: IfcIndexedPolyCurve is a segmented curve defined by an ordered list of points stored in an IfcCartesianPointList, which provides the coordinate data for the curve segments.
conditions: When representing the polycurve as a segmented curve with explicit point coordinates

subject: IfcIndexedPolyCurve
rationale: IfcIndexedPolyCurve is a subtype of IfcBoundedCurve, inheriting its properties and constraints on curve bounds.
conditions: For classification as a subtype of bounded curve in the IFC schema

subject: IfcIndexedPolyCurve
rationale: As a geometric representation item, the curve typically requires placement context within an object's local coordinate system.
conditions: When placed within a building element coordinate system

subject: IfcIndexedPolyCurve
rationale: The curve implicitly contains the Cartesian points that define its vertices through an index into a point list.
conditions: Through the indexed point list referencing

subject: IfcIndexedPolyCurve
rationale: IfcIndexedPolyCurve with linear interpolation between points effectively defines a polyline, providing the same geometric semantics.
conditions: When the curve consists of straight line segments between consecutive indexed points

subject: IfcIndexedPolyCurve
rationale: The indexed poly curve can be trimmed to create bounded sub-curves for specific building geometry applications.
conditions: When trimming the curve to a specific parameter range
exceptions: IfcTrimmedCurve is a separate entity and is not directly 'supported by' IfcIndexedPolyCurve in the IFC schema. IfcIndexedPolyCurve provides a different indexing mechanism for polycurves; trimming would be done by wrapping it in an IfcTrimmedCurve if needed, but the assertion 'supports IfcTrimmedCurve' is vague and could be misinterpreted as a subtype relationship or direct functional association, which does not exist.

subject: IfcIndexedPolygonalFace
rationale: IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids is a subtype of IfcIndexedPolygonalFace that extends it to include inner loops for voids.
applicability: The assertion states 'When the face has internal openings or voids' but IfcIndexedPolygonalFace itself never has voids — only the subtype IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids does. The condition is misattributed to the wrong entity.
conditions: When the face has internal openings or voids

subject: IfcIndexedPolygonalFace
rationale: IfcIndexedPolygonalFace is typically aggregated within IfcPolygonalFaceSet which organizes the face collection and coordinates.
conditions: When used as part of a tessellated face set

subject: IfcIndexedPolygonalFace
rationale: Indexed polygonal faces can be used to construct faceted boundary representations of building elements.
conditions: When used in boundary representation modeling

subject: IfcIndexedPolygonalFace
rationale: IfcIndexedPolygonalFace serves as a fundamental building block for tessellated face sets used in mesh-based geometry.
conditions: When used in tessellated geometry representations

subject: IfcIndexedPolygonalFace
rationale: The indexed polygonal face references coordinates from an IfcCartesianPointList3D to position its vertices in 3D space.
conditions: For providing the 3D coordinate data

subject: IfcIndexedPolygonalFace
rationale: IfcIndexedPolygonalFace connects to IfcShapeRepresentation when it is used to define the shape of a building element.
conditions: When used in the context of product shape representation

subject: IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids
rationale: IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids references vertex coordinates from an IfcCartesianPointList3D via its CoordIndex attribute.
conditions: when representing face geometry with indexed vertices

subject: IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids
rationale: Can be used as the boundary of a polygonal bounded half-space.
conditions: when used as bounding geometry for half-space operations
exceptions: IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids does not have a direct dependency on IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace in the IFC schema. IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace is a subtype of IfcHalfSpaceSolid used in Boolean operations (e.g., via IfcBooleanResult), not in defining face geometry with indexed vertices. The half-space relationship is at the geometric model level, not at the indexed polygonal face level.

subject: IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids
rationale: This entity extends IfcIndexedPolygonalFace with inner void boundaries (inner loops) defining holes in the face.
conditions: when voids are defined via inner loops

subject: IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids
rationale: The face coordinates are typically interpreted within a local coordinate system defined by placement.
conditions: when the face is placed within a geometric representation context
exceptions: IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids itself is a geometry definition entity and does not directly reference IfcLocalPlacement. The placement is handled by the containing IfcPolygonalFaceSet which references IfcObjectPlacement (via IfcProduct). The dependency on IfcLocalPlacement is indirect through IfcPolygonalFaceSet and the product that uses it.

subject: IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids
rationale: The face is assigned as part of a shape representation for an IFC product.
conditions: when used in a product representation
exceptions: IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids does not directly depend on IfcShapeRepresentation. The shape representation is a container for representation items; IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids is a representation item that can be part of an IfcShapeRepresentation, but this is a 'contained in' relationship rather than a dependency. The dependency direction is reversed compared to what is stated.

subject: IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids
rationale: IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids can be used within IfcTessellatedItem or similar tessellated face set structures.
conditions: when the indexed face set defines the faces of a tessellated geometry

subject: IfcIndexedPolygonalFaceWithVoids
rationale: Inner void boundaries correspond to polygonal loops defined within the geometry.
conditions: when describing void boundaries as polygonal loops

subject: IfcIndexedTextureMap
rationale: IfcIndexedTextureMap is a subtype of IfcTextureCoordinate and relies on texture coordinate mapping to function.
applicability: All building types with textured surfaces
conditions: texture mapping requires coordinate assignment

subject: IfcIndexedTextureMap
rationale: IfcIndexedTextureMap is specifically designed to map textures onto tessellated face sets (IfcTessellatedFaceSet and its subtypes).
applicability: All building types using mesh/tessellated geometry
conditions: must be applied to a tessellated geometry representation

subject: IfcIndexedTextureMap
rationale: IfcIndexedTextureMap stores texture coordinates that reference texture image data, typically provided by IfcImageTexture.
applicability: All building types using image textures on 3D surfaces
conditions: required when using image-based texture maps
exceptions: Not needed if using other texture types like IfcPixelTexture

subject: IfcIndexedTextureMap
rationale: IfcIndexedTextureMap contains or references a list of texture coordinates (IfcTextureVertexList) that define the mapping of 2D texture space to 3D geometry.
applicability: All building types with textured 3D geometry
conditions: texture vertices are indexed by the texture map

subject: IfcIndexedTextureMap
rationale: IfcIndexedTextureMap maps texture coordinates to geometry, but the actual texture appearance is defined by an IfcSurfaceTexture instance.
applicability: All building types with rendered 3D surfaces

IfcIndexedTextureMap does not 'require' IfcSurfaceTexture in the sense of a hard dependency. While IfcIndexedTextureMap is typically associated with a surface texture to be meaningful, it is technically possible to define an IfcIndexedTextureMap without an IfcSurfaceTexture reference (it would just be an unused mapping). The assertion overstates the dependency as a requirement rather than a practical necessity.
conditions: must be assigned a surface texture to apply

subject: IfcIndexedTextureMap
rationale: IfcIndexedTextureMap contributes to the visual styling of building elements by providing texture mapping information that IfcStyledItem may reference.
applicability: All building types using visual styles with textures

IfcIndexedTextureMap does not directly 'support' IfcStyledItem in the IFC schema. IfcStyledItem relates to IfcRepresentationItem via IfcPresentationStyleAssignment. IfcIndexedTextureMap is a subclass of IfcTextureCoordinate, which is a subclass of IfcRepresentationItem. The indirect connection through the presentation/appearance model does not constitute a direct 'supports' relationship as asserted.
conditions: textured surfaces contribute to styled visual representation

subject: IfcIndexedTextureMap
rationale: IfcIndexedTextureMap helps visualize building elements in layers, supporting presentation layer assignments for visual clarity.
applicability: All building types with layered graphical presentation

IfcIndexedTextureMap does not directly 'support' IfcPresentationLayerAssignment. IfcPresentationLayerAssignment can be assigned to any IfcRepresentationItem via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial or IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle. Since IfcIndexedTextureMap is an IfcRepresentationItem, it can be assigned to a layer, but the connection is indirect and not unique to IfcIndexedTextureMap.
conditions: textured geometry may be organized into presentation layers

subject: IfcIndexedTextureMap
rationale: By providing texture mapping on tessellated geometry, IfcIndexedTextureMap improves the visual realism of building element proxies.
applicability: All building types using proxy representations
conditions: texture mapping improves visual realism of proxy elements

subject: IfcIndexedTextureMap
rationale: Texture mapping connects geometric surfaces to texture coordinate points, indirectly relating to Cartesian point definitions.
conditions: texture coordinates are defined in 2D or 3D coordinate space

subject: IfcIndexedTriangleTextureMap
rationale: IfcIndexedTriangleTextureMap references IfcTextureVertexList to provide the texture coordinate vertices indexed by the triangle faces.
applicability: IfcIndexedTriangleTextureMap depends directly on IfcTextureVertexList via the 'TexCoords' attribute (an IfcTextureVertexList reference), but it also depends on IfcTextureVertexList indirectly through the inheritance of mapped textures. The statement is correct as a direct dependency but omits that the real texture coordinate mapping is through indexed references (TexCoordIndex) into the IfcTextureVertexList, not a simple 'depends_on' relationship.
conditions: When mapping texture coordinates to triangle faces

subject: IfcIndexedTriangleTextureMap
rationale: The texture map applies a texture to surfaces; IfcSurfaceTexture defines the actual texture (image file, color, etc.) being mapped.
conditions: When a texture image or procedural texture is applied

subject: IfcIndexedTriangleTextureMap
rationale: IfcIndexedTriangleTextureMap is specifically used to map textures onto IfcTessellatedFaceSet (or its subtypes like IfcTriangulatedFaceSet) by indexing triangle faces.
conditions: When mapping textures onto a triangulated mesh geometry

subject: IfcIndexedTriangleTextureMap
rationale: IfcIndexedTriangleTextureMap provides the texture mapping needed for realistic visualization of IfcTriangulatedFaceSet geometry.
conditions: When visualizing surfaces with applied textures in BIM models

subject: IfcIndexedTriangleTextureMap
rationale: Indirectly supports visualization of building elements that use tessellated geometry representations with textures.
conditions: When generic building elements have triangulated mesh geometry with textures

subject: IfcIndexedTriangleTextureMap
rationale: The texture vertex list depends on Cartesian points to define texture coordinate locations in UV space.
applicability: IfcIndexedTriangleTextureMap depends on IfcTextureVertexList (which contains IfcCartesianPoint references), not directly on IfcCartesianPoint. The direct dependency is on IfcTextureVertexList, and IfcTextureVertexList in turn references IfcCartesianPoint. Stating a direct dependency on IfcCartesianPoint is misleading as it skips the intermediate IfcTextureVertexList.
conditions: As part of the referenced IfcTextureVertexList which stores point coordinates

subject: IfcInterceptorType
rationale: An IfcInterceptorType defines the type information for an IfcInterceptor (a device that separates pollutants from fluids), so it depends on the existence of interceptors that instantiate it.

subject: IfcInterceptorType
rationale: The type definition may specify materials of construction such as concrete, steel, or plastic for the interceptor body.

subject: IfcInterceptorType
rationale: Interceptor types depend on property sets to define nominal dimensions, flow rate capacity, and other technical parameters.

subject: IfcInterceptorType
rationale: Interceptors are a type of flow treatment device; the type definition supports the correct classification and specification of such devices.
conditions: when classified as a subtype of flow treatment device

subject: IfcInterceptorType
rationale: Interceptors protect downstream piping from clogging, grease buildup, or chemical damage by separating contaminants before they enter the pipe network.
applicability: The assertion states IfcInterceptorType protects_from IfcPipeSegment, but interceptors protect downstream equipment from solids/grease, not pipe segments specifically. Pipe segments may still require their own protection. More commonly, interceptors protect treatment equipment, not the piping itself. The 'protects_from' relationship with IfcPipeSegment is too narrow and potentially misleading.
conditions: when installed upstream of piping systems
exceptions: if bypass is provided

subject: IfcInterceptorType
rationale: An interceptor system may require valves or flow controllers to regulate inlet/outlet flow for proper operation.
conditions: when flow regulation or shutoff is needed

subject: IfcInterceptorType
rationale: Piping connections, elbows, tees, and couplings are required to connect the interceptor to the drainage system.

subject: IfcInterceptorType
rationale: Sanitary terminals such as sinks and floor drains connect to interceptors (e.g., grease interceptors under sinks).
conditions: when interceptors serve sanitary fixtures

subject: IfcInterceptorType
rationale: Interceptor installations may be supported by or integrated into structural building elements such as trench covers or support frames.
conditions: when interceptors are embedded in floor slabs or trenches

subject: IfcIntersectionCurve
rationale: IfcIntersectionCurve is a subtype of IfcCurve and is used to define the intersection of two surfaces in 3D space, inheriting geometric properties from IfcCurve.
conditions: when defining a 3D curve for geometric representation

subject: IfcIntersectionCurve
rationale: An intersection curve by definition results from the intersection of two surfaces; thus it depends on those surfaces for its geometric definition.
conditions: when computing the intersection curve between two surfaces

subject: IfcIntersectionCurve
rationale: In advanced boundary representations, intersection curves describe edges where faces meet, supporting the overall shape definition.
conditions: when representing complex boundary surfaces with intersection edges
exceptions: IfcIntersectionCurve supports IfcAdvancedBrep only when the advanced B-rep uses explicit intersection curve geometry for its edges. However, IfcAdvancedBrep can also represent complex boundary surfaces using other edge curve types (e.g., IfcTrimmedCurve, IfcLine) that are not IfcIntersectionCurve. The assertion overgeneralizes — it holds only for those IfcAdvancedBrep instances that actually have intersection edges represented as IfcIntersectionCurve.

subject: IfcIntersectionCurve
rationale: Boolean operations produce intersection curves as edges of the resulting solid geometry.
conditions: after boolean operations (union, intersection, difference) between solids

subject: IfcIntersectionCurve
rationale: The curve is typically defined by a set of Cartesian points in 3D space.
conditions: when defining control points along the intersection curve

subject: IfcIntersectionCurve
rationale: Intersection curves contribute to the geometric representation of building elements within a defined subcontext.
applicability: IfcGeometricRepresentationSubContext is a context that can refine a parent context (e.g., adding a plan view on top of a model view). While IfcIntersectionCurve can appear in a subcontext, the assertion omits that the parent context must support 3D representation and the subcontext must inherit the correct model dimensionality (usually 3D). Additionally, IfcIntersectionCurve is rarely used directly in subcontexts intended for 2D plan representations.
conditions: when used in a 3D geometric representation context for building elements

subject: IfcIntersectionCurve
rationale: Intersection curves help define precise geometry where building elements meet at complex surface intersections.
applicability: IfcIntersectionCurve is a low-level geometric representation type typically used in advanced B-rep, tessellation, or STEP-derived geometry exchange. Building elements at the IFC architectural level (e.g., IfcWall, IfcSlab) rarely directly reference IfcIntersectionCurve; instead, they use higher-level representations like extruded solids or tessellated faceted geometry. The assertion that IfcIntersectionCurve 'supports IfcBuildingElement' is misleading for 90%+ of typical building element representations.
conditions: when a building element's geometry involves complex surface intersections (e.g., curtain wall mullion intersections, roof surface intersections)

subject: IfcInventory
rationale: IfcInventory is always associated with an IfcProject as the root context for the inventory definition.
applicability: IfcInventory does not strictly require IfcProject in the IFC schema. IfcInventory is a subtype of IfcObjectDefinition and can be assigned to projects via IfcRelAssignsToProject, but it can also exist without a project context in some IFC model setups, e.g., in early design or asset libraries. The assertion overstates the requirement.
conditions: inventory must be assigned to a project context

subject: IfcInventory
rationale: IfcInventory may reference IfcOrganization as the responsible party for the inventory.
conditions: when inventory is managed by an external organization
exceptions: if inventory is managed internally without a formal organization reference

subject: IfcInventory
rationale: IfcInventory can relate to actors (IfcActor) with specific roles who manage or are responsible for the inventory.
conditions: when actors are assigned to manage inventory items

subject: IfcInventory
rationale: IfcInventory may be the basis for or relate to IfcAsset, where inventoried items become tracked assets.
conditions: when inventory items are tracked as assets

subject: IfcInventory
rationale: IfcInventory can contain classification references to categorize inventoried items (e.g., UNICLASS, MasterFormat).
conditions: when items within the inventory are classified

subject: IfcInventory
rationale: IfcInventory often works with cost schedules to assign costs to inventoried items for budgeting purposes.
conditions: when inventory is used for cost estimation or budgeting

subject: IfcIrregularTimeSeries
rationale: IfcIrregularTimeSeries is a container for irregular time series data, and its values are stored in IfcIrregularTimeSeriesValue entities.
applicability: all IFC models with time series data
conditions: when representing time series data points

subject: IfcIrregularTimeSeries
rationale: IfcIrregularTimeSeries contains a list of IfcIrregularTimeSeriesValue records representing individual data points.
applicability: The assertion says 'contains' without specifying whether it is a direct attribute containment or a relationship-based containment. In IFC, IfcIrregularTimeSeries has a direct attribute 'Values' of type LIST [1:?] OF IfcIrregularTimeSeriesValue, so the containment is direct via attribute. This should be clarified to distinguish from relationship-based containment (e.g., IfcRelAggregates).
conditions: when the time series has recorded values

subject: IfcIrregularTimeSeries
rationale: IfcIrregularTimeSeries is a subtype of IfcTimeSeries, so it inherits all its attributes and behaviors.
conditions: for inheriting basic time series attributes

subject: IfcIrregularTimeSeriesValue
rationale: IfcIrregularTimeSeriesValue is specifically a value element within an IfcIrregularTimeSeries, which collects multiple such values. It requires the parent time series container to give it context and meaning.
applicability: All building types using IFC for facilities management data
conditions: When the time series data has irregular intervals between data points
exceptions: If the time series is regular (IfcRegularTimeSeries), this parent class is not applicable

subject: IfcIrregularTimeSeriesValue
rationale: IfcIrregularTimeSeriesValue can store sensor data points that occur at uneven intervals (e.g., door open/close events, alert-based readings).
conditions: When sensor readings are recorded at non-uniform intervals (e.g., event-based triggers rather than fixed sampling rate)
exceptions: Sensors that report at fixed regular intervals use IfcRegularTimeSeriesValue instead

subject: IfcIrregularTimeSeriesValue
rationale: Time series values are often assigned to properties within property sets (e.g., Pset_SensorHistory). The property definition provides the semantic context for what the value represents.
conditions: When the time series value is associated with a property or property set

subject: IfcJunctionBox
rationale: Junction boxes are physically attached to building structural elements such as walls, ceilings, or floors.
applicability: The assertion does not account for junction boxes that are embedded within wall cavities (e.g., behind drywall with only a cover plate exposed), which is also a common installation method. The current conditions only mention surface-mounted or flush-mounted, which may be interpreted as fully exposed installations, thereby missing the concealed/embedded scenario.
conditions: when surface-mounted or flush-mounted on walls

subject: IfcJunctionBox
rationale: Overhead junction boxes are commonly attached to ceiling structures for lighting and power distribution.
conditions: when mounted overhead for lighting or equipment connections

subject: IfcJunctionBoxType
rationale: Cable carriers (trays, conduits) bring cables to and from junction boxes.
conditions: when used for routing cables through the junction box

subject: IfcJunctionBoxType
rationale: Cables are the primary elements passing through a junction box.
conditions: for electrical connectivity
exceptions: when box is unused/spare

subject: IfcJunctionBoxType
rationale: Junction boxes physically contain cable connections and splices.
conditions: when cables terminate or splice inside the box

subject: IfcJunctionBoxType
rationale: Junction boxes protect cable connections from dust, moisture, and physical damage.
conditions: in normal operation

subject: IfcJunctionBoxType
rationale: Junction boxes can connect to appliances as part of branch circuits.
conditions: when junction box serves as a connection point for appliances

subject: IfcJunctionBoxType
rationale: Junction boxes are installed within building spaces (walls, ceilings, floors).
conditions: for physical installation location
exceptions: IfcJunctionBoxType does not always depend_on IfcSpace. Junction boxes can be installed directly on equipment (e.g., on an IfcElectricMotor or IfcMachine), outdoors on a pole or structure not within a defined IfcSpace, or in underground/ceiling voids without an assigned IfcSpace.

subject: IfcJunctionBoxType
rationale: Junction boxes are often mounted on walls or embedded in wall constructions.
applicability: The assertion only mentions wall mounting but junction boxes can also be mounted on or embedded in ceilings (IfcSlab), floors, or embedded in concrete columns. The condition is too narrowly scoped to walls only.
conditions: when mounted on or embedded in a wall

subject: IfcJunctionBoxType
rationale: Potential spatial conflicts when installing junction boxes near plumbing or HVAC terminals.
conditions: if space is limited and both require the same physical location

subject: IfcJunctionBoxType
rationale: IfcJunctionBoxType defines the type, which can contain instances of IfcJunctionBox.
conditions: when type definition includes actual box instances

subject: IfcLShapeProfileDef
rationale: L-profiles are connected to beams, columns, and gusset plates in structural assemblies.
conditions: when part of a steel frame

subject: IfcLShapeProfileDef
rationale: The profile definition contains geometric parameters defined by Cartesian points (e.g., corner points).
conditions: in parametric definition

subject: IfcLShapeProfileDef
rationale: The profile needs an associated material (e.g., steel grade) via a material profile set to define its physical properties.
conditions: when assigned to a structural member

subject: IfcLShapeProfileDef
rationale: The profile definition relies on placement coordinates to define its orientation in the model.
conditions: for positioning in 3D space

subject: IfcLaborResource
rationale: IfcLaborResource represents the labor skills, trades, and workforce required for construction. It depends on IfcPerson (the actual individual performing the work) and IfcOrganization (the company providing the labor).
applicability: The assertion says IfcLaborResource 'depends_on IfcPerson' with condition 'when the labor resource is an individual person', but in IFC schema IfcLaborResource actually references IfcPerson via IfcResourceObjectSelect (through IfcActorSelect), not a direct dependency. The dependency may also be optional - IfcLaborResource can exist without an IfcPerson assigned (e.g., crew-based resource).
conditions: when the labor resource is an individual person

subject: IfcLaborResource
rationale: Labor resources are often associated with an organization (contractor, subcontractor) that supplies the workforce.
applicability: The assertion says IfcLaborResource depends_on IfcOrganization with condition 'when labor is supplied by a contracting company', but in IFC the relationship is through IfcRelAssignsToResource which uses IfcResourceObjectSelect. IfcOrganization is an option but not a mandatory dependency - IfcLaborResource can reference IfcPerson, IfcOrganization, or neither.
conditions: when labor is supplied by a contracting company

subject: IfcLaborResource
rationale: IfcLaborResource is a subtype of IfcConstructionResource, so it inherits its properties and depends on the general resource management framework.

subject: IfcLaborResource
rationale: Labor resources are assigned to tasks (IfcTask) to perform construction work. The labor resource directly supports the execution of construction tasks.

subject: IfcLaborResource
rationale: Labor resources are allocated within work plans for construction projects.

subject: IfcLaborResource
rationale: Labor resources have a base cost (hourly rate, etc.) associated with them, requiring cost value assignment for budget tracking.
conditions: when cost estimation is needed

subject: IfcLagTime
rationale: IfcLagTime represents a time delay/lag between tasks and is always associated with an IfcTask (or IfcTaskTime) in a work schedule context.
conditions: When used in a work schedule

subject: IfcLagTime
rationale: IfcLagTime defines the lag or delay between the predecessor and successor tasks, commonly stored in IfcTaskTime recurrence or related attributes.
conditions: When scheduling tasks

subject: IfcLagTime
rationale: Lag time is defined in the context of a sequence relationship (predecessor-successor) between tasks, formalized via IfcRelSequence.
conditions: When establishing task dependencies

subject: IfcLagTime
rationale: Lag time definitions support the creation of realistic work schedules by accounting for delays, curing times, or required gaps between activities.
conditions: In project planning and control

subject: IfcLagTime
rationale: IfcLagTime connects to tasks as part of the predecessor/successor relationship definition, specifying the offset between them.
conditions: Via sequence relationships

subject: IfcLaborResourceType
rationale: IfcLaborResourceType is the type definition that classifies and defines properties for labor resources. The actual labor resource instances (IfcLaborResource) depend on this type for their classification and property definitions.
conditions: When used as a type definition for labor resources

subject: IfcLaborResourceType
rationale: IfcLaborResourceType is a subtype of IfcConstructionResourceType, inheriting its properties and behaviors.

subject: IfcLaborResourceType
rationale: Labor resource types can have property sets assigned to define type-specific attributes such as skill levels, hourly rates, or union requirements.
applicability: All projects requiring specific labor type properties
conditions: When custom properties are assigned

subject: IfcLaborResourceType
rationale: Labor resource types can be associated with classification references to categorize the type of labor according to industry standards.
applicability: Projects using standardized work classifications (e.g., MasterFormat, Uniclass)
conditions: When the labor type is classified according to a standard classification system

subject: IfcLaborResourceType
rationale: IfcLaborResourceType defines the type of labor that can be assigned to perform construction tasks (IfcTaskType instances), supporting the execution of construction work.
applicability: The relationship between IfcLaborResourceType and IfcTaskType is indirect through IfcRelAssignsToProcess at the occurrence level (IfcLaborResource assigned to IfcTask). IfcLaborResourceType does not directly 'support' IfcTaskType in a semantic relationship in the IFC schema. The relationship exists at instance level, not type level.
conditions: When labor is assigned to perform specific construction tasks
exceptions: If the task does not require human labor (fully automated)

subject: IfcLaborResourceType
rationale: Certain labor types (e.g., carpenters, concrete workers, welders) depend on specific materials to perform their work. The type definition may relate to the materials they work with.
applicability: Construction trades working with specific materials
conditions: When labor type is specialized for specific material handling
exceptions: For non-material-specific labor (e.g., administration)

subject: IfcLaborResourceType
rationale: Many labor types (operators, riggers) depend on specific construction equipment to perform their function.
conditions: When labor type requires equipment to perform work (e.g., crane operator requires crane)
exceptions: Manual labor types that do not require equipment

subject: IfcLaborResourceType
rationale: Proper classification and selection of labor resource types contributes to project efficiency, cost control, and quality of construction.
conditions: When properly skilled labor is allocated to construction activities

subject: IfcLampType
rationale: Electrical cables are needed to connect the lamp to the power source.
conditions: for electrical wiring connection

subject: IfcLampType
rationale: Switches are commonly required to control lamp operation.
applicability: The existing exception mentions 'lamps with integrated sensors may not require separate switch,' but there are other exceptions: lamps controlled via a building automation system (e.g., DALI, BACnet) may use a control bus rather than a physical switching device, and emergency exit signage lamps often have no manual switch. The scope of exceptions is narrower than the full set.
conditions: if manual or automatic control of lamp is desired
exceptions: lamps with integrated sensors may not require separate switch

subject: IfcLampType
rationale: Lamp typically depends on a fixture for mechanical support and housing.
conditions: lamp must be housed in a compatible fixture
exceptions: some lamps are self-contained units

subject: IfcLampType
rationale: The lamp supports the lighting function of a space for occupant visibility and safety.
conditions: when lamp is installed in a room or space

subject: IfcLampType
rationale: IfcLampType defines the type properties for individual IfcLamp instances; it contains the shared definition.
conditions: as a type definition for individual lamp instances

subject: IfcLampType
rationale: IfcLampType is a component of the lighting system which supports building functionality.
conditions: lighting system within a building

subject: IfcLampType
rationale: In controlled environments, lamps depend on control elements like dimmers or occupancy sensors.
applicability: The assertion says 'if part of an automated lighting control system' but in IFC, IfcDistributionControlElement represents control devices like controllers, not sensors or actuators. A lamp may depend on IfcSensor or IfcActuator instead. Also, the applicability says 'smart buildings; commercial' but many residential lamps (e.g., smart bulbs) also involve control elements — excluding residential is overly narrow.
conditions: if part of an automated lighting control system
exceptions: simple standalone lamps do not require control elements

subject: IfcLampType
rationale: Cable trays or conduits may be required to route electrical cables to the lamp.
conditions: for cable management in exposed or concealed runs
exceptions: direct wiring may not require cable carriers

The existing exception says 'direct wiring may not require cable carriers,' but there is another key exception: cable carriers are typically used for power cabling, while data/control cabling (e.g., for smart lamps) may use separate pathways or raceways that are modeled as different entities (e.g., IfcCableSegment, IfcDuctSegment). The condition should further clarify the cable type.

subject: IfcLampType
rationale: Protective devices safeguard the lamp and circuit from overcurrent or short circuits.
conditions: circuit protection like fuses or circuit breakers in the lamp circuit
exceptions: IfcProtectiveDevice protects a circuit, not the lamp type itself. Low-voltage lamps (e.g., 24V LED strips) are often protected by the driver's internal protection or by a protective device at the transformer/driver, not directly attributed to the lamp type entity. Also, SELV (Safety Extra Low Voltage) circuits may not require overcurrent protection per electrical codes.

subject: IfcLamp
rationale: Recessed and surface-mounted lamps require a ceiling structure for support.
applicability: The assertion covers 'all buildings' but the concept of 'Ceiling' as a spatial element may be modeled differently across building information standards (e.g., IFC2x3 vs IFC4). In some models, ceilings are represented as coverings or slabs, and a direct 'depends_on' relationship may not be valid or semantically defined. The assertion may not apply to non-IFC-based building representations.
conditions: for ceiling-mounted or recessed lamps
exceptions: wall-mounted, pole-mounted, or freestanding lamps

Lamps integrated into a suspended ceiling grid (e.g., grid-mounted troffers) may not directly 'depend_on' the Ceiling as a structural element but rather on the suspension grid or the ceiling tile system. The semantic relationship may be to the grid or support system rather than the Ceiling element itself.

subject: IfcLibraryInformation
rationale: IfcLibraryInformation is associated with building elements through IfcRelAssociatesLibrary relationships; without this association the information is not usable.
applicability: The assertion omits that IfcRelAssociatesLibrary links from IfcLibraryInformation to products/objects, NOT the other direction. IfcLibraryInformation does not 'depend on' IfcRelAssociatesLibrary to exist; the relationship is optional and the direction of dependency is reversed from what is stated.
conditions: when library information needs to be linked to building elements or other objects

subject: IfcLibraryInformation
rationale: IfcLibraryInformation can contain or reference IfcLibraryReference objects that point to specific documents or URLs.
applicability: IfcLibraryReference is associated with IfcLibraryInformation via the 'LibraryReference' attribute (a SET of IfcLibraryReference), so 'contains' is directionally accurate. However, this relationship is optional and not all IfcLibraryInformation instances contain references. The condition should specify that this is an optional aggregation.
conditions: when multiple references are organized under a single library information entry

subject: IfcLibraryInformation
rationale: IfcLibraryInformation often works alongside IfcDocumentInformation to provide structured library/document metadata in building information models.
conditions: when library information acts as metadata for documents

subject: IfcLibraryInformation
