rationale: IfcLibraryInformation may reference an IfcActor as the publisher or creator of the library information.
conditions: when a publisher, author, or creator of the library is specified

subject: IfcLibraryInformation
rationale: IfcOrganization can be used within IfcLibraryInformation to specify the publishing organization.
conditions: when the library is published by an organization

subject: IfcLibraryInformation
rationale: IfcLibraryInformation enriches the overall IfcProject by providing structured library and classification references.
conditions: when library data is used to enrich project documentation and classification

subject: IfcLibraryInformation
rationale: IfcLibraryInformation may reference classification systems but does not directly contain IfcClassification objects in the model hierarchy.
conditions: when library information includes classification references or notations

subject: IfcLibraryInformation
rationale: IfcLibraryInformation is a subtype of IfcRoot, so its identity and basic attributes depend on this parent class.
applicability: IfcLibraryInformation is indeed a subtype of IfcRoot, but stating it 'depends_on' IfcRoot is misleading. All IFC entities that are subtypes of IfcRoot inherit from it; this is a subtype/supertype relationship, not a dependency. The term 'depends_on' incorrectly characterizes an inheritance hierarchy as a functional dependency.
conditions: as a subtype of IfcRoot, it inherits core attributes like GlobalId, Name, and Description

subject: IfcLibraryReference
rationale: IfcLibraryReference is a reference to an external library, and IfcLibraryInformation provides the metadata about that library source.
applicability: The assertion states IfcLibraryReference depends_on IfcLibraryInformation, but in the IFC schema IfcLibraryReference has a RequiredReference relationship to IfcLibraryInformation, not a dependency in the sense that it cannot exist without it. IfcLibraryReference instances can exist without being associated with IfcLibraryInformation (e.g., a simple external document link). The condition 'when the library reference needs to be associated with a specific library' makes this conditional, but the assertion 'depends_on' is too strong for cases where no library information context is needed.
conditions: when the library reference needs to be associated with a specific library

subject: IfcLibraryReference
rationale: IfcLibraryReference is associated with building objects through IfcRelAssociatesLibrary relationships.
applicability: The assertion states IfcLibraryReference depends_on IfcRelAssociatesLibrary, but in IFC, IfcRelAssociatesLibrary is an association relationship that links library information to objects. IfcLibraryReference itself does not depend on this relationship to exist. The relationship uses IfcLibraryReference, not the other way around. The reference can exist without being associated to any building element via IfcRelAssociatesLibrary.
conditions: when linking the library reference to building elements

subject: IfcLibraryReference
rationale: IfcLibraryReference can support linking to document-based libraries that may be represented by IfcDocumentInformation.
conditions: when the library reference points to a structured document library

subject: IfcLibraryReference
rationale: IfcLibraryReference can support building elements by linking them to external library definitions, catalogs, or specification documents.
applicability: The assertion states IfcLibraryReference supports IfcBuildingElement, but in IFC, IfcLibraryReference is linked to elements via IfcRelAssociatesLibrary, not directly. conditions: manual or automatic control of light fixture is needed

The assertion that IfcLightFixtureType depends_on IfcSwitchingDevice does not account for dimmer-controlled fixtures on protocols like DALI or PoE (Power over Ethernet) where the switching/logic is handled by a control module or gateway rather than a separate IfcSwitchingDevice element. Also, smart/connected lighting systems may use occupancy sensors or building management system logic that does not map to an explicit switching device element.

subject: IfcLightFixtureType

applicability: The assertion says IfcLightFixtureType requires IfcSpace and lists outdoor fixtures as an exception. However, fixtures in semi-enclosed spaces (e.g., covered walkways, atriums, canopies, parking garages) may be associated with IfcSpace, IfcExternalSpace, or neither depending on modeling convention. Additionally, fixtures in interstitial spaces (plenums, service shafts) may not have a dedicated IfcSpace. This creates ambiguity beyond just the indoor/outdoor distinction.

subject: IfcLine
rationale: In topological representations, a line segment (edge) connects vertices. IfcLine can serve as the underlying geometry for an edge that conceptually 'contains' or connects the bounding vertices.
applicability: Building geometry representations, structural wireframe models

IfcLine does not 'contain' IfcVertex in the IFC schema. IfcVertex is part of the topology model (IfcTopologicalRepresentationItem) while IfcLine is a geometric curve (IfcGeometricRepresentationItem). They exist in separate representation layers. The edge geometry may reference an IfcLine via IfcEdgeCurve, but IfcLine does not 'contain' IfcVertex. The relationship is indirect through IfcEdge/IfcEdgeCurve, not direct containment.
conditions: When representing edges in a topological model
exceptions: IfcLine used purely as an abstract geometric curve

rationale: IfcLine is frequently used as the geometric representation of an IfcEdge in IFC models, connecting two vertices that define a topologically constrained line.
conditions: When IfcLine is used as the edge geometry in a topological model

applicability: All polyline representations in IFC models
conditions: When a polyline is composed of multiple IfcLine segments

subject: IfcLine

applicability: Modeled architectural edges, structural member axes

IfcTrimmedCurve can use an IfcLine as its BasisCurve, but this is not limited to 'modeled architectural edges, structural member axes'. IfcTrimmedCurve with an IfcLine basis is widely used across all domains (architectural, structural, MEP, etc.) and the applicability is overly restrictive.
conditions: When a basis curve is an IfcLine that gets trimmed

subject: IfcLine
rationale: IfcLine inherits from IfcRepresentationItem and requires the context of a geometric representation (IfcRepresentation) to be meaningfully placed in a model.
applicability: IfcLine inherits from IfcCurve -> IfcGeometricRepresentationItem -> IfcRepresentationItem. It does not 'require' IfcRepresentationItem as a separate entity — it 'is_a' IfcRepresentationItem. The dependency phrasing is misleading: IfcLine is a subtype of IfcRepresentationItem, not something that requires it as a separate dependency.

subject: IfcMapConversion
rationale: IfcMapConversion requires an IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem to define the target coordinate system for the conversion operation.

conditions: When map conversion is applied to transform local engineering coordinates to a projected coordinate system

applicability: Projects using projected coordinate systems (e.g., UTM, State Plane)

subject: IfcMapConversion
rationale: IfcMapConversion is typically associated with an IfcSite to position it in global coordinates.
applicability: All projects requiring georeferencing of the building site
conditions: When the map conversion is applied to the site location for georeferencing
exceptions: IfcMapConversion does not inherently depend on IfcSite. In IFC, IfcSite contains the 'RefLatitude', 'RefLongitude', and 'RefElevation' attributes for georeferencing, and IfcMapConversion is assigned to IfcSite via IfcRelAssociates or similar. However, IfcMapConversion can also be associated directly with IfcGeometricRepresentationContext (via 'WorldCoordinateSystem' attribute in IfcProject). The assertion that IfcMapConversion 'depends_on' IfcSite fails when the map conversion is defined on the representation context of the project rather than on a specific site, such as in infrastructure projects with linear referencing where no IfcSite is present.

subject: IfcMapConversion

applicability: All IFC models using geographic coordinate systems
conditions: When the representation context's coordinate system is transformed via the map conversion

subject: IfcMapConversion
rationale: IfcMapConversion is a subtype of IfcCoordinateOperation, connecting local engineering CRS to a map CRS.
applicability: Complex georeferencing workflows involving multiple coordinate transformations

In IFC, IfcMapConversion is a subtype of IfcCoordinateOperation, so the 'connects_to IfcCoordinateOperation' is trivially true via inheritance, not by reference/association. The assertion would be meaningful only if it referred to IfcMapConversion being connected to OTHER coordinate operations (e.g., IfcCoordinateTransformation or another IfcMapConversion) in a chain. But IfcMapConversion does not have an attribute to reference another IfcCoordinateOperation—it has SrcCRS (inherited from IfcCoordinateOperation) and TargetCRS, neither of which points to another operation. True chaining of coordinate operations in IFC would require IfcCoordinateReferenceSystemSelect or similar mechanisms, not direct operation-to-operation links.
conditions: When the map conversion is part of a coordinate operation chain

subject: IfcMaterialClassificationRelationship
rationale: IfcMaterialClassificationRelationship associates an external classification reference with one or more IfcMaterialDefinition entities. It depends on material definitions to exist.
conditions: when establishing classification relationships between materials
exceptions: The IfcMaterialClassificationRelationship does not always depend on IfcMaterialDefinition. In IFC4 and later, this relationship actually depends on IfcMaterialDefinition's subtypes (IfcMaterial, IfcMaterialLayer, IfcMaterialLayerSet, IfcMaterialProfile, IfcMaterialConstituent) individually, not on the abstract superclass directly in all implementations/usage contexts. Some relationships may skip the abstract class and point directly to subtypes.

subject: IfcMaterialClassificationRelationship
rationale: The relationship connects a material definition to a classification reference from an external classification system (e.g., Uniclass, MasterFormat).
conditions: when linking materials to classification systems

subject: IfcMaterialClassificationRelationship
rationale: IfcClassificationReference typically points to an IfcClassification which defines the classification system itself.
conditions: when the classification reference belongs to a classification system

subject: IfcMaterialClassificationRelationship
rationale: IfcMaterial is one common subtype of IfcMaterialDefinition that can be classified via this relationship.
conditions: when the material definition is an IfcMaterial

subject: IfcMaterialClassificationRelationship
rationale: IfcMaterialLayer is a subtype of IfcMaterialDefinition and can be associated with a classification.
conditions: when the material definition is an IfcMaterialLayer

subject: IfcMaterialClassificationRelationship
rationale: IfcMaterialLayerSet is a subtype of IfcMaterialDefinition that can be classified.
conditions: when the material definition is an IfcMaterialLayerSet

subject: IfcMaterialClassificationRelationship
rationale: IfcMaterialProfile is a subtype of IfcMaterialDefinition used for profile-based material definitions.
conditions: when the material definition is an IfcMaterialProfile

subject: IfcMaterialClassificationRelationship
rationale: IfcMaterialConstituent is a subtype of IfcMaterialDefinition that can be classified.
conditions: when the material definition is an IfcMaterialConstituent

subject: IfcMaterialClassificationRelationship
rationale: IfcMaterialClassificationRelationship is the material-specific version of classification association, supporting the broader classification modeling pattern defined by IfcRelAssociatesClassification.
conditions: at a higher abstraction level for associating classification to objects

subject: IfcMaterialConstituent
rationale: IfcMaterialConstituent is a subtype of IfcMaterialDefinition, so it inherits and depends on that base class for its core definition and properties.
conditions: IfcMaterialConstituent is a subtype of IfcMaterialDefinition

subject: IfcMaterialConstituent
rationale: Each IfcMaterialConstituent is part of an IfcMaterialConstituentSet which groups material constituents for an element.
conditions: IfcMaterialConstituent must be assigned to an IfcMaterialConstituentSet

subject: IfcMaterialConstituent
rationale: IfcMaterialConstituent requires a reference to an IfcMaterial to define what the constituent is made of.
conditions: Each constituent must reference a specific IfcMaterial

subject: IfcMaterialConstituent
rationale: In many cases IfcMaterialConstituent relates to IfcMaterialLayer for multi-layer building elements.
conditions: When used in layered constructions
exceptions: Not required if constituent is used in non-layered contexts

subject: IfcMaterialConstituent
rationale: The relationship linking material constituents to building elements uses IfcRelAssociatesMaterial.
applicability: The assertion states IfcMaterialConstituent depends_on IfcRelAssociatesMaterial. In IFC4, IfcRelAssociatesMaterial associates an IfcMaterialDefinition (or subtype) to an element. IfcMaterialConstituent (as a subtype of IfcMaterialDefinition) can be the target of IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, but it does not 'depend on' it - the relationship goes both ways or is mediated by the association. The constituent can exist without being associated to an element.
conditions: For associating material constituents to building elements

subject: IfcMaterialConstituent
rationale: IfcMaterialConstituent supports building elements by defining their material composition (e.g., a window's frame material, a wall's finish material).
conditions: When IfcMaterialConstituent defines the material breakdown of a building element

subject: IfcMaterialConstituent
rationale: IfcMaterialConstituent helps describe the material breakdown of element components like door panels, window frames, etc.
conditions: When the element has identifiable material constituents

subject: IfcMaterialConstituent
rationale: IfcMaterialConstituent can have associated property sets that define its material properties, though this relationship is indirect.
conditions: When material properties are defined for the constituent

subject: IfcMaterialConstituent
rationale: IfcMaterialConstituent can supplement material profile sets by defining material constituents within a profile.
conditions: When used in conjunction with profiled elements like beams or columns
exceptions: Not applicable for non-profiled elements

subject: IfcMaterialConstituentSet
rationale: IfcMaterialConstituentSet is a container that holds a set of IfcMaterialConstituent entities, each defining a material constituent for a specific part or layer of an element.

subject: IfcMaterialConstituentSet
rationale: IfcMaterialConstituentSet depends on the material definitions (IfcMaterial) assigned to its constituent members to specify actual materials.
conditions: When used to define material composition of an element

subject: IfcMaterialConstituentSet
rationale: IfcMaterialConstituentSet is typically associated with an IfcElement (e.g., wall, slab, beam) via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial to define its material composition by constituents.
conditions: When assigned through IfcRelAssociatesMaterial

subject: IfcMaterialConstituentSet
rationale: Each IfcMaterialConstituent within the set requires a reference to an IfcMaterial entity to define the actual material properties.
conditions: For each constituent in the set to define a specific material

subject: IfcMaterialConstituentSet
rationale: IfcRelAssociatesMaterial is the relationship entity used to assign IfcMaterialConstituentSet to building elements.
conditions: When establishing the relationship between element and material set

subject: IfcMaterialDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinition depends on IfcRelAssociatesMaterial to be linked to building elements it defines the material for.
conditions: when material definitions need to be associated with elements

subject: IfcMaterialDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinition is an abstract supertype that contains IfcMaterial as a concrete subtype representing specific materials.

subject: IfcMaterialDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinition is an abstract supertype that contains IfcMaterialLayer as a concrete subtype.

subject: IfcMaterialDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinition is an abstract supertype that contains IfcMaterialLayerSet as a concrete subtype.

subject: IfcMaterialDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinition is an abstract supertype that contains IfcMaterialProfile as a concrete subtype.

subject: IfcMaterialDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinition is an abstract supertype that contains IfcMaterialProfileSet as a concrete subtype.

subject: IfcMaterialDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinition is an abstract supertype that contains IfcMaterialConstituent as a concrete subtype.

subject: IfcMaterialDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinition is an abstract supertype that contains IfcMaterialConstituentSet as a concrete subtype.

subject: IfcMaterialDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinition supports the relationship entity IfcRelAssociatesMaterial by serving as the material end of the association.
conditions: when linking materials to building elements

subject: IfcMaterialDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinition can have property sets assigned to define material properties.
conditions: when material properties need to be defined

subject: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation is a subtype of IfcMaterialDefinition and inherits its representation capabilities. It depends on the base material definition entity to define material properties that need representation.
applicability: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation inherits from IfcRepresentation and relates to IfcMaterialDefinition via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, but the IFC schema does not define a direct 'depends_on' relationship from IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation to IfcMaterialDefinition. The representation can exist independently of a material definition association.
conditions: When representing material properties

subject: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation uses IfcRepresentation entities (often IfcStyledRepresentation) to graphically depict material definitions.
applicability: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation is itself a subtype of IfcRepresentation, so saying it 'depends_on' IfcRepresentation is trivially true via inheritance but misleading as a dependency statement. The condition 'for visual or geometric representation of material properties' is actually its entire purpose, not a specific condition.
conditions: For visual or geometric representation of material properties

subject: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation often represents IfcMaterialLayerSet definitions to visualize material layering in building elements.
applicability: structural building elements with layered construction
conditions: When representing layered building constructions (walls, floors, roofs)

subject: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation
rationale: The representation of material profiles depends on IfcMaterialProfileSet for elements with cross-section profiles.
conditions: When representing profile-based elements like beams or columns

subject: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation
rationale: For composite elements made of multiple distinct materials, IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation depends on IfcMaterialConstituentSet definitions.
conditions: When representing composite materials with distinct constituents

subject: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation provides the visual representation support for IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage which defines how layer sets are used by specific elements.
applicability: building elements with layered material definitions
conditions: When material layer sets need to be referenced and visualized in element definitions

subject: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation
rationale: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation typically uses IfcStyledRepresentation to assign visual styles to material definitions for display purposes.
conditions: When visual styling (colors, textures, hatch patterns) is needed for material definitions

subject: IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation
rationale: Material representations are often associated with IfcProduct subtypes (walls, slabs, etc.) which provide the spatial context for the material representation.
applicability: All building types with physical elements
conditions: When material representations need to be spatially located or associated with physical elements

subject: IfcMaterialLayer
rationale: IfcMaterialLayer must be part of an IfcMaterialLayerSet to be functionally assigned to an element
conditions: when defining multilayered material compositions

subject: IfcMaterialLayer
rationale: The layer's material definition relies on an IfcMaterial entity
conditions: each layer references a single IfcMaterial
exceptions: Assertion says each layer references a single IfcMaterial, but in IFC schema the Material attribute of IfcMaterialLayer is OPTIONAL (0..1). A layer may have no material assignment (e.g., an air gap layer).

subject: IfcMaterialLayer
rationale: IfcMaterialLayer contains/aggregates a reference to a specific IfcMaterial

subject: IfcMaterialLayer
rationale: IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage defines how the layer set is positioned relative to the element reference axis
conditions: when the layer set is applied to an element with directional layering
exceptions: IfcMaterialLayer does not require IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage. IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage is associated with IfcMaterialLayerSet (not individual layers) to define layering direction. A single IfcMaterialLayer can exist without any IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage reference.

subject: IfcMaterialLayer
rationale: Material layers form the structural/functional composition of a wall assembly
applicability: Assertion uses 'supports' which is ambiguous. IfcMaterialLayer does not directly 'support' IfcWall; rather, IfcWall has a material association that may reference an IfcMaterialLayerSet which contains IfcMaterialLayers. The relationship is indirect through IfcMaterialLayerSet and material associations.
conditions: when used as part of a wall's material layer set

subject: IfcMaterialLayer
rationale: Material layers define the composition of slab constructions
applicability: Same issue as 18b906bd: 'supports' is ambiguous. IfcMaterialLayer does not directly 'support' IfcSlab; the relationship is indirect via IfcMaterialLayerSet and material association relationships.
conditions: when used as part of a slab's material layer set

subject: IfcMaterialLayer
rationale: Individual layers are aggregated into a layer set which is then associated with the element
conditions: for proper assignment to building elements

subject: IfcMaterialLayerSet
rationale: IfcMaterialLayerSet is defined as an ordered collection of IfcMaterialLayer instances. Without at least one IfcMaterialLayer, the set has no meaning.
conditions: When defining ordered sets of material layers

subject: IfcMaterialLayerSet
rationale: The set aggregates multiple IfcMaterialLayer objects that together define a layered material structure.
exceptions: An empty set is allowed in schema but has no practical use

subject: IfcMaterialLayerSet
rationale: Each IfcMaterialLayer in the set references an IfcMaterial for its constituent material.
conditions: Indirectly via IfcMaterialLayer, which references IfcMaterial

subject: IfcMaterialLayerSet
rationale: IfcMaterialLayerSet is referenced by IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage to define how the layer set is applied (e.g., offset direction, extruded direction) to an element.
conditions: When a material layer set is assigned to a building element via IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage

subject: IfcMaterialLayerSet
rationale: IfcMaterialLayerSet can be part of IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation to associate presentation info with layers.
conditions: When used in material definition representations for styled items

subject: IfcMaterialLayerSet
rationale: The relationship entity IfcRelAssociatesMaterial connects IfcMaterialLayerSet to building elements like IfcWall.
conditions: When the layer set needs to be associated to building elements

subject: IfcMaterialLayerSet
rationale: In some advanced composite constructions, a layer set may be combined with profile sets, though this is not a direct schema relationship.
conditions: When defining composite material stacks that include both layered and profiled materials

subject: IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage
rationale: IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage describes how an IfcMaterialLayerSet is positioned relative to a building element's reference axis or plane. It depends on an IfcMaterialLayerSet to define the actual material layers.
applicability: All building elements using layered materials
conditions: Must be assigned to an IfcMaterialLayerSet

subject: IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage
rationale: IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage inherits from IfcMaterialUsageDefinition, which defines the abstract concept of material usage.
conditions: Inheritance relationship - IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage is a subtype of IfcMaterialUsageDefinition

subject: IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage
rationale: The IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage requires underlying IfcMaterialLayers (defined in the referenced IfcMaterialLayerSet) to define the individual material layers that make up the layered element.
conditions: Referenced through IfcMaterialLayerSet

subject: IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage
rationale: IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage provides the layer direction, offset, and reference information needed to correctly position materials within building elements.
applicability: IfcWall, IfcSlab, IfcRoof, IfcPlate, IfcColumn (layered elements)
conditions: When the element has material layer set usage assigned via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial

subject: IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage
rationale: IfcRelAssociatesMaterial is the relationship entity that connects IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage to the building element it describes.
applicability: All elements using material layer sets
conditions: Via the N° relation that associates material definitions to elements

subject: IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage
rationale: IfcWallStandardCase specifically requires IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage to define its material layers, thickness, and positioning.
conditions: When IfcWallStandardCase uses layered material definition
exceptions: Non-layered walls

subject: IfcMaterialLayerWithOffsets
rationale: IfcMaterialLayerWithOffsets is a subtype of IfcMaterialLayer that adds offset information to the material layer definition.
conditions: when defining layered material compositions with offset properties

subject: IfcMaterialLayerWithOffsets
rationale: IfcMaterialLayerWithOffsets is typically aggregated within an IfcMaterialLayerSet to define the complete layered construction.
conditions: when used as part of a layered material set

subject: IfcMaterialLayerWithOffsets
rationale: Offset information may be represented via material definition representations for visualization.
conditions: when offsets need to be visualized or styled in a model
exceptions: not required for analytical or property-only usage

subject: IfcMaterialLayerWithOffsets
rationale: The material layer with offsets is connected to building elements through material association relationships.
conditions: when the material layer set with offsets is assigned to an element

subject: IfcMaterialList
rationale: IfcMaterialList is an IFC entity that contains a list of IfcMaterial entities, as defined in the IFC schema.

subject: IfcMaterialList
rationale: IfcMaterialList is typically referenced through IfcRelAssociatesMaterial to associate material information with building elements.
conditions: When material information needs to be associated with building elements

subject: IfcMaterialList
rationale: IfcMaterialList can support material definitions that are used in material definition representations.
conditions: When materials need to be visually represented

subject: IfcMaterialList
rationale: IfcMaterialList is fundamentally a container for IfcMaterial entities; to function as a material list it requires IfcMaterial entries.
conditions: When the list is non-empty
exceptions: An empty IfcMaterialList is allowed

The existing exception says 'An empty IfcMaterialList is allowed', but per the IFC schema (IFC2x3 and IFC4), IfcMaterialList.Materials is defined as LIST [1:?] OF IfcMaterial — meaning at least one item is required. An empty list (zero elements) is not schema-valid. The 'existing exceptions' field contains information that contradicts the IFC schema.

subject: IfcMaterialProfile
rationale: IfcMaterialProfile is used within IfcMaterialProfileSet to assign material properties to a specific profile definition.
conditions: When defining material properties for profile-based elements

subject: IfcMaterialProfile
rationale: IfcMaterialProfile references an IfcProfileDef to define the cross-section shape to which the material applies.
conditions: Must be associated with a valid profile definition

subject: IfcMaterialProfile
rationale: IfcMaterialProfile associates a material with a specific profile, so IfcMaterial is the core material definition it depends on.
conditions: Must have a material assigned

subject: IfcMaterialProfile
rationale: IfcMaterialProfile can reference material properties to define mechanical, thermal or other characteristics of the material in the profile context.
conditions: When additional material properties need to be defined

subject: IfcMaterialProfile
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage uses the material profile set (which includes IfcMaterialProfile) to assign material/profile combinations to a shaping element like a beam or column.
conditions: When the profile set is used in an element occurrence

subject: IfcMaterialProfile
rationale: The material-profile combination defined by IfcMaterialProfile is essential for structural members such as beams and columns to have correct structural properties.
conditions: For structural analysis of profile-based elements

subject: IfcMaterialProfile
rationale: Beams often need profile-specific material properties defined via IfcMaterialProfile.
conditions: When beams require profile-specific material assignments
exceptions: If the beam uses a non-profile-based material definition

subject: IfcMaterialProfile
rationale: Columns commonly rely on profile-specific material definitions for structural calculations.
conditions: When columns require profile-specific material assignments
exceptions: If the column uses a non-profile-based material definition

subject: IfcMaterialProfile
rationale: IfcMember entities such as bracing or struts benefit from profile-specific material assignments.
conditions: When structural members use profile-based material definitions

subject: IfcMaterialProfile
rationale: IfcMaterialProfile contains a reference to an IfcMaterial as the material that applies to the profile.
conditions: When the material is assigned to the profile

subject: IfcMaterialProfile
rationale: IfcMaterialProfile contains a reference to an IfcProfileDef that defines the shape/profile of the material cross-section.
conditions: When the profile geometry is defined

subject: IfcMaterialProfile
rationale: The relationship from elements to material profiles is established through IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, connecting IfcMaterialProfileSet to elements.
conditions: When linking the material profile to building elements

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSet
rationale: An IfcMaterialProfileSet aggregates one or more IfcMaterialProfile instances that define the cross-section layers of a material.
applicability: IfcMaterialProfileSet is used to aggregate material profiles
conditions: when defining a set of material profiles for layered elements

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSet
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSet references IfcMaterial to define the physical material of each profile layer.
applicability: all cases where material properties are defined
conditions: when specific material composition is needed

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSet
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage associates the profile set with a specific element's usage context (e.g., cardinal point, orientation).
conditions: when the profile set is applied to an element like IfcBeam or IfcColumn

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSet
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSet provides the material layer profile information used by IfcBeam.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcMaterialProfileSet supports IfcBeam' is too broad. IfcMaterialProfileSet does not directly support IfcBeam; instead, IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage (or IfcRelAssociatesMaterial) is used to assign the profile set to the beam element. The relationship is indirect through an association entity.
conditions: when defining the cross-section material layers of a beam

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSet
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSet provides the material layer profile information used by IfcColumn.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcMaterialProfileSet supports IfcColumn' is too broad. IfcMaterialProfileSet does not directly support IfcColumn; the assignment happens through IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage or IfcRelAssociatesMaterial. The direct relationship is missing.
conditions: when defining the cross-section material layers of a column

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSet
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSet provides the material layer profile information used by IfcMember.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcMaterialProfileSet supports IfcMember' is too broad. IfcMaterialProfileSet does not directly support IfcMember; the assignment happens through IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage or IfcRelAssociatesMaterial. The direct relationship is missing.
conditions: when defining the cross-section material layers of a member

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSet
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSet is a container that aggregates multiple IfcMaterialProfile entities (HasProperties relationship).
applicability: all cases where IfcMaterialProfileSet is used

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSet
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSet is conceptually related to IfcMaterialLayerSet as both define material cross-sections but for profile vs. layered elements respectively.
applicability: alternative material definitions for different IFC elements

The assertion says IfcMaterialProfileSet 'connects_to' IfcMaterialLayerSet, but as the existing exception itself notes, they are not directly connected in the IFC schema. This relationship is conceptual rather than a direct schema-level connection, which could mislead users into thinking there is a direct association.
conditions: when mapping between profile-based and layer-based material definitions is needed
exceptions: not directly connected in IFC schema, but are alternatives for different element types

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSet
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSet contributes to the material definition representation by providing profile curves and material assignments.
conditions: when visual representation of the material profile is needed

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage references an IfcMaterialProfileSet to define the material and cross-section profile for a specific usage of a material in a structural element.
applicability: While IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage does reference IfcMaterialProfileSet via the ForProfileSet attribute, the nature of this relationship is a direct association (reference), not a 'depends_on' in a lifecycle or dependency sense. IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage can exist in the model without an IfcMaterialProfileSet being present (though it would be semantically incomplete), so this is more accurately described as an optional reference rather than a hard dependency.

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage is typically associated with products via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial relationship.

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage defines the profile and material assignment for structural elements like beams and columns.
conditions: When assigned to beam, column, or other structural members

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage
rationale: IfcMember elements commonly use IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage to describe their cross-section and material composition.
conditions: When used to define material profile for a member element

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage
rationale: IfcBeam uses IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage to define its material and profile properties.
conditions: When assigned as material profile definition for beams

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage
rationale: IfcColumn uses IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage to define its material and profile properties.
conditions: When assigned as material profile definition for columns

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage provides contextual usage information for one or more IfcMaterialProfile instances within the referenced IfcMaterialProfileSet.

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage may reference a material definition representation for visualization purposes.
conditions: When visual representation of the material profile is needed

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsageTapering
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsageTapering is a subtype that depends on IfcMaterialProfileSet to define the starting and ending profile definitions for tapering.
applicability: The condition 'when defining tapered material profiles along a member' is redundant with the entity's purpose. The dependency on IfcMaterialProfileSet is structural (the tapering usage references two IfcMaterialProfileSets via the base type), not just a usage condition. The condition should be more precise: the dependency exists because the Tapering entity references 'ForProfileSet' and 'ForProfileEndSet' which are both IfcMaterialProfileSet instances.
conditions: when defining tapered material profiles along a member

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsageTapering
rationale: It extends IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage which provides the base material profile assignment mechanism.
conditions: as base type for tapered usage definition

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsageTapering
rationale: The material profile set usage must be associated to an element via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial to take effect.
conditions: when associating the material profile set usage to a building element

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsageTapering
rationale: Tapering requires both a start profile and an end profile definition within the material profile set.
conditions: at least two profiles needed: start and end profiles for tapering

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsageTapering
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsageTapering contains usage of material profile sets for tapering definitions.

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsageTapering
rationale: This entity supports the definition of tapered structural members where cross-section changes along the length.
conditions: when member has varying cross-section along its length

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsageTapering
rationale: Tapered beams commonly use this concept to define changing profile sections.
conditions: when beam has varying depth or width along span

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsageTapering
rationale: Tapered columns in architectural design can be represented using this tapering definition.
conditions: when column tapers from base to top

subject: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsageTapering
rationale: The tapering material definition may connect to representation for visualization purposes.
applicability: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsageTapering does not have a direct 'connects_to' relationship with IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation in the IFC schema. IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation is typically associated with IfcMaterial (the material definition) rather than the profile usage. The visualization connection would be through IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage being assigned to an element via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, and then the material representation being associated with that element. This indirect relationship is not accurately captured as a direct connection.
conditions: when visualized in BIM models

subject: IfcMaterialProfileWithOffsets
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileWithOffsets is a subtype of IfcMaterialDefinition.
conditions: when inheriting base material definition properties

subject: IfcMaterialProfileWithOffsets
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileWithOffsets extends IfcMaterialProfile by adding offset attributes.
conditions: when extending with offset attributes

subject: IfcMaterialProfileWithOffsets
rationale: The profile must reference a specific IfcMaterial.
conditions: when specifying the material of the profile

subject: IfcMaterialProfileWithOffsets
rationale: Each material profile references an IfcProfileDef for cross-section shape.
conditions: when defining the cross-section shape

subject: IfcMaterialProfileWithOffsets
rationale: Material profiles with offsets define individual layers within layered material sets.
applicability: multi-layer wall, slab, or roof assemblies
conditions: when used in layered material set definitions

subject: IfcMaterialProfileWithOffsets
rationale: Offset values help position layers correctly within a material layer set.
applicability: layered building elements like walls, floors, roofs
conditions: when profile offsets define layer positioning

subject: IfcMaterialProfileWithOffsets
rationale: The material profile is associated to building elements through IfcRelAssociatesMaterial.
conditions: when the material profile is assigned to an element

subject: IfcMaterialProfileWithOffsets
rationale: Can define material constituents with specific profile and offset information.
conditions: when defining material constituents with profile offsets

subject: IfcMaterialProperties
rationale: IfcMaterialProperties is a subtype of IfcPropertyDefinition in the IFC schema, so it inherently depends on the parent class structure to function within the IFC data model.
conditions: when used to define material properties in IFC data models

subject: IfcMaterialProperties
rationale: IfcMaterialProperties defines properties for a specific IfcMaterial, so it depends on the IfcMaterial entity to which its property set is assigned.
conditions: when associated with a specific material in building models

subject: IfcMaterialProperties
rationale: IfcMaterialProperties often aggregates property sets (IfcPropertySet) that group individual properties together for a material.
conditions: when the material properties are organized within a named property set

subject: IfcMaterialProperties
rationale: IfcMaterialProperties consists of or references individual IfcProperty entities (e.g., IfcPropertySingleValue) to store actual property values.
conditions: when individual property values (e.g., density, thermal conductivity) are defined

subject: IfcMaterialProperties
rationale: IfcMaterialProperties provides descriptive property data that supports the definition and understanding of IfcMaterialDefinition entities.
applicability: IfcMaterialProperties 'supports' IfcMaterialDefinition is technically correct only if considering that IfcMaterial is a subtype of IfcMaterialDefinition. However, the assertion is true only when IfcMaterialProperties is assigned to an IfcMaterial (the most common case) and not necessarily for other subtypes of IfcMaterialDefinition (e.g., IfcMaterialLayerSet, IfcMaterialProfileSet) which have their own property mechanisms.
conditions: when used to enrich material definitions with property data

subject: IfcMaterialProperties
rationale: Material properties for each layer (e.g., thermal resistance) support the definition of multilayer constructions via IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage.
conditions: when specifying layer-specific material properties in composite constructions

subject: IfcMaterialProperties
rationale: To associate material properties with building elements, the IfcRelAssociatesMaterial relationship entity is required to establish the link between elements and materials.
conditions: when material properties need to be linked to building elements

subject: IfcMaterialProperties
rationale: IfcMaterialProperties can be used alongside IfcElementQuantity to provide both properties and quantities for materials used in building elements.
conditions: when quantities and properties are defined together for a material

subject: IfcMaterialUsageDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialUsageDefinition is an abstract supertype; IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage is its primary concrete subtype that defines material layer assignments to elements.
applicability: IfcMaterialUsageDefinition is an abstract supertype, not a concrete entity that 'depends_on' IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage. The direction is inverse: IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage is a subtype of IfcMaterialUsageDefinition, meaning IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage inherits from IfcMaterialUsageDefinition, not the other way around. The assertion suggests a dependency relationship that is structurally reversed relative to the IFC inheritance hierarchy.
conditions: When defining how materials are used in building elements

subject: IfcMaterialUsageDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage is another concrete subtype of IfcMaterialUsageDefinition for profile-based material definitions.
applicability: IfcMaterialUsageDefinition is an abstract supertype, not a concrete entity that 'depends_on' IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage. The direction is inverse: IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage is a subtype of IfcMaterialUsageDefinition, meaning the profile set usage inherits from the usage definition, not the reverse. The dependency arrow points the wrong way.
conditions: When defining how profiles of materials are used in elements like beams or columns

subject: IfcMaterialUsageDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialList is a simpler subtype of IfcMaterialUsageDefinition used for unordered material lists.
conditions: When defining a simple list of materials

subject: IfcMaterialUsageDefinition
rationale: IfcMaterialConstituentSet is a subtype of IfcMaterialUsageDefinition for constituent-based material definitions.
applicability: IfcMaterialUsageDefinition is an abstract supertype, not a concrete entity that 'depends_on' IfcMaterialConstituentSet. subject: IfcMeasureWithUnit
rationale: IfcMeasureWithUnit is defined in the IFC schema as a wrapper that pairs a numeric value (IfcValue) with a unit. It depends on the unit definition system which is typically managed through IfcUnitAssignment or directly referenced units.

subject: IfcMeasureWithUnit
rationale: IfcMeasureWithUnit often references IfcSIUnit as its unit definition for standardized metric measurements.
applicability: IfcMeasureWithUnit's Unit attribute can be of type IfcSIUnit, IfcConversionBasedUnit, or IfcDerivedUnit (via the IfcUnit select type). The assertion correctly identifies IfcSIUnit as one possible dependency, but states it as a dependency when using SI units - in fact IfcMeasureWithUnit can use IfcSIUnit directly as its Unit attribute, but also the relationship is through inheritance of being one of the IfcUnit select options, not a 'depends_on' in a strict schema dependency sense.
conditions: When using SI (International System of Units) measurements

subject: IfcMeasureWithUnit
rationale: IfcMeasureWithUnit can reference IfcConversionBasedUnit for units defined relative to SI units.
applicability: IFC models using imperial or other non-SI units

IfcMeasureWithUnit can also use IfcDerivedUnit (e.g., m/s for velocity) as its Unit attribute via the IfcUnit select type, which is neither IfcSIUnit nor IfcConversionBasedUnit. The assertion omits the IfcDerivedUnit case and overstates exclusivity of IfcConversionBasedUnit for non-SI units.
conditions: When using non-SI units that need conversion to SI

subject: IfcMeasureWithUnit
rationale: IfcMeasureWithUnit provides the structured measurement that populates quantity sets with unit-aware values.
applicability: Quantity takeoff and cost estimation in BIM
conditions: When quantities need to be expressed with explicit units

subject: IfcMeasureWithUnit
rationale: IfcPropertySingleValue uses IfcMeasureWithUnit (through IfcValue) to define single-valued properties with associated units.
conditions: When a property has a single numerical value with a unit

subject: IfcMeasureWithUnit
rationale: IfcMeasureWithUnit provides the unit-aware measurement foundation for physical quantities like length, area, volume, etc.
applicability: All physical quantity definitions in IFC
conditions: When physical measurements need unit definitions

subject: IfcMeasureWithUnit
rationale: Material properties often require measurements with units (e.g., W/mK for thermal conductivity), which are defined using IfcMeasureWithUnit.
conditions: When material properties (e.g., thermal conductivity, density) need unit specifications

subject: IfcMeasureWithUnit
rationale: Building elements (walls, slabs, columns) have dimensional and performance properties that rely on IfcMeasureWithUnit for accurate numerical representation.
conditions: When element dimensions, loads, or properties need quantified values with units

subject: IfcMeasureWithUnit
rationale: IfcCostValue uses the measure-with-unit pattern to associate monetary amounts with currency units.
applicability: Cost estimation and quantity surveying in BIM
conditions: When cost estimates and actual costs need monetary units

subject: IfcMechanicalFastenerType

subject: IfcMechanicalFastenerType
rationale: Mechanical fasteners (bolts, screws, rivets) support structural connections between elements.
conditions: when the fastener type is used to join structural members

subject: IfcMechanicalFastenerType
rationale: The type definition supports the creation and classification of fastener instances.

subject: IfcMechanicalFastenerType
rationale: The type can be connected to material definitions through the IfcRelAssociatesMaterial relationship.
applicability: IfcMechanicalFastenerType 'connects_to IfcRelAssociatesMaterial' — RelAssociatesMaterial is a relationship object, not an entity that type definitions directly 'connect to'. The assertion would be more accurate if describing that IfcRelAssociatesMaterial can associate IfcMaterial to IfcMechanicalFastenerType. The phrasing implies a direct connection that is misleading.

subject: IfcMechanicalFastenerType

Properties are assigned to type definitions via IfcRelDefinesByProperties referencing IfcPropertySetDefinition. The condition 'when associating properties with the type definition' is incorrect — RelDefinesByType relates occurrences TO the type, not properties TO the type.

subject: IfcMechanicalFastenerType
rationale: The type definition contains the common information shared by all occurrence instances of IfcMechanicalFastener.
conditions: when the type is assigned to multiple instances

subject: IfcMemberStandardCase

subject: IfcMemberStandardCase
rationale: Standard member placement relies on a local coordinate system for correct orientation.
conditions: For 3D positioning and orientation

subject: IfcMemberStandardCase
rationale: Members (beams/joists) commonly support slabs in framed structures.
applicability: IfcMemberStandardCase supports IfcSlab only when the member acts as a beam or joist, but in IFC, beams are more typically represented as IfcBeam rather than IfcMemberStandardCase. The domain overlap with IfcBeam creates ambiguity.

subject: IfcMemberStandardCase
rationale: Vertical members can provide structural support to wall panels.
applicability: IfcMemberStandardCase acting as a stud in a wall is valid, but column functionality would typically be represented by IfcColumn rather than IfcMemberStandardCase. The vertical structural element role overlaps with IfcColumn definition.

subject: IfcMember
rationale: IfcMember (beams, braces) often depends on columns for vertical support and load transfer in frame structures.
conditions: When acting as a primary structural member in frames
exceptions: In steel frames, primary members can be columns (vertical), not just members. An IfcMember acting as a column (compression member) does not depend on another IfcColumn - it IS the column. The assertion incorrectly implies all primary structural members that are IfcMember depend on IfcColumn.

subject: IfcMember
rationale: Members require connections (bolted, welded, pinned, or fixed) to transfer loads to other structural elements.
applicability: IfcMember end joints can be connected to IfcStructuralConnection directly OR via IfcPlate (base plates), IfcStiffenerPlate, or other connection elements. The member does not always 'depend_on' IfcStructuralConnection directly - in some joint types (e.g., welded moment connections), the connection is modeled differently or the dependency is indirect through connection elements.
conditions: At all member end joints

subject: IfcMember
rationale: An IfcMember must have an associated material (steel, concrete, timber, etc.) to be physically realized.
conditions: Always required for physical instantiation
exceptions: IfcMember in early design stages (conceptual/schematic) or in non-structural contexts (e.g., decorative members) may not require IfcMaterial assignment. Also, IfcMembers can be defined with material set via IfcMaterialProfileSet which is a different path than a simple IfcMaterial relationship.

subject: IfcMember
rationale: Beams and joists (IfcMember) support slabs by carrying their dead and live loads to columns or walls.
conditions: When members act as beams or joists under a floor or roof slab
exceptions: IfcMember supports IfcSlab is only true for beam/joist systems. In flat slab or flat plate systems (no beams), IfcSlab is supported directly by IfcColumn, not by IfcMember. Also, in composite deck systems, the slab is supported by metal deck which might be modeled as IfcPlate or as part of the slab itself.

subject: IfcMember
rationale: Lintel members support the wall above openings; spandrel beams support wall loads at floor levels.
conditions: When members act as lintels or spandrel beams above openings or at floor edges
exceptions: In structural walls (shear walls, load-bearing concrete walls), lintels and spandrel beams are often integral parts of the wall, modeled as IfcWall (with openings) rather than separate IfcMember elements. This assertion may not apply to monolithic concrete or masonry wall construction where the lintel is part of the wall itself.

subject: IfcMember
rationale: Roof members support roof covering and transfer loads (snow, wind, dead) to supporting structure.
conditions: When members are rafters, purlins, or roof beams
exceptions: In many modern flat roof systems (especially membrane roofs on metal decking), the IfcRoof does not 'depend on' rafters/purlins/roof beams as distinct IfcMember elements - the roof structure is a composite deck assembly or precast concrete plank system where the structural support is integrated into the roof element itself.

subject: IfcMember
rationale: IfcMember (e.g., as a beam) connects to other beams at moment connections or through gusset plates in trusses.
applicability: The assertion only lists steel and timber frames, omitting concrete frames where IfcMember (as a precast concrete beam) also connects to IfcBeam. Additionally, in truss systems, the distinction between IfcMember and IfcBeam is ambiguous - some truss modeling conventions use IfcMember for all truss elements rather than mixing IfcMember and IfcBeam.
conditions: When members are part of a continuous frame or truss system

subject: IfcMember
rationale: Members such as furring channels or framing members support coverings like drywall, ceiling tiles, or cladding.
conditions: When members provide substrate for finishes
exceptions: For ceiling systems suspended by hangers or wires, the IfcCovering (ceiling) is supported by hangers attached to the structural deck/slab above, not directly by IfcMember. Similarly, for cladding systems attached to girts/sub-girts, the supporting elements are often purlins/girts (IfcMember) but the relationship in IFC modeling is frequently through IfcRelConnectsElements or containment, not a direct 'supports' relationship.

subject: IfcMember
rationale: Members are designed and verified using structural analysis models to ensure they can resist applied loads.
conditions: During design phase for sizing and verification

subject: IfcMetric

conditions: when used in performance-based design

subject: IfcMetric
rationale: IfcMetric is associated with IfcConstraint to define measurement criteria and benchmark values for constraints.

subject: IfcMemberType

subject: IfcMirroredProfileDef
rationale: IfcMirroredProfileDef is a subtype of IfcProfileDef, inheriting all its properties and requiring an IfcProfileDef as its parent.
conditions: parent class relationship

subject: IfcMirroredProfileDef
rationale: The entity has a 'MirroredProfile' attribute that must reference another IfcProfileDef (or its subtype) to define what profile is being mirrored.
applicability: The assertion states IfcMirroredProfileDef depends_on IfcProfileDef when the MirroredProfile property references an IfcProfileDef instance. However, IfcMirroredProfileDef is a subtype of IfcProfileDef (via IfcAbstractProfileDef), meaning the MirroredProfile attribute actually points to IfcProfileDef itself, not a separate object. This creates a self-referential and potentially circular dependency that should be noted as a modeling limitation.
conditions: The MirroredProfile property references an IfcProfileDef instance as the source profile being mirrored

subject: IfcMirroredProfileDef
rationale: Mirrored profiles can be assigned to material profile sets to define cross-section properties for mirrored shapes in structural members.
conditions: when used in structural or section definitions

subject: IfcMirroredProfileDef
rationale: The mirrored profile can be used as a profile definition for extrusion operations to create symmetric solid geometry.
applicability: IfcMirroredProfileDef supports IfcExtrudedAreaSolid when used as SweptArea is partially correct, but IfcExtrudedAreaSolid.SweptArea is defined as IfcProfileDef, and IfcMirroredProfileDef is a subtype of IfcProfileDef. However, the engine for extruding a mirrored profile may produce unexpected geometry because IfcMirroredProfileDef does not actually transform coordinates - it indicates that the source profile should be mirrored about its local coordinate system's y-axis. The extrusion may yield results not expected by typical users, and this semantic nuance is missing from the assertion.
conditions: when the mirrored profile is used as the SweptArea

subject: IfcMotorConnection
rationale: The motor connection point is typically fed from a distribution board or motor control center in the building.
applicability: The existing exception 'Direct utility connection' is vague and does not clarify what it means. Does it refer to direct connection from a utility meter to a motor? This exception description is insufficiently defined and could lead to misinterpretation.
conditions: In building electrical distribution
exceptions: Direct utility connection

applicability: All building types with mechanical systems

The assertion uses 'depends_on' which is ambiguous in IFC: IfcMotorConnectionType is a type definition that classifies IfcMotorConnection instances, not a dependency relationship. The relationship in IFC is IfcMotorConnectionType.RelatedObjects referencing IfcMotorConnection via IfcRelDefinesByType, not a dependency.
conditions: The motor connection must be physically attached to the motor and the driven equipment
exceptions: IfcMotorConnection may exist as a generic element without an assigned type, or be assigned to IfcMotorConnectionType indirectly through other relationships (e.g., ifcRelDefinesByProperties), in which case the 'depends_on' relationship as stated does not hold.

subject: IfcMotorConnectionType
rationale: Motors commonly drive pumps, and the motor connection provides the mechanical link.
applicability: Pumping systems in plumbing or HVAC
conditions: When the motor is driving a pump

subject: IfcMotorConnectionType

conditions: When the motor is driving a fan

subject: IfcMotorConnectionType

subject: IfcMotorConnectionType

subject: IfcNamedUnit
rationale: IfcNamedUnit is an abstract supertype; IfcSIUnit is a common concrete subtype that defines SI-based measurement units.
applicability: IfcNamedUnit is an abstract class; it does not directly 'depend_on' IfcSIUnit. Rather, IfcSIUnit is a subtype of IfcNamedUnit (IfcSIUnit inherits from IfcNamedUnit via IfcNamedUnit > IfcSIUnit in the IFC EXPRESS schema). The direction of dependency is reversed: IfcSIUnit specializes IfcNamedUnit, not the other way around.
conditions: When the unit is a SI unit

subject: IfcNamedUnit
rationale: IfcNamedUnit is an abstract supertype; IfcConversionBasedUnit is a concrete subtype for units defined by conversion to another unit.
applicability: Same structural issue as the SIUnit case: IfcConversionBasedUnit is a subtype of IfcNamedUnit (IfcNamedUnit > IfcConversionBasedUnit), not a dependent entity. The assertion reverses the inheritance hierarchy.
conditions: When the unit is not an SI unit and requires conversion

subject: IfcNamedUnit
rationale: Every IfcNamedUnit must have associated dimensional exponents to define its physical quantity (length, mass, time, etc.).
applicability: IfcDimensionalExponents is not a subtype or direct dependency of IfcNamedUnit. Rather, IfcNamedUnit has an attribute 'Dimensions' of type IfcDimensionalExponents. The relationship is that IfcNamedUnit references (has an attribute pointing to) IfcDimensionalExponents, but the phrasing 'depends_on' is ambiguous and the assertion implies a subtype or derived relationship that does not match the IFC schema.
conditions: For all named units

subject: IfcNamedUnit
rationale: IfcNamedUnit provides the unit definition used by IfcMeasureWithUnit to express a measured quantity with its unit.
applicability: IfcMeasureWithUnit does not reference IfcNamedUnit directly; it references IfcUnit (the abstract supertype). IfcNamedUnit is one possible subtype of IfcUnit that could be used, but the assertion overstates the relationship by saying IfcNamedUnit specifically 'supports' IfcMeasureWithUnit — IfcMeasureWithUnit accepts any IfcUnit, not just IfcNamedUnit.
conditions: When a measure value needs a unit definition

subject: IfcNamedUnit
rationale: IfcNamedUnit instances are collected within IfcUnitAssignment to define the set of units used in an IFC model.
applicability: IfcUnitAssignment contains a list 'Units' of type IfcUnit (the abstract supertype), not specifically IfcNamedUnit. IfcNamedUnit is only one subtype; IfcDerivedUnit and IfcConversionBasedUnit are also valid. The assertion is overly narrow in stating that IfcNamedUnit specifically 'supports' IfcUnitAssignment.
conditions: When defining project or model units

subject: IfcNamedUnit
rationale: IfcNamedUnit is used as the unit for single-value properties, allowing values like lengths, areas, or volumes to be interpreted correctly.
applicability: IfcPropertySingleValue has an attribute 'Unit' of type IfcUnit (the abstract supertype), not specifically IfcNamedUnit. The unit associated with a property value can be any IfcUnit subtype, not just IfcNamedUnit. The assertion inappropriately narrows the relationship.
conditions: When a property value has an associated unit

rationale: IfcObjectDefinition is the abstract supertype that contains IfcObject as a direct subtype in the IFC hierarchy.

subject: IfcObjectDefinition
rationale: IfcObjectDefinition is the abstract supertype that contains IfcContext as a direct subtype in the IFC hierarchy.

subject: IfcObjectDefinition
rationale: IfcObjectDefinition indirectly contains IfcProduct through IfcObject.

rationale: IfcObjectDefinition indirectly contains IfcElement through IfcObject > IfcProduct.

subject: IfcObjectDefinition
rationale: IfcObjectDefinition indirectly contains IfcBuildingElement through the inheritance chain.

rationale: IfcObjectDefinition is the root for both object and process definitions in IFC; IfcProcess inherits from IfcObjectDefinition indirectly in some IFC versions via IfcProcess subtypes.

rationale: IfcObjectDefinition participates in IfcRelAggregates relationships for whole-part decomposition.

subject: IfcOccupant
rationale: IfcOccupant is a subtype of IfcActor and is typically associated with an IfcBuilding as the overall context.

subject: IfcOccupant
rationale: The relationship assigning an occupant to a building element or space is handled via IfcRelAssignsToActor.
conditions: when occupant is assigned to a building element or space

subject: IfcOccupant
rationale: Occupants depend on doors for movement between spaces.
conditions: when occupant requires access/egress
exceptions: emergency egress scenarios

IfcOccupant does not inherently depend on IfcDoor. The assertion claims dependency for access/egress, but in open-plan buildings or buildings with large open bays (e.g., warehouses, auditoriums, stadiums), occupants may not require doors for access/egress at the individual occupant level. The existing exception 'emergency egress scenarios' is actually a scenario where doors are most critical, not an exception.

subject: IfcOccupant
rationale: Occupants often depend on windows for daylight, views, and natural ventilation.
conditions: for natural light and ventilation
exceptions: fully mechanically ventilated buildings

subject: IfcOccupant
rationale: Occupants depend on stairs for vertical circulation between floors.
conditions: in multi-story buildings
exceptions: buildings with elevators only
single-story buildings

The exception 'buildings with elevators only' is insufficient. Even in multi-story buildings with elevators, stairs may be required as a secondary means of egress per building codes (e.g., IBC requires at least two means of egress). Many jurisdictions mandate stairs regardless of elevator availability.

subject: IfcOccupant
rationale: Occupants with mobility challenges depend on ramps for barrier-free access.
conditions: for accessibility requirements
exceptions: buildings where all levels are accessible via elevators

The existing exception 'buildings where all levels are accessible via elevators' is incomplete. Even with elevators, building codes often require ramps as an accessible means of egress (e.g., areas of refuge, accessible egress routes). Additionally, existing buildings with step-free ground-floor-only occupancy would also not require ramps.

subject: IfcOccupant
rationale: Occupants depend on building systems (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, fire safety) for comfort, safety, and function.
conditions: during building occupancy

subject: IfcOccupant
rationale: Occupants depend on distribution systems for conditioned air, water, power, and data.
conditions: during normal occupancy

subject: IfcOccupant
rationale: Occupants depend on furniture for daily activities such as working, sitting, or storing items.
conditions: for workspace, seating, or storage
exceptions: unfurnished spaces

subject: IfcOccupant
rationale: Occupants depend on toilets, sinks, and other sanitary fixtures for basic hygiene.
conditions: for hygiene and sanitation
exceptions: Not all building types require sanitary terminals for occupants. Examples include: warehouses with no plumbing (storage-only), temporary structures (construction site trailers may have portable toilets not modeled as IfcSanitaryTerminal), and some industrial facilities where sanitation is handled off-site or via centralized facilities.

subject: IfcOccupant

subject: IfcOpeningElement
rationale: An opening element can contain (be filled by) a window via IfcRelFillsElement.

In IFC, stairwell openings use IfcRelVoidsElement to relate the opening to a slab, and the stair flight is related via IfcRelFillsElement or IfcRelAssociates. subject: IfcOpeningElement

subject: IfcOpeningStandardCase

More precisely, IfcPcurve IS_A IfcRepresentationItem; this is true in all contexts, not just 'when used within a geometric representation context'. The condition is unnecessarily restrictive.

subject: IfcPerformanceHistory

applicability: The assertion states IfcPerformanceHistory depends_on IfcRelDefinesByProperties, but the existing exception already notes this is not the case when performance history is static. Additionally, IfcRelDefinesByProperties is a relationship entity that links objects to property sets, not a direct dependency of IfcPerformanceHistory — IfcPerformanceHistory may be linked via IfcRelDefinesByProperties from the object side, but IfcPerformanceHistory itself does not 'depend on' this relationship class as a prerequisite; it more accurately relates via IfcRelDefinesByProperties to attach property sets. The phrasing obscures the directionality.

exceptions: if performance history is static and not linked to property definitions
