IfcPerformanceHistory can store time series data through IfcPropertySingleValue or IfcPropertyBoundedValue with IfcTimeSeries as a value, or via IfcTimeSeries directly as an inverse attribute, but a time series is not a mandatory dependency — performance history can exist without temporal data via IfcTimeSeries, e.g., when storing static measurements.

subject: IfcPerformanceHistory
rationale: Performance history can be assigned to processes (e.g., commissioning, periodic testing) via IfcRelAssignsToProcess.
conditions: when performance history is part of a work or maintenance process

subject: IfcPerformanceHistory
rationale: IfcPerformanceHistory can be linked to building elements to track element-specific performance over time (e.g., energy use of an HVAC unit).
conditions: when performance data relates to a specific building element

subject: IfcPerformanceHistory
rationale: Performance history can be associated with building systems (e.g., HVAC system efficiency tracking).
conditions: when tracking system-level performance

subject: IfcPerformanceHistory
rationale: IfcPerformanceHistory may reference property sets which contain IfcPropertySingleValue entries for recorded performance data points.
applicability: IfcPerformanceHistory contains IfcPropertySingleValue through its inherited property set definitions (via IfcPropertySet and IfcRelDefinesByProperties), not directly. IfcPerformanceHistory itself has no direct containment attribute for IfcPropertySingleValue. The property values are contained within IfcPropertySet which is linked via IfcRelDefinesByProperties. The assertion is an oversimplification of the actual IFC relationship chain.
conditions: when storing individual performance measurements

subject: IfcPermeableCoveringProperties
rationale: IfcPermeableCoveringProperties defines properties for permeable coverings, which are a subtype of IfcCovering.
conditions: when applied as a covering type

subject: IfcPermeableCoveringProperties
rationale: The permeable covering properties often relate to layered constructions for drainage and filtration.
conditions: when constructed with layered assembly

subject: IfcPermeableCoveringProperties
rationale: Permeable coverings are often applied to slab-type elements to allow water passage.
conditions: when used as a permeable slab covering

subject: IfcPermit
rationale: An IfcPermit is typically issued by or depends on an IfcOrganization (e.g., building department, municipality, authority having jurisdiction) to be valid.
conditions: A permit is issued by an authoritative organization

subject: IfcPermit
rationale: Permits may be applied for by or assigned to an IfcPerson acting as applicant, responsible officer, or inspector.
applicability: Many permits are issued to legal entities (corporations, LLCs) rather than natural persons, and the applicant can be an organization without naming a specific individual. The dependency on IfcPerson is thus not always applicable.
conditions: When a specific individual is the permit applicant or authorized signatory

subject: IfcPermit
rationale: IfcPermit is typically associated with an IfcBuilding or project as the subject of the permit.
conditions: Permit is related to a specific building project

subject: IfcPermit
rationale: An IfcPermit is contextualized within an IfcProject, which aggregates the work to which the permit applies.
conditions: Permit applies to a construction or renovation project

subject: IfcPermit
rationale: Permits may require an associated work plan to define the scope and schedule of permitted work.
conditions: When permits are linked to scheduled work tasks

subject: IfcPermit
rationale: A permit requires supporting documents such as approved drawings, certificates, and inspection reports to be valid.
conditions: Permit documentation includes certificates, drawings, or approvals

subject: IfcPermit
rationale: IfcPermit often functions as or requires an IfcApproval record from the issuing authority to be effective.
conditions: The permit itself is a type of approval or requires approval from an authority

subject: IfcPermit
rationale: A permit often references the site address (IfcAddress) of the building or facility.
applicability: Not all permits reference a site address; some permits (e.g., for mobile equipment, temporary structures, or facility-wide permits) may not have or require a specific IfcAddress. The address may be optional or derived from the project.
conditions: Permit references the site location or postal address

subject: IfcPermit
rationale: Relationships such as IfcRelAggregates are used to nest the permit under a project or building in the IFC model.
conditions: To relate the permit to the building or project elements

subject: IfcPerson
rationale: IfcPerson is defined within IFC as a person who may be associated with an organization. In IFC schema, an IfcPerson can exist independently but is typically related to an IfcOrganization for role and responsibility context.
conditions: when representing a person within an organizational context

subject: IfcPerson
rationale: IfcPerson can have one or more addresses (IfcAddress) for postal, email, or telecom contact. This is optional but required for full contact data.
applicability: The assertion states IfcPerson 'requires' IfcAddress when contact information is needed, but IfcAddress is optional in IFC and can also be attached to IfcOrganization or IfcPersonAndOrganization rather than directly to IfcPerson.
conditions: when contact information is needed
exceptions: not required if person is only referenced by name

subject: IfcPerson
rationale: IfcPerson is often assigned roles via IfcActorRole to define their function (e.g., architect, engineer) within a construction project.
conditions: when defining the person's role in a project

subject: IfcPerson
rationale: IfcActor is a subtype that inherits from IfcPerson and IfcOrganization, representing a person or organization actively involved in a project. IfcPerson supports the definition of IfcActor.
applicability: The 'supports' relationship should be reversed: IfcActor uses IfcPerson (via IfcActorSelect), not the other way around. IfcPerson does not 'support' IfcActor in an architectural sense.
conditions: when the person is acting in a project context

subject: IfcPerson
rationale: IfcPersonAndOrganization combines IfcPerson and IfcOrganization to represent a person acting on behalf of an organization. IfcPerson is a fundamental component of this relationship.
applicability: The 'supports' relationship direction is imprecise. IfcPersonAndOrganization aggregates IfcPerson, not the reverse. IfcPerson does not 'support' IfcPersonAndOrganization.
conditions: when a person is linked to an organization for a project role

subject: IfcPerson
rationale: IfcOwnerHistory references IfcPerson and IfcOrganization to record authorship and modification history of IFC objects.
conditions: when tracking who created or last modified IFC data

subject: IfcPerson
rationale: IfcPerson is an actor/personnel entity, not a physical building element. It is unsuitable for representing building components like walls, slabs, or beams.
conditions: when direct assignment as a building component is attempted

subject: IfcPersonAndOrganization
rationale: IfcPersonAndOrganization combines IfcPerson and IfcOrganization entities, connecting a person entity to an organization entity.

subject: IfcPersonAndOrganization
rationale: IfcPersonAndOrganization combines IfcPerson and IfcOrganization entities, connecting a person entity to an organization entity.

subject: IfcPersonAndOrganization
rationale: The IfcPersonAndOrganization entity requires a reference to an IfcPerson to be valid, as per IFC schema definition.
conditions: the person must exist in the model

subject: IfcPersonAndOrganization
rationale: The IfcPersonAndOrganization entity requires a reference to an IfcOrganization to be valid, as per IFC schema definition.
conditions: the organization must exist in the model

subject: IfcPersonAndOrganization
rationale: IfcPersonAndOrganization is typically assigned to IfcActor entities to identify the person and organization responsible for a role.
conditions: when used as a role for an actor in the building model
exceptions: IfcPersonAndOrganization does not directly support IfcActor via its own attributes. IfcActor has an attribute called 'TheActor' which can be of type IfcPerson, IfcOrganization, or IfcPersonAndOrganization. So the relationship is that IfcActor references IfcPersonAndOrganization, not the other way around. The assertion direction 'IfcPersonAndOrganization supports IfcActor' is backwards - IfcActor uses/supports IfcPersonAndOrganization.

subject: IfcPersonAndOrganization
rationale: IfcPersonAndOrganization can be referenced in IfcOwnerHistory to identify the person/organization that created or last modified model data.
conditions: when used in the context of model ownership and modification tracking
exceptions: IfcPersonAndOrganization does not directly support IfcOwnerHistory. IfcOwnerHistory has attributes 'OwningUser' (IfcPersonAndOrganization) and 'LastModifiedBy' (IfcPersonAndOrganization). The relationship is that IfcOwnerHistory references IfcPersonAndOrganization, not the other way around. The assertion direction is backwards.

subject: IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity
rationale: IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity is a subtype that aggregates multiple IfcPhysicalQuantity instances (e.g., IfcQuantityLength, IfcQuantityArea) to describe complex physical properties of an element.
conditions: when used as a container for physical quantities

subject: IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity
rationale: IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity contains or aggregates multiple IfcPhysicalQuantity objects to represent a compound property.
conditions: when grouping related quantities under a single complex quantity

subject: IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity
rationale: IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity is typically assigned to building elements through IfcPropertySet or IfcElementQuantity.
conditions: when the complex quantity is assigned to an element via a property set

subject: IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity
rationale: The complex quantity provides measurements for an element defined as IfcObjectDefinition (e.g., IfcWall, IfcSlab).
applicability: IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity does not directly 'depend_on' IfcObjectDefinition. The relationship chain is: IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity is assigned to IfcElementQuantity (via HasQuantities), which is then related to IfcObjectDefinition via IfcRelDefinesByProperties. The assertion oversimplifies the indirect dependency.
conditions: when quantifying properties of a specific building element or system

subject: IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity
rationale: IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity can be nested inside IfcElementQuantity to support quantity take-off for cost estimation and material scheduling.
conditions: when used as part of quantity take-off specifications

subject: IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity
rationale: The complex quantity relies on being part of a quantity set structure for semantic grouping.
conditions: when organized within a named set of quantities

subject: IfcPhysicalQuantity
rationale: Physical quantities typically quantify properties of building elements, so they depend on being assigned to IfcElement subtypes.
conditions: when associated via IfcRelDefinesByProperties

subject: IfcPhysicalQuantity
rationale: IfcPhysicalQuantity can be part of IfcElementQuantity, which is a subtype of IfcPropertySetDefinition, but the quantity itself depends on being contained in a property set for assignment.
conditions: when used within a property set

subject: IfcPhysicalQuantity
rationale: Physical quantities feed into cost estimation by providing measurable quantities of building works.
applicability: IfcPhysicalQuantity does not directly support IfcCostSchedule. Cost schedules use IfcCostItem which references IfcQuantityResource (via IfcRelNests or IfcRelAssignsToControl), and quantities are related to cost items, not to the cost schedule directly. The assertion has the wrong target entity in the dependency chain.
conditions: when used for cost estimation

subject: IfcPhysicalQuantity
rationale: Quantities help determine required construction resources like materials and labor.
applicability: IfcPhysicalQuantity supports IfcConstructionResource through IfcQuantityResource (a subtype of IfcConstructionResource), not IfcConstructionResource directly. This is an indirect relationship via the subtype hierarchy that should be clarified.
conditions: for resource planning

subject: IfcPhysicalQuantity
rationale: Physical quantities contain or reference units of measurement (IfcNamedUnit) via their associated measure types.
conditions: implicitly through measure values

subject: IfcPhysicalQuantity
rationale: Quantities depend on the project's unit assignment to ensure consistent measurement interpretation.
conditions: for unit context

subject: IfcPhysicalQuantity
rationale: Complex physical quantities depend on simpler quantity components.
conditions: when representing complex quantities that aggregate simpler ones
exceptions: IfcPhysicalQuantity does not require IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity; the relationship is the opposite. IfcPhysicalComplexQuantity contains (aggregates) IfcPhysicalQuantity instances as its components, not the other way around. A simple IfcPhysicalQuantity can exist independently without being part of a complex quantity.

subject: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity
rationale: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity is the abstract parent type from which specific quantity types like IfcQuantityLength inherit.
conditions: when representing length measurements

subject: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity
rationale: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity is the abstract parent type from which specific quantity types like IfcQuantityArea inherit.
conditions: when representing area measurements

subject: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity
rationale: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity is the abstract parent type from which specific quantity types like IfcQuantityVolume inherit.
conditions: when representing volume measurements

subject: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity
rationale: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity is the abstract parent type from which specific quantity types like IfcQuantityWeight inherit.
conditions: when representing weight measurements

subject: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity
rationale: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity is the abstract parent type from which specific quantity types like IfcQuantityCount inherit.
conditions: when representing count measurements

subject: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity
rationale: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity is the abstract parent type from which specific quantity types like IfcQuantityTime inherit.
conditions: when representing time measurements

subject: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity
rationale: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity is a subtype of IfcPhysicalQuantity, so it depends on the parent class for its definition and structure.
conditions: as the parent abstraction for simple quantities

subject: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity
rationale: IfcPhysicalSimpleQuantity instances are typically aggregated within IfcElementQuantity to provide measured quantities for building elements.
conditions: when used to define quantities of building elements

subject: IfcPile
rationale: Piles are the primary structural element of deep foundations, transferring loads to deeper bearing strata.
applicability: The assertion states 'IfcPile supports Foundation' but does not specify which foundation types (shallow vs deep, spread footings vs mat foundations vs pile caps). IfcPile is specifically a deep foundation element; it does not support shallow foundation systems like footings or mats. The assertion is ambiguous and could be misinterpreted as general foundation support.
conditions: Deep foundation systems

subject: IfcPile
rationale: Concrete is the primary material for forming the pile shaft in concrete pile types.
conditions: For concrete piles (cast-in-place or precast)
exceptions: Steel H-piles, timber piles, or composite piles

subject: IfcPipeFitting
rationale: Pipe fittings connect to flow segments (pipes, ducts) to form a continuous flow distribution system.
conditions: hydraulic or pneumatic continuity required
exceptions: capped fittings used as end closures

subject: IfcPipeFitting
rationale: IfcPipeFitting is defined with inlet and outlet ports that establish connectivity with other elements in the IFC model.
applicability: all building information models using IfcPipeFitting

The assertion states IfcPipeFitting depends_on IfcPort applies to 'all building information models using IfcPipeFitting', but IfcPipeFitting can use IfcDistributionPort (subtype of IfcPort) through its inherited property from IfcDistributionElement. However, IfcPipeFitting does not necessarily directly depend on IfcPort in all models — in simplified BIM models, pipe fittings may be connected purely via IfcRelConnectsElements without port-based topology, making this dependency not universal.
conditions: for connection definition and topology

subject: IfcPipeFitting
rationale: Fittings such as tees or flanges often connect directly to valves to enable flow regulation or isolation in the network.
conditions: when used in a flow control arrangement
exceptions: IfcValve is a subtype of IfcFlowController, which is a subtype of IfcDistributionElement, and IfcPipeFitting is also a subtype of IfcFlowSegment. A direct 'connects_to' relationship between IfcPipeFitting and IfcValve is not always a valid IFC relationship; in IFC schema, connections between distribution elements typically go through IfcRelConnectsPorts via IfcPort objects, not direct element-to-element relationships. This assertion may require a port-based intermediate connection rather than a direct connection.

subject: IfcPipeFitting
rationale: Pipe fittings at pump connections allow transition between pump flanges and piping, including reducers or expansion joints.
conditions: when part of a pumped fluid system
exceptions: Similar to the valve case, IfcPump (subtype of IfcFlowMovingDevice) and IfcPipeFitting connect via ports in a standard IFC topology. In many hydronic systems, pumps are often connected to pipe fittings (like flanges, reducers, or elbows) through flanged connections, but in IFC this is typically modeled via IfcRelConnectsPorts rather than a direct 'connects_to' relationship. Additionally, some pumped systems may have the pump directly connected to straight pipe (IfcFlowSegment) rather than a fitting.

subject: IfcPipeFittingType
rationale: Pipe fittings may connect to flow terminals such as faucets, sprinkler heads, or equipment connections at the extremities of a piping system.
applicability: The condition 'at end-of-run locations in piping networks' is ambiguous. End-of-run could mean a terminal fitting (e.g., end cap) or the last fitting before a terminal. The assertion does not specify whether this refers to the physical connection topology or logical connectivity in the IFC model.
conditions: at end-of-run locations in piping networks

subject: IfcPipeSegment
rationale: In IFC schema, pipe segments depend on relationship objects to establish connectivity within the piping network topology.
conditions: for logical connectivity
exceptions: IfcPipeSegment may be connected via IfcRelConnectsPorts (through ports) or IfcRelNests (for assemblies) in some IFC implementations, not exclusively through IfcRelConnectsPathElements. The assertion overstates the dependency by implying it is the only or mandatory relationship.

subject: IfcPipeSegment
rationale: Pumps are often required to maintain fluid pressure and flow through pipe segments, though gravity systems are an exception.
conditions: when fluid must be moved against gravity or over long distances
exceptions: gravity-fed systems

Pumps are not required when fluid flow is driven by existing system pressure (e.g., city water main pressure) even if moving against gravity or over long distances within a building — the pump requirement depends on the available head from the supply source, not solely on the pipe segment properties.

subject: IfcPipeSegment
rationale: Thermal insulation is often required around pipe segments to prevent heat loss/gain and condensation.
conditions: when pipe carries hot or cold fluids
when condensation control is needed
when energy efficiency is required
exceptions: non-temperature-critical pipes
interior drain pipes

subject: IfcPipeSegment
rationale: In IFC-based BIM, a pipe segment depends on property sets to define its physical and performance characteristics.
conditions: for defining pipe properties (diameter, material, pressure rating)
exceptions: IfcPipeSegment properties such as diameter, material, and pressure rating can be defined directly via IfcPropertySet or through predefined property sets in the IFC schema (e.g., Pset_PipeSegmentPHistory) or through IfcElementQuantity. The assertion does not account for cases where properties are inherited from type definitions (IfcPipeSegmentType) rather than directly associated via IfcPropertySet on the occurrence.

subject: IfcPipeSegment
rationale: Pipe segments connect to flow terminals such as sinks, toilets, faucets, sprinklers, or equipment nozzles.
conditions: at endpoints of piping network
exceptions: IfcPipeSegment does not always connect to IfcFlowTerminal at endpoints — in the case of a fire sprinkler system, a pipe segment may terminate at an IfcFlowTerminal (sprinkler head), but in other cases a pipe segment may end at a cap, plug, or blind flange which are IfcPipeFitting elements, not IfcFlowTerminal.

subject: IfcPipeSegment
rationale: Multiple pipe segments connect to each other to form continuous runs within a piping system.
conditions: in continuous piping runs

subject: IfcPipeSegmentType
rationale: Pipe segments require fittings (elbows, tees, reducers) to change direction, branch, or change diameter in a piping system.
applicability: An IfcPipeSegmentType does not always require an IfcPipeFitting when connecting pipe segments. Pipe segments can be joined by welding, flanging, or other direct connection methods that use no discrete 'fitting' entity (e.g., butt-welded straight runs). A fitting is only required when the connection involves a change in direction, diameter, or branch.
conditions: when connecting different pipe segments

subject: IfcPipeSegmentType
rationale: IfcPipeSegmentType is a subtype of IfcFlowSegment, so it inherently requires connection to other flow segments to form a continuous piping network.
conditions: part of a flow distribution system

subject: IfcPipeSegmentType
rationale: Pipe performance depends entirely on its material (e.g., steel, copper, PVC, HDPE, concrete) which dictates strength, corrosion resistance, and temperature limits.
conditions: material selection based on fluid type, temperature, and pressure

subject: IfcPipeSegmentType
rationale: Pipe segments provide the structural mounting and flow path for valves that control or isolate sections of the piping system.
applicability: An IfcPipeSegmentType does not inherently 'support' IfcValve. Valves are typically connected (connects_to) to pipe segments at specific points, not structurally supported by the pipe segment type. In IFC terms, IfcValve is a separate element that is placed in-line with piping, but semantic relationship is connection/placement, not 'support'.
conditions: where flow regulation or isolation is needed

subject: IfcPipeSegmentType
rationale: Pipe segments connect pumps to distribution networks to move fluid through the system.
conditions: in pressurized systems

subject: IfcPipeSegmentType
rationale: Pipe segments connect storage tanks or water heaters to the distribution network.
conditions: at supply or storage points

subject: IfcPipeSegmentType
rationale: Pipe segments connect sanitary fixtures (toilets, sinks, urinals) to the drainage/waste system.
conditions: in drainage systems
exceptions: IfcPipeSegmentType can connect to IfcSanitaryTerminal in drainage systems, but this is not universally true. In many plumbing configurations, sanitary terminals (e.g., toilets, sinks) connect first to traps or waste branches via short pipe segments before reaching the main drainage pipe. The direct connection assertion may not hold for all sanitary terminal types.

subject: IfcPixelTexture
rationale: IfcPixelTexture is a subtype of IfcImageTexture, providing texture data at the pixel level for surface visualization.
applicability: All building models using IFC schema
conditions: When used as a texture mapping for surfaces

subject: IfcPixelTexture
rationale: Texture mapping requires coordinate references to position the pixel data on surfaces.
applicability: All building models using IFC schema
conditions: For defining texture coordinates

subject: IfcPixelTexture
rationale: IfcPixelTexture inherits from IfcSurfaceTexture, which provides the base texture attribute structure.
applicability: All building models using IFC schema
conditions: As parent class relationship

subject: IfcPixelTexture
rationale: IfcPixelTexture provides pixel-level color data that can be used in IfcStyledItem for visual presentation of building elements.
conditions: When pixel texture is used for rendering surface appearance

subject: IfcPixelTexture
rationale: The texture contributes to the graphical representation that can be assigned to presentation layers.
applicability: Visualization and presentation in IFC models
conditions: When texture is part of a graphical presentation layer

subject: IfcPixelTexture
rationale: IfcPixelTexture connects to surface geometry through IfcTextureCoordinate relationships that define how pixel data maps to faces.
applicability: All IFC models using texture mapping
conditions: When mapping texture to geometry

subject: IfcPlacement
rationale: IfcPlacement is an abstract supertype; IfcAxis2Placement3D is a concrete subtype that provides the actual 3D coordinate system definition.
conditions: when representing 3D placement

subject: IfcPlacement
rationale: IfcPlacement is an abstract supertype; IfcAxis2Placement2D is the concrete subtype for 2D coordinate systems.
conditions: when representing 2D placement

subject: IfcPlacement
rationale: IfcPlacement.Location references IfcCartesianPoint, which defines the origin of the placement coordinate system.
conditions: always

subject: IfcPlacement
rationale: Placement axes (P, RefDirection, Axis) are defined using IfcDirection to orient the local coordinate system.
conditions: when using IfcAxis2Placement3D or IfcAxis2Placement2D

subject: IfcPlacement
rationale: IfcLocalPlacement contains a PlacementRelTo attribute that references a supertype IfcPlacement to define relative positioning.
applicability: IfcPlacement supports IfcLocalPlacement only when used as the PlacementRelTo attribute (relative placement). However, IfcLocalPlacement also supports an absolute placement when PlacementRelTo is not provided (omitted), in which case the placement is relative to the world coordinate system and no IfcPlacement is referenced for relative positioning.
conditions: when used as PlacementRelTo attribute

subject: IfcPlacement
rationale: IfcProduct.ObjectPlacement uses IfcObjectPlacement which ultimately relies on IfcPlacement to define its position in the coordinate system.
applicability: all IFC models requiring spatial positioning
conditions: when ObjectPlacement references IfcLocalPlacement containing IfcPlacement

subject: IfcPlacement
rationale: IfcGridPlacement is a subtype relationship within the placement hierarchy that leverages IfcPlacement definitions.
applicability: all IFC models with grid-based layouts
conditions: when defining placement relative to a grid

subject: IfcPlacement
rationale: IfcPlacement is used within IfcLocalPlacement which is a subtype of IfcObjectPlacement, forming part of the object placement system.
conditions: as a subtype of IfcObjectPlacement definitions

subject: IfcPlanarBox
rationale: IfcPlanarBox requires Cartesian point coordinates to define its extent in the plane.
applicability: IfcPlanarBox does not directly 'depend_on' IfcCartesianPoint. IfcPlanarBox inherits from IfcPlacement (via IfcAxis2Placement2D or IfcAxis2Placement3D), which itself references IfcCartesianPoint for the placement location. However, IfcPlanarBox is defined as a subtype of IfcProductRepresentationSelect using PlacementRelTo (relative placement), not through direct IfcCartesianPoint dependency for 'corner points'. The corner points are defined by the PlacementRelTo relationship with IfcProductDefinitionShape or IfcShapeRepresentation, not by a direct dependency on IfcCartesianPoint.
conditions: for defining corner points of the box

subject: IfcPlanarBox
rationale: The planar box contains placement point coordinates that define its location and size.
applicability: The assertion states IfcPlanarBox 'contains' IfcCartesianPoint as corner points. In the IFC specification, IfcPlanarBox does not directly 'contain' IfcCartesianPoint instances. IfcPlanarBox has attributes such as Placement and Size. The corner points are derived from the Placement (which uses IfcAxis2Placement2D referencing IfcCartesianPoint for origin) and the size (x-dim, y-dim). The 'contains' semantics could be misleading — IfcCartesianPoint instances are not aggregated or composed within IfcPlanarBox in the containment sense.
conditions: as corner points defining the planar box

subject: IfcPlanarBox
rationale: The planar box placement depends on direction vectors to orient the coordinate axes.
applicability: IfcPlanarBox does not depend on IfcDirection directly. In IFC2x3/IFC4, IfcPlanarBox has a Placement attribute of type IfcAxis2Placement2D, which includes a RefDirection of type IfcDirection. So the dependency is indirect — through IfcAxis2Placement2D, not direct. The assertion oversimplifies the relationship.
conditions: for defining the axis directions of the placement

subject: IfcPlanarExtent
rationale: IfcPlanarExtent is an abstract entity that defines the extent of a planar geometric representation, typically used as a supertype for elements like IfcWall, IfcSlab, etc.
applicability: any building element that can be represented as a planar extent
conditions: when used as a base type for elements with planar geometry

subject: IfcPlanarExtent
rationale: IfcPlanarExtent defines the extent of a planar shape used in shape representations
conditions: when representing geometry in a 2D planar context

subject: IfcPlanarExtent
rationale: IfcPlanarExtent is typically associated with IfcProduct for geometric representation
conditions: when used as a representation for a building product

subject: IfcPlanarExtent
rationale: IfcPlanarExtent can be used to define the extent of annotation elements in 2D representations
conditions: when used to represent annotation extents in plan views

subject: IfcPlanarExtent
rationale: IfcPlanarExtent may contain or define the extent that can be encapsulated in a bounding box
applicability: all building elements with planar geometry
conditions: when a bounding box representation is derived from the planar extent

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: IfcPlane is defined by a position (IfcAxis2Placement3D) which requires an IfcCartesianPoint for its origin.
conditions: when defining geometry

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: IfcPlane's placement (IfcAxis2Placement3D) requires two direction vectors (typically Z-axis and X-axis directions) to fully orient the plane in 3D space.
conditions: when defining orientation

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: IfcPlane inherits from IfcElementarySurface and always has a Position attribute of type IfcAxis2Placement3D.
conditions: always

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: IfcPlane is often used as the base surface for IfcHalfSpaceSolid to define half-space volumes in boolean subtraction operations.
conditions: when used as a clipping plane in boolean operations

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: IfcPlane serves as the boundary surface that defines the limit of a half-space solid.
conditions: when defining clipping geometry

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: IfcPlane can be used as a bounding or limiting surface for spatial containment checks.
conditions: when defining planar bounding geometry

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: The IfcAxis2Placement3D that defines the plane contains a Location point of type IfcCartesianPoint.
conditions: as part of placement definition

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: The IfcAxis2Placement3D contains up to two direction vectors (P[0], P[1]) of type IfcDirection.
conditions: as part of placement definition

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: IfcPlane can be the basis for creating IfcSurfaceOfLinearExtrusion, where the plane is extruded along a direction vector.
conditions: when used as the base/profile surface for extrusion
exceptions: IfcPlane connects_to IfcSurfaceOfLinearExtrusion only when the plane is used as the swept surface (SweptSurface) of the extrusion, not merely as a base/profile surface. IfcSurfaceOfLinearExtrusion requires its SweptSurface to be a subtype of IfcSweptSurface, but IfcPlane is not a subtype of IfcSweptSurface — it is a subtype of IfcElementarySurface. Therefore, IfcPlane cannot be used as the SweptSurface of IfcSurfaceOfLinearExtrusion according to the IFC schema.

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: IfcCurveBoundedPlane uses IfcPlane as its BasisSurface, connecting the unbounded plane with bounding curves.
conditions: when the plane is trimmed by boundaries

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: Every IfcPlane instance must have a Position attribute of type IfcAxis2Placement3D to be defined.
applicability: IfcPlane requires IfcAxis2Placement3D only when used in 3D contexts. IfcPlane could also be placed in 2D using IfcAxis2Placement2D in some IFC implementations or in 2D geometric representations.
conditions: always

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: The IfcAxis2Placement3D requires a Location point, so IfcPlane always requires an IfcCartesianPoint defined somewhere.
conditions: always, indirectly through IfcAxis2Placement3D

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: IfcAxis2Placement3D requires at least one direction (Z-axis) for orientation, so IfcPlane always requires IfcDirection instances.
conditions: always, indirectly through IfcAxis2Placement3D

subject: IfcPlane
rationale: Using IfcPlane as a clipping surface enables clean planar cuts in boolean operations, improving geometric modeling precision.
conditions: when used as the clipping surface
exceptions: The assertion says IfcPlane 'improves' IfcBooleanClippingResult. IfcBooleanClippingResult does not have a formal relationship to IfcPlane in the IFC schema. IfcPlane is used as a clipping surface via IfcHalfSpaceSolid, not directly with IfcBooleanClippingResult. The improvement may be indirect through IfcHalfSpaceSolid, making the direct improvement claim misleading.

subject: IfcPlate
rationale: Structural plates often span between and connect to beams.
applicability: In timber or light-gauge steel construction, floor deck plates often sit on top of walls (IfcWall) or are nailed to studs, not only to beams. The assertion as stated fails to account for these construction typologies.
conditions: when used as floor or roof deck plate
exceptions: IfcPlate used as a floor or roof deck plate may also connect to IfcWall (e.g., ledger plates, rim joists bearing on walls) or IfcColumn (e.g., point-supported flat slabs with plate elements). The exclusive 'connects_to IfcBeam' ignores these common structural connections.

subject: IfcPlate
rationale: Plates can be connected to walls for lateral load transfer.
conditions: when used as a bracing or gusset plate
exceptions: Bracing/gusset plates commonly connect IfcBeam to IfcColumn (moment connections) or IfcBeam to IfcBeam (splice plates), not solely IfcWall. The assertion is overly narrow.

subject: IfcPlateStandardCase
rationale: IfcPlateStandardCase as a standard plate may transfer loads to structural members in certain applications.
applicability: The assertion conditions specify 'when acting as structural cladding or bracing', but cladding panels are often attached to structural members (e.g., purlins, girts) rather than semantically 'depending on' them in IFC terms. The relationship is more of an attachment or connection than a dependency.
conditions: when acting as structural cladding or bracing
exceptions: non-loadbearing applications

subject: IfcPlateStandardCase
rationale: Standard plates often have layered material definitions.
conditions: for multi-layer composite panels
exceptions: single-layer homogeneous plates

subject: IfcPlateStandardCase
rationale: Plates can serve as substrate to which finishes are applied.
conditions: when used as base substrate
exceptions: IfcCovering can be directly applied to a substrate without the plate being the 'base substrate' — for example, IfcCovering can be applied to IfcWall or IfcSlab directly without an intervening IfcPlateStandardCase. The assertion should note that this applies only when the plate itself is the substrate layer.

subject: IfcPlateStandardCase
rationale: Standard plates are often connected to wall constructions.
conditions: when used as wall panel or sheathing
exceptions: free-standing plates

subject: IfcPlateStandardCase
rationale: Plates can form or be attached to slab elements.
conditions: when used as floor plate or decking

subject: IfcPlateStandardCase
rationale: Plates may contain openings for building services or fenestration.
conditions: when fabricated with openings for windows/doors
exceptions: solid plates without penetrations

subject: IfcPlateType
rationale: Load-bearing plates depend on structural members for support.
conditions: when used as load-bearing plate
exceptions: non-structural partition plates

subject: IfcPlateType
rationale: Plate elements need connection relationships defined for proper placement.
conditions: for proper connection to other building elements
exceptions: IfcPlateType does not directly depend on IfcRelConnectsElements. IfcRelConnectsElements connects element instances (occurrences), not types. An IfcPlateType can be used by many plates that have connections, but the type definition itself does not have a dependency on this relationship object. This mixes type-level and occurrence-level concepts.

subject: IfcPlateType
rationale: Plate types require material definitions to specify what they are made of.
conditions: to define material properties like steel, concrete, or timber

subject: IfcPlateType
rationale: Geometric representation is necessary for 3D modeling and analysis.
conditions: for geometric definition

subject: IfcPlateType
rationale: Property sets define technical characteristics of the plate type.
conditions: for specifying thickness, fire rating, acoustic properties

subject: IfcPlateType
rationale: Plates can serve as substrate supporting coverings like finishes.
conditions: when plate is used as sheathing or substrate
exceptions: structural plates only

subject: IfcPlateType
rationale: Exterior plates can protect internal elements from weather.
conditions: when used as cladding or shielding element

subject: IfcPlateType
rationale: Plates often connect to beams for load transfer.
conditions: at plate edges or supports

subject: IfcPlateType
rationale: Plates connect to columns in floor slab systems.
conditions: at column-plate intersections

subject: IfcPlateType
rationale: Solid plates may conflict with MEP routing unless penetrations are designed.
conditions: when plates are solid without penetrations for MEP routing
exceptions: if penetrations are pre-planned

subject: IfcPlateType
rationale: Bracing plates improve lateral stability of walls.
conditions: when used as bracing or diaphragm plate
exceptions: non-structural plates

subject: IfcPlateType
rationale: IFC schema requires material associations for plate type definitions.
conditions: for material assignment in IFC data model

subject: IfcPlateType
rationale: Type-object relationship is fundamental in IFC for type definitions.
conditions: to associate occurrences with the plate type

subject: IfcPoint
rationale: IfcPoint is an abstract supertype; its concrete instantiation is always via subtypes like IfcCartesianPoint for geometric representation.
conditions: when representing a point coordinate in 2D or 3D space

subject: IfcPoint
rationale: IfcPoint can be specialized as IfcPointOnCurve for parametric point definitions on curves.
conditions: when a point is defined relative to a curve

subject: IfcPoint
rationale: IfcPoint can be specialized as IfcPointOnSurface for parametric point definitions on surfaces.
conditions: when a point is defined relative to a surface

subject: IfcPoint
rationale: IfcPoint may be used as the geometry underlying IfcVertexPoint in topology representations.
conditions: when representing a point as a topological vertex

subject: IfcPoint
rationale: IfcPoint provides the location origin for IfcAxis2Placement2D, IfcAxis2Placement3D, and IfcLocalPlacement.
conditions: when used as the location of an axis2 or axis3 placement

subject: IfcPoint
rationale: IfcPoint subtypes are used as geometric items within IfcShapeRepresentation for defining point-based geometry.
conditions: when points are used as part of a geometric representation of a product shape

subject: IfcPoint
rationale: IfcPoint provides positioning and geometric definition for IfcProduct subtypes via ObjectPlacement and Representation.
conditions: when a product placement or shape is defined using point geometry

subject: IfcPoint
rationale: IfcPoint is an abstract superclass that contains IfcCartesianPoint as its primary concrete subtype.
conditions: as a specialization in the IFC schema hierarchy

subject: IfcPoint
rationale: IfcPoint is the abstract supertype that contains IfcPointOnCurve as a subtype.
conditions: as a specialization in the IFC schema hierarchy

subject: IfcPoint
rationale: IfcPoint is the abstract supertype that contains IfcPointOnSurface as a subtype.
conditions: as a specialization in the IFC schema hierarchy

subject: IfcPointOnCurve
rationale: IfcPointOnCurve is a subtype of IfcPoint that defines a point on a parametric curve. It inherently depends on an IfcCurve entity to define its position along the curve.
conditions: Must be a valid geometric curve representation

subject: IfcPointOnCurve
rationale: IfcPointOnCurve inherits from IfcRepresentationItem and must be placed within a geometric representation context (e.g. IfcShapeRepresentation) to be meaningful in a building model.
conditions: When used in a geometric representation context

subject: IfcPointOnCurve
rationale: IfcPointOnCurve can be evaluated to produce a Cartesian point on the curve, supporting downstream geometric computations.
conditions: When the point location is derived from the curve parameterization
exceptions: Direct Cartesian coordinates are not stored; only the parameter value and curve reference exist

The assertion states IfcPointOnCurve supports IfcCartesianPoint, but IfcPointOnCurve may also be used in contexts where no Cartesian point is ever derived (e.g., in purely parametric representation pipelines where the curve parameter is never evaluated to a Cartesian location).

subject: IfcPointOnCurve
rationale: Points on curves can serve as reference points for placement of building elements along curved paths (e.g. curtain wall mullions along a curved facade).
conditions: When used as part of axis or positioning definitions

subject: IfcPointOnCurve
rationale: The point location is conceptually contained within the domain of the underlying bounded curve.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcPointOnCurve contains IfcBoundedCurve' is ambiguous. IfcPointOnCurve references a single IfcCurve via its 'BasisCurve' attribute, which may be an IfcBoundedCurve. However, the word 'contains' could misleadingly imply collection/multiple containment, whereas the IFC schema allows only one reference curve. Additionally, if the BasisCurve is unbounded (e.g., IfcLine, IfcCircularArc), there is no IfcBoundedCurve involved.
conditions: Only when the parent curve is bounded

subject: IfcPointOnCurve
rationale: IfcPointOnCurve can be associated with IfcVertexPoint in topological models to define vertex locations along curves.
applicability: The assertion states IfcPointOnCurve connects_to IfcVertexPoint, but IfcPointOnCurve is a subtype of IfcPoint and not inherently a topological entity. The connection to IfcVertexPoint would require it to be used within an IfcTopologicalRepresentationItem context (e.g., as the point geometry of an IfcVertexPoint). The assertion lacks this topological context condition.
conditions: In topological representations where point geometry is needed

subject: IfcPointOnSurface
rationale: IfcPointOnSurface is a subtype of IfcPoint that defines a point on a parametric surface, so it depends on a surface definition.
conditions: The point must lie on a valid surface entity

subject: IfcPointOnSurface
rationale: The point cannot exist without a parent surface entity to position it.
conditions: The surface must be a valid IfcSurface subtype (e.g., IfcPlane, IfcCylindricalSurface, IfcBSplineSurface)
exceptions: The condition restricts valid surface subtypes to IfcPlane, IfcCylindricalSurface, and IfcBSplineSurface, but IfcPointOnSurface can also reference IfcFaceBasedSurfaceModel, IfcFaceSurface, and other surface representations. The listed subtypes are incomplete as valid IfcSurface subtypes.

subject: IfcPointOnSurface
rationale: IfcPointOnSurface can support more complex parametric geometry definitions that combine curves and points on surfaces.
applicability: The assertion says IfcPointOnSurface 'supports' IfcPointOnCurve but provides no semantic detail about what 'supports' means. IfcPointOnSurface and IfcPointOnCurve are siblings (both subtypes of IfcPoint) and neither references the other in the IFC schema. The relationship is through IfcCurveOnSurface (pcurve), not a direct support relationship between the point types.
conditions: When used in combined curve-on-surface and point-on-surface geometry

subject: IfcPointOnSurface
rationale: IfcPointOnSurface can be used to define the geometry of a vertex in a topological representation.
conditions: When the point is used as a topological vertex

subject: IfcPointOnSurface
rationale: IfcPointOnSurface can be evaluated to produce an IfcCartesianPoint representing the 3D location.
applicability: The assertion states IfcPointOnSurface 'supports' IfcCartesianPoint with a condition about evaluating parametric coordinates, but IfcPointOnSurface provides a 2D parametric coordinate (u,v) on the surface, not a direct IfcCartesianPoint (which is 3D). The conversion from parametric to Cartesian coordinates requires the surface's geometry evaluation, which is not inherent to IfcPointOnSurface alone.
conditions: When evaluating the parametric point to get cartesian coordinates

subject: IfcPolyLoop
rationale: IfcPolyLoop is defined by an ordered list of IfcCartesianPoint coordinates that form the vertices of the polygonal loop.
conditions: When defining polygonal geometry

subject: IfcPolyLoop
rationale: IfcPolyLoop is conceptually similar to IfcPolyline but explicitly defines a closed loop by implicitly connecting the last point back to the first.
conditions: When used to define a closed boundary curve

subject: IfcPolyLoop
rationale: Each point in the poly loop can be interpreted as an IfcVertexPoint in topological contexts.
conditions: When the poly loop is interpreted as a topological path

subject: IfcPolyLoop
rationale: IfcPolyLoop provides the outer or inner boundary (IfcFaceBound -> IfcPolyLoop) for polygonal faces in IfcFacetedBrep or IfcPolyLoop-based face geometry.
conditions: When used as the boundary of a polygonal face

subject: IfcPolyLoop
rationale: IfcPolyLoop is the fundamental boundary definition used by IfcFacetedBrep to create planar polygonal faces.
conditions: When the faceted B-rep uses polygonal face geometry

subject: IfcPolyLoop
rationale: IfcPolyLoop defines the closed loops that bound each face in an IfcPolygonalFaceSet.
conditions: When defining a set of polygonal faces

subject: IfcPolyLoop
rationale: The concept of a closed polygonal loop underlies indexed polygonal face definitions in IFC.
conditions: When used in combination with coordinate indexing

subject: IfcPolyLoop
rationale: The points in IfcPolyLoop define the extent that can be used to compute a bounding box, though this is an indirect relationship.
conditions: When computing the bounding box of a polygonal shape

subject: IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace
rationale: IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace is a subtype of IfcHalfSpaceSolid, so it depends on the base concept of half-space solids for its definition and functionality.
conditions: When used as a Boolean operand

subject: IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace
rationale: The polygonal boundary is defined by a polyline (IfcPolyline) which provides the 2D shape that bounds the half-space.
conditions: For defining the polygonal boundary

subject: IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace
rationale: The bounding polygon requires a placement coordinate system in 3D space to be correctly located.
conditions: For positioning the polygonal boundary in 3D space

subject: IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace
rationale: The polyline defining the boundary consists of Cartesian points as its vertices.
conditions: As vertices of the bounding polyline

subject: IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace
rationale: IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace is commonly used as a clipping tool in Boolean operations, requiring IfcBooleanClippingResult to perform the actual CSG operation.
conditions: When used in Boolean clipping operations

subject: IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace
rationale: The clipped shapes resulting from polygonal bounded half-spaces can be used to define the geometry of building elements.
conditions: When used to define element geometry via Boolean operations

subject: IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace
rationale: The half-space may be positioned relative to a local placement of the parent element or building structure.
conditions: When the half-space is part of a local coordinate system

subject: IfcPolygonalBoundedHalfSpace
rationale: Polygonal bounded half-spaces can be used to define the subtraction volumes for openings in building elements.
conditions: Used for clipping openings in walls or slabs

subject: IfcPolygonalFaceSet
rationale: IfcPolygonalFaceSet references IfcCartesianPointList3D to define the coordinates of its vertices; the point list is essential for geometric representation.
conditions: When defining vertices for the polygonal faces

subject: IfcPolygonalFaceSet
rationale: IfcPolygonalFaceSet contains a collection of IfcIndexedPolygonalFace entities that define individual faces by referencing vertex indices.
conditions: For defining each face of the polygonal set

subject: IfcPolygonalFaceSet
rationale: IfcPolygonalFaceSet is typically embedded in an IfcShapeRepresentation to provide the geometric shape of a building element.
applicability: The relationship 'connects_to' is vague and not an IFC-specific term. IfcPolygonalFaceSet is used as part of IfcShapeRepresentation only indirectly through IfcTriangulatedFaceSet or other topology items, not directly. The assertion lacks precision about the actual IFC relationship (e.g., IfcShapeRepresentation.Items includes RepresentationItem subclasses).
conditions: When used as part of a product's geometric representation

subject: IfcPolygonalFaceSet
rationale: IfcPolygonalFaceSet serves as the core geometric definition within IfcFacetedBrep, where it defines the polygonal faces of a faceted boundary representation.
conditions: When used to define the boundary of a solid
exceptions: IfcPolygonalFaceSet does not directly support IfcFacetedBrep. IfcFacetedBrep is defined using IfcClosedShell which contains IfcFace(s) - not IfcPolygonalFaceSet. IfcPolygonalFaceSet is a separate representation type (tessellation) under IfcTessellatedFaceSet, not a boundary representation construct.

subject: IfcPolygonalFaceSet
rationale: IfcPolygonalFaceSet is a subtype of IfcRepresentationItem and inherits its core properties for being part of a geometric representation.
conditions: For inheritance of geometric representation capabilities

subject: IfcPort
rationale: IfcPort is the abstract supertype for distribution ports like IfcDistributionPort which connect distribution elements.
conditions: when used in distribution systems

subject: IfcPort
rationale: IfcPort provides connectivity to distribution elements (pipes, ducts, cables).
conditions: as part of a distribution system

subject: IfcPort
rationale: IfcPort requires the relationship object IfcRelConnectsPortToElement to formally define its connection to an element.
conditions: for formal connection relationship definition

subject: IfcPort
rationale: IfcPort depends on IfcRelConnectsPorts to establish logical connections between two ports.
conditions: for defining port-to-port connections

subject: IfcPort
rationale: IfcPort is typically contained within or attached to IfcDistributionFlowElement to allow flow of energy, material, or data.
conditions: when port is part of a flow distribution system

subject: IfcPort
rationale: IfcPort may require IfcRelNests to define aggregation relationships when multiple ports are nested in one element.
conditions: when ports are aggregated/nested within an element
exceptions: IfcRelNests is used for aggregating elements into a nesting structure, but IfcPort is not typically the subject of IfcRelNests. Ports are related to elements via IfcRelConnectsPortToElement and to each other via IfcRelConnectsPorts. The use of IfcRelNests for ports is a non-standard IFC pattern and may only apply in very specific extended schemas or user-defined property sets.

subject: IfcPort
rationale: IfcPort may connect via realizing elements that physically implement the port connection.
conditions: when physical realization is needed for connection

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: An IfcPolyline is defined as a sequence of IfcCartesianPoint coordinates that form its vertices.
applicability: The depends_on relationship is not limited to 'when defining polyline vertices' — IfcPolyline always depends on IfcCartesianPoint because its point list attribute is mandatory, not just when defining vertices. The condition is overly narrow.
conditions: when defining polyline vertices

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: IfcPolyline contains a list of Cartesian points as its vertex coordinates.
applicability: The contains relationship exists regardless of 'when defining the polyline geometry' — IfcCartesianPoint is always contained in IfcPolyline's Points attribute. The condition is misleadingly narrow.
conditions: when defining the polyline geometry

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: Like all IFC geometric representation items, an IfcPolyline depends on placement to be located in the building coordinate system.
conditions: when placed in a building model context

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: The geometric representation context provides the coordinate space and precision for the polyline.
conditions: for being part of a valid IFC model

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: IfcPolyline can be used as the basis for closed polygonal loops in boundary representations.
conditions: when defining closed boundaries

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: IfcPolyline is a simpler form that can be subsumed by indexed poly curves for more efficient representation.
conditions: when representing complex polygonal curves

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: A point on curve can reference a polyline to define a point at a specific parameter along it.
conditions: when parameterized references along the polyline are needed

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: An IfcPolyline can serve as a basis curve that gets trimmed at specific parameter values.
conditions: when the polyline needs to be trimmed to a subset

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: IfcPolyline inherits from IfcRepresentationItem and thus requires that base class's mechanisms for styling and layer management.
conditions: for inheritance of layer assignment and styling

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: IfcPolyline is commonly used to represent annotation curves, outline edges, and dimension lines in architectural drawings.
applicability: IfcAnnotation uses IfcRepresentation which may contain IfcPolyline, but IfcPolyline does not directly 'support' IfcAnnotation. This is an indirect relationship through representation items, and the assertion should clarify the chain.
conditions: when used for 2D annotation lines in drawings

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: Simple building element proxies may use polylines as part of their geometric representation.
applicability: IfcBuildingElementProxy has no special relationship with IfcPolyline beyond any other IfcProduct. Any IfcProduct representation can use IfcPolyline. This assertion is too specific and could mislead about a unique or special relationship.
conditions: when representing generic building element geometry as linear segments

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: A wall's centerline/axis can be defined using an IfcPolyline for segmented or polygonal wall layouts.
applicability: IfcWall axis representation as polyline is a common pattern, but the 'supports' relationship is indirect — through IfcShapeRepresentation. The condition should clarify this is via the representation hierarchy, not a direct relationship.
conditions: when wall axis is represented as a polyline for non-straight walls

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: Slab footprints are often defined by polyline boundaries in plan view.
conditions: when slab outline boundary is defined as a polyline

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: Curved or segmented beams can have their axis represented via polylines.
conditions: when beam axis follows a segmented line path

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: Door swing arcs may be approximated by polylines in some simplified representations.
conditions: when door swing or opening path is shown in plan

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: A polyline can serve as an outer boundary curve, protecting the bounded plane definition from being unbounded.
conditions: when the polyline defines the boundary of a planar region

subject: IfcPolyline
rationale: IfcPolyline provides only piecewise linear segments whereas IfcBSplineCurve provides smooth curvature; they are alternatives for different geometric precision needs.
conditions: when smooth curved geometry is needed instead of linear segments

subject: IfcPostalAddress

subject: IfcPostalAddress

subject: IfcPostalAddress
rationale: IfcPostalAddress provides the mailing address for individuals involved in a building project.
conditions: when the person is a stakeholder (architect, engineer, project manager)

subject: IfcPostalAddress
rationale: IfcPostalAddress supports combined person-and-organization records by providing a postal address.
conditions: when a person is acting on behalf of an organization

subject: IfcPostalAddress
rationale: The address only has context within a project that defines the stakeholders.
conditions: when used within a building information model context

subject: IfcPreDefinedColour
rationale: IfcPreDefinedColour is an abstract supertype; IfcColourRgb is a concrete subtype that requires RGB color definitions to function.
conditions: when defining a pre-defined color by RGB values

subject: IfcPreDefinedColour
rationale: IfcPreDefinedColour is the abstract parent of IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour, which requires standard color names to be defined.
conditions: when using standard named colors for drafting purposes

subject: IfcPreDefinedColour
rationale: IfcPreDefinedColour is used within presentation style assignments to define surface or line colors.
conditions: when assigned to a presentation style

subject: IfcPreDefinedColour
rationale: IfcPreDefinedColour provides color definitions that are referenced by surface shading styles.
conditions: when used as the surface colour property

subject: IfcPreDefinedColour
rationale: Predefined colours can be used to set text color in annotation text styles.
conditions: when defining text color in annotations

subject: IfcPreDefinedColour
rationale: IfcPreDefinedColour is abstract and depends on its concrete subtypes for actual use and instantiation.
conditions: for concrete instantiation via subtypes

subject: IfcPreDefinedColour
rationale: Predefined colours can be used to style elements within presentation layers.
conditions: when colors are assigned per layer

subject: IfcPreDefinedItem
rationale: IfcPreDefinedItem is an abstract supertype for predefined items that typically require an IfcRepresentationItem for geometric representation.
conditions: when used as a predefined type definition

subject: IfcPreDefinedItem
rationale: Predefined items often depend on property set definitions for their attributes and behavior.
conditions: when assigned to an object via property sets

subject: IfcPreDefinedItem
rationale: IfcPreDefinedItem is the abstract parent; IfcPreDefinedColour is one of its specializations.
conditions: when IfcPreDefinedItem is specialized as a colour definition

subject: IfcPreDefinedItem
rationale: IfcPreDefinedTextFont is a specialization of IfcPreDefinedItem.
conditions: when IfcPreDefinedItem is specialized as a text font definition

subject: IfcPreDefinedItem
rationale: IfcPreDefinedCurveFont is a specialization of IfcPreDefinedItem.
applicability: IFC models with curve font definitions
conditions: when IfcPreDefinedItem is specialized as a curve font definition

subject: IfcPreDefinedItem
rationale: Predefined items support presentation style assignments by providing predefined colour, font, or curve definitions.
conditions: when used in presentation style assignments

subject: IfcPreDefinedItem
rationale: IfcPreDefinedItem inherits from IfcNamedUnit and ultimately from IfcRoot in some IFC versions, requiring basic IFC root attributes.
conditions: for object identification and ownership

subject: IfcPreDefinedCurveFont
rationale: IfcPreDefinedCurveFont has concrete subtypes including IfcDraughtingPreDefinedCurveFont, which defines standard curve fonts for draughting purposes.

subject: IfcPreDefinedCurveFont
rationale: IfcPreDefinedCurveFont is used within curve style definitions (IfcCurveStyleFontAndScaling) to define line patterns for graphical presentation in BIM models.
conditions: when assigning a predefined curve font to a presentation style

subject: IfcPreDefinedCurveFont
rationale: IfcPreDefinedCurveFont provides predefined line patterns (e.g., dashed, dotted, continuous) that are referenced by IfcCurveStyle to define the visual appearance of curves in IFC models.
applicability: any IFC model with graphical presentation
conditions: when used for presentation of curve-based geometry

subject: IfcPreDefinedCurveFont
rationale: Predefined curve fonts are used in annotation presentation to distinguish different types of annotations (e.g., hidden lines, center lines) in drawings.

subject: IfcPreDefinedCurveFont

subject: IfcPreDefinedProperties

subject: IfcPreDefinedProperties
rationale: IfcPreDefinedProperties contains predefined property sets like IfcDoorLiningProperties and IfcWindowLiningProperties.

subject: IfcPreDefinedProperties

subject: IfcPreDefinedProperties
rationale: IfcPreDefinedProperties provides the structure for property enumerations used across building elements.

subject: IfcPreDefinedProperties

subject: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet

subject: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet
rationale: As a subtype of IfcPropertyDefinition, IfcPreDefinedPropertySet depends on this abstract class for its foundational structure.
conditions: When used to attach properties to IFC objects

subject: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet
rationale: Predefined property sets contain individual properties (IfcProperty instances) that describe characteristics of building elements.

subject: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet
rationale: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet serves as a predefined, standardized template that supports the definition of property sets for IFC entities.
applicability: The assertion uses 'supports IfcPropertySet' but IfcPreDefinedPropertySet is a subtype of IfcPropertySetDefinition, which is itself a subtype of IfcPropertyDefinition. IfcPreDefinedPropertySet is a specialization, not a 'template' that 'supports' its parent class. The relationship is inheritance/generalization, not a support/template relationship.

subject: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet
rationale: Property sets are connected to IFC objects via the IfcRelDefinesByProperties relationship.

subject: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet
rationale: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet inherits from IfcPropertyDefinition which inherits from IfcRoot, depending on it for object identification and ownership.

subject: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet

subject: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet
rationale: IfcPreDefinedPropertySets commonly contain IfcPropertySingleValue instances as part of their property definitions.
conditions: When the property set includes single-value properties
exceptions: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet is an abstract class and cannot be directly instantiated to 'contain' IfcPropertySingleValue. Only concrete subtypes can contain properties. Additionally, predefined property sets in IFC are typically predefined as fixed schemas and do not always allow arbitrary IfcPropertySingleValue instances — they often have predefined property definitions.

subject: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet

conditions: When the property set includes enumerated properties
exceptions: Same as above: IfcPreDefinedPropertySet is abstract and cannot directly contain IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue instances. Only concrete subtypes can. Moreover, predefined property sets often have fixed enumerated value definitions rather than allowing arbitrary IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue instances.

subject: IfcPreDefinedTextFont

subject: IfcPreDefinedTextFont

subject: IfcPreDefinedTextFont
