subject: IfcPreDefinedTextFont
rationale: IfcPreDefinedTextFont supplies font styling for annotation text occurrences in building information models.
applicability: IfcPreDefinedTextFont does not directly 'support' IfcAnnotation. IfcAnnotation may contain text elements that use IfcPreDefinedTextFont indirectly through IfcTextLiteral and IfcTextStyle, but the relationship is transitive (IfcAnnotation -> IfcTextLiteral -> IfcTextStyle -> IfcPreDefinedTextFont), not a direct support relationship. The assertion oversimplifies the dependency chain.
conditions: when annotations contain text elements with predefined fonts
exceptions: IfcPreDefinedTextFont is not supported by older IFC2x3 coordination view

subject: IfcPreDefinedTextFont
rationale: IfcPreDefinedTextFont contributes to the visual presentation of text within defined planar extents in building drawings.
conditions: when text extent/box dimensions are defined for annotation text

subject: IfcPresentationItem
rationale: IfcPresentationItem is the abstract base type for presentation items that can be assigned to presentation layers via IfcPresentationLayerAssignment. Without layer assignment, they cannot be properly organized in presentation views.
applicability: The assertion uses 'depends_on' but in IFC, IfcPresentationItem is an abstract supertype and does not directly reference IfcPresentationLayerAssignment. Instead, IfcRepresentationItem (a subtype of IfcPresentationItem) is assigned to layers via IfcPresentationLayerAssignment. The dependency relationship is inverted or indirect.
conditions: when defining how presentation items are layered in drawings

subject: IfcPresentationItem
rationale: IfcPresentationItem subclasses use presentation styles (IfcPresentationStyle) to define visual characteristics like colors, hatching, text fonts, and symbols.
conditions: when visual presentation attributes are needed

subject: IfcPresentationItem
rationale: IfcCurveStyle is a subtype of IfcPresentationStyle that can be used by IfcPresentationItem subclasses to define curve presentation properties.

subject: IfcPresentationItem
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyle is a subtype of IfcPresentationStyle that defines hatching and fill patterns used by presentation items.

subject: IfcPresentationItem
rationale: IfcTextStyle is a subtype of IfcPresentationStyle that defines text presentation properties used by presentation items.

subject: IfcPresentationItem
rationale: IfcSurfaceStyle is a subtype of IfcPresentationStyle that defines surface rendering properties for presentation of surfaces.

subject: IfcPresentationItem
rationale: IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle is a subtype of IfcPresentationLayerAssignment that also assigns style information to layers containing presentation items.
applicability: IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle is a subtype of IfcPresentationLayerAssignment, not a separate entity that IfcPresentationItem depends on. The dependency is actually through IfcPresentationLayerAssignment, and the 'with style' variant merely adds style attributes to the layer assignment itself.
conditions: when presentation layer needs visual style assignment

subject: IfcPresentationItem
rationale: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedColour provides predefined colors that can be used by presentation items and their styles for consistent drafting presentation.
conditions: when standard colors are used in presentation

subject: IfcPresentationItem
rationale: IfcDraughtingPreDefinedCurveFont provides predefined curve fonts for presentation items defining curves.
conditions: when standard curve fonts are used in presentation

subject: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment
rationale: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment can be assigned to a presentation layer with style, but IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle is a subtype that specifically adds style capabilities.
conditions: When layer has style information

subject: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment
rationale: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment assigns visual presentation attributes to a collection of IfcRepresentationItem objects, effectively grouping or containing them under a common layer.
conditions: When assigned to a layered representation

subject: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment
rationale: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment often groups geometric representation items for display and organization purposes in CAD/BIM models.
conditions: When assigning geometric representations to layers

subject: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment
rationale: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment provides the base layer assignment mechanism that IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle extends with style information for rendering.
conditions: When additional visualization styling is required

subject: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment
rationale: The layer assignment organizes items that can have styled presentations through IfcStyledItem.
conditions: When presentation styles are assigned to representation items within a layer

subject: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment
rationale: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment may be used alongside style assignments to define visual properties of layers in a model.
conditions: When style information is associated with the layer
exceptions: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment itself does not carry style info

The assertion says IfcPresentationLayerAssignment 'connects_to' IfcPresentationStyleAssignment, but the existing exception already notes that IfcPresentationLayerAssignment itself does not carry style information. In IFC, the connection from layers to presentation styles is handled through IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle (not the base IfcPresentationLayerAssignment). Since the exception acknowledges the base class lacks style info, the connection assertion only holds for the subtype IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle, not for the base class directly.

subject: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment
rationale: By grouping representation items into named layers, IfcPresentationLayerAssignment improves the organization and manageability of product representations in BIM models.
conditions: When organizing product representations into layers for clarity and visualization control

subject: IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle
rationale: IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle extends IfcPresentationLayerAssignment with style information, so it depends on the layer assignment mechanism.
applicability: All building models using presentation layers
conditions: When assigning presentation information to geometric representation items

subject: IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle
rationale: The 'WithStyle' suffix indicates this entity contains presentation style definitions such as colour, hatching, or text styles assigned to the layer.
applicability: All building models with styled layers

IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle contains an attribute 'Styles' of type SET OF IfcPresentationStyle, but this attribute was introduced in IFC2x and may not be present in IFC2.0 or earlier versions. The assertion should be conditioned on IFC2x or later.
conditions: When layer has associated style information

subject: IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle
rationale: Presentation layers typically group geometric representation items for visualization purposes.
applicability: All building models with geometric representations

IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle does not directly depend on IfcGeometricRepresentationItem. The relationship is indirect: IfcPresentationLayerAssignment (the supertype) has a relationship via IfcPresentationLayerAssignment.LayerAssignments which references IfcRepresentationItem, and IfcGeometricRepresentationItem is a subtype of IfcRepresentationItem. This indirect dependency should be clarified.
conditions: When geometric items are assigned to this layer

subject: IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle
rationale: IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle specializes and extends the functionality of IfcPresentationLayerAssignment with additional style capabilities.
applicability: All IFC models with layered presentation
conditions: When layer visibility and style control is needed

subject: IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle
rationale: This entity supports the assignment of presentation styles to geometric items within a layer context.
conditions: When multiple presentation styles are assigned to a layer

subject: IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle
rationale: Presentation layers with styles support the visual representation of building products and their components.
applicability: All building models with product representations
conditions: When product representations need layered visualization

subject: IfcPresentationStyle
rationale: IfcPresentationStyle is an abstract entity that is typically referenced through IfcPresentationLayerAssignment to define how geometric items are visually presented
applicability: all IFC models using presentation styles
conditions: when presentation style is assigned to geometric representation items

subject: IfcPresentationStyle
rationale: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment is used to assign one or more IfcPresentationStyle objects to geometric representation items
applicability: all IFC models using style assignments
conditions: when style is assigned to representations via style assignment

subject: IfcPresentationStyle
rationale: IfcPresentationStyle can be specialized by IfcCurveStyle, IfcFillAreaStyle, IfcSurfaceStyle, IfcTextStyle which all depend on colour definitions like IfcColourRgb
conditions: when a colour-based presentation style is required

subject: IfcPresentationStyle
rationale: IfcPresentationStyle provides visual appearance information (color, texture, line style, etc.) for geometric representation items
applicability: all IFC models requiring visual presentation of geometry
conditions: when geometric items have assigned presentation styles for visualization

subject: IfcPresentationStyle
rationale: IfcProducts use IfcProductDefinitionShape which references representations that may have presentation styles assigned
conditions: when products have shape representations with assigned presentation styles

subject: IfcPresentationStyle
rationale: IfcCurveStyle is a subtype of IfcPresentationStyle, defining visual properties for curves
conditions: when defining curve presentation attributes

subject: IfcPresentationStyle
rationale: IfcFillAreaStyle is a subtype of IfcPresentationStyle, defining visual properties for filled areas
conditions: when defining fill area presentation attributes

subject: IfcPresentationStyle
rationale: IfcSurfaceStyle is a subtype of IfcPresentationStyle, defining visual properties for surfaces
conditions: when defining surface presentation attributes

subject: IfcPresentationStyle
rationale: IfcTextStyle is a subtype of IfcPresentationStyle, defining visual properties for text
conditions: when defining text presentation attributes

subject: IfcPresentationStyle
rationale: IfcPresentationLayerWithStyle extends IfcPresentationLayerAssignment to include presentation style information
conditions: when layers require presentation style information

subject: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment
rationale: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment is an IFC entity that assigns one or more presentation styles (IfcPresentationStyle) to a styled item. It contains references to presentation styles.

subject: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment
rationale: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment can assign curve styles, which are subtypes of IfcPresentationStyle.

subject: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment
rationale: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment can assign fill area styles, which are subtypes of IfcPresentationStyle.

subject: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment
rationale: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment can assign text styles, which are subtypes of IfcPresentationStyle.

subject: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment
rationale: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment can assign surface styles, which are subtypes of IfcPresentationStyle.

subject: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment
rationale: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment is used by IfcStyledItem to provide the set of styles that determine how an element is visually presented.
applicability: Any IFC model that uses presentation/graphical styling of elements
conditions: The IfcStyledItem must reference the IfcPresentationStyleAssignment as its style assignment.

subject: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment
rationale: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment aggregates IfcPresentationStyle instances; without them it has no styling content.
conditions: At least one IfcPresentationStyle must be assigned to the IfcPresentationStyleAssignment to have any effect.
exceptions: If no styles are assigned, the assignment is essentially empty and does nothing.

subject: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment
rationale: The IfcPresentationStyleAssignment itself is often instantiated only in relation to an IfcStyledItem which binds it to a product representation.
conditions: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment is typically referenced by an IfcStyledItem to have meaning in the IFC model.

subject: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment
rationale: Through IfcStyledItem, IfcPresentationStyleAssignment indirectly connects to IfcRepresentationItem, enabling visual styling of geometric representation items.
conditions: Via IfcStyledItem which links IfcPresentationStyleAssignment to IfcRepresentationItem

subject: IfcPresentationStyleAssignment
rationale: In some IFC modeling workflows, IfcPresentationStyleAssignment may be used in conjunction with layer assignments, but this is not a strict dependency.
conditions: When layered presentation is used in the model

subject: IfcProcedure
rationale: IfcProcedure often defines steps within a larger work plan; the plan provides the scheduling context.
conditions: when procedure is part of a scheduled work sequence

subject: IfcProcedure
rationale: Work schedules assign timing to procedures defined in IfcProcedure.
conditions: when time-constrained sequencing is required

subject: IfcProcedure
rationale: IfcProcedure may be composed of or reference IfcTask for detailed work breakdown.
conditions: when procedure is decomposed into discrete tasks

subject: IfcProcedure
rationale: IfcProcedure is a subtype of IfcProcess and inherits its attributes; the process framework is required for proper definition.
conditions: when inheriting process definitions

subject: IfcProcedure
rationale: Sequencing relationships (IfcRelSequence) define the order in which procedures must occur.
conditions: when procedures have predecessor/successor ordering

subject: IfcProcedure
rationale: IfcProcedure supports work control by providing defined steps for execution and tracking.
conditions: as a controlled activity within project management

subject: IfcProcedure
rationale: IfcProcedure can have property sets assigned via IfcRelDefinesByProperties, containing procedure-specific data.
conditions: procedure has associated properties describing its parameters

subject: IfcProcedure
rationale: Assignment relationships link IfcProcedure to the building elements or resources it acts upon.
conditions: when procedure is assigned to products or resources

subject: IfcProcedure
rationale: IfcTypeProcess can define shared procedure type information, which IfcProcedure instances may reference.
conditions: when procedure is typed and uses predefined process type definitions

subject: IfcProcedureType
rationale: IfcProcedureType defines the type information for IfcProcedure entities. A procedure type depends on having actual procedure occurrences (IfcProcedure) to be instantiated.
conditions: When defining procedure types

subject: IfcProcedureType
rationale: IfcProcedureType is assigned to IfcProcedure instances via IfcRelDefinesByType relationship.
conditions: During type assignment

subject: IfcProcedureType
rationale: IfcProcedureType can contain property set definitions (IfcPropertySetDefinition) that define the properties of the procedure type.
conditions: When defining procedure type properties

subject: IfcProcedureType
rationale: Property sets are typically assigned to IfcProcedureType through IfcRelDefinesByProperties relationships.
conditions: When property sets are assigned to the type

subject: IfcProcedureType
rationale: IfcProcedureType provides the template/type definition that supports the instantiation of specific IfcProcedure entities.
conditions: During procedure execution

subject: IfcProcedureType
rationale: Procedure types may be nested using IfcRelNests to define sub-procedures.
conditions: When procedures are nested in a hierarchy

subject: IfcProcess
rationale: IfcProcess is commonly linked to other building elements via IfcRelAssignsToProcess, which assigns processes to products, resources, or controls.
conditions: When establishing process hierarchy or workflow

subject: IfcProcess
rationale: IfcProcess can be sequenced using IfcRelSequence to define predecessor/successor relationships.
conditions: When processes are scheduled in sequence

subject: IfcProcess
rationale: IfcProcess can reference IfcWorkCalendar to define valid working times for tasks.
conditions: When scheduling tasks with working/non-working days

subject: IfcProcess
rationale: IfcTask is a subtype of IfcProcess representing discrete activities in a construction or facility management workflow.
conditions: When modeling a specific task or activity

subject: IfcProcess
rationale: IfcProcedure is another subtype of IfcProcess used to document standard operating procedures.
conditions: When modeling a step-by-step procedure

subject: IfcProcess
rationale: IfcProcess relies on IfcResource (via IfcRelAssignsToProcess) to allocate labor, materials, or equipment needed to execute the process.
applicability: IfcProcess does not directly 'depend_on' IfcResource in the IFC schema. The relationship is mediated through IfcRelAssignsToProcess or IfcRelAssignsToResource. IfcResource is assigned to a process via IfcRelAssignsToProcess, not directly referenced by IfcProcess. The dependency direction and directness are imprecise.
conditions: When processes require resources such as labor, material, or equipment

subject: IfcProcess
rationale: Processes such as installation or manufacturing support the creation or placement of IfcProduct instances.
conditions: When a process produces or modifies a building product

subject: IfcProcess
rationale: IfcProcess can be nested using IfcRelNests, allowing sub-processes to be grouped under a parent process.
conditions: When processes have parent-child (nesting) relationships

subject: IfcProcess
rationale: Processes may be linked to cost schedules to track budget and expenses.
conditions: When processes are associated with cost estimation or budgeting

subject: IfcProcess
rationale: IfcProcess instances are aggregated into IfcWorkPlan to define a complete set of scheduled activities.
conditions: When processes are grouped into a work plan

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcProduct is a subtype of IfcObjectDefinition and is part of the IFC kernel hierarchy, containing all elements that represent physical products or spatial structures.
conditions: When considering product hierarchy

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcProduct is the abstract supertype for IfcElement, which represents physical building elements like walls, beams, columns, etc.
conditions: When considering physical building components

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcProduct includes IfcSpatialStructureElement as a subtype for site, building, storey, and space definitions.
conditions: When considering spatial organization

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcElement subtypes require IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure relationship to be placed within a spatial structure element like IfcBuildingStorey or IfcSpace.
applicability: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure is used for containment of products in spatial structures, but it is not a requirement for all IfcProduct instances. Many IfcProduct subclasses (e.g., IfcProxy, certain IfcElement types) may not have spatial containment relationships in valid IFC models.
conditions: For spatial containment relationships

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcProduct has an ObjectPlacement attribute typically defined by IfcLocalPlacement for positioning within a building coordinate system.
applicability: IfcLocalPlacement is the most common positioning method, but IfcGridPlacement and IfcLinearPlacement are also valid placement types for IfcProduct. The assertion limits positioning to IfcLocalPlacement when other IfcObjectPlacement subtypes exist.
conditions: When absolute or relative positioning is needed

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcProduct has a Representation attribute that typically uses IfcProductDefinitionShape to provide geometric representation.
conditions: When geometric representation is needed

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcProduct inherits OwnerHistory from IfcRoot, required by IFC schema for tracking creation and modification.
conditions: For data provenance and version control
exceptions: When minimal schema compliance is acceptable

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcProduct can be decomposed into sub-products using IfcRelAggregates (e.g., building decomposed into storeys).
conditions: For decomposition of products into sub-products

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcProduct supports material association through IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, linking products to their material definitions.
conditions: When material information needs to be associated with products

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcProduct supports typing via IfcRelDefinesByType to associate occurrence products with their type definitions.
conditions: When type-based product definitions are used

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcElement subtypes can connect to spaces through IfcRelSpaceBoundary, defining physical or virtual boundaries of spaces.
conditions: When products define boundaries of spaces

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcElement (as a subtype of IfcProduct) supports opening relationships via IfcRelVoidsElement for doors, windows, or other voids.
conditions: When openings are created in elements

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcProduct can have property sets (IfcPropertySet) attached via IfcRelDefinesByProperties to store domain-specific attributes.
conditions: When extended attribute data is required beyond base schema

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcProduct includes IfcAnnotation as a subtype for text notes, dimensions, and other non-physical product information.
conditions: When product includes annotations

subject: IfcProduct
rationale: IfcProduct can be associated with spatial structure elements through reference relationships for non-contained elements.
conditions: When referencing spatial context without full containment

subject: IfcProductDefinitionShape
rationale: IfcProductDefinitionShape contains one or more IfcShapeRepresentation instances that define the actual geometric shape.
conditions: When representing product shape in multiple geometric representations

subject: IfcProductDefinitionShape
rationale: IfcProductDefinitionShape is always associated with an IfcProduct via the ProductRepresentation relationship.
conditions: When assigned as the geometric representation of a product

subject: IfcProductDefinitionShape
rationale: IfcProductDefinitionShape has a HasRepresentations attribute that contains one or more IfcShapeRepresentation objects.

subject: IfcProductDefinitionShape
rationale: IfcProductDefinitionShape provides the geometric shape for IfcProduct, supporting its spatial representation.
conditions: When used as the shape representation of a product

subject: IfcProductDefinitionShape
rationale: IfcProductDefinitionShape may reference IfcRepresentationMap for block/cell-based representations.
conditions: When the product shape is defined via a mapped representation

subject: IfcProductDefinitionShape
rationale: Shape representations within IfcProductDefinitionShape may be defined in specific geometric subcontexts.
applicability: IFC models with multiple representation contexts
conditions: When shape representations require specific geometric contexts

subject: IfcProductDefinitionShape
rationale: Multiple shape representations allow different levels of detail for different use cases.
applicability: BIM coordination, clash detection, quantity takeoff

'improves' is not a standard IFC relationship. While multiple shape representations can provide different LODs, the formal relationship is defined via multiple IfcShapeRepresentation entries with different context identifiers, not an 'improves' relationship from the ProductDefinitionShape to the Product.
conditions: When providing multiple Levels of Detail (LOD) for the same product

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: IfcProfileDef relies on coordinate points (IfcCartesianPoint) to define its shape in 2D.
conditions: when defining profile geometry

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: The profile position in the plane may depend on an axis placement.
conditions: when position reference is needed for the profile

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: Arbitrary profile definitions contain curves as their outer or inner boundaries.
conditions: when using IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef or IfcArbitraryOpenProfileDef

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: IfcProfileDef is the abstract supertype; parameterized profiles depend on parameter definitions inherited from IfcParameterizedProfileDef.
conditions: when using a standard parametric profile subtype

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: IfcProfileDef provides the 2D cross-section that is extruded to create IfcExtrudedAreaSolid.
conditions: when used to define the cross-section for extrusion

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: IfcProfileDef provides the 2D profile that is revolved to create IfcRevolvedAreaSolid.
conditions: when used to define the cross-section for revolution

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: IfcProfileDef is the swept area concept used by all swept area solids.
conditions: when used as the swept area in any swept solid geometry

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: Sectioned spine geometry uses IfcProfileDef at cross-section locations.
conditions: when used to define cross-sections along a spine curve

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: Structural analysis often references profile definitions for cross-section properties.
conditions: when defining structural member cross-section properties

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: IfcMaterialProfileSet uses IfcProfileDef to define the shape to which material properties apply.
conditions: when a material is assigned to a specific profile shape

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: The profile's coordinate system may reference the representation context.
conditions: when the profile is used in a geometric representation context

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: IfcProfileProperties can be assigned to IfcProfileDef to hold physical property values.
conditions: when profile properties such as area, moment of inertia are defined
exceptions: IfcProfileDef does not contain IfcProfileProperties directly via containment. IfcProfileProperties has a HasProperties attribute referencing IfcProfileDef (inverse: HasProperties), making this an inverse relationship, not containment. Also, IfcProfileProperties defines extended properties via IfcProperty, not directly the basic properties like area or moment of inertia — those are typically defined via IfcProfileDef subtypes' own computed attributes or via IfcProfileProperties with IfcProperty instances.

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: Beam elements commonly reference IfcProfileDef for their cross-section shape.
conditions: when beam cross-section is defined by a standard or arbitrary profile

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: Columns use IfcProfileDef for their cross-section definition.
conditions: when column cross-section is defined by a profile

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: Steel or timber members cross-sections are defined via IfcProfileDef.
conditions: when structural member profile is defined

subject: IfcProfileDef
rationale: IfcProfileDef is often referenced within IfcShapeRepresentation for geometric modeling.
conditions: when the profile is part of a shape representation

subject: IfcProductRepresentation
rationale: IfcProductRepresentation is an abstract supertype that holds one or more Representations (IfcRepresentation) which define the geometric or topological shape of a product.
conditions: IfcProductRepresentation uses one or more IfcRepresentation objects to define geometric or topological representation

subject: IfcProductRepresentation
rationale: The Representations attribute of IfcProductRepresentation is a list of IfcRepresentation items.
conditions: IfcProductRepresentation contains a set of IfcRepresentation objects via its Representations attribute

subject: IfcProductRepresentation
rationale: IfcProductRepresentation is linked to IfcProduct; the product references a representation for its shape or spatial definition.
conditions: IfcProductRepresentation is assigned to an IfcProduct (or its subtype) via the Representation attribute of IfcProduct

subject: IfcProductRepresentation
rationale: IfcProductRepresentation supports the visualization, analysis, and calculation needs of IfcProduct by defining its shape.
conditions: Provides geometric or topological representation for the product

subject: IfcProductRepresentation
rationale: The representations contained in IfcProductRepresentation rely on a geometric representation context for coordinate space definition.
conditions: Each IfcRepresentation references an IfcRepresentationContext (e.g., model or plan context)

subject: IfcProductRepresentation
rationale: The actual geometric data exists at the IfcRepresentationItem level, which is aggregated within IfcRepresentation held by IfcProductRepresentation.
conditions: Each IfcRepresentation contains one or more IfcRepresentationItem objects

subject: IfcProductRepresentation
rationale: IfcProductRepresentation provides the container for shape representations that define the geometric form of the product.
conditions: IfcShapeRepresentation is a common subtype of IfcRepresentation contained in IfcProductRepresentation

subject: IfcProfileProperties
rationale: IfcProfileProperties is an IFC entity that holds properties associated with a profile definition (IfcProfileDef). It depends on IfcProfileDef as the core geometric profile it describes.
applicability: Any building element using profile-based geometry
conditions: IfcProfileProperties must reference a valid IfcProfileDef instance

subject: IfcProfileProperties
rationale: IfcProfileProperties can contain one or more IfcProperty instances that describe properties of the profile (e.g., area, weight, etc.).
conditions: When IfcProfileProperties has associated property data

subject: IfcProfileProperties
rationale: Profile properties define the cross-section dimensions and structural properties of beams.
applicability: Steel beams, concrete beams, timber beams
conditions: Beam elements using standard or custom profiles

subject: IfcProfileProperties
rationale: Profile properties define the cross-section dimensions and structural properties of columns.
applicability: Steel columns, concrete columns, timber columns
conditions: Column elements using standard or custom profiles

subject: IfcProfileProperties
rationale: Profile properties define cross-section properties of structural members.
applicability: Steel members, truss elements, bracing members
conditions: Member elements using profile cross-sections

subject: IfcProfileProperties
rationale: IfcProfileProperties is a subtype of IfcPropertyDefinition, so it inherits requirements for property definition relationships.
conditions: To be properly instantiated in an IFC data model

subject: IfcProfileProperties
rationale: IfcProfileProperties can be referenced in IfcMaterialProfileSet to associate material properties with profile shapes.
conditions: When profiles are associated with material layering

subject: IfcProject
rationale: IfcProject is the root container that aggregates IfcSite (and optionally other spatial structure elements). Every IFC model must have exactly one IfcProject that contains one or more IfcSite objects.
exceptions: IfcProject does not directly contain IfcSite as a direct attribute. IfcSite is related via IfcRelAggregates (IfcRelAggregates.RelatingObject = IfcProject, RelatedObjects = IfcSite). The 'contains' term is misleading if interpreted as a direct attribute.

subject: IfcProject
rationale: IfcProject can contain IfcBuilding directly or through IfcSite. Building is a core spatial component within a project.
exceptions: IfcProject does not directly contain IfcBuilding as a direct attribute. IfcBuilding is related via IfcRelAggregates (IfcRelAggregates.RelatingObject = IfcSite or IfcProject, RelatedObjects = IfcBuilding). The relationship is indirect through aggregation.

subject: IfcProject
rationale: IfcProject uses IfcRelAggregates relationship to contain spatial structure elements (sites, buildings, storeys).
applicability: IfcProject references IfcRelAggregates as a relation, but does not 'contain' it as a direct attribute. IfcRelAggregates is a relationship entity that connects IfcProject to its spatial structure elements, not a contained child.

subject: IfcProject
rationale: IfcProject requires an IfcOwnerHistory to track authorship, ownership, and modification history of the project data.

subject: IfcProject
rationale: IfcProject contains IfcUnitAssignment to define the measurement units used throughout the project (SI, imperial, etc.).

subject: IfcProject
rationale: IfcProject requires IfcGeometricRepresentationContext to define the coordinate system and precision for all geometric representations in the project.
conditions: Must have at least one 3D model context

subject: IfcProject
rationale: IfcProject depends on representation contexts to establish coordinate systems for geometric model definitions.

subject: IfcProject
rationale: IfcProject uses IfcRelDeclares to declare project-level definitions such as property sets, quantity sets, and material definitions.
exceptions: IfcProject does not directly contain IfcRelDeclares. IfcRelDeclares relates IfcProject to declared entities (property sets, quantity sets, etc.) via RelatingContext = IfcProject. The relationship is inverse - IfcRelDeclares has IfcProject as its RelatingContext.

subject: IfcProject
rationale: Property set templates can be declared at the project level to define standard property definitions used across the project.
conditions: If defined at project level via IfcRelDeclares
exceptions: IfcProject does not contain IfcPropertySetTemplate. IfcPropertySetTemplate is related to IfcProject via IfcRelDeclares (RelatingContext = IfcProject). Only the relationship object is directly involved.

subject: IfcProject
rationale: IfcProject provides the root container and coordinate context that supports the entire building storey hierarchy.

subject: IfcProject
rationale: IfcProject is the top-level container that supports spatial decomposition down to IfcSpace (rooms).

subject: IfcProject
rationale: IfcProject can reference an IfcProjectLibrary to share common type definitions across multiple projects.
conditions: If using library references for shared definitions
exceptions: IfcProject does not contain IfcProjectLibrary. IfcProjectLibrary is a separate root-level entity that can be referenced via IfcRelDeclares, not directly contained by IfcProject.

subject: IfcProject
rationale: IfcProject can contain type definitions for building elements that are shared across multiple occurrences.
conditions: When type definitions are used
exceptions: IfcProject does not contain IfcRelDefinesByType. IfcRelDefinesByType relates an IfcTypeObject to instances, not directly to IfcProject as a container.

subject: IfcProject
rationale: IfcProject as the root spatial container supports the containment relationships that place elements within the spatial hierarchy.

subject: IfcProjectLibrary
rationale: IfcProjectLibrary is a container for project library items, but it does not directly contain IfcProject. However, in IFC schema, IfcProjectLibrary is a subtype of IfcContext and can contain library elements.
applicability: IfcProjectLibrary is contained within IfcProject via IfcRelDeclares (the inverse relationship), not the other way. The 'contains' direction is reversed.

subject: IfcProjectLibrary
rationale: IfcProjectLibrary depends on relationship objects like IfcRelDeclares to associate library elements with the project.
conditions: When library elements are declared within a project context

subject: IfcProjectLibrary
rationale: IfcProjectLibrary can contain or reference IfcLibraryInformation entities that define external library references.
conditions: When library information is associated with the project library

subject: IfcProjectLibrary
rationale: IfcProjectLibrary supports IfcProject by providing reusable library definitions (such as types, properties, and materials) that can be shared across multiple projects.
conditions: When used as a library for a specific project

subject: IfcProjectLibrary
rationale: IfcProjectLibrary can contain type product definitions (e.g., IfcFurnitureType, IfcDoorType) that are reused across projects.
conditions: When type product definitions are stored in the library

subject: IfcProjectLibrary
rationale: IfcProjectLibrary can contain material definitions (IfcMaterial, IfcMaterialLayerSet) for reuse.
conditions: When material definitions are part of the library

subject: IfcProjectLibrary
rationale: IfcProjectLibrary can contain property set templates that define reusable property definitions.
conditions: When property set templates are defined in the library

subject: IfcProjectOrder
rationale: Project orders require work plans to define scheduling and sequencing of tasks.
conditions: when project orders need to be scheduled

subject: IfcProjectOrder
rationale: Work schedules define the timeline for project order execution.
conditions: for time-based planning of project orders

subject: IfcProjectOrder
rationale: Project orders often require cost items to track budgets and expenses.
conditions: when cost tracking is needed for the order

subject: IfcProjectOrder
rationale: Project orders need actors (persons or organizations) to be assigned for responsibility.
applicability: IfcActor is a broad type (organization, person, etc.). The assertion 'requires IfcActor' is overly broad — not all project orders require an actor. In many workflows, project orders can exist without an assigned responsible party until later stages. The condition 'when assigning responsible parties' already suggests this is optional, contradicting the 'requires' semantics.
conditions: when assigning responsible parties

subject: IfcProjectOrder
rationale: Project orders often require approvals from relevant authorities.
conditions: when formal authorization is needed

subject: IfcProjectOrder
rationale: Project orders may depend on referenced documents (specs, drawings, contracts).
conditions: when supporting documents are attached

subject: IfcProjectOrder
rationale: A project order can contain a collection of tasks to be performed.
conditions: when the order is broken down into activities

subject: IfcProjectOrder
rationale: Project orders may contain resources like materials, equipment, or labor.
conditions: when resources are allocated to the order

subject: IfcProjectOrder
rationale: An IfcProjectOrder is always part of a parent IfcProject that provides context.
conditions: as the overarching project context

subject: IfcProjectOrder
rationale: The order relationship is formalized through assignment relationships to controlled objects.
conditions: to associate the order with controlled items

subject: IfcProjectOrder
rationale: Project orders may connect to building service systems via service relationships.
conditions: when the order pertains to building services

subject: IfcProjectedCRS
rationale: IfcProjectedCRS is a subtype of IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem, establishing a parent-child dependency relationship for coordinate definition.
applicability: All projects using projected coordinate reference systems
conditions: When IfcProjectedCRS inherits from IfcCoordinateReferenceSystem

subject: IfcProjectedCRS
rationale: IfcProjectedCRS is used together with IfcMapConversion to convert local engineering coordinates to a projected map coordinate system.
applicability: Projects requiring coordinate transformation between engineering and map coordinate systems
conditions: When converting between coordinate systems

subject: IfcProjectedCRS
rationale: IfcSite can reference IfcProjectedCRS to define its geographic location in projected coordinates.
applicability: Building projects with site location defined in a projected coordinate system
conditions: When IfcSite references a projected CRS for geolocation

subject: IfcProjectedCRS
rationale: IfcProjectedCRS provides the coordinate reference system for building placement within a site.
applicability: All building projects using geospatial positioning

IfcBuilding does not directly reference IfcProjectedCRS; it references it indirectly through IfcSite and IfcLocalPlacement. The assertion implies a direct relationship, but in the IFC data model, IfcBuilding's placement is typically relative to IfcSite's placement, not directly to IfcProjectedCRS.
conditions: When building placement uses projected coordinates

subject: IfcProjectedCRS
rationale: IfcProjectedCRS connects to the geometric representation context to define the world coordinate system used for 3D models.
applicability: Projects with 3D geometric representations tied to real-world coordinates
conditions: When establishing the coordinate context for geometric representations

subject: IfcProjectionElement
rationale: IfcProjectionElement is a subtype of IfcBuildingElement and typically requires a host building element (e.g., wall, slab, column) to be attached to.
conditions: when acting as a structural or non-structural attachment

subject: IfcProjectionElement
rationale: IfcProjectionElement must be related via IfcRelProjectsElement to its host element in the IFC schema.
conditions: for logical connection in IFC data model

subject: IfcProjectionElement
rationale: Projections like pilasters depend on a wall for structural support.
applicability: buildings with masonry or concrete walls
conditions: when used as a wall projection such as a pilaster or corbel

subject: IfcProjectionElement
rationale: Cantilevered projections depend on the slab for structural continuity.
conditions: when used as a slab projection such as a balcony or cantilever

subject: IfcProjectionElement
rationale: Projections can support covering elements like decorative cladding or panels.
conditions: when projection serves as a base or frame for cladding
exceptions: IfcProjectionElement does not directly 'support' IfcCovering in the IFC data model. IfcCovering is typically related to the element it covers via IfcRelCoversBldgElements or IfcRelCoversSpaces, not via IfcProjectionElement. A projection acting as a base for cladding would require IfcCovering to be related to the projected element (e.g., the wall), not to the projection itself. The assertion incorrectly implies a direct relationship between these two entities.

subject: IfcProjectionElement
rationale: Projections may connect to proxy elements in non-standard assemblies.
conditions: when custom or undefined building elements interface with projections

subject: IfcProperty
rationale: IfcProperty instances are typically grouped within IfcPropertySet containers that logically organize properties and link them to IFC objects.
applicability: All IFC models using property-based data
conditions: When IfcProperty is assigned to an object via a property set

subject: IfcProperty
rationale: IfcProperty is designed to be assigned to IFC objects (e.g., walls, doors, beams) to describe their characteristics.
applicability: All building elements, products, and systems
conditions: When property values are attached to a building element, system, or product

subject: IfcProperty
rationale: IfcProperty inherits from IfcPropertyDefinition, which provides the foundational attributes for property definitions.
conditions: In the inheritance hierarchy of IFC data schema

subject: IfcProperty
rationale: IfcPropertySingleValue is the most common subtype of IfcProperty used to hold a single scalar value (e.g., length, width).
applicability: All building components with single-valued properties
conditions: When a property with a single nominal or measured value is needed

subject: IfcProperty
rationale: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue allows a property to hold one or more values from an IfcPropertyEnumeration.
applicability: Components with properties limited to predefined options
conditions: When a property value is selected from an enumerated list

subject: IfcProperty
rationale: IfcPropertyBoundedValue represents a property with a bounded range of values (e.g., nominal min/max).
conditions: When a property is defined by upper and lower bounds

subject: IfcProperty
rationale: IfcPropertyTableValue maps defined values at specified reference points for interpolation.
conditions: When a property is defined by a table of (key, value) pairs or interpolated values

subject: IfcProperty
rationale: IfcPropertyListValue stores a sequential list of values for a single property.
conditions: When a property holds an ordered list of values

subject: IfcProperty
rationale: IfcPropertyReferenceValue enables a property whose value is a reference to another entity.
conditions: When a property references another entity rather than holding a literal value

subject: IfcProperty
rationale: IfcProperty instances, via IfcPropertySet, support the IfcRelDefinesByProperties relationship that links property definitions to objects.
applicability: All IFC models needing object-to-property associations
conditions: When establishing the relationship between objects and property sets

subject: IfcProperty
rationale: IfcComplexProperty can contain multiple sub-IfcProperty instances, forming a parent-child property hierarchy.
conditions: When a property contains sub-properties in a hierarchical structure

subject: IfcProperty
rationale: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue references IfcPropertyEnumeration to define the set of acceptable values.
applicability: Properties using predefined lists of values
conditions: When enumerated property values reference a shared enumeration list

subject: IfcPropertyAbstraction
rationale: IfcPropertyAbstraction is the abstract base class for property definitions in IFC; IfcPropertySet is one of its primary specializations that groups properties.
conditions: when properties need to be grouped into sets

subject: IfcPropertyAbstraction
rationale: IfcComplexProperty is a subtype of IfcPropertyAbstraction that contains nested properties.
conditions: when properties contain sub-properties

subject: IfcPropertyAbstraction
rationale: IfcSimpleProperty (and its subtypes like IfcPropertySingleValue) are direct specializations of IfcPropertyAbstraction.
conditions: when single-value property definitions are needed

subject: IfcPropertyAbstraction
rationale: IfcPropertyEnumeration inherits from IfcPropertyAbstraction and supports defining enumerated property values.
conditions: when predefined enumerations of property values are needed

subject: IfcPropertyAbstraction
rationale: IfcPropertyAbstraction can participate in dependency relationships with other properties.
conditions: when relationships between properties are explicitly defined

subject: IfcPropertyAbstraction
rationale: IfcPropertySingleValue is a subtype of IfcSimpleProperty which inherits from IfcPropertyAbstraction.
conditions: when a property has a single nominal value

subject: IfcPropertyAbstraction
rationale: IfcPropertyBoundedValue is a subtype of IfcSimpleProperty which inherits from IfcPropertyAbstraction.
conditions: when a property is defined with a bound/range of values

subject: IfcPropertyAbstraction
rationale: IfcPropertyTableValue is a subtype of IfcSimpleProperty which inherits from IfcPropertyAbstraction.
conditions: when a property is defined via a table of values

subject: IfcPropertyAbstraction
rationale: IfcPropertyReferenceValue is a subtype of IfcSimpleProperty which inherits from IfcPropertyAbstraction.
conditions: when a property references another entity

subject: IfcPropertyAbstraction
rationale: IfcPropertyListValue is a subtype of IfcSimpleProperty which inherits from IfcPropertyAbstraction.
conditions: when a property has multiple ordered values

subject: IfcPropertyAbstraction
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByProperties uses property sets that contain IfcPropertyAbstraction subtypes to define properties on objects.
conditions: when property definitions need to be assigned to IFC objects

subject: IfcPropertyAbstraction
rationale: IfcPropertyAbstraction subtypes are used within property set templates to define reusable property patterns.
conditions: when reusable property set definitions are created

subject: IfcPropertyBoundedValue
rationale: IfcPropertyBoundedValue is a subtype of IfcSimpleProperty, which inherits from IfcPropertyDefinition. It depends on its parent class definition for proper schema interpretation.
conditions: When used as a property value for property sets

subject: IfcPropertyBoundedValue
rationale: It is typically contained within an IfcPropertySet to associate properties with objects.
conditions: When included within a property set
exceptions: While IfcPropertyBoundedValue can be contained within an IfcPropertySet (via IfcPropertySet.HasProperties), it can also exist independently or within other property containers such as IfcElementQuantity (if part of a complex property). The assertion is generally true but has exceptions for non-property-set contexts.

subject: IfcPropertyBoundedValue
rationale: Bounded values may support enumerations by providing min/max constraints on enumerated property values.
conditions: When defining enumerated ranges

subject: IfcPropertyDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertyDefinition is abstract; its instances (e.g., IfcPropertySet) must be linked to objects via IfcRelDefinesByProperties to have meaning in a model.
conditions: when property definitions need to be assigned to objects

subject: IfcPropertyDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertyDefinition is typically instantiated as IfcPropertySet or IfcPropertySetTemplate, which group individual properties.
conditions: when used as a container for individual properties

subject: IfcPropertyDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertyDefinition serves as a container; concrete IfcProperty instances give it content.
conditions: when the property definition must contain concrete property values

subject: IfcPropertyDefinition
rationale: Property definitions enrich objects with attributes; they support object classification and specification.
conditions: when property sets are assigned to objects via relationships

subject: IfcPropertyDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertyDefinition enables type-level property definitions that standardize object types.
conditions: when defining type-level properties shared across multiple occurrences

subject: IfcPropertyDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertyDefinition (via IfcPropertySet) contains individual IfcProperty instances that hold named values.
conditions: when instantiated as IfcPropertySet

subject: IfcPropertyDefinition
rationale: Property definitions can contain or reference dependency relationships between their properties.
conditions: when dependencies between properties are defined

subject: IfcPropertyDefinition
rationale: Template definitions provide the blueprint for consistent property set structures across a project.
conditions: when using a template-driven workflow for consistent property definitions

subject: IfcPropertyDefinition
rationale: Property definitions at the project level support the overall project information model.
conditions: when project-level metadata and parameters need to be defined

subject: IfcPropertyDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertyDefinition may reference enumerations for property value sets.
conditions: when properties have enumerated values defined

subject: IfcPropertyDependencyRelationship
rationale: IfcPropertyDependencyRelationship is defined in the IFC schema to relate two IfcProperty instances, establishing a dependency between them.
applicability: All IFC models using property dependencies
conditions: When defining property dependencies

subject: IfcPropertyDependencyRelationship
rationale: The dependency relationship can involve property enumerations as either the depending or the depended-upon property.
applicability: All IFC models using property dependencies
conditions: When property values reference enumeration lists

subject: IfcPropertyDependencyRelationship
rationale: Property dependency relationships help define the structure and validation rules within property sets, supporting their correct interpretation.
applicability: All IFC models using property sets
conditions: When property sets include dependent properties

subject: IfcPropertyDependencyRelationship
rationale: Complex properties can contain multiple related sub-properties where dependencies may be defined using IfcPropertyDependencyRelationship.
applicability: All IFC models using complex properties
conditions: When complex properties have sub-properties with dependencies

subject: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue
rationale: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue must be contained within an IfcPropertySet to be assigned to an object in the IFC data model.
conditions: when used as part of a property set definition

subject: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue
rationale: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue references an IfcPropertyEnumeration which defines the list of allowed enumerators (names).
conditions: when referencing a predefined enumeration

subject: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue
rationale: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue provides property data that supports the definition of building elements like IfcWall, IfcDoor, etc.
conditions: when the property set containing this value is assigned to an object
exceptions: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue does not directly support IfcObject. The support chain is: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue is contained in IfcPropertySet (via HasProperties), and IfcPropertySet is assigned to IfcObject via IfcRelDefinesByProperties. The relationship is indirect, not a direct 'supports' relationship.

subject: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue
rationale: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue may relate to an IfcSimplePropertyTemplate that defines the expected property structure.
conditions: when property templates are used for property set definitions

subject: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue
rationale: The enumerated value contributes to the complete property set definition assigned to building objects.
conditions: when used to define a property in a property set
exceptions: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue does not support IfcPropertySetDefinition; it is a subtype of IfcSimpleProperty which inherits from IfcPropertyAbstraction, not from IfcPropertySetDefinition. IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue is a member (part) of a property set, not a definition of one.

subject: IfcPropertyEnumeration
rationale: IfcPropertyEnumeration is a container for a list of IfcProperty objects in IFC schema.

subject: IfcPropertyEnumeration
rationale: IfcPropertyEnumeration is typically referenced within IfcPropertySet definitions for grouping properties.
conditions: when used within property set definitions

subject: IfcPropertyEnumeration
rationale: IfcPropertyEnumeration defines the list of enumerators used by IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue.
applicability: The dependency direction should be reversed: IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue references IfcPropertyEnumeration (via the 'EnumerationReference' attribute), not the other way around. IfcPropertyEnumeration does not depend on IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue; it is referenced by it.
conditions: when defining enumerated property values

subject: IfcPropertyEnumeration
rationale: IfcPropertyEnumeration inherits from IfcPropertyDefinition and contributes to the overall property definition framework.

subject: IfcPropertyEnumeration
rationale: Indirect connection: property enumerations can be linked to classification systems for structured property definitions.
conditions: when properties are classified

subject: IfcPropertyListValue
rationale: IfcPropertyListValue is a subtype of IfcSimpleProperty and typically contains a list of IfcPropertySingleValue or IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue entries as its 'ListValues' attribute according to the IFC schema.
conditions: when representing a list of single values

subject: IfcPropertyListValue
rationale: IfcPropertyListValue can contain enumerated values as part of its list data.
conditions: when representing enumerated property lists

subject: IfcPropertyListValue
rationale: IfcPropertyListValue is typically contained within an IfcPropertySet which groups properties for an object.
conditions: when used as a property within a property set

subject: IfcPropertyListValue
rationale: IfcPropertyListValue is ultimately assigned to an IfcObject (e.g., IfcWall, IfcWindow) to define its properties.
conditions: when assigned to a building element via property sets

subject: IfcPropertyListValue
rationale: IfcPropertyListValue supports IfcPropertySet by providing multi-value property definitions that can describe ranges, lists of allowable values, or historical measurements.
conditions: when providing multiple allowable or measured values for a single property

subject: IfcPropertyListValue
rationale: IfcPropertyListValue inherits from IfcSimpleProperty, which inherits from IfcProperty, which inherits from IfcPropertyDefinition.
conditions: in the context of the IFC inheritance hierarchy

subject: IfcPropertyReferenceValue
rationale: IfcPropertyReferenceValue is a subtype of IfcSimpleProperty that allows referencing a property value defined elsewhere, typically within an IfcPropertySet.
conditions: When IfcPropertyReferenceValue is used to reference a property from another property set

subject: IfcPropertyReferenceValue
rationale: IfcPropertyReferenceValue can reference IfcPropertyEnumeration as its property reference.
conditions: When referencing an enumeration value

subject: IfcPropertyReferenceValue
rationale: IfcPropertyReferenceValue can reference IfcPropertyTableValue as its referenced property.
conditions: When referencing a table value

subject: IfcPropertyReferenceValue
rationale: IfcPropertyReferenceValue can reference IfcPropertyListValue as its referenced property.
conditions: When referencing a list value

subject: IfcPropertyReferenceValue
rationale: IfcPropertyReferenceValue can reference IfcPropertyBoundedValue as its referenced property.
conditions: When referencing a bounded value

subject: IfcPropertyReferenceValue
rationale: IfcPropertyReferenceValue can reference IfcPropertySingleValue as its referenced property.
conditions: When referencing a single value

subject: IfcPropertyReferenceValue
rationale: IfcPropertyReferenceValue can reference IfcComplexProperty as its referenced property.
conditions: When referencing a complex property

subject: IfcPropertyReferenceValue
rationale: IfcPropertyReferenceValue enables property sets to include references to properties defined elsewhere, supporting modular and reusable property definitions.
conditions: When used within a property set definition

subject: IfcPropertySet
rationale: IfcPropertySet is a subtype of IfcPropertyDefinition, so it depends on the parent class for its definition and structure.
conditions: When used as a container for property sets

subject: IfcPropertySet
rationale: IfcPropertySet is specifically designed to contain IfcProperty entities.

subject: IfcPropertySet
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByProperties is the relationship class that associates IfcPropertySet with IFC objects.
conditions: When attaching property sets to objects

subject: IfcPropertySet
rationale: IfcPropertySet provides structured property data to IFC objects (e.g., IfcWall, IfcBeam) through the IfcRelDefinesByProperties relationship.
conditions: When property values need to be assigned to an object instance

subject: IfcPropertySet
rationale: IfcPropertySet inherits from IfcRoot, which provides the core identification (GUID), ownership, and history attributes.

subject: IfcPropertySet
rationale: IfcPropertySet can be associated with IfcPropertySetTemplate to define the expected properties and data types.
applicability: Building information modeling workflows using standards
conditions: When using predefined property sets from standards or building codes
exceptions: Custom ad-hoc property sets do not require a template

subject: IfcPropertySet
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate links IfcPropertySet to IfcPropertySetTemplate.
conditions: When defining property set definitions with templates

subject: IfcPropertySet
rationale: IfcPropertySet can define properties for IfcTypeObject, which then apply to all occurrences of that type.
conditions: When defining type-level properties shared by all occurrences of a type

subject: IfcPropertySet
rationale: IfcPropertySet may contain properties that reference IfcPropertyEnumeration for enumerated values.
conditions: When property values reference predefined enumerations

subject: IfcPropertySet
rationale: IfcPropertySet can be assigned to IfcMaterialDefinition objects to define material properties.
conditions: When materials have associated property sets

subject: IfcPropertySetDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertySetDefinition is a subtype (child) of IfcPropertyDefinition in the IFC schema hierarchy, so it depends on the parent class for inheritance.
conditions: When IfcPropertySetDefinition is a subtype of IfcPropertyDefinition

subject: IfcPropertySetDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertySetDefinition defines a container that groups individual IfcProperty instances (e.g., IfcSingleProperty, IfcComplexProperty) together.
conditions: When the property set contains individual properties

subject: IfcPropertySetDefinition
rationale: The assignment relationship that links IfcPropertySetDefinition to objects is handled via IfcRelDefinesByProperties, so the property set depends on this relationship to be associated with building elements.
conditions: When the property set is assigned to an object

subject: IfcPropertySetDefinition
rationale: Property sets can be defined at the type level (e.g., for IfcWallType) and then inherited by occurrences; this depends on IfcTypeObject for type-based definition.
conditions: When IfcPropertySetDefinition is used as a type property set (via IfcRelDefinesByType)
exceptions: IfcPropertySetDefinition does not truly 'depend on' IfcTypeObject. When used as a type property set, IfcRelDefinesByType links IfcTypeObject to IfcPropertySetDefinition. The property set can exist independently and be defined before being assigned to a type. The dependency direction is more accurately on IfcRelDefinesByType, not IfcTypeObject.

subject: IfcPropertySetDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertySetDefinition provides additional property data to IfcObjectDefinition instances, supporting their semantic description without altering geometry.
conditions: When the property set is assigned to an object (product, process, resource, etc.)
exceptions: IfcPropertySetDefinition does not 'support' IfcObjectDefinition in a general sense. It is only assigned to IfcObjectDefinition via IfcRelDefinesByProperties. IfcPropertySetDefinition itself does not provide functional support to IfcObjectDefinition — it is merely a container of properties that can be associated. The term 'supports' is ambiguous and could imply a capability or interface that does not exist.

subject: IfcPropertySetDefinition
rationale: Predefined property sets can reference IfcPropertySetTemplate to define the expected structure and properties, ensuring consistency.
conditions: When a predefined property set is defined according to a standard template
exceptions: User-defined custom property sets may not use a template

subject: IfcPropertySetDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertySetDefinition can contain IfcComplexProperty instances, which themselves contain further sub-properties, enabling nested data structures.
conditions: When hierarchical or nested property definitions are used

subject: IfcPropertySetDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertySetDefinition directly contains IfcSimpleProperty subclasses such as IfcPropertySingleValue, IfcPropertyEnumeratedValue, IfcPropertyBoundedValue, and IfcPropertyTableValue.
conditions: When individual property values (text, number, boolean, etc.) are defined

subject: IfcPropertySetDefinition
