conditions: When building elements (walls, slabs, doors, windows, etc.) have associated property sets

subject: IfcPropertySetTemplate
rationale: IfcPropertySetTemplate defines the schema/template for IfcPropertySet instances. Without the template concept, property sets would have no defined structure.
conditions: When defining property sets for IFC entities

subject: IfcPropertySetTemplate
rationale: IfcPropertySetTemplate contains property definitions that specify the name, data type, and other attributes of properties within a property set template.
conditions: When templates define individual property definitions

subject: IfcPropertySetTemplate
rationale: IfcPropertySetTemplate acts as a container that defines the set of properties (by name, type, and constraints) that can appear in a property set.
conditions: When the property set template defines one or more properties
exceptions: Empty property set templates may not contain any properties

subject: IfcPropertySetTemplate
rationale: IfcPropertySetTemplate provides the template/blueprint that property sets conform to, ensuring consistency in IFC data exchange.
conditions: When defining the expected structure for a property set

subject: IfcPropertySetTemplate
rationale: IfcTypeObject (e.g., IfcWallType) can reference IfcPropertySetTemplate to define which properties are available for all occurrences of that type.
applicability: All IFC models with typed objects
conditions: When type objects reference property set templates to define their property schema

subject: IfcPropertySetTemplate
rationale: For property templates that specify enumerations as the data type, IfcPropertyEnumeration defines the list of allowed values.
applicability: All IFC models with enumerated properties
conditions: When a property template defines an enumerated value property
exceptions: Not needed for non-enumerated property types

subject: IfcPropertySetTemplate
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate is the relationship entity that links IfcPropertySetTemplate to IfcPropertySet instances that conform to it.
conditions: When establishing the relationship between template and property sets

subject: IfcPropertySetTemplate
rationale: Property templates may reference units, which are defined globally in the IfcProject's IfcUnitAssignment.
applicability: All IFC models with measured properties

IfcPropertySetTemplate does not directly depend on IfcUnitAssignment. Units in property templates are defined at the property template level (e.g., via IfcPropertyTemplate.HasUnit attribute referencing IfcUnit), which is distinct from the project-level IfcUnitAssignment. These are different mechanisms for unit specification.
conditions: When property templates define properties with units
exceptions: When properties are unit-less (e.g., Boolean, text, enumeration)

subject: IfcPropertySingleValue
rationale: IfcPropertySingleValue is always contained within an IfcPropertySet to define a property with a single value.
conditions: When used as part of a property set definition

subject: IfcPropertySingleValue
rationale: IfcPropertySingleValue can participate in dependency relationships to express property dependencies.
applicability: IfcPropertyDependencyRelationship describes dependencies between properties themselves (e.g., one property value depends on another), not a dependency of IfcPropertySingleValue on the relationship entity. IfcPropertySingleValue does not depend on IfcPropertyDependencyRelationship for its existence; rather, the relationship can optionally reference IfcPropertySingleValue instances as related properties.
conditions: When property dependencies need to be described

subject: IfcPropertySingleValue
rationale: IfcPropertySingleValue contributes to defining property sets (IfcPropertySetDefinition) used in building element definitions.

subject: IfcPropertySingleValue
rationale: IfcPropertySingleValue can be used within property sets that accompany IfcElementQuantity definitions.
conditions: When property values represent quantified measures

subject: IfcPropertySingleValue
rationale: Material properties like thermal conductivity or density are often expressed as IfcPropertySingleValue within material property sets.
conditions: When material properties are defined as single values

subject: IfcPropertySingleValue
rationale: Building elements (walls, slabs, etc.) use IfcPropertySingleValue within property sets to define their properties.
applicability: IfcBuildingElement does not directly relate to IfcPropertySingleValue. The relationship is indirect: IfcBuildingElement relates to IfcPropertySet (via IfcRelDefinesByProperties), and IfcPropertySet contains IfcPropertySingleValue. The assertion bypasses the intermediate relationships and is imprecise.
conditions: When element properties are defined using property sets

subject: IfcPropertyTemplate
rationale: IfcPropertyTemplate is used as part of IfcPropertySetTemplate to define property sets for IFC entities.
conditions: when defining property sets for building elements

subject: IfcPropertyTemplate
rationale: Property templates are applied to objects via IfcRelDefinesByTemplate relationships in IFC.
conditions: when property templates need to be associated with objects

subject: IfcPropertyTemplate
rationale: IfcPropertyTemplate is abstract and IfcSimplePropertyTemplate is a concrete subtype that contains simple property definitions.
conditions: when defining single property definitions

subject: IfcPropertyTemplate
rationale: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate is another concrete subtype of IfcPropertyTemplate for composite properties.
conditions: when defining complex/composite property definitions

subject: IfcPropertyTemplate
rationale: Property templates define the structure for property sets that are actually applied to building elements.
conditions: when property definitions are instantiated for building elements

subject: IfcPropertyTemplate
rationale: Some property templates reference enumeration lists for property values.
conditions: when property templates use enumerated property values

subject: IfcPropertyTableValue
rationale: IfcPropertyTableValue is a subtype of IfcSimpleProperty which inherits from IfcPropertyDefinition. It depends on this parent class for its core definition and structure within the IFC schema.
conditions: when used as a property value type in IFC data models

subject: IfcPropertyTableValue
rationale: IfcPropertyTableValue is typically contained within IfcPropertySet to be associated with building elements.
applicability: All IFC building models using property sets
conditions: when IfcPropertyTableValue is assigned as part of a property set

subject: IfcPropertyTableValue
rationale: The table structure can support enumeration-like definitions by defining a set of key-value pairs representing allowable options.
conditions: when tabular values define a lookup enumeration

subject: IfcPropertyTableValue
rationale: Both property types define structured value constraints; they may connect where tables define boundary values for ranges.
conditions: when table values define range boundaries

subject: IfcPropertyTableValue
rationale: IfcPropertyTableValue is attached to building elements via IfcRelDefinesByProperties, enabling the property definition to support element characterization.
conditions: when the property table is assigned to building elements

subject: IfcPropertyTableValue
rationale: IfcPropertyTableValue can be seen as a collection of IfcPropertySingleValue-like entries organized in a table.
applicability: Property definitions with multiple possible values
conditions: when the table is used as an alternative to single value definitions

subject: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition is the abstract supertype for property template definitions; its primary concrete subtypes include IfcPropertySetTemplate. Property templates depend on property set templates for grouping.
conditions: when used to define property templates for property sets

subject: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition can contain IfcSimplePropertyTemplate instances (or other property templates) as part of a property set definition.
conditions: when the template definition is a property set template

subject: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition
rationale: IfcComplexPropertyTemplate is a subtype of IfcPropertyTemplate that can be contained within an IfcPropertySetTemplate.
conditions: when the template definition is a property set template that includes complex properties

subject: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition provides the template/blueprint that structures how actual IfcPropertySet instances should be populated.
conditions: when property templates are used to define the property set structure

subject: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition provides the schema/template for individual property values and their metadata.
conditions: when property definitions are derived from the template

subject: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition
rationale: As the abstract root, concrete subtypes like IfcPropertySetTemplate, IfcSimplePropertyTemplate, and IfcComplexPropertyTemplate are needed for actual use.
conditions: when grouping hierarchical property templates

subject: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition inherits from IfcPropertyDefinition which inherits from IfcRoot, requiring the root-level attributes like GlobalId, OwnerHistory, etc.
conditions: for inheritance of identity and ownership data

subject: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition
rationale: IfcPropertyTemplateDefinition is a subtype of IfcPropertyDefinition, providing template support for property definitions in the IFC schema.
conditions: when providing the template layer for property definitions

subject: IfcProtectiveDevice
rationale: Protective devices are connected via cables to the circuit they protect.

subject: IfcProtectiveDevice
rationale: Protective devices prevent damage to appliances from overcurrents and short circuits.
conditions: when connected downstream

subject: IfcProtectiveDevice
rationale: Protective devices guard cables from overheating due to overcurrent conditions.
exceptions: There are scenarios where a protective device does not protect from a cable segment, such as when the cable is on the supply side (upstream) of the protective device rather than the load side. The assertion 'all installations' is too broad without limiting to downstream cable segments.

subject: IfcProtectiveDevice
rationale: RCDs/GFCI protective devices protect people from electric shock.
conditions: when providing residual current or ground fault protection

subject: IfcProtectiveDevice
rationale: A protective device may contain a tripping unit that triggers the opening of the circuit.
applicability: circuit breakers with electronic or thermal-magnetic trip units

subject: IfcProtectiveDevice
rationale: Protective devices are often assigned to a group for selectivity coordination studies.
conditions: when grouped into a protective device system for selectivity coordination
exceptions: The depends_on relationship between IfcProtectiveDevice and IfcRelAssignsToGroup is expressed backwards. IfcProtectiveDevice depends_on IfcRelAssignsToGroup is unusual - IfcRelAssignsToGroup is a relationship object (a relation entity), not a physical element. Typically it is the group assignment that relates devices, not the device depending on the relationship object itself.

subject: IfcProtectiveDevice
rationale: Protective devices prevent motor damage from overcurrent or phase failure.
conditions: when protecting motor circuits

subject: IfcProtectiveDeviceTrippingUnit
rationale: The tripping unit is a sub-component of a protective device (e.g., circuit breaker).
applicability: The assertion states 'requires IfcProtectiveDevice' but does not specify the relationship type. In IFC, the association could be via IfcRelConnectsElements, IfcRelNests, or IfcRelAggregates. Some implementations allow a tripping unit to reference a protective device through IfcRelAssignsToProduct without being physically contained.
conditions: Typically mounted within or attached to a protective device like a circuit breaker or fuse
exceptions: In IFC4x3, IfcProtectiveDeviceTrippingUnit can be associated with IfcProtectiveDevice through IfcRelAggregates or IfcRelNests, but IFC allows the tripping unit to also be defined as an independent product assembly that is not directly nested inside an IfcProtectiveDevice (e.g., a standalone tripping unit that connects remotely to a protective device via wiring).

subject: IfcProtectiveDeviceTrippingUnitType
rationale: The tripping unit is a sub-component of a protective device (circuit breaker). It is not a standalone entity; it is always embedded in or associated with a protective device.
applicability: The assertion states that IfcProtectiveDeviceTrippingUnitType requires IfcProtectiveDevice, but in IFC4 and IFC4x3, an IfcProtectiveDeviceTrippingUnitType can also be associated with an IfcElectricDistributionBoard or an IfcPanel (via IfcRelAggregates or IfcRelNests) as a sub-assembly, not strictly requiring a protective device. Some tripping units are standalone components mounted in distribution panels.
conditions: Must be assigned to or contained within a protective device (circuit breaker)
exceptions: In some national electrical standards and BIM workflows, the IfcProtectiveDeviceTrippingUnitType may be directly related to an IfcProtectiveDeviceTrippingUnit (the occurrence entity) without an intervening IfcProtectiveDevice, particularly when modeling replaceable trip units in modular circuit breakers at the type level.

subject: IfcPump
rationale: Pumps are typically connected to isolation valves on suction/discharge sides and a check valve on discharge.
applicability: The assertion is stated to apply to 'all building types', but pump-to-valve connectivity varies significantly by building system context. For example, in fire protection systems pumps connect to different valve types (e.g., OS&Y valves) than in HVAC hydronic systems. In some domestic water booster pump configurations, the pump skid may come pre-piped with no distinguishable point-to-point IfcRelConnects relationship between the pump and valve entities. The assertion overgeneralizes the connection pattern across diverse building system types.
conditions: isolation or check valves typically installed

subject: IfcProxy
rationale: IfcProxy is a subtype of IfcRoot, the abstract base class for all IFC entities; it requires this inheritance for basic IFC compliance.
conditions: When used as a valid IFC entity

subject: IfcProxy
rationale: IfcProxy inherits from IfcObjectDefinition, which provides core object definition capabilities.

subject: IfcProxy
rationale: IfcProxy typically requires property sets to define its custom behavior and attributes since it is a placeholder for objects not fully defined in the schema.
conditions: When additional attributes beyond the base class are needed to describe the proxy

subject: IfcProxy
rationale: Every IFC entity including IfcProxy must reference IfcOwnerHistory as part of the IFC data model.
conditions: When the proxy is part of an IFC file

subject: IfcProxy
rationale: IfcProxy often depends on IfcLocalPlacement to define its position in the building model.
conditions: When the proxy represents a spatially located object

subject: IfcProxy
rationale: IfcProxy can contain other objects via aggregation relationships.
conditions: When the proxy is used to group or contain other objects

subject: IfcProxy
rationale: IfcProxy supports the attachment of property definitions via IfcRelDefinesByProperties for custom data.
conditions: When property definitions are attached

subject: IfcProxy
rationale: IfcProxy is typically connected to spatial structure elements via containment relationships.
conditions: When the proxy is assigned to a building story, building, or other spatial structure

subject: IfcProxy
rationale: IfcProxy often depends on IfcProductRepresentation for geometric shape definitions.
conditions: When the proxy needs a geometric representation
exceptions: If the proxy is used for non-geometric metadata only

subject: IfcPumpType
rationale: IfcPumpType is a subtype of IfcEnergyConversionDevice in IFC, meaning pumps are energy conversion devices that move fluids.
conditions: when pump is part of HVAC system

subject: IfcPumpType
rationale: IfcPumpType is categorized under IfcFlowMovingDevice in the IFC hierarchy, indicating it is a device that moves fluids.

subject: IfcPumpType
rationale: Pumps require connected piping (pipe segments) to transport fluid to/from the pump.
applicability: Pumps do not always require IfcPipeSegment; they may connect directly to other equipment, flexible hose connections, or flanged connections to other devices without an intermediate pipe segment. The assertion overly constrains valid pump configurations.
conditions: when pump is part of a piping system

subject: IfcPumpType
rationale: A pump typically depends on a motor connection (either directly coupled or via belt) to convert electrical energy into mechanical rotation.

subject: IfcPumpType
rationale: Pumps support distribution systems (e.g., HVAC hydronic systems, water supply, drainage) by providing the necessary fluid flow and pressure.
conditions: when pump is used for fluid circulation in a distribution system

subject: IfcPumpType
rationale: Pumps are often connected to valves (isolation, check, control valves) to manage flow direction, pressure, and maintenance isolation.
applicability: Pumps do not always connect to valves. In many configurations, especially with inline pumps, there may be no valve directly connected to the pump. The assertion applies unconditionally to all building types and all pump configurations, which is overly broad.

subject: IfcPumpType
rationale: Pumps often connect to storage tanks (e.g., expansion tanks, water storage tanks) for suction or discharge.
conditions: when pump is part of a storage or booster system

subject: IfcQuantityArea
rationale: IfcQuantityArea is an element quantity that belongs to an IfcQuantitySet to define the area property of an element.
conditions: when quantifying building elements

subject: IfcQuantityArea
rationale: IfcQuantityArea quantifies area properties of building elements like walls, slabs, roofs, etc.
conditions: when used in element quantification

subject: IfcQuantityArea
rationale: IfcQuantityArea inherits from IfcPhysicalQuantity which provides the base structure for physical quantities.

subject: IfcQuantityArea
rationale: The area quantity value is typically expressed with units (e.g., square meters) via IfcMeasureWithUnit.
conditions: when area value needs unit assignment

subject: IfcQuantityArea
rationale: IfcQuantityArea provides quantitative data that enriches property sets for building elements.
conditions: when quantities are used to define element properties

subject: IfcQuantityArea
rationale: The quantity includes a unit reference to define the measurement scale (e.g., m², ft²).
conditions: when area is expressed in a specific unit

subject: IfcQuantityArea
rationale: IfcQuantityArea is assigned to elements via IfcRelDefinesByProperties relationship.
conditions: when property/quantity sets are assigned to elements

subject: IfcQuantityArea
rationale: Area quantities often reference spatial context like IfcBuildingStorey or IfcSpace.
conditions: when area is computed per spatial zone or storey

subject: IfcQuantityCount
rationale: IfcQuantityCount is typically associated with IfcElement objects (e.g., doors, windows, columns) to record their count.
conditions: When IfcQuantityCount is assigned to a building element
exceptions: IfcQuantityCount can exist as a standalone property set without an element

IfcQuantityCount may be assigned to a spatial structure element (e.g., IfcSpace, IfcBuildingStorey) rather than only to 'building element' (IfcElement subtypes). The applicability says 'All building element types' but spatial elements are not IfcElement subtypes in IFC.

subject: IfcQuantityCount
rationale: IfcQuantityCount is usually contained within an IfcElementQuantity or IfcPropertySet to be assigned to an element.
applicability: IfcQuantityCount can also be assigned directly to an element via IfcRelDefinesByProperties without being grouped within an IfcPropertySet, which means the dependency on IfcPropertySet is not always present. The condition 'When quantities are grouped within a property set' already qualifies this, so the assertion is correct in that qualified context, but the applicability 'All IFC models' is too broad since the dependency does not hold in models where quantities are assigned directly.
conditions: When quantities are grouped within a property set

subject: IfcQuantityCount
rationale: IfcQuantityCount may appear alongside other quantity types (area, volume, length) within the same IfcElementQuantity.
applicability: The 'connects_to' relationship between IfcQuantityCount and IfcQuantityArea is semantic/conceptual, not an explicit IFC relationship. In IFC, these are independent properties within the same IfcElementQuantity, and there is no explicit connection or reference from one quantity to the other. The nature of the connection is ambiguous.
conditions: When used in the same quantity set for an element

subject: IfcQuantityLength
rationale: IfcQuantityLength as a quantity type depends on IfcMeasureWithUnit to define the unit of measurement (e.g., meters, millimeters) for the length value.
applicability: The condition 'when representing physical quantities with units' is circular reasoning. IfcQuantityLength is itself a physical quantity with a length unit, so the condition does not add meaningful context.
conditions: when representing physical quantities with units

subject: IfcQuantityLength
rationale: IfcQuantityLength typically depends on SI length units (meters) as the standardized unit system in IFC.
conditions: when using the SI system (meters)
exceptions: when using imperial units

subject: IfcQuantityLength
rationale: IfcQuantityLength requires an IfcElementQuantity parent relationship to be associated with a building element.
conditions: when assigned to a building element

subject: IfcQuantityLength
rationale: IfcQuantityLength supports building elements by providing length measurements used for quantities take-off, costing, and analysis.
applicability: 'supports IfcElement' is imprecise. IfcQuantityLength does not directly relate to IfcElement; it is associated via IfcElementQuantity (which aggregates quantities) or directly via IfcRelDefinesByProperties. The assertion should clarify the indirect relationship.
conditions: when quantifying element properties

subject: IfcQuantityLength
rationale: IfcQuantityLength is a subtype of IfcPhysicalQuantity, inheriting its properties and requiring the parent type definition.
conditions: as a subtype relationship

subject: IfcQuantityLength
rationale: Length quantities support construction resource planning by providing data for material quantities like linear meters of piping, cabling, or structural members.
conditions: during construction planning and resource estimation
exceptions: IfcQuantityLength does not support IfcConstructionResource directly. IfcConstructionResource uses IfcPhysicalQuantity via IfcAppliedValue or IfcCostValue, but IfcQuantityLength is not a standard direct relationship. Construction resource quantities typically use IfcQuantityCount or IfcQuantityWeight, not length.

subject: IfcQuantitySet
rationale: IfcQuantitySet is typically associated with an IfcElement via IfcRelDefinesByProperties to provide measured quantities for that element.
conditions: to associate quantities to building elements

subject: IfcQuantitySet
rationale: IfcQuantitySet is assigned to elements through IfcRelDefinesByProperties relationships.
conditions: when relating quantity sets to elements

subject: IfcQuantitySet
rationale: IfcQuantitySet complements IfcPropertySet by focusing on measurable quantities rather than properties. They are often used together but not strictly dependent.
conditions: when quantities and properties are managed together

subject: IfcQuantitySet
rationale: IfcQuantitySet is a container for individual quantity measures like length, area, volume, weight, count, and time.
conditions: when length measurements are defined
exceptions: IfcQuantityLength is contained in IfcQuantitySet only if IfcQuantitySet is realized as IfcElementQuantity. As an abstract type, IfcQuantitySet itself does not contain anything.

subject: IfcQuantitySet
rationale: IfcQuantitySet is a container for individual quantity measures like area.
conditions: when area measurements are defined
exceptions: IfcQuantityArea is contained in IfcQuantitySet only if IfcQuantitySet is realized as IfcElementQuantity. As an abstract type, IfcQuantitySet itself does not contain anything.

subject: IfcQuantitySet
rationale: IfcQuantitySet is a container for individual quantity measures like volume.
conditions: when volume measurements are defined
exceptions: IfcQuantityVolume is contained in IfcQuantitySet only if IfcQuantitySet is realized as IfcElementQuantity. As an abstract type, IfcQuantitySet itself does not contain anything.

subject: IfcQuantitySet
rationale: IfcQuantitySet is a container for individual quantity measures like weight.
conditions: when weight measurements are defined
exceptions: IfcQuantityWeight is contained in IfcQuantitySet only if IfcQuantitySet is realized as IfcElementQuantity. As an abstract type, IfcQuantitySet itself does not contain anything.

subject: IfcQuantitySet
rationale: IfcQuantitySet is a container for individual quantity measures like count.
conditions: when count measurements are defined
exceptions: IfcQuantityCount is contained in IfcQuantitySet only if IfcQuantitySet is realized as IfcElementQuantity. As an abstract type, IfcQuantitySet itself does not contain anything.

subject: IfcQuantitySet
rationale: IfcQuantitySet is a container for individual quantity measures like time.
conditions: when time measurements are defined
exceptions: IfcQuantityTime is contained in IfcQuantitySet only if IfcQuantitySet is realized as IfcElementQuantity. As an abstract type, IfcQuantitySet itself does not contain anything.

subject: IfcQuantitySet
rationale: IfcQuantitySet is defined within the context of an IfcProject which provides global units and project standards.
conditions: for project-level definitions and units

subject: IfcQuantityTime
rationale: IfcQuantityTime stores time-related quantities, which are typically associated with tasks (IfcTask) for scheduling and work planning.
conditions: when time quantities are used to measure task duration

subject: IfcQuantityTime
rationale: IfcQuantityTime must be associated with an element through IfcRelDefinesByProperties (or equivalent property definition relationship) to have context.
applicability: IfcQuantityTime can also be attached via IfcRelDefinesByTemplate (for type products) or directly via IfcRelDefinesByProperties only for occurrences. The assertion does not account for the IfcRelDefinesByTemplate scenario used with element types.
conditions: when attached to an element as a property set

subject: IfcQuantityTime
rationale: Time quantities (e.g., hours worked) support resource allocation and costing for construction resources.
applicability: IfcQuantityTime also supports IfcTask and IfcProcess as primary contexts, not just IfcConstructionResource. The assertion over-narrows the purpose to construction resource quantification only, whereas IfcQuantityTime is a general quantity type usable in any scheduling or process context.
conditions: when quantifying labor or equipment usage time

subject: IfcQuantityTime
rationale: IfcQuantityTime can be part of IfcQuantitySet (or custom quantity sets) alongside other quantity types (length, area, volume, etc.).
conditions: when grouped with other quantities in a quantity set

subject: IfcQuantityTime
rationale: Work plans use time quantities to define activity durations and sequence logic.
conditions: when time quantities define durations of work activities

subject: IfcQuantityTime
rationale: Time quantities rely on unit definitions (e.g., TIMEUNIT, hours, minutes) to be interpretable correctly.
conditions: when a specific time unit (e.g., hours, days) needs to be explicitly defined

subject: IfcQuantityVolume
rationale: IfcQuantityVolume is typically embedded in an IfcPropertySet that groups properties for an element.
applicability: IfcQuantityVolume does not always depend on IfcPropertySet. In IFC, quantities can be assigned directly via IfcElementQuantity without being contained in an IfcPropertySet. The condition correctly identifies one path, but the assertion could mislead into thinking this dependency is mandatory in all cases.
conditions: when volume quantity is defined within a property set

subject: IfcQuantityVolume
rationale: IfcQuantityVolume is a quantity that measures volume of an IfcElement (e.g., wall, slab, beam).
conditions: when assigned as a quantity for a building element

subject: IfcQuantityVolume
rationale: IfcQuantityVolume is a subtype of IfcPhysicalQuantity; it requires the base class definition to function in the schema.

subject: IfcQuantityVolume
rationale: While IfcElementQuantity contains IfcQuantityVolume, the volume quantity also supports the element quantity by providing specific measurement data.

subject: IfcQuantityVolume
rationale: The quantity must be associated with an IfcObjectDefinition or its subtypes to be meaningful in the IFC model.
conditions: when attached to any building object via property sets

subject: IfcQuantityVolume
rationale: The relationship object that attaches property sets (containing quantities) to elements.
conditions: when linking quantities to building elements through property set relationships

subject: IfcQuantityWeight
rationale: IfcQuantityWeight is typically part of an IfcQuantitySet that groups quantities for a building element.
conditions: when defining measurable attributes of building elements

subject: IfcQuantityWeight
rationale: IfcQuantityWeight is used to measure the weight of an IfcElement like a beam, column, slab, etc.
conditions: when quantifying the weight of a physical building component

subject: IfcQuantityWeight
rationale: Weight quantities are essential inputs for structural analysis models to compute dead loads.
conditions: when performing structural load calculations

subject: IfcQuantityWeight
rationale: Weight quantities can be used to derive material quantities for cost estimation.
conditions: when estimating material costs based on weight

subject: IfcQuantityWeight
rationale: Weight information helps size transport elements for moving heavy components.
conditions: when calculating load capacity requirements for hoists, cranes, or conveyors

subject: IfcQuantityWeight
rationale: IfcQuantityWeight inherits from IfcPropertyDefinition, so it depends on that base class.
conditions: when the quantity weight is part of a property definition relationship

subject: IfcRailing
rationale: A handrail is often an integral part of a railing system to provide gripping support for users.
conditions: Required for railings on stairs, ramps, and elevated walkways
exceptions: Some decorative railings without handrail function

Building codes such as IBC and ADA allow handrail exceptions on stairs with fewer than 4 risers or where stair width is very narrow. The assertion does not account for code-based exceptions where a handrail is not required even on stairs.

subject: IfcRailing
rationale: Stair railings physically connect to and run along the edge of stair flights.
conditions: When railing is installed along a stair
exceptions: Railings not associated with stairs

subject: IfcRailing
rationale: Ramp railings connect to and run alongside ramp surfaces.
conditions: When railing is installed on a ramp
exceptions: Railings not associated with ramps

subject: IfcRailing
rationale: Railings often connect to walls at their ends or along their length for support.
conditions: When railing terminates at or is mounted to a wall
exceptions: Freestanding railings

When a railing connects to a wall but also extends to a post or newel at a corner or turn, the primary structural connection may be to the post rather than directly to the wall. The assertion overstates connection to wall when post-mediated connections exist.

subject: IfcRailingType
rationale: Railing systems are typically fastened to the building structure using bolts, anchors, brackets or similar connectors.
applicability: The assertion states 'IfcRailingType requires IfcFastener' but the existing exceptions already note that cast-in-place or welded connections may not need discrete fasteners. This significantly undercuts the assertion's general validity - if entire common construction methods don't require fasteners, the condition 'when mechanical fixing is used' should be promoted from condition to a core part of the assertion, not just a condition. The assertion as stated is misleading because it presents a general requirement that is only true for a subset of railing installations.
conditions: when mechanical fixing is used
exceptions: cast-in-place or welded connections may not need discrete fasteners

subject: IfcRailingType
rationale: IfcRailingType is the type definition that can contain occurrences of IfcRailing in the model.

subject: IfcRailingType
rationale: A railing type typically includes handrails as a sub-component providing hand grasp support.
conditions: when railing type includes handrail component
exceptions: some guardrails may not have handrails

subject: IfcRailingType
rationale: Railing types often include guardrails to prevent falls from elevated surfaces.
conditions: when railing serves edge protection function

subject: IfcRailingType
rationale: Many railing types contain balusters (vertical spindles/pickets) as infill between top rail and bottom rail/base.
conditions: when railing has vertical infill design
exceptions: glass panel or solid panel railings may not have balusters

subject: IfcRailingType
rationale: Railings are typically connected physically to floor slabs, balcony slabs, or roof slabs at their base.
conditions: when mounted on floor/balcony slab
exceptions: stair railings connect to stair structure

subject: IfcRailingType
rationale: Handrails and stair guards are physically connected to stair flights or landings.
conditions: when installed along stairs
exceptions: guardrails on balconies do not connect to stairs

The existing exception acknowledges guardrails on balconies don't connect to stairs, but there are additional missing exceptions: railings on ramps (accessible paths) may connect to IfcRamp rather than IfcStair, and railing systems that wrap around a stair opening but are floor-mounted on the landing connect to IfcSlab, not IfcStair. Also, spiral stairs and curved monumental stairs may have different connection behaviors not covered.

subject: IfcRailingType
rationale: Wall-mounted handrails are physically attached to adjacent walls for support and lateral stability.
conditions: when railing is wall-mounted
exceptions: freestanding railings do not connect to walls

The assertion fails to account for railings that are both wall-mounted and floor-mounted (e.g., wall-mounted handrails that also have balusters landing on a stair tread or slab). These hybrid installations connect to both walls and slabs/stairs simultaneously, not just walls. The existing exception only covers freestanding railings, missing this mixed connection scenario.

subject: IfcRailingType
rationale: Railing type definition requires material specification (steel, wood, glass, aluminum, etc.) for its realization.
conditions: for fabrication of railing components

subject: IfcRamp
rationale: Ramps are attached to the building and need a foundation for stability.
conditions: Must be stable and level

subject: IfcRamp
rationale: In many buildings, a ramp connects different floor levels and depends on slab connections.
applicability: The assertion says IfcRamp 'depends_on Slab' but this is not an IFC schema-level dependency. In many building contexts (e.g., exterior ramps on grade, or ramps on structural beams/framing), the ramp does not depend on a slab. The condition 'ramp often integrates with floor slabs' does not justify a 'depends_on' relationship; it should be 'may_connect_to' or similar.
conditions: Ramp often integrates with floor slabs

subject: IfcRamp
rationale: Ramps require landings for safe entry, exit, and turning.
conditions: Required at top, bottom, and at direction changes
exceptions: In IFC, a simple straight ramp connecting two level surfaces (e.g., a curb ramp or threshold ramp) does not necessarily require an IfcLanding entity. Landings are required for changes in direction or significant height changes, but very short ramps or those with a single continuous slope may have no separate landing element.

subject: IfcRamp
rationale: Handrails provide safety and support for ramp users.
conditions: When slope exceeds 1:20 or required by code

subject: IfcRamp
rationale: Guardrails prevent falls from the sides of the ramp.
applicability: All building types with elevated ramps
conditions: When ramp is elevated or adjacent to a drop
exceptions: Guardrails are not universally required for all elevated ramps. Ramps with very low elevation (e.g., a single step-up ramp of 6 inches) or ramps bounded by walls on both sides may not require guardrails. The condition 'when ramp is elevated or adjacent to a drop' is vague — many building codes allow curb-like barriers instead of guardrails for low elevations.

subject: IfcRamp
rationale: Ramps require more horizontal space than stairs for the same vertical rise.
applicability: In IFC, IfcRamp and IfcStair do not inherently 'conflict_with' each other at the schema level — they are both subtypes of IfcBuildingElement and can coexist in the same model. The intent (space conflict) is a design/coordination issue, not an IFC relationship. This assertion appears to conflate a spatial design constraint with an IFC entity relationship.
conditions: When space is limited

subject: IfcRampFlight
rationale: The ramp flight supports must transfer loads to a foundation system.
exceptions: Prefabricated ramp flight sections may be self-supporting on level ground

subject: IfcRampFlight
rationale: Ramp flights typically connect to landings at top and bottom for safe transition and accessibility.
conditions: When ramp flight connects multiple levels or changes direction
exceptions: Single continuous ramp between two levels without intermediate landing

subject: IfcRampFlight
rationale: IfcRampFlight is a sub-component of IfcRamp in IFC schema, representing a continuous segment of a ramp.

subject: IfcRampFlightType
rationale: Ground-supported ramp flights require a foundation to distribute loads to the soil.
applicability: The assertion states 'IfcRampFlightType requires Foundation' but this conflates the type definition (IfcRampFlightType) with the occurrence (IfcRampFlight). The type entity does not physically require a foundation; it is the individual ramp flight occurrence that may require one. Additionally, in IFC, foundation relationships are typically modeled via IfcRelConnectsElements or containment, not as a type-level requirement.
conditions: When ramp flight is ground-bearing
exceptions: Suspended ramp flights may not require direct foundation contact

subject: IfcRampFlightType
rationale: Handrails are typically mounted on or adjacent to ramp flights to provide support and safety for users.
conditions: For safety and code compliance
exceptions: Very short or low-slope ramps may not require handrails

subject: IfcRampFlightType
rationale: Ramp flights often connect to floor slabs at their start and end points.
applicability: Similar to the foundation assertion, IfcRampFlightType (the type object) does not have physical connections; connections occur at the occurrence level (IfcRampFlight). Stating that a type 'connects_to' another type misrepresents the IFC relationship structure.
conditions: When ramp terminates at a floor level
exceptions: The assertion that IfcRampFlightType connects_to IfcSlab when the ramp terminates at a floor level does not account for ramps that terminate directly at grade (ground level) without a slab, such as exterior ramps transitioning from a building entrance to natural ground.

subject: IfcRampFlightType
rationale: Ramp flights may be flanked by walls that provide lateral support or enclosure.
applicability: The assertion says IfcRampFlightType connects_to IfcWall when bounded by walls, but in IFC, ramp flights that are bounded by walls are typically related via spatial containment (IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure) or adjacency, not a direct connection relationship. 'Connects_to' implies a physical connection which may not be semantically correct when walls merely bound the ramp without structural connection.
conditions: When ramp is bounded by walls
exceptions: The assertion does not account for ramps that are bounded by guardrails, balustrades, or other non-wall elements instead of walls. In many ramp designs, the bounding element is a handrail/guardrail system, not an IfcWall.

subject: IfcRampType
rationale: IfcRampType defines the type information for IfcRamp occurrences; the ramp itself is the physical component instantiated from the type.
conditions: when the ramp type includes a structural flight

subject: IfcRampType
rationale: Ramp types often aggregate ramp flight types for the sloped walking surface segments.
conditions: when the ramp consists of one or more flights
exceptions: single-flight ramps may reference a combined definition

The existing exception mentions 'single-flight ramps may reference a combined definition' but the assertion still says IfcRampType depends_on IfcRampFlightType unconditionally. A single-flight ramp type that uses a combined definition (e.g., IfcRampType.PREFABRICATED) may not reference IfcRampFlightType at all.

subject: IfcRampType
rationale: Ramp landings are commonly represented by slab elements that provide level resting platforms.
conditions: for landings at top and bottom of ramp flights

subject: IfcRampType
rationale: A ramp type may reference material definitions for construction specification.
conditions: if the ramp type specifies a material composition

subject: IfcRampType
rationale: The IFC schema uses IfcRelDefinesByType to link occurrences to their type definition.
applicability: all BIM workflows using type definitions
conditions: when instantiating ramp occurrences from the type

subject: IfcRampType
rationale: Ramps often serve as accessible alternatives alongside stairs, but they don't structurally support stair flights.
conditions: in mixed stair/ramp circulation systems where the ramp supports accessibility adjacent to stairs

subject: IfcRampType
rationale: Railing types are often associated with ramp types to provide fall protection and user support.
conditions: when guardrails or handrails are required by code on the ramp
exceptions: ramps with very low rise may not require railings

The assertion says IfcRampType protects_from IfcRailingType, but the existing exception only mentions 'ramps with very low rise' may not require railings. Additional exceptions include: interior ramps not open to the public, ramps bounded by walls on both sides, and ramps with a combined curb/railing solution that uses a different Ifc element type (e.g., IfcWall).

subject: IfcRampType

subject: IfcRampType

subject: IfcRationalBSplineCurveWithKnots
rationale: The curve's position in the building model depends on the placement context (ObjectPlacement) typically provided through its parent IfcProduct or IfcRepresentation.
applicability: All building elements referencing this curve
conditions: When the curve is placed in 3D space

subject: IfcRationalBSplineCurveWithKnots
rationale: The curve must be interpreted within a geometric representation context that defines coordinate system, precision, and units.
conditions: For the coordinate system and precision

subject: IfcRationalBSplineCurveWithKnots
rationale: Rational B-spline curves with knots can serve as basis curves for trimmed curves, enabling partial curve segments to be used for modeling.
applicability: Complex curved geometries in building models
conditions: When the rational B-spline is used as a basis curve for trimming

subject: IfcRationalBSplineCurveWithKnots
rationale: The curve can serve as a directrix (centerline) for swept solids along a surface, enabling complex 3D building geometry.
applicability: Swept geometry elements like curved walls, rails, or beams
conditions: When used as a directrix for swept solids

subject: IfcRationalBSplineCurveWithKnots
rationale: B-spline curves often act as boundary curves or iso-parametric curves for corresponding B-spline surfaces.
conditions: When the curve is used in surface definition via boundary representation

subject: IfcRationalBSplineCurveWithKnots
rationale: The control points of the B-spline curve are represented as a list of IfcCartesianPoint instances defining the polygon vertices.
applicability: All IFC models using this entity
conditions: Always, as control points are Cartesian points

subject: IfcRationalBSplineCurveWithKnots
rationale: The curve can define the geometry of an edge in a topological edge curve representation.
applicability: IfcRationalBSplineCurveWithKnots connects_to IfcEdgeCurve is imprecise. IfcEdgeCurve references an IfcCurve via its EdgeGeometry attribute, so the direction of relationship is IfcEdgeCurve -> IfcCurve (from topology to geometry), not the reverse. While a B-spline curve can be the EdgeGeometry of an IfcEdgeCurve, it is more accurate to say IfcEdgeCurve references IfcRationalBSplineCurveWithKnots rather than the curve 'connecting to' the edge. The wording implies a bidirectional connection where none exists in the schema.
conditions: When the curve defines an edge in a topological model

subject: IfcRationalBSplineSurfaceWithKnots
rationale: IfcRationalBSplineSurfaceWithKnots is a subtype of IfcBSplineSurface, inheriting its properties and requiring its parent concept for its definition.
conditions: when representing rational B-spline surfaces

subject: IfcRationalBSplineSurfaceWithKnots
rationale: In IFC, all geometric representations depend on a representation context for coordinate system and geometric interpretation.
conditions: when placed in a geometric model context

subject: IfcRationalBSplineSurfaceWithKnots
rationale: Control points are defined using Cartesian points in 3D space, which IfcRationalBSplineSurfaceWithKnots depends on.
conditions: for defining control points

subject: IfcRectangleProfileDef

subject: IfcRectangleProfileDef

subject: IfcRectangleProfileDef

subject: IfcRectangleProfileDef

subject: IfcRectangleProfileDef

subject: IfcRectangleProfileDef

conditions: when beam has a rectangular cross-section

subject: IfcRectangleProfileDef

subject: IfcRectangleProfileDef

subject: IfcRectangleProfileDef

subject: IfcRectangularPyramid

subject: IfcRectangularPyramid

subject: IfcRectangularTrimmedSurface
rationale: IfcRectangularTrimmedSurface is a subtype of IfcBoundedSurface and trims a base surface (IfcSurface) with rectangular boundaries in parametric space.

subject: IfcRectangularTrimmedSurface

conditions: when defining trimming boundaries in parametric space
exceptions: The trimming boundaries for IfcRectangularTrimmedSurface are defined by two u and two v parameter values (u1, u2, v1, v2) selected from the base surface's parametric range, not by IfcCurve objects. This differs from IfcTrimmedCurve which does use IfcCurve for trimming. In parametric space trimming, curves are not involved - only scalar parameter values.

subject: IfcRectangularTrimmedSurface

subject: IfcRegularTimeSeries

subject: IfcRegularTimeSeries

exceptions: IfcRegularTimeSeries and IfcIrregularTimeSeries are mutually exclusive subtypes of IfcTimeSeries, not containment

subject: IfcRegularTimeSeries
rationale: Regular time series data can be used to record performance history such as energy consumption, temperature readings, or equipment operation over regular intervals.
applicability: IfcRegularTimeSeries is a subtype of IfcTimeSeries and can be referenced by any object that has a reference to IfcTimeSeries, not just IfcPerformanceHistory. This is an overly narrow assertion. IfcPerformanceHistory may use IfcRegularTimeSeries via IfcRelAssignsToControl, but many other IFC entities can also reference time series data.
conditions: when recording time-based performance data of a building element or system

subject: IfcRegularTimeSeries
rationale: Regular time series data is commonly used to store periodic sensor readings (e.g., temperature every 5 minutes).
conditions: when sensor readings are taken at regular intervals

subject: IfcRegularTimeSeries
rationale: IfcRegularTimeSeries can provide time-dependent property values for building elements.
applicability: IfcBuildingElementProxy is a generic proxy element; its support for IfcRegularTimeSeries is indirect through property sets and relational associations, not a direct 'supports' relationship. Time-varying properties are stored in IfcPropertySet which may reference IfcTimeSeries, but IfcBuildingElementProxy itself doesn't directly support IfcRegularTimeSeries.
conditions: when used to store time-varying properties of an element

subject: IfcRegularTimeSeries
rationale: IfcRegularTimeSeries is often assigned to building elements through IfcPropertySet and IfcPropertySingleValue or IfcPropertyBoundedValue.
applicability: The 'depends_on' relationship is vague. IfcRegularTimeSeries does not depend on IfcPropertySet for its existence or definition. An IfcRegularTimeSeries can exist independently. However, IfcTimeSeries can be assigned as a property value within an IfcPropertySet via IfcPropertySingleValue. The dependency is only in the specific usage context where the time series is used as a property value, not a general dependency.
conditions: when the time series is associated as a property value

subject: IfcReinforcementDefinitionProperties
rationale: IfcReinforcementDefinitionProperties defines properties for reinforcement arrangement and typically applies to structural connections like beam-column joints or foundation connections.
conditions: when defining reinforcement for structural elements

subject: IfcReinforcementDefinitionProperties
rationale: The properties defined relate to reinforcing bar parameters such as spacing, quantity, and arrangement.
applicability: all building types with reinforced concrete
conditions: when specifying reinforcement layout

subject: IfcReinforcementDefinitionProperties
rationale: Reinforcement definition properties can also apply to welded wire mesh.
conditions: when defining mesh reinforcement properties

subject: IfcReinforcementDefinitionProperties
rationale: This property set is designed to define properties of reinforcing elements broadly.
conditions: general

subject: IfcReinforcementDefinitionProperties
rationale: The reinforcement properties are assigned to structural members to define their reinforcement configuration.
conditions: when assigning reinforcement properties to beams, columns, slabs or walls

subject: IfcReinforcementDefinitionProperties
rationale: IfcReinforcementDefinitionProperties is itself a subtype of IfcPropertySetDefinition, connecting to the broader property set framework.
conditions: as a subtype of property set definition

subject: IfcReinforcementDefinitionProperties
rationale: Material properties of the reinforcement (yield strength, grade) are needed to fully define reinforcement.

subject: IfcReinforcementBarProperties
rationale: IfcReinforcementBarProperties defines steel bar characteristics for IfcReinforcingBar or IfcReinforcingBarType entities.
conditions: when assigning properties to a specific reinforcing bar type or instance

subject: IfcReinforcementBarProperties
rationale: The property set is often assigned to an IfcReinforcingBarType to define standard bar specifications.
conditions: when used as a type product property set

subject: IfcReinforcementBarProperties
rationale: As a property set, IfcReinforcementBarProperties requires IfcRelDefinesByProperties to be associated with the reinforcing bar element or type.
conditions: when establishing relationship between property set and the reinforcing element

subject: IfcReinforcementBarProperties
rationale: In some IFC schemas, IfcReinforcementBarProperties is referenced from IfcReinforcementDefinitionProperties.
conditions: when used within a broader reinforcement definition context

subject: IfcReinforcementBarProperties
rationale: IfcReinforcementBarProperties can support the definition of reinforcing mesh properties.
applicability: IfcReinforcementBarProperties is specifically designed for bar reinforcement properties (bar diameter, cross-section area, steel grade, etc.). IfcReinforcingMesh uses IfcReinforcementMeshProperties (or the more general IfcReinforcementBarProperties in early IFC versions). The assertion that IfcReinforcementBarProperties 'supports' IfcReinforcingMesh needs clarification — in IFC4+, IfcReinforcementMeshProperties is the correct property set for welded wire mesh and IfcReinforcementBarProperties may not be appropriate.
conditions: when defining properties for welded wire mesh

subject: IfcReinforcementBarProperties
rationale: Reinforcement steel may be linked to an IfcMaterial definition for consistency.
conditions: when steel material is referenced through material association
exceptions: properties may be defined without separate material entity if steel grade is embedded as a property value

While steel grade can be embedded as a property value, IfcReinforcementBarProperties itself has a direct attribute 'SteelGrade' (in IFC2x3) which makes the dependency on IfcMaterial unnecessary when steel grade is defined inline within the property set. The assertion states a dependency that is optional at best and not a hard requirement.

subject: IfcReinforcingBar
rationale: Reinforcing bars require mesh or stirrups for shear reinforcement and to hold bars in position during concrete placement.
conditions: when used as primary reinforcement

subject: IfcReinforcingBar
rationale: Concrete cover (IfcCovering) protects rebar from corrosion and fire, and is essential for structural durability.
applicability: all concrete elements exposed to environment

The assertion that IfcReinforcingBar depends_on IfcCovering for durability and fire protection is overly broad. In many structural elements (e.g., interior beams, columns in conditioned spaces, foundations below grade), the concrete cover itself provides durability and fire protection, not a separate IfcCovering element. IfcCovering in IFC typically represents finishes like plaster, tiles, or cladding, not the concrete cover zone.
conditions: for durability and fire protection
exceptions: temporary works

subject: IfcReinforcingBar
rationale: Reinforcing bars provide tensile reinforcement within concrete slabs, enabling them to resist bending moments.
conditions: when embedded in reinforced concrete slabs

subject: IfcReinforcingBar
rationale: Rebars are placed longitudinally and as stirrups in beams to carry tensile and shear forces.
conditions: when embedded in reinforced concrete beams

subject: IfcReinforcingBar
rationale: Vertical rebars in columns carry compressive loads and, together with ties, provide ductility and buckling resistance.
conditions: when embedded in reinforced concrete columns

subject: IfcReinforcingBar
rationale: Rebars in footings resist tensile stresses from soil pressure and thermal/moisture movements.
applicability: spread footings, strip footings, mat foundations
conditions: when used in reinforced concrete foundations

subject: IfcReinforcingBar
rationale: Rebars in walls provide tensile and shear resistance, especially in retaining walls and seismic shear walls.
applicability: retaining walls, shear walls, basement walls
conditions: when used in reinforced concrete or masonry walls

subject: IfcReinforcingBar
rationale: Longitudinal and spiral rebars reinforce concrete piles against bending during driving and service loads.
conditions: when used in reinforced concrete piles

subject: IfcReinforcingBar
rationale: Stirrups and spiral reinforcement around prestressing tendons protect against bursting and splitting forces at anchorages.
conditions: when used as confinement reinforcement in prestressed members

subject: IfcReinforcingBar
rationale: Rebars must be properly anchored and lapped at connections to ensure force transfer continuity across structural joints.
applicability: IfcReinforcingBar typically connects_to IfcStructuralConnection only indirectly via the concrete matrix or through engineered connection details. In most structural joints, reinforcing bars pass through the joint but are not directly connected to an IfcStructuralConnection element in IFC. Direct connection is primarily a modeling convention for specific detailing scenarios, not a general engineering requirement.
conditions: at structural joints and overlaps

subject: IfcReinforcingBar
rationale: Mechanical couplers (e.g., threaded splices) may be required for bar continuity in high-stress zones where lap splices are impractical.
conditions: when mechanical couplers are used instead of lapping
exceptions: traditional lap splices

subject: IfcReinforcingBar
rationale: The sizing, spacing, and detailing of reinforcing bars depend on structural analysis results (moments, shears, axial forces).
conditions: during design stage

subject: IfcReinforcingBarType
rationale: Reinforcing bars often work together with reinforcing meshes in slabs and walls to form a complete reinforcement system.
applicability: The assertion uses 'depends_on' without clarifying whether this is a logical dependency, a modeling dependency (e.g., IfcReinforcingBarType must reference an IfcReinforcingMeshType), or a physical dependency in design. In many reinforced concrete slabs and walls, bars are used without meshes (e.g., individual bars placed manually), so the dependency is not universal even within the stated conditions.
conditions: when used for slab or wall reinforcement

subject: IfcReinforcingBarType
rationale: Reinforcing bars provide tensile strength to concrete slabs, supporting structural loads.
applicability: IfcReinforcingBarType supports IfcSlab is too broad. In IFC, IfcReinforcingBar (the occurrence) is related to IfcSlab via IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure or IfcRelAggregates, not IfcReinforcingBarType directly. The type entity does not 'support' the slab element in a direct IFC relationship sense — the relationship is through the occurrence and containment/aggregation.
conditions: when embedded in concrete slabs as tension reinforcement

subject: IfcReinforcingBarType
rationale: Reinforcing bars resist tensile and shear forces in concrete beams.
applicability: The assertion uses 'supports' but in IFC, IfcReinforcingBar (the occurrence element) is related to IfcBeam, not the type entity. IfcReinforcingBarType defines properties of a bar type, but the structural relationship (placement as longitudinal reinforcement or stirrups) occurs at the occurrence level via IfcRelAggregates or IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure, not via the type.
conditions: when placed as longitudinal reinforcement or stirrups in beams

subject: IfcReinforcingBarType
rationale: Longitudinal bars and ties in columns resist compression and bending forces.
applicability: Similar to the beam and slab cases, in IFC the relationship between reinforcing bars and columns is at the occurrence level (IfcReinforcingBar contained in IfcColumn), not at the type level. IfcReinforcingBarType stores shared property sets and material definitions but does not directly participate in a 'supports' relationship with IfcColumn.
conditions: when used as vertical reinforcement in concrete columns

subject: IfcReinforcingBarType
rationale: Reinforcing bars provide structural integrity to concrete footings.
applicability: Same issue as above — IfcReinforcingBarType does not directly support IfcFooting in the IFC schema. The occurrence IfcReinforcingBar is related to the footing via spatial containment. Additionally, the IFC schema has IfcFooting as a subtype of IfcBuildingElement, and reinforcement is related through IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure or IfcRelAggregates at the occurrence level.
conditions: when used in reinforced concrete foundations

subject: IfcReinforcingBarType
rationale: Reinforcement in walls resists lateral loads, bending, and cracking.
applicability: Same type-vs-occurrence issue as other assertions. IfcReinforcingBarType does not directly relate to IfcWall in IFC — it is the occurrence IfcReinforcingBar that is placed within IfcWall. The type entity defines bar geometry, material, and properties but has no direct 'supports' relationship to wall elements.
conditions: when used in reinforced concrete walls or shear walls

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: IfcReinforcingElement is an abstract supertype; IfcReinforcingBar is its most common concrete subtype that provides actual tensile strength in concrete.
conditions: when reinforcement is in the form of bars

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: Tendons are a subtype of reinforcing elements used for prestressed concrete.
conditions: when prestressing/post-tensioning is used

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: Reinforcing mesh is a common subtype of IfcReinforcingElement for slab and wall reinforcement.
conditions: when welded wire fabric is used

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: Reinforcing bars need proper connections and anchorage to develop stress transfer.
applicability: IfcReinforcingElement does not 'require' IfcStructuralConnection at lap splices — lap splices create a connection between reinforcing bars themselves, not between the reinforcing element and a separate IfcStructuralConnection entity. The structural connection is more relevant at the member level (beam-column joints) rather than between rebar and connection objects.
conditions: at lap splices and anchorages

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: Reinforcement provides tensile capacity to concrete slabs, preventing flexural failure.
conditions: when embedded in concrete slabs
exceptions: IfcReinforcingElement also supports precast concrete slabs (prestressed hollow-core planks, precast double tees) where reinforcement is embedded but the slab is not cast-in-place concrete. The condition 'when embedded in concrete slabs' is correct but could be extended. More critically, reinforcement in a slab is not typically described as 'supporting' the slab — the reinforcement is embedded within it, and the structural action is different. This relationship is more of an aggregation/containment than a support.

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: Reinforcement provides tensile resistance in concrete beams.
conditions: when embedded in concrete beams

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: Reinforcement provides compressive and tensile capacity and ductility to columns.
conditions: when embedded in concrete columns

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: Reinforcement in footings resists bending and shear from soil pressure.
conditions: when embedded in concrete foundations

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: Reinforcement provides tensile and shear capacity to walls, especially retaining walls and shear walls.
conditions: when embedded in concrete or masonry walls

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: Anchorage hardware is required to lock in prestressing force.
conditions: when post-tensioning system is used

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: IfcReinforcingElement as an abstract class contains IfcReinforcingBar as a subtype.
conditions: as the primary type of reinforcement

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: IfcReinforcingElement contains IfcTendon as a subtype.
conditions: for prestressing applications

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: IfcReinforcingElement contains IfcReinforcingMesh as a subtype.
conditions: for distributed reinforcement

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: Reinforcing elements connect to each other via laps, hooks, or couplers to form continuous reinforcement.
conditions: through hooks, bends, and mechanical couplers

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: Reinforcement must be anchored into structural connections for load transfer.
conditions: at beam-column joints and foundations

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: Reinforcement sizing and placement depends on structural analysis results.
conditions: for design and detailing

subject: IfcReinforcingElement
rationale: Openings in reinforced concrete can conflict with reinforcement layout and require special detailing.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcReinforcingElement conflicts_with IfcOpeningElement' could be misinterpreted. In practice, reinforcement is detailed around openings (doors, windows, MEP penetrations) with trim bars, not in fundamental conflict. The condition 'without proper detailing' acknowledges this, but the 'conflicts_with' relationship name may be too strong — reinforcement and openings coexist in all reinforced concrete structures as long as detailing is correct.
conditions: when openings are placed without proper detailing

subject: IfcReinforcingElementType
rationale: IfcReinforcingElementType is the abstract type; IfcReinforcingMesh is a subtype for welded wire fabric.
conditions: when reinforcement is mesh-type

subject: IfcReinforcingElementType
rationale: IfcTendon is a subtype of IfcReinforcingElementType for prestressing steel.
conditions: when prestressed reinforcement

subject: IfcReinforcingElementType
rationale: IfcTendonAnchor is a subtype for anchorage devices in prestressed concrete.
conditions: when prestressed reinforcement

subject: IfcReinforcingElementType
rationale: Reinforcement is embedded within structural members like beams, columns, slabs.
conditions: when placed inside structural elements

subject: IfcReinforcingElementType
rationale: Reinforcing elements primarily support tensile forces in concrete structures.
conditions: under tensile loading

subject: IfcReinforcingElementType
rationale: Reinforcement in beams provides tensile capacity.
conditions: when embedded in beams

subject: IfcReinforcingElementType
rationale: Reinforcement in columns provides compression and bending resistance.
conditions: when embedded in columns

subject: IfcReinforcingElementType
rationale: Reinforcement in slabs provides flexural capacity.
conditions: when embedded in slabs

subject: IfcReinforcingElementType
rationale: Reinforcement in footings provides structural integrity under loads.
conditions: when embedded in footings

subject: IfcReinforcingElementType
rationale: Concrete cover (IfcCovering) protects reinforcement from fire and corrosion.
conditions: concrete cover is required for fire and corrosion protection

subject: IfcReinforcingElementType
rationale: IfcReinforcingElementType contains property sets for bar diameter, area, grade, etc.
conditions: for defining mechanical properties
exceptions: IfcReinforcingElementType (via IfcTypeObject) does contain IfcPropertySet, but property sets can also define other properties beyond mechanical properties (e.g., geometric, identification, thermal). The condition is overly restrictive.

subject: IfcReinforcingElementType
rationale: Reinforcing bars connect to each other at laps and splices.
conditions: at lap splices and mechanical couplers

subject: IfcReinforcingElementType
rationale: Tendons connect to anchors to transfer prestressing force to concrete.
conditions: at anchorage zones

subject: IfcReinforcingMesh
rationale: Reinforcing mesh typically requires reinforcing bars as its constituent elements when defined as an aggregate of bar members.
conditions: when mesh is composed of individual bars

subject: IfcReinforcingMesh
rationale: Reinforcing mesh must be connected to structural connections for proper load transfer within concrete elements.
conditions: for placement in structural elements

subject: IfcReinforcingMesh
rationale: Reinforcing mesh is commonly designed to be placed within slabs to control cracking and provide structural strength.
applicability: The assertion states IfcReinforcingMesh 'depends_on' IfcSlab, implying a dependency relationship. However, reinforcing mesh can also be used in other contexts such as walls, columns, beams, and foundations without a slab. The condition 'when used for slab reinforcement' correctly scopes this, but the relationship type 'depends_on' is ambiguous - in IFC, the mesh is contained within or assigned to the slab, not strictly dependent on it (a mesh product definition can exist without being assigned to any slab element).
conditions: when used for slab reinforcement

subject: IfcReinforcingMesh
rationale: Reinforcing mesh is frequently specified for wall elements to resist tensile and shear forces.
applicability: Similar to the slab assertion - IfcReinforcingMesh 'depends_on' IfcWall is too strong. The mesh can be defined as a product independently and later assigned to a wall. The dependency relationship in IFC is not a hard dependency but an aggregation/containment. Also, reinforcing mesh can be used in tilt-up panels, shotcrete applications, and other wall-like elements that may not be classified strictly as IfcWall (e.g., IfcWallStandardCase, IfcCurtainWall).
conditions: when used for wall reinforcement

subject: IfcReinforcingMesh
rationale: Reinforcing mesh structurally supports slabs by carrying tensile loads and controlling crack widths.
conditions: when embedded within the slab

subject: IfcReinforcingMesh
rationale: Reinforcing mesh structurally supports walls by providing tensile and shear reinforcement.
conditions: when embedded within the wall

subject: IfcReinforcingMesh
rationale: Concrete cover (IfcCovering) protects the reinforcing mesh from corrosion and fire; conversely, the mesh requires adequate cover to be protected from environmental damage.
conditions: concrete cover is specified

subject: IfcReinforcingMesh
rationale: A reinforcing mesh assembly typically contains multiple reinforcing bars or wires arranged in a grid pattern.
conditions: when mesh is a welded wire fabric assembly
exceptions: when mesh is a single wire fabric sheet without discrete bars

subject: IfcReinforcingMesh
rationale: The longitudinal and transverse wires in a reinforcing mesh are connected to each other at intersections, typically by welding.
applicability: The assertion that IfcReinforcingMesh 'connects_to' IfcReinforcingBar at intersections in welded wire mesh is imprecise. In a welded wire mesh assembly, the longitudinal and transverse wires are typically both part of the same IfcReinforcingMesh product at the factory. They are not separate IfcReinforcingBar entities that get 'connected' at intersections - they are welded together as a single mesh product. The individual wires may be represented as properties of the mesh, not as separate connected entities.
conditions: at intersections in welded wire mesh

subject: IfcReinforcingMesh
rationale: Reinforcing mesh (passive reinforcement) is generally unsuitable for use in the same capacity as prestressing tendons, though they can coexist in partially prestressed members.
conditions: in the same structural element section

subject: IfcReinforcingMeshType
rationale: IfcReinforcingMeshType is a type of reinforcing mesh used to provide tensile strength in concrete. It requires concrete to function as intended.
applicability: The assertion states IfcReinforcingMeshType 'requires Concrete', but IfcReinforcingMeshType could also be used in masonry reinforcement (e.g., reinforcing mesh in brick or block walls), not exclusively in concrete structures. The condition 'when used as reinforcement in concrete structures' partially covers this, but the assertion phrasing 'requires Concrete' is overly restrictive and misleading for non-concrete applications.
conditions: when used as reinforcement in concrete structures
exceptions: IfcReinforcingMeshType can be part of an IfcReinforcementAssembly or used in prestressed concrete where the mesh itself is not embedded in cast-in-place concrete but in a grouted or post-tensioned assembly. The simple 'requires Concrete' assertion does not hold for such composite reinforcement scenarios.

subject: IfcRelAssigns

subject: IfcRelAssigns
rationale: IfcRelAssigns relates IfcObjectDefinition instances; the related objects must be IfcObjectDefinition subtypes.

subject: IfcRelAssigns

conditions: when grouping objects
exceptions: IfcRelAssigns does not directly 'contain' IfcRelAssignsToGroup. IfcRelAssignsToGroup is a subtype of IfcRelAssigns, so the relationship is one of inheritance (is-a), not containment. The phrase 'contains' is imprecise when describing subtype relationships.

subject: IfcRelAssigns

conditions: when assigning objects to a process
exceptions: IfcRelAssigns does not directly 'contain' IfcRelAssignsToProcess. IfcRelAssignsToProcess is a subtype of IfcRelAssigns. 'Contains' is not the correct term for an inheritance relationship.

subject: IfcRelAssigns

rationale: IfcRelAssignsToResource is a subtype for resource assignments.

subject: IfcRelAssigns

Additionally, IfcFeatureElement subtypes (e.g., IfcOpeningElement) are also IfcElements but are not typically aggregated via IfcRelAggregates in the same way — they use IfcRelVoidsElement instead.

subject: IfcRelAggregates
rationale: IfcRelAggregates is used to relate IfcBuilding to its IfcBuildingStorey parts.

subject: IfcRelAggregates
rationale: IfcRelAggregates can aggregate IfcSpaces within an IfcBuildingStorey.

subject: IfcRelAggregates
rationale: IfcRelAggregates is used to relate IfcSite to its IfcBuilding parts.

subject: IfcRelAggregates
rationale: IfcRelAggregates relates IfcProject to IfcSite.

subject: IfcRelAggregates
rationale: IfcRelAggregates can group IfcSystem subtypes and their components.

subject: IfcRelAggregates
rationale: IfcRelAggregates supports the overall project structure by defining how the project breaks down into sites, buildings, storeys, and spaces.
applicability: IfcRelAggregates supports IfcProject is imprecise. IfcProject itself is not directly contained in an aggregation — IfcProject is the root entity that contains sites via IfcRelAggregates. The relationship is that IfcProject uses IfcRelAggregates to relate IfcSite, but the assertion 'supports IfcProject' is vague and could be misinterpreted as IfcProject being a child in an aggregation.
conditions: In the project decomposition hierarchy

subject: IfcRelAggregates
rationale: IfcRelAggregates inherits from IfcRelationship which inherits from IfcRoot, thus depending on the basic IFC infrastructure.
applicability: IfcRelAggregates depends_on IfcRoot is technically true via inheritance chain (IfcRelAggregates -> IfcRelDecomposes -> IfcRelationship -> IfcRoot), but this is true for all IFC entities, not specific to IfcRelAggregates. subject: IfcRelAssignsToActor

conditions: for tracking authorship and modification history

subject: IfcRelAssignsToControl

subject: IfcRelAssignsToControl

conditions: When the RelatingControl is a subtype of IfcWorkControl, such as IfcWorkPlan or IfcWorkSchedule

subject: IfcRelAssignsToControl
rationale: IfcRelAssignsToControl can link performance history data to building elements, supporting performance monitoring.

subject: IfcRelAssignsToControl
rationale: Control relationships can assign cost information to building components, supporting cost control workflows.

subject: IfcRelAssignsToControl
rationale: IfcRelAssignsToControl inherits the ability to connect objects, and control relationships often involve property definitions that constrain or define controlled elements.
conditions: Through the IfcRelAssigns inheritance, property definitions can be assigned along with control information

subject: IfcRelAssignsToGroup

subject: IfcRelAssignsToGroup

subject: IfcRelAssignsToGroupByFactor

subject: IfcRelAssignsToGroupByFactor

However, the assertion says 'supports IfcTask' which is vague - IfcTask is actually the RelatingProcess (the process being related to), not something that the relationship 'supports'. In IFC schema, IfcTask can be the RelatingProcess in the assignment, meaning the relationship assigns objects to tasks.

subject: IfcRelAssignsToProduct

subject: IfcRelAssociates

subject: IfcRelAssociates

subject: IfcRelAssociatesApproval
rationale: IfcRelAssociatesApproval links an approval (IfcApproval) to objects; the approval entity is essential for the relationship to function.

conditions: The IfcRelAssociatesApproval relationship must reference a valid IfcApproval entity
exceptions: The assertion states IfcRelAssociatesApproval 'depends_on' IfcApproval, which is partially correct. However, there is an exception: IfcRelAssociatesApproval can exist (in a modeling/schema sense) without an IfcApproval instance if the RelatingApproval attribute is omitted or set to an optional reference, depending on the IFC schema version. In IFC2x3, the RelatingApproval attribute is mandatory, but in IFC4, the inverse attribute relationships changed, and some implementations may handle this differently.

subject: IfcRelAssociatesApproval

IfcRelAssociatesApproval depends on IfcApproval as the relating approval, and on an IfcRoot subtype as the related object. The dependency chain is not simply 'depends_on IfcRoot' — it specifically depends on IfcRoot subtypes that serve as RelatedObjects in the association. The condition correctly notes the related object must be IfcRoot or subtype, but the assertion label 'depends_on IfcRoot' is imprecise and could mislead about the nature of the dependency.
conditions: The related object must be an instance of IfcRoot or its subtypes

subject: IfcRelAssociatesApproval

subject: IfcRelAssociatesApproval
rationale: Approval associations support building elements by providing documented review/acceptance (e.g., structural approval for beams/columns).

subject: IfcRelAssociatesApproval

subject: IfcRelAssociatesApproval

subject: IfcRelAssociatesApproval

rationale: IfcRelConnects is a direct subtype of IfcRelationship, meaning it inherits its structure and requires the relationship framework.
conditions: As part of the IFC inheritance hierarchy

subject: IfcRelConnects
rationale: IfcRelConnects is the abstract generalization that contains and encompasses all specific connection subtypes.
conditions: In typical IFC model implementations

subject: IfcRelConnects
rationale: The abstract IfcRelConnects class contains the port connectivity relationship subtype.
conditions: In typical IFC model implementations

subject: IfcRelConnects
rationale: Path element connections are a contained subtype within the IfcRelConnects hierarchy.
conditions: In typical IFC model implementations

subject: IfcRelConnects
rationale: Structural member connections are a contained subtype within IfcRelConnects.
applicability: all building types with structural systems
conditions: In typical IFC model implementations

subject: IfcRelConnects
rationale: Realizing element connections are a contained subtype within the IfcRelConnects hierarchy.
conditions: In typical IFC model implementations

subject: IfcRelConnects
rationale: Structural activity connections are a subtype contained within IfcRelConnects.
