applicability: all building types with structural analysis
conditions: In typical IFC model implementations

subject: IfcRelConnects
rationale: IfcRelConnects, through its subtypes, supports the connection and relationship management between building elements in an IFC model.
conditions: When used via IfcRelConnectsElements

subject: IfcRelConnectsElements
rationale: IfcRelConnectsElements is a specific subtype of the abstract IfcRelConnects relationship, which is the general supertype for all connectivity relationships in IFC.
conditions: When representing any connectivity relationship between building elements

subject: IfcRelConnectsElements
rationale: IfcRelConnectsElements requires two or more IfcElement objects (RelatingElement and RelatedElement) to establish a connection.
conditions: Must have at least two IfcElement instances to define a connection relationship

subject: IfcRelConnectsElements
rationale: IfcRelConnectsElements is specifically designed to represent connectivity between building elements, typically subtypes of IfcBuildingElement.
conditions: Used for connections between physical building elements such as walls, slabs, columns, beams, etc.

subject: IfcRelConnectsElements
rationale: In structural engineering contexts, IfcRelConnectsElements can represent structural connections that support load transfer between elements.
conditions: When used in structural analysis models to represent physical joints or connections

subject: IfcRelConnectsElements
rationale: IfcRelConnectsElements can represent connections between distribution elements such as ducts, pipes, cables, and equipment.
conditions: When representing connections in MEP (mechanical, electrical, plumbing) distribution systems

subject: IfcRelConnectsElements
rationale: IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements is a subtype that adds realizing elements (e.g., fasteners) that physically realize the connection.
conditions: When a connection is realized by an additional real element like a bolt, weld, or connector

subject: IfcRelConnectsElements
rationale: IfcRelConnectsElements can represent the connection between a covering element and its base element.
conditions: When coverings (e.g., finishes, cladding) are connected to structural elements

subject: IfcRelConnectsElements
rationale: IfcRelConnectsElements can reference fastener elements that physically connect two building elements.
conditions: When mechanical fasteners realize the connection between elements

subject: IfcRelConnectsPathElements
rationale: IfcRelConnectsPathElements is a subtype of IfcRelConnectsElement and connects elements in a path network.
conditions: When used in IFC data exchange for building path networks

subject: IfcRelConnectsPathElements
rationale: This relationship type is used to define connectivity of elements within a path (e.g., a circulation path).
conditions: When modeling circulation and path networks

subject: IfcRelConnectsPathElements
rationale: Path elements may connect to walls as boundary elements.
conditions: When walls define path boundaries

subject: IfcRelConnectsPathElements
rationale: Doors are common path elements connected via this relationship.
conditions: When doors are part of a path/egress route

subject: IfcRelConnectsPathElements
rationale: Stairs are path elements for vertical circulation.
conditions: When stairs are part of a vertical circulation path

subject: IfcRelConnectsPathElements
rationale: Slabs can form the walking surface of a path.
conditions: When slabs serve as path surfaces (floors, landings)

subject: IfcRelConnectsPathElements
rationale: Ramps are path elements for accessible circulation.
conditions: When ramps are part of accessible circulation

subject: IfcRelConnectsPathElements
rationale: Transport elements can be part of path connectivity.
conditions: When elevators, escalators or moving walkways are part of a path

subject: IfcRelConnectsPathElements
rationale: IfcRelConnectsPathElements is a subtype of IfcRelConnectsElement, inheriting its structure.
conditions: As the supertype relationship

subject: IfcRelConnectsPathElements
rationale: Virtual elements can represent connections or openings in path networks.
conditions: When connecting path segments without a physical element

subject: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement
rationale: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement is a relationship that connects an IfcPort to an IfcElement. The port must be connected to an element for the relationship to function.
applicability: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement connects_to IfcPort is too broad. The relationship specifically connects an IfcPort to an IfcDistributionElement or IfcElement, not any IfcPort. IfcPort is abstract and includes subclasses like IfcDistributionPort. The assertion should clarify the context of distribution elements.

subject: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement
rationale: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement connects one or more ports to an element. Both the port and the element are essential participants in this relationship.
applicability: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement connects_to IfcElement is too broad. In IFC, IfcRelConnectsPortToElement relates an IfcPort to an IfcDistributionElement (a subtype of IfcElement), not any arbitrary IfcElement like IfcBuildingElement (e.g., IfcWall, IfcSlab). The range is more restricted than stated.

subject: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement
rationale: The subtype IfcDistributionPort is commonly used with distribution elements. IfcRelConnectsPortToElement is used in the context of distribution systems (electrical, HVAC, plumbing) where distribution ports connect to distribution elements.
exceptions: IfcFlowController
IfcFlowSegment
IfcFlowFitting
IfcFlowTerminal
IfcFlowMovingDevice
IfcFlowTreatmentDevice
IfcEnergyConversionDevice

subject: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement
rationale: For a complete connectivity path, IfcRelConnectsPortToElement pairs are complemented by IfcRelConnectsPorts which connects two ports together, forming a distribution path.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcRelConnectsPortToElement requires IfcRelConnectsPorts' is not universally true. In IFC, a port can be connected to an element via IfcRelConnectsPortToElement without there necessarily being an IfcRelConnectsPorts relationship between that port and another port. IfcRelConnectsPorts connects two ports (on different elements), which is a separate concern. The relationship is more of a 'may be followed by' or 'often used together with' rather than a hard requirement.
conditions: Ports on different elements are connected via IfcRelConnectsPorts

subject: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement
rationale: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement is commonly used to attach ports to flow segments like pipes, ducts, and cables in distribution networks.
conditions: Used in duct, pipe, or cable routing

subject: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement
rationale: Flow terminals like diffusers, sinks, or outlets have ports connected to them via this relationship.
conditions: At endpoints of distribution systems

subject: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement
rationale: Flow controllers like valves, dampers, and switches have ports connected to them using this relationship.
conditions: Where control devices are part of distribution paths

subject: IfcRelConnectsPortToElement
rationale: Energy conversion devices such as boilers, chillers, and transformers have ports connected via this relationship.
conditions: At energy conversion points in systems

subject: IfcRelConnectsPorts
rationale: IfcRelConnectsPorts is defined in IFC schema as a relationship that connects two ports (IfcPort) together, typically for distributing energy, fluid, or data.
conditions: The relationship must be established through connected ports

subject: IfcRelConnectsPorts
rationale: In practice, IfcRelConnectsPorts most commonly connects IfcDistributionPort instances for MEP distribution systems.
applicability: All building types with MEP systems
conditions: When used in distribution systems (HVAC, electrical, plumbing)
exceptions: IfcPort can also be used without being a subtype of IfcDistributionPort in some cases

The assertion states IfcRelConnectsPorts depends_on IfcDistributionPort under condition 'When used in distribution systems'. However, IfcRelConnectsPorts can also connect IfcPort objects that are not of type IfcDistributionPort, such as IfcStructuralPort or other port subtypes in non-distribution contexts, which is recognized in the existing exception but contradicts the dependency framing.

subject: IfcRelConnectsPorts
rationale: Ports are typically assigned to distribution elements (ducts, pipes, cables, equipment) to define connectivity in MEP networks.
applicability: Buildings with HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire protection systems
conditions: The ports being connected must belong to distribution elements
exceptions: Ports could theoretically belong to other element types

subject: IfcRelConnectsPorts
rationale: Port connections at the element level support higher-level path and flow connectivity representations.
conditions: When building a complete connectivity graph for distribution systems

subject: IfcRelConnectsPorts
rationale: Port connections define the topology of distribution systems by linking elements (ducts, pipes, fittings, equipment).
applicability: HVAC, electrical, plumbing, fire protection systems

The assertion states IfcRelConnectsPorts 'connects_to' IfcDistributionSystem. However, IfcRelConnectsPorts establishes a connection between two ports, not directly to a system. A port connection is part of a system via the elements' membership in the system, but the relationship object itself does not directly reference IfcDistributionSystem.
conditions: When ports connect elements within the same distribution system

subject: IfcRelConnectsPorts
rationale: Distribution elements that own ports are often related to building elements for spatial context.
conditions: When distribution elements are hosted by or related to building elements (walls, slabs, etc.)
exceptions: Free-standing equipment may not depend directly on building elements

subject: IfcRelConnectsPorts
rationale: The port-to-element relationship (IfcRelConnectsPortToElement) is typically a prerequisite for port-to-port connections.
conditions: A port must first be assigned to an element before two ports can be connected
exceptions: Ports can theoretically exist without being assigned to an element

The assertion says IfcRelConnectsPorts 'requires' IfcRelConnectsPortToElement. While in practice ports are nearly always assigned to elements, the IFC schema does not mandate this as a prerequisite for IfcRelConnectsPorts. The existing exception acknowledges this, yet the assertion still says 'requires', which is too strong for the schema-level constraint.

subject: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity is a subtype of IfcRelConnects, inheriting its general connectivity semantics.
conditions: When establishing connectivity relationships

subject: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity
rationale: The purpose of IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity is to connect a structural activity (action or reaction) to a structural member or element.
conditions: To define a structural activity relationship

subject: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity
rationale: The relationship connects a structural member (e.g., column, beam, wall) to a structural activity.
applicability: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity can relate an IfcStructuralActivity to either an IfcStructuralMember or an IfcStructuralConnection (via inherited RelatingElement of type IfcStructuralMember or IfcStructuralConnection). The assertion limits the scope to only IfcStructuralMember, omitting IfcStructuralConnection as a valid relating element.
conditions: As the relating element in the relationship

subject: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity can be used to assign reactions (forces, displacements) to structural members.
conditions: When modeling structural analysis results

subject: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity can be used to assign actions (loads) to structural members.
conditions: When modeling applied loads

subject: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity
rationale: The relationship explicitly connects structural items (members) to their associated activities.
conditions: When the structural item is a member or element

subject: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity
rationale: This relationship type may work alongside other structural connectivity relationships to form a complete structural model.
conditions: In a comprehensive structural model
exceptions: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity does not connect to IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember. The RelatingElement is an IfcStructuralMember (or IfcStructuralConnection) and RelatedStructuralActivity is an IfcStructuralActivity. There is no relationship between IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity and IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember in the IFC schema.

subject: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity instances are typically grouped within an IfcStructuralAnalysisModel.
conditions: When part of a structured analysis model group

subject: IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember
rationale: IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember is a relationship class that requires at least one IfcStructuralMember as the relating or related element in the connection.
conditions: When representing a structural connection relationship
exceptions: IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember can also be used to connect a structural member directly to another structural member (as noted in the exception of assertion f183c63b), meaning IfcStructuralMember is not always required — the relationship can exist between a structural member and a connection, but when connecting two structural members the connecting element may be another member rather than a connection point.

subject: IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember
rationale: The relationship can connect a structural member to a structural connection (e.g., IfcStructuralPointConnection) representing a node.
conditions: When connecting a structural member to a connection point or node
exceptions: May also connect two structural members directly without a connection element

subject: IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember
rationale: IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember is a subtype of IfcRelConnects, depending on it for basic relationship semantics.
conditions: As part of the IFC inheritance hierarchy

subject: IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember
rationale: The primary purpose is to connect structural members to each other or to structural connections, establishing load paths.
conditions: When establishing a connection between structural elements

subject: IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember
rationale: Structural members are often connected at connection points represented by IfcStructuralConnection subtypes.
conditions: When a structural member is connected at a node or connection point

subject: IfcRelConnectsWithEccentricity
rationale: IfcRelConnectsWithEccentricity is a subtype of IfcRelConnects, inheriting its structure and requiring the base connection relationship.
conditions: When used as a subtype of IfcRelConnects

subject: IfcRelConnectsWithEccentricity
rationale: The entity is used to define eccentricity relationships between structural members and structural connection points.
applicability: IfcRelConnectsWithEccentricity can also connect a structural member to a structural surface connection or curve connection, not solely to IfcStructuralConnection. The assertion should specify that it connects a structural member to a structural connection point via an IfcStructuralConnection subtype (e.g., IfcStructuralPointConnection, IfcStructuralCurveConnection, IfcStructuralSurfaceConnection), not the abstract type IfcStructuralConnection directly.
conditions: When connecting a structural member to a structural connection point

subject: IfcRelConnectsWithEccentricity
rationale: One of the primary roles is relating a structural member to a connection with eccentricity.
conditions: When representing the link between a structural member and a connection

subject: IfcRelConnectsWithEccentricity
rationale: The entity uses coordinate systems to define the eccentricity relationship in 3D space.
applicability: The ConditionCoordinateSystem attribute is of type IfcAxis2Placement (an abstract select type including IfcAxis2Placement2D or IfcAxis2Placement3D), not exclusively IfcAxis2Placement3D. In 2D structural models, IfcAxis2Placement2D would be used instead. The assertion incorrectly restricts this to only 3D placement.
conditions: When 3D eccentricity data is defined via the ConditionCoordinateSystem

subject: IfcRelConnectsWithEccentricity
rationale: The eccentricity relationship feeds into structural analysis models to ensure accurate load transfer representation.
conditions: When the eccentricity data is used within a structural analysis context

subject: IfcRelConnectsWithEccentricity
rationale: Eccentricity can be defined at point connections, line connections, or surface connections.
conditions: When the connection point is a point (node) type connection

subject: IfcRelConnectsWithEccentricity
rationale: Eccentricity can be defined at curve/line connections between structural members.
conditions: When the connection is a linear/edge type connection (e.g., beam-to-beam along a line)

subject: IfcRelConnectsWithEccentricity
rationale: Eccentricity can be defined at surface connections between structural elements.
conditions: When the connection is a surface type connection (e.g., wall-to-slab)

subject: IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements
rationale: IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements is a subtype of IfcRelConnects, therefore it depends on the general connection relationship structure.
conditions: When establishing any connectivity relationship

subject: IfcRelConnectsWithRealizingElements
rationale: The relationship connects IfcElement subtypes through realizing elements.
conditions: All related and relating elements must be IfcElement instances

subject: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure
rationale: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure is a relationship that links element occurrences (IfcProduct) to spatial structure elements (IfcSpatialStructureElement). It depends on the existence of a spatial container.
conditions: parent spatial element must exist

subject: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure
rationale: The relationship connects one or more IfcProduct elements to a spatial structure, so it depends on having valid product elements to contain.
conditions: element must be an IfcProduct subtype

subject: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure
rationale: Typical usage contains building elements like walls, slabs, columns, beams within a storey or building spatial structure.
conditions: element must be contained within a spatial structure like IfcBuildingStorey

subject: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure
rationale: Furnishing elements can be contained within spatial structures via this relationship.
conditions: furniture must be assigned to a spatial location

subject: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure
rationale: Distribution elements like ducts, pipes, cables are contained within spatial structures.
conditions: distribution elements must have a spatial context

subject: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure
rationale: Transport elements like elevators, escalators are contained within spatial structures.

subject: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure
rationale: While IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure handles containment of elements, spatial decomposition into sub-spaces uses IfcRelAggregates; containment supports the spatial hierarchy by placing physical elements into spatial nodes.
conditions: spatial decomposition uses aggregation relationship

subject: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure
rationale: The spatial structure ultimately roots from IfcProject which contains the building/site/storey hierarchy.
conditions: the project defines the spatial context hierarchy

subject: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure
rationale: The relationship supports the concept of storey-based organization by assigning building elements to specific floors/storeys.
conditions: elements are assigned to a specific storey

subject: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure
rationale: Opening elements like voids for windows/doors can be contained within spatial structures.
conditions: openings are spatially contained

subject: IfcRelCoversSpaces
rationale: IfcRelCoversSpaces is an IFC relationship that links covering elements (like ceilings, floors, wall coverings) to the IfcSpace they cover. The relationship requires an IfcSpace as the relating object.
conditions: must be the space being covered

subject: IfcRelCoversSpaces
rationale: IfcRelCoversSpaces links one or more IfcCovering elements to an IfcSpace. Without IfcCovering entities, this relationship has no purpose.
conditions: must be the covering element(s) related to the space

subject: IfcRelCoversSpaces
rationale: Spaces are often part of a building storey or building via IfcRelAggregates, which provides the spatial context for the covers relationship.
applicability: IFC models with hierarchical spatial decomposition
conditions: when the space is part of a spatial structure hierarchy

subject: IfcRelCoversSpaces
rationale: The relationship semantically contains the covering elements that are applied to a space, such as ceilings, floor coverings, wall coverings.
conditions: covers are assigned to the space via this relationship

subject: IfcRelCoversSpaces
rationale: Both relationships handle coverings but at different levels: spaces vs. individual building elements. They are conceptually connected in a complete BIM model.
applicability: IFC models with both types of covering relationships
conditions: when a building element has its own covering relationship
exceptions: IfcRelCoversSpaces is for space coverings, not element coverings

subject: IfcRelCoversSpaces
rationale: Spaces are typically nested within storeys, so the storey provides the vertical context for the covering-to-space relationship.
conditions: when the space is contained within a specific storey
exceptions: spaces can be directly under the building level

IfcRelCoversSpaces does not require IfcBuildingStorey. The relationship is between an IfcSpace and IfcCoverings. The space itself may be placed under an IfcBuildingStorey via IfcRelAggregates or IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure, but IfcRelCoversSpaces has no direct attribute referencing IfcBuildingStorey and no schema-level dependency on it.

subject: IfcRelCoversBldgElements
rationale: IfcRelCoversBldgElements is used to assign coverings to building elements. It inherently depends on the existence of a building element to be covered.
applicability: IfcRelCoversBldgElements relates to IfcElement (the supertype), not specifically IfcBuildingElement. IFC schema allows RelatingObject to be any IfcElement, including IfcBuildingElement, IfcFurnishingElement, IfcOpeningElement, etc. The dependency is more accurately on IfcElement, not the subtype IfcBuildingElement.
conditions: When relating covering elements to building elements

subject: IfcRelCoversBldgElements
rationale: IfcRelCoversBldgElements contains references to one or more IfcCovering entities that are applied to a building element.
conditions: When defining covering relationships

subject: IfcRelCoversBldgElements
rationale: Coverings support building elements by providing finishes, cladding, or protective layers that enhance durability and aesthetics.
conditions: By providing surface coverage or protection

subject: IfcRelCoversBldgElements
rationale: The building element being covered needs to be placed within a spatial structure via IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure.
conditions: For spatial context of covered building elements

subject: IfcRelDeclares
rationale: IfcRelDeclares is a relationship that links IfcProject (or its subclasses) to objects declared in the context of that project. IfcRelDeclares depends on IfcProject as the owning context.
conditions: When IfcRelDeclares is used to declare objects in the context of a project

subject: IfcRelDeclares
rationale: IfcRelDeclares relates an IfcProject to a set of IfcObjectDefinitions (e.g., types, properties, materials) that are declared within the project context.
applicability: All IFC models using declaration relationships
conditions: General usage of IfcRelDeclares

subject: IfcRelDeclares
rationale: IfcRelDeclares is commonly used to declare IfcPropertySetTemplate objects within a project scope.
applicability: IFC models with custom property sets
conditions: When declaring property set templates

subject: IfcRelDeclares
rationale: IfcRelDeclares can contain IfcTypeObject (including IfcElementType, IfcSpaceType, etc.) to declare them within the project.
conditions: When declaring element types or style types

subject: IfcRelDeclares
rationale: IfcRelDeclares works in conjunction with IfcRelDefinesByTemplate to define property sets for types.
conditions: When property set templates are associated with types

subject: IfcRelDeclares
rationale: IfcRelDeclares can support the declaration of objects in an IfcProjectLibrary context for reusable library definitions.
conditions: When used in a library context

subject: IfcRelDeclares
rationale: IfcRelDeclares can contain material definitions declared within the project scope.
conditions: When declaring materials at project level

subject: IfcRelDeclares
rationale: Profile definitions can be declared within a project using IfcRelDeclares.
conditions: When declaring structural profiles

subject: IfcRelDeclares
rationale: IfcRelDeclares, like all IFC entities, depends on IfcOwnerHistory for tracking authorship and changes.
conditions: When recording ownership and modification history

subject: IfcRelDeclares
rationale: Once objects are declared via IfcRelDeclares, they can be associated with classifications.
conditions: When classifying declared objects

subject: IfcRelDecomposes
rationale: IfcRelDecomposes is the abstract supertype; IfcRelAggregates is its primary concrete subtype for part-whole relationships between building elements.
conditions: when modeling hierarchical decomposition of building elements

subject: IfcRelDecomposes
rationale: IfcRelNests is another concrete subtype of IfcRelDecomposes for ordered decomposition relationships.
conditions: when modeling ordered containment like assembly sequences

subject: IfcRelDecomposes
rationale: IfcRelDecomposes relates an IfcObjectDefinition (the whole) to other IfcObjectDefinitions (the parts). The RelatingObject attribute must be an IfcObjectDefinition.
conditions: for the RelatingObject relationship

subject: IfcRelDecomposes
rationale: IfcRelAggregates contains IfcElement parts within a whole element (e.g., columns in a building, walls in a floor).
conditions: when using IfcRelAggregates subtype
exceptions: IfcRelNests typically contains IfcObjectDefinition types not necessarily physical elements

subject: IfcRelDecomposes
rationale: IfcRelAggregates is used to decompose spatial structure elements like IfcBuilding into IfcBuildingStorey, and IfcBuildingStorey into IfcSpace.
conditions: when decomposing spatial structure (site, building, storey, space)

subject: IfcRelDecomposes
rationale: IfcRelAggregates supports the spatial hierarchy by decomposing IfcProject into IfcSite, IfcSite into IfcBuilding, etc.
conditions: at the top level of decomposition

subject: IfcRelDecomposes
rationale: While IfcRelDecomposes handles part-whole relationships, IfcRelAssociates can link external classifications or properties to the same IfcObjectDefinitions.
conditions: when classifying or assigning properties to the decomposition hierarchy

subject: IfcRelDecomposes
rationale: IfcElementAssembly uses IfcRelAggregates to contain individual elements that form an assembled unit.
conditions: when modeling assemblies of elements like reinforcement cages, trusses

subject: IfcRelDefines
rationale: IfcRelDefines is the abstract supertype; its primary concrete subtype IfcRelDefinesByProperties depends on property set definitions to function as an object-property assignment relationship.
applicability: IfcRelDefines is abstract and does not directly depend on IfcRelDefinesByProperties in a dependency sense. IfcRelDefinesByProperties is a subtype of IfcRelDefines, so the directionality is inheritance, not 'depends_on'. The statement conflates subtype relationships with dependency relationships.
conditions: when defining property sets for objects

subject: IfcRelDefines
rationale: IfcRelDefines typically links IfcPropertySet instances to IfcObject instances, so it depends on the property sets being defined.
applicability: IfcRelDefines (abstract) does not directly depend on IfcPropertySet. IfcRelDefinesByProperties (a subtype) references IfcPropertySetDefinition (not IfcPropertySet directly). IfcPropertySet is a subtype of IfcPropertySetDefinition, so the relationship is indirect through the inheritance hierarchy.
conditions: when used to assign properties to objects

subject: IfcRelDefines
rationale: IfcRelDefines relates object occurrences to type definitions or property sets, so it requires the existence of at least one IfcObject to connect to.
applicability: IfcRelDefines in its subtypes (IfcRelDefinesByProperties, IfcRelDefinesByType) relates to IfcObjectDefinition (the supertype), not specifically to IfcObject. IfcObject is a subtype of IfcObjectDefinition, so limiting the dependency to IfcObject ignores other valid subtypes like IfcTypeObject, IfcProcess, etc.
conditions: when defining relationships between objects and their definitions

subject: IfcRelDefines
rationale: IfcRelDefines formally connects IfcObjectDefinition subtypes (objects) to their corresponding definitions/properties.
conditions: when used to relate an object to its type or property definition

subject: IfcRelDefines
rationale: As the abstract supertype, IfcRelDefines provides the foundational relationship structure that supports its concrete subtype IfcRelDefinesByType for type assignments.
applicability: IfcRelDefines does not 'support' IfcRelDefinesByType in a dependency sense. IfcRelDefinesByType is a subtype of IfcRelDefines via inheritance, not a separately supported relationship. The phrasing 'supports IfcRelDefinesByType' is misleading as IfcRelDefines is the abstract superclass.
conditions: when defining type-instance relationships

subject: IfcRelDefines
rationale: The relationship structure of IfcRelDefines can be thought of as containing or encapsulating property set definitions as part of the definition-to-object linking mechanism.
applicability: The assertion states IfcRelDefines 'contains' IfcPropertySetDefinition, but IfcRelDefines itself does not directly contain IfcPropertySetDefinition. The relationship is via IfcRelDefinesByProperties, which has a 'RelatedPropertyDefinitions' attribute that references IfcPropertySetDefinition. IfcRelDefines is abstract and its subtype IfcRelDefinesByProperties is the one that contains property set definitions.
conditions: when used in property assignment scenarios

subject: IfcRelDefines
rationale: For type assignment, IfcRelDefines depends on the existence of IfcTypeObject instances that define the common properties for object occurrences.
applicability: IfcRelDefines does not directly depend on IfcTypeObject. IfcRelDefinesByType.RelatingType references IfcTypeObject, but IfcRelDefines is abstract and the dependency belongs to the subtype. Additionally, IfcRelDefinesByType can also relate to IfcTypeProcess or other subtypes of IfcTypeObject depending on the domain.
conditions: when used as IfcRelDefinesByType to assign a type to occurrences

subject: IfcRelDefinesByObject
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByObject links an IfcObject (or subtype) to an IfcObjectDefinition that defines its properties. The relationship depends on the existence of the defining object.
conditions: When establishing object relationships

subject: IfcRelDefinesByObject
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByObject relates one or more IfcObjects to an IfcObjectDefinition that acts as the defining object.
conditions: When defining object relationships in IFC models

subject: IfcRelDefinesByObject
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByObject can indirectly support property assignment when the relating object carries property set definitions.
applicability: The assertion states IfcRelDefinesByObject 'supports' IfcPropertySetDefinition, but the IFC schema does not allow IfcRelDefinesByObject to relate IfcPropertySetDefinition directly — property sets are assigned via IfcRelDefinesByProperties, not IfcRelDefinesByObject. The existing exception already acknowledges this but the assertion itself is misleading.
conditions: When property sets are assigned via object definition
exceptions: Property sets may also be assigned directly via IfcRelDefinesByProperties

subject: IfcRelDefinesByObject
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByObject can relate occurrences to their type definitions, supporting type-based object definitions.
conditions: When defining types for multiple occurrences

subject: IfcRelDefinesByObject
rationale: The defining object may carry material definitions that apply to the related objects.
conditions: When material information is associated via the defining object

subject: IfcRelDefinesByProperties
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByProperties is a relationship object in IFC that links elements to property set definitions. It requires IfcPropertySetDefinition objects to function, as its purpose is to assign property sets to objects.
conditions: When defining properties for building elements

subject: IfcRelDefinesByProperties
rationale: This relationship connects property sets to objects (elements, spaces, etc.), so it requires an IfcObjectDefinition as the relating or related object.
conditions: When linking properties to building elements

subject: IfcRelDefinesByProperties
rationale: The most common usage involves IfcPropertySet (a subtype of IfcPropertySetDefinition) which contains individual properties assigned to building elements.
applicability: All IFC models that use property sets
conditions: When using predefined property sets

subject: IfcRelDefinesByProperties
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByProperties links to property set definitions that themselves contain individual IfcProperty objects.
conditions: Indirectly through IfcPropertySetDefinition

subject: IfcRelDefinesByProperties
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByProperties supports property set definitions by formally linking them to building elements in the IFC hierarchy.
conditions: By establishing the assignment relationship in the IFC data model

subject: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate links property set definitions (IfcPropertySetDefinition) to property set templates. It requires the existence of templates to define the structure of property sets.
applicability: All IFC models using property sets
conditions: When defining property sets for elements

subject: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate
rationale: The relationship directly associates an IfcPropertySetDefinition with an IfcPropertySetTemplate, so the template is required.
conditions: When defining property sets via templates

subject: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate
rationale: The RelDefinesByTemplate relationship contains the association between a property set definition and its template.
conditions: When property sets are defined by a template

subject: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate supports consistent property definitions by linking property sets to reusable templates.
conditions: When standardizing property definitions across multiple elements

subject: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate can be used to define properties for IfcTypeObject (and subtypes like IfcWallType), depending on the type definition being present.
conditions: When applying property templates to type objects

subject: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate
rationale: The relationship inherits from IfcRelDefines which links property definitions to objects; thus it depends on IfcPropertyDefinition instances.
conditions: When linking property definitions to templates

subject: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate connects an IfcPropertySetDefinition to its defining IfcPropertySetTemplate.
conditions: When a property set is defined by a template

subject: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate connects an IfcPropertySetDefinition to its defining IfcPropertySetTemplate.
conditions: When a template defines the structure of a property set

subject: IfcRelDefinesByTemplate
rationale: Using property set templates improves consistency and reduces redundancy across a project.
applicability: Large IFC projects with many similar elements
conditions: When standardizing property definitions across a project

subject: IfcRelDefinesByType
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByType is a subtype of IfcRelDefines, which is the abstract supertype for object definition relationships.
conditions: When establishing type-instance relationships

subject: IfcRelDefinesByType
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByType relates object instances to a type definition (IfcTypeObject or its subtypes).
conditions: For defining the type information that applies to related objects

subject: IfcRelDefinesByType
rationale: The relationship connects IfcObject instances (or subtypes like IfcProduct, IfcProcess, etc.) to an IfcTypeObject.
conditions: When relating object occurrences to a type

subject: IfcRelDefinesByType
rationale: Type objects often have property set definitions that apply to all related instances.
conditions: When property sets are assigned at the type level

subject: IfcRelDefinesByType
rationale: Type definitions exist within the context of a project, though indirectly.
conditions: During model setup for type declarations

subject: IfcRelFillsElement
rationale: IfcRelFillsElement in the IFC schema always relates an IfcOpeningElement (relatingElement) to an IfcElement (relatedElement) that fills it.
conditions: The IfcRelFillsElement relationship requires an IfcOpeningElement (opening) to exist as the relating element

subject: IfcRelFillsElement
rationale: The relationship connects an opening to the element (typically a door, window, or other infill) that fills that opening.
conditions: The related element must be capable of filling an opening (e.g., IfcDoor, IfcWindow, or similar building element)

subject: IfcRelFillsElement
rationale: IfcRelFillsElement commonly contains IfcDoor as the related element that fills an opening in a wall.
conditions: When the filling element is a door

subject: IfcRelFillsElement
rationale: IfcRelFillsElement commonly contains IfcWindow as the related element that fills an opening in a wall.
conditions: When the filling element is a window

subject: IfcRelFillsElement
rationale: While the direct relating element is IfcOpeningElement, that opening is typically voiding an IfcWall (via IfcRelVoidsElement) in common construction scenarios.
conditions: The opening is typically created within a wall
exceptions: Openings can also exist in slabs, roofs, or other elements

subject: IfcRelFillsElement
rationale: The relationship semantically supports the opening by filling it, thereby completing the building element assembly.
conditions: By filling the opening, the element (door/window) provides closure and spatial separation

subject: IfcRelFillsElement
rationale: Before an opening can be filled, it must exist. IfcRelVoidsElement creates the opening in a parent element (e.g., wall, slab).
conditions: The IfcOpeningElement must first be created via IfcRelVoidsElement from a building element

subject: IfcRelFillsElement
rationale: Properly filling openings with doors and windows improves the building envelope's thermal, acoustic, and weather-tightness performance.
conditions: When the filling element provides proper sealing, insulation, and weatherproofing
exceptions: If improperly installed, it may reduce envelope performance

subject: IfcRelFlowControlElements
rationale: IfcRelFlowControlElements is an objectified relationship in IFC that links flow control elements (like valves, dampers, switches) to other flow elements (like pipes, ducts, cables). It inherently depends on IfcFlowController elements to establish the control relationship.
conditions: when defining control relationships between flow elements

subject: IfcRelFlowControlElements
rationale: The relationship connects flow control elements to distribution flow elements (pipes, ducts, conduits) within building services systems.
conditions: when relating control elements to distribution systems

subject: IfcRelFlowControlElements
rationale: IfcRelFlowControlElements can be contained within or referenced by group relationships that organize flow control elements into systems.
conditions: when used as part of a group assignment hierarchy

subject: IfcRelFlowControlElements
rationale: The relationship supports the definition of building service systems by formally establishing control dependencies between flow elements, which is essential for system behavior modeling.
conditions: when modeling building services systems like HVAC, plumbing, electrical

subject: IfcRelFlowControlElements
rationale: To properly define the flow control relationship, IfcPort connections (via IfcRelConnectsPortToElement) are typically required to establish the physical connectivity between the control element and the controlled element.
conditions: when defining connectivity between controlled elements

subject: IfcRelFlowControlElements
rationale: IfcRelFlowControlElements relates to IfcRelConnectsPortToElement to define the port-based connectivity between flow control elements and the distribution elements they control.
conditions: when establishing physical connectivity

subject: IfcRelFlowControlElements
rationale: Flow control elements (like valves or dampers) are typically placed within flow segments (pipes/ducts) to regulate flow, so the relationship depends on the existence of flow segments.
conditions: when controlling flow in a segmented distribution network

subject: IfcRelFlowControlElements
rationale: The flow control elements involved in the relationship often require property definitions (e.g., flow rate, pressure drop, control type) assigned via IfcRelDefinesByProperties to function properly in the model.
conditions: when property sets define control parameters

subject: IfcRelInterferesElements
rationale: IfcRelInterferesElements is a relationship object that connects two IfcElement instances to indicate they interfere with each other — it cannot function without the related elements.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcRelInterferesElements depends_on IfcElement' is overly broad because IfcRelInterferesElements actually references two distinct IfcElement roles (RelatingElement and RelatedElement), not just a generic IfcElement dependency. This assertion does not distinguish between the two mandatory element roles.
conditions: When interference relationships between building elements need to be tracked

subject: IfcRelInterferesElements
rationale: The relationship requires both a RelatingElement and a RelatedElement (both IfcElement subtypes) to define which two elements interfere.
applicability: The IFC schema (IFC4) defines that IfcRelInterferesElements references RelatingElement and RelatedElement as mandatory references to IfcElement. The 'RelatedElement' role is mandatory, not conditional on any specific scenario. The condition 'For the RelatedElement role in the relationship' makes it sound optional when it is in fact a required attribute.
conditions: For the 'RelatedElement' role in the relationship

subject: IfcRelInterferesElements
rationale: The relating element is the primary element in the interference relationship, required by the schema definition.
applicability: Similar to the RelatedElement assertion: the 'RelatingElement' role is a mandatory attribute of IfcRelInterferesElements in the IFC schema, not optional. The condition phrasing implies it may apply only in certain cases, which is misleading.
conditions: For the 'RelatingElement' role in the relationship

subject: IfcRelInterferesElements
rationale: IfcRelInterferesElements contains references to the two elements that interfere with each other.
conditions: When the relationship is instantiated

subject: IfcRelInterferesElements
rationale: As an IfcRoot subtype, IfcRelInterferesElements inherits the OwnerHistory attribute for tracking authorship and changes.
conditions: When persistence of the interference record is needed

subject: IfcRelNests
rationale: IfcRelNests is a subtype of IfcRelDecomposes, as is IfcRelAggregates. While IfcRelAggregates handles part-whole composition, IfcRelNests handles ordered grouping (e.g., containment within a distribution element). Understanding the relationship between the two is necessary to correctly apply nesting vs. aggregation.
conditions: When modeling hierarchical decomposition in IFC

subject: IfcRelNests
rationale: IfcRelNests relates instances of IfcObjectDefinition. Both the RelatingObject (the container/nest) and RelatedObjects (the contained items) must be IfcObjectDefinition subtypes.
conditions: When defining the RelatingObject or RelatedObjects in the nesting relationship

subject: IfcRelNests
rationale: IfcRelNests is often used to represent containment and ordering of distribution elements such as cable carriers, pipe segments within a fitting, or ducts within a chassis.
conditions: When nesting elements within a distribution system, e.g., ducts within a chassis, or cable carriers

subject: IfcRelNests
rationale: IfcRelNests can be used for ordered arrangement of structural components where the sequence or position within an assembly is important.
conditions: When nesting structural components where order matters, such as rebar within a concrete beam
exceptions: IfcRelNests is not intended for structural members according to IFC schema. IfcRelAggregates is the standard relationship for part-whole decomposition of structural members (e.g., rebar within a concrete beam uses IfcRelAggregates, not IfcRelNests). IfcRelNests is primarily used for ordered, port-based nesting in distribution systems (e.g., ports nested within distribution elements). Using IfcRelNests for structural members like rebar in a beam would violate expected IFC modeling practices.

subject: IfcRelNests
rationale: Every IFC relationship must exist within the context of an IfcProject. The IfcRelNests relationship is owned by the project and links objects that are part of the project's decomposition.
conditions: When included in a valid IFC model

subject: IfcRelProjectsElement
rationale: IfcRelProjectsElement is a relationship that projects an element (feature addition) onto a building element, so it requires a building element as the target.
conditions: When projecting elements onto building elements

subject: IfcRelProjectsElement
rationale: IfcRelProjectsElement relates a feature element addition (like a projection) to a building element; it depends on the feature element being defined.
conditions: When defining a projection relationship

subject: IfcRelProjectsElement
rationale: As an IfcRelationship subtype, it operates within an IfcProject context.
conditions: When used in a project context

subject: IfcRelProjectsElement
rationale: IfcRelProjectsElement logically contains or references a feature element addition that is being projected onto a building element.
conditions: In the context of the relationship

subject: IfcRelProjectsElement
rationale: Projections can add structural support or functional features (e.g., corbels, brackets) to building elements.
conditions: When the projection adds structural or functional benefit
exceptions: Decorative projections that do not carry load

subject: IfcRelProjectsElement
rationale: Projections and voids are complementary relationships in IFC; a projection adds material while a void removes it.
applicability: Complex building elements with both additions and voids
conditions: When the projection complements a void (e.g., adding material to fill a cutout)

subject: IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure
rationale: IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure is a relationship that assigns elements to a spatial structure element (like building, storey, space). It depends on the existence of spatial structure elements to define the reference context.
applicability: The 'depends_on' relationship is misleading: IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure has RelatingStructure (IFC4: IfcSpatialElement, IFC2x3: IfcSpatialStructureElement) and RelatedElements (SET OF IfcProduct). The relationship is from spatial element to products, so products depend on the spatial element, not the other way around. Also in IFC4 the type is IfcSpatialElement (not IfcSpatialStructureElement).
conditions: For the relationship to be established

subject: IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure
rationale: The relationship links elements (IfcElement subtypes) to spatial structure elements, so it requires elements to be referenced.
conditions: For referencing assignment

subject: IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure
rationale: Commonly used to reference building elements to a building storey without implying containment (unlike IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure).
applicability: The RelatingStructure in IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure can be any IfcSpatialElement (IFC4) or IfcSpatialStructureElement (IFC2x3), which includes IfcBuildingStorey but also IfcSpace, IfcBuilding, IfcSite, etc. The 'connects_to' phrasing with a condition of 'storey-level referencing' is incomplete - it does connect to storeys but also to many other spatial structure types.
conditions: When used for storey-level referencing

subject: IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure
rationale: Elements can be referenced to the overall building spatial structure.
applicability: Same as above - IfcBuilding is valid but not exhaustive as the sole connects_to target. The assertion is too narrow by limiting to building-level referencing only.
conditions: When used for building-level referencing

subject: IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure
rationale: Elements can be referenced to individual spaces without being physically contained.
applicability: Same as above - IfcSpace is valid but not exhaustive. The assertion is too narrow by limiting to space-level referencing only.
conditions: When used for space-level referencing

subject: IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure
rationale: The relationship requires related objects (IfcObjectDefinition) that are being referenced to the spatial structure.
conditions: For related objects parameter

subject: IfcRelSequence
rationale: IfcRelSequence is a subtype of IfcRelConnects, so it depends on the parent relationship type for its connectivity semantics.
conditions: when defining sequence relationships between building elements

subject: IfcRelSequence
rationale: IfcRelSequence defines the sequence relationship between two IfcProcess objects (predecessor and successor processes).
conditions: when specifying predecessor/successor relationships

subject: IfcRelSequence
rationale: IfcRelSequence is commonly used to relate IfcTask instances in a construction or maintenance schedule.
conditions: for construction scheduling and workflow planning

subject: IfcRelSequence
rationale: IfcRelSequence is often used within IfcWorkPlan to define the ordering of tasks.
conditions: when planning construction workflows over time

subject: IfcRelSequence
rationale: IfcRelSequence may work in conjunction with IfcRelAssignsToProcess to specify which resources are assigned to sequenced processes.
conditions: when relating resources or products to processes in a sequence

subject: IfcRelServicesBuildings
rationale: IfcRelServicesBuildings relates services (IfcSystem) to one or more IfcBuilding elements - the building is a required participant in the relationship.
conditions: Must have a referencing building element

subject: IfcRelServicesBuildings
rationale: IfcRelServicesBuildings requires at least one IfcSystem (or subtype) to define what service is related to the building.
conditions: Must have a referenced system/service

subject: IfcRelServicesBuildings
rationale: IfcRelServicesBuildings inherits from IfcRelConnects and can contain assignment relationships linking systems to buildings.
conditions: When systems are grouped and assigned to buildings

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary
rationale: IfcRelSpaceBoundary is a relationship object that connects an IfcSpace to a bounding element (e.g., wall, slab). The space is the primary entity being bounded.
conditions: The IfcRelSpaceBoundary must relate to a valid IfcSpace

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary
rationale: The relationship object binds a space to its bounding building elements such as IfcWall, IfcSlab, IfcColumn, IfcDoor, IfcWindow, etc.
applicability: The assertion 'IfcRelSpaceBoundary requires IfcBuildingElement' is misleading because the RelatedBuildingElement attribute can accept IfcVirtualElement (for virtual boundaries that are already mentioned as an exception) and also IfcExternalSpatialElement in IFC4. The existing exception about virtual boundaries is noted but the assertion title still states it requires IfcBuildingElement categorically.
conditions: The boundary is tied to a physical building element that defines the space boundary
exceptions: Virtual boundaries (e.g., for air walls) may not require a physical element

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary
rationale: IfcRelSpaceBoundary can have a 'ParentBoundary' relationship linking to a higher-level (1stLevel) space boundary for hierarchical decomposition.
applicability: Buildings requiring thermal, acoustic, or energy analysis
conditions: When detailed space boundary decomposition is used
exceptions: Not required if only first-level boundaries are used

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary
rationale: IfcRelSpaceBoundary may reference IfcConnectionGeometry to define the exact geometric surface of the boundary between space and element.
applicability: All building types with BIM Level 2/3 requirements
conditions: When geometric representation of the boundary is required
exceptions: Can function without connection geometry if only attribute-level relationships are needed

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary
rationale: IfcRelSpaceBoundary can contain an IfcConnectionSurfaceGeometry object that defines the 3D surface of the boundary.
conditions: When detailed surface geometry is associated with the boundary
exceptions: May not contain geometry if the boundary is abstract (e.g., virtual boundaries)

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary
rationale: IfcRelSpaceBoundary participates in the spatial structure of the building by relating spaces to the spatial decomposition hierarchy (site, building, story, space).
applicability: All building types with zone/space aggregation
conditions: When spaces are aggregated into zones or stories

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary
rationale: Through the IfcSpace, IfcRelSpaceBoundary indirectly supports the IfcZone grouping for thermal and functional zone analysis.
applicability: HVAC zoning, fire compartmentation, occupancy grouping
conditions: When spaces assigned to boundaries are grouped into zones

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary1stLevel
rationale: IfcRelSpaceBoundary1stLevel defines a relationship between a space and its bounding elements, so it depends on the existence of IfcSpace entities.
applicability: In IFC2x3, IfcRelSpaceBoundary1stLevel does not exist as a class; it was introduced in IFC4. For IFC2x3 models, the dependency is on IfcRelSpaceBoundary directly, not on IfcSpace via a 1stLevel subtype.
conditions: The space boundary must be assigned to a valid IfcSpace

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary1stLevel
rationale: The relationship connects spaces to bounding building elements (walls, slabs, columns, etc.) to define spatial boundaries.
conditions: The building element must physically bound the associated space

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary1stLevel
rationale: As a subtype, it inherits from and depends on the general IfcRelSpaceBoundary entity.
conditions: IfcRelSpaceBoundary1stLevel is a subtype of IfcRelSpaceBoundary

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary1stLevel
rationale: IfcRelSpaceBoundary1stLevel can contain connection surface geometry defining the physical interface between space and element.
conditions: When the boundary includes geometric representation of the interface

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary1stLevel
rationale: 1st level boundaries typically correspond to boundaries at the building storey level, supporting storey-based spatial organization.
conditions: When used to organize spaces by floor level

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary1stLevel
rationale: IfcRelSpaceBoundary1stLevel can be further decomposed into 2nd level boundaries for finer spatial subdivision.
applicability: All building types with detailed BIM

IfcRelSpaceBoundary1stLevel and IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel are alternative levels of decomposition for the same physical boundary, not connected via a 'connects_to' relationship in the IFC schema. A 2ndLevel boundary refines a 1stLevel boundary but is not a separate connected entity.
conditions: When a more detailed boundary decomposition exists

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel
rationale: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel defines relationships between spaces and their bounding elements; spaces are the primary entities being bounded.
applicability: All building types with spatial decomposition
conditions: Spaces must exist for boundary definitions

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel
rationale: 2nd level is the third tier in the space boundary hierarchy (0th, 1st, 2nd level), requiring lower-level boundaries as foundation.
applicability: Projects with multi-level space boundary hierarchies
conditions: Must be part of a hierarchical space boundary structure

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel
rationale: The 2nd level extends from the base IfcRelSpaceBoundary relationship.
conditions: Base space boundary relationships must exist

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel
rationale: Space boundaries are defined relative to building elements like walls, slabs, and columns that enclose or bound spaces.
conditions: Elements must physically bound the space

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel
rationale: Curtain walls can serve as space-bounding elements and are commonly captured in 2nd level boundaries.
conditions: When curtain wall acts as space boundary

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel
rationale: Walls are the most common space-bounding elements captured in space boundary relationships.
applicability: All building types with walled spaces
conditions: When wall acts as space boundary

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel
rationale: Slabs define horizontal space boundaries between floors.
conditions: When slab acts as floor or ceiling boundary

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel
rationale: The 2nd level provides additional precision to the basic space boundary for downstream analysis.
applicability: All IFC models with space boundaries
conditions: As part of hierarchical boundary structure

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel
rationale: 2nd level space boundaries enable more accurate space quantification and thermal/energy calculations.
conditions: For quantity takeoff and thermal analysis

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel
rationale: The relationship entity explicitly connects a space to a building element that bounds it.
conditions: Each 2nd level boundary connects one space to one bounding element

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel
rationale: 2nd level boundaries are specialized subtypes of 1st level boundaries, forming a connected hierarchy.
conditions: When 1st level boundaries exist

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel
rationale: Space boundaries can contain surface geometry defining the exact connection surface between space and element.
conditions: When geometric representation is provided

subject: IfcRelSpaceBoundary2ndLevel
rationale: The relationship entity may contain connection geometry for the bounding surface.
conditions: Optional geometric representation
exceptions: May be omitted for abstract relationships

subject: IfcRelVoidsElement
rationale: IfcRelVoidsElement is a relationship object that voids a hole in an element. It must have a 'RelatedOpeningElement' (IfcOpeningElement) that is the void and a 'RelatingBuildingElement' (IfcElement) that is being voided.
conditions: When used in a valid IFC model

subject: IfcRelVoidsElement
rationale: IfcRelVoidsElement connects an IfcOpeningElement (the void) to an IfcElement (the host). The opening element is the dependent component that represents the void itself.
conditions: When used in a valid IFC model

subject: IfcRelVoidsElement
rationale: IfcRelVoidsElement provides the void geometry and location that IfcRelFillsElement later fills with a door, window, or other building element.
applicability: All building types with doors, windows, or penetrations
conditions: When an opening is later filled by a door, window, or other filler
exceptions: Openings that remain unfilled

subject: IfcRelVoidsElement
rationale: The IfcRelVoidsElement relationship 'contains' the opening element as its RelatedOpeningElement, defining the void shape within the host element.
conditions: Always true for the relationship instance

subject: IfcRelVoidsElement
rationale: IfcRelVoidsElement requires a host IfcElement (RelatingBuildingElement) that the opening is created in. Without a host element, the void relationship has no meaning.
conditions: Must be a subtype of IfcElement that can host a void (e.g., IfcWall, IfcSlab, IfcBeam, IfcColumn)
exceptions: Some element types may not support voids

subject: IfcRelVoidsElement
rationale: IfcRelVoidsElement requires an IfcOpeningElement as the RelatedOpeningElement to define the void's geometry and properties.
conditions: Always

subject: IfcRelVoidsElement
rationale: The IfcOpeningElement typically uses IfcLocalPlacement to define its position relative to the host IfcElement, enabling coordinated void placement.
applicability: The assertion states IfcRelVoidsElement 'depends_on' IfcLocalPlacement. In IFC, IfcRelVoidsElement itself does not have a placement. The IfcOpeningElement has its own ObjectPlacement (which can be IfcLocalPlacement, IfcGridPlacement, etc.). Also, the opening element's placement may be relative to the host element via the 'PlacementRelTo' attribute, but this is not a dependency of IfcRelVoidsElement - it's a property of the opening element. This conflates the relationship with the opening element's own attributes.
conditions: When the opening element has its own placement relative to the host element

subject: IfcRelVoidsElement
rationale: The IfcOpeningElement needs a geometric representation (typically an extrusion or boolean subtraction shape) to define the void volume within the host element.
applicability: The assertion states IfcRelVoidsElement 'depends_on' IfcProductRepresentation. Similar to the placement issue, IfcRelVoidsElement itself does not have a representation. The IfcOpeningElement may have a representation, but this is not a dependency of the IfcRelVoidsElement relationship. The representation is a property of the opening element or the host element, not of the void relationship itself.
conditions: When the opening element has a 3D geometric representation

subject: IfcReparametrisedCompositeCurveSegment
rationale: This segment is designed to be part of an IfcCompositeCurve that aggregates multiple segments.
applicability: All building geometry representations using composite curves
conditions: When used as part of a composite curve definition

subject: IfcReparametrisedCompositeCurveSegment
rationale: Reparametrised segments allow consistent parameterisation across composite curves, supporting accurate geometry representation.
applicability: Curved building elements, facades, structural arches

IfcReparametrisedCompositeCurveSegment does not 'support' IfcCompositeCurve in a functional sense; it is a component contained within an IfcCompositeCurve. The assertion uses vague relational language ('supports') without specifying whether this refers to inheritance, aggregation, or functional dependency. The IFC EXPRESS schema defines IfcReparametrisedCompositeCurveSegment as a subtype of IfcCompositeCurveSegment, which itself is used in the list of segments of IfcCompositeCurve — there is no 'supports' relationship in the formal schema.
conditions: When representing complex curved building geometry

subject: IfcReparametrisedCompositeCurveSegment
rationale: As a subtype of IfcBoundedCurve, it supports bounded curve functionality.
applicability: All cases where parametric continuity is required
conditions: When the composite curve needs bounded parameterisation

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelationship is a subtype of IfcRoot in the IFC schema, so it inherits all root-level properties (GlobalId, OwnerHistory, Name, Description) and depends on these being properly defined.
conditions: When used as a fundamental element in the IFC data model hierarchy

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelationship connects IfcObjectDefinition instances (or their subtypes). It requires at least one related object to form a valid relationship.
conditions: When IfcRelationship is used to link objects

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelationship is the abstract supertype for all relationship objects; IfcRelDefinesByProperties is a concrete subtype that depends on IfcRelationship's abstract definition for its structure.
applicability: All IFC models requiring property definitions
conditions: When assigning property sets to objects

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelationship is the supertype from which IfcRelAssociates inherits; the association relationship depends on the parent relationship framework.
conditions: When linking external information (classification, document, library) to IFC objects

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelConnects is a concrete subtype of IfcRelationship that depends on the abstract relationship structure for its connectivity semantics.
applicability: All IFC models requiring spatial or physical connections
conditions: When establishing connectivity or containment between objects

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelAggregates inherits from IfcRelationship and depends on it to define aggregation relationships between objects.
conditions: When establishing part-of hierarchies

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelAssigns is a key subtype of IfcRelationship used for assignment relationships.
conditions: When assigning objects to groups, processes, or other collections

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelationship is the abstract parent that conceptually contains all subtypes including IfcRelDecomposes (which covers aggregation and nesting).
applicability: All IFC models with hierarchical decomposition
conditions: When modeling decomposition relationships

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelationship as the supertype contains the definition for association relationships within its subtype hierarchy.
conditions: When linking external references to objects

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelationship contains IfcRelConnects as one of its primary concrete subtypes.
conditions: When defining physical or logical connections

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelDeclares is a subtype of IfcRelationship used for declaring relationships in project declarations.
conditions: When declaring object types or property types in a project

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelDefines is a subtype of IfcRelationship used for type and property definitions.
conditions: When defining properties or types for objects

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelationship subtypes form the glue that connects objects within an IfcProject, supporting the overall project data model structure.
conditions: When used to define relationships within a project structure

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelAggregates and IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure (subtypes of IfcRelationship) support the spatial decomposition of buildings.
applicability: Building information models with spatial hierarchy
conditions: When establishing spatial containment (e.g., building contains storey, storey contains space)

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: Relationship objects link IfcElement instances to their containing spaces, systems, or to each other via connectivity relationships.
conditions: When relating building elements to spaces, systems, or each other

subject: IfcRelationship
rationale: IfcRelAssignsToGroup (a subtype of IfcRelationship) supports the creation of groups and systems from individual elements.
applicability: All IFC models with system grouping
conditions: When grouping elements into systems (e.g., HVAC, electrical)

subject: IfcRepresentationContext
rationale: IfcRepresentationContext is the abstract base class; IfcGeometricRepresentationContext is its primary concrete subtype used for geometric representations in 3D space.
conditions: when used for geometric representations

subject: IfcRepresentationContext
rationale: Directions are used in placement and coordinate system definitions within a representation context.
conditions: when defining axes and orientations

subject: IfcRepresentationContext
rationale: Cartesian points define the origin and positions in geometric representation contexts.
conditions: when defining origin and positions

subject: IfcRepresentationContext
rationale: IfcRepresentation is assigned to a specific IfcRepresentationContext via the ContextOfItems attribute, meaning representations are contained within a context.

subject: IfcRepresentationContext
rationale: IfcRepresentationItems are part of IfcRepresentation objects which are assigned to a representation context.

subject: IfcRepresentationContext
rationale: Representation contexts provide the coordinate space and semantics for product shape representations.
conditions: when products have shape representations

subject: IfcRepresentationContext
rationale: IfcShapeRepresentation is a subtype of IfcRepresentation that is always associated with a representation context.

subject: IfcRepresentationContext
rationale: Product definition shapes contain shape representations that reference a representation context.

subject: IfcRepresentationContext
rationale: Geometric representation contexts (world coordinate system) may conflict with projected coordinate reference systems if not properly aligned.
conditions: when mixing geometric and projected coordinate systems without proper conversion
exceptions: can coexist if proper transformations are applied

subject: IfcRepresentation
rationale: An IfcRepresentation always belongs to a specific representation context (IfcRepresentationContext) that defines the geometric or topological coordinate space.
applicability: Any building information model using IFC
conditions: Representations must be assigned to a representation context (e.g., model world, plan, or annotation)

subject: IfcRepresentation
rationale: IfcRepresentation is a collection of one or more IfcRepresentationItems that define the actual geometric or topological shape.
conditions: The representation must consist of at least one representation item

subject: IfcRepresentation
rationale: IfcRepresentation contains representation items that together describe the shape of a product.
conditions: An IfcRepresentation aggregates one or more IfcRepresentationItems

subject: IfcRepresentation
rationale: IfcRepresentation is used within IfcProductRepresentation to define the geometric representation of a product.
applicability: Any product with geometric or topological definition

The 'supports' relationship is misleading. IfcRepresentation does not support IfcProductRepresentation; rather, IfcProductRepresentation aggregates IfcRepresentation via the Representations attribute. The direction of the relationship is inverse: IfcProductRepresentation contains multiple IfcRepresentations.
conditions: When the representation is part of a product definition

subject: IfcRepresentation
rationale: IfcGeometricRepresentationSubContext further refines the coordinate space for specific views (e.g., plan, section, annotation).
applicability: Detailed IFC models with multiple view types
conditions: When used in a sub-context like plan view or model view
exceptions: Not required if only using the base representation context

subject: IfcRepresentation
rationale: IfcCoordinateOperation may be required to define transformations between the representation context's coordinate system and the world coordinate system.
applicability: Projects using map coordinates or local coordinate transformations
conditions: When the representation context involves non-identity transformation between coordinate systems
exceptions: Not needed if the representation context uses the world coordinate system directly

subject: IfcRepresentation
rationale: IfcShapeRepresentation is the most common subtype of IfcRepresentation, used for geometric shape definitions of products.
conditions: When the representation is specifically for shape definition

subject: IfcRepresentation
rationale: IfcTopologyRepresentation is another subtype of IfcRepresentation focusing on topological constructs.
conditions: When the representation defines topological relationships rather than geometry

subject: IfcRepresentation
rationale: Geometric representations often depend on IfcPlacement (e.g., IfcAxis2Placement3D) to define local coordinate systems for shape items.
conditions: For representations using local coordinate systems (e.g., object placement)
exceptions: Not required for representations that use global coordinates directly

subject: IfcRepresentation
rationale: An IfcRepresentation may contain IfcStyledItems that assign graphical styles (color, transparency, hatching) to the representation items.
conditions: When presentation information (color, texture, etc.) is associated with the representation
exceptions: May be omitted for purely analytical models

subject: IfcRepresentation
rationale: IfcRepresentation provides the geometric shape for building elements like walls, slabs, beams, enabling visualization, clash detection, and quantity takeoff.
applicability: All building elements requiring spatial definition
conditions: When the building element has a geometric representation defined

subject: IfcRepresentation
rationale: IfcRepresentation enables proxy elements to have a geometric shape, improving their utility in coordination and visualization.
conditions: When a proxy element has no standard geometric definition but needs a shape
exceptions: If the proxy is defined purely by properties with no geometry

subject: IfcRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcRepresentationItem is part of the IfcRepresentation structure in IFC schema; it is contained within IfcRepresentation as a list of representation items.

subject: IfcRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcRepresentationItem is the abstract supertype from which IfcGeometricRepresentationItem and other subtypes inherit.

subject: IfcRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcRepresentationItem is the abstract supertype that also covers topological representation items.

subject: IfcRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcRepresentationItem instances are generally aggregated within IfcRepresentation objects to form meaningful geometric or topological representations of building elements.
conditions: IfcRepresentationItem must be assigned to an IfcRepresentation to have context

subject: IfcRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcRepresentationItem forms the geometry or topology that defines the shape of IfcProduct subtypes (e.g., IfcWall, IfcSlab), enabling visualization, clash detection, and quantity takeoff.
conditions: when IfcRepresentationItem is part of a representation used to visualize or analyze a building element
exceptions: abstract or non-geometric representation items may not directly support a product

subject: IfcRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcRepresentationItem is the core element within IfcShapeRepresentation, providing the actual geometric or topological shape data.

subject: IfcRepresentationItem
rationale: Geometric IfcRepresentationItems depend on a coordinate system and precision defined by IfcGeometricRepresentationContext for correct interpretation.
conditions: when IfcRepresentationItem contains geometric data that needs coordinate reference
exceptions: topological items without geometric placement

subject: IfcRepresentationItem
rationale: Many geometric representation items rely on IfcPlacement (e.g., IfcAxis2Placement3D) to define orientation and position in space.
conditions: when the representation item is a placed geometric entity like IfcLocalPlacement
exceptions: items like IfcCartesianPoint that define implicit positions

subject: IfcRepresentationItem
rationale: IfcRepresentationItem can have associated IfcStyledItem for presentation styling, though this is optional.
conditions: when visual presentation (color, surface style) is needed
exceptions: items used only for analysis, not visualization

subject: IfcRepresentationMap
rationale: IfcRepresentationMap is a subtype of IfcRepresentation and serves as a map definition that can be reused by multiple product representations via mapped geometric representations.
conditions: when used as a map for multiple representations

subject: IfcRepresentationMap
rationale: IfcRepresentationMap is referenced by IfcMappedItem elements which place copies of the map in the model.
conditions: when used for geometric mapping
exceptions: IfcMappedItem references an IfcRepresentationMap via its MappingSource attribute, it does not mean IfcRepresentationMap 'contains' IfcMappedItem. The relationship is an inverse usage: many IfcMappedItem instances can reference the same IfcRepresentationMap. The directionality of 'contains' is inaccurate.

subject: IfcRepresentationMap
rationale: IfcRepresentationMap allows multiple products to reuse the same geometric definition, reducing redundancy.
conditions: when a product's Representation uses IfcMappedItem referencing the map

subject: IfcRepresentationMap
rationale: Type products can have an associated IfcRepresentationMap for their typical geometry.
conditions: when a type product has mapped representations

subject: IfcRepresentationMap
rationale: The IfcRepresentationMap contains a MappedRepresentation which is an IfcShapeRepresentation defining the geometry to be mapped.
conditions: as the MappedRepresentation attribute

subject: IfcResourceApprovalRelationship
rationale: IfcResourceApprovalRelationship is defined in IFC schema as a relationship that associates an approval (IfcApproval) with one or more resources (IfcResource). It depends on IfcResource entities to function properly.
conditions: The relationship must link a resource to an approval

subject: IfcResourceApprovalRelationship
rationale: IfcResourceApprovalRelationship requires IfcApproval entities as the approval object being related to the resources.
conditions: The relationship must link resources to an approval process

subject: IfcResourceApprovalRelationship
rationale: This relationship supports the approval process by linking the resources that need to be approved to the corresponding approval record.
conditions: The relationship assigns resources to an approval for review

subject: IfcResourceApprovalRelationship
rationale: The relationship can contain multiple IfcResource entities that are all subject to the same approval.
conditions: When multiple resources are linked to a single approval

subject: IfcResourceApprovalRelationship
