rationale: By formally linking resources to approvals, the relationship improves traceability and compliance management in the approval process.
conditions: When structured resource-to-approval tracking is needed

subject: IfcResource
rationale: Resources in IFC are associated with cost values to represent labor, material, and equipment costs.
conditions: For cost estimation and budgeting purposes

subject: IfcResource
rationale: IfcConstructionResource is a subtype of IfcResource used for construction labor, equipment, and material resources.
conditions: When modeling construction-specific resources

subject: IfcResource
rationale: IfcResource is assigned to IfcTask via IfcRelAssignsToProcess, indicating the resource supports the task.
applicability: All building types with construction scheduling

The relationship between IfcResource and IfcTask is indirect via IfcRelAssignsToProcess (which subtypes IfcRelAssigns). IfcResource does not directly 'support' IfcTask; rather, IfcRelAssignsToProcess assigns resources to tasks. The assertion oversimplifies the relationship.
conditions: When resources are assigned to construction or maintenance tasks

subject: IfcResource
rationale: IfcResource can be assigned to processes (IfcProcess subtypes) to indicate which resources support which activities.
applicability: Similar to the IfcTask case, IfcResource is assigned to IfcProcess via IfcRelAssignsToProcess, not a direct 'supports' relationship. The mediation through the relationship entity is missing.
conditions: When resource allocation to processes is modeled

subject: IfcResource
rationale: IfcLaborResource is a subtype of IfcConstructionResource which inherits from IfcResource, thus conceptually contained.
conditions: When labor is modeled as a resource subtype

subject: IfcResource
rationale: IfcConstructionEquipmentResource is a subtype of IfcConstructionResource (subtype of IfcResource).
conditions: When construction equipment is modeled as resources

subject: IfcResource
rationale: IfcConstructionMaterialResource is a subtype of IfcConstructionResource (subtype of IfcResource).
conditions: When construction materials are modeled as resources

subject: IfcResource
rationale: IfcRelAssignsToResource is the relationship object that connects IfcResource to actors, processes, or products.
conditions: When relationships between resources and other objects need to be formalized

subject: IfcResource
rationale: Resources are defined within the scope of an IfcProject and have no meaning outside a project context.
conditions: For resource context within a building project

subject: IfcResource
rationale: Proper resource modeling improves cost schedule accuracy by linking resources to cost items.
applicability: All building types with cost management
conditions: When detailed resource tracking is used for cost control

subject: IfcResourceConstraintRelationship
rationale: IfcResourceConstraintRelationship links resource constraint information to resources; it depends on IfcResource entities being defined.
applicability: all building projects using IFC schema
conditions: when defining resource allocation relationships

subject: IfcResourceConstraintRelationship
rationale: The relationship connects a constraint to resources, so IfcConstraint is a fundamental dependency.
applicability: all building projects using IFC schema
conditions: when defining constraint relationships

subject: IfcResourceConstraintRelationship
rationale: IfcResourceConstraintRelationship is a subtype or related to constraint association relationships in IFC.
conditions: in IFC data model hierarchy

subject: IfcResourceLevelRelationship
rationale: IfcResourceLevelRelationship is an abstract generalization in IFC schema that connects resource-level objects, primarily relating IfcResource subtypes together in hierarchical or grouped structures.
conditions: When modeling resource allocation and level relationships in BIM

subject: IfcResourceLevelRelationship
rationale: IfcResourceLevelRelationship can contain or aggregate multiple IfcResource entities in a relationship structure, such as in IfcResourceApprovalRelationship or similar subclasses.
conditions: When representing nested or grouped resource structures

subject: IfcResourceLevelRelationship
rationale: IfcResourceLevelRelationship is an abstract class that depends on IfcResource subtypes (like IfcLaborResource, IfcConstructionEquipmentResource, IfcMaterialResource) to be meaningfully instantiated.
conditions: When establishing relationships between resources
exceptions: If the relationship is abstract and not instantiated directly

subject: IfcResourceTime
rationale: IfcResourceTime defines time-related resource allocation data; it depends on IfcWorkSchedule for context of when resources are needed.
conditions: when scheduling construction tasks

subject: IfcResourceTime
rationale: IfcResourceTime describes time usage of a resource assigned to a task, so it depends on IfcTask for the task context.
conditions: when assigning resources to specific tasks

subject: IfcResourceTime
rationale: IfcResourceTime is a subtype of IfcResource, and it defines time-related quantities for that resource.
conditions: when defining resource time profiles

subject: IfcResourceTime
rationale: IfcResourceTime is typically associated with subtypes of IfcConstructionResource to define their time-dependent availability and usage.
conditions: when modeling construction resource usage over time

subject: IfcResourceTime
rationale: IfcResourceTime can define work schedules and time allocations for crew resources.
conditions: when scheduling labor crews

subject: IfcResourceTime
rationale: IfcResourceTime can specify working hours, overtime, and time allocation for labor resources.
conditions: when defining labor schedules

subject: IfcResourceTime
rationale: IfcResourceTime can define availability schedules for construction equipment.
conditions: when scheduling equipment usage

subject: IfcResourceTime
rationale: IfcResourceTime can define time-based material consumption and delivery schedules.
conditions: when tracking material delivery and usage schedules

subject: IfcResourceTime
rationale: IfcResourceTime can specify time allocations for subcontracted work.
conditions: when scheduling subcontractor work periods

subject: IfcResourceTime
rationale: IfcResourceTime supports overall project planning by providing time-based resource data needed for schedule management.
conditions: when managing project schedules and resource allocation

subject: IfcRevolvedAreaSolid
rationale: IfcRevolvedAreaSolid often depends on specific profile definitions to define the 2D shape being rotated.
conditions: When the swept profile is an arbitrary closed shape rather than a standard rectangle/circle
exceptions: Standard profiles like IfcRectangleProfileDef or IfcCircleProfileDef do not require this

subject: IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered requires an IfcAxis1Placement to define the axis around which the area is revolved.
conditions: When defining the axis of revolution

subject: IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: The tapered solid requires a starting profile definition as the base shape to be revolved.
conditions: For the starting (first) swept profile

subject: IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: The tapered solid requires an ending profile definition to create the taper between the start and end profiles.
conditions: For the ending (second) swept profile

subject: IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: The axis of revolution depends on a direction vector to define its orientation in 3D space.
conditions: For defining the axis direction within IfcAxis1Placement

subject: IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: The axis location depends on a Cartesian point to position the revolution axis in space.
conditions: For defining the axis location within IfcAxis1Placement

subject: IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: Proper positioning in the building model depends on the local placement system.
conditions: When the IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered is used within a larger object placement hierarchy

subject: IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered inherits from IfcRevolvedAreaSolid and extends it with a second profile.
conditions: As the base representation before tapering is applied

subject: IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: Both are tapered profile sweeping representations, supporting similar geometric modeling approaches.
conditions: As an alternative tapered solid representation using revolution instead of extrusion

subject: IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: For engineering analysis, material properties may be required for the tapered profiles.
conditions: When the tapered solid is part of a structural element with material assignment

subject: IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered
rationale: Using IfcRevolvedAreaSolidTapered improves the geometric representation of complex elements compared to simpler approximations.
conditions: When modeling complex non-standard tapered revolved shapes

subject: IfcRightCircularCone
rationale: A right circular cone requires a Cartesian point to define its apex location in 3D space.
conditions: When defining the apex and base center points

subject: IfcRightCircularCone
rationale: The cone requires axis placement to define its direction/orientation in 3D space.
conditions: When defining the orientation axis of the cone

subject: IfcRightCircularCone
rationale: As a geometric representation item, the cone depends on local placement for positioning within the building model.
conditions: When placing the cone within a building model coordinate system

subject: IfcRightCircularCone
rationale: The cone must be contained within a shape representation to be used as geometric representation of a building element.
conditions: When the cone is used as part of a product's geometric representation

subject: IfcRightCircularCone
rationale: The base of the cone is a circular planar surface which can be represented as a curve-bounded plane.
conditions: When the cone's base is represented as a closed face
exceptions: When the cone is part of a tessellated or BREP representation (not CSG), a face representing the base might be included, but 'contains' in the IfcRightCircularCone sense (as a CSG primitive) would not use IfcCurveBoundedPlane. In IfcCsgSolid, the primitive's base is part of the mathematical definition, not an explicit sub-entity.

subject: IfcRightCircularCone
rationale: A right circular cone may be used as a geometric representation for conical architectural elements like spires or decorative features.
applicability: Similar to the column issue - IfcRightCircularCone is a geometry primitive, not an element. It cannot have a 'connects_to' relationship with IfcBuildingElementProxy in the IFC relationship model. The geometry could be part of the proxy's representation, but the dependency direction and relationship type are incorrect.
conditions: When the cone geometry is used to represent a decorative or architectural feature

subject: IfcRightCircularCone
rationale: Conical shapes can appear in column capitals, bases, or tapered column designs.
applicability: Column design in classical or decorative architecture

IfcRightCircularCone is a geometric representation primitive (IfcCsgPrimitive3D), not a product or element. It cannot 'connect_to' IfcColumn via IFC relationships (IfcRelConnectsElements). The cone geometry could be used in the representation of a column capital, but the assertion implies a direct connection relationship between the geometry primitive and an element, which is not how IFC works.
conditions: When the cone is used as a column capital or base detail

subject: IfcRightCircularCone
rationale: The IfcRightCircularCone can be used to represent a conical roof geometry, which provides enclosure and weather protection.
applicability: Buildings with conical roofs, towers, silos

IfcRightCircularCone is a geometric representation item (subtype of IfcCsgPrimitive3D), not a building element. It cannot 'support' IfcRoof in a relational sense. In IFC, support relationships (IfcRelConnectsElements) exist between IfcElement subtypes, not between geometric primitives and elements. The cone could be a representation of a conical roof but the assertion uses 'supports' in a structural/physical connection sense that doesn't apply to geometry primitives.
conditions: When used to model a conical roof shape

subject: IfcRightCircularCone
rationale: A physical cone element requires material assignment for construction, structural analysis, and quantity takeoff.
applicability: All building types where the cone is a physical element

IfcRightCircularCone as a geometric representation item (IfcCsgPrimitive3D) does not directly depend on IfcMaterial. Material assignment in IFC happens at the product level (IfcElement) or through styled items / surface rendering, not as a dependency of the geometric primitive itself. The cone geometry primitive has no material association attribute.
conditions: When the cone represents a physical building element (e.g., concrete cone, steel cone)

subject: IfcRightCircularCone
rationale: The cone requires a geometric representation context defining the coordinate space, precision, and units of the model.
conditions: When used in a model coordinate system

subject: IfcRightCircularCylinder
rationale: IfcRightCircularCylinder is a geometric representation item that requires an axis placement to define its location and orientation in 3D space.
conditions: When defining the cylinder orientation and position in 3D space

subject: IfcRightCircularCylinder
rationale: IfcRightCircularCylinder inherits from IfcRepresentationItem and depends on being placed within a representation context.
conditions: When used as part of a product representation or shape model

subject: IfcRightCircularCylinder
rationale: The cylinder axis direction contains directional information as part of its geometric definition.
conditions: When the cylinder's axis direction is explicitly defined

subject: IfcRightCircularCylinder
rationale: The cylinder geometry supports the shape representation of building elements like columns, pipes, or ducts.
conditions: When the cylinder is used as a representation of a building element
exceptions: IfcRightCircularCylinder does not 'support' IfcShapeRepresentation in IFC. IfcShapeRepresentation is a subtype of IfcRepresentation that contains Items of type IfcRepresentationItem. IfcRightCircularCylinder (subtype of IfcRepresentationItem) participates as an Item in an IfcShapeRepresentation, but the relationship is the opposite - IfcShapeRepresentation contains IfcRightCircularCylinder, not the other way around. The direction of 'supports' is incorrect.

subject: IfcRightCircularCylinder
rationale: Circular columns are commonly represented using IfcRightCircularCylinder geometry.
conditions: When used to represent circular columns in a building model
exceptions: Non-circular columns

subject: IfcRightCircularCylinder
rationale: Circular piles can be geometrically represented as right circular cylinders.
conditions: When used to represent circular foundation piles

subject: IfcRightCircularCylinder
rationale: Straight pipe segments are often modeled as right circular cylinders.
conditions: When representing straight cylindrical pipe sections in MEP systems
exceptions: Curved or bent pipe sections

IfcPipeSegment in MEP typically uses IfcSweptDiskSolid or IfcExtrudedAreaSolid for representation in modern IFC schemas (IFC4 and later). IfcRightCircularCylinder (CSG primitive) is rarely used and often not supported by MEP authoring tools. Additionally, IfcPipeSegment often requires IfcConnectedFaceSet or other boundary representations for proper connectivity in network analysis, which IfcRightCircularCylinder does not provide.

subject: IfcRightCircularCylinder
rationale: Circular duct segments can be geometrically represented as right circular cylinders.
conditions: When representing straight circular duct sections in HVAC systems
exceptions: Rectangular ducts

IfcDuctSegment in HVAC systems is commonly represented using IfcExtrudedAreaSolid or IfcSweptDiskSolid in IFC4. IfcRightCircularCylinder (CSG primitive) is rarely used for ductwork in practice. Ducts frequently require non-circular profiles, transitions, and connections to fittings that IfcRightCircularCylinder cannot represent. The existing exception mentions only 'Rectangular ducts' but circular ducts also use SweptDiskSolid or ExtrudedAreaSolid more commonly.

subject: IfcRightCircularCylinder
rationale: Generic cylindrical elements can use this geometry representation.
conditions: When representing cylindrical building elements not covered by specific types

subject: IfcRoofType
rationale: Roofs typically require a slab or deck as a base structural layer for support.
conditions: For structural support of roof covering

subject: IfcRoofType
rationale: Roof structures often depend on beams or rafters for load distribution.
conditions: For pitched or large-span roofs requiring structural framing
exceptions: Flat roofs with concrete deck slabs or prefabricated panel systems often do not use beams for structural framing, yet are still valid IfcRoofType instances.

subject: IfcRoofType
rationale: Roofs depend on walls to transfer vertical loads to the foundation.
conditions: As load-bearing walls supporting roof edges
exceptions: Roofs supported by trusses or beams that transfer load directly to columns do not necessarily have load-bearing walls supporting the roof edges (e.g., portal frame buildings, beam-and-column structures).

subject: IfcRoofType
rationale: Columns may be required to support roof spans in large buildings.
conditions: For large-span flat roofs or roofs with internal supports
exceptions: Small-span roofs (e.g., residential gable roofs with load-bearing walls) may not require columns for support, yet are valid IfcRoofType instances.

subject: IfcRoofType
rationale: The roof structural layer supports coverings such as waterproofing membranes or insulation.
conditions: As a substrate for roof coverings
exceptions: Some roof systems are self-finishing (e.g., standing seam metal roofs, structural glazing, green roofs with integrated waterproofing) and do not have a separate IfcCoveringType as a covering layer.

subject: IfcRoofType
rationale: Roofs provide mounting surface for mechanical, electrical, and plumbing equipment.
conditions: When roof-mounted HVAC, solar panels, or mechanical units are installed
exceptions: Many roofs have no mechanical units, HVAC, solar panels, or distribution systems mounted on them (e.g., simple residential roofs, roofs in mild climates).

subject: IfcRoofType
rationale: Roofs physically connect to walls at the building perimeter.
conditions: At roof-to-wall interfaces and eaves

subject: IfcRoofType
rationale: Roofs may connect to guardrails or parapets for safety.
conditions: On accessible rooftops or roof edges requiring fall protection
exceptions: Non-accessible roofs

subject: IfcRoof
rationale: Thermal insulation in roofs reduces heat loss/gain and prevents condensation.
conditions: Must meet local thermal performance codes
Vapor barrier may be required depending on climate
exceptions: Unconditioned spaces or open shelters

Green roofs (living roofs) with intensive growing media may not require traditional insulation; the soil and vegetation layer itself provides thermal mass and R-value, potentially making separate insulation layers unnecessary in some climate zones.

subject: IfcRoof
rationale: Flashing (metal or membrane) seals transitions and penetrations to prevent water entry.
conditions: Required at all roof penetrations, valleys, and wall-roof junctions
exceptions: Single-ply membrane roofs (e.g., EPDM, TPO, PVC) with heat-welded seams and integrated flashing strips may not use separate flashing pieces; flashing can be an integral part of the membrane material rather than a distinct 'Flashing' element.

subject: IfcRoof
rationale: The roof perimeter connects to and rests upon the top of walls, transferring loads and requiring waterproof junctions.
conditions: Roof-to-wall connection must be weather-tight and structurally sound

subject: IfcRoof
rationale: In framed buildings, the roof structure is directly connected to columns.
conditions: Connection may be pinned, fixed, or sliding for thermal movement
exceptions: Buildings without columns

subject: IfcRoot
rationale: IfcRoot is the abstract base class in IFC from which IfcObjectDefinition (and all other root entities) are derived. It conceptually contains/generalizes its subtypes.
conditions: As a supertype in the IFC schema hierarchy

subject: IfcRoot
rationale: IfcRelationship is another direct subtype of IfcRoot, so IfcRoot conceptually contains this subtype as part of its inheritance tree.
conditions: As a supertype in the IFC schema hierarchy

subject: IfcRoot
rationale: IfcPropertyDefinition is a direct subtype of IfcRoot, making it part of the root hierarchy.
conditions: As a supertype in the IFC schema hierarchy

subject: IfcRoot
rationale: IfcRoot includes the OwnerHistory attribute to record who created/modified the object and when.
applicability: All IFC models requiring version tracking

The existing exception already notes that minimal or legacy IFC files may omit owner history. This is a significant exception that should make clear that the dependency is not universal but conditional on the IFC schema version and file completeness requirements.
conditions: For tracking authorship, ownership, and change history
exceptions: Minimal or legacy IFC files may omit owner history

subject: IfcRoot
rationale: IfcObject is a subtype of IfcObjectDefinition, which itself is a subtype of IfcRoot. IfcRoot provides the base identification and ownership attributes that IfcObject builds upon.
applicability: All IFC models containing physical or spatial objects
conditions: Through inheritance via IfcObjectDefinition

subject: IfcRoot
rationale: IfcProject is the top-level container in an IFC model and inherits all root-level attributes from IfcRoot.
conditions: Through the inheritance chain IfcRoot -> IfcObjectDefinition -> IfcObject -> IfcProject

subject: IfcRoot
rationale: IfcRoot subtypes (through IfcObjectDefinition) can be related to property sets via IfcRelDefinesByProperties relationships.
applicability: All IFC models with property sets
conditions: When property definitions are assigned to root entities

subject: IfcSIUnit
rationale: IfcSIUnit inherits from IfcNamedUnit which is abstract; IfcSIUnit specifies the SI unit prefix and unit name, but the actual measure value requires IfcMeasureWithUnit to associate a numeric measure with the unit.
applicability: all building information models using IFC
conditions: when defining unit definitions in IFC models

subject: IfcSIUnit
rationale: IfcSIUnit is part of the unit system where dimensional exponents define the physical quantity type (length, mass, time, etc.). IfcDimensionalExponents is referenced by IfcNamedUnit to define the dimension of the unit.
conditions: when verifying dimensional consistency of units

subject: IfcSIUnit
rationale: IfcSIUnit instances are used within IfcUnitAssignment to define the set of units used globally in an IFC model.
applicability: all IFC projects with SI unit systems
conditions: when assigning unit definitions to an IFC project

subject: IfcSIUnit
rationale: IfcSIUnit provides the standardized units needed by quantity definitions (e.g., area in square metres, volume in cubic metres).
applicability: quantity takeoffs and cost estimation in BIM

IfcQuantitySet uses IfcPhysicalQuantity subtypes (e.g., IfcQuantityLength) which reference units, but the unit reference is through IfcPhysicalQuantity.Name/Description and not directly via IfcSIUnit. The quantity definitions reference unit assignments from IfcUnitAssignment, so the relationship is indirect via IfcUnitAssignment, not a direct support relation from IfcSIUnit to IfcQuantitySet.
conditions: when quantities need standardized measurement units

subject: IfcSIUnit
rationale: IfcSIUnit can be referenced as the Unit attribute of IfcPropertySingleValue to define the unit of a measured property value.
applicability: IfcPropertySingleValue has a Unit attribute of type IfcUnit (not IfcSIUnit specifically), which means it can reference IfcSIUnit OR other unit types (IfcConversionBasedUnit, IfcDerivedUnit). The assertion is too narrow by restricting to IfcSIUnit only.
conditions: when property values include a unit specification

subject: IfcRoundedRectangleProfileDef
rationale: IfcRoundedRectangleProfileDef requires a position reference (IfcAxis2Placement2D) to define its placement in 2D space.
applicability: IfcRoundedRectangleProfileDef actually depends_on IfcAxis2Placement2D indirectly through its supertype IfcRectangleProfileDef (which inherits from IfcProfileDef). The direct dependency is via the supertype chain, not a direct attribute reference on IfcRoundedRectangleProfileDef itself.
conditions: when defining the profile coordinate system

subject: IfcRoundedRectangleProfileDef

The assertion uses 'improves' which is ambiguous in an IFC ontology context. RoundedRectangleProfileDef does not functionally 'improve' RectangleProfileDef; it is a specialized variant. The existing exception 'not applicable when sharp corners are required' is the defining scenario - it should be the primary condition, not an exception.

subject: IfcSchedulingTime

subject: IfcSchedulingTime

subject: IfcSeamCurve
rationale: IfcSeamCurve is a subtype of IfcCurve in the IFC schema, therefore it depends on the base curve entity for its definition and properties.
applicability: The assertion states IfcSeamCurve depends_on IfcCurve as a subtype of IfcCurve, but this is a standard inheritance relationship, not a domain dependency. IfcSeamCurve is defined as a subtype of IfcCurve in the IFC schema, so this dependency is inherent to the type hierarchy. The assertion may be redundant with schema inheritance.

subject: IfcSeamCurve

subject: IfcSeamCurve
rationale: As a subtype of IfcCurve which inherits from IfcRepresentationItem, it depends on the representation layer.
applicability: The assertion states IfcSeamCurve depends_on IfcRepresentationItem without conditions, but IfcSeamCurve inherits from IfcCurve -> IfcGeometricRepresentationItem -> IfcRepresentationItem, so this dependency is an indirect inheritance dependency, not a domain dependency. Every IfcCurve subtype already depends on IfcRepresentationItem by inheritance. This assertion is either redundant or misleading without clarifying that it's an inheritance-based dependency.

subject: IfcSeamCurve
rationale: Seam curves may be defined via control points or interpolation points depending on representation.

subject: IfcSeamCurve

subject: IfcSeamCurve

conditions: when modeling advanced B-rep geometry with parametric surfaces

subject: IfcSectionProperties

subject: IfcSectionProperties

subject: IfcSectionProperties

subject: IfcSectionProperties

subject: IfcSectionReinforcementProperties

In IFC4, IfcSectionReinforcementProperties has a 'ReinforcementBarProperties' attribute that references a set of IfcReinforcementBarProperties instances, but this is an aggregation reference, not a containment (part-of) relationship as typically understood in IFC (PartOf composition).

subject: IfcSectionReinforcementProperties
rationale: The reinforcement properties complement the material profile set which defines the concrete material and cross-section shape for a reinforced concrete member.

subject: IfcSectionedSpine

conditions: Each cross-section is defined by a profile definition
exceptions: IfcSectionedSpine contains cross-sections via IfcSectionedSpine.CrossSectionPositions and IfcSectionedSpine.CrossSections attributes, which reference IfcProfileDef. However, older IFC2x3 implementations or simplified representations may use IfcArbitraryClosedProfileDef without requiring IfcProfileDef subtypes, and the relationship is an aggregation not always mandatory.

subject: IfcSectionedSpine
rationale: The sectioned spine connects to material association relationships to assign materials to its cross-sections.
conditions: When material information is associated with the spine

subject: IfcSensorType
rationale: IfcSensorType defines the type information for IfcSensor occurrences; it depends on the existence of the IfcSensor entity as its instantiable occurrence.
conditions: when instantiated as a type object

subject: IfcSensorType
rationale: IfcSensorType often requires property sets (IfcPropertySet) to define sensor characteristics like range, accuracy, and measurement type.
applicability: IfcSensorType does not universally 'require' IfcPropertySet — property sets are optional in IFC. Many valid IfcSensorType instances exist without any property sets (e.g., simple type definitions with only predefined type and material). This requirement is overly strong.
conditions: when sensor properties need to be defined

subject: IfcSensorType
rationale: IfcRelDefinesByType is the relationship that associates IfcSensorType to its corresponding IfcSensor occurrences.
applicability: IfcRelDefinesByType is the relationship that goes from IfcTypeObject to IfcObject occurrences, not the other way. While IfcSensorType participates in IfcRelDefinesByType as the RelatingType, it's more accurate to say it 'is referenced by' or 'is the relating type in' IfcRelDefinesByType. The direction of 'requires' is ambiguous here.
conditions: when linking type to occurrences

subject: IfcSensorType
rationale: IfcSensorType may depend on IfcPropertySetTemplate to define the template for sensor property sets in a standardized way.
conditions: when predefined property definitions are needed

subject: IfcSensorType
rationale: IfcSensorType contains property values that define sensor attributes like measurement range, accuracy, and units.
conditions: within property sets assigned to the type

subject: IfcSensorType
rationale: Sensor types connect to controller types as part of control loops where sensor input is processed by controllers.
applicability: IfcSensorType does not directly 'connect_to' IfcControllerType in IFC schema. The connection between a sensor and a controller in a control loop is typically modeled at the occurrence level (IfcSensor and IfcController) through IfcRelConnectsElements or distribution port connections, not at the type level. Type-to-type connectivity is not a standard IFC relationship.
conditions: in a control loop configuration

subject: IfcSensorType
rationale: In building automation, sensor types connect to actuator types indirectly via controllers, where sensors measure and actuators respond.
applicability: IfcSensorType does not directly 'connect_to' IfcActuatorType in standard IFC schema. As with the controller connection, sensor-to-actuator links occur at the occurrence level (IfcSensor to IfcActuator), not at the type level. Type-level entities in IFC define templates/properties but do not participate in connectivity relationships.
conditions: through a control system chain

subject: IfcShadingDevice
rationale: Shading devices require structural support from the building elements they are attached to.
conditions: When attached to a building's exterior envelope
exceptions: Freestanding shading devices not directly connected to structural elements

subject: IfcShadingDevice
rationale: Shading devices are physical objects that require materials (e.g., metal, wood, fabric, glass) for construction.
conditions: For fabrication and installation

subject: IfcShadingDevice
rationale: Mechanical attachment to the building typically requires brackets, bolts, screws, or other fasteners.
conditions: When mechanically fixed to a building surface
exceptions: Freestanding or self-supporting shading structures

subject: IfcShadingDevice
rationale: Shading devices can support photovoltaic panels or solar thermal collectors, creating a dependency for combined functionality.
conditions: In integrated renewable energy systems

subject: IfcShadingDevice
rationale: Shading devices protect windows from direct solar radiation, reducing glare and solar heat gain.

subject: IfcShadingDevice
rationale: Complex shading devices (e.g., brise-soleil, louvers) may consist of multiple parts such as blades, frames, and support arms.

subject: IfcShadingDevice

subject: IfcShadingDevice

subject: IfcShapeAspect

Even when defined in the context of a product, IfcShapeAspect does not 'depend_on' IfcProduct directly. It is associated via IfcProductDefinitionShape. The existing exception correctly identifies that the aspect can be defined independently, but the core relationship is still indirect — through IfcProductDefinitionShape, not a direct dependency on IfcProduct.

subject: IfcShadingDeviceType

exceptions: standalone shading devices not associated with specific windows

Window-attached shading devices (like overhangs above windows) in IFC are typically represented using IfcRelAttachesToElement or IfcRelFillsElement relationships between IfcShadingDevice instances and IfcWindow instances, not at the type level (IfcShadingDeviceType). Type-level dependency (IfcShadingDeviceType depends_on IfcWindow) is not a standard IFC pattern because type definitions are independent of occurrence-level attachments. The assertion applies a relationship at the type level that only exists at the instance level.

subject: IfcShadingDeviceType

The 'depends_on' relationship is only applicable when a subcontext has been defined and assigned. This is a specific case, not a general dependency.

subject: IfcShapeRepresentation

subject: IfcShapeRepresentation

conditions: Proxy elements also need shape representations for geometry definition

subject: IfcShapeRepresentation

subject: IfcSlabElementedCase

subject: IfcSlabStandardCase

subject: IfcSlabStandardCase
rationale: The structural and functional behavior of slabs depends on their material layering configuration.
applicability: composite steel deck slabs, built-up floor constructions

IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage requires an IfcMaterialLayerSet to be defined first. The assertion correctly states the dependency in principle, but should clarify that IfcMaterialLayerSet (not just SetUsage) is the prerequisite definition, and this applies only when the slab references material layers via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial.
conditions: when slab is a layered construction (e.g., composite deck, built-up floor)

subject: IfcSlabStandardCase
rationale: Slab standard cases require associated property sets to define performance attributes like fire resistance and load rating.
applicability: all building types under regulatory compliance
conditions: when slab property definitions (fire rating, load capacity) are needed for design compliance

subject: IfcSlabType
rationale: IfcSlabType is the type definition (entity) that defines common properties for IfcSlab occurrences. It requires the IfcSlab entity to instantiate actual slab elements.
conditions: When IfcSlabType is used as a type definition for slab elements

subject: IfcSlabType
rationale: Slab types often depend on material layer set definitions to specify their composition (e.g., concrete + insulation + finish layers).
applicability: The assertion states IfcSlabType depends_on IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage, but material layering can also be represented via IfcMaterialLayer (without set usage) or IfcMaterialList in some workflows. The dependency should account for these alternative material representations.
conditions: When slab has layered construction
exceptions: Monolithic slabs without layers

subject: IfcSlabType
rationale: Slabs (floors/roofs) provide structural support for walls above them.
applicability: All building types with load-bearing slabs
conditions: When walls are supported by the slab
exceptions: Non-load-bearing walls supported directly by foundation

subject: IfcSlabType
rationale: Slab surfaces support floor finishes, tiles, screeds, or roof membranes applied as coverings.
conditions: When floor or roof covering is applied on top of slab
exceptions: Exposed structural slabs without finishes

subject: IfcSlabType
rationale: Slabs act as supporting surfaces for furniture, fixtures, and equipment loads.
conditions: When furniture or equipment is placed on slab surface

subject: IfcSlabType
rationale: Slabs (especially roof slabs) protect interior spaces from weather, and floor slabs provide separation between spaces.
applicability: IfcSlabType protects_from IfcSpace only when the slab is a flooring slab forming the lower boundary of the space above or a roof slab forming the upper boundary. Intermediate slabs (e.g., mezzanine structural slabs not serving as space boundaries) may not participate in IfcSpace containment. The applicability should be restricted to space-bounding slabs.
conditions: When slab forms horizontal boundary of a space

subject: IfcSlabType
rationale: Reinforced concrete slabs contain rebar (reinforcing bars) embedded within the concrete matrix.
conditions: When slab is made of reinforced concrete
exceptions: Timber slabs
Steel deck slabs without rebar

The assertion 'IfcSlabType contains IfcReinforcingBar' does not cover slabs with welded wire fabric (WWF) or welded wire mesh, which is a common reinforcement type for slabs-on-grade and light-duty slabs. WWF is typically modeled as IfcReinforcingMesh, not IfcReinforcingBar. This is a missing exception for wire mesh reinforced slabs.

subject: IfcSlabType
rationale: Post-tensioned slabs contain tendons (cables/strands) for pre-stressing.
conditions: When slab is post-tensioned or pre-stressed
exceptions: Non-post-tensioned slabs

subject: IfcSlabType
rationale: HVAC duct segments can be embedded within slab construction (e.g., in slab-on-grade or concrete void slabs).
conditions: When ducts are embedded within slab depth
exceptions: Ducts routed below slab

subject: IfcSlabType
rationale: In typical framed structures, slabs connect to and are supported by beams.
conditions: When slab is supported by beams
exceptions: Flat slabs without beams
Flat plates

subject: IfcSlabType
rationale: Slabs connect to columns (either directly in flat slabs or through beams) to transfer vertical loads to foundation.
conditions: When slab transfers loads to columns directly or via beams

subject: IfcSlabType
rationale: Openings in slabs disrupt the structural continuity and require special detailing to maintain structural integrity.
conditions: When openings (e.g., stairwells, shafts) are cut through slabs
exceptions: Pre-planned openings with edge stiffening

subject: IfcSlippageConnectionCondition
rationale: IfcSlippageConnectionCondition is a type of connection condition entity in IFC used to define slippage behavior in structural connections; it depends on a structural connection element to be applied to.
conditions: when slippage needs to be estimated or modeled

subject: IfcSlippageConnectionCondition
rationale: IfcSlippageConnectionCondition is a subtype of IfcStructuralConnectionCondition and inherits its properties and dependencies.
applicability: While IfcSlippageConnectionCondition is indeed a subtype of IfcStructuralConnectionCondition, this class is only defined in IFC4x3 and later (via IfcStructuralAnalysisDomain). It is not available in IFC2x3 or IFC4. The applicability 'all building types' is misleading because it is only available in recent IFC schema versions and within structural analysis contexts.

subject: IfcSlippageConnectionCondition
rationale: Connection conditions in IFC are typically associated with structural members through relationship entities like IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember.
applicability: IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember relates a structural member to a structural connection (via the 'RelatedStructuralConnection' attribute of type IfcStructuralConnection), not to an IfcSlippageConnectionCondition directly. IfcSlippageConnectionCondition is assigned to the connection (as a condition), not directly linked via IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember. The connection condition is typically referenced via the 'AppliedCondition' attribute of IfcStructuralConnection or IfcStructuralMember, not through IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember.
conditions: when linking connection conditions to structural members

subject: IfcSolidModel
rationale: IfcSolidModel is the abstract supertype; IfcManifoldSolidBrep is a common subtype providing boundary representation.
conditions: When representing boundary representation geometry

subject: IfcSolidModel
rationale: IfcSweptAreaSolid is another key subtype of IfcSolidModel for extruded/rotated shapes.
conditions: When using swept solid geometry

subject: IfcSolidModel
rationale: IfcBooleanResult is a subtype of IfcSolidModel for CSG modeling.
conditions: When performing Boolean operations on solids

subject: IfcSolidModel
rationale: IfcCsgSolid is a subtype of IfcSolidModel for CSG representation.
conditions: When using Constructive Solid Geometry

subject: IfcSolidModel
rationale: IfcSolidModel is used as the geometry representation item for solid body representations of building elements.
conditions: When the representation identifier is 'Body' or 'Solid'

subject: IfcSolidModel
rationale: IfcSolidModel provides the geometric shape for product definitions.
conditions: When a building element has a solid geometry

subject: IfcSolidModel
rationale: IfcSolidModel can contain or relate to face/shell structures as part of its boundary representation.
conditions: When the solid model is decomposed into faces

subject: IfcSolidModel
rationale: IfcManifoldSolidBrep (a subtype of IfcSolidModel) contains IfcClosedShell to define its boundary.
conditions: When using boundary representation (B-rep)

subject: IfcSolidModel
rationale: Swept solids inherit placement from IfcSweptAreaSolid which uses IfcAxis2Placement3D.
conditions: When IfcSweptAreaSolid requires local coordinate placement

subject: IfcSolidModel
rationale: IfcExtrudedAreaSolid is the most common swept area solid subtype used for building elements.
conditions: When using extrusion as the solid modeling method

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Spaces require doors for entry, exit, and circulation between spaces.
applicability: The assertion states 'all buildings' as applicability, but some codes allow spaces that are not enclosed or have alternative egress (e.g., open balconies, roof terraces). The 'all buildings' scope is too broad.
conditions: for access and egress
exceptions: Building codes (e.g., IBC) allow mezzanines, open-plan areas, or very small spaces (e.g., phone booths, tiny closets) that are accessible directly from an exterior door or are not enclosed, thus requiring no IfcDoor. Also, some spaces like attics or crawlspaces may have hatches rather than doors.

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Windows provide daylight and natural ventilation to occupied spaces.
conditions: if space requires natural light or ventilation
exceptions: windowless spaces such as server rooms, storage

Interior occupied spaces in certain building types (e.g., movie theaters, auditoriums, museums with light-sensitive exhibits) are occupied but intentionally designed without windows. The existing exceptions only list server rooms and storage, missing these common cases.

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Spaces intended for occupancy typically require heating devices.
conditions: for thermal comfort in conditioned spaces
exceptions: unconditioned spaces like corridors, stairwells

Occupied and habitable spaces can be thermally conditioned via radiant floor systems, ducted HVAC without local space heaters, or centralized systems that do not use IfcSpaceHeater instances. Thermal comfort does not imply the presence of IfcSpaceHeater.

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Each space belongs to a specific building storey, which defines its vertical location.
conditions: for vertical positioning and floor level assignment

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Space boundaries link spaces to walls, floors, ceilings, and other bounding elements.
conditions: for defining relationships to building elements

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Spaces may be aggregated into zones for systems analysis and energy simulation.
conditions: for grouping spaces with similar thermal or functional requirements
exceptions: spaces not assigned to any zone

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: This relationship links IfcSpace to its parent spatial structure element (e.g., storey).
conditions: for correct spatial containment hierarchy
exceptions: IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure is not strictly required for spatial containment hierarchy in all IFC models — some models use IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure instead for referencing without containment, or use IfcRelAggregates for certain spatial decompositions.

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Spaces provide the functional volume for occupants to perform activities.
conditions: when space is occupied
exceptions: unoccupied storage or equipment spaces

Not all occupied spaces have IfcOccupant — temporary occupancy (e.g., airport waiting areas, transit stations, public lobbies) may have transient occupants not modeled as IfcOccupant. IfcOccupant typically represents organizational tenants or resident owners, not all people in a space.

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Spaces contain and support the arrangement of furniture.
conditions: for interior furnishing of spaces

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Spaces accommodate distribution elements like ducts, pipes, and cables.
conditions: for HVAC, electrical, plumbing distribution within the space

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Furniture items are physically located within and contained by spaces.

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Air terminals, diffusers, and other flow terminals are contained within spaces.

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Spaces are bounded and protected by walls that separate interior from exterior and between spaces.
applicability: 'protects_from' is not a standard IFC relationship. IfcSpace does not protect IfcWall — rather, IfcWall bounds IfcSpace via IfcRelSpaceBoundary. The directionality is reversed in standard IFC semantics.
conditions: as bounding elements of the space

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Coverings protect the underlying structure and provide a finished surface within the space.
applicability: The relationship 'protects_from' is non-standard. IfcCovering does cover or finish IfcSpace surfaces, but 'protects_from' implies the space protects the covering, which is semantically reversed from the IFC view where coverings are finishes applied to the space's bounding elements.
conditions: floor, wall, and ceiling coverings
exceptions: unfinished spaces

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Most interior spaces require artificial lighting for visibility and tasks.
conditions: for artificial lighting in spaces without adequate daylight
exceptions: daylit-only spaces or storage

Some occupied spaces may use emergency-only lighting or have specific lighting integrated into furniture or architectural features (e.g., cove lighting) rather than distinct IfcLightFixture instances. Also, building code egress lighting requirements might be met by self-luminous exit signs or emergency path marking, not IfcLightFixture.

subject: IfcSpace
rationale: Spaces on different floors are connected via vertical transport elements.
conditions: elevators, escalators, ramps connecting spaces across storeys
exceptions: single-storey buildings

In multi-storey buildings, adjacent spaces on different floors may connect via interior stairs (IfcStair, not IfcTransportElement) or via ramps that are part of the floor slab. Also, dumbwaiters and material lifts are IfcTransportElement types but may not connect occupied spaces.

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: Hydronic space heaters require a boiler or heat pump (IfcEnergyConversionDevice) to supply hot water or steam for heat delivery.
conditions: When space heater is hydronic type
exceptions: Electric resistance space heaters do not require central energy conversion devices

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: Space heaters need connection ports for piping, wiring, or duct connections.
conditions: When connected to a hydronic or steam system
exceptions: Electric resistance heaters may not require fluid ports

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: Hot water or steam space heaters require piping to transport heating fluid.
conditions: Hydronic or steam space heaters
exceptions: Electric space heaters do not require piping

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: Valves and control valves regulate flow to the space heater.
conditions: When part of a hydronic distribution system
exceptions: Simple electric heaters may not need valves

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: A space heater serves a specific thermal zone or room (IfcSpace) and is typically located within that space.
conditions: Always

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: The space heater is typically connected to a heating distribution system.
conditions: When part of a central heating system
exceptions: Standalone electric space heaters may not belong to a distribution system

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: A space heater provides heat to maintain thermal comfort in a zone.
conditions: When the heater serves a designated thermal zone

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: Space heaters support the overall building heating function by providing localized or supplemental heat.
conditions: When heater contributes to overall building heating

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: Many space heaters contain a heat exchanger surface (fins, coils) to transfer heat from the heating medium to the air.
applicability: The assertion says IfcSpaceHeater 'contains' IfcHeatExchanger for fan coil units, radiators, or convectors. However, many radiators and convectors do not contain a discrete IfcHeatExchanger element — the heat exchange occurs directly via the radiator/convector body itself, which is already classified as IfcSpaceHeater. The assertion over-applies the decomposition to simple radiator types.
conditions: When space heater is a fan coil unit, radiator, or convector
exceptions: Simple electric resistance heaters may not contain a separate heat exchanger element

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: Fan-forced space heaters include an internal fan to circulate air across the heating element.
conditions: When space heater is a fan-forced unit
exceptions: Natural convection radiators and baseboard heaters do not contain fans

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: Space heaters connect to supply and return piping or electrical circuits via ports.
conditions: For supply and return connections
exceptions: Electric heaters connect to electrical ports rather than fluid ports

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: Space heaters connect to pipe fittings for branching or joining the piping system.
conditions: When part of a piping network
exceptions: Electric space heaters

The existing exception only mentions 'Electric space heaters' but there are also steam space heaters that may connect directly to steam piping via flanges without intermediate IfcPipeFitting elements. Additionally, hydronic systems sometimes use direct pipe-to-heater connections using unions integrated into the heater valve, not separate IfcPipeFitting instances.

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: Space heaters may conflict with unitary HVAC equipment if both heat and cool the same space without coordination.
conditions: When both attempt to serve the same thermal zone without proper zoning controls
exceptions: If properly integrated via a building management system

subject: IfcSpaceHeater
rationale: Certain space heater types (combustion) are unsuitable for humid or clean environments due to corrosion or contamination risks.
conditions: In spaces with high humidity or where combustion products must be avoided (for gas-fired units)
exceptions: Electric or hydronic heaters are suitable in those spaces

subject: IfcSpaceHeaterType
rationale: IfcSpaceHeaterType defines the type information for IfcSpaceHeater instances, so it requires the occurrence entity to function.
applicability: All building types with hydronic heating systems
conditions: when functioning as a terminal heating device

subject: IfcSpaceHeaterType
rationale: Space heaters require a distribution system (typically hot water or steam piping) to deliver the heating medium.
conditions: hydronic heating system must be present
exceptions: An IfcSpaceHeaterType can exist in a model for cataloging or specification purposes even where no distribution system is modeled (e.g., early design phase, product library). The hydronic system condition is already stated but the assertion should also note this broader exception.

subject: IfcSpaceHeaterType
rationale: Hydronic space heaters require supply and return piping for hot water or steam.
conditions: for hydronic space heaters
exceptions: electric space heaters do not require piping

subject: IfcSpaceHeaterType
rationale: Valves and flow controllers regulate the flow of heating medium through the space heater.
conditions: for hydronic systems requiring flow regulation

subject: IfcSpaceHeaterType
rationale: Space heaters provide heat to maintain thermal comfort within specific zones or spaces.
conditions: when used for space heating in a thermal zone

subject: IfcSpaceHeaterType
rationale: Space heaters deliver heat to indoor spaces to maintain desired temperature conditions.
conditions: where the space heater is installed

subject: IfcSpaceHeaterType
rationale: If the space heater is installed within a wall opening or niche, it requires that opening relationship.
applicability: Buildings with recessed or in-wall space heaters
conditions: when space heater is placed in an opening

subject: IfcSpaceHeaterType
rationale: IfcSpaceHeaterType relies on property sets to define its technical parameters (heating capacity, pressure drop, etc.).
conditions: for defining performance characteristics like heat output, dimensions, and flow rate

subject: IfcSpaceHeaterType
rationale: Space heaters may require enclosure elements for safety or aesthetics.
conditions: when used as part of architectural enclosure or trim

subject: IfcSpaceHeaterType
rationale: The type relationship is essential for linking IfcSpaceHeaterType to IfcSpaceHeater instances.
applicability: All IFC models using type definitions
conditions: to associate the type with occurrences

subject: IfcSpaceHeaterType
rationale: IfcSpaceHeaterType contains property set definitions that apply to all occurrences of that type.
conditions: type-level property definitions

subject: IfcSpaceHeaterType
rationale: Protective covers may be needed to prevent burns from hot surfaces of space heaters.
applicability: Buildings with exposed hot surface space heaters in occupied areas
conditions: when safety covers or guards are required

subject: IfcSpaceHeaterType
rationale: Space heaters connect to piping systems via fittings such as elbows, tees, and unions.
applicability: IfcSpaceHeaterType is a type entity (IfcTypeObject) and does not directly 'connect_to' IfcPipeFitting. Pipe connections occur at the occurrence level (IfcSpaceHeater instances) using IfcRelConnectsPorts or IfcRelConnectsPathElements, not at the type definition level.
conditions: for hydronic space heater connections to piping system
exceptions: electric space heaters

subject: IfcSpaceType
rationale: Relationship entity used to assign boundaries to an IfcSpace.
conditions: for assigning boundaries to spaces

subject: IfcSpaceType
rationale: Spaces are typically contained within building storeys.
conditions: when space is part of a building story
exceptions: attic or roof-level spaces not on a storey

subject: IfcSpaceType
rationale: An IfcZone is a group of spaces, and an IfcSpaceType can be part of a zone.
conditions: when grouping spaces into zones

subject: IfcSpaceType
rationale: Spaces support grouping for analysis (e.g., HVAC zones, fire compartments).
conditions: when assigning spaces to groups like zones or systems

subject: IfcSpaceType
rationale: This relationship is required to place the space within the building spatial hierarchy.
conditions: to relate space to its containing spatial structure element

subject: IfcSpaceType
rationale: Spaces may require openings, but not all spaces have voids.
conditions: if space includes voids like openings or shafts
exceptions: spaces without voids

subject: IfcSpaceType
rationale: Coverings define the finished surfaces of a space but are not mandatory for all space types.
conditions: for finishing of space surfaces (floor, wall, ceiling coverings)
exceptions: unfinished spaces like service voids

subject: IfcSpaceType
rationale: Functional spaces generally require lighting for usability.
conditions: for occupied spaces requiring illumination
exceptions: unoccupied spaces like crawl spaces

subject: IfcSpaceType
rationale: Occupied spaces need HVAC for thermal comfort and air quality.
conditions: for conditioned spaces requiring heating, ventilation, or cooling
exceptions: unconditioned spaces like storage or parking

subject: IfcSpaceType
rationale: Spaces connect via doors for circulation.
conditions: for access between spaces or to outside
exceptions: spaces without doors like open-plan areas

subject: IfcSpaceType
rationale: Windows connect spaces to the exterior for light and air.
applicability: perimeter spaces in all building types
conditions: for natural light and ventilation
exceptions: interior spaces without exterior walls

subject: IfcSpaceType
rationale: Spaces often contain furniture and equipment.
conditions: when space is furnished
exceptions: empty or shell spaces

subject: IfcSpaceType
rationale: Flow terminals like diffusers and vents are contained within spaces.
conditions: for air diffusers, lighting fixtures, etc.
exceptions: spaces without mechanical systems

subject: IfcSpatialElement
rationale: IfcSpatialElement relies on IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure to establish containment relationships between building elements and spatial elements.
applicability: All IFC models using spatial decomposition
conditions: when used in a spatial structure hierarchy

subject: IfcSpatialElement
rationale: IfcSpatialElement uses IfcRelAggregates to define the hierarchical spatial structure (site, building, storey, space).
applicability: All IFC models using spatial decomposition
conditions: when used in a spatial decomposition hierarchy

subject: IfcSpatialElement
rationale: Spatial elements such as spaces and storeys contain building elements like columns, walls, and slabs via containment relationships.
conditions: when IfcSpatialElement is a subtype like IfcSpace or IfcBuildingStorey

subject: IfcSpatialElement
rationale: Spaces contain furniture and equipment elements.
conditions: when IfcSpatialElement is IfcSpace

subject: IfcSpatialElement
rationale: Spatial elements provide the spatial context and boundaries that support the proper placement and orientation of building elements.
conditions: when the spatial element defines the bounding geometry for building elements

subject: IfcSpatialElement
rationale: Spatial elements depend on local placement definitions to position themselves within the project coordinate system.
conditions: when placement within a spatial hierarchy is needed
exceptions: IfcSpatialElement can also use IfcGridPlacement (e.g., IfcSite positioned via a grid) or IfcLinearPlacement (e.g., IfcSpatialZone along a linear infrastructure alignment). Not all placements require IfcLocalPlacement.

subject: IfcSpatialElement
rationale: Spatial elements (specifically IfcSpace) can be grouped into zones for energy, lighting, or safety purposes.
applicability: HVAC zoning, fire safety analysis, facility management
conditions: when used for grouping spaces for analysis or services

subject: IfcSpatialElement
rationale: Spatial elements may have coverings (walls, floors, ceilings) that protect internal conditions from environmental factors.
conditions: when spatial element boundaries are finished or protected with coverings
exceptions: only applicable to IfcSpace surfaces

subject: IfcSpatialElement
rationale: IfcSpatialElement (especially IfcSpace) requires space boundary relationships to define its physical limits and interactions with building elements.
applicability: Thermal analysis, lighting simulation, quantity take-off
conditions: when physical boundaries between spaces and elements must be defined

subject: IfcSpatialElement
rationale: Spatial elements can reference building elements that are not physically contained but are associated with that spatial context.
applicability: All IFC models using spatial references
conditions: when referencing elements that are not physically contained but associated

subject: IfcSpatialElement
rationale: Spatial elements may contain openings (doors, windows, voids) within their spatial footprint.
applicability: IfcOpeningElement is typically contained in IfcBuildingElement (e.g., IfcWall, IfcSlab) via IfcRelVoidsElement, not directly contained in IfcSpatialElement. While IfcOpeningElement can be spatial-decomposed under IfcBuildingStorey in some reference views, the primary relationship is voiding an element, not containment by a spatial element. The assertion may be misleading without clarifying the indirect nature.
conditions: when IfcSpatialElement is IfcBuildingStorey or IfcSpace

subject: IfcSpatialElementType
rationale: IfcSpatialElementType is the type definition for IfcSpatialElement, which is the abstract supertype for all spatial elements like spaces, zones, buildings, storeys. The type definition depends on the existence of the spatial element concept.
conditions: When classifying spatial elements in the IFC data model

subject: IfcSpatialElementType
rationale: The IfcSpatialElementType hierarchy includes IfcSpaceType, which defines types of spaces (e.g., rooms, areas) and contains the definition for IfcSpace entities.
conditions: When the spatial element type is related to space classification

subject: IfcSpatialElementType
rationale: IfcSpatialElementType includes IfcBuildingStoreyType, defining types of building storeys.
conditions: When the spatial element type is related to storey classification

subject: IfcSpatialElementType
rationale: IfcSpatialElementType includes IfcBuildingType, defining types of buildings (e.g., residential, commercial).
conditions: When the spatial element type is related to building classification

subject: IfcSpatialElementType
rationale: IfcSpatialElementType includes IfcSiteType, defining types of sites.
conditions: When the spatial element type is related to site classification

subject: IfcSpatialElementType
rationale: IfcSpatialElementType includes IfcZoneType (where applicable in the IFC schema), defining types of zones for grouping spaces.
conditions: When the spatial element type is related to zone classification

subject: IfcSpatialElementType
rationale: IfcSpatialElementType instances are linked to their occurrences (IfcSpatialElement entities) via the IfcRelDefinesByType relationship, which depends on the type definition to classify spatial elements.
conditions: When relating type definitions to spatial element occurrences

subject: IfcSpatialElementType
rationale: Types in IFC often have associated property set definitions (IfcPropertySetDefinition) that define the properties applicable to all occurrences of that type.
conditions: When defining property sets for the spatial element type

subject: IfcSpatialElementType
rationale: Spatial element types may be associated with materials through material definitions, but this is more common for physical elements rather than spatial types.
applicability: IfcSpatialElementType can have material associations via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, but in IFC4 this is more commonly handled through IfcMaterialLayerSetUsage or aggregated material sets on the type. However, spatial element types (e.g., IfcSpaceType) are less likely to have material layer associations compared to IfcElementType subtypes (e.g., IfcWallType). The assertion should clarify that material association for spatial element types is atypical in practice.
conditions: When the spatial element type has an associated material layer or assembly

subject: IfcSpatialElementType
rationale: IfcSpatialElementType supports the aggregation relationships (IfcRelAggregates) that structure spatial elements into a hierarchy (site contains building, building contains storey, storey contains space).
conditions: When spatial elements are aggregated into spatial structures

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElement
rationale: IfcSpatialStructureElement is the abstract supertype for spatial structures that contain spaces (IfcSpace) and other spatial elements.
conditions: when functioning as a container for spatial organization

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElement
rationale: IfcSpatialStructureElement is the generalization that includes IfcBuildingStorey as a subtype.

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElement
rationale: IfcSpatialStructureElement is the abstract supertype that contains IfcBuilding.

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElement
rationale: IfcSpatialStructureElement is the abstract supertype that contains IfcSite.

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElement
rationale: IfcSpatialStructureElement can contain spatial zones as part of the decomposition structure.
conditions: when used for spatial organization grouping

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElement
rationale: IfcSpatialStructureElement depends on IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure relationship to associate building elements with the spatial structure.

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElement
rationale: IfcSpatialStructureElement depends on IfcRelAggregates for decomposition into sub-spatial structures (e.g., building decomposed into storeys).

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElement
rationale: IfcSpatialStructureElement can depend on this relationship for referencing elements without containment.
conditions: when elements are referenced rather than contained

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElement
rationale: Spatial structure elements typically require placement information to define their location in the project coordinate system.
conditions: when spatial position is defined
exceptions: optional if placement is inherited or not specified

The existing exception states 'optional if placement is inherited or not specified', but IfcSpatialStructureElement does not always have its own IfcObjectPlacement — for example, IfcSite typically inherits placement from the project coordinate system, and IfcBuilding may inherit from IfcSite. The assertion should more clearly reflect that placement is often inherited rather than directly specified.

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElement
rationale: IfcSpatialStructureElement inherits from IfcObject and is part of the project spatial structure, requiring the project context.
applicability: IfcSpatialStructureElement depends on IfcProject only indirectly — IfcProject is the root of the entire IFC model, not specifically of the spatial decomposition hierarchy. The spatial decomposition hierarchy root is typically IfcSite (or IfcBuilding for simpler projects). IfcProject contains spatial structure elements via IfcRelAggregates, but the dependency is not specific to spatial decomposition as stated.
conditions: as the root of the spatial decomposition hierarchy

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElement
rationale: Spatial structure elements support the definition of space boundaries for spaces contained within them.
conditions: when defining space boundaries

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElement
rationale: Spatial structure elements may participate in interference detection relationships.
conditions: when spatial interference checking is performed

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElementType
rationale: IfcSpatialStructureElementType depends on the aggregation relationship (IfcRelAggregates) to define the hierarchical decomposition of spatial elements (site, building, storey, space).
conditions: when decomposing spatial structure into parts

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElementType
rationale: Spatial structure elements depend on containment relationships to hold building elements like walls, slabs, and columns within spaces, storeys, or buildings.
conditions: when containing building elements within spatial structure

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElementType
rationale: IfcSpatialStructureElementType includes subtypes like IfcSpaceType, which define the type of spatial elements that contain spatial boundaries and zones.
conditions: when type is IfcSpaceType

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElementType
rationale: The spatial structure element type includes building storey types, representing vertical levels that contain spaces and building elements.
conditions: when type is IfcBuildingStoreyType

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElementType
rationale: The spatial structure element type includes site types, which define the land parcel containing buildings.
conditions: when type is IfcSiteType

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElementType
rationale: The spatial structure element type includes building types as a top-level spatial container.
conditions: when type is IfcBuildingType

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElementType
rationale: IfcSpatialStructureElementType may include spatial zone types for grouping spaces functionally (e.g., fire zones, rental zones).
conditions: when type is IfcSpatialZoneType

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElementType
rationale: The spatial structure element type supports the definition of space boundaries, which relate spaces to physical building elements.
conditions: when defining spatial boundaries of spaces

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElementType
rationale: Spatial structure element types depend on object placement definitions to locate spatial elements in 3D space relative to the project coordinate system.
conditions: when defining the local placement of spatial elements

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElementType
rationale: Spatial elements are typically placed using IfcLocalPlacement relative to their container (e.g., a storey placed relative to a building).
conditions: when spatial element has a relative placement within a parent spatial structure

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElementType
rationale: Spatial structure element types support the assignment of building service systems to the spatial elements they serve.
conditions: when systems or zones are assigned to spatial structure

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElementType
rationale: All IFC entities require owner history for tracking authorship and versioning of spatial structure element type definitions.
conditions: when creating instances of spatial structure element types

subject: IfcSpatialStructureElementType
rationale: IfcSpatialStructureElementType depends on IfcRelDefinesByType to associate type properties (e.g., predefined type enums) with spatial structure occurrences.
conditions: when assigning the type to occurrences

subject: IfcSpatialZone
rationale: An IfcSpatialZone can aggregate IfcSpaces into a logical grouping (e.g., a fire zone, rental zone, or security zone) even if the spaces are not physically contiguous.
conditions: when the spatial zone is defined as a grouping of spaces

subject: IfcSpatialZone
rationale: IfcSpatialZone can nest or contain other spatial zones (via IfcRelAggregates or IfcRelNests) to create hierarchical groupings.

subject: IfcSpatialZone
rationale: The assignment of elements to a spatial zone is done via IfcRelAssignsToGroup, so the zone depends on this relationship to define its members.

subject: IfcSpatialZone
rationale: An IfcSpatialZone can group any product (IfcProduct) including building elements like walls, slabs, columns, etc., for analytical or functional purposes.
conditions: when the element is assigned to the zone via IfcRelAssignsToGroup

subject: IfcSpatialZone
rationale: Distribution elements (ducts, pipes, cables) can be assigned to a spatial zone for systems analysis (e.g., mechanical zones).
conditions: when assigned to the zone via group assignment

subject: IfcSpatialZone
rationale: Furniture and equipment can be grouped into functional zones (e.g., a security zone, a rental zone).
applicability: IfcSpatialZone does not directly 'contain' IfcFurnishingElement in the IFC schema without an explicit assignment mechanism. IfcFurnishingElement would typically be assigned to an IfcSpatialZone via IfcRelAssignsToGroup, not via direct spatial containment (which applies to IfcSpatialStructureElement). The assertion lacks the necessary condition about the assignment relationship.

subject: IfcSpatialZone
rationale: Spatial zones often reference the physical spatial structure (IfcBuilding, IfcBuildingStorey, IfcSpace) as context, though they can also be virtual.
conditions: if the zone is defined in reference to a physical spatial structure

subject: IfcSpatialZone
rationale: IfcSpatialZone can be related to IfcSystem via IfcRelServicesBuildings, linking functional zones to the systems serving them.
conditions: when the zone is assigned to a building system (e.g., HVAC zone, electrical zone)

subject: IfcSpatialZone
rationale: Spatial zones typically require property sets to define their functional requirements (e.g., Pset_SpatialZoneCommon).
conditions: for defining zone-specific properties like design criteria, loads, or occupancy type

subject: IfcSpatialZone
rationale: Zones often need classification references to categorize their purpose (e.g., 'Fire Zone', 'Security Zone', 'Rental Zone').
conditions: when the zone needs a classification (e.g., UniFormat, OmniClass, or building code classification)

subject: IfcSpatialZone
rationale: IfcRelNests allows decomposition of a spatial zone into sub-zones, enabling hierarchical organization.
conditions: when zones are hierarchically structured (parent-child relationships)

subject: IfcSpatialZone
rationale: Annotations like text labels or symbols can be assigned to a zone for documentation purposes.
conditions: when textual or graphical annotations are assigned to the zone

subject: IfcSpatialZoneType
rationale: IfcSpatialZoneType defines types for spatial zones, which are aggregations of spaces (IfcSpace). A spatial zone depends on underlying spaces to define its boundaries and occupancy.
applicability: In IFC4X3 schema, IfcSpatialZoneType does not have a direct 'depends_on' relationship to IfcSpace via any predefined attribute or relationship. IfcSpatialZone can contain IfcSpace via IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure, but that is an instance-level containment, not a type-level dependency. The assertion conflates type-level dependency with instance-level spatial containment.
conditions: when used for spatial programming and zone allocation

subject: IfcSpatialZoneType
rationale: Spatial zones logically group spaces (e.g., a fire zone contains multiple rooms/spaces).
applicability: IfcSpatialZoneType does not directly 'contain' IfcSpace at the type level. Containment at the instance level uses IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure, but IfcSpatialZone is not a subtype of IfcSpatialStructureElement, so this relationship is not standard. The assertion misrepresents the actual IFC schema structure.
conditions: when IfcSpatialZone is used as a grouping container

subject: IfcSpatialZoneType
rationale: IfcSpatialZoneType may extend or specialize IfcZone concepts in some IFC schemas; however, IfcSpatialZone is not universally dependent on IfcZone.
conditions: when spatial zones are defined as sub-classifications of zones

subject: IfcSpatialZoneType
rationale: Spatial zones support building systems by defining service areas for HVAC, lighting, fire safety, etc.
conditions: when the zone is used for system allocation (e.g., HVAC zones, electrical zones)

subject: IfcSpatialZoneType
rationale: Zones can aggregate distribution elements (ductwork, piping) for analysis and simulation.
applicability: All building types with MEP systems
conditions: when spatial zones group distribution elements for analysis

subject: IfcSpatialZoneType
rationale: The relationship entity IfcRelAssignsToGroup is required to assign building elements to a spatial zone.
applicability: IfcSpatialZoneType (type-level) does not directly depend on IfcRelAssignsToGroup. It is instances of IfcSpatialZone (via IfcRelAssignsToGroup) that establish membership, not the type definition itself. The assertion incorrectly attributes an instance-level relationship to the type object.
conditions: for establishing membership relationships between zones and elements

subject: IfcSpatialZoneType
rationale: IfcSpatialZoneType often references property set definitions to describe zone characteristics (e.g., fire rating, occupancy classification).
conditions: when zone type has predefined property sets like Pset_SpatialZoneCommon
exceptions: If no property sets are defined for the zone type

subject: IfcSpatialZoneType
rationale: There may be connections between spatial zones and building service systems via relationship entities.
conditions: when linking the zone to building service systems

subject: IfcSpatialZoneType
rationale: A spatial zone can aggregate spatial elements (spaces, external areas) under a functional category.
applicability: IfcSpatialZoneType does not have a direct 'contains' relationship to IfcSpatialElement at the type level. Instances of IfcSpatialZone can have spatial elements assigned via IfcRelReferencedInSpatialStructure, but this is not a containment relationship in the strict sense, and the assertion generalizes this incorrectly.
conditions: when subtypes of IfcSpatialElement (e.g., IfcSpace, IfcExternalSpatialStructure) are assigned to the zone

subject: IfcSpatialZoneType
rationale: IfcSpatialZoneType may reference external classification systems to define its type (e.g., 'Office Zone', 'Public Zone').
conditions: when the zone type uses a classification system (e.g., Uniclass, OmniClass, NRM)
exceptions: If no external classification is applied

subject: IfcSphere
rationale: IfcSphere, like all IFC representation items, depends on placement definitions to be located in 3D space.
conditions: When the sphere is placed in a building model

subject: IfcSphere
rationale: IfcSphere must be part of a representation context to be meaningful in an IFC model.
conditions: When used in a geometric representation

subject: IfcSphere
rationale: The sphere's position and orientation are defined via an axis2 placement in 3D.
conditions: When defining the sphere center and orientation

subject: IfcSphere
rationale: IfcSphere can be a primitive solid used in CSG boolean operations within IfcCsgSolid.
conditions: When used in Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) operations

subject: IfcSphere
rationale: IfcSphere can be an operand in boolean operations with other solids.
conditions: When used in boolean operations (union, intersection, difference)

subject: IfcSphere
rationale: A sphere can be approximated as a faceted boundary representation for visualization or analysis.
conditions: When a tessellated approximation is needed

subject: IfcSphere
rationale: IfcSphere is typically contained within an IfcShapeRepresentation that aggregates geometric items.
conditions: When included as part of a product shape definition

subject: IfcSphere
rationale: Spheres are rarely used as building slabs due to impractical geometry for horizontal building elements.
conditions: In typical building design
exceptions: While spherical slabs are uncommon, IfcSphere could be used for specialized IfcSlab geometries such as domed slabs, spherical tank bases, or architectural feature slabs (e.g., spherical roof slabs, observation deck slabs in spherical structures).
