The assertion 'unsuitable_for IfcSlab' is too absolute for 'typical building design' because there are legitimate use cases.

subject: IfcSphere
rationale: Spheres are not typical wall geometries; walls are planar or extruded.
conditions: In conventional building construction
exceptions: Although rare, spherical wall geometries do exist in building design — e.g., spherical domes, curved retaining walls, igloo structures, or spherical auditorium walls. IfcSphere could legitimately be used as part of a CSG Boolean operation to define such wall geometries in specialist building design.

subject: IfcSphericalSurface
rationale: The spherical surface requires a placement coordinate system (center point and orientation) to be located in 3D space.
conditions: for defining position and orientation

subject: IfcSphericalSurface
rationale: A spherical surface can serve as the base surface for a bounded surface sub-type that is trimmed by curves.
applicability: IfcCurveBoundedSurface is not contained within IfcSphericalSurface. IfcCurveBoundedSurface has a 'BasisSurface' attribute that references an IfcSurface (which could be an IfcSphericalSurface), making this an association/reference relationship rather than containment. The direction of the relationship should be inverted: IfcCurveBoundedSurface references IfcSphericalSurface as its basis.
conditions: when the spherical surface is trimmed by boundary curves

subject: IfcSphericalSurface
rationale: In IFC boundary representation (B-rep), an IfcSphericalSurface can be the surface geometry of an IfcAdvancedFace.
conditions: when the spherical surface is used as the underlying geometry of a face

subject: IfcStackTerminalType
rationale: To maintain weathertightness at the roof penetration point, flashing is required around the stack terminal.
applicability: The condition 'When penetrating a roof assembly' is stated, but the applicability field says 'roof-installed stack terminals'. Not all roof-installed stack terminals penetrate a roof assembly (e.g., terminals mounted on a roof curb or on a flat roof with a pre-fabricated flashing boot may not penetrate the roof membrane). The condition and applicability are inconsistent.
conditions: When penetrating a roof assembly
exceptions: IfcStackTerminalType elements that do not penetrate a roof assembly (e.g., wall-vented stack terminals, soffit-mounted vents) do not require flashing, even though they may be roof-installed stack terminals in a broader sense.

subject: IfcStackTerminal
rationale: If mounted on a roof, the roof structure provides the support and weatherproofing penetration needed for the stack terminal.
applicability: The assertion presumes IfcStackTerminal depends_on IfcRoof only when mounted on a roof, but this is an overly narrow view. In many building contexts, a stack terminal (venting a soil/waste stack) penetrates the roof regardless of whether it is 'mounted on' it—the structural dependency is on the roof slab or deck for weatherproofing and structural support even if the terminal itself is a pipe penetration rather than a mounted appliance. The condition 'when mounted on a roof' conflates two different scenarios: a roof-mounted mechanical unit vs. a plumbing vent stack penetration.
conditions: when mounted on a roof
exceptions: wall-mounted installations

subject: IfcStackTerminal
rationale: Some stack terminal assemblies incorporate dampers for airflow control or fire safety.
conditions: when the terminal includes an integral backdraft or fire damper
exceptions: simple open terminals without dampers

subject: IfcStackTerminal
rationale: A wall-mounted stack terminal requires the wall structure for support and proper penetration sealing.
conditions: when mounted on an exterior wall
exceptions: roof-mounted installations

Stack terminals can also be mounted on or penetrate a roof curb or a roof-mounted mechanical frame that is structurally supported by the roof, not the wall, even when serving wall-adjacent equipment. Additionally, in many modern construction types, stack terminals for plumbing systems penetrate the roof deck and have no wall relationship at all, which contradicts the assertion's implication that wall mounting is the primary relationship.

subject: IfcStairFlight
rationale: Building codes typically require handrails on stair flights for safety and accessibility.
applicability: Building codes in some jurisdictions (e.g., IBC) only require a handrail on one side of stair flights less than a certain width (e.g., 44 inches), not on both sides as implied by 'requires Handrail' without qualification.
conditions: For user safety
exceptions: Service stairs in limited-access areas

Spiral stairs and ship ladders (very steep stairs) often do not require handrails on both sides or in some cases any handrail due to their geometry, yet these are not covered by the existing exception for service stairs.

subject: IfcStairFlight
rationale: Nosing provides edge protection and visual contrast on stair treads.
conditions: For finished appearance and slip resistance
exceptions: Cast-in-place concrete stairs where nosing is integral

Exterior steel stairs (e.g., fire escapes) and stairs with nosings formed by the tread profile itself (e.g., solid metal treads with upturned lip) do not need separate nosing elements, and this is not covered by the cast-in-place concrete exception.

subject: IfcStairFlight
rationale: Landings provide resting points and are required by building codes at top and bottom of flights.
conditions: At top and bottom of each stair flight
At changes in direction
exceptions: Very short flights with fewer than 3 risers

subject: IfcStairFlight
rationale: Each stair flight contains a series of treads as horizontal stepping surfaces.
conditions: As part of each step

subject: IfcStairFlight
rationale: Each stair flight contains risers as vertical components between treads (except open-riser types).
conditions: For closed-riser stair designs
exceptions: Open-riser stair designs

subject: IfcStairFlight
rationale: Guardrails are required on open sides of stairs to prevent falls per building codes.
applicability: Guardrail requirements vary significantly by jurisdiction and stair width. For example, IBC requires guardrails on open sides only when the drop exceeds 30 inches, and stairs less than 44 inches wide may only need a handrail (not a guardrail) on one open side.
conditions: On open sides of stair flights
Above a certain height threshold
exceptions: Stairs enclosed on both sides by walls

subject: IfcStairFlight
rationale: Stair flights structurally connect to floor slabs at landing points.
conditions: At each floor level

subject: IfcStairFlight
rationale: Stair flights often connect to adjacent walls for lateral support and enclosure.
conditions: When stairs are enclosed or supported by walls
exceptions: Free-standing stairs

subject: IfcStair
rationale: Handrails are required by most building codes (IBC, ADA) for stair safety and accessibility.
applicability: Residential buildings with more than 2 risers

The assertion does not address spiral stairs, which often have different handrail requirements (e.g., may only require one handrail regardless of width). This is a common exception in building codes across many jurisdictions.
conditions: When stairs serve as egress path
When required by building code
exceptions: One or two riser stairs may not require handrails in some jurisdictions

subject: IfcStair
rationale: Guardrails prevent falls from open sides of stair flights.
applicability: The distinction between handrail and guardrail is critical: when a stair is open on both sides but has a handrail mounted on the wall, a separate guardrail may not be required if the handrail itself serves as the guard (depending on height and graspability requirements). The assertion does not address this overlap.
conditions: When stairs are open on one or both sides
exceptions: Guardrails may not be required on open sides of stairs with very small drop heights (e.g., less than 30 inches or 762 mm in many codes). The existing conditions and applicability do not account for minimal elevation change exceptions.

subject: IfcStair
rationale: Landings provide resting points and safe transition areas at stair entries and direction changes.
conditions: At top and bottom of each stair flight
When stair changes direction

subject: IfcStair
rationale: In IFC schema, IfcStair is an aggregation container for IfcStairFlight entities.
applicability: In IFC2x3 and IFC4, IfcStair can also be decomposed into IfcStairFlight, IfcLanding, and IfcRailing according to the IFC schema. The assertion states it 'contains IfcStairFlight' exclusively, but a stair may also contain explicit landing elements (IfcLanding) as part of its decomposition, particularly in precast or detailed BIM models.

subject: IfcStair
rationale: In IFC, IfcStair may contain IfcRailing as part of the stair assembly.
applicability: The existing exception 'If railings are modeled separately adjacent to the stair' is vague and underspecified. In IFC, IfcRailing can be contained by IfcStair via IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure, or can be an independent element. The assertion should clarify whether containment through spatial structure is intended vs. direct aggregation.
exceptions: If railings are modeled separately adjacent to the stair

subject: IfcStair
rationale: Stairs connect to floor slabs at each landing point.
conditions: At floor levels
exceptions: An IfcStair may connect to an IfcLanding element rather than directly to an IfcSlab at intermediate floor levels, particularly in detailed stair models where the landing is modeled as its own element. The assertion does not account for this decomposition pattern.

subject: IfcStair
rationale: Stair enclosures connect to surrounding walls for support and fire separation.
applicability: The assertion states 'IfcStair connects_to IfcWall' when enclosed by walls, but does not specify the connection type (e.g., IfcRelConnectsPathElements or IfcRelConnectsElements). In IFC, this connection may be modeled differently depending on whether the stair is structurally connected to the wall or simply adjacent.
conditions: When stair is enclosed by walls
exceptions: Free-standing stairs

subject: IfcStairFlightType
rationale: A stair flight is typically a component within a complete stair assembly (IfcStair), requiring containment within or connection to a stair structure.
conditions: when the stair flight is part of a larger stair assembly

subject: IfcStairFlightType
rationale: IfcStairFlightType defines the type information; the actual occurrence (IfcStairFlight) depends on the type definition for its properties.
conditions: when the type is instantiated in a project

subject: IfcStairFlightType
rationale: Stair flights typically require handrails for safety, support, and code compliance.
conditions: for safety compliance (e.g., building codes)
exceptions: very short flights with low rise

subject: IfcStairFlightType
rationale: A stair flight requires treads (horizontal stepping surfaces) to function as a means of vertical circulation.
conditions: for pedestrian use
exceptions: Some stair designs (e.g., ship stairs, alternating tread stairs, ladder stairs, or spiral stairs with continuous tread surfaces) may not have conventional separate tread elements. Additionally, stair flights in industrial settings or as catwalk access may use grating or chequer plate surfaces rather than discrete treads.

subject: IfcStairFlightType
rationale: Traditional stair flights have risers (vertical components between treads), though open-riser stairs are an exception.
conditions: for enclosed stair construction
exceptions: open-riser stair designs

subject: IfcStairFlightType
rationale: Building codes often require landings at top and bottom, and intermediate landings for long flights.
conditions: when flight exceeds maximum continuous run per code
exceptions: short flights not requiring intermediate landings

subject: IfcStairFlightType
rationale: A stair flight connects to floor slabs (landings or floors) at its top and bottom.
applicability: IfcStairFlightType connects_to IfcSlab only at floor levels where the stair flight terminates at a slab. However, stair flights can also terminate at intermediate landings (IfcLanding), other stair flights, or structural beams, not exclusively at IfcSlab elements. The assertion should include these alternatives or clarify that this is just one possible connection.
conditions: at floor levels

subject: IfcStairFlightType
rationale: A stair flight often contains stringers (inclined beams) that support the treads and risers.
conditions: for structural support of treads and risers
exceptions: monolithic precast stairs without separate stringers

Stringer-less stair designs are already noted, but additional exceptions include: (1) cantilevered stairs where treads are embedded into a wall with no stringer; (2) spine-beam stairs where a central beam supports treads; (3) glass or cable-supported stair systems that use alternative structural systems. These are distinct from the 'monolithic precast' exception listed.

subject: IfcStairType
rationale: An IfcStairType is a type definition for stairs, and stairs typically consist of stair flights (IfcStairFlight) as the primary functional component for vertical circulation.
applicability: The assertion says IfcStairType 'requires' IfcStairFlight, but IfcStairType is a type definition that can exist without any flights being instantiated (e.g., in a type library). The 'requires' relationship should be on IfcStair (the occurrence), not the type definition. Additionally, the condition 'when the stair type includes flights' makes the assertion tautological.
conditions: when the stair type includes flights

subject: IfcStairType
rationale: Building codes require railings/guardrails on stairs for safety, especially on open sides; this is a standard requirement for stair assemblies.
conditions: for safety compliance (building codes)
when stair has open sides or open risers
exceptions: stairs with closed sides and handrails integrated into wall may not need separate IfcRailing entity

subject: IfcStairType
rationale: Stairs typically land on or are supported by floor slabs (landings and floors at top and bottom).
applicability: IfcStairType is a type definition and does not have a dependency relationship with IfcSlab occurrences. A stair type can be defined in a library without any slab dependency. The dependency relationship would apply to IfcStair (occurrences) that are placed on slabs. The existing exception about free-standing stairs confirms this is about occurrences, not types.
conditions: when stair is supported by a floor/landing slab
exceptions: free-standing stairs with self-supporting structure may not require a supporting slab

subject: IfcStairType
rationale: Larger stair types may depend on structural beams for support, but smaller residential stairs often do not.
applicability: IfcStairType (type definition) does not depend on IfcBeam occurrences. Beam dependencies apply to stair occurrences structurally supported by beams. A stair type can be defined with no knowledge of structural beam support. The existing exception about stairs between walls reinforces that this is about occurrences, not types.
conditions: when stair is supported by structural beams
for monumental or wide-span stairs
exceptions: simple stairs embedded between walls may not require beams

subject: IfcStairType
rationale: The IfcStairType defines a type that can contain multiple stair flights as parts of the stair assembly.
applicability: IfcStairType is an object type definition that defines properties of a stair type, but it does not physically 'contain' IfcStairFlight entities in the IFC containment hierarchy. In IFC, spatial containment (IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure) or aggregation (IfcRelAggregates) is used. IfcStairType is a type definition (IfcTypeProduct) that defines common properties for occurrences. The assertion should reference IfcStair (occurrence) containing IfcStairFlight, or IfcStairType being the type definition that applies to IfcStairFlight instances.

subject: IfcStairType
rationale: Railings are often contained within a stair type assembly as per IFC decomposition.
applicability: Same issue as with flight containment: IfcStairType is a type definition, not a spatial or aggregate container. The assertion that IfcStairType 'contains' IfcRailing misrepresents the IFC relationship model. IfcStairType can define a railing type reference via property sets, but does not 'contain' railing entities.

subject: IfcStairType
rationale: In some configurations the stair structure can support intermediate landings, though more commonly the slab supports the stair.
applicability: IfcStairType (type definition) does not structurally 'support' IfcSlab. Structural support relationships (IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember) are between physical element occurrences (IfcStair, IfcSlab), not type definitions. An IfcStairType cannot support a slab instance.
conditions: when stair provides structural support to a landing slab

subject: IfcStairType
rationale: Stairs connect different floor levels; the connection points are typically slabs at each floor.
applicability: IfcStairType (type definition) does not 'connect to' IfcSlab instances. Connectivity relationships in IFC (IfcRelConnectsElements) occur between element occurrences, not type definitions. The assertion conflates IfcStairType with IfcStair occurrence.
conditions: at floor levels (top and bottom of stair)

subject: IfcStairType
rationale: Stairs are often adjacent to or enclosed by walls, especially in stairwells, and connect to them structurally.
applicability: IfcStairType (type definition) does not physically 'connect to' IfcWall instances. Connectivity in IFC is between placed element occurrences (IfcStair, IfcWall), not between type definitions and elements. The assertion should apply to IfcStair occurrences.
conditions: when stair is bounded by or attached to walls
exceptions: free-standing stairs not adjacent to walls

subject: IfcStairType
rationale: Stairs improve accessibility and vertical circulation between different storeys in a building.
conditions: when providing vertical circulation between storeys

subject: IfcStairType
rationale: A stair type depends on the material it is constructed from (concrete, steel, wood, etc.) for its structural capacity, fire resistance, and durability.
applicability: IfcStairType does not 'depend on' IfcMaterial in a required relationship sense. IfcStairType may have material associations (via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial) but this is optional in IFC. Stair type definitions can exist without specified materials (e.g., in early design stages). The assertion overstates the dependency as a hard requirement.
conditions: for structural integrity and fire rating

subject: IfcStairType
rationale: An IfcStairType requires an IfcBuilding context for spatial placement and project assignment.
conditions: when stair type is assigned to a specific building project

subject: IfcStructuralAction
rationale: An IfcStructuralAction must reference an IfcStructuralLoad to define the actual force or displacement it represents.
conditions: to define the load values and direction

subject: IfcStructuralAction
rationale: A structural action (load) is applied to a structural member (beam, column, slab, etc.) to define the structural behavior.
conditions: to be applied on a structural element
exceptions: abstract actions used in load grouping without direct assignment

The existing exception notes 'abstract actions used in load grouping without direct assignment', but there is another significant exception: IfcStructuralAction can be assigned to IfcStructuralActivityAssignmentSelect which includes IfcStructuralMember, IfcStructuralElementGroup, or IfcStructuralConnection. When assigned to an IfcStructuralConnection (a subtype of IfcStructuralItem but not IfcStructuralMember), the assertion that it requires IfcStructuralMember does not hold.

subject: IfcStructuralAction
rationale: Individual structural actions collectively support the definition of structural analysis models by providing the loading conditions.
conditions: when grouped into load cases or load combinations

subject: IfcStructuralAction
rationale: IfcStructuralAction instances are grouped into load groups or combinations via IfcRelAssignsToGroup relationships.
applicability: IfcStructuralAction does not depend_on IfcRelAssignsToGroup directly. In IFC4, IfcStructuralAction (as a subtype of IfcObject) can be assigned to IfcGroup via IfcRelAssignsToGroup, but this is an optional relationship used for load grouping. The direction 'depends_on' overstates the relationship - IfcStructuralAction does not require IfcRelAssignsToGroup to exist. The condition already notes 'when actions are grouped', which acknowledges this limitation, but the depends_on semantics are too strong.
conditions: when actions are grouped into load groups or load combinations

subject: IfcStructuralAction
rationale: The structural action may reference an object placement to define its location and orientation in the model.
applicability: structural models with defined coordinate systems
conditions: when the structural action has a defined local placement
exceptions: actions defined globally without placement

subject: IfcStructuralAction
rationale: IfcStructuralAction can have a product representation shape for visualization purposes.
conditions: when the structural action has a geometric representation
exceptions: analytical actions without geometry

subject: IfcStructuralAction
rationale: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity is the specific relationship used to connect a structural action (activity) to a structural member.
conditions: to relate the action to a structural member or element

subject: IfcStructuralAction
rationale: An IfcStructuralAction contains or references a structural load definition that quantifies the action (force, moment, displacement, etc.).
applicability: IfcStructuralAction does not 'contain' IfcStructuralLoad via a composition relationship (contains). The load definition is referenced via IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity which has an optional reference to IfcStructuralLoad via the inherited SELF\IfcRelConnects.SpecifiedLoad (or via AppliedLoad on IfcStructuralActivity). This is an association/reference, not containment. In IFC4, IfcStructuralAction has an ObjectType of 'load' but does not have direct containment of IfcStructuralLoad instances.
conditions: as the load definition data

subject: IfcStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcStructuralActivity relies on IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity to be linked to structural members (IfcStructuralMember) or elements (IfcElement).
applicability: all building types with structural analysis
conditions: when associating structural activities to structural members or elements

subject: IfcStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcStructuralActivity (e.g., loads) must be connected to an IfcStructuralMember to define where the load acts.
conditions: when the activity is an action (load) applied to a structure

subject: IfcStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcStructuralActivity defines the application of a load; the load values are defined by IfcStructuralLoad or its subtypes.
conditions: always

subject: IfcStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcStructuralPlanarAction is a subtype of IfcStructuralActivity for surface loads.
applicability: building types with slab, wall, or shell analysis
conditions: when representing 2D distributed loads on surfaces

subject: IfcStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcStructuralPointAction is a subtype of IfcStructuralActivity for point loads.
conditions: when representing concentrated loads at a point

subject: IfcStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcStructuralLinearAction is a subtype of IfcStructuralActivity for line loads.
applicability: building types with beam or edge analysis
conditions: when representing line loads along edges or beams

subject: IfcStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcStructuralActivity instances are aggregated into IfcStructuralAnalysisModel to define load cases and combinations.
applicability: all building types with structural analysis
conditions: when the activity is part of a structural analysis model

subject: IfcStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcStructuralActivity references an IfcStructuralLoadOrResult to define the actual load values or analysis results.
conditions: always

subject: IfcStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcStructuralActivity uses IfcObjectPlacement (via IfcProduct) to define its spatial location on the structure.
applicability: building types where load positions matter
conditions: when the activity has a defined location in 3D space

subject: IfcStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcStructuralActivity as a subtype of IfcProduct can have a ProductRepresentation for geometric display.
conditions: when a visual representation of the load is required

subject: IfcStructuralActivity
rationale: IfcStructuralActivity (especially reactions and results) can be grouped via IfcStructuralResultGroup for result analysis.
conditions: when structural analysis results are grouped for reporting

subject: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel
rationale: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel depends on IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity to associate structural activities (loads) to the analysis model.
applicability: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel depends_on IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity is stated as applicable to 'All structural analysis models', but IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity is only required when structural activities (loads/boundary conditions) are explicitly connected to structural members or connections. For analysis models that only define member topology without applied loads (e.g., during preliminary design), this relationship is not needed.
conditions: When structural analysis results need to be linked to the model

subject: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel
rationale: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel requires load groups to define load cases and combinations for structural analysis.
conditions: When loads are grouped for analysis cases or combinations

subject: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel
rationale: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel contains IfcStructuralMember entities representing beams, columns, braces, etc. that are part of the analysis.
conditions: When the analysis model includes physical or analytical structural members
exceptions: If the model is only a void or reference model type

IfcStructuralAnalysisModel contains IfcStructuralMember may not hold in the opposite direction: IfcStructuralMember is typically related to IfcStructuralAnalysisModel via IfcRelAssignsToProduct or IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember, not directly through a 'contains' relationship. The IFC schema uses IfcRelAssignsToProduct for this aggregation, so 'contains' as a direct containment may be inaccurate.

subject: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel
rationale: The analysis model contains structural connections (nodes) for the analysis.
applicability: Frame, truss, and shell analysis models
conditions: When connections between structural members are modeled

subject: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel
rationale: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel contains IfcStructuralActivity (loads, displacements, etc.) assigned to the model.
conditions: When loads or boundary conditions are applied to the model
exceptions: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel does not directly 'contain' IfcStructuralActivity in the IFC schema. IfcStructuralActivity is related to IfcStructuralMember or IfcStructuralConnection via IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity, not directly contained by the analysis model. The indirect dependency is through IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity, so the direct 'contains' relationship is misleading.

subject: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel
rationale: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel requires IfcStructuralResultGroup to organize and store analysis outcomes like forces and displacements.
applicability: IfcStructuralResultGroup is applicable only when analysis results are stored within the IFC model itself. Many structural analysis workflows export results externally (e.g., in analysis software native formats or CSV/XML), and the IFC model may only contain the analysis model definition and loads without any result grouping. The condition should clarify that this is only when results are persisted in IFC.
conditions: When analysis results are to be stored and grouped

subject: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel
rationale: The structural analysis model supports the design and verification of building elements by providing stress, deflection, and stability results.
conditions: When the structural analysis model is used to verify structural safety of building elements
exceptions: Non-structural elements

subject: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel
rationale: Structural analysis depends on material properties (steel grade, concrete class, reinforcement) for accurate simulation.
applicability: All structural analysis requiring stiffness and strength properties
conditions: When material properties are required for analysis calculations
exceptions: Simplified rigid-body or kinematic models

subject: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel
rationale: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel depends on IfcStructuralCurveMember for line-type structural members.
conditions: When 1D structural members such as beams or columns are analyzed

subject: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel
rationale: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel depends on IfcStructuralSurfaceMember for area-type structural members.
conditions: When 2D structural elements such as slabs or walls are analyzed

subject: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel
rationale: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel connects to IfcRelAssignsToGroup to associate structural members, connections, and activities to the model.
conditions: When the analysis model groups related structural items

subject: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel
rationale: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel may conflict with IfcBuildingStorey if the analytical model uses different reference levels than architectural storeys.
applicability: Buildings where structural grid differs from spatial floor layout
conditions: When analytical axes do not align with architectural floor levels
exceptions: When analysis nodes are placed at floor levels

subject: IfcStructuralConnection
rationale: IfcStructuralConnection is a structural connection node that connects structural members (e.g., IfcBeam, IfcColumn, IfcMember) in an analytical model. It requires associated structural members to define the connected elements.
conditions: When acting as part of a structural analysis model

subject: IfcStructuralConnection
rationale: Structural connections must have associated loads (IfcStructuralLoad) applied at the connection point for analysis of forces and reactions.
conditions: When performing structural analysis

subject: IfcStructuralConnection
rationale: IfcStructuralConnection may have an associated IfcConnectionGeometry defining the geometric constraints and location of the connection between structural members.
conditions: When geometric representation of the connection is needed

subject: IfcStructuralConnection
rationale: The connection requires a coordinate placement (IfcAxis2Placement3D) to define its location in 3D space.
conditions: When 3D placement is required for the connection

subject: IfcStructuralConnection
rationale: IfcStructuralConnection depends on the IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember relationship entity to formally link it to structural members in the IFC model.
conditions: When establishing relationships between structural members and connections

subject: IfcStructuralConnection
rationale: IfcStructuralConnection instances are typically grouped within or referenced by an IfcStructuralAnalysisModel which defines the analysis context.
conditions: When part of a structural analysis context

subject: IfcStructuralConnection
rationale: Structural connections provide support and transfer loads between connected structural members (beams, columns, braces), acting as nodes in the structural system.
conditions: In load-bearing configurations

subject: IfcStructuralConnection
rationale: The connection supports and transfers structural loads (point loads, moments, forces) from one member to another or to supports.
conditions: Under applied loading conditions

subject: IfcStructuralConnection
rationale: IfcStructuralConnection is the abstract supertype; IfcStructuralPointConnection is a subtype representing connections at a single point (e.g., pinned connections).
conditions: When the connection is a point-type connection

subject: IfcStructuralConnection
rationale: IfcStructuralCurveConnection is a subtype of IfcStructuralConnection representing connections along a curve (e.g., continuous beam connections).
conditions: When the connection occurs along a curve/edge

subject: IfcStructuralConnection
rationale: IfcStructuralSurfaceConnection is a subtype representing connections along a surface area (e.g., slab-to-wall connections).
conditions: When the connection occurs along a surface

subject: IfcStructuralConnection
rationale: IfcStructuralConnection can contain applied loads and reactions through its 'AppliedLoad' and 'Condition' attributes.
conditions: When loads are directly assigned to the connection

subject: IfcStructuralConnectionCondition
rationale: IfcStructuralConnectionCondition is a subtype or related concept that defines conditions for structural connections, thus depends on the existence of an IfcStructuralConnection.
applicability: IfcStructuralConnectionCondition is an abstract entity that cannot be instantiated directly; it is usually referenced via IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember, not directly through a depends_on relationship from IfcStructuralConnection. The IFC schema defines IfcStructuralConnection as having an attribute 'AppliedCondition' of type IfcStructuralConnectionCondition, but the relationship direction is association, not dependency in the traditional sense.
conditions: When modeling structural connections in IFC

subject: IfcStructuralConnectionCondition
rationale: Structural connection conditions often depend on the structural loads applied at the connection.
conditions: For defining load-bearing conditions

subject: IfcStructuralConnectionCondition
rationale: Connection conditions in structural models often require boundary conditions for completeness.
conditions: When specifying support or restraint conditions

subject: IfcStructuralConnectionCondition
rationale: IfcStructuralConnectionCondition provides the necessary condition definitions that support structural analysis modeling.
conditions: When used as part of a structural analysis model
exceptions: If not assigned to any analysis model

IfcStructuralConnectionCondition supports IfcStructuralAnalysisModel only indirectly through its assignment to IfcStructuralConnection which may be part of an analysis model. There is no direct 'supports' relationship in the IFC schema between a connection condition and the analysis model itself.

subject: IfcStructuralConnectionCondition
rationale: IfcStructuralConnectionCondition supports the relationship entity that connects structural members at joints.
applicability: IfcStructuralConnectionCondition is referenced by IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember (via the 'RelatedStructuralConnection' attribute chain), not the other way around. The support direction is reversed compared to the actual IFC schema relationship.
conditions: When defining how structural members connect

subject: IfcStructuralCurveAction
rationale: IfcStructuralCurveAction applies a load along a curve, so a structural load definition (IfcStructuralLoad) is required to define the magnitude and distribution.
conditions: when representing a distributed line load along a curve

subject: IfcStructuralCurveAction
rationale: The curve action is typically applied to or referenced by an IfcStructuralCurveMember (e.g., beam, column) which carries the action.
conditions: when the action is assigned to a curve member for structural analysis

subject: IfcStructuralCurveAction
rationale: IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity is the relationship object used to connect a structural activity (such as this curve action) to a structural member.
conditions: to formally assign the action to a structural item or element

subject: IfcStructuralCurveAction
rationale: For certain analysis types, the action point or curve may connect to a structural connection (support) node.
applicability: IfcStructuralCurveAction does not generally require IfcStructuralConnection. IfcStructuralConnection is relevant for support conditions in structural analysis models, but a curve action (e.g., a distributed load on a beam) does not always involve a connection. The assertion overly restricts the usage.
conditions: when the curve action is at a boundary condition or support location

subject: IfcStructuralCurveAction
rationale: IfcStructuralCurveAction contains or references an IfcStructuralLoadOrResult which specifies the actual load values (force per length, etc.).
conditions: as the load values/parameters assigned to the curve action

subject: IfcStructuralCurveAction
rationale: The curve geometry and position depend on the object placement to locate the action correctly in the model.
conditions: for defining the 3D placement and orientation of the curve along which the action is applied

subject: IfcStructuralCurveAction
rationale: For visualization purposes, the action may have a product representation shape.
conditions: when the curve action has a geometric representation (e.g., a line with arrows)

subject: IfcStructuralCurveAction
rationale: IfcStructuralCurveAction is assigned to an analysis model via IfcRelAssignsToGroup to define loading scenarios.
conditions: as a load case component for structural analysis

subject: IfcStructuralCurveAction
rationale: Structural actions are grouped into load groups/load cases for analysis and design.
conditions: to be grouped into load cases and load combinations

subject: IfcStructuralCurveConnection
rationale: IfcStructuralCurveConnection is a subtype of IfcStructuralConnection, inheriting its connection properties.
conditions: Must have at least one connected structural member

subject: IfcStructuralCurveConnection
rationale: A curve connection joins two or more curve members (e.g., beams, columns) at a common point.
conditions: Must be connected at curve endpoints or intersection points

subject: IfcStructuralCurveConnection
rationale: The connection point needs geometric positioning in 3D space.
conditions: Defines local coordinate system for the connection

subject: IfcStructuralCurveConnection
rationale: Placement in the building coordinate system is required for all structural items.
conditions: Relative to parent spatial structure

subject: IfcStructuralCurveConnection
rationale: The connection supports the relationship between structural members and the connection node.
conditions: When used as part of a structural analysis model

subject: IfcStructuralCurveConnection
rationale: For structural analysis, the connection must reference applied loads.
applicability: IfcStructuralCurveConnection does not 'depend_on' IfcStructuralLoad as a general assertion. IfcStructuralConnectionCondition (applied at the connection) references applied loads, but the connection itself does not directly depend on IfcStructuralLoad. The condition 'when loads are applied at the connection point' is accurate but the dependency phrasing is misleading - loads are associated via IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity, not directly by the connection entity.
conditions: When loads are applied at the connection point

subject: IfcStructuralCurveConnection
rationale: Curve connections are defined within the context of a structural analysis model.
applicability: IfcStructuralCurveConnection can exist as a structural connection item without being part of an IfcStructuralAnalysisModel. In IFC, structural connection items can be defined in the building model context (e.g., via IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure) without an analysis model. The assertion that it 'requires' an IfcStructuralAnalysisModel is too strong - it only requires this for analysis purposes.
conditions: Must be part of a structural analysis model to be meaningful

subject: IfcStructuralCurveConnection
rationale: The connection may contain boundary condition definitions.
conditions: When connection properties (stiffness, eccentricity) are defined

subject: IfcStructuralCurveConnection
rationale: IfcStructuralCurveConnection is a subtype of IfcStructuralConnection, and related to point connections via structural members.
conditions: When used in a structural model hierarchy

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMember
rationale: Curve members typically connect to point connections (nodes) at their ends to form a structural frame.
applicability: In IFC2x3 and IFC4, IfcStructuralCurveMember can also connect to IfcStructuralSurfaceMember (e.g., a beam connected to a wall or slab) at certain topological junctions, not just IfcStructuralPointConnection.
conditions: at member ends

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying
rationale: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying is a subtype of IfcStructuralCurveMember, inheriting its properties while adding varying cross-section definitions.
conditions: when modeling varying cross-sections along a curve member

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying
rationale: Structural members require defined load cases for proper analysis and design.
conditions: for load assignment and structural analysis

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying
rationale: A varying curve member needs material profile definitions that capture changing cross-section properties along its length.
applicability: While IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying can reference IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage via its material association, the assertion should clarify that the relationship is through IfcRelAssociatesMaterial, not a direct requirement. Also, IfcMaterialProfileSet was renamed to IfcMaterialProfileSetUsage in IFC4.
conditions: when material and cross-section properties vary along the member

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying
rationale: The member's orientation and placement in 3D space depends on axis placement definitions.
conditions: for defining the local coordinate system and axis alignment

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying
rationale: A curve member depends on a curve entity to define its path and geometry.
conditions: for defining the reference line or axis of the member

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying
rationale: Structural connections are required to transfer loads and provide boundary conditions.
conditions: at member ends and intermediate support points

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying
rationale: The structural curve member is designed to support various structural loads transferring them to supports.
conditions: when vertical or lateral loads are applied to the member

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying
rationale: Varying curve members like tapered beams often support floor or deck elements.
applicability: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying does not directly 'support' IfcSlab. The slab would be connected through IfcRelConnectsStructuralElement, which relates structural members to structural elements (or directly to building elements). The wording 'supports' is ambiguous and may misrepresent the IFC relationship model.
conditions: when slabs bear on the varying curve member (e.g., edge beams)
exceptions: when the slab is supported by other means

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying
rationale: The member can contain applied curve actions as part of the structural analysis model.
conditions: when loads are applied directly to the member

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying
rationale: Structural curve members connect to point connections at their ends or intermediate nodes.
conditions: at endpoints and intermediate nodes of the member

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying
rationale: The varying curve member can connect to other curve members at curve connections.
conditions: when multiple curve members meet at a junction

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying
rationale: The IFC schema requires relationship entities to formally connect structural members to their supports.
conditions: to formally establish relationships with structural connections in the IFC model

subject: IfcStructuralCurveMemberVarying
rationale: The member is typically part of a larger structural analysis model context.
conditions: for coordinated analysis and design workflow

subject: IfcStructuralCurveReaction
rationale: A structural curve reaction must be assigned to a structural curve member (beam, column, or other line element) to define its support condition.
conditions: When acting as a structural reaction assignment

subject: IfcStructuralCurveReaction
rationale: The reaction value (force or moment) is derived from applied loads; a load case or load group must be defined.
conditions: When defining the reaction force or moment magnitude

subject: IfcStructuralCurveReaction
rationale: The relationship connecting the reaction to a member and an activity is established via IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember.
conditions: When linking the reaction to the structural member and the structural activity

subject: IfcStructuralCurveReaction
rationale: The reaction exists within an analysis model that groups structural members, connections, and actions or results.
conditions: When part of a structural analysis

subject: IfcStructuralCurveReaction
rationale: The reaction provides the force or moment that supports the structural curve member against applied loads.
applicability: IfcStructuralCurveReaction does not 'support' IfcStructuralCurveMember in a dependency sense. Rather, the reaction is *applied to* or *occurs at* the curve member. The direction of the semantic relationship is reversed: the member supports loads; the reaction is the result.
conditions: When representing a support reaction at a node or along a curve

subject: IfcStructuralCurveReaction
rationale: Linear force per unit length values are needed to define the distributed reaction magnitude.
conditions: When the reaction is defined per unit length

subject: IfcStructuralCurveReaction
rationale: A linear reaction distribution requires a planar force load definition specifying the variation along the curve.
conditions: When the reaction is distributed along the curve as a varying load

subject: IfcStructuralCurveReaction
rationale: In some analysis models, a distributed curve reaction may be lumped to a point connection for simplified calculations.
conditions: When the curve reaction is discretized or summarized at a point

subject: IfcStructuralCurveReaction
rationale: In a combined model, curve reactions on edges may relate to surface reactions on adjacent shell elements.
conditions: When the structure includes both line and surface elements interacting

subject: IfcStructuralCurveReaction
rationale: The reaction entity must reference a load or result entity that carries the numerical values of the reaction.
conditions: When specifying the actual reaction force or moment values

subject: IfcStructuralCurveReaction
rationale: IfcStructuralCurveReaction is a subtype of IfcStructuralReaction; the parent concept is implicit in the IFC schema.
conditions: As the parent type for classification

subject: IfcStructuralItem
rationale: Structural items are connected at nodes/connections which transfer forces between elements.
conditions: For stability and load transfer

subject: IfcStructuralItem
rationale: Structural items must be designed for applied loads (dead, live, wind, seismic).
applicability: IfcStructuralLoad is not a direct dependency of the abstract IfcStructuralItem in IFC. Loads are typically assigned to structural items via IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity (which relates IfcStructuralActivity to IfcStructuralItem). The assertion is directionally correct but oversimplifies the relationship — loads are assigned via a relationship entity, not a direct attribute dependency.
conditions: For verification of structural capacity

subject: IfcStructuralItem
rationale: Structural items are made of materials (concrete, steel, timber) which provide their structural behavior.
applicability: IfcStructuralItem depends_on IfcMaterial is generally correct, but not all structural items have material associations directly. In IFC, material information is typically assigned via IfcRelAssociatesMaterial to elements, and for structural analysis models, material properties may be defined at the member section level. The assertion is broadly accurate but oversimplifies the IFC material assignment mechanism.
conditions: For strength and stiffness properties

subject: IfcStructuralItem
rationale: Structural items like beams and columns support slabs above them.
conditions: Vertical load transfer

subject: IfcStructuralItem
rationale: Structural items can support non-structural or structural walls.
conditions: When walls are supported by beams or columns

subject: IfcStructuralItem
rationale: Structural items transfer roof loads down to foundations.
conditions: Load-bearing function

subject: IfcStructuralItem
rationale: Concrete structural items contain reinforcement to resist tensile forces.
conditions: For reinforced concrete structural items

subject: IfcStructuralItem
rationale: Prestressed structural items contain tendons for compression.
conditions: For prestressed concrete items

subject: IfcStructuralItem
rationale: Structural items connect at nodes defined by point, line, or surface connections.
conditions: At joints and supports

subject: IfcStructuralItem
rationale: Beams and columns form curve connections at their intersections.
conditions: Along edges/curves

subject: IfcStructuralItem
rationale: IfcStructuralItem is abstract; it requires concrete subtypes like IfcStructuralCurveMember for linear elements or IfcStructuralSurfaceMember for planar elements.
conditions: When the item is a linear element

subject: IfcStructuralItem
rationale: IfcStructuralItem requires concrete subtypes for surface-type elements.
conditions: When the item is a planar element

subject: IfcStructuralItem
rationale: Structural items collectively support the floors and levels of a building.
conditions: As part of the structural frame

subject: IfcStructuralLoad
rationale: IfcStructuralLoad represents a structural load entity; it requires a load case definition (IfcStructuralLoadCase) to group and apply loads in analysis scenarios.
conditions: When defining load combinations for structural analysis

subject: IfcStructuralLoad
rationale: IfcStructuralLoad is associated with IfcStructuralLoadGroup for grouping loads (e.g., dead loads, live loads) in structural analysis.
conditions: When loads need to be organized into groups for analysis

subject: IfcStructuralLoad
rationale: Structural loads depend on connection elements (IfcStructuralConnection) to define where loads are applied in the structural model.
conditions: When transferring loads to structural supports

subject: IfcStructuralLoad
rationale: IfcStructuralLoad depends on structural members (IfcStructuralMember) such as beams, columns, and slabs to which the loads are applied.
conditions: When loads are assigned to structural members for analysis

subject: IfcStructuralLoad
rationale: IfcStructuralLoad provides input data that supports the structural analysis model (IfcStructuralAnalysisModel) for calculating structural responses.
conditions: When performing structural analysis simulations

subject: IfcStructuralLoad
rationale: IfcStructuralLoad is an abstract supertype that contains/defines subtypes including ifcstructuralLoadStatic for static load definitions.
conditions: When defining static loads

subject: IfcStructuralLoad
rationale: IfcStructuralLoad as a supertype contains specialized subtypes like IfcStructuralLoadTemperature for temperature-induced loads.
conditions: When defining thermal loads

subject: IfcStructuralLoad
rationale: IfcStructuralLoad connects to structural elements via IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity relationship entities.
conditions: When relating loads to structural elements or connections

subject: IfcStructuralLinearAction
rationale: An IfcStructuralLinearAction must reference a load definition (IfcStructuralLoad) to specify the force distribution along a line.
conditions: for defining the magnitude and distribution of the linear action

subject: IfcStructuralLinearAction
rationale: The action needs to be connected to structural elements via relationship entities to have engineering meaning.
conditions: to relate the action to a structural member or element

subject: IfcStructuralLinearAction
rationale: A linear action is typically applied along a curve member; the member provides the geometric context for the action.
conditions: when the action is applied to a curve member (beam, column, cable)

subject: IfcStructuralLinearAction
rationale: Linear actions may be assigned to point connections where loads are transferred.
conditions: if the linear action is applied at connection points along the member

subject: IfcStructuralLinearAction
rationale: IfcStructuralLinearAction contributes to the load cases and load combinations within a structural analysis model.
applicability: The assertion says IfcStructuralLinearAction 'supports' IfcStructuralAnalysisModel, but this is backwards: IfcStructuralAnalysisModel contains or references actions via IfcRelAssignsToProduct. The direction 'supports' is vague and potentially misleading.
conditions: when included as part of a structural analysis model

subject: IfcStructuralLinearAction
rationale: A linear force action requires a load definition of type linear force to describe its intensity.
conditions: when the action is a force-type linear load (e.g., distributed force per unit length)

subject: IfcStructuralLinearAction
rationale: Temperature loads applied along lines require temperature load definitions.
conditions: if the linear action is a thermal load acting on a linear element

subject: IfcStructuralLinearAction
rationale: The action entity contains or references a load value/definition that quantifies the action.
conditions: as part of the action definition

subject: IfcStructuralLinearAction
rationale: Linear actions can be assigned to load groups via IfcRelAssignsToGroup for load combination purposes.
conditions: when grouped into load groups or load cases

subject: IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration is used to group and configure individual IfcStructuralLoad instances for structural analysis.
conditions: when defining structural loading configurations

subject: IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration
rationale: The load configuration relies on relationship objects to associate loads with structural members or elements.
conditions: when linking loads to structural members

subject: IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration is typically defined within or referenced by a structural analysis model.
conditions: when used in a structural analysis context

subject: IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration
rationale: The load configuration supports structural members by defining how loads are applied to them.
conditions: when assigning load cases to structural elements

subject: IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration
rationale: Load configurations often belong to or reference load cases which define combinations of actions.
applicability: IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration does not depend on IfcStructuralLoadCase in the IFC schema directly. IfcStructuralLoadCase groups loads, and IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration is a load subtype that may be assigned to a load case, but there is no formal dependency or composition relationship. The configuration entity is used within load definitions, not as something that depends on load cases.
conditions: when grouping loads by load case

subject: IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration can be part of a load group hierarchy.
applicability: IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration does not depend on IfcStructuralLoadGroup. IfcStructuralLoadGroup organizes load cases and loads, but IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration is a subtype of IfcStructuralLoad and could be assigned to a group indirectly via load cases. There is no direct dependency from the configuration entity to the group entity in IFC.
conditions: when organizing loads into groups

subject: IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration
rationale: The configuration connects to actions that represent actual forces or displacements.
conditions: when defining actions with specific configurations

subject: IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration
rationale: Reactions can be configured in relation to the applied loads.
conditions: when analyzing reactions from loads

subject: IfcStructuralLoadCase
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadCase is a subtype of IfcStructuralLoadGroup and is used to group individual IfcStructuralLoad instances (such as point loads, line loads, etc.) into a load case combination.
applicability: All building types with structural analysis
conditions: When representing load cases as collections of individual loads

subject: IfcStructuralLoadCase
rationale: Load cases are typically part of an IfcStructuralAnalysisModel, which defines the overall analysis context including load groups and results.
conditions: For load cases to be assigned to a structural analysis context

subject: IfcStructuralLoadCase
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadCase inherits from IfcGroup, and relationships to its members are established via IfcRelAssignsToGroup.
applicability: All IFC models using load cases

The statement says 'requires IfcRelAssignsToGroup' but IfcRelAssignsToGroup is a relationship entity, not a required element in the sense of containment. The relationship goes in the other direction: IfcRelAssignsToGroup.RelatingGroup points to IfcStructuralLoadGroup (supertype of IfcStructuralLoadCase), and RelatedObjects are the assigned loads. The assertion describes the direction backwards.
conditions: When associating loads or other group members to the load case

subject: IfcStructuralLoadCase
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadCase groups multiple IfcStructuralAction instances representing individual actions like point loads, line loads, or temperature actions.
conditions: When defining actions (forces, displacements) that belong to the load case

subject: IfcStructuralLoadCase
rationale: Reactions can be grouped by load case, though typically IfcStructuralLoadCase contains actions, and reactions are derived results.
conditions: In analysis results context where reactions are associated with load cases
exceptions: Typically reactions are outputs, not inputs; this applies to result grouping

subject: IfcStructuralLoadCase
rationale: Additional metadata about the load case (e.g., load case type, description) can be stored in property sets attached via IfcRelDefinesByProperties.
applicability: IfcStructuralLoadCase can have property sets via IfcRelDefinesByProperties (or IfcRelDefinesByTemplate in IFC4+), but this is optional, not a dependency. The 'depends_on' relationship overstates the requirement — property sets are not mandatory for a valid IfcStructuralLoadCase instance. Many basic structural load cases are defined without any property sets.
conditions: When load case properties (e.g., nature, type, duration) need to be defined via property sets

subject: IfcStructuralLoadCase
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadCase is a specialization of IfcStructuralLoadGroup, so all base class attributes and relationships apply.
conditions: IfcStructuralLoadCase is a subtype of IfcStructuralLoadGroup, inheriting its structure

subject: IfcStructuralLoadCase
rationale: While IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity connects activities to structural members, the load case groups those activities, enabling traceability from load case to affected elements.
conditions: When relating structural actions/reactions to elements they act upon

subject: IfcStructuralLoadGroup
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadGroup groups instances of IfcStructuralLoad for structural analysis purposes, so it depends on the existence of individual loads to group.
conditions: when grouped for load combination analysis

subject: IfcStructuralLoadGroup
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadGroup is typically assigned to an IfcStructuralAnalysisModel which provides the context for the structural analysis.

subject: IfcStructuralLoadGroup
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadGroup may reference related result groups for the analysis outcomes.
conditions: when results are linked to the load group

subject: IfcStructuralLoadGroup
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadGroup serves as a container that groups multiple IfcStructuralLoad instances (actions such as dead load, live load, wind load, etc.) for load case and load combination definitions.

subject: IfcStructuralLoadGroup
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadGroup can represent a load case (using PredefinedType LOAD_CASE) which contains a set of loads.

subject: IfcStructuralLoadGroup
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadGroup organizes structural actions (loads applied to the structure) into meaningful groups for analysis.
applicability: IfcStructuralLoadGroup does not directly 'support' IfcStructuralAction. In IFC, IfcStructuralAction can be assigned to a load group via IfcRelAssignsToGroup, and load cases (IfcStructuralLoadCase, a subtype of IfcStructuralLoadGroup) group actions. However, the term 'supports' is ambiguous - actions are assigned to groups, not 'supported by' them. The relationship exists but the semantics of 'supports' differs from the standard IFC definition.
conditions: through grouping of actions into load cases

subject: IfcStructuralLoadGroup
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadGroup inherits from IfcGroup which is its direct supertype in the IFC schema.
conditions: as supertype

subject: IfcStructuralLoadGroup
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadGroup uses the relationship IfcRelAssignsToGroup to associate IfcStructuralLoad (or subclasses) to the group.
conditions: when assigning loads to the group

subject: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult is the abstract supertype for both load definitions and result definitions in structural analysis; it depends on the IfcStructuralLoad entity which defines the actual load values.
conditions: when representing load values in structural analysis

subject: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult is the supertype of IfcStructuralActivity (loads/actions) and IfcStructuralReaction (results), so activity entities depend on this type for classification.
conditions: when used to represent actions on structures

subject: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult provides the load and result definitions that populate an IfcStructuralAnalysisModel.
applicability: all building types with structural analysis requirements
conditions: when building a structural analysis model in IFC

subject: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult
rationale: Load or result instances (subtypes of IfcStructuralLoadOrResult) are connected to structural members via IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity relationships.
conditions: when linking loads/results to structural members

subject: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult can contain or be aggregated into configurations that group multiple load or result values together.
conditions: when multiple load cases or combinations are defined

subject: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult
rationale: Load instances under IfcStructuralLoadOrResult are typically assigned to an IfcStructuralLoadCase for organized analysis.
conditions: when loads are grouped into cases for analysis

subject: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult
rationale: IfcStructuralReaction is a direct subtype of IfcStructuralLoadOrResult, so the supertype supports the definition of reaction entities.
applicability: all building types undergoing structural analysis
conditions: when representing analysis results like support reactions or internal forces

subject: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult
rationale: IfcStructuralAction is a direct subtype of IfcStructuralLoadOrResult, so the supertype supports the definition of action entities.
conditions: when representing applied loads such as point loads, line loads, or area loads

subject: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult instances are connected to IfcStructuralMember entities (such as columns, beams, walls) through relationship objects.
conditions: when loads or results are assigned to a specific structural member

subject: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult can be connected to IfcStructuralConnection entities for representing forces at connections.
conditions: when loads or results are assigned to connections (supports, joints)

subject: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadOrResult requires the IfcStructuralLoad entity to define the actual load values (forces, moments, displacements) that constitute the load or result definition.
conditions: when defining the actual numeric values of a load or result

subject: IfcStructuralLoadLinearForce
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadLinearForce represents a linear force (force per unit length) load definition and requires a configuration context (e.g., IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration) to specify which structural members or edges it applies to.
conditions: when defined as distributed load along a line

subject: IfcStructuralLoadLinearForce
rationale: The linear load must be connected to a structural member (e.g., beam, edge of a slab) via an IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember relationship to define which physical element carries the load.
conditions: when assigned to a structural member

subject: IfcStructuralLoadLinearForce
rationale: A linear force load is typically applied to structural members (beams, columns, edges of slabs, walls) to represent distributed loads along their length.
applicability: The assertion says IfcStructuralLoadLinearForce requires IfcStructuralMember when used in a structural analysis context, but IfcStructuralLoadLinearForce is a load definition that can be referenced by IfcStructuralAction or IfcStructuralReaction which are then connected to IfcStructuralMember. The load definition itself does not have a direct relationship to IfcStructuralMember. The existing exception correctly notes it can exist standalone, but the 'requirement' itself is misleadingly stated.
conditions: when used in a structural analysis context
exceptions: can exist as a standalone load definition without assignment

subject: IfcStructuralLoadLinearForce
rationale: IfcStructuralCurveMember is the specific structural member type that receives linear loads along a curve/edge, making it the primary carrier of linear force loads.
conditions: when the load acts along a curve/beam

subject: IfcStructuralLoadLinearForce
rationale: The linear force load definition includes a coordinate system (LoadPlanarForce has placement) to define the load direction and orientation within the structural model.
conditions: when the load orientation requires 3D placement

subject: IfcStructuralLoadLinearForce
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadLinearForce is a subtype of IfcStructuralLoadPlanarForce, inheriting its properties for defining load components in the local coordinate system.

subject: IfcStructuralLoadLinearForce
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadLinearForce can be applied as a structural action (e.g., IfcStructuralLinearAction) that represents the physical load effect on the structure.
conditions: when the linear force is defined as an action on the structure

subject: IfcStructuralLoadPlanarForce
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadPlanarForce represents a planar force distribution and typically requires an IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration to define how the load is applied across the surface.
conditions: when representing distributed loads on surfaces

subject: IfcStructuralLoadPlanarForce
rationale: Planar force loads are applied to structural surface members such as walls, slabs, or shells.
conditions: when assigned to a structural analysis model

subject: IfcStructuralLoadPlanarForce
rationale: The load entity is typically part of a structural analysis model that governs load cases and combinations.
conditions: for structural load assignment and analysis

subject: IfcStructuralLoadPlanarForce
rationale: Planar force loads are grouped under specific load cases for analysis.
conditions: to categorize the load type (e.g., dead, live, wind, snow)

subject: IfcStructuralLoadPlanarForce
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadPlanarForce provides the force values for structural actions acting on planar surfaces.
conditions: when used as a load value in an action definition

subject: IfcStructuralLoadPlanarForce
rationale: In some analysis workflows, planar loads can be transformed into equivalent curve actions.
conditions: when planar force distributions are converted to equivalent line loads

subject: IfcStructuralLoadPlanarForce
rationale: The IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity relationship entity links loads to the structural members they act upon.
conditions: when assigning the load to a structural member or connection

subject: IfcStructuralLoadPlanarForce
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadPlanarForce inherits from IfcStructuralLoadOrResult, which is the abstract supertype for all structural loads and results.
conditions: as the abstract supertype hierarchy

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleDisplacement
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadSingleDisplacement inherits from IfcStructuralLoad and is used in structural analysis models; a configuration context may be required to specify how the displacement applies.
conditions: When the displacement load has multiple load cases or positional variations

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleDisplacement
rationale: A structural load (including a displacement) must be applied to a structural member (e.g., column, beam, foundation) to have engineering meaning.
conditions: Must be assigned to a structural member via IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember
exceptions: IfcStructuralLoadSingleDisplacement does not always depend_on IfcStructuralMember. It can be assigned directly to an IfcStructuralActivity via IfcRelConnectsStructuralActivity, which relates to IfcStructuralItem (the parent of IfcStructuralMember). The relationship through IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember is only one possible path, and the load can also be assigned to an IfcStructuralCurveMember or IfcStructuralSurfaceMember without going through the exact IfcRelConnectsStructuralMember relationship.

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleDisplacement
rationale: The displacement load definition is used within a structural analysis model context for computing structural responses.
conditions: The load must be part of a structural analysis model for simulation

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleDisplacement
rationale: Displacement loads typically have a direction vector (e.g., x, y, z components). IfcDirection may be used to specify this orientation.
conditions: When the displacement is defined with orientation
exceptions: If the displacement is defined as a scalar magnitude without direction

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleDisplacement
rationale: The relationship entity is used to assign the load definition to products in the IFC model.
conditions: For assigning the load to a structural item or group

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleDisplacement
rationale: A single displacement load is often applied at a structural connection point where boundary conditions or supports are defined.
conditions: When the displacement is applied at a point (point displacement)
exceptions: Not applicable for linear or planar displacement loads

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleForce
rationale: A single force load may depend on a load configuration context.
conditions: when the load is part of a load case with multiple configurations

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleForce
rationale: Single force loads are inputs to structural analysis models.
conditions: when used in structural analysis

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleForce
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadSingleForce inherits from IfcStructuralLoadOrResult.
conditions: as parent type for classification

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleForce
rationale: A single point force is typically applied at a structural point connection.
conditions: when the force is applied at a point

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleForce
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadSingleForce can be assigned to a structural action instance.
conditions: when used to define a structural action

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleForce
rationale: Assignment relationships may be needed to link loads to analysis tasks.
conditions: when the load is assigned to a structural analysis process

subject: IfcStructuralLoadStatic
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadStatic is abstract, typically associated with IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration that groups load values.
conditions: when analyzing load cases

subject: IfcStructuralLoadStatic
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadStatic is a subtype of IfcStructuralLoadOrResult, so it depends on that supertype for its definition.
conditions: as part of inheritance hierarchy

subject: IfcStructuralLoadStatic
rationale: Static loads are applied through structural actions (point loads, line loads, area loads) in IFC.
conditions: when assigning loads to structural members

subject: IfcStructuralLoadStatic
rationale: A static load must be related to a structural member (beam, column, wall, etc.) to have meaning in a model.
conditions: when the load is assigned to a structural element

subject: IfcStructuralLoadStatic
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadStatic can be concretely represented as a linear force load.
conditions: when representing line loads

subject: IfcStructuralLoadStatic
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadStatic can be concretely represented as a planar force load on surfaces.
conditions: when representing area/surface loads

subject: IfcStructuralLoadStatic
rationale: Static loads support the connection relationships between loads and structural members.
conditions: when connecting loads to members

subject: IfcStructuralLoadStatic
rationale: Temperature loads can be a type of static load in IFC, grouped under the static load concept.
conditions: when thermal effects are considered

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleForceWarping
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadSingleForceWarping is a subtype of IfcStructuralLoadSingleForce, extended with warping moment capability. It depends on the base force load type.
conditions: When modeling structural point loads with warping effects

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleForceWarping
rationale: This load definition supports point actions that include warping torsion, enabling more accurate structural analysis for certain member types.
applicability: Structural analysis of beams and columns with torsion
conditions: When a point action needs warping torsion effects included

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleForceWarping
rationale: The load definition connects to structural members (beams, columns, etc.) that carry the load and experience warping effects.
conditions: When assigning the warping load to a structural element

subject: IfcStructuralLoadSingleForceWarping
rationale: The load type is part of a structural analysis model that defines the overall analysis framework.
conditions: When used within a structural analysis context

subject: IfcStructuralMember
rationale: Structural members connect to structural connections (nodes) to form load paths in a structural system.
applicability: all building types with load-bearing structures
conditions: when transferring loads between structural elements

subject: IfcStructuralMember
rationale: Structural members are designed to carry and transfer loads; loads are essential to their function.
conditions: during structural analysis and design

subject: IfcStructuralMember
rationale: A structural member must be made of a material (e.g., steel, concrete, timber) to have physical properties.
conditions: for physical realization
exceptions: if modeled only as an abstract analytical element

Even for physical realization, an IfcStructuralMember may use IfcMaterialProfileSet or IfcMaterialConstituentSet rather than a direct IfcMaterial, or may reference material properties via IfcMaterialDefinitionRepresentation. The assertion oversimplifies the material assignment pathway.

subject: IfcStructuralMember
rationale: IfcStructuralMember is the abstract supertype; curve members are common specializations.
conditions: when the member functions as a beam or column

subject: IfcStructuralMember
rationale: Structural members like beams and columns support slabs.
conditions: when slab is supported by beams or columns
exceptions: The assertion says IfcStructuralMember supports IfcSlab, but slabs can also be supported by walls (load-bearing walls), directly on columns without beams (flat slabs/flat plates), or on grade. The condition only mentions 'when slab is supported by beams or columns' but misses wall-supported slabs.

subject: IfcStructuralMember
rationale: Structural members can support walls, transferring their load to foundations.
conditions: when walls are supported by grade beams or foundations
exceptions: load-bearing walls that are themselves structural members

subject: IfcStructuralMember
rationale: Structural members provide the substrate and support for coverings.
conditions: when cladding or finishes are attached to the structural frame

subject: IfcStructuralMember
rationale: Structural members connect at point connections (e.g., beam-column joints).
conditions: at nodes or joints in a structural frame

subject: IfcStructuralMember
rationale: Surface members (walls, slabs) connect with linear members for load transfer.
applicability: buildings with shear walls and frames
conditions: when used together in a combined structural system

subject: IfcStructuralMember
rationale: The structural member's behavior is analyzed within a structural analysis model.
applicability: all building types undergoing structural analysis

While IfcStructuralMember participates in structural analysis models via IfcRelAssignsToGroup, the dependency direction is more accurately that the analysis model groups/aggregates multiple structural members. A member does not 'depend_on' the analysis model; rather the model includes the member. This is a semantic direction reversal.
conditions: when performing structural analysis and simulation

subject: IfcStructuralLoadTemperature
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadTemperature often requires an IfcStructuralLoadConfiguration to define how temperature varies spatially on the structural member.
conditions: When temperature loads vary across the structure

subject: IfcStructuralLoadTemperature
rationale: The effect of temperature loads depends on the material thermal properties (e.g., thermal expansion coefficient) stored in property sets attached to the structural element.
conditions: When material thermal properties are assigned

subject: IfcStructuralLoadTemperature
rationale: Temperature load effects depend on material properties like coefficient of thermal expansion, which are defined via IfcMaterialDefinition.
conditions: For calculating thermal strains and stresses

subject: IfcStructuralLoadTemperature
rationale: Temperature loads need to be assigned to load groups/cases for structural analysis.
conditions: When grouping temperature loads into load cases

subject: IfcStructuralLoadTemperature
rationale: IfcStructuralLoadTemperature is applied to structural members (e.g., beams, columns, slabs) to represent thermal effects.
conditions: When applying temperature load to a structural element

subject: IfcStructuralLoadTemperature
